universe.title: Status and Reporting Line of Chief Compliance Officers
universe.description: Financial institutions are required to appoint Chief Compliance Officers and compliance officers at managerial level in their branches. The required minimum grades for the appointment of CCOs and COs have been reviewed, along with the option for banks to operate a cluster structure where a designated CO is responsible for a cluster of branches instead of having a CO at each branch. Compliance Officers must be clearly separated from internal control and audit functions, and compliance officers must meet specific criteria based on the category of their institution. Compliance with these requirements is mandatory for all financial institutions.

universe.commentOnStatus: Still applicable for financial institutions to maintain effective compliance structures.

universe.title: Regulatory Framework for Mobile Payments Services in Nigeria

Ensure a structured and orderly development of mobile money services in Nigeria with clear definition of various participants and their expected roles and responsibilities. c. Specification of the minimum technical and business requirements for the various participants recognized for the mobile money services industry in Nigeria.

conduct_risk.source: Pension Reform Act (Amendment) 2014
conduct_risk.title: Objectives
conduct_risk.description: The objectives of this Act are to –  (a) establish a uniform set of rules, regulations and standards for the administration and payments of retirement benefits for the Public Service of the Federation, the Public Service of the Federal Capital Territory, the Public Service of the State Governments, the Public Service of the Local Government Councils and the Private Sector;  (b) make provision for the smooth operations of the Contributory Pension Scheme(CPS) ;  (c) ensure that every person who worked in either the Public Service of the Federation, Federal Capital Territory, States and Local Governments or the Private Sector receives his retirement benefits as and when due; and  (d) assist improvident individuals by ensuring that they save in order to cater for their livelihood during old age.
conduct_risk.plain: The Bank shall:  1. Apply a uniform pension process by ensuring compliance with the rules and standards of the Contributory Pension Scheme (CPS) for all eligible employees, whether in public or private sector alignment.  2. Enroll eligible employees in the Contributory Pension Scheme (CPS) and ensure consistent monthly remittance of pension contributions (both employer and employee portions) to their Pension Fund Administrator (PFA).  3. Ensure timely retirement benefits, by keeping accurate records and remitting contributions promptly, so that employees receive their pension entitlements as and when due.  4. Promote financial discipline by helping employees save regularly toward their retirement, thus preventing hardship in old age.
conduct_risk.riskDescription: Failure to enroll staff or remit pension may lead to penalties, staff dissatisfaction, or legal claims
conduct_risk.primaryControl: Staff enrollment in CPS, regular payroll deduction, and monthly pension remittance
conduct_risk.additionalControl: HR audit and PenCom reporting

conduct_risk.source: Pension Reform Act (Amendment) 2014
conduct_risk.title: Application
conduct_risk.description: (1) The provisions of this Act shall apply to any employment in the Public Service of the Federation, the Public Service of the Federal Capital Territory, the Public Service of the States, the Public Service of the Local Governments and the Private Sector.  (2) In the case of the Private Sector, the Scheme shall apply to employees who are in the employment of an organization in which there are 15 or more employees.  (3) Notwithstanding the provisions of subsection (2) of this section, employees of organisations with less than three employees as well as self-employed persons shall be entitled to participate under the scheme in accordance with guidelines issued by the Commission.
conduct_risk.plain: The Bank shall implement the CPS for all employees, especially since it has more than 15 staff. Voluntary participation may also be allowed for smaller staff groups or self-employed roles under PenCom guidelines.
conduct_risk.riskDescription: Non-compliance with participation rules may result in sanctions
conduct_risk.primaryControl: Ensure onboarding includes CPS explanation and registration
conduct_risk.additionalControl: Orientation checklist and HRMIS flag

conduct_risk.source: Pension Reform Act (Amendment) 2014
conduct_risk.title: Rate of Contribution & Group Life
conduct_risk.description: (1) The contribution for any employee to which this Act applies shall be made in the following rates relating to his monthly emoluments –  (a) a minimum of ten per cent by the employer; and (b) a minimum of eight per cent by the employee.  (5) In addition to the rates specified in subsection (1) of this section, every employer shall maintain a Group Life Insurance Policy in favour of each employee for a minimum of three times the annual total emolument of the employee and premium shall be paid not later than the date of commencement of the cover.  (6) Where the employer failed, refused or omitted to make payment as and when due, the employer shall make arrangement to effect the payment of claims arising from the death of any staff in its employment during such period.

conduct_risk.source: Discontinuation of Death Benefits Account (DBA) for Deceased Employees under the Contributory Pension Scheme
conduct_risk.title: PRA 2014, s. 11(1), (5); PenCom Notice (DBA Discontinuation, 2020)
conduct_risk.description: Section 11(1) of the Pension Reform Act (PRA) 2014 mandates every eligible employee to maintain a Retirement Savings Account (RSA) with a Pension Fund Administrator of his/her choice.  The Act also mandates every employer to open a nominal RSA within six months of assumption of duty for the employee who fails to open an RSA in accordance with section 11(5) of the PRA 2014. Employers are therefore required to ensure that RSAs are opened for all their employees.  Prior to the PRA 2014, Death Benefits Accounts (DBA) have been used by legal beneficiaries to access the benefits of the deceased employees who did not open RSA during their lifetime. However, pursuant to the above cited statutory provisions, this practice is no longer valid.  Accordingly, the general public is hereby notified that the processing of DBA for death benefits claims would be discontinued with effect from 1 February, 2020. All PFAs have been directed to stop the opening of DBAs with effect from 31 January, 2020.  The National Pension Commission reiterates the need for all employees to ensure that they open RSAs with any PFA of their choice. A list of licensed PFAs can be found on the Commission’s website: www.pencom.gov.hg
conduct_risk.plain: The Bank shall:  1. Ensure that every eligible employee opens a Retirement Savings Account (RSA) with a licensed Pension Fund Administrator (PFA) upon employment. 2. If an employee fails to open an RSA within six months of joining, the Bank must open a nominal RSA on the employee’s behalf, as required by law. 3. Stop the use of Death Benefits Accounts (DBAs) for deceased employees. As of 1 February 2020, DBAs are no longer valid for processing death benefit claims. 4. Ensure that no DBA is opened or processed after 31 January 2020, in compliance with PenCom’s directive. 5. Educate and encourage all employees to promptly register and maintain their RSAs to secure future pension benefits.

conduct_risk.source: Employee Compensation Act, 2010
conduct_risk.title: Compensation for Injury
conduct_risk.description: 1. Any employee, whether or not in a workplace, who suffers any disabling injury arising out of or in the course of employment shall be entitled to payment of compensation in accordance with Part IV of this Act. 2. An employee is entitled to payment of compensation with respect to any accident sustained while on the way between the place of work and— (a) the employee’s principal or secondary residence; (b) the place where the employee usually takes meals; or (c) the place where he usually receives remuneration, provided that the employer has prior notification of such place.  3. Where an injury disables an employee from earning full remuneration at the workplace, compensation shall be payable pursuant to this Act from the first working day following the day of the injury, except that only a health care benefit shall be payable in respect of the day of the injury.  4.  Where the injury or disease is caused by accident and the accident arose out of the employment, unless the contrary is shown, it shall be presumed that the injury occurred in the course of the employment. Where an injury or disease is superimposed on an already existing disability, compensation shall be allowed only for the proportion of the disability following the personal injury or disease that may reasonably be attributed to the personal injury or disease, the measure of the disability attributable to the personal injury or disease shall, unless the contrary is shown, be the amount of the difference between the employee’s disability before and disability after the occurrence of the personal injury or disease.
conduct_risk.plain: The Bank shall:  1. Ensure that any employee who suffers a disabling injury arising out of or in the course of their work duties (even outside the physical workplace) receives compensation under Part IV of the Act.  2. Compensate an employee for injuries sustained while traveling between work and their residence, meal location, or remuneration point.  3. Begin paying compensation from the first working day after the injury if the employee cannot earn full wages. Only health care costs are covered on the day of injury.  4. Treat any workplace accident as having occurred in the course of employment unless proven otherwise.   5. Compensate only for the new disability portion caused by a work-related injury or disease if it worsens a pre-existing condition.
conduct_risk.riskDescription: Undercompensation or denial of benefits
conduct_risk.primaryControl: Incident reports, eligibility checks, legal vetting
conduct_risk.additionalControl: Periodic claims review

conduct_risk.source: Employee Compensation Act, 2010
conduct_risk.title: Compensation for Mental Stress
conduct_risk.description: (1) Subject to sub-section (2) of this section, an employee shall be entitled to compensation for mental stress not resulting from an injury for which the employee is otherwise entitled to compensation, only if the mental stress is— (a) an acute reaction to a sudden and unexpected traumatic event arising out of or in the course of the employee's employment; or (b) diagnosed by an accredited medical practitioner as a mental or physical condition amounting to mental stress arising out of the nature of work or the occurrence of any event in the course of the employee's employment. (2) Where the mental stress is caused as a result of the decision of the employer to change the work, the working conditions of work organization in such a way as to unfairly exceed the work ability and capacity of the employee thereby leading to mental stress, such situation shall be liable to compensation in the form as may be determined under any regulation made by the Board.
conduct_risk.plain: The Bank shall ensure:  1. That employees are protected from mental stress caused by their work. If an employee suffers mental stress due to: - a sudden and unexpected traumatic event during work, or - work-related stress diagnosed by a certified medical practitioner,  the employee is entitled to compensation.  2. That it does not change an employee’s job, work conditions, or workload in a way that unfairly exceeds the employee’s ability or capacity. If such changes occur and lead to mental stress, the Bank may be required to compensate the employee, in line with the rules made by the regulatory Board.
conduct_risk.riskDescription: Work stress resulting in unclaimed or mishandled claims
conduct_risk.primaryControl: Fair work allocation, EAP (if available), grievance mechanism
conduct_risk.additionalControl: Annual stress audit

conduct_risk.source: Industrial Training Fund (ITF) Act, Cap I9
conduct_risk.title: Liability to Contribute to the Fund
conduct_risk.description: (1) Every employer having either 5 or more employees in its establishment, or having less than 5 employees but with a turnover of N50m and above per annum, shall, in respect of each calendar year and or the prescribed date, contribute to the Fund one per centum of its total annual payroll. (2) Any supplier, contractor or consultant bidding or soliciting contracts, businesses, goods and services from any Federal Government Ministry, Department, Agency, commercial, industrial and private entity shall fulfill the statutory obligations of its employees with respect to payment of training contribution to the Fund. (3) Any liable organization, public or private including companies situate in the Free Trade Zones requiring approval for expatriate quota and/or utilizing custom services in matters of export and import, must show proof of compliance with this Act in respect of payment of training contribution of its employees and all regulatory agencies of the Federal Government shall ensure compliance with section 6 (1) - (3) of this Act
conduct_risk.plain: The Bank shall: 1. Contribute 1% of its total annual payroll to the Industrial Training Fund (ITF) every calendar year if it: a) Employs 5 or more staff, or  b) Has a turnover of ₦50 million or more per annum.  2. Ensure ITF compliance is up to date before bidding for any contract with Federal Government MDAs or private entities.  3. Provide proof of ITF contribution compliance when:  a) Applying for expatriate quotas, or  b) Using customs services for imports and exports.  4. Be aware that Federal Government agencies are mandated to enforce compliance with these obligations.
conduct_risk.riskDescription: Failure to contribute may lead to fines, contract disqualification, or denial of quotas and customs services
conduct_risk.primaryControl: Annual payroll review, ITF registration, remittance schedule, compliance certificate file
conduct_risk.additionalControl: ITF liaison officer; internal checklist before bidding or quota requests

conduct_risk.source: National Minimum Wage Act, 2019
conduct_risk.title: Enforcement.
conduct_risk.description: The national minimum wage may be enforced by the aggrieved worker, trade unions and Minister of Labour and Employment as follows— (a) a worker who is paid an amount less than the national minimum wage is contractually entitled to whichever is the higher amount of the difference between his pay and the amount of the national minimum wage that he should have been paid ; (d) where an employer fails to pay the national minimum wage to a worker or a group of workers, an authorised officer shall serve a notice of enforcement requiring the employer to pay the arrears of the wage to the worker named on the notice within 30 days, but the employer is entitled to appeal the notice to the Minister of Labour and Employment who shall resolve the matter within 30 days of the receipt of the appeal ; (e) the notice of enforcement shall state the— (i) amount owed to the worker, (ii) period to which the payment applies, and (iii) time limit for the payment ; and
conduct_risk.plain: The Bank shall: 1. Ensure that no worker is paid less than the national minimum wage, as any underpaid employee has a legal right to claim the difference between what was paid and what should have been paid.  2. Comply with enforcement notices issued by an authorised officer if found in breach—such notices:  a) Require the Bank to pay wage arrears within 30 days. b) May be appealed to the Minister of Labour and Employment, who must decide within 30 days of receiving the appeal.  3. Take note that any enforcement notice must specify:  a) The amount owed to each affected worker, b) The time period the unpaid wages relate to, and c) The deadline for payment.
conduct_risk.riskDescription: Legal action and reputational risk if wage arrears go unpaid
conduct_risk.primaryControl: Wage compliance monitoring, enforcement response workflow
conduct_risk.additionalControl: Maintain a wage compliance register and response SOP

conduct_risk.source: Trade Dispute Act, 2006
conduct_risk.title: Prohibition of lock-outs and strikes before issue of award of National Industrial Court.
conduct_risk.description: (1) An employer shall not declare or take part in a lock-out and a worker shall not take part in a strike in connection with any trade dispute where— (a) the procedure specified in section 4 or 6 of this Act has not been complied with in relation to the dispute; or (b) a conciliator has been appointed under section 8 of this Act for the purpose of effecting a settlement of the dispute; or (c) the dispute has been referred for settlement to the Industrial Arbitration Panel under section 9 of this Act; or (d) an award by an arbitration tribunal has become binding under section 13 (3) of this Act; or (e) the dispute has subsequently been referred to the National Industrial Court under section 14 (1) or 17 of this Act; or (f) the National Industrial Court has issued an award on the reference.
conduct_risk.plain: The Bank shall not engage in a lock-out related to a trade dispute if:  a) The dispute resolution steps in Sections 4 or 6 (internal settlement or report to the Minister) have not been followed, or b) A conciliator has been appointed to resolve the dispute, or c) The dispute has been referred to the Industrial Arbitration Panel, or d) An arbitration award has become binding, or e) The dispute has been referred to the National Industrial Court, or f) The National Industrial Court has issued a ruling on the matter.  The Bank must wait for final resolution through proper legal processes before initiating or participating in a lock-out.
conduct_risk.riskDescription: Illegal lock-out leading to legal sanction or reputational harm
conduct_risk.primaryControl: Labour relations protocol aligned to Act
conduct_risk.additionalControl: Periodic labour law training for HR/legal

conduct_risk.source: Trade Dispute Act, 2006
conduct_risk.title: Power to appoint board of inquiry.
conduct_risk.description: (1) Where any trade dispute exists or is apprehended, the Minister may cause inquiry to be made into the causes and circumstances of the dispute and, if he thinks fit, may refer any matter appearing to him to be connected with or relevant to the dispute to a board of inquiry appointed for the purpose by the Minister; and the board shall inquire into the matter referred to it and report thereon to the Minister. (2) The Minister may refer any other matter connected with industrial conditions in Nigeria to a board of inquiry appointed for the purpose by the Minister; and the board shall inquire into the matter referred to it and report thereon to the Minister.
conduct_risk.plain: The Bank shall:  a) Cooperate fully if the Minister appoints a Board of Inquiry to investigate the causes or circumstances of a trade dispute involving the Bank. b) Provide relevant information and participate in the inquiry process when requested. c) Be aware that the Minister may refer any issue related to industrial conditions (even outside a specific dispute) to such a board.  This means the Bank must be prepared to support formal inquiries into workplace or dispute-related matters initiated by government authorities.
conduct_risk.riskDescription: Obstruction of inquiry or failure to provide relevant info
conduct_risk.primaryControl: Centralised case file management and inquiry liaison protocol
conduct_risk.additionalControl: Appoint liaison officer for government inquiries

conduct_risk.source: Nigeria Labour Act (Cap L1, Laws of the Federation of Nigeria) (2004)
conduct_risk.title: Manner of payment
conduct_risk.description: (1) Subject to this section‐   (a)     the wages of a worker shall in all contracts be made payable in legal tender and  not otherwise; and   (b)     if in any contract the whole or any part of the wages of a worker is made payable in any other manner the contract shall be illegal, null and void.   (2) An employer may provide food, a dwelling place or any other allowance or privilege as a part of a worker's remuneration if the food, dwelling place, allowance or  privilege is prescribed by law, by a collective agreement or by an arbitration award because it is customary or desirable in view of the nature of the industry or occupation in  which the worker is engaged; but in no case shall an employer give to any worker any  intoxicating liquor or noxious drug by way of remuneration.   (3) Except where otherwise expressly permitted by this Act, wages payable in money  shall be paid only in legal tender or, with the prior consent in writing of the worker con‐  cerned, by cheque or postal order and payment or purported payment in any other form  shall be illegal, null and void.
conduct_risk.plain: The Bank shall : 1a. Ensure that all employee wages are paid in Nigerian legal tender (naira) only. Any contract that stipulates payment in any other form is illegal and must not be used.  b. Not enter into or enforce any employment contract that pays wages in forms other than legal tender, as such contracts are invalid and unlawful.  2. Offer allowances (e.g. housing, food) as part of employee remuneration only if: – such allowances are permitted by law, – included in a collective agreement or arbitration award, or – customary in the banking industry.  3. Pay all monetary wages only in cash (legal tender), or by cheque but only with the employee’s prior written consent. Any other payment method  is not allowed and shall be treated as illegal.

conduct_risk.primaryControl: All wage contracts and payroll transactions reviewed and processed only via legal tender or approved alternatives.

conduct_risk.source: Nigeria Labour Act (Cap L1, Laws of the Federation of Nigeria) (2004)
conduct_risk.title: Advances
conduct_risk.description: (1) No employer may make to a worker an advance of wages in excess of one  month's wages.   (2) Where an advance in respect of wages has been paid to a worker the minimum  period for the recovery of the advance by the employer shall be three months.   (3) No advance in respect of wages shall be paid to a worker who is liable to repay  any part of such an advance paid to him previously, except in cases of necessity as so  approved by the employer.   (4) No employer shall make any deduction by way of discount, interest or any similar  charge on account of any advance of wages paid to a worker in anticipation of the regular period of payment of the wages.   (5) The State Authority may by order declare that this section shall not apply to any  particular kind of advance paid to any particular class of worker or to all workers.
conduct_risk.plain: The Bank shall:  1. Limit wage advances to no more than one month’s salary per employee. Any advance beyond this limit is unlawful and void.  2. Ensure that any wage advance given is recovered over a minimum period of three (3) months. Recovery in less time violates the law.  3. Not approve a new wage advance for an employee who is still repaying a previous advance, unless it is a case of necessity and is formally approved by the Bank.  4. Not apply any interest, discount, fee, or similar charge on wage advances. Employees must repay only the original amount advanced.
conduct_risk.riskDescription: Financial loss, employee disputes, or regulatory penalties if wage advance terms breach legal requirements.
conduct_risk.primaryControl: Payroll policies explicitly limit wage advances; HR approvals required; system-enforced recovery schedules.
conduct_risk.additionalControl: Mandatory HR review for each advance request and exception-based approval by senior HR.

conduct_risk.source: Nigeria Labour Act (Cap L1, Laws of the Federation of Nigeria) (2004)
conduct_risk.title: Deductions (including deductions for overpayment of wages)
conduct_risk.description: 5.  (1) Except where it is expressly permitted by this Act or any other law, no employer shall make any deduction or make any agreement or contract with a worker for any deduction from the wages to be paid by the employer to the worker, or for any payment  to the employer by the worker, for or in respect of any fines: Provided that, with the prior consent in writing of an authorised labour officer, a  reasonable deduction may be made in respect of injury or loss caused to the employer by  the wilful misconduct or neglect of the worker.   (2) An employer may with the consent of a worker make deductions from the wages of the worker and pay to the appropriate person any contributions to provident or pension funds or other schemes agreed to by the worker and approved by the State Authority.   (3) Upon the registration and recognition of any of the trade unions specified in Part  A of Schedule 3 to the Trade Unions Act, the employer shall‐    (a)     make deductions from the wages of all workers eligible to be members of the  union for the purpose of paying contributions to the trade union so recognised;  and   (b)             pay any sum so deducted to the union, but a worker may contract out of the system, in writing, and where he has done so, no deductions shall be made from his wages in respect of contributions mentioned in paragraph (a) of this section.   (4) No deductions shall be made from the wages and salaries of persons who are eligible members of any of the trade unions specified in Part B of Schedule 3 of the Trade  Unions Act except if the person concerned has accepted, in writing, to make voluntary  contributions to the trade union.   (5) Deductions may be made from the wages of a worker in respect of overpayment of wages, but only in respect of any such overpayment made during the three months  immediately preceding the month in which the overpayment was discovered.   (6) An employer shall, when making a payment to a trade union under paragraph (b) of subsection (3) of this section, include with such payment a list of the employees from whom deductions were made pursuant to paragraph (c) of the said subsection.   (7) Notwithstanding any other provisions of this Act, the total amount of deductions that may be made from the wages of a worker in anyone month shall not exceed one third of the wages of the worker for that month.
conduct_risk.plain: The Bank shall:  1. Not deduct any fines or make contracts for deductions from an employee's wages unless it is: a) Permitted by this Act or another law, and b) Approved in writing by an authorised labour officer for losses caused by the employee’s wilful misconduct or neglect.  2. Only deduct contributions to pension, provident funds, or other schemes with the employee’s consent, and only if approved by the State Authority.  3. Deduct union dues from the wages of workers who are eligible members of registered and recognised trade unions listed in Part A of Schedule 3 of the Trade Unions Act, and: a) Pay the deducted sums directly to the trade union, and b) Not deduct dues from workers who opt out in writing.  4. Not deduct union dues from wages of workers in trade unions listed in Part B of Schedule 3, unless the employee has voluntarily agreed in writing.  5. Only deduct overpaid wages if the overpayment was made within the three months immediately before the month the error was discovered.  6. Provide a list of employees alongside any payment of union dues, showing whose wages were deducted.  7. Ensure total deductions in any given month do not exceed one-third (1/3) of the employee’s wages for that month.
conduct_risk.riskDescription: Unlawful deductions may lead to labour disputes, financial penalties, or reputational harm due to non-compliance with employee rights and wage protection laws.
conduct_risk.primaryControl: - Payroll system enforces maximum deduction limits.- Written consents required for union dues and fund contributions.- Overpayment recovery tracked by payroll system.- HR/labour officer authorisation processes in place for misconduct deductions.
conduct_risk.additionalControl: Annual payroll compliance audit and HR staff training on labour law
conduct_risk.residualLikelihood: - HR audit for compliance with deduction authorisations.- Trade union payments verified monthly.- Automatic rejection of deductions exceeding 1/3 limit.
conduct_risk.residualImpact: Monthly payroll cycle or when deductions are triggered

conduct_risk.source: Nigeria Labour Act (Cap L1, Laws of the Federation of Nigeria) (2004)
conduct_risk.title: Written particulars of terms of employment
conduct_risk.description: (1) Not later than three months after the beginning of a worker's period of employment with an employer, the employer shall give to the worker a written statement specifying‐   (a)   the name of the employer or group of employers, and where appropriate, of the undertaking by which the worker is employed; (b)    the name and address of the worker and the place and date of his engagement;   (c)    the nature of the employment;   (d)    if the contract is for a fixed term, the date when the contract expires;   (e)    the appropriate period of notice to be given by the party wishing to terminate the contract, due regard being had to section 11 of this Act;   (f)       the rates of wages and method of calculation thereof and the manner and periodicity of payment of wages;   (g)     any terms and conditions relating to‐      (i)  hours of work; or     (ii)  holidays and holiday pay; or        (iii)  incapacity for work due to sickness or injury, including any provisions  for sick pay; and   (h)     any special conditions of the contract.   (2) If after the date to which the said statement relates there is a change in the terms  to be included or referred to in the statement the employer‐   (a)   shall, not more than one month after the change, inform the worker of the nature of the change by a written statement; and     (b)   if he does not leave a copy of the statement with the worker, shall preserve the statement and ensure that the worker has reasonable opportunities of reading it       (c)     in the course of his employment, or that it is made reasonably accessible to the  worker in some other way. (3) A statement under subsection (1) or (2) of this section may, for all or any of the particulars to be given by the statement, refer the worker to some other document which the worker has reasonable opportunities of reading in the course of his employment or  which is made reasonably accessible to the worker in some other way.   (4) If the employer, in referring in the said statement to any such document, indicates  to the worker that future changes in the terms particularised in the document will be entered in the document (or recorded by some other means for the information of persons  referred to in the document), the employer need not under subsection (2) of this section  inform the worker of any such change which is duly entered or recorded not more than  one month after the change is made.   (5) If, not more than six months after the termination of a worker's period of employment, a further period of employment is begun with the same employer and the terms  of employment are the same, no statement need be given under subsection (1) of this section in respect of the second period of employment, so however that this subsection shall be without prejudice to the operation of subsection (2) of this section if there is a change in the terms of employment. (6) The provisions of this section in respect of written statements shall not apply if‐   (a)      a worker has a written contract of employment which covers each of the particulars mentioned in subsection (1) of this section; and   (b)    he has a copy of that written contract.
conduct_risk.plain: The Bank shall:  1. Provide a written statement of employment to each employee within three months of starting work, specifying: a) Name of the bank (employer) and, where applicable, the department or business unit; b) Name, address, and engagement details of the employee (place and date hired); c) The job title or nature of the employment; d) Expiry date if it is a fixed-term contract; e) Required notice period for contract termination (in line with Section 11 of the Labour Act); f) Wages (rate, calculation method, and payment frequency); g) Terms and conditions on working hours, holidays and holiday pay, sick leave or incapacity and sick pay; h) Any special conditions attached to the contract.  2. Notify the employee in writing of any change in the employment terms within one month of such change.  3. If the written statement is not handed to the employee: keep a copy, and ensure it is reasonably accessible to the employee, either during employment or via other means.  4. The written statement may refer the employee to another accessible document containing the required employment terms, provided: (i) The employee has a fair opportunity to read it during employment or via a reasonable method.  5. If such referenced documents are updated within one month of a change, the bank does not need to re-issue a new statement under (2).  6. If a former employee resumes work within six months under identical employment terms, the bank does not need to reissue the statement, except where terms have changed.  7. The obligations under this section do not apply where: (a) The worker already has a written contract of employment that fully covers all the above particulars, and (b) The worker has a copy of that contract.

conduct_risk.title: Contracts: general
conduct_risk.description: (2) An employer shall be responsible for the performance of any contract made by  any person acting on his behalf.   (3) Except in the case of a contract of apprenticeship, no person under the age of  sixteen years shall be capable or entering into a contract of employment under this Act.   (4) No contract shall provide for the payment of wages at intervals exceeding one  month unless the written consent of the State Authority has been previously obtained.    (6) No contract shall‐   (a)     make it a condition of employment that a worker shall or shall not join a trade   union or shall or shall not relinquish membership or a trade union; or   (b)   cause the dismissal of, or otherwise prejudice, a worker‐      (i)  by reason of trade union membership; or    (ii)  because of trade union activities outside working hours or, with the consent of the employer, within working hours; or    (iii)   by reason of the fact that he has lost or been deprived of membership of a  trade union or has refused or been unable to become, or for any other reason is not, a member of a trade union.   (7) A contract shall be terminated‐   (a)       by the expiry of the period for which it was made; or   (b)       by the death of the worker before the expiry of that period; or   (c)      by notice in accordance with section 11 of this Act or in any other way in which a contract is legally terminable or held to be terminated.   (8) The termination of a contract by the death of a worker shall be without prejudice   to the legal claims of his personal representatives or dependants.What is the subsections that is relevant and actionable for the commercial bank alone and only
conduct_risk.plain: The Bank shall: 1. Be responsible for any employment contract entered into by any person acting on its behalf, including HR officers, managers.  2. Not employ any person under the age of 16, except under a lawful apprenticeship arrangement.  3. Not enter into any employment contract that provides for wage payments at intervals longer than one month, unless the Bank obtains prior written approval from the relevant State Authority.  4. Not include any condition in an employment contract requiring an employee to join or not to join a trade union.  5. Not dismiss or prejudice any employee based on their trade union membership.  6. Not dismiss or prejudice any employee for participating in trade union activities outside working hours, or within working hours where permitted by the Bank.  7. Not penalise any employee because they have lost or refused union membership, or for any reason related to trade union status.  8. terminate employment contracts only by (a) expiry of the contract period, (b) death of the employee, or (c) proper legal notice under Section 11 of the Labour Act or other lawful termination methods.  9. recognise and process any valid legal claims from the personal representatives or dependants of a deceased employee, including outstanding salary, benefits, and entitlements.
conduct_risk.riskDescription: Illegality can void contracts and invite sanctions.
conduct_risk.primaryControl: Use legally vetted contract templates.
conduct_risk.additionalControl: Annual legal review of templates.

conduct_risk.title: Transfer to other employment
conduct_risk.description: (1) The transfer of any contract from one employer to another shall be subject to the   consent of the worker and the endorsement of the transfer upon the contract by an au‐   thorised labour officer.   (2) Before endorsing the transfer upon the contract, the officer in question‐   (a)    shall ascertain that the worker has freely consented to the transfer and that his consent has not been obtained by coercion or undue influence or as a result of  misrepresentation or mistake; and   (b)     if by the transfer the worker will‐      (i)   change his form of employment from one which is the subject of an  exemption order made under section 8 (2) of this Act; or      (ii)   be subject to such a change of conditions as in the officer's opinion  renders such a course advisable,  may require the worker to be medically examined or re‐examined, as the case may be.
conduct_risk.plain: The Bank shall : 1. Not transfer an employee's contract to another employer (e.g. outsourced service provider, merger partner, etc.) without the employee’s written consent and endorsement of the transfer by an authorised labour officer.  2. Before facilitating any transfer, the Bank shall ensure the employee’s consent is obtained freely and not through coercion, misrepresentation, or undue influence.  3. Comply with any requirement by a labour officer for the employee to undergo a medical examination or re-examination.
conduct_risk.riskDescription: Transfers without proper process can be invalid.
conduct_risk.primaryControl: Consent and endorsement recorded; liaise with labour officer.
conduct_risk.additionalControl: Maintain a central register of transfers.

conduct_risk.source: Nigeria Labour Act (Cap L1, Laws of the Federation of Nigeria) (2004)
conduct_risk.title: Termination of contracts by notice
conduct_risk.description: (1) Either party to a contract of employment may terminate the contract on the expiration of notice given by him to the other party of his intention to do so.   (2) The notice to be given for the purposes of subsection (1) of this section shall be‐   (a)           one day, where the contract has continued for a period of three months or less;   (b)          one week, where the contract had continued for more than three months but  less than two years (c)                  two weeks, where the contract has continued for a period of two years but less  than five years; and (d)                  one month, where the contract had continued for five years or more. (3) Any notice for a period of one week or more shall be in writing.   (4) The periods of notice specified in subsection (2) of this section exclude the day  on which notice is given.   (5) Nothing in this section affects any right of either party to a contract to treat the contract as terminable without notice by reason of such conduct by the other party as  would have enabled him so to treat it before the making of this Act. (6) Nothing in this section shall prevent either party to a contract from waiving his  right to notice on any occasion, or from accepting a payment in lieu of notice.   (7) All wages payable in money shall be paid on or before the expiry of any period of  notice.   (8) If an employer gives notice to terminate the contract of employment of a worker  who has been continuously employed for three months or more, the employer shall not be  liable under this section to make any payment in respect of a period during which the  worker is absent from work with the leave of the employer granted at the request of the  worker.   (9) In the calculation of a payment in lieu of notice, only that part of the wages which  a worker receives in money, exclusive of overtime and other allowances, shall be taken  into account.
conduct_risk.plain: The Bank shall:  1. Allow either the Bank or the employee to terminate the employment contract upon the expiration of a valid notice period.  2. Provide the following minimum notice periods based on the length of the employee’s continuous service:  a) 1 day – if employed for 3 months or less; b) 1 week – if employed for more than 3 months but less than 2 years; c) 2 weeks – if employed for 2 years but less than 5 years; d) 1 month – if employed for 5 years or more.  3. Ensure that any notice lasting 1 week or more is given in writing.  4. Exclude the day the notice is given when calculating the notice period.  5. Reserve the right to terminate an employment contract without notice if the employee commits a serious breach of conduct justifying such action.  6. Recognise that either the Bank or the employee may:  a) Waive their right to notice, or b) Accept payment in lieu of notice.  7. Pay all due wages in money on or before the expiration of any notice period.  8. Not be liable to pay wages for any period of leave granted to the employee (upon the employee’s request) that falls within the notice period, if the Bank initiated the termination.  9. In calculating any payment in lieu of notice, use only the part of the wages paid in money, excluding overtime or other allowances.
conduct_risk.riskDescription: Legal risk from wrongful termination or contract disputes.
conduct_risk.primaryControl: HR-reviewed termination templates and exit checklist.
conduct_risk.additionalControl: Training for line managers on termination rules.

conduct_risk.source: Nigeria Labour Act (Cap L1, Laws of the Federation of Nigeria) (2004)
conduct_risk.title: Common employment not a defence
conduct_risk.description: (1) It shall not be a defence to an employer who is sued in respect of personal injuries caused by the negligence of a person employed by him, that that person was, at the time the injuries were caused, in common employment with the person injured.   (2) Any provisions contained in a contract of service or apprenticeship, or in an agreement collateral thereto (including a contract or agreement entered into before the  commencement of this section) shall be void in so far as it would have the effect of excluding or limiting any liability of the employer in respect of personal injuries caused to  the person employed or apprenticed by the negligence of persons in common employment with him.   (3) For the purposes of this section, the expression "personal injuries" includes any  disease and any impairment of a person's physical or mental condition arising out of his employment, and "injury" and cognate expressions shall be construed accordingly.
conduct_risk.plain: The Bank shall:  1. Not rely on a defence that an injured employee was in common employment with the person who caused the injury, in any case involving personal injury caused by negligence.  2. Avoid including any contractual terms—in employment or apprenticeship agreements—that attempt to exclude or limit the Bank’s liability for personal injuries caused by a co-worker's negligence. Such terms are void and unenforceable.  3. Recognise that “personal injuries” include: a) Physical injuries, b) Work-related diseases, c) Any impairment of the employee’s physical or mental health arising from employment.
conduct_risk.riskDescription: Injury-related liability despite shared employment duties.
conduct_risk.primaryControl: Workplace safety program and liability insurance.
conduct_risk.additionalControl: Routine HSE inspections and staff safety training.

conduct_risk.source: Nigeria Labour Act (Cap L1, Laws of the Federation of Nigeria) (2004)
conduct_risk.title: Hours of work and overtime
conduct_risk.description: 13.    (1) Normal hours of work in any undertaking shall be those fixed‐          (a)           by mutual agreement; or   (b)            by collective bargaining within the organisation or industry concerned; or   (c)     by an industrial wages board (established by or under an enactment providing  for the establishment of such boards) where there is no machinery for collective bargaining.   (2) Hours which a worker is required to work in excess of the normal hours fixed under subsection (1) of this section shall constitute overtime.   (3) Where a worker is at work for six hours or more a day, his work shall be interrupted (to the extent which is necessary, having regard to its character and duration and to working conditions in general) by allowing one or more suitably spaced rest‐intervals of  not less than one hour on the aggregate: Provided that‐   (a)   exceptions may be made to the rule in this subsection where unforeseen circumstances render them necessary; and   (b)   where it is found unavoidable in view of the nature of the work and the working conditions in general, time‐off for a meal at the worksite or in the immediate vicinity may be substituted for the rest‐interval.      (5) Where, by reason of its connection with a mechanical process or as a result of  other circumstances, the work involves continuous strain or is particularly trying in other ways, the worker shall be allowed the requisite number of suitably adjusted and spaced  breaks in the work.   (6) In subsection (5) of this section, "break in the work" means a short intermission  in the work fixed beforehand which is ordered with a view to allowing the worker to detach himself from his work and which is not to be counted as a rest‐interval or time‐off  under subsection (3) of this section.   (7) In every period of seven days a worker shall be entitled to one day of rest which  shall not be less than 24 consecutive hours; if any reduction takes place in the weekly  rest‐period‐   (a)     corresponding time‐off from work shall be allowed as soon as possible (and in  any case not later than fourteen days thereafter); or        (b)              wages at overtime rates shall be paid in lieu thereof.
conduct_risk.plain: The Bank shall:  1. Set normal working hours by mutual agreement, collective bargaining, or by the relevant industrial wages board standards where applicable.  2. Treat any work required beyond the agreed normal working hours as overtime, and apply appropriate compensation policies in line with labour laws.  3. Ensure that employees working six hours or more per day are granted one or more rest intervals totaling at least one hour, except in special or unforeseen circumstances.  4. Provide short, spaced work breaks (not to be counted as lunch or rest time) where the nature of the job involves continuous mental or physical strain.  5. Provide at least 1 full day of rest every 7 days. If not, equivalent time off or overtime pay must be provided.
conduct_risk.riskDescription: Risk of non-compliance with work hours or inadequate breaks leading to fatigue or legal penalties.
conduct_risk.primaryControl: Standard work schedules, time tracking, and overtime policy.
conduct_risk.additionalControl: Automated time-tracking system audits.

conduct_risk.title: Sick leave
conduct_risk.description: Subject to the Workmen's Compensation Act, a worker shall be entitled to be paid  wages up to twelve working days in anyone calendar year during absence from work  caused by temporary illness certified by a registered medical practitioner:   Provided that this section shall not apply unless‐   (a)     the contract remains in existence during the period of absence and the worker  is ready and willing to perform his part of the contract save for the incapacity  produced by the illness; and   (b)     the worker, if so requested by the employer, consents to be examined by a  qualified medical practitioner nominated by the employer.
conduct_risk.plain: The Bank shall: 1. Pay wages for up to 12 working days per calendar year to an employee who is absent due to temporary illness, provided the illness is certified by a registered medical practitioner.  2. Ensure that: a) The employment contract remains valid during the sick period. b) The employee is willing to work but unable to do so due to illness. c) If requested, the employee agrees to be examined by a qualified medical practitioner nominated by the bank.

conduct_risk.source: Nigeria Labour Act (Cap L1, Laws of the Federation of Nigeria) (2004)
conduct_risk.title: Duty of employer to provide work
conduct_risk.description: 17.  (1) Except where a collective agreement provides otherwise, every employer shall,  unless a worker has broken his contract, provide work suitable to the worker's capacity  on every day (except rest days and public holidays) on which the worker presents himself  and is fit for work; and, if the employer fails to provide work as aforesaid, he shall pay to the worker in respect of each day on which he has so failed wages at the same rate as  would be payable if the worker had performed a day's work:   Provided that‐   (a)     where, owing to a temporary emergency or other circumstances beyond the  employer's control (the period of which shall not exceed one week or such   longer period as an authorised labour officer may allow in any particular case), the employer is unable to provide work, the worker shall be entitled to those   wages only on the first day of the period in question; and   (b)     this subsection shall not apply where the worker is suspended from work as a  punishment for a breach of discipline or any other offence.     (3) Any dispute between an employer and a worker as to the worker's fitness for  work under subsection (1) or (2) of this section may be referred to an authorised labour  officer, who may take such medical or other advice as he thinks appropriate and whose  decision shall be final.
conduct_risk.plain: The Bank shall: 1. Provide suitable work each working day (excluding rest days and public holidays) to any employee who: a) Reports for duty, and b) Is fit for work, unless otherwise stated in a collective agreement or the employee has breached the contract.  2. Pay full daily wages to any eligible employee if the Bank fails to provide work, as if the employee had worked that day.  3. Limit wage liability to only the first day of work non-provision if the failure is due to a temporary emergency or force majeure, lasting no more than one week, unless an authorised labour officer extends that period.  4. Ensure that wages are not due under this provision if the employee is: a) Suspended as punishment for misconduct, or b) Absent without valid justification.  5. Refer disputes about a worker's fitness for work to an authorised labour officer, whose decision shall be final, and may be based on medical or other expert advice.

conduct_risk.title: Annual holidays with pay
conduct_risk.description: 18.  (1) Every worker shall be entitled after twelve months' continuous service to a holi‐  day with full pay of‐   (a)            at least six working days; or   (b)     in the case of a person under the age of sixteen years (including an apprentice),  at least twelve working days.      (3) It shall be unlawful for an employer to pay wages in lieu of the holiday mentioned  in subsection (1) of this section to a worker whose contract has not terminated.   (4) A person who ceases to be employed after having completed‐   (a)     less than twelve but not less than six months in the continuous employment of  an employer; or   (b)     not less than six months in the continuous employment of an employer since  he last qualified for a holiday under subsection (1) of this section,   shall be paid with respect to that period of employment an amount bearing the same proportion to full pay for one week at his normal rate as that period bears to twelve months.
conduct_risk.plain: The Bank shall: 1. Grant annual holiday with full pay to every employee who has completed 12 months of continuous service, as follows: a) At least 6 working days for adult employees. b) At least 12 working days for employees under 16 years of age, including apprentices.  2. Not pay wages in lieu of annual holiday for any employee whose employment has not been terminated. Leave must be actually taken.  3. Upon termination or cessation of employment, pay the affected employee a pro-rated amount of annual holiday pay if: a) The employee has completed at least 6 months but less than 12 months of continuous service, or b) The employee has worked for at least 6 months since they last qualified for annual leave under Section 18(1).

conduct_risk.title: Redundancy
conduct_risk.description: 20.    (1) In the event of redundancy‐   (a)   the employer shall inform the trade union or workers' representative concerned  of the reasons for and the extent of the anticipated redundancy;   (b)   the principle of "last in, first out" shall be adopted in the discharge of the particular category of workers affected, subject to all factors of relative merit, in‐   cluding skill, ability and reliability; and   (c)     the employer shall use his best endeavours to negotiate redundancy payments to any discharged workers who are not protected by regulations made under  subsection (2) of this section.   (3) In this section "redundancy" means an involuntary and permanent loss of employment caused by an excess of manpower
conduct_risk.plain: The Bank shall: 1. Notify the relevant trade union or workers' representative of: a) The reasons for the redundancy, and b) The number of roles or extent of employees to be affected.  2. Apply the "last in, first out" (LIFO) principle when selecting employees for redundancy within the same job category, unless other factors such as: Skill, Ability, or Reliability justify an alternative selection.  3. Use best efforts to negotiate redundancy compensation for affected employees not covered by existing regulations (e.g. staff not under statutory protection or collective bargaining agreements).
conduct_risk.riskDescription: Legal or reputational risk due to victimization of staff.
conduct_risk.primaryControl: Staff grievance and union neutrality policies.
conduct_risk.additionalControl: Training on labour rights and neutrality.

conduct_risk.title: Repatriation
conduct_risk.description: (1) Any recruited worker who‐   (a)   becomes incapacitated by sickness or accident during the journey to the place of employment; or   (b)   is found on medical examination to be unfit for employment; or   (c)   for a reason for which he is not responsible, is not engaged after being recruited; or   (d)   is found by an authorised labour officer to have been recruited by misrepresentation or mistake, shall be repatriated at the expense of the recruiter or employer.   (2) Where the family of a recruited worker accompanies him under section 34 or 44  of this Act, sections 27 (6) and 28 of this Act (and any requirements or directions thereunder) shall apply to the family as nearly as may be; and, if the worker‐   (a) is repatriated under subsection (1) of this section; or   (b) dies during the journey to the place of employment, the family shall be repatriated at the expense of the recruiter or employer.

conduct_risk.source: Nigeria Labour Act (Cap L1, Laws of the Federation of Nigeria) (2004)
conduct_risk.title: Neglect or ill‐treatment
conduct_risk.description: 46.   (1) Any employer who neglects or ill‐treats any worker whom he has contracted to  employ in accordance with this Part of this Act shall be guilty of an offence, and on conviction shall be liable to a fine not exceeding N500 or to imprisonment for a term not exceeding one year, or to both.   (2) Where an employer or his agent is convicted of an offence under subsection (1) of  this section, the convicting court shall report the case to the Minister, who may by notice   in the Federal Gazette cancel any contract into which the employer or his agent may have  entered in accordance with this Part of this Act.   (3) Any cancellation under subsection (2) of this section shall have effect from the date of the publication of the relevant notice.   (4) Every worker whose contract has been cancelled under subsection (2) of this section shall be maintained and conveyed to his place of abode (together with any members  of his family who have accompanied him) at the expense of the Federal Government, and  all sums reasonably expended upon the maintenance and conveyance, together with any   wages due to the worker under the cancelled contract, may be recovered from the employer or his agent by deduction from any deposit or security given under section 24 (7)   of this Act or by civil proceedings.   (5) The cancellation of a contract under this section shall not prevent the taking of legal proceedings in respect of the contract under this or any other enactment.
conduct_risk.plain: The Bank shall ensure that no worker is neglected or ill-treated. Any act of mistreatment is a criminal offence and may result in fines, imprisonment, or contract cancellation. conduct_risk.source: Nigeria Labour Act (Cap L1, Laws of the Federation of Nigeria) (2004)
conduct_risk.title: Maternity protection
conduct_risk.description: 54.  (1) In any public or private industrial or commercial undertaking or in any branch thereof, or in any agricultural undertaking or any branch thereof, a woman‐   (a)     shall have the right to leave her work if she produces a medical certificate given by a registered medical practitioner stating that her confinement will   probably take place within six weeks;   (b)             shall not be permitted to work during the six weeks following her confinement;   (c)   if she is absent from her work in pursuance of paragraph (a) or (b) of this subsection and had been continuously employed by her then employer for a period   of six months or more immediately prior to her absence, shall be paid not less than fifty per cent of the wages she would have earned if she had not been ab‐   sent; and   (d)     shall in any case, if she is nursing her child, be allowed half an hour twice a day during her working hours for that purpose.   (2) Subsection (1) (c) of this section shall have effect notwithstanding any law relating to the fixing and payment of a minimum wage.   (3) No employer shall be liable, in his capacity as an employer, to pay any medical  expenses incurred by a woman during or on account of her pregnancy or confinement.   (4) Where a woman‐   (a)     is absent from her work in pursuance of subsection (1) (a) or (b) of this section; or   (b)     remains absent from her work for a longer period as a result of illness certified  by a registered medical practitioner to arise out of her pregnancy or confinement and to render her unfit for work,then, until her absence has exceeded such a period (if any) as may be prescribed, no em‐   ployer shall give her notice of dismissal during her absence or notice of dismissal expiring during her absence.
conduct_risk.plain: The Bank shall:  1. Allow maternity leave if a female employee presents a medical certificate from a registered medical practitioner indicating that her delivery is expected within six weeks.  2. Prohibit the employee from working during the six weeks immediately following childbirth (mandatory post-natal leave).  3. Pay at least 50% of the employee's wages during the maternity leave (pre- and post-natal), provided she has worked continuously for at least six months prior to the leave.  4. Permit nursing breaks: If the employee is nursing a child, she must be allowed 30 minutes twice daily during working hours for nursing.  5. Not dismiss or give notice of dismissal during her maternity leave or during an extended absence certified as due to post-natal illness by a registered medical practitioner.  6. Not be required to pay medical expenses related to the pregnancy or childbirth (this cost is excluded from employer responsibility under the Act).
conduct_risk.riskDescription: Labour law breaches, employee litigation, and reputational damage.
conduct_risk.primaryControl: Maternity policy aligned with law; salary automation for leave.
conduct_risk.additionalControl: Manager sensitization on employee maternity rights.

conduct_risk.source: Nigeria Labour Act (Cap L1, Laws of the Federation of Nigeria) (2004)
conduct_risk.title: Records
conduct_risk.description: (1) It shall be the duty of every employer to keep such records of wages and conditions of employment as are necessary to show that this Act is being complied with.   (2) Without prejudice to the generality of subsection (1) of this section, every employer shall keep in respect of each of his workers to whom a statement has been given under section 7 of this Act, a record showing‐   (a)       the name and address of the worker;   (b)       his town (or other place) of origin; (c)           the date of his birth;   (d)           the name and address of his next of kin;   (e)           the date and place of his engagement;   (f)            his Nigerian Social Insurance Trust Fund number; and   (g)           the date of cessation of employment.   (3) Records kept pursuant to subsections (1) and (2) of this section shall be retained  for three years after the time to which they refer.   (4) Any employer who‐   (a)     knowingly and with intent to avoid compliance with any provision of this Act,  omits to keep any or any sufficient record of any particular wages or condi‐   tions of employment; or   (b)             fails to comply with subsection (2) or (3) of this section,  shall be guilty of an offence and on conviction shall be liable to a fine not exceeding   N200.
conduct_risk.plain: The Bank shall: 1. Keep accurate and up-to-date records of employee wages and employment conditions to demonstrate compliance with the Labour Act. 2. For each employee, maintain a record that includes: a) Full name and address b) Town or place of origin c) Date of birth d) Name and address of next of kin e) Date and place of engagement (hiring) f) Nigerian Social Insurance Trust Fund (NSITF) number g) Date of cessation of employment (if applicable)  2. Retain all employment records for at least 3 years after the period to which the record relates.  3. Never omit or falsify employment records with the intent of evading any requirement of the Labour Act, as such actions constitute an offence.
conduct_risk.riskDescription: Risk of fines or enforcement actions due to poor recordkeeping.
conduct_risk.primaryControl: Secure HRIS or employee files maintained and archived.
conduct_risk.additionalControl: Internal quarterly checks and offboarding audits.

conduct_risk.source: Compliance with Bank Employees, Etc (Declaration of Assets) Act
conduct_risk.title: Annual Assets Declaration
conduct_risk.description: (1) An employee who has made a declaration in accordance with section 1 of this Act shall, within seven days of the anniversary of the initial declaration and every subsequent year thereafter, make a further full disclosure of all assets acquired or disposed of during the immediately preceding year to which the declaration relates.   (2) The full disclosure required to be made in subsection (1) of this section shall be in the manner prescribed in the Annual Assets Declaration Form contained in Form C of the Schedule to this Act and shall be duly executed and attested to in the manner prescribed in section 2 of this Act.   (3) The Chief Executive of every Bank shall, within seven days of receipt, submit to the appropriate authority all Annual Assets Declaration Forms submitted to him under this section.   (4) The obligation of an employee to make an annual declaration of assets as required in this section shall extend to a period of two years after the determination of his employment with the Bank; and for this purpose, it shall be the duty of the employee to collect the appropriate form from the Chief Executive of his Bank or a person authorised by him in that behalf and to submit the completed form to the Chief Executive within the time stipulated in subsection (1) of this section.   (5) Notwithstanding the circumstances of the determination of the employment of an employee affected by this Act, the Chief Executive shall, whenever requested by a former employee, promptly deliver to the former employee concerned the stipulated form to enable him to comply with the provisions of this section.
conduct_risk.plain: The Bank shall:  1. Ensure every employee who has previously submitted a Declaration of Assets Form submits an annual update within 7 days of the anniversary of the initial declaration, disclosing any assets acquired or disposed of in the past year.  2. Ensure the declaration is made using Form C (Annual Assets Declaration Form) and that it is properly executed and attested as required by law.  3. Ensure the Chief Executive submits all Annual Assets Declarations received to the appropriate authority within 7 days of receipt.  4. Ensure that employees continue to make annual asset declarations for two years after leaving the Bank, and that the Bank provides them the required forms upon request.  5. Ensure the Chief Executive (or authorized person) promptly provides the declaration form to any former employee who requests it, regardless of how their employment ended.

conduct_risk.source: Revised Guidelines for Blacklisting for Banks and OFIs in Nigeria
conduct_risk.title: Blacklisting by FIs
conduct_risk.description: In order to ensure fairness and accountability, FIs shall adhere to the following procedure before the decision to blacklist an individual: i. Where an alleged offence as outlined in this Guidelines is discovered/reported/made against an individual, an investigation shall be conducted by the FI to determine the veracity of the allegations. ii. Upon verification of the existence of grounds for blacklisting, the FI shall notify the affected individual in writing, of the allegations timeously and he/she shall be required to respond to the allegations within 14 days from the receipt of the notification. iii. Upon receipt of the individual’s response, a Disciplinary Committee (DC) shall be setup to review the matter. iv. The individual shall be invited by the DC to present evidence that may aid in his/her defense. This invitation shall be received within 14 days prior to the sitting of the committee. v. Where an individual fails to appear before the DC after invitation, without any written notice stating the reasons for not appearing, the DC shall proceed with the process. However, where the individual has justifiable reasons for not appearing, the DC shall extend the invitation for a reasonable period that may allow the  individual to appear. vi. Based on the evidence presented during the hearing, the DC shall make a decision regarding the individual. vii. If the individual is indicted, the case shall be referred to an IRP for further review and validation. ix. The decision(s) of the DC and the IRP shall be communicated to the individual involved. xi. The above procedure shall also apply to individuals who have resigned prior to discovery of an eligible offence.
conduct_risk.plain: The Bank shall ensure that the following fair and accountable procedures are followed before blacklisting any individual: 1.  Conduct an internal investigation when any blacklisting-related offence is discovered, reported, or alleged.  2. Notify the Individual a) If grounds for blacklisting are found, issue a written notice to the individual with details of the allegation. b) Allow the individual 14 days from receipt of the notice to respond.  3. Form a Disciplinary Committee to review the case upon receiving the individual's response.  4. Invite the individual to a hearing and allow them to present relevant evidence in their defense and ensure the invitation is received at least 14 days before the hearing date.  5. Proceed If No Response a) If the individual fails to appear without a valid written explanation, the DC may proceed with the review. b) If there is a justified reason for non-appearance, allow additional time for them to appear.  6. The DC must make a decision based on the evidence presented during the hearing.  7. If the individual is found culpable, refer the case to the IRP for a second-level review and validation.  8. Communicate the final decisions of the DC and IRP to the individual involved.  9. This procedure also applies to individuals who have already resigned before the offence was discovered.
conduct_risk.deadlineType: Within 14 days of notification; IRP review after DC decision
conduct_risk.riskDescription: Risk of blacklisting without due process, which could lead to legal claims, reputational damage, and regulatory sanctions.
conduct_risk.responsibility: Compliance Officer; Head HR; Company Secretary
conduct_risk.primaryControl: Documented investigation procedures; written communication templates; hearing calendar; IRP structure in place
conduct_risk.additionalControl: Use compliance checklist before blacklisting; maintain audit trail for all actions taken; training for DC and HR teams

conduct_risk.source: De-marketing of Banks by Other Banks
conduct_risk.title: Circular
conduct_risk.description: It will be recalled that the CBN had earlier issued a circular reference BSD/08/2006 on the above subject titled “The Unethical and Unprofessional Practice of De-Marketing Colleagues/Other Banks in the Industry by Spreading False Rumours”, dated April 12, 2006. The CBN has again noted with serious concern the recent practice whereby some officers of deposit money banks engage in the de-marketing of other banks through disparaging comments and the use of negative text messages.  This development, which constitutes a threat to the safety and soundness of the banking system, is unprofessional, unethical and unacceptable. Banks and their staff are by this circular reminded that the responsibility for ensuring the safety and soundness of the banking system is a collective one for all stakeholders.  Banks are therefore advised to caution their staff on this practice as henceforth, any staff of a bank found to be involved in such an act will be summarily dismissed and blacklisted. Also, if another staff of the same bank is involved in such a practice, the institution will face severe sanctions including but not limited to a monetary fine of ₦10 million (Ten Million Naira only). Appropriate channel will be opened by the CBN for the report of such unwholesome practice by banks’ customers and the general public.  Furthermore, in the overall interest of the banking system, all banks are advised to enthrone an appropriate corporate culture that would guide against such practices in the future.
conduct_risk.plain: The Bank shall:  1. Prohibit staff from making disparaging, false, or negative comments or messages about other banks, whether verbally, in writing, or via text.  2. Educate and warn employees that any staff caught engaging in de-marketing will be summarily dismissed and blacklisted.  3. Ensure that if more than one staff member is found guilty of de-marketing, the Bank may be subject to severe sanctions, including a ₦10 million fine.  4. Promote a corporate culture of professionalism and mutual respect within the banking industry to maintain system-wide confidence and ethical conduct.  5. Cooperate with the CBN by using the designated channels for reporting any de-marketing practices by competitors or customers.
conduct_risk.riskDescription: Reputational harm and regulatory sanction from unethical employee conduct
conduct_risk.primaryControl: Code of conduct policy, employee declarations, ethics training
conduct_risk.additionalControl: Whistleblower channel and disciplinary matrix

conduct_risk.source: Re: The Need for the CBN Prior Clearance of Prospective Employees of Banks
conduct_risk.title: Circular
conduct_risk.description: Following representations made by banks during the CBN/Banks' Human Resources forum held in December 2013 regarding difficulties in the strict implementation of the above circular, the Management of the CBN hereby approves the following amendments:  i. New employees of banks and discount houses may assume duty prior to obtaining the approval of the CBN, if this proves difficult or impractical. ii. However, for employees that assume duty without CBN's prior approval, banks and discount houses shall, within 30 days of their assumption of duty, submit their curriculum vitae and other relevant information on the new employees to the CBN for clearance. iii. Banks and discount houses shall include as part of the terms of employment (OFFER LETTER) that "the offer is subject to the receipt of satisfactory responses on any background checks or other inquiries on the employee from relevant authorities". iv. The above amendments shall NOT apply to new employees on the grade of Assistant General Manager and above. Banks are required to continue to obtain the prior written approval of the CBN before resumption of duty for these categories of staff.
conduct_risk.plain: The Bank shall ensure that:  1. New employees may resume work before CBN approval only if prior clearance is impractical or difficult. 2. Within 30 days of the employee’s assumption of duty, the bank must submit the individual’s CV and other relevant documents to the CBN for background clearance. 3. The employment offer letter must state clearly that the appointment is subject to satisfactory background checks or inquiries from relevant authorities. 4. For new hires at Assistant General Manager (AGM) level and above, the bank must obtain prior written CBN approval before the employee is allowed to assume duty.
conduct_risk.riskDescription: Regulatory breach if bank fails to get timely clearance or miscommunicates offer terms
conduct_risk.primaryControl: Onboarding checklist, standard contract template, HRIS alerts
conduct_risk.additionalControl: Internal audit spot checks, escalation protocol for executive hires

conduct_risk.source: Immigration Act
conduct_risk.title: Employment of immigrants.
conduct_risk.description: (1) Where any person in Nigeria is desirous of employing a person who is a national  of any other country he shall, unless exempted under this section, make application to the   Director of Immigration in such manner as may be prescribed and shall give such information as to the provision to be made for repatriation of that national and his dependants   as the Director of Immigration may reasonably require; and no such person shall be employed without the permission of the Director of Immigration given on such terms as he  thinks fit; the provisions of this section shall extend and apply to persons in employment immediately before, as well as to those employed or to be employed at any time after, the commencement of this Act.   (2) The Director of Immigration shall record the information in such form as he thinks necessary; and where he is so satisfied, the Director of Immigration may require provision to be made for repatriation either generally as to all persons so employed by a person in Nigeria and their dependants or with reference to any particular person, by payment into the Consolidated Revenue Fund by way of deposit of such amount as the Minister may prescribe for the repatriation, or by a bond in such form as the Director of Immigration may approve for such purpose.   (3) The Minister may, by notice, exempt any person from the requirements of this section on such conditions as he thinks fit, and subject thereto any person to whom this section applies who is employed in Nigeria, shall on ceasing for any reason to be so employed be deemed to be a prohibited immigrant as from the date of his entry into Nigeria;  and the person who employed him shall be liable to pay all costs of and incidental to deportation of the prohibited immigrant and of his dependants.
conduct_risk.plain: The Bank shall:  1. Not employ any foreign national without first obtaining written approval from the Director of Immigration. 2. Provide necessary information and arrangements for the repatriation of the foreign employee and their dependants (such as a bond, deposit, or other assurance), if required by the Director of Immigration. 3. Cover all deportation-related costs if the foreign employee ceases employment and becomes a prohibited immigrant — unless an exemption has been granted. 4. Ensure that foreign nationals already in employment at the time the Act took effect are also compliant — including fulfilling any retroactive approval or repatriation requirements.
conduct_risk.riskDescription: Financial liability for repatriation and deportation; immigration sanctions for non-compliance
conduct_risk.primaryControl: Pre-employment immigration due diligence; include repatriation clauses in contracts
conduct_risk.additionalControl: Regular audit of all foreign staff immigration status and compliance filings

conduct_risk.title: Significant Influence Functions
conduct_risk.description: i) These include entity significant influence roles such as Chairman, Managing Director, Deputy Managing Director, Executive Directors, Non-executive Directors, Independent Directors,  ii) These include the Audit and Compliance functions. Iii) These include Finance, Risk, Internal Audit and Information Technology functions iv) These include key management functions such as company secretariat, investment business, financial resources functions, Settlement and other key business operations functions. v) This is applicable where a financial institution is a subsidiary and there are directors or employees of the parent company whose decisions or actions significantly impact the decisions of the board and management of the financial institution. vi) These are investors with shareholding of 5% or more in the financial institution
conduct_risk.plain: The Bank shall: Identify and classify the following as “Significant Influence Functions” due to their impact on the institution’s operations and governance:  a) Chairman, Managing Director, Deputy Managing Director, Executive Directors, Non-Executive Directors, and Independent Directors b) Heads or officers responsible for Audit and Compliance c) Personnel in Finance, Risk Management, Internal Audit, and Information Technology functions d) Key managers such as the Company Secretary, those in charge of investment, financial resources, settlements, or other core business operations e) Parent company directors or employees whose decisions significantly influence the bank (if the bank is a subsidiary) f) nvestors holding 5% or more of the bank’s shares
conduct_risk.riskDescription: Unfit individuals in SIF roles may cause regulatory violations and reputational damage.
conduct_risk.primaryControl: Role-mapping process; SIF registry; board approval
conduct_risk.additionalControl: Regular review of SIF list; regulatory screening
