data_protection.title: Lawful Processing
data_protection.description: Without prejudice to the principles set out in this Regulation, processing shall be lawful if at least one of the following applies:  a) the Data Subject has given consent to the processing of his or her Personal Data for one or more specific purposes;  b) processing is necessary for the performance of a contract to which the Data Subject is party or in order to take steps at the request of the Data Subject prior to entering into a contract;  c) processing is necessary for compliance with a legal obligation to which the Controller is subject;  d) processing is necessary in order to protect the vital interests of the Data Subject or of another natural person, and  e) processing is necessary for the performance of a task carried out in the public interest or in exercise of official public mandate vested in the controller;
data_protection.plain: The Bank shall ensure that personal data is processed lawfully and only when at least one of the following legal bases applies:  a) The data subject has given clear consent for one or more specific purposes.  b) The processing is necessary to perform or enter into a contract with the data subject.  c) The processing is required to meet a legal obligation.  d) The processing is necessary to protect the vital interests of the data subject or another person.  e) The processing is required to carry out a task in the public interest or under a lawful public mandate.
data_protection.riskDescription: Unlawful processing exposes the bank to NITDA sanctions and lawsuits.
data_protection.primaryControl: Consent documentation, legal basis checklist, automated legal basis tagging
data_protection.additionalControl: DPO review of new processing activities

data_protection.title: Procuring Consent
data_protection.description: (1) No data shall be obtained except the specific purpose of collection is made known to the Data Subject;  (2) Data Controller is under obligation to ensure that consent of a Data Subject has been obtained without fraud, coercion or undue influence; accordingly:  a) where processing is based on consent, the Controller shall be able to demonstrate that the Data Subject has consented to processing of his or her Personal Data and the legal capacity to give consent;  b) if the Data Subject's consent is given in the context of a written declaration which also concerns other matters, the request for consent shall be presented in a manner which is clearly distinguishable from the other matters, in an intelligible and easily accessible form, using clear and plain language. Any part of such a declaration which constitutes an infringement of this Regulation shall not be binding on the Data Subject;  c) prior to giving consent, the Data Subject shall be informed of his right and method to withdraw his consent at any given time. However, the withdrawal of consent shall not affect the lawfulness of processing based on consent before its withdrawal;  d) when assessing whether consent is freely given, utmost account shall be taken of whether the performance of a contract, including the provision of a service, is conditional on consent to the processing of Personal Data that is not necessary (or excessive) for the performance of that contract; and  e) where data may be transferred to a third party for any reason whatsoever
data_protection.plain: The Bank shall:  a) Ensure that no Personal Data is collected unless the purpose of collection is clearly communicated to the Data Subject. b) Obtain the Data Subject’s consent without fraud, coercion, or undue influence, and be able to prove that valid consent was given. Consent must be presented separately from unrelated terms, using clear and plain language. c) Inform Data Subjects of their right to withdraw consent at any time and how to do so. Consent must not be required for processing that is unnecessary for a contract. If data will be transferred to third parties, the Bank must obtain specific consent for such transfers.
data_protection.riskDescription: Invalid or coerced consent can nullify processing legality and attract regulatory sanctions.
data_protection.primaryControl: Standardized consent forms, withdrawal mechanisms
data_protection.additionalControl: UX testing for clarity, multilingual support

data_protection.title: Due Diligence and Prohibition of Improper Motives
data_protection.description: (a) No consent shall be sought, given or accepted in any circumstance that may engender direct or indirect propagation of atrocities, hate, child rights violation, criminal acts and anti-social conducts;  (b) A party to any data processing contract, other than an individual Data Subject, shall take reasonable measures to ensure the other party does not have a record of violating the principles set out in Part 3 and he is accountable to NITDA or a regulatory authority for data protection within or outside Nigeria; accordingly, every Data Processor or Controller shall be liable for the actions or inactions of third parties who handle the Personal Data of Data Subjects under this Regulation;  (c) In this Part, "a party" shall include directors, shareholders, servants and privies of the contracting party; and record shall include report of public records and reports in credible news media. Accordingly, the distinction between legal and natural persons for the purpose of limiting due diligence is irrelevant.
data_protection.plain: The Bank shall:  a) Not seek, give, or accept consent for Personal Data processing in any situation that may promote atrocities, hate, child rights violations, criminal acts, or anti-social behavior.  b) Conduct due diligence before entering any data processing contract to ensure that the other party has no record of violating data protection principles. The Bank remains responsible and accountable to NITDA or any relevant data protection authority for the actions or omissions of third parties handling Personal Data on its behalf.  c) Ensure due diligence covers both individuals and organizations, including directors, shareholders, employees, and affiliates of the contracting party, and must include checks on public records and credible news media sources.
data_protection.riskDescription: Association with non-compliant vendors can result in indirect violations.
data_protection.primaryControl: Vendor due diligence checklist, DPAs, blacklisting policy
data_protection.additionalControl: Ongoing vendor audits and certifications

data_protection.title: Privacy Policy
data_protection.description: Notwithstanding anything contrary in this Regulation or any instrument for the time being in force, any medium through which Personal Data is being collected or processed shall display a simple and conspicuous privacy policy that the class of Data Subject being targeted can understand. The privacy policy shall in addition to any other relevant information contain the following:  a) what constitutes the Data Subject's consent;  b) description of collectable personal information;  c) purpose of collection of Personal Data;  d) technical methods used to collect and store personal information, cookies, JWT, web tokens etc.;  e) access (if any) of third parties to Personal Data and purpose of access;  f) a highlight of the principles stated in Part 2;  g) available remedies in the event of violation of the privacy policy;  h) the time frame for remedy; and  i) provided that no limitation clause shall avail any Data Controller who acts in breach of the principles set out in this Regulation.
data_protection.plain: The Bank shall:  Ensure that any platform or medium used to collect or process Personal Data (e.g., websites, apps, forms) displays a simple, clear, and easily visible Privacy Policy that is understandable to the target audience.  The Privacy Policy must include:  a) A clear explanation of what constitutes the Data Subject’s consent.  b) A description of the types of personal data collected.  c) The purposes for collecting Personal Data.  d) The technical methods used for data collection and storage (e.g., cookies, JWT, web tokens).  e) Whether any third parties will have access to the data, and the reasons for such access.  f) A summary of the data protection principles under NDPR Part 2.  g) The remedies available to Data Subjects if their privacy rights are violated.  h) The timeframe within which remedies will be provided.  i) A reminder that no limitation clause will protect a Data Controller that violates NDPR principles.
data_protection.riskDescription: Opaque or missing privacy policies breach transparency obligations and reduce customer trust.
data_protection.primaryControl: Published privacy policy, multilingual display, policy version control
data_protection.additionalControl: Annual policy review, customer feedback loop

data_protection.title: Data Security
data_protection.description: Anyone involved in data processing or the control of data shall develop security measures to protect data; such measures include but not limited to protecting systems from hackers, setting up firewalls, storing data securely with access to specific authorized individuals, employing data encryption technologies, developing organizational policy for handling Personal Data (and other sensitive or confidential data), protection of emailing systems and continuous capacity building for staff.
data_protection.plain: The Bank shall:  a) Develop and implement security measures to protect Personal Data. These must include, at a minimum: b) Protecting systems from hackers, c) Setting up firewalls, d) Storing data securely with access limited to authorized individuals, e) Using data encryption technologies, f) Establishing organizational policies for handling Personal and other sensitive or confidential data, g) Securing email systems, and h) Providing continuous capacity building and training for staff.

data_protection.title: Third-Party Processing
data_protection.description: Data processing by a third party shall be governed by a written contract between the third party and the Data Controller. Accordingly, any person engaging a third party to process the data obtained from Data Subjects shall ensure adherence to this Regulation.
data_protection.plain: The Bank shall ensure that any third party engaged to process Personal Data does so under a written contract, and that the third party complies fully with the NDPR. The Bank remains responsible for ensuring the third party adheres to all data protection requirements.

data_protection.title: Objections by the Data Subject
data_protection.description: The right of a Data Subject to object to the processing of his data shall always be safeguarded. Accordingly, a Data Subject shall have the option to:  a) object to the processing of Personal Data relating to him which the Data Controller intend to process for the purpose of marketing;  b) be expressly and manifestly offered the mechanism for objection to any form of data processing free of charge.
data_protection.plain: The Bank shall: a) Respect the Data Subject’s right to object to the processing of their Personal Data, especially for marketing purposes. b) Provide a clear and accessible way for Data Subjects to object to any form of data processing, at no cost to them.
data_protection.riskDescription: Failure to honor objections may lead to reputational risk and penalties
data_protection.primaryControl: Opt-out options in all communications
data_protection.additionalControl: Automate opt-out mechanism and monitor compliance

data_protection.description: Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Regulation, the privacy right of a Data Subject shall be interpreted for the purpose of advancing and never for the purpose of restricting the safeguards Data Subject is entitled to under any data protection instrument made in furtherance of fundamental rights and the Nigerian laws.
data_protection.plain: The Bank shall ensure that the Data Subject’s right to privacy is always interpreted in a way that enhances—not restricts—the protections they are entitled to under Nigerian data protection laws and fundamental rights.
data_protection.riskDescription: Restrictive interpretation could lead to legal action or sanctions

data_protection.title: Rights of Data Subjects
data_protection.description: (1) The Controller shall take appropriate measures to provide any information relating to processing to the Data Subject in a concise, transparent, intelligible and easily accessible form, using clear and plain language, and for any information relating to a child. The information shall be provided in writing, or by other means, including, where appropriate, by electronic means. When requested by the Data Subject, the information may be provided orally, provided that the identity of the Data Subject is proven by other means. (2) If the Controller does not act on the request of the Data Subject, the Controller shall inform the Data Subject without delay and at the latest within one month of receipt of the request of the reasons for not taking action and on the possibility of lodging a complaint with a supervisory authority. (3) Except as otherwise provided by any public policy or Regulation, information provided to the Data Subject and any communication and any actions taken shall be provided free of charge. Where requests from a Data Subject are manifestly unfounded or excessive, in particular because of their repetitive character, the controller may either: a) Charge a reasonable fee considering the administrative costs of providing the information or communication or taking the action requested; or, . (4) The Controller shall bear the burden of demonstrating the manifestly unfounded or excessive character of the request. (5) Where the Controller has reasonable doubts concerning the identity of the natural person making the request for information, the Controller may request the provision of additional information necessary to confirm the identity of the Data Subject. (6) The information to be provided to Data Subject may be provided in combination with standardized icons in order to give in an easily visible, intelligible and clearly legible manner a meaningful overview of the intended processing. Where the icons are presented electronically, they shall be machine-readable.
data_protection.plain: The Bank shall: 1. Provide all information about personal data processing to the Data Subject in clear, plain, and accessible language, including for children, and through writing, electronic means, or orally (where identity is verified). 2.  Inform the Data Subject within one month if it chooses not to act on a request, and explain the reason and how to lodge a complaint. 3. Provide information and actions to the Data Subject free of charge, unless requests are clearly unfounded or excessive. 4. Charge a reasonable fee only if requests are repetitive or excessive. 5. Inform the Data Subject and copy the NDPC when it refuses to act on such requests. 6. Be able to prove that the request was unfounded or excessive. 7. Verify the identity of the person making the request and may request additional information to confirm identity. 8.  Use standardized, easily understood icons (machine-readable if electronic) to convey processing information.

data_protection.title: Rights of Data Subjects
data_protection.description: (7) Prior to collecting Personal Data from a Data Subject, the Controller shall provide the Data Subject with all the following information: a) the identity and the contact details of the Controller; b) the contact details of the Data Protection Officer; c) the purpose(s) of the processing for which the Personal Data are intended as well as the legal basis for the processing; d) the legitimate interests pursued by the Controller or by a third party; e) the recipients or categories of recipients of the Personal Data, if any; f) where applicable, the fact that the Controller intends to transfer Personal Data to a third country or international organization and the existence or absence of an adequacy decision by The Agency; g) the period for which the Personal Data will be stored, or if that is not possible, the criteria used to determine that period; h) the existence of the right to request from the Controller access to and rectification or erasure of Personal Data or restriction of processing concerning the Data Subject or to object to processing as well as the right to Data Portability; i) the existence of the right to withdraw consent at any time, without affecting the lawfulness of processing based on consent before its withdrawal; j) the right to lodge a complaint with a relevant authority; k) whether the provision of Personal Data is a statutory or contractual requirement, or a requirement necessary to enter into a contract, as well as whether the Data Subject is obliged to provide the Personal Data and of the possible consequences of failure to provide such data; l) the existence of automated decision-making, including profiling and, at least, in those cases, meaningful information about the logic involved, as well as the significance and the envisaged consequences of such processing for the Data Subject; m) Where the Controller intends to further process the Personal Data for a purpose other than that for which the Personal Data were collected, the controller shall provide the Data Subject prior to that further processing with information on that other purpose, and with any relevant further information; and n) Where applicable, that the Controller intends to transfer Personal Data to a recipient in a foreign country or international organization and the existence or absence of an adequacy decision by The Agency.
data_protection.plain: The Bank shall :  1. Disclose its name and contact details.  2. Share the contact details of its Data Protection Officer (DPO).  3. Explain the purpose(s) and legal basis for processing the data.  4. Explain any legitimate interest it or others are pursuing.  5. State the recipients or types of recipients of the personal data.  6. Tell the customer if it intends to send data to another country or international organization and whether this location has been approved by the regulator (NDPC).  7. Specify the data retention period or explain how it determines this.  8. Inform the customer of their right to:  a) Access their data b) Correct or erase it c) Restrict processing d) Object to processing e) Request data portability  9. Inform the customer that they can withdraw consent at any time.  10. Inform the customer of their right to lodge a complaint with the relevant data protection authority.  11. Explain whether providing personal data is a legal or contract requirement, and the consequences if the customer refuses.  12. Use automated decision-making (like credit scoring), it must explain:  a) How the system works b) The impact on the customer  13. To use the customer’s data for a new reason later, it must inform the customer before doing so.  14. Reiterate plans to transfer data outside Nigeria and whether the destination is approved by the NDPC.

data_protection.title: Rights of Data Subjects
data_protection.description: (8) Where Personal Data are transferred to a foreign country or to an international organization, the Data Subject shall have the right to be informed of the appropriate safeguards for data protection in the foreign country. The Data Subject shall have the right to obtain from the Controller without undue delay the rectification of inaccurate Personal Data concerning him or her. Considering the purposes of the processing, the Data Subject shall have the right to have incomplete Personal Data completed, including by means of providing a supplementary statement.
data_protection.plain: The Bank shall: 1. Inform customers if their personal data is transferred to a foreign country or international organization, and clearly explain the data protection safeguards that are in place in that destination.  2. Allow customers to correct inaccurate personal data about them without undue delay upon request.  3. Allow customers to complete any incomplete data, including by providing a supplementary statement, where necessary based on the reason the data is being used.
data_protection.riskDescription: Data subjects unaware of international risks or denied their rights.

data_protection.title: Rights of Data Subjects
data_protection.description: (9) The Data Subject shall have the right to request the Controller to delete Personal Data without delay, and the Controller shall delete Personal Data where one of the following grounds applies: a) the Personal Data are no longer necessary in relation to the purposes for which they were collected or processed; b) the Data Subject withdraws consent on which the processing is based; c) the Data Subject objects to the processing and there are no overriding legitimate grounds for the processing; d) the Personal Data have been unlawfully processed; and e) the Personal Data must be erased for compliance with a legal obligation in Nigeria. (10) The Controller who has made the Personal Data public and is obliged to delete the Personal Data shall, take all reasonable steps, to inform Controllers processing the Personal Data of the Data Subject’s request.
data_protection.plain: The Bank shall: 1. Delete a customer’s personal data without delay if any of the following apply:  a) The data is no longer needed for the purpose it was collected. b) The customer withdraws their consent for the data to be used. c) The customer objects to the processing and the bank has no overriding legal reason to continue. d) The data was unlawfully processed. e) The data must be erased to comply with Nigerian law.  2. If the Bank has shared the personal data publicly and is later required to delete it, it must take all reasonable steps to notify any other organizations that may also be processing that data of the customer’s deletion request.

data_protection.description: (11) The Data Subject shall have the right to obtain from the Controller restriction of processing where one of the following applies: a) The accuracy of the Personal Data is contested by the Data Subject for a period enabling the Controller to verify the accuracy of the Personal Data; b) The processing is unlawful, and the Data Subject opposes the erasure of the Personal Data and requests the restriction of their use instead; c) The Controller no longer needs the Personal Data for the purposes of the processing, but they are required by the Data Subject for the establishment, exercise or defence of legal claims; and d) The Data Subject has objected to processing pending the verification whether the legitimate grounds of the Controller override those of the Data Subject. (12) Where processing has been restricted such Personal Data shall, except for storage, only be processed with the Data Subject's consent or for the establishment, exercise or defence of legal claims or for the protection of the rights of another natural or legal person or for reasons of important public interest in Nigeria.
data_protection.plain: The Bank shall: 1. Restrict the use of a customer’s personal data if any of these apply:  a) The customer challenges the accuracy of the data, and the Bank is verifying it. b) The data was processed unlawfully, but the customer chooses restriction over deletion. c) The Bank no longer needs the data, but the customer requires it for a legal claim. d) The customer has objected to processing, and the Bank is checking whether it has stronger legal grounds to continue.  2. When processing is restricted, the Bank must not use the data for any other purpose except:  a) With the customer’s consent, b) For a legal claim, c) To protect someone else’s rights, or d) For important public interest reasons in Nigeria.

data_protection.title: Rights of Data Subjects
data_protection.description: (14) The Data Subject shall have the right to receive the Personal Data concerning him or her, which he or she has provided to a controller, in a structured, commonly used and machine-readable format, and have the right to transmit those data to another controller without hindrance from the controller to which the Personal Data have been provided, where: (a) The processing is based on consent, or (b) On a contract, and (c) The processing is carried out by automated means. (15) In exercising his right to Data Portability, the Data Subject shall have the right to have the Personal Data transmitted directly from one controller to another, where technically feasible. Provided that this right shall not apply to processing necessary for the performance of a task carried out in the public interest or in the exercise of official authority vested in the Controller.
data_protection.plain: The Bank shall: 1. Allow customers to access and download the personal data they provided to the Bank in a structured, commonly used, and machine-readable format.  2. Allow customers to move their personal data to another organization (data portability), without blocking or delaying the transfer.  This right applies only if:  a) The processing is based on the customer’s consent or a contract, and b) The processing is done by automated systems.  3. If technically possible, the Bank must transfer the data directly to another organization on the customer’s request.  4. This obligation does not apply if the data is being processed for tasks:  a) Performed in the public interest, or b) That involve official authority granted to the Bank by law or regulation.

data_protection.title: Implementation Mechanisms
data_protection.description: (1) All public and private organizations in Nigeria that control data of natural persons shall, within three (3) months after the date of the issuance of this Regulation, make available to the general public their respective data protection Policies; these Policies shall be inconformity with this Regulation. (2) Every Data Controller shall designate a Data Protection Officer for the purpose of ensuring adherence to this Regulation, relevant data privacy instruments and data protection directives of the Data Controller; provided that a Data Controller may outsource data protection to a verifiably competent firm or person. (3) A Data Controller or Processor shall ensure continuous capacity building for Data Protection Officers and the generality of her personnel involved in any form of data processing.  (5) Within six (6) months after the date of issuance of this Regulations, each organization shall conduct a detailed audit of its privacy and data protection practices with at least each audit stating: a. personally identifiable information the organization collects on employees of the organization and members of the public; b. any purpose for which the personally identifiable information is collected; c. any notice given to individuals regarding the collection and use of personal information relating to that individual; d. any access given to individuals to review, amend, correct, supplement, or delete personal information relating to that individual; e. whether or not consent is obtained from an individual before personally identifiable information is collected, used, transferred, or disclosed and any method used to obtain consent; f. the policies and practices of the organization for the security of personally identifiable information; g. the policies and practices of the organization for the proper use of personally identifiable information; h. organization policies and procedures for privacy and data protection; i. the policies and procedures of the organization for monitoring and reporting violations of privacy and data protection policies; and j. the policies and procedures of the organization for assessing the impact of technologies on the stated privacy and security policies.
data_protection.plain: The Bank shall:  1. Publish its data protection policy and make it available to the public within 3 months of this Regulation’s issuance. The policy must comply fully with the Regulation.  2. Appoint a qualified Data Protection Officer (DPO) responsible for ensuring compliance with data privacy laws. The Bank may outsource this role to a competent person or firm if necessary.  3. Provide continuous training for the DPO and all staff involved in processing personal data to maintain their knowledge and skills.  4. Conduct a detailed privacy and data protection audit within 6 months of the Regulation’s issuance. The audit must document:  a) The personal data collected about employees and customers. b) The purposes for collecting this data. c) How individuals are informed about the data collection and use. d) How individuals can access, correct, or delete their data. e) Whether and how consent is obtained before collecting or sharing personal data. f) The Bank’s policies and practices for securing personal data. g) The Bank’s policies for proper use of personal data. h) The Bank’s overall privacy and data protection policies and procedures. i) How the Bank monitors and reports privacy breaches. j) How the Bank evaluates technology’s impact on privacy and security policies.
data_protection.riskDescription: NDPR violation, audit failure, weak compliance culture

data_protection.title: Application
data_protection.description: (1) This Act shall apply to the processing of personal data, whether by automated means or not.  (2) This Act shall apply, where the— (a) data controller or the data processor is domiciled in, resident in, or operating in Nigeria; (b) processing of personal data occurs within Nigeria; or (c) the data controller or the data processor is not domiciled in, resident in, or operating in Nigeria, but is processing personal data of a data subject in Nigeria.
data_protection.plain: The Bank shall:  1. Comply with this Act when processing any personal data, whether manually or by automated means.   2. Ensure compliance if: a) It is domiciled, resident, or operating in Nigeria, b) The processing of personal data takes place within Nigeria, or c) It is outside Nigeria but processes personal data of individuals located in Nigeria.
data_protection.riskDescription: Non-compliance could result in unlawful processing of personal data, even if operations are offshore.
data_protection.primaryControl: Legal and compliance assessment of all operations and data processing activities for NDPA coverage.
data_protection.additionalControl: Annual jurisdictional mapping of cross-border data processing activities.

data_protection.title: Principles of personal data processing
data_protection.description: (1) A data controller or data processor shall ensure that personal data is—  (a) processed in a fair, lawful and transparent manner; (b) collected for specified, explicit, and legitimate purposes, and not to be further processed in a way incompatible with these purposes; (c) adequate, relevant, and limited to the minimum necessary for the purposes for which the personal data was collected or further processed; (d) retained for not longer than is necessary to achieve the lawful bases for which the personal data was collected or further processed; (e) accurate, complete, not misleading, and, where necessary, kept up to date having regard to the purposes for which the personal data is collected or is further processed; and (f) processed in a manner that ensures appropriate security of personal data, including protection against unauthorised or unlawful processing, access, loss, destruction, damage, or any form of breach. (2) A data controller and data processor shall use appropriate technical and organisational measures to ensure confidentiality, integrity, and availability of personal data.
data_protection.plain: The Bank shall:  1. Ensure that all personal data is:  a) Processed fairly, lawfully, and transparently. b) Collected for specific, clear, and lawful purposes, and not used for unrelated reasons. c) Relevant and limited to what is strictly necessary for the intended purpose. d) Kept only as long as necessary for the lawful reason it was collected. e) Accurate, complete, and up to date to avoid errors or misleading records. f) Protected with appropriate security measures to prevent unauthorised access, loss, damage, or data breaches.  2. Implement appropriate technical and organisational safeguards to maintain the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of personal data.
data_protection.riskDescription: Breach of personal data protection principles may result in regulatory penalties, reputational damage, or legal claims.
data_protection.primaryControl: Data Protection Policy, secure IT systems, staff training, data minimisation policy, and retention schedules.
data_protection.additionalControl: Periodic data audits, DLP tools, encryption, and breach simulation drills.

data_protection.title: Lawful Basis of Personal Data Processing
data_protection.description: (1) Without prejudice to the principles set out in this Act, data processing shall be lawful, where—  (a) the data subject has given and not withdrawn consent for the specific purpose or purposes for which personal data is to be processed; (b) the processing is necessary— (i) for the performance of a contract to which the data subject is a party or to take steps at the request of the data subject prior to entering into a contract, (ii) for compliance with a legal obligation to which the data controller or data processor is subject, (iii) to protect the vital interest of the data subject or another person, (iv) for the performance of a task carried out in the public interest or in the exercise of official authority vested in the data controller or data processor, or (v) for the purposes of the legitimate interests pursued by the data controller or data processor, or by a third party to whom the data is disclosed. (2) Interests in personal data processing shall not be legitimate for the purposes of subsection (1) (b) (v), where— (a) they override the fundamental rights, freedoms and the interests of the data subject; (b) they are incompatible with other lawful basis of processing under subsection subsection (1) (b) (i)-(iv); or (c) the data subject would not have a reasonable expectation that the personal data would be processed in the manner envisaged.
data_protection.plain: The Bank shall:  1. Only process personal data if there is a lawful basis, including:  a) Consent: The individual has given valid consent (and not withdrawn it) for the specific purpose. b) Contract: The processing is needed to enter into or fulfill a contract with the data subject. c) Legal obligation: The processing is required to comply with a legal duty. d) Vital interest: The processing is necessary to protect someone’s life or safety. e) Public interest or official authority: The processing is needed to carry out a task in the public interest or in the exercise of legal powers. f) Legitimate interest: The processing serves the Bank’s or a third party’s legitimate interests.  2. Avoid relying on “legitimate interest” as a legal basis if: a) It conflicts with the data subject’s rights and freedoms. b) It contradicts other legal bases, such as contract or consent. c) The data subject would not reasonably expect their data to be used that way.
data_protection.riskDescription: Processing personal data without a lawful basis may lead to regulatory penalties, loss of trust, and lawsuits.
data_protection.owner: DPO, Legal & Compliance, IT Security, Operations
data_protection.primaryControl: - Document legal basis for each processing activity - Consent tracking - DPIAs for legitimate interest - Regular audits
data_protection.additionalControl: Include lawful basis documentation as part of all data lifecycle management processes.

data_protection.title: Consent
data_protection.description: 26.—(1) A data controller shall bear the burden of proof for establishing a data subject’s consent. (2) In determining whether consent was freely and intentionally given, account shall be taken of whether the performance of a contract, including the provision of a service, is conditional on consent to the processing of personal data that is not necessary for the performance of that contract. (3) Silence or inactivity of the data subject shall not constitute consent. (4) Where the processing of personal data is based on the consent of the data subject, the data subject shall be informed of the right to withdraw consent, prior to the granting of consent. (5) The withdrawal of consent under subsection (4) shall not affect the lawfulness of data processing that occurred before the withdrawal of the consent. (6) A request for consent shall be in clear and simple language and accessible format. (7) Consent — (a) shall be in the affirmative, and not based on a pre-selected confirmation; and (b) may be provided in writing, orally, or through electronic means.
data_protection.plain: The Bank shall:  1. Be responsible for proving that a customer (data subject) has given valid consent to process their personal data. 2. Ensure that consent is not forced. If the Bank makes access to services or contracts dependent on agreeing to unnecessary data processing, such consent shall not be considered valid. 3. Not treat silence, inactivity, or inaction by the customer as consent. 4. Clearly inform customers, before they give consent, that they have the right to withdraw their consent at any time. 5. Recognize that if a customer withdraws their consent, it does not affect any data processing that was lawfully carried out before the withdrawal. 6. Ensure all requests for consent are presented in clear, simple language and in a format that is easy to understand. 7. Obtain consent in an active, affirmative way — not through pre-ticked boxes or implied consent. Consent may be given in writing, orally, or electronically.
data_protection.riskDescription: Invalid or coerced consent may render processing unlawful and expose the Bank to enforcement actions.
data_protection.owner: Product Development, Legal & Compliance, Data Protection Officer
data_protection.primaryControl: - Consent mechanisms must be separate from T&Cs - Justify data necessity - Clear communication on consent
data_protection.additionalControl: Periodic review of service agreements and consent forms for compliance.

data_protection.title: Provision of information to the data subject
data_protection.description: 1) Before a data controller collects personal data directly from a data subject, the data controller shall inform the data subject of the—  (a) identity, residence or place of business of, and means of communication with the data controller and its representatives, where necessary; (b) specific lawful basis of processing under section 25(1) or 30(1) of this Act, and the purposes for which the personal data are intended; (c) recipients or categories of recipients of the personal data, if any; (d) existence of the rights of the data subject under Part VI; (e) retention period for the personal data; (f) right to lodge a complaint with the Commission in accordance with section 46 (1) of this Act; and (g) existence of automated decision-making, including profiling, the significance and envisaged consequences of such processing for the data subject, and the right to object to and challenge such processing. (2) Before a data controller collects personal data, other than directly from the data subject, the data controller shall inform the data subject of the matters set out in subsection (1), except where the— (a) data subject already has been provided with such information; or (b) provision of such information is impossible or would involve a disproportionate effort or expense. (3) The information referred to in subsection (1) shall be contained in a privacy policy and expressed in clear, concise, transparent, intelligible, and easily accessible format, taking into consideration the class of data subjects targeted by the data processing.
data_protection.plain: The Bank shall:  1. Before collecting personal data directly from individuals, clearly inform them of the following:  a) The Bank’s identity, business address, and how to contact it (and its representative, if any). b) The specific legal basis for processing their data and the purpose of the processing. c) Who will receive the data or the categories of potential recipients. d) The rights the individual has under the law (e.g., access, correction, objection, deletion). e) How long the data will be retained. f) The individual’s right to file a complaint with the Data Protection Commission. g) If decisions are made automatically (e.g., via profiling), explain this and the potential impact, along with the right to challenge such decisions.  2. Before collecting data from third parties (i.e., not directly from the individual), the Bank must also provide the same information—unless: a) The data subject already has the information, or b) It is impossible or would require disproportionate effort or cost to provide.  3. Ensure this information is included in the Bank’s privacy policy, which must be: a) Clear, concise, transparent, and intelligible, and b) Easily accessible, considering the audience the Bank is targeting.
data_protection.riskDescription: Failure to inform data subjects appropriately can result in non-compliance, fines, and reputational damage.
data_protection.primaryControl: Publish clear, concise privacy policies; embed compliance into data collection practices.
data_protection.additionalControl: Annual review of privacy notices for completeness and clarity.

data_protection.title: Data privacy impact assessment
data_protection.description: (1) Where the processing of personal data may likely result in high risk to the rights and freedoms of a data subject by virtue of its nature, scope, context, and purposes, a data controller shall, prior to the processing, carry out a data privacy impact assessment.  (2) The data controller shall consult the Commission prior to the processing if, notwithstanding the measures envisaged under this section, the data protection impact assessment indicates that the processing of the data would result in a high risk to the rights and freedoms of a data subject.
data_protection.plain: The Bank shall:  1. Conduct a Data Privacy Impact Assessment (DPIA) before starting any personal data processing activity that is likely to pose a high risk to individuals’ rights and freedoms—based on the nature, scope, context, or purpose of the processing.  2. If the DPIA shows that high risks remain despite proposed safeguards, the Bank must consult the Data Protection Commission before proceeding with the processing.
data_protection.riskDescription: Not conducting DPIAs may result in unlawful processing and significant fines.
data_protection.primaryControl: Mandatory DPIAs during project initiation for relevant use cases.
data_protection.additionalControl: DPIA checklist and risk flagging system in project lifecycle.

data_protection.title: Obligations of the data controller and data processor
data_protection.description: (1) Where a data controller engages the services of a data processor, or a data processor engages the services of another data processor, the data controller or data processor engaging another shall ensure that the engaged data processor —  (a) complies with the principles and obligations set out in this Act as applicable to the data controller; (b) assists the data controller or data processor, as the case may be, by the use of appropriate technical and organisational measures, in the fulfilment of the data controller's obligations to honour the rights of a data subject under Part VI; (c) implements appropriate technical and organisational measures to ensure the security, integrity, and confidentiality of personal data as required in Part VII; (d) provides the data controller or engaging data processor, where applicable, with information reasonably required to comply and demonstrate compliance with this Act; and (e) notifies the data controller or engaging data processor, where applicable, when a new data processor is engaged. (2) The measures under subsection (1) include a written agreement between the data controller and the data processor, or between data processors, as the case may be,
data_protection.plain: The Bank shall:  1. When engaging a data processor (or when the processor engages another processor), ensure that the engaged party: a) Complies with all applicable data protection principles and obligations under the Act, just as the data controller would. b) Helps the Bank (or original processor) to respect the rights of data subjects by using appropriate technical and organisational measures. c) Implements strong safeguards to maintain the security, integrity, and confidentiality of personal data. d) Provides necessary information to help the Bank demonstrate compliance with the law. e) Notifies the Bank if it plans to hire another data processor (i.e. sub-processor).  2. Formalise these obligations in a written contract between:  a) The Bank and the data processor, or b) Between data processors, if applicable.
data_protection.riskDescription: Third-party non-compliance can cause data breaches or regulatory action.
data_protection.primaryControl: Due diligence, standard contracts, and audits for data processors.
data_protection.additionalControl: Annual processor audits and contract reviews.

data_protection.title: Sensitive Personal Data
data_protection.description: 1) Without prejudice to the principles set out in this Act, a data controller or data processor shall not process or permit the processing of a data subject's processing of sensitive personal data, unless the—  (a) data subject has given and not withdrawn consent to the processing for the specific purpose or purposes for which it will be processed; (b) processing is necessary for the purposes of performing the obligations of the data controller or exercising right of the data subject under employment or social security laws or any other similar laws; (c) processing is necessary to protect the vital interests of the data subject or of another person, where the data subject is physically or legally incapable of giving consent; (e) processing is necessary for the establishment, exercise, or defence of a legal claim, obtaining legal advice, or conduct of a legal proceeding; (f) processing is necessary for reasons of substantial public interest, on the basis of a law, which shall be proportionate to the aim pursued, and provides for suitable and specific measures to safeguard the fundamental rights, freedoms and interests of the data subject;
data_protection.plain: The Bank shall not process sensitive personal data (such as health records, biometric data, religious beliefs, etc.) unless one of the following lawful grounds applies:  1. The data subject has explicitly given consent for the specific purpose and has not withdrawn it.  2. The processing is required to fulfil legal obligations under employment, social security, or similar laws.  3. The processing is necessary to protect the life or safety of the data subject or another person, particularly when the data subject is unable to give consent due to physical or legal incapacity.  4. The processing is necessary for: a. Establishing, exercising, or defending a legal claim, b. Obtaining legal advice, or c. Conducting legal proceedings.  5. The processing is justified by law for reasons of substantial public interest, and the law: a. Is proportionate to the objective being pursued, and b. Provides appropriate safeguards to protect the rights and freedoms of the data subject.
data_protection.riskDescription: Unlawful processing of sensitive data leading to regulatory sanctions, reputational damage, or lawsuits.
data_protection.primaryControl: Data classification policies; consent management system; legal basis register; DPO oversight
data_protection.additionalControl: Regular data protection audits; training for departments handling sensitive data

data_protection.title: Data Protection Officers
data_protection.description: (1) A data controller of major importance shall designate a Data Protection Officer or expert knowledge of data protection law and practices, and the ability to carry out the tasks prescribed under this Act and subsidiary legislation made under it.  (2) The Data Protection Officer may be an employee of a data controller or engaged by a service contract. (3) The Data Protection Officer shall— (a) advise the data controller or the data processor, and their employees, who carry out processing made under this Act; (b) monitor compliance with this Act and related policies of the data controller or data processor; and (c) act as the contact point for the Commission on issues relating to data processing.
data_protection.plain: The Bank shall:  1. Appoint a Data Protection Officer (DPO) if it is a data controller of major importance, ensuring the person has expert knowledge of data protection laws and practices and is capable of performing duties under the Act.  2. The DPO may either be:  a) An internal employee, or b) An external service provider under a contract.  3. The DPO’s responsibilities must include:  a) Advising the Bank and its staff on their data protection obligations, b) Monitoring compliance with the Act and the Bank’s data protection policies, and c) Acting as the main point of contact between the Bank and the Nigeria Data Protection Commission on all data processing matters.
data_protection.riskDescription: Non-compliance due to absence of a competent DPO, leading to systemic privacy breaches and enforcement actions.
data_protection.primaryControl: Appointment letter; role description; DPO reporting line; independence assurance
data_protection.additionalControl: Ongoing competency training for DPO; periodic performance reviews

data_protection.title: Data protection compliance services
data_protection.description: The Commission may license a person having a requisite level of expertise, in relation to data protection and this Act, to monitor, audit and report on compliance by data controllers and data processors with—  (a) this Act; and (b) regulations, guidelines, directives, and codes of conduct issued by the Commission made under the provisions of this Act.
data_protection.plain: The Bank shall cooperate with any licensed data protection compliance service provider authorised by the Nigeria Data Protection Commission to monitor, audit, and report on the Bank’s compliance with the provisions of the Data Protection Act, and any regulations, guidelines, directives, or codes of conduct issued under it.
data_protection.riskDescription: Regulatory breach for failing to cooperate with NDPC-appointed monitors or auditors.
data_protection.primaryControl: External audit facilitation procedures; cooperation protocols; record-keeping of audit responses
data_protection.additionalControl: Pre-audit readiness reviews; engagement with external data protection consultants

data_protection.title: Rights of a Data Subject
data_protection.description: (1) A data subject has the right to obtain from a data controller, without constraint or unreasonable delay—  (a) confirmation as to whether the data controller or a data processor operating on its behalf, is storing or otherwise processing personal data relating to the data subject, and where that is the case— (i) the purposes of the processing, (ii) the categories of personal data concerned, (iii) the recipients or categories of recipient to whom the personal data have been or will be disclosed, particularly recipients in third countries or international organisations, (iv) where possible, the period for which the personal data will be stored, or, if not possible, the criteria used to determine that period, (v) the existence of the right to request from the data controller rectification or erasure of personal data or restriction of processing of personal data concerning the data subject or to object to such processing, (vi) the right to lodge a complaint with the Commission; (vii) where the personal data is not collected from the data subject, any available information as to their source; and (viii) the existence of automated decision-making, including profiling, the significance and envisaged consequences for the data subject; (b) a copy of data subject's personal data in a commonly used electronic format, except to the extent that providing such data would impose unreasonable costs on the data controller, in which case the data subject may be required by the data controller to pay all or part of such costs; (c) the correction or, if correction is not feasible or suitable, deletion of the data subject's personal data that is inaccurate, out of date, incomplete, or misleading; (d) the erasure of personal data concerning the data subject, without undue delay; and (e) restriction of data processing pending— (i) the resolution of a request, (ii) objection by the data subject under this Act, or (iii) the establishment, exercise, or defence of legal claims. (2) A data controller shall erase personal data without undue delay, where— (a) the personal data is no longer necessary, in relation to the purposes for which it was collected or processed; or (b) the data controller has no other lawful basis to retain the personal data.
data_protection.plain: The Bank shall:  1. Respond promptly and without delay when a data subject exercises their rights. This includes the right to:  a) Confirm whether the Bank or its processor is handling their personal data, and if so, provide: b) The purpose of the data processing, c) The type of personal data being processed, d) Who the data has been or will be shared with (especially international recipients), e) How long the data will be kept, or how that duration is decided, f) The individual’s rights to request correction, deletion, restriction, or objection to processing, g) The right to file a complaint with the Data Protection Commission, h) The source of the data (if not collected directly), i) Whether automated decision-making (including profiling) is used and its potential effects.  2. Provide a copy of the individual's personal data in a commonly used electronic format, unless doing so would create an unreasonable cost—in which case the Bank may charge the individual some or all of that cost.  3. Correct or delete personal data that is inaccurate, outdated, incomplete, or misleading, unless correction is not feasible.  4. Erase personal data without delay if:  a) The data is no longer needed for the original purpose, or b) There is no lawful reason to keep it.  5. Temporarily restrict processing of personal data when:  a) A request or objection is being handled, b) Or legal claims are involved.
data_protection.riskDescription: Failure to honour data subject rights, leading to fines, complaints, or reputational loss.
data_protection.primaryControl: DSAR (Data Subject Access Request) process; identity verification procedures; data inventory; secure deletion tools
data_protection.additionalControl: Automated DSAR portal; regular staff training on handling privacy requests

data_protection.description: (1) A data subject shall have the right to withdraw, at any time, consent to the processing of personal data under this Act.  (2) The data controller shall ensure that it is as easy for the data subject to withdraw, as to give consent.
data_protection.plain: The Bank shall:  1. Respect the right of any individual to withdraw their consent to the processing of their personal data at any time.  2. data_protection.title: Right to Object
data_protection.description: 1) A data subject shall have the right to object to the processing of personal data relating to the data subject.  (2) A data controller shall discontinue the processing of personal data, unless the data controller demonstrates a compelling public interest or other lawful grounds, which overrides the fundamental rights and freedoms, and the interests of the data subject. (3) Where personal data is processed for direct marketing purposes, the data subject shall have the right to object, at any time, to the processing of personal data concerning the data subject, which includes profiling, in so far as it is related to such direct marketing. (4) Where the data subject objects to processing for direct marketing purposes, the personal data shall no longer be processed for such purposes.
data_protection.plain: The Bank shall:  1. Respect the right of any individual to object to the processing of their personal data.  2. Stop processing the individual’s personal data unless the Bank can prove that there are compelling public interest reasons or other lawful grounds that override the individual’s rights and interests.  3. If personal data is being used for direct marketing (including profiling), the Bank must:  a) Allow individuals to object at any time, and b) Immediately stop processing their data for that purpose once they object.
data_protection.riskDescription: Continued processing after objection can result in regulatory action and loss of customer trust.
data_protection.primaryControl: Objection logging process; suppression list for marketing.
data_protection.additionalControl: Automation of opt-out handling and suppression.

data_protection.title: Automated Decision-Making
data_protection.description: (1) A data subject shall have the right not to be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing of personal data, which produces legal or similarly significant effects concerning the data subject.  (2) Subsection (1) shall not apply, where the decision is— (a) necessary for entering into or the performance of a contract between the data subject and a data controller; (b) authorised by a written law, which establishes suitable measures to safeguard the fundamental rights and freedoms, and the interests of the data subject; or (c) authorised by the consent of the data subject. (3) The data controller shall implement suitable measures to safeguard the data subject's fundamental rights, freedoms and interests, including the rights to— (a) obtain human intervention on the part of the data controller; (b) express the data subject's point of view; and (c) contest the decision.
data_protection.plain: The Bank shall:  1. Not make decisions solely based on automated processing (such as profiling) that significantly affect individuals unless:  a. The decision is necessary to enter into or perform a contract with the individual, b. It is expressly permitted by law, with safeguards for the individual's rights, or c. The individual has given explicit consent.  2. Where automated decision-making is allowed, the Bank must ensure the individual has the right to:  a) Request human involvement in reviewing the decision, b) Present their point of view, and c) Challenge or contest the decision.
data_protection.riskDescription: Unlawful profiling or decision-making may violate rights and trigger regulatory enforcement.
data_protection.primaryControl: Automated processing review; human-in-the-loop systems.
data_protection.additionalControl: Transparency measures and review procedures.

data_protection.title: Security, Integrity, and Confidentiality
data_protection.description: (1) A data controller and data processor shall implement appropriate technical and organisational measures to ensure the security, integrity and confidentiality of personal data in its possession or under its control, including protection against accidental or unlawful destruction, loss, misuse, alteration, unauthorised disclosure, or access, taking into account—  (a) the amount and sensitivity of the personal data; (b) the nature, degree and likelihood of harm to a data subject that could result from the loss, disclosure, or other misuse of the personal data; (c) the extent of the processing; (d) the period of data retention; and (e) the availability and cost of any technologies, tools, or other measures to be implemented relative to the size of the data controller or data processor. (2) Measures implemented under subsection (1) may include— (a) pseudonymisation or other methods of de-identification of personal data; (b) encryption of personal data; (c) processes to ensure security, integrity, confidentiality, availability and resilience of processing systems and services; (d) processes to restore availability of and access to personal data in a timely manner, in the event of a physical or technical incident; (e) periodic assessment of risks to processing systems and services, including where the processing involves the transmission of data over an electronic communications network; (f) regular testing, assessing, and evaluation of the effectiveness of the measures implemented against current and evolving risks identified; (g) regular updating of the measures and introduction of new measures to address shortcomings in effectiveness, and accommodate evolving risks.
data_protection.plain: The Bank shall implement and regularly update appropriate technical and organisational measures to protect personal data against unauthorized access, loss, misuse, or breach. Specifically, the Bank must:  1. Ensure the security, integrity, and confidentiality of personal data in its control, by taking into account:  a) The amount and sensitivity of the data, b) The likelihood and severity of harm to data subjects, c) The scope and scale of processing, d) The duration of data retention, and e) The cost and availability of security tools, relative to the Bank’s size.  2. Implement protective measures, which may include:  a) Pseudonymisation or data de-identification, b) Encryption of data, c) Systems to ensure availability, resilience, and confidentiality, d) Disaster recovery processes to restore access and availability after incidents, e) Risk assessments, especially for data transmitted electronically, f) Regular testing and evaluation of security controls, and g) Ongoing updates to security measures to address evolving risks and inefficiencies.
data_protection.riskDescription: Data breaches due to poor security measures can lead to fines, reputational damage, or lawsuits.
data_protection.primaryControl: Encryption, role-based access control, DR plans, regular risk assessments.
data_protection.additionalControl: Annual security audits and employee training.

data_protection.title: Personal Data Breaches
data_protection.description: (1) Where personal data breach has occurred with respect to personal data being stored or processed by a data controller or data processor, the data processor shall, on becoming aware of a breach—  (a) notify the data controller or data processor that engaged it, describing the nature of the personal data breach including, where possible, the categories and approximate numbers of data subjects and personal data records concerned; and (b) respond to all information requests from the data controller or data processor that engaged it, as they may require to comply with their obligations under this section. (2) A data controller shall, within 72 hours of becoming aware of a breach which is likely to result in a risk to the rights and freedoms of individuals, notify the Commission of the breach and, where feasible, describe the nature of the personal data breach including, where possible, the categories and approximate numbers of data subjects and personal data records concerned. (3) Where a personal data breach is likely to result in a high risk to the rights and freedoms of a data subject the data controller shall immediately communicate the personal data breach to the data subject in plain and clear language, including advice about measures the data subject should take to mitigate the possible adverse effects of the personal data breach and if a direct communications to the data subject would involve disproportionate effort or expense, or is otherwise not feasible, the data controller may instead make a public communication in one or more widely used media sources such that the data subject is likely to be informed.
data_protection.plain: The Bank shall:  1. Ensure third-party service providers (data processors) immediately notify the Bank of any personal data breach and provide details such as:  a) The type of data involved, b) The number of affected customers or records, c) And respond promptly to any requests for further information.  2. Notify the Nigeria Data Protection Commission (NDPC) within 72 hours of becoming aware of any breach that could affect the rights and freedoms of customers. This report must include, where possible:  a) A description of the breach, b) The types of data and individuals affected, c) The number of people or records involved.  3. Immediately inform affected customers if the breach is likely to cause serious harm or risk to their rights. The notice must be:  a) Clear and easy to understand, b) Include steps customers can take to protect themselves.  If it’s not possible to notify individuals directly, the Bank must issue a public notice through widely used media channels to reach those affected.
data_protection.riskDescription: Delayed or missed breach notifications could lead to regulatory penalties and erosion of user trust.
data_protection.primaryControl: Incident response policy, breach log, 72-hour breach reporting checklist.
data_protection.additionalControl: Breach simulation drills; notification templates.

data_protection.title: Personal Data Breaches
data_protection.description: (7)  In evaluating whether a personal data breach is likely to result in a risk to the rights and freedoms of a data subject under subsection (3), a data controller and the Commission may take into account —  (a)  the likely effectiveness of any technical and administrative measures implemented to mitigate the likely harm resulting from the personal data breach,  including any encryption or de-identification of the data ;  (b)  any subsequent measures taken by the data controller to mitigate such risk ; and  (c)  the nature, scope and sensitivity of the personal data involved.   (8)  A data controller and data processor shall keep a record of all personaldata breaches, comprising the facts relating to the personal data breach, its effects and the remedial action taken in a manner that enables the Commission to verify compliance with this section.  (9)  Where it is not possible to provide information under this section at the same time, the information may be provided in phases without undue delay.
data_protection.plain: The Bank shall: 1. Evaluate each data breach to see if it could harm individuals. a) Consider how well your security measures (like encryption or masking of data) worked. b) Review what has already been done to reduce the risk. c) Think about how sensitive or large the data breach was.  2. Keep full records of all breaches, even if they seem minor. These records should include: (a) What exactly happened. (b) How it affected people or could affect them. (c) What the Bank did to fix or limit the damage.  3. Store the breach records properly, so that NDPC (the regulator) can check later to confirm the Bank followed the rules.  4. If the Bank cannot provide all the details at once, it must: (a) Share what information is available immediately. (b) Then send the rest in parts, as soon as it becomes available — no unnecessary delay.

data_protection.additionalControl: - Breach documentation SOPs updated and audited quarterly.- Train key staff on phased disclosure procedures.- Implement breach tracking system.

data_protection.title: Basis for Cross-Border Data Transfer of Personal Data
data_protection.description: 1) A data controller or data processor shall not transfer or permit personal data to be transferred from Nigeria to another country, unless—  (a) the recipient of the personal data is subject to a law, binding corporate rules, code of conduct, code of conduct, or certification mechanism that affords an adequate level of protection with respect to the personal data in accordance with this Act; or (b) one of the conditions set out in section 43 of this Act applies. (2) A data controller or data processor shall record the basis for transfer of personal data to another country under subsection (1) and the adequacy of protection under section 42 of this Act.
data_protection.plain: The Bank shall:  1. Not transfer personal data outside Nigeria unless:  a) The receiving country or organization has laws, binding corporate rules, or certifications that provide adequate protection for personal data; or b) The transfer falls under specific exceptions listed in Section 43 of the Act.  2. Keep a written record of:  a) The legal basis for the transfer, and b) How the Bank assessed the adequacy of protection in the recipient country, in line with Section 42
data_protection.riskDescription: Unlawful transfer to non-compliant countries may result in international data privacy violations and sanctions.
data_protection.primaryControl: Cross-border data transfer policy, data transfer risk assessment template.
data_protection.additionalControl: Legal review before each transfer.

data_protection.title: Adequacy of Protection
data_protection.description: (1) A level of protection is adequate for the purposes of this section if it upholds principles that are substantially similar to the conditions for processing of the personal data provided for in this Act.  (2) The adequacy of protection referred to in subsection (1) shall be assessed taking into account the— (a) availability of enforceable data subject rights, the ability of a data subject to enforce such rights through administrative or judicial redress, and the rule of law; (b) existence of any appropriate instrument between the Commission and a competent authority in the recipient jurisdiction that ensures adequate data protection; (c) access of a public authority to personal data; (d) existence of an effective data protection law; (e) existence and functioning of an independent, competent data protection, or similar supervisory authority with adequate enforcement powers; and (f) international commitments and conventions binding on the relevant country and its membership of any multilateral or regional organisations.  (6) The absence of a determination by the Commission under subsection (4) or (5) with respect to a country, territory, or sector, binding corporate rules, codes of conduct, code of conduct, or certification mechanism shall not imply the adequacy of the protections afforded by it.
data_protection.plain: The Bank shall:  1. Ensure that any foreign country or recipient of personal data provides protection that is substantially similar to the principles under the Nigeria Data Protection Act before transferring personal data there.  2. Assess the adequacy of protection based on several factors, including:  a) Whether data subjects in the recipient country have enforceable rights and legal redress; b) Whether there are data protection agreements between the NDPC and that country’s authorities; c) Limitations on government access to personal data; d) Whether the country has effective data protection laws; e) The presence of an independent data protection authority with enforcement powers; f) The country’s participation in international or regional data protection agreements.  3. Not assume adequacy of protection just because the Commission has not made a specific decision about the country or mechanism.
data_protection.riskDescription: Assuming adequacy without due diligence could lead to invalid international transfers.
data_protection.primaryControl: Adequacy assessment checklist, NDPC guidance review.
data_protection.additionalControl: Document legal basis and assessment for each cross-border activity.

data_protection.title: Other bases for transfer of personal data outside Nigeria
data_protection.description: (1) In the absence of adequacy of protection under section 42 of this Act, a data controller or data processor shall only transfer personal data from Nigeria to another country if the—  (a) data subject has provided and not withdrawn consent to such transfer after having been informed of the possible risks of such transfers for the data subject due to the absence of adequacy decision; (b) transfer is necessary for the performance of a contract to which a data subject is a party or in order to take steps at the request of the data subject prior to entering into a contract; (c) transfer is for the sole benefit of a data subject and— (i) it is not reasonably practicable to obtain the consent of the data subject to that transfer; and (ii) if it were reasonably practicable to obtain such consent, the data subject would likely give it; (d) transfer is necessary for important reasons of public interest; (e) transfer is necessary for the establishment, exercise, or defence of legal claims; or (f) transfer is necessary to protect the vital interests of a data subject or of other persons, where a data subject is physically or legally incapable of giving consent.
data_protection.plain: The Bank shall:  If a destination country does not provide adequate data protection as required under Section 42, the Bank may only transfer personal data outside Nigeria if one or more of the following conditions apply:  1. The customer (data subject) has explicitly consented to the transfer after being informed of the risks involved due to lack of protection — and has not withdrawn that consent.  2. The transfer is necessary for fulfilling a contract with the customer or to take steps at the customer’s request before entering a contract.  3. The transfer is entirely for the benefit of the customer, and:  a) It is not reasonably possible to get their consent; and b) If it were possible, the customer would likely consent.  4. The transfer is required for public interest reasons.  5. The transfer is needed for the establishment, exercise, or defense of legal claims.  6. The transfer is required to protect the vital interests of the customer or another person, especially when the customer cannot legally or physically give consent.
data_protection.riskDescription: Unlawful data transfers to jurisdictions with weak protection.

data_protection.title: Registration of data controllers and data processors of major importance
data_protection.description: (1) Data controllers and data processors of major importance shall register with the Commission within six months after the commencement of this Act or on becoming a data controller or data processor of major importance.  (2) Registration under subsection (1) shall be made by notifying the Commission of— (a) the name and address of the data controller or data processor, and name and address of the data protection officer of the data controller or data processor; (b) a description of personal data and the categories and number of data subjects to which the personal data relate; (c) the purposes for which personal data is processed; (d) the categories of recipients to whom the data controller or data processor intends or is likely to disclose personal data; (e) the name and address, or name and address of any representative of any data processor operating directly or indirectly on its behalf; (f) the country to which the data controller or data processor intends, directly or indirectly to transfer or disclose the personal data; (g) a general description of the risks, safeguards, security measures and mechanisms to ensure the protection of the personal data; and (h) any other information required by the Commission.  (3)  A data controller or data processor of major importance shall notify the Commission of any significant change to the information submitted under  subsection (2) within 60 days after such change.   (5)  A data controller or data processor shall be removed from the register of the Commission, where it notifies the Commission that it has ceased to operate as a data controller or data processor of major importance.
data_protection.plain: The Bank shall:  1. Register with the Nigeria Data Protection Commission (NDPC) if classified as a data controller or data processor of major importance within six months of the Act's commencement or upon becoming one. The registration must include a notification to the Commission providing:  a) Name and address of the Bank and its Data Protection Officer (DPO) b) Description of the types of personal data processed, the number and categories of affected data subjects c) The purposes for which personal data is processed d) The categories of recipients the Bank may disclose personal data to e) Details of any data processors or representatives acting on its behalf f) Countries to which personal data may be transferred g) Overview of risks, safeguards, and security mechanisms in place h) Any other information required by the NDPC  2. Notify the NDPC within 60 days of any significant change in the information submitted during registration (e.g., DPO details, processing purpose, data categories, etc.).  3. Notify the NDPC when the Bank ceases to operate as a data controller or processor of major importance, so it can be removed from the Commission's register.
data_protection.riskDescription: Fines or suspension for failure to register or provide accurate information.
data_protection.primaryControl: Registration logs; Periodic data inventory reviews
data_protection.additionalControl: Internal escalation workflows; Regulatory calendar

data_protection.title: Complaints and Investigations
data_protection.description: (4) The Commission may, for the purpose of an investigation, order a person to— (a) attend at a specific time and place for the purpose of being examined orally in relation to a complaint; (b) produce such document, record, or article, as may be required with respect to any matter relevant to the investigation, which the person is not prevented by any other written law from disclosing; or (c) furnish a statement in writing made under oath or an affirmation setting out all information, which may be required under this Act. (5) Where any material to which an investigation relates, consists of information stored in any electronic record, printed, mechanical or electronic device, the Commission may require the person named to produce such material or give access to the Commission to conduct or inspect on the material. (6) For the purposes of subsection (5), the person shall ensure that the information relating to the material under investigation is visible and legible, in a structured, commonly used and machine-readable format.
data_protection.plain: The Bank shall:  When being investigated by the Nigeria Data Protection Commission (NDPC), the Bank must promptly comply with any formal request by the Commission to:  1. Appear for oral examination at a specified time and location, if required.  2. Submit documents, records, or items relevant to the investigation, unless another law legally prevents such disclosure.  3. Provide written statements under oath or affirmation, containing any information required under the Act.  4. If the investigation relates to electronic records or materials, the Bank must:  a) Produce or grant access to the relevant digital or physical information. b) Ensure the information is presented in a visible, legible, structured, commonly used, and machine-readable format.
data_protection.riskDescription: Obstruction of investigation or non-cooperation may lead to sanctions.
