data_protection.title: Exercise of Right to Rectification
data_protection.description: (1) The right to data rectification is essential to the operation of the principle of data accuracy under the NDP Act.  (2) A data controller or processor shall ensure that the platforms through which it processes personal data also provides an effective opportunity for data rectification.  (3) Data rectification may not depend on the provision of an affidavit or a publication in a newspaper provided that the rectification is to bring the data into alignment with the personal data relating to the data subject’s National Identification Number (NIN).  (4) Where data rectification is for the purpose of correcting an error made by a data controller or a data processor in inputting the personal data of a data subject, the data subject shall not be required to pay in order to correct an error which is not his or her fault. Accordingly, it is important to ensure that a data subject is provided with manifestly ample opportunity to verify his or her data before such data is submitted in a permanent format.   (5) Whenever there is a dispute as to whether a data subject was provided with manifestly ample opportunity to verify his or her personal data before being submitted in a permanent format, the data controller or data processor shall provide the evidence of the manifestly ample opportunity. Accordingly, data processing platforms together with the technical and organisational measures for their operations shall be designed in a way that may allow a data controller or data processor to audit any source of error.
data_protection.plain: The Bank shall: 1. Recognize and uphold the data subject’s right to correct inaccurate personal data, as part of its duty to ensure data accuracy.  2. Ensure its data platforms (e.g., apps, databases, portals) provide effective ways for customers to request and obtain correction of their personal data.  3. Not require affidavits or newspaper publications for corrections, especially when the correction is to align with NIN records.  4. Not charge customers to fix data errors caused by the Bank’s own staff or systems, and must ensure customers are clearly given the opportunity to review their data before it's finalized.  5. Maintain audit trails and systems capable of proving that customers were given clear opportunities to verify their data before submission.
data_protection.riskDescription: Failure to rectify inaccurate data could violate data accuracy principles and expose the bank to customer complaints or sanctions.
data_protection.primaryControl: Customer data portals with rectification forms; integration with NIMC for NIN verification.
data_protection.additionalControl: Implement backend audit logs and automated verification prompts before data is submitted permanently.

data_protection.title: Exercise of Right to Data Portability
data_protection.description: (1) A data subject has a right to data portability.  (2) The right to data portability shall apply where the data subject provided the personal data on the basis of his or her consent or the processing is necessary for the performance of a contract. It may not apply where processing is based on a legal ground other than consent or contract.  (3) The right to data portability may not apply against a data controller or data processor in the performance of its public duties; unless there is a compelling legitimate interest or right of a data subject that may be abridged by reason of denying the data subject's right of data portability.  (4) Where, in a certain set of personal data, more than one data subject is concerned, the right to receive the personal data should be without prejudice to the rights and freedoms of other data subjects in accordance with the NDP Act or any regulatory instrument issued by the Commission.  (5) The right to data portability shall not prejudice the right of the data subject to obtain the erasure of personal data and the limitations of that right as prescribed under the NDP Act.  (6) Nothing in this Article shall imply the erasure of personal data concerning the data subject which has been provided by him or her for the performance of a contract to the extent that and for as long as are necessary for the performance of that contract.
data_protection.plain: The Bank shall:  1. Allow customers (data subjects) to request and receive a copy of their personal data in a usable, machine-readable format, if the data was provided based on consent or for a contract (e.g., account opening, loan application).  2. Transfer the personal data directly to another service provider at the customer’s request, where technically feasible.  3. Refuse portability only if the data was collected based on legal obligations or public interest, unless denying it would unfairly harm the customer's legitimate rights.  4. Ensure that providing a customer’s data does not infringe on the privacy rights of any other person whose data might be included in the same dataset.  5. Honour portability requests without affecting the customer’s separate right to request data erasure, unless the bank must retain the data to perform a contract.  6. Retain personal data needed to fulfil a contract only as long as necessary, even if the customer has exercised their right to data portability.
data_protection.riskDescription: Complaints or customer churn if not supported.
data_protection.primaryControl: Portability SOP, data extract tool.
data_protection.additionalControl: Periodic check of formats and response time.

data_protection.title: Exercise of Right to be Forgotten
data_protection.description: (1) A data subject has the right to have his or her personal data erased if: a) The personal data is no longer necessary for the purpose a data controller or data processor originally collected or processed it. b) A data controller or data processor is relying on an individual's consent as the lawful basis for processing the data and that individual withdraws his or her consent. c) A data controller or data processor is relying on legitimate interest as its justification for processing an individual's data, of which, the individual objects to this processing, and there is no overriding legal ground for the organisation to continue with the processing. d) A data controller or data processor is processing personal data for direct marketing purposes and the individual objects to this processing. e) A data controller or data processor processed an individual's personal data unlawfully. f) A data controller or data processor must cause personal data in order to comply with a legal ruling or obligation.  (2) However, an organisation's interest in processing the personal data may override a data subject's right to be forgotten if: a) The data is being used to exercise the right of freedom of expression and information subject to the limit of derogation permitted under Section 45 of the 1990 Constitution and other safeguards of the NDP Act. b) The data processing is necessary:  to receive complaints by any reasonable means through which it may be contacted by a complainant (including but not limited to hard copies at its known offices and emails).
data_protection.plain: The Bank shall:  1. Erase a customer’s personal data (Right to be Forgotten) if any of the following apply:  (a) The data is no longer needed for the reason it was originally collected. (b) The customer withdraws their consent, and consent was the legal basis for processing. (c) The customer objects to processing based on legitimate interest, and there is no stronger legal reason to continue. (d) The customer objects to the use of their data for direct marketing. (e) The data was processed unlawfully. (f) The bank is legally required (e.g., by court order) to erase the data.  2. Not erase the data, even when a customer requests it, if:  (a) The data is being used lawfully for freedom of expression or information, within constitutional and legal boundaries. (b) The data is needed to receive and handle complaints through recognized means (e.g., email, hard copy, etc.).
data_protection.riskDescription: Failure to act on or wrongly deny a valid erasure request can lead to regulatory action, data subject complaints, or reputational damage.
data_protection.primaryControl: Data subject request workflow; consent management system; defined retention policies.
data_protection.additionalControl: Automate checks for legal bases before processing erasure; provide clear refusal notices with legal justification when erasure is denied.

data_protection.plain: The Bank shall: 1. Include a clear clause in every regulation, policy, framework, contract, or other legal document that involves the processing of personal data, informing data subjects of their right to lodge a complaint with the Nigeria Data Protection Commission (NDPC).  2. Maintain and be able to provide, when requested by the NDPC, a list of all third-party data processors, agents, or contractors it engages for data processing, along with copies of data processing agreements and proof of compliance with the NDP Act.  3, Maintain and disclose, when requested, a list of foreign countries to which it transfers personal data, including the lawful basis relied upon for each transfer.  4. Produce Data Protection Impact Assessments (DPIAs) for the technologies and methods it uses to process personal data when required by the NDPC.  5. Maintain and provide, on request, the name and official contact information of its designated and certified Data Protection Officer (DPO).  6. Respond to any notice of investigation issued by the NDPC within twenty-one (21) days, unless a different deadline is specified by the Commission.

data_protection.title: Evidence of Compliance with the NDP Act
data_protection.description: (1) Evidence by a data controller or a data processor relating to compliance with the NDP Act or any regulatory instrument issued by the Commission shall be evaluated in the context they directly relate to.  (2) Compliance in relation to registration, filing of annual CAE, submission of DPIA or cross-border transfer instruments approved by the Commission shows commitment to accountability and prima facie good faith in data processing. It does not replace the need to provide concrete evidence in defence of any complaint of violation relating to other provisions of the NDP Act.
data_protection.plain: The Bank shall: 1.Provide clear and relevant evidence of compliance with the NDP Act and any directives issued by the Nigeria Data Protection Commission, ensuring that such evidence is directly related to the specific context of the obligation.  2.Understand that while actions like registration, filing of annual CAE, submission of DPIA, or cross-border data transfer approvals demonstrate accountability and good faith, they do not replace the need to present concrete evidence in the event of a complaint or violation.
data_protection.riskDescription: Inability to demonstrate compliance during audit or investigation may result in fines, reputational damage, or enforcement actions.
data_protection.primaryControl: Maintain compliance documentation; retain audit trails; track all filings with NDPC.
data_protection.additionalControl: Annual compliance file review and audit trail repository.

capital_market.source: Investment and Securities Act 2025
capital_market.title: Filing of annual and periodic reports with the Commission
capital_market.description: 88.—(1) A public company whose securities are required to be registered under this Act shall file with the Commission on an annual basis, its audited financial statements and such other periodic returns as may be prescribed by the Commission.  (2) The chief executive officer and the chief financial officer or officers or persons performing similar functions in a public company filing periodic or annual reports under subsection (1), shall certify in each annual or periodic report filed, that —  (a) the signing officer has reviewed the report;  (b) based on the knowledge of the officer, the report does not — (i) contain any untrue statement of a material fact, or (ii) omit to state a material fact, which may make the statement misleading in the light of the circumstances under which such statement was made;  (c) based on the knowledge of such officer, the financial statements and other financial information included in the report fairly present in all material respects the financial condition and results of operations of the company as of, and for the period presented in the report;  (d) the signing officers — (i) are responsible for establishing and maintaining internal controls, (ii) have established such internal controls to ensure that material information relating to the company and its consolidated subsidiaries is made known to such officers by others within those entities particularly during the period in which the periodic reports are being prepared, (iii) have evaluated the effectiveness of the company’s internal controls as of a date within 90 days prior to the report, and (iv) have presented in the report their conclusions about the effectiveness of their internal controls based on their evaluation as of that date;  (e) the signing officers have disclosed to the auditors of the company and audit committee — (i) all significant deficiencies in the design or operation of internal controls which may adversely affect the company’s ability to record, process, summarise and report financial data and have identified for the company’s auditors any material weakness in internal controls, and (ii) any fraud, whether or not material, that involves management or other employees who have significant role in the company’s internal controls; and  (f) the signing officers have identified in the report whether or not there were significant changes in internal controls or other factors that may significantly affect internal controls subsequent to the date of their evaluation, including any corrective actions with regard to significant deficiencies and material weaknesses.
capital_market.plain: The Bank shall:  1. File its audited financial statements and other required periodic reports with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) every year, or as otherwise specified by the Commission.  2. The Bank’s Managing Director (CEO) and Chief Financial Officer (CFO), or anyone performing similar roles, shall certify in each report that:  a) They have reviewed the report.  b) To the best of their knowledge, the report does not contain any false or misleading information, or leave out any important facts.  c) The financial statements and other financial information in the report fairly reflect the Bank’s financial condition and performance for the period covered.  d) They are responsible for the Bank’s internal control systems.  e) They have set up internal controls to ensure that important information about the Bank and its subsidiaries is shared with them, especially while preparing the reports.  f) They have assessed how effective the internal controls are within 90 days before the report date.  g) They have included their conclusions about the effectiveness of internal controls in the report.  3. They have informed the Bank’s auditors and the Audit Committee about:    i. Any major problems or weaknesses in the internal controls that could affect the accuracy of financial reporting.   ii.  Any fraud (whether major or minor) involving management or staff in key control functions.  4. They have stated in the report whether there have been any significant changes in internal controls after the last evaluation and whether corrective actions were taken to fix any issues.
capital_market.riskDescription: Failure to submit accurate and timely reports to the SEC or submit false/misleading statements could result in regulatory sanctions and reputational damage.
capital_market.primaryControl: Internal control framework, financial reporting processes, periodic board/Audit Committee reviews
capital_market.additionalControl: Quarterly internal audit review of reporting processes; training for CFO/CEO on disclosure requirements

capital_market.source: Investment and Securities Act 2025
capital_market.title: System of internal control of public companies
capital_market.description: 89.—(1) A public company shall establish a system of internal controls over its financial reporting and security of its assets and the board of directors shall ensure the integrity of the company’s internal controls and reporting. (2) The board of directors of a public company shall report on the effectiveness of the company’s internal control system in its annual report. (3) In this section, “internal control” means policies, procedures and practices prescribed by management to ensure safety of assets, accuracy of financial records and reports, achievement of corporate objectives and compliance with laws, regulations and applicable corporate governance standards. (4) A public company which contravenes the provisions of section 88 and this section, is liable to a penalty of not less than **₦5,000,000** and a further penalty of **₦50,000 per day** for every day the violation continues.
capital_market.plain: The Bank shall put in place a system of internal controls to safeguard its assets and ensure accurate financial reporting.  The Board of Directors is responsible for making sure that these internal controls are reliable and effective. The Board shall include in the Bank’s annual report an assessment of how well the internal control system is working.  Internal control means the policies, procedures, and practices set by management to:  a) Protect the Bank’s assets, b) Ensure the accuracy of financial records and reports, c) Help the Bank meet its business goals, and d) Comply with laws, regulations, and corporate governance standards.  If the Bank fails to comply with this requirement or with the reporting obligation under Section 88, it may face a penalty of at least ₦5,000,000, and an additional ₦50,000 for each day, the violation continues.
capital_market.riskDescription: Weak or ineffective internal controls may lead to asset loss, inaccurate financial statements, regulatory non-compliance, and reputational damage.
capital_market.owner: Board of Directors, Internal Audit, Risk & Compliance
capital_market.primaryControl: Internal control policies, annual board review, internal audit assessments
capital_market.additionalControl: Regular board risk workshops; enhanced compliance oversight of control design

(2) Every public company shall appoint a compliance officer who in conjunction with the chief financial officer shall ensure compliance with all regulatory requirements of the Commission.

capital_market.title: Annual Report
capital_market.description: (1) The annual report to be filed with the Commission shall in all material facts comply with the relevant accounting standard. It shall also make disclosures of its unclaimed dividend fund with respect to bank balance, investments and earned income by way of notes to the audited accounts and other periodic reports filed with the Commission. (2) The annual reports shall be filed with the Commission, not later than ninety (90) days after the financial year end in line with the provisions of CAMA; (3) The chief executive officer and chief financial officer or officers or persons performing similar functions in a public company shall in filing the annual account, attach a duly signed certification letter to the matters specified in section 60(2) of the Act; (4) The auditor to the public company shall be registered by the Commission in line with Section 62 of the Act; (5) The auditor of a public company shall in his audit report to the company issue a statement as to the existence, adequacy and effectiveness or otherwise of the internal control system of the company; (6) The annual report shall state the level of compliance of the public company with the Code of Corporate Governance for public companies as contained in schedule X of these rules and regulation. [SECRR(A) September, 2011] (7) Any company who fails to file its annual report with the Commission as in ( 1) above shall be liable to a fine of N1million and the sum of N25,000 for every day the default continues.
capital_market.plain: (1) The Bank shall ensure that its annual report fully complies with all relevant accounting standards. The report must include disclosures on unclaimed dividends, covering bank balances, investments, and any income earned. These details should be included in the notes to the audited accounts and other reports filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC).  (2) The Bank shall file its annual report with the SEC no later than 90 days after the end of its financial year, in line with the Companies and Allied Matters Act (CAMA).  (3) The Bank shall ensure that its Chief Executive Officer (CEO) and Chief Financial Officer (CFO)—or anyone performing similar roles—attach a signed certification letter to the annual report. This letter must confirm the matters stated in Section 60(2) of the Investment and Securities Act.  (4) The Bank shall ensure that its appointed auditor is registered with the SEC in accordance with Section 62 of the Act.  (5) The Bank shall require its auditor to include in the audit report a statement on whether the Bank’s internal control system is in place, adequate, and effective.  (6) The Bank shall disclose in its annual report the extent to which it complies with the Code of Corporate Governance for public companies, as outlined in Schedule X of the SEC Rules and Regulations.
capital_market.riskDescription: Failure to comply may lead to regulatory sanctions, reputational damage, financial penalties, and loss of investor confidence due to inadequate transparency or delayed disclosure.
capital_market.primaryControl: Timely internal preparation of reports; compliance calendar; external audit coordination; corporate governance disclosure checklist
capital_market.additionalControl: Pre-submission compliance review by legal/compliance unit; early scheduling of audits

capital_market.title: Rule on Earnings Forecast
capital_market.description: (1) All public quoted companies shall release its earnings forecast to the relevant securities exchange, the Commission and the investing public twenty (20) days prior to the commencement of a quarter. (2) The forecast shall be in line with the company’s policy and securities exchange listing requirements; (3) Underlying assumptions that formed the bases of the forecast shall also be disclosed; (4) The forecast shall be certified by the chief executive officer and chief financial officer or officers or persons performing similar functions in the company; (5) All public companies shall notify the relevant securities exchanges as soon as it is known that the forecast will not be realized and the reasons for the non-realization shall be stated.
capital_market.plain: (1) The Bank shall release its earnings forecast at least 20 days before the start of each quarter. The forecast must be sent to the relevant securities exchange, the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), and made available to the investing public.  (2) The Bank shall ensure that the forecast aligns with its internal policy and complies with the listing requirements of the securities exchange where it is quoted.  (3) The Bank shall disclose the key assumptions on which the earnings forecast is based.  (4) The Bank shall ensure that the earnings forecast is certified by the Chief Executive Officer (CEO) and Chief Financial Officer (CFO), or by other officers performing similar roles.  (5) The Bank shall immediately notify the relevant securities exchange if it becomes clear that the earnings forecast will not be met. The Bank must also explain the reasons for the shortfall.

capital_market.riskDescription: Failure to issue timely and accurate earnings forecasts can lead to investor misinformation, market manipulation concerns, penalties from the SEC or exchange, and reputational damage.
capital_market.primaryControl: Forecast preparation process with documented assumptions, approval workflow, certification, and disclosure tracking
capital_market.additionalControl: Quarterly forecast validation review; automated alert for market disclosure deadlines

capital_market.source: SECURITIES AND EXCHANGE COMMISSION RULES AND REGULATIONS, 2013
capital_market.title: Quarterly Reports
capital_market.description: (1) Public quoted companies shall not later than thirty (30) days from the end of each quarter file with the Commission and simultaneously with the relevant securities exchanges and the investing public a quarterly report prepared in accordance with the International Financial Reporting Standard (IFRS). (2) The quarterly report shall contain the following by way of notes: (a) Accounting policy changes; (b) Seasonality or cyclicality of operations; (c) Unusual items; (d) Changes in estimates; (e) Issuance, repurchase, and repayment of debts and equity securities; (f) Dividends; (g) Items of segment information (where applicable); (h) Significant events after the end of the interim period; (i) Business combinations; (j) Long term investments; (k) Restructuring and reversals of restructuring provisions; (l) Discontinuing operations; (m) Correction of prior errors; (n) Write-down of inventory to net realizable value; (o) Impairment loss of property, plant, equipment, intangible or other; assets, and reversal of such impairment loss; (p) Litigation settlements; (q) Any debt default or any breach of a debt covenant that has not been corrected subsequently; (r) Related party transactions; (s) Acquisitions and disposals of property, plant and equipment; (t) Commitments to purchase property, plant and equipment. (3) The chief executive officer and chief financial officer or officers or persons performing similar functions in a public company shall in filing the quarterly report attach a duly signed certification letter. (4) Publication of Interim Financial Statement. All public companies shall publish their “signed” quarterly balance sheet, income statement and cash flow statements in at least one (1) national daily newspaper. However, the accounting policies, notes and other relevant information shall be posted on the company’s website which address shall be disclosed in the newspaper publication. The publication shall be signed by the officers mentioned in (3) above. (5) Any company which fails to file quarterly report with the Commission shall be liable to a fine of N1million and the sum of N25,000 for every day the default continues.
capital_market.plain: Quarterly Financial Reporting Obligations (1) The Bank shall file its quarterly financial report with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), the relevant securities exchange, and the investing public within 30 days after the end of each quarter. The report must be prepared in line with International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS).  (2) The Bank shall include the following disclosures as notes to the quarterly report (where applicable):  a) Changes in accounting policies b) Seasonal or cyclical patterns in operations c) Unusual or non-recurring items d) Changes in estimates e) Issuance, buy-back, or repayment of debt and equity f) Dividends paid or declared g) Segment information h) Major events occurring after the end of the quarter i) Business combinations j) Long-term investments k) Restructuring or reversal of provisions l) Discontinued operations m) Corrections of prior errors n) Inventory write-downs o) Impairment or reversal of impairment on assets p) Litigation settlements r) Defaults or breaches of debt covenants s) Related party transactions t) Purchases or sales of property, plant, and equipment u) Commitments to acquire new assets  (3) The Bank shall attach a signed certification letter from the Chief Executive Officer (CEO) and Chief Financial Officer (CFO), or other designated officers, when submitting the quarterly report.  (4) The Bank shall publish its signed quarterly balance sheet, income statement, and cash flow statement in at least one national newspaper. Additional details such as accounting policies and explanatory notes shall be made available on the Bank’s website, and the website address must be included in the newspaper publication. The publication must also be signed by the CEO and CFO or their equivalents.  Sanction for Non-Compliance: If the Bank fails to file its quarterly report as required, it will be liable to:  A fine of ₦1,000,000, and  An additional ₦25,000 for each day the delay continues.
capital_market.deadlineType: Within 30 days after each quarter end
capital_market.riskDescription: Late or inaccurate reporting may attract regulatory fines, erode investor confidence, affect market integrity, and cause reputational damage.
capital_market.primaryControl: Automated report calendar, IFRS-aligned report templates, dual officer sign-off, newspaper and website disclosure process
capital_market.additionalControl: Internal review checkpoints before submission, external audit liaison, public communication schedule

capital_market.source: SECURITIES AND EXCHANGE COMMISSION RULES AND REGULATIONS, 2013
capital_market.title: Half Yearly Returns
capital_market.description: (1) Public companies shall file half yearly returns with the Commission in the prescribed manner and shall contain the following: (a) General information; (b) Corporate Governance issues; (c) Unclaimed dividends; (d) Audit Committee; (e) Undertaking by the company secretary, chief internal auditor, financial controller, managing director, board chairman and chairman of audit committee certifying the reliability of the information in the format provided. (2) The completed form shall be returned to the Commission within thirty (30) days from the end of the half year period, either in hard or electronic copy. (3) Any company which fails to file its half yearly returns with the Commission shall be liable to a fine of N1million and the sum of N25,000 for every day the default continues. (4) Unclaimed Dividend All public companies shall file with the Commission in the prescribed form a report of unclaimed dividends on half a yearly basis. (5) Audit Committee (a) Every public company shall establish an audit committee with written term of reference. The committee shall be independent in carrying out its terms of reference. (b) The audit committee shall maintain records of attendance and deliberations of its meeting and interactions. (c) The audit committee of every public company shall review the company’s financial statements prior to approval by the board of the company and present the report at the annual general meeting.  (d) All members of the audit committee of the board shall be financially literate.
capital_market.plain: Half-Yearly Reporting and Audit Committee Requirements (1) The Bank shall file half-yearly returns with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) in the required format. The report must include: i. General company information ii. Corporate governance matters iii. Details of unclaimed dividends iv. Information about the Audit Committee  A signed declaration by the Company Secretary, Chief Internal Auditor, Financial Controller, Managing Director, Board Chairman, and Chairman of the Audit Committee, confirming the accuracy and reliability of the information provided  (2) The Bank shall submit the completed half-year return to the SEC within 30 days after the end of the half-year period. The report may be submitted either as a hard copy or electronically.  (3) The Bank shall also file a separate report on unclaimed dividends using the prescribed form on a half-yearly basis.  Audit Committee Requirements (4a) The Bank shall establish an Audit Committee with a clearly written terms of reference, and the committee must function independently.  (4b) The Audit Committee shall keep records of its meetings, including attendance, discussions, and decisions.  (4c) The Audit Committee shall review the Bank’s financial statements before they are approved by the Board and shall present its report at the Annual General Meeting (AGM).  (4d) All members of the Bank’s Audit Committee shall be financially literate.  Sanction for Non-Compliance: If the Bank fails to file its half-yearly return with the SEC as required, it will be liable to:  A fine of ₦1,000,000, and An additional ₦25,000 for each day the default continues.
capital_market.riskDescription: Failure to submit half-yearly reports or meet audit committee obligations can lead to regulatory penalties, undermine financial governance, weaken stakeholder trust, and increase legal liability.
capital_market.primaryControl: SEC filing tracker, committee charter, internal reporting protocols, signed certifications
capital_market.additionalControl: Periodic SEC compliance checklists, board/Audit Committee evaluation logs, capacity-building for committee members

capital_market.title: Risk Management
capital_market.description: (1) Risk Management by public companies  Every public company shall: (a) include risk management as part of its accounting policies; (b) disclose by way of notes any material effect of unmitigated risk on corporate profitability; (c) disclose by way of notes strategies for preventing risks the company is exposed to. (2) Risk Management by the Board  The board shall establish a risk management committee to assist it in its oversight of the risk profile, risk management framework and the risk reward strategy determined by the board.
capital_market.plain: Risk Management by the Bank (1) The Bank shall:  Include risk management policies as part of its accounting policies.  Disclose, in the notes to its financial statements, any significant impact of unaddressed risks on the Bank’s profitability.  Disclose, in the same notes, the strategies it has adopted to manage or prevent the risks it faces.  Risk Management by the Board (2) The Bank’s Board of Directors shall establish a Risk Management Committee to support the Board in:  Overseeing the Bank’s overall risk profile,  Monitoring the effectiveness of the risk management framework, and  Reviewing the Bank’s risk-reward strategy as approved by the Board.
capital_market.riskDescription: Failure to embed and disclose risk management practices may lead to regulatory scrutiny, poor strategic decisions, financial losses, or stakeholder mistrust.
capital_market.primaryControl: Risk disclosures in financial statements; periodic risk committee meetings; board-approved risk policy
capital_market.additionalControl: Annual board training on risk oversight; independent review of risk framework

capital_market.title: Payment of dividend
capital_market.description: (1) Dividend declared shall be paid en-bloc by the issuance of a cheque or transfer of funds to the registrar not later than seven (7) working days after the annual general meeting where the dividend was declared.  (2) Dividend shall be paid only out of the current profits or revenue reserves of the company. No company shall borrow for the purpose of paying dividend. (3) A company shall not declare or pay dividend if there are reasonable grounds to believe that the company is or would be, after payment, unable to pay its liabilities as they fall due.  (4) (a) All directors who pay or are party to the payment of dividend out of capital shall be  personally liable to refund to the company any payment so made.  (b) All directors who recommend the payment of dividend when it is apparent that the company has no resources to pay, shall be personally liable to pay the declared dividend to shareholders.
capital_market.plain: Dividend Payment Obligations (1) The Bank shall pay declared dividends in full (en-bloc) by issuing cheques or transferring funds to its registrar no later than 7 working days after the Annual General Meeting (AGM) where the dividend was approved.  (2) The Bank shall only pay dividends from current profits or retained earnings (revenue reserves). It is not allowed to borrow money for the purpose of paying dividends.  (3) The Bank shall not declare or pay dividends if there is any reasonable concern that it may become unable to meet its financial obligations or pay its debts after making the dividend payment.  Director Liability for Improper Dividend Payments (4a) If any director authorizes or is involved in paying dividends from capital, they shall be personally liable to return the amount to the Bank.  (4b) If any director recommends dividend payments when it is clear the Bank lacks the resources to pay, that director shall be personally responsible for paying the declared dividend to shareholders.
capital_market.riskDescription: Paying dividends without adequate profits or against financial prudence could lead to regulatory penalties, liquidity crisis, shareholder disputes, and director liability.
capital_market.primaryControl: Dividend declaration checklist, profit verification, board minutes, AGM resolution tracking
capital_market.additionalControl: Pre-AGM legal and financial review; board training on dividend governance and liabilit

capital_market.source: Rulebook of the Nigerian Stock Exchange
capital_market.title: Market Abuse
capital_market.description: “No issuer, director, employee, or any person acting on behalf of the issuer shall engage in any act or practice that constitutes market abuse. This includes engaging in or facilitating insider dealing, market manipulation, the dissemination of false or misleading information, or any conduct that creates a false or misleading appearance of active trading, or with respect to the market for or the price of any security.”
capital_market.plain: The Bank and its insiders shall not trade on confidential information, manipulate prices, or release false or misleading information.
capital_market.riskDescription: Insider trading or manipulation can result in NGX/SEC sanctions, loss of investor trust, or criminal liability.
capital_market.primaryControl: Insider trading policy, employee certification, training
capital_market.additionalControl: Surveillance systems, external audit review, whistleblowing

capital_market.source: Rulebook of the Nigerian Stock Exchange
capital_market.title: Disclosure of Material Circumstances
capital_market.description: "An issuer shall disclose to The Exchange and the public, without delay, any material information that may affect the market price of its securities or the investment decisions of investors. Such information shall be disclosed in a clear and accurate manner and shall not be misleading."
capital_market.plain: The Bank shall promptly and accurately disclose any important information that may influence investor decisions or the price of its securities.
capital_market.riskDescription: Failure to disclose material changes may mislead investors, lead to regulatory penalties, or cause market distortions.
capital_market.primaryControl: Material disclosure policy, early warning framework
capital_market.additionalControl: Disclosure committee oversight, media scan alerts

capital_market.source: Rulebook of the Nigerian Stock Exchange
capital_market.title: Dealing with Insider Information
capital_market.description: "An issuer shall establish appropriate arrangements to restrict access to insider information to persons who require it for the proper discharge of their duties and shall ensure that such persons are aware of their legal and regulatory duties and responsibilities with respect to insider dealing."
capital_market.plain: The company shall restrict access to inside information to only those who need it and ensure they understand insider trading laws.
capital_market.riskDescription: Uncontrolled access to insider information could lead to illegal trading, reputational damage, or regulatory sanctions.
capital_market.primaryControl: Insider list, confidentiality undertakings, internal training
capital_market.additionalControl: Access control logs, NDAs, periodic compliance attestation

capital_market.source: Rulebook of the Nigerian Stock Exchange
capital_market.title: Disclosure of Other Major Changes
capital_market.description: "An issuer shall also notify The Exchange and the public of any other major changes in its affairs not specifically referred to in these Rules which are necessary to enable the public to appraise the position of the issuer and to avoid the establishment of a false market in its securities."
capital_market.plain: The company shall publicly disclose any major development that could affect investor understanding or market pricing, even if not specifically listed in the rules.
capital_market.riskDescription: Failure to disclose significant non-standard events (e.g., leadership crisis, legal judgment) could mislead the market and result in regulatory action.
capital_market.owner: CEO / Company Secretary / Head of Legal
capital_market.primaryControl: Crisis reporting protocol, management disclosure review
capital_market.additionalControl: Board oversight, post-event media and analyst briefing

capital_market.source: Rulebook of the Nigerian Stock Exchange
capital_market.title: Confidentiality Requirements
capital_market.description: "Until such time as the major developments referred to in Rules 17.2 to 17.6 are made public, the issuer, its directors, employees and advisers shall ensure that such information is kept strictly confidential. The issuer shall ensure that any insider who is not a director or employee of the issuer, is subject to a duty of confidentiality."
capital_market.plain: The company shall ensure all insiders and advisers keep material information confidential until it is officially disclosed to the public.
capital_market.riskDescription: Leak of price-sensitive or undisclosed material information may result in insider trading, market disruption, or regulatory sanction.
capital_market.primaryControl: Insider list, NDA execution, training on confidentiality
capital_market.additionalControl: Secure information sharing platforms, access logs, whistleblowing

capital_market.source: Rulebook of the Nigerian Stock Exchange
capital_market.title: Duty to Maintain Insider List
capital_market.description: "The issuer shall draw up a list of all persons who have access to insider information and shall update it regularly. The issuer shall ensure that every person on the insider list acknowledges the legal and regulatory duties involved and is aware of the sanctions applicable to the misuse or improper circulation of such information."
capital_market.plain: The company shall maintain and update a list of all individuals who have access to insider information and ensure they understand their obligations and consequences of misuse.
capital_market.riskDescription: Failure to track insiders and educate them may lead to regulatory violations, insider trading, or reputational risk.
capital_market.primaryControl: Insider list maintained and reviewed quarterly; signed acknowledgements
capital_market.additionalControl: Compliance declarations, targeted training, restricted access systems

capital_market.source: Rulebook of the Nigerian Stock Exchange
capital_market.title: Disclosure of Unusual Price Movements
capital_market.description: "Upon a significant movement in the price of its listed securities, The Exchange may require an issuer to issue a press release to the market in order to clarify the reason for the unusual price movement or to state that the issuer is not aware of any reason for such movement."
capital_market.plain: If NGX observes a major price change in the company’s shares, the company shall publicly explain the reason or confirm it has no knowledge of the cause.
capital_market.riskDescription: Delay or failure to respond to NGX requests on price movement can cause investor uncertainty or raise suspicion of insider trading.
capital_market.primaryControl: Monitoring of market prices, media watch, response templates
capital_market.additionalControl: Quick response protocol, standby press release drafts

capital_market.source: Rulebook of the Nigerian Stock Exchange
capital_market.title: Dealing with Rumour
capital_market.description: "Where The Exchange determines that there is rumour or speculation in the market about the issuer, it may require the issuer to make a definitive public statement in response to the rumour or speculation."
capital_market.plain: If NGX detects market rumours about the company, the company shall issue a clear public response either confirming or denying them.
capital_market.riskDescription: Delay or failure to respond to market rumours may cause misinformation, reputational damage, and regulatory scrutiny.
capital_market.primaryControl: Market intelligence scanning, media tracking
capital_market.additionalControl: Pre-approved disclosure protocol, response statement templates

capital_market.source: Rulebook of the Nigerian Stock Exchange
capital_market.title: Clarification of News Published by Media
capital_market.description: "Where The Exchange determines that a media publication or report contains material information about an issuer which is likely to affect the price of the issuer’s listed securities or the investment decisions of investors, the issuer shall immediately issue a press release to clarify the position of the issuer with respect to the media publication or report."
capital_market.plain: If the media publishes market-sensitive information about the company, the company shall promptly issue a public clarification to confirm or deny it.
capital_market.riskDescription: Failure to clarify market-sensitive news may lead to false market signals, price volatility, and loss of investor confidence.
capital_market.primaryControl: Real-time media monitoring, pre-drafted press release templates
capital_market.additionalControl: Media response plan, investor Q&A briefings

capital_market.source: Rulebook of the Nigerian Stock Exchange
capital_market.title: Disclosure of Significant Occurrence
capital_market.description: "An Issuer shall without any delay, announce via The Exchange’s Issuers’ Portal any significant occurrence concerning publicly disclosed inside information after these events occur."
capital_market.plain: The company shall immediately report any major event involving inside information through the NGX portal.
capital_market.riskDescription: Delayed or non-disclosure could mislead investors, violate market transparency rules, and trigger penalties.
capital_market.primaryControl: Event monitoring, escalation protocols, Issuers’ Portal access controls
capital_market.additionalControl: Periodic compliance reviews and employee training

capital_market.source: Rulebook of the Nigerian Stock Exchange
capital_market.title: Disclosure of Changes in Beneficial Ownership of Shares
capital_market.description: (a) "Every Issuer shall notify The Exchange immediately on any transaction that brings the beneficial ownership in the company’s shares to five percent (5%) or more not later than ten (10) business days after such transaction." (b) "In the event of any breach... the Issuer shall be liable to pay a fine of fifty percent (50%) of its annual listing fee."
capital_market.plain: The company shall inform NGX within 10 business days if someone acquires 5% or more of its shares. If it fails to do so, it faces a penalty of 50% of its annual listing fee.
capital_market.deadlineType: Within 10 business days of the transaction
capital_market.riskDescription: Failure to disclose changes in significant shareholding may result in regulatory penalties and loss of market trust.

capital_market.additionalControl: Compliance audits, system triggers for share threshold changes

capital_market.title: Disclosure in the Annual Report of Shareholding
capital_market.description: (a) "Every Issuer shall disclose in its Annual Report the details of shareholders holding five percent (5%) or more in the company." capital_market.source: Rulebook of the Nigerian Stock Exchange
capital_market.title: Disclosure of Dealings in Issuers’ Shares
capital_market.description: (a) Every Issuer must create a Securities Trading Policy for all employees and directors, and enforce confidentiality on external advisers.(b) The policy must be publicized internally and published on the company’s website.(c) Directors and other insiders must notify the Company Secretary of personal share transactions on the same day; records must be kept and made available to The Exchange within 2 business days of request.(d) Issuers must disclose in interim and annual reports: (1) if it has adopted a compliant code; (2) if directors complied or not; and (3) any non-compliance details and remedial steps.
capital_market.plain: Issuers shall: create and circulate a trading policy; keep records of insiders' share dealings; publish the policy; and report compliance and breaches in their financial reports.
capital_market.deadlineType: Ongoing; Disclosures per transaction and in periodic reports
capital_market.riskDescription: Non-compliance with trading disclosure obligations could result in regulatory sanctions and loss of investor confidence.

capital_market.source: Rulebook of the Nigerian Stock Exchange
capital_market.title: Trading Restrictions for Restricted Persons
capital_market.description: (a) No Director, Adviser, or person discharging managerial responsibility, including their connected persons, may trade in the Issuer’s securities during periods when they possess unpublished price-sensitive information.(b) Such persons may only trade during “free periods”, and not during closed periods or any other restricted periods specified by The Exchange.
capital_market.plain: Directors and advisers shall not buy or sell company shares during periods when they may have insider or sensitive information.
capital_market.riskDescription: Unauthorized trading during restricted periods could result in insider trading allegations and severe regulatory penalties.
capital_market.primaryControl: Insider trading blackout calendar; mandatory disclosure policy; pre-clearance protocols

capital_market.title: Closed Period
capital_market.description: (a) No Director, person discharging managerial responsibility, Adviser, or their connected persons shall deal in the securities of the Issuer during a closed period, which is any time the trading window is restricted.(b) Closed periods include times such as:1. Declaration of financial results2. Dividend announcements3. Issuance of securities4. Major projects, mergers, or acquisitions5. Asset disposals6. Strategic changes7. Natural disruptions8. Material litigation9. Any other price-sensitive developments.
capital_market.plain: Insiders shall not trade company shares during specific events when market-sensitive information is not yet public.
capital_market.riskDescription: Trading during a closed period may constitute insider trading and attract regulatory and reputational penalties.
capital_market.primaryControl: Pre-defined closed period calendar, internal notifications, and trading blackout list
capital_market.additionalControl: System alerts and external auditor review of insider trades

capital_market.source: Rulebook of the Nigerian Stock Exchange
capital_market.title: Period of Closure
capital_market.description: (a) “The period of closure shall be effective from fifteen (15) days prior to the date of any meeting of the Board of Directors proposed to be held to consider any of the matters referred to above or the date of circulation of agenda papers pertaining to any of the matters referred to above, whichever is earlier, up to twenty-four (24) hours after the price sensitive information is submitted to The Exchange. The trading window shall thereafter be opened.”(b) “Every Issuer shall notify The Exchange in advance of the commencement of each closed period.”
capital_market.plain: The company shall close the trading window at least 15 days before board meetings on price-sensitive matters and notify NGX in advance.
capital_market.deadlineType: At least 15 days before relevant Board meetings
capital_market.riskDescription: Failure to enforce the correct period of closure may result in insider trading and regulatory breaches.
capital_market.primaryControl: Calendar-based control, Board schedule coordination, advance NGX notification
capital_market.additionalControl: Use of digital alerts for all insiders and trade system controls

capital_market.source: Rulebook of the Nigerian Stock Exchange
capital_market.title: Directors’ Obligations to Monitor Changes
capital_market.description: "The Directors of the Issuer shall scrutinize on an on-going basis, within the scope of their competence, all the events and changes taking place in the Issuer’s operations in order to assess what information requires immediate disclosure in accordance with these Rules."
capital_market.plain: Directors shall continuously monitor company events and operations to determine if any information must be disclosed immediately.
capital_market.riskDescription: Failure to promptly identify and disclose material information may lead to regulatory penalties and reputational harm.
capital_market.primaryControl: Periodic Board briefings; structured reporting from management to the Board
capital_market.additionalControl: Compliance/legal oversight on disclosure obligations

capital_market.source: Rulebook of the Nigerian Stock Exchange
capital_market.title: Financial Reporting and Periodic Disclosure
capital_market.description: (a) All Issuers shall publish on their website all documents requiring publication on The Exchange’s website, including announcements, circulars, annual and interim financial and other reports, listing documents etc. (b) The financial statements submitted with an Application for listing and future periodic financial reports shall be prepared using accounting policies and methods that comply with IFRS and other FRCN standards and shall contain information required by the Rules. (c) The full financial statements (annual and interim reports) shall be submitted electronically to The Exchange. (d) Where the securities of an Issuer’s parent or significant subsidiary are listed on another exchange, the Issuer shall ensure that such reports are made public simultaneously across exchanges. (e) An Issuer shall announce the full-year financial statements immediately after they are available, and not later than 90 days after the period. Reports must be accessible to the public for at least 5 years. (f) Issuers shall announce quarterly statements for the first 3 quarters no later than 30 days after the relevant financial period. (g) An Issuer shall not announce Interim Accounts without first filing its last Audited Financial Statements.
capital_market.plain: Issuers shall publish their full-year and quarterly financial statements promptly, use IFRS, and ensure reports are submitted to NGX and published on their website.
capital_market.deadlineType: Annual (90 days), Quarterly (30 days), Ongoing publication
capital_market.riskDescription: Late, incomplete, or non-compliant financial reporting may result in sanctions, loss of investor confidence, or suspension.
capital_market.primaryControl: Financial reporting calendar, internal review, external auditor sign-off
capital_market.additionalControl: Internal audit; compliance oversight; board audit committee review

capital_market.source: Rulebook of the Nigerian Stock Exchange
capital_market.title: Issuers to Co-operate with The Exchange
capital_market.description: (a) All Issuers are subject to and shall comply with the Rules and Regulations of The Exchange as stipulated by it from time to time. (b) All Issuers shall cooperate with The Exchange and shall supply The Exchange with all the information it may require or request from time to time for: (1) The adequate supervision of Issuers’ compliance with The Exchange’s Rules and Regulations as well as other relevant legislation; or (2) The Exchange’s collaboration with other regulatory organizations in ensuring the Issuers’ compliance with such organizations’ Rules or requirements; or (3) Ensuring generally acceptable behaviour in the securities market.
capital_market.plain: The Issuer shall comply with all NGX rules and provide any information requested by NGX or partner regulators.
capital_market.riskDescription: Failure to comply or provide timely information may result in penalties, reputational damage, or trading suspension.
capital_market.primaryControl: Compliance calendar, document repository, regulatory correspondence protocol

capital_market.title: Mandatory Use of Issuers’ Portal by all Issuers
capital_market.description: (a) Every Issuer shall utilize the Issuers’ Portal for the online submission to The Exchange of all information intended for release to the market in compliance with the Listings Rules, unless such information falls within an excluded category as The Exchange may in its sole discretion prescribe from time to time. (b) The Issuers’ Portal shall be the single gateway for filing all Periodic/Structured and Continuous disclosures. (c) Periodic/Structured Disclosures are all financial notifications including: (1) Financial Statements (Both Audited and Unaudited); (2) Earnings Forecast; and (3) Corporate Actions. (d) Continuous Disclosures are notifications of material information including: (1) Notice of Annual General Meeting, (2) Notice of Board Meeting, (3) Notice of Change of Auditors, (4) Notice of Change of Company Secretary, (5) Notice of Change of Name and Registered Address, (6) Notice of Change of Registrars, (7) Notice of Completion Board Meeting, (8) Notice of Court Ordered Meeting, (9) Notice of Directors Dealings, (10) Notice of Extra-Ordinary General Meeting, and (11) Notice of Resignation and Appointment of Directors.
capital_market.plain: Issuers shall submit all periodic and material disclosure documents through the NGX Issuers’ Portal as the only authorized platform.
capital_market.riskDescription: Failure to use the Portal may result in late disclosures, regulatory sanctions, or reputational damage.
capital_market.primaryControl: Use of NGX Issuers’ Portal, training, and compliance calendar
capital_market.additionalControl: Internal compliance audits and escalation framework

capital_market.source: Rulebook of the Nigerian Stock Exchange
capital_market.title: Accounting Standard
capital_market.description: "All Periodic/Structured Disclosure as set forth in Rule 18.2(c) above submitted via the Issuers’ Portal shall be prepared using the accounting policies and methods that comply with International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) and other accounting standards set forth by the Financial Reporting Council of Nigeria and contain the information required by The Exchange."
capital_market.plain: All periodic disclosures shall comply with IFRS and FRCN standards and meet NGX disclosure requirements.
capital_market.riskDescription: Use of non-compliant accounting standards may lead to inaccurate reporting, penalties, or loss of investor trust.
capital_market.primaryControl: Adoption of IFRS-compliant accounting policies and regular external audit reviews
capital_market.additionalControl: Periodic internal IFRS training and FRCN compliance checks

capital_market.source: Rulebook of the Nigerian Stock Exchange
capital_market.title: Notification and Communication with The Exchange via the Issuers’ Portal
capital_market.description: "(a) The only representatives of an Issuer authorized to use the Issuers’ Portal to submit information to The Exchange are the Company Secretary (and his or her designee) and the Chief Financial Officer of the Issuer. (b) Issuers that outsource the company secretarial function to a separate entity distinct from the Issuer shall designate one representative of such separate entity to The Exchange, which person shall act as the Company Secretary for the purposes of this rule no later than five (5) business days before the designee uses the Issuers’ Portal for the first time."
capital_market.plain: Only the Company Secretary (or designee) and CFO are allowed to use the Issuers’ Portal. If secretarial duties are outsourced, the designated representative shall be registered with NGX 5 days before using the Portal.
capital_market.riskDescription: Unauthorized individuals using the Portal may result in non-compliant submissions, data breaches, or regulatory sanctions.
capital_market.primaryControl: Role-based access controls; designation of authorized representatives
capital_market.additionalControl: Periodic review of user access and training

capital_market.source: Rulebook of the Nigerian Stock Exchange
capital_market.title: Issuer to Exercise Reasonable Care in Relation to any Submission
capital_market.description: "An Issuer is required to exercise all reasonable care to ensure that any information it submits via the Issuers’ Portal is accurate, not misleading, false or deceptive and does not omit any material facts likely to affect the import of such information."
capital_market.plain: The Issuer shall carefully review all information before submission to ensure it is true, complete, and not misleading.
capital_market.riskDescription: Inaccurate or misleading disclosure may result in regulatory sanctions, reputational damage, or legal liability.
capital_market.primaryControl: Internal review and approval process before submission

capital_market.source: Rulebook of the Nigerian Stock Exchange
capital_market.title: Requirements for Information Submitted via the Issuers’ Portal
capital_market.description: "All information submitted to The Exchange via the Issuers’ Portal must meet the following requirements: (a) The contents of the documents must comply with the minimum disclosures as set forth in the Appendix to this Chapter or as may be prescribed by The Exchange from time to time; (b) The portal will be available to Issuers to submit their documents at any time. However a document to be submitted by a specific date would be considered late if submitted after midnight. A document submitted during the official business hours of The Exchange which is 08.00 hours and 17.00 hours may be viewed by staff of The Exchange before it is released to the market; and (c) The information must be duly authenticated electronically by the authorized representatives of the Issuer."
capital_market.plain: Issuers shall ensure all submissions via the portal: (a) meet disclosure requirements, (b) are submitted on time, and (c) are electronically authenticated.
capital_market.riskDescription: Non-compliance could lead to delayed market disclosures, regulatory sanctions, or invalid filings.
capital_market.primaryControl: Internal disclosure checklist; submission calendar; authentication protocol

capital_market.source: Rulebook of the Nigerian Stock Exchange
capital_market.title: Financial Reporting (Periodic/Structured Disclosure)
capital_market.description: "No later than the close of business on the day after an Issuer submits any Periodic/Structured Disclosure as set forth in Rule 18.2(c) above to The Exchange via the Issuers’ Portal, it shall publish the same information on its corporate website and shall ensure that the information remains on its corporate website for a period of three (3) years from the date it is posted."
capital_market.plain: After submitting financial disclosures to the NGX, the Issuer shall publish the same on its corporate website by the next business day and keep it there for at least 3 years.

capital_market.source: Rulebook of the Nigerian Stock Exchange
capital_market.title: Sanctions for Breach of Issuers’ Portal Rules
capital_market.description: (a) In the event of any breach of the Issuers’ Portal Rules set forth in Rules 18.4 and 18.5 above, the Issuer shall be liable to pay a fine of fifty per-cent (50%) of its annual listing fee. (b) In the event of any breach of the Issuers’ Portal Rules set forth in Rules 18.8 and 18.9 above, the Issuer shall be liable to pay a fine of fifty per-cent (50%) of its annual listing fee. (c) If an Issuer fails to submit the information set forth in Rules 18.2(c) and 18.2(d) above via the Issuers’ Portal, the Issuer shall be liable to pay a fine of fifty per-cent (50%) of its annual listing fee. (d) The sanctions set forth in Paragraph 14 of Appendix III (General Undertaking) to the Listings Rules (Green Book) shall apply in regard to an Issuers’ use of the Issuers’ Portal.
capital_market.plain: Any failure to comply with portal rules or submission requirements will lead to a 50% annual listing fee fine, plus other applicable sanctions.
capital_market.primaryControl: Automated portal access controls, submission logs

capital_market.source: Rulebook of the Nigerian Stock Exchange
capital_market.title: Board Meetings
capital_market.description: (a) Every Issuer shall notify The Exchange within twenty-four (24) hours after the relevant board meeting or after receipt of any required approval from its primary regulator(s) of: (1) Its decision to make a drawing or redemption of any securities, intimating at the same time the date of the drawing, and in the case of a registered security, the period of the closing of the transfer books (or the date of the striking of the balance) for the drawing; (2) The amount of the security outstanding after any purchase or drawing has been made; (3) Any preliminary results for any year, half-year, quarter and the comparative figures in respect of profits before taxation and after taxation, including instances where it becomes necessary for qualification that the figures are provisional or unaudited; (4) Any dividend or bonus recommendation and other distributions to members including approvals for payment of declared dividends, Bonus issuance and or, Rights or scrip issues; (5) Short particulars of any proposed change in the capital structure, or redemption of securities; (b) Every Issuer shall notify The Exchange in writing of the date and time of its’ Board of Directors’ meeting at which recommendation of dividends, bonus or issuance of rights will be discussed, at least fourteen (14) days in advance

capital_market.source: Rulebook of the Nigerian Stock Exchange
capital_market.title: General Meetings of Members
capital_market.description: (a) Every Issuer shall hold sessions of the general meetings of shareholders or holders of other securities in accordance with the relevant provisions in the Companies and Allied Matters Act Cap C20 LFN (CAMA) and any other relevant legislation, these Rules and the Issuer’s Articles of Association. The Issuer shall also ensure that shareholders or holders of other securities are allowed to lawfully exercise their rights at the meetings. (b) The Annual General Meeting (“AGM”) provides shareholders or holders of other securities with the opportunity of questioning the Directors and Management on the accounts and reports, which are presented at the meeting and matters relating to the Issuer in general. Such questions shall - (1) be relevant to the Issuer or its business, (2) not result in the release of commercially or price sensitive information, or (3) not be obnoxious or vexatious.
capital_market.plain: Issuers shall hold shareholder and securities holders’ meetings in compliance with CAMA, NGX Rules, and their Articles, and must allow lawful participation.
capital_market.riskDescription: Failure to hold or properly conduct general meetings may lead to regulatory sanctions or shareholder disputes.
capital_market.primaryControl: Annual calendar for meetings; adherence to statutory and NGX timelines
capital_market.additionalControl: Shareholder engagement plan and legal advisory review

capital_market.source: Rulebook of the Nigerian Stock Exchange
capital_market.title: Notice of Meeting
capital_market.description: (a) The Board of Directors or Trustees of the Issuer shall give Notice of Meeting as provided in Rule 19.8(c) below, to each security holder to ensure that each security holder has a reasonable opportunity to attend the meeting and exercise his voting rights thereat. (b) The Notice shall state the nature of the meeting, time and venue and shall include a proxy form which shall include clearly worded resolution proposals in order that securities’ holders may be properly guided in casting their votes either for or against each resolution.
capital_market.plain: Issuers shall notify all security holders about meetings in a timely and clear manner, including resolutions and proxy forms.
capital_market.deadlineType: In advance of every general meeting (per CAMA & NGX)
capital_market.riskDescription: Inadequate or non-compliant meeting notices may result in invalid meetings or regulatory breaches.
capital_market.primaryControl: Compliance calendar; verified AGM/EGM notices; proxy resolution review
capital_market.additionalControl: Legal review before circulation of notices

capital_market.source: Rulebook of the Nigerian Stock Exchange
capital_market.title: Notice to be Displayed on the Website
capital_market.description: (a) Upon receiving the approval of The Exchange every Issuer shall immediately publish on its website the Notice of Meeting, circulars, annual reports, scheme document and other information memorandum that will be considered at the general meeting. (b) Upon request by shareholders or holders of other securities and where practicable, Issuers shall forward to the email addresses of shareholders or holders of other securities the soft copies of the approved documentation in addition to the hard copies which will be sent by post. Copies of such documentation shall also be published on the Issuer’s website. (c) Issuers shall ensure that the Notice of Meeting and the full copy of the Annual Reports or any other relevant documentation are dispatched to shareholders or holders of other securities and the relevant Regulatory authorities at least twenty-one (21) days before the date of the meeting and evidence of postage shall be made available for inspection by the Regulators at the meeting. Where the notice is personally delivered, evidence of such delivery shall be produced. Issuers shall allow at least five (5) business days for delivery of the Notice of Meeting if sent out by post from the day the letter containing same is posted.
capital_market.plain: Issuers shall publish meeting notices and relevant documents on their website after NGX approval, send soft copies to shareholders when requested, and ensure physical delivery of documents at least 21 days before the meeting.
capital_market.deadlineType: At least 21 days before any general meeting
capital_market.riskDescription: Failure to comply could result in shareholder disputes, regulatory penalties, or invalidated meetings.
capital_market.primaryControl: Use of automated mailing system, tracking of dispatch, website upload logs
capital_market.additionalControl: External verification and regulatory review

capital_market.source: Rulebook of the Nigerian Stock Exchange
capital_market.title: Venue of Meeting
capital_market.description: (a) General meetings shall be held within business hours at any venue that is reasonably accessible to shareholders or holders of other securities. (b) The venue of the meeting shall be easily accessible by all shareholders or holders of other securities including persons with physical disabilities.
capital_market.plain: General meetings shall be held during working hours at venues that are accessible to all shareholders, including those with physical disabilities.
capital_market.riskDescription: Inaccessible venues may prevent shareholder participation, lead to legal challenges, or regulatory sanctions.
capital_market.primaryControl: Venue selection checklist and stakeholder communication
capital_market.additionalControl: Pre-meeting accessibility assessment and feedback system

capital_market.title: Date of Meeting
capital_market.description: "No general meeting shall be held on a day declared by the Federal Government of Nigeria as a public holiday."
capital_market.plain: General meetings shall not be scheduled on public holidays declared by the Federal Government.
capital_market.riskDescription: Holding meetings on public holidays may invalidate resolutions or limit participation.

capital_market.source: Rulebook of the Nigerian Stock Exchange
capital_market.title: Right of Attendance
capital_market.description: "Notice of meetings shall be restricted to only those entitled to receive Notice of the Meeting in accordance with the provisions of Section 219 of CAMA. Any other attendee not being a person contemplated under Section 219 of CAMA shall be identified in an obvious manner as an observer and distinctly segregated as such."
capital_market.plain: Only those legally entitled under CAMA Section 219 should receive meeting notices; others must be treated strictly as observers.
capital_market.riskDescription: Unauthorized persons participating as members may invalidate meeting proceedings or raise governance issues.
capital_market.primaryControl: Verify attendees against the register of members and proxies
capital_market.additionalControl: Pre-registration and security badge system

capital_market.source: Rulebook of the Nigerian Stock Exchange
capital_market.title: Voting Procedure
capital_market.description: "(a) Voting at general meetings may be conducted through the use of an electronic voting device or by any other means prescribed by law. (b) Where an Issuer proposes to use an electronic voting device, no voting shall take place until proper arrangements have been made to allow all shareholders or holders of other securities in attendance to participate in the electronic voting and they have all been adequately instructed by the Registrars or the Issuer on how to operate the device."
capital_market.plain: Issuers may use electronic voting, but must ensure all attendees can participate and receive clear instructions on using the system.
capital_market.riskDescription: Improper voting procedures or lack of shareholder participation may lead to disputes or invalidate meeting outcomes.
capital_market.primaryControl: Testing of voting systems, shareholder guidance, registrar briefing

capital_market.source: Rulebook of the Nigerian Stock Exchange
capital_market.title: Announcements
capital_market.description: "Where an announcement is required to be made under these Rules, the party concerned shall satisfy that requirement by publishing such announcement in at least two (2) daily newspapers with nationwide circulation. capital_market.title: Sanctions
capital_market.description: "(a) Where an Issuer or any of its directors or any of the Trustees of a Bond contravene or fail to adhere to any of these provisions, The Exchange may censure the Issuer and/or the Issuer’s director(s) or the Trustees individually or jointly, either privately or in public. (b) In the event of breach of any of these Rules, The Exchange shall impose the following penalties: (1) A form of censure which it determines to be appropriate; and (2) A fine not exceeding fifty per-cent (50%) of the listing fees of the Issuer."

crmp.title: Designated categories of predicate offences
crmp.description: (1) Financial Institutions shall identify and file suspicious transaction reports to the NFIU, where funds, assets or property are suspected to have been derived from any, but not limited to, the following criminal activities— (a) participation in an organized criminal group and racketeering; (b) terrorism, including terrorism financing; (c) financing the proliferation of weapons of mass destruction; (d) trafficking in persons and migrant smugglings; (e) sexual exploitation, including sexual exploitation of children; (f) illicit trafficking in narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances; (g) illicit arms trafficking; (h) illicit trafficking in stolen and other goods; (i) corruption; (j) bribery; (k) fraud; (l) currency counterfeiting; (m) counterfeiting and piracy of products; (n) environmental crime; (o) murder; (p) grievous bodily injury; (q) kidnapping, illegal restraint and hostage-taking; (r) robbery or theft; (s) smuggling, including smuggling done in relation to customs and excise duties and taxes; (t) tax crimes, related to direct taxes and indirect taxes; (u) extortion; (v) forgery; (w) piracy; (y) insider trading and market manipulation; or (z) any other predicate offence under the MLPPA, TPPA, other relevant laws and regulations.

crmp.title: Targeted Financial Sanctions Related to Terrorism Financing and Proliferation Financing
crmp.description: (1)  Financial Institutions shall undertake targeted financial sanctions in relation to TP and PF as provided for under TPPA and Regulations. (2) Financial Institutions shall report to the NFIU any assets frozen, or actions taken in compliance with— (a) the prohibition requirements of the relevant United Nations Security Council Resolutions ('UNSCRs') on terrorism, financing of proliferation of weapons of mass destruction, any future successor resolutions; and (b) the TPPA and Regulations and any amendments that may be reflected by the competent authorities. (3) The reports in sub-regulation (2) of this regulation shall include all transactions involving attempted and concluded transactions in compliance with the MLPPA, TPPA and Regulations and any amendments that may be reflected by the competent authorities.
crmp.plain: The Bank shall: 1. Implement targeted financial sanctions related to terrorism financing (TF) and proliferation financing (PF) in line with the TPPA and applicable regulations. 2. Report to the NFIU any frozen assets or compliance actions taken under:  a. UN Security Council Resolutions (UNSCRs) on terrorism or proliferation of weapons of mass destruction.  b. TPPA, related regulations, and any amendments from competent authorities. 3. Include in such reports all related transactions—both attempted and completed—in line with TPPA, MLPPA, and applicable regulations.
crmp.riskDescription: Non-compliance with targeted financial sanctions may expose the Bank to regulatory penalties and reputational damage.
crmp.owner: Compliance Officer, AML/CFT/CPF Desk, Operations Head
crmp.primaryControl: - Sanctions screening against designated lists - System-based flagging of attempted or completed suspicious transactions - Prompt asset freezing mechanisms - Timely reporting to NFIU
