crmp.source: Guidance Note on Politically Exposed Persons (PEP)
crmp.title: Customer Due Diligence
crmp.description: 4.1 Financial Institutions (FIs) are expected to carry out Customer Due Diligence (CDD) measures proportionate to the risks posed by customers. When dealing with Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs), their family members, or known close associates, additional measures in the form of Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) are to be applied by the FIs to mitigate the higher Money Laundering/Terrorist Financing/Proliferation Financing (ML/TF/PF) risks. FIs are, however, not to turn away a prospective customer or close a business relationship simply on the basis that the customer, or beneficial owner, is a PEP (or a family member or person known to be their close associate).  4.2 When considering whether to establish or continue a business relationship with a PEP, the focus should be on the level of ML/TF/PF risk posed by the PEP, and whether the FI has adequate controls in place to mitigate such risks. This is to prevent the FI from being used for illicit purposes should the PEP be involved in criminal activities.  4.3 Once it has been established that a new or existing customer is a PEP, the FI should undertake a risk assessment to determine the level of risk posed by that customer and the proportionate levels of due diligence and monitoring required.  4.4 The FI should use its customer risk assessment policy/process, considering risk factors such as geography, product, business type, and delivery channel. For geographical risk, FIs should consider information available from reliable and independent sources as to the levels of systemic ML/TF risk in the country of political exposure.  4.5 When assessing the ML/TF/PF risk level of a relationship with a domestic/international organization PEP, FIs should take into account factors such as whether the PEP:  a) Has business interests related to his/her public functions (i.e., conflict of interest);  b) Is involved in public procurement processes; or holds several (related or unrelated) prominent public functions that may enable influence to be exerted at key decision-making processes.  c) Is from a country identified by the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) or others as having strategic AML/CFT/CPF regime deficiencies or is known to have a high level of corruption.  d) Holds a prominent public function in sectors exposed to higher corruption levels (e.g., oil and gas, mining, construction, natural resources, defense industries, sports, gaming, gambling).  e) Holds a prominent public function that could enable him/her to negatively impact the effective implementation of FATF Recommendations in his/her country.  4.6 For medium or low-risk domestic PEPs or international organization PEPs who are customers or beneficial owners, FIs must, at a minimum, apply the customer identification procedures.  4.7 Where a board member, senior management, or corporate officer of the following types of organizations is a PEP, an FI may be exposed to lower risk and may apply commensurate due diligence accordingly:  a) A publicly quoted company listed on a recognized exchange, subject to appropriate listing rules, good corporate governance, and transparent reporting.  b) Well-regulated organizations subject to independent supervision (e.g., banks and other FIs).  c) Private or state-owned organizations (including Central Banks, sovereign wealth funds), except those from designated high-risk countries, subject to good governance and transparent reporting.  4.8 For high-risk PEPs and foreign PEPs who are customers or beneficial owners, FIs must apply customer identification procedures for individuals and undertake Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD).  4.9 When assessing whether adequate controls are in place to mitigate the risk of doing business with a particular PEP, consideration should be given to the level, frequency, and extent of ongoing monitoring and (enhanced) due diligence required. FIs must ensure their systems are appropriate and efficient based on the risks posed.  4.10 Where a customer’s circumstances change, FIs must reassess the risk posed by that change, conduct EDD if the PEP is high-risk or foreign, and adjust transaction monitoring processes to account for the higher risk associated with the customer.
crmp.plain: The Bank shall: (1) Apply CDD proportional to the risk level of each customer. (2) Conduct Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) for PEPs, their close associates, or family members. (3) Not automatically reject or exit relationships solely due to PEP status. (4) Use a risk-based approach in establishing or continuing relationships with PEPs. (5) Undertake a risk assessment once PEP status is confirmed. (6) Apply customer risk assessment across geography, sector, product, delivery channels, and political exposure. (7) Apply full identification and EDD for high-risk or foreign PEPs. (8) Monitor transactions and customer behavior regularly and adjust controls when the customer's circumstances change.
crmp.riskDescription: Failure to identify and manage PEP risks may result in the bank being used for corruption, money laundering, or terrorist financing, attracting regulatory sanctions, reputational damage, and possible criminal liability.
crmp.owner: Compliance Officer, KYC Unit, Relationship Managers, Risk Management Team
crmp.primaryControl: - Conduct PEP screening at onboarding and periodically. - Use automated watchlists and questionnaires. - Perform EDD for high-risk/foreign PEPs. - Maintain a PEP Risk Register. - Monitor transactions linked to PEPs continuously. - Reassess risks when customer status or circumstances change.

crmp.source: Guidance Note on Politically Exposed Persons (PEP)
crmp.title: SOURCES OF INFORMATION FOR THE DETERMINATION OF PEPS, THEIR FAMILY MEMBERS & CLOSE ASSOCIATES
crmp.description: There are several sources of information that can be used by FIs in determining whether a customer is a PEP. In determining whether the customer or a beneficial owner is a PEP, FI may consider the following:  5.1. Periodic review of customer database FIs are required to ensure that CDD information is up-to-date as provided by the CBN AML/CFT/CPF Regulations. Existing customers may become PEPs after they enter a business relationship, so it is essential that FIs monitor non-PEP accounts for a change in the PEP status, customer profile or account activity and update customer information. Such ongoing monitoring should be on a risk basis.  5.2 conduct internet and media searches FIs may use the internet and media as sources of information for the determination, monitoring, verification of information in relation to PEPs, although it should be noted that such information may not be comprehensive or reliable.  5.3. conduct searches using commercial databases 5.3.1 There are a variety of commercial databases available which may assist in the detection of PEPs, FIs may acquire access to such databases. 5.3.2 The use of these databases should never replace traditional CDD processes as contained in the CBN AML/CFT/CPF Regulations 2022. 5.3.3 FIs using such databases as a support tool should ensure that they are fit for the purpose and are not simply outsourcing their risk assessment. 5.3.4 FIs should also determine whether the use of commercial databases, to confirm the information provided by the customer, is necessary. Prior to making use of any commercial databases, FIs should understand how commercial databases are populated and how these are able to detect and flag PEPs, family members and persons known to be close associates of PEPs.  5.4. create in-house databases and share information within financial groups or countries 5.4.1. FIs may choose to develop in-house databases as tools to assist in determining PEPs, and such database should be kept up-to-date. 5.4.2. In line with provisions of the CBN AML/CFT/CPF Regulations, Financial Groups are required to implement procedures for sharing information with the Group for AML/CFT/CPF purposes. In relation to foreign PEPs, it is best practice for institutions within Financial Groups to share information on PEPs for AML purposes.  5.5. customer questionnaire/self-declaration Information obtained directly from the customer may be obtained in response to questionnaires and/or on-boarding forms. FIs may develop questionnaires with specific reference to criteria that identify PEPs including family members and persons known to be close associates of the PEP. Such a questionnaire would be required to be completed and signed by the customer and the beneficial owner, where applicable. Information obtained directly from the customer may be obtained in response to the questionnaire and/or on-boarding form.  5.6 information sharing by competent authorities FIs may rely on the information shared by competent authorities which is helpful in determining whether a particular customer is a PEP or the PEP is trying to abuse the financial system (e.g., the level of corruption in the country, the level of income for certain types of positions, etcetera) or specific information about particular persons which would facilitate the detection of foreign PEPs. Both general information concerning the country from which a foreign PEP originates and more specific information (e.g., about particular persons) are useful tools for verifying CDD information.
crmp.plain: The Bank shall: 1. Periodically review its customer database to detect any status changes to PEPs. 2. Conduct internet and media searches to aid in identifying or verifying PEP information. 3. Use commercial databases for screening and detection but not as a substitute for CDD processes. 4. Maintain and update in-house PEP databases and share PEP-related information within the financial group. 5. Use self-declaration and customer questionnaires to detect PEPs and their close associates. 6. Rely on information from competent authorities, especially when identifying foreign PEPs and assessing country risk.
crmp.riskDescription: Inadequate identification of PEPs increases exposure to corruption, money laundering, and terrorist financing. Reliance on unreliable sources or failure to monitor PEP status may lead to non-compliance and regulatory sanctions.
crmp.owner: Compliance Officer, Customer Onboarding Team, AML Monitoring Unit, Relationship Managers
crmp.primaryControl: - Maintain an up-to-date PEP screening tool. - Conduct scheduled PEP status reviews. - Perform multi-source checks (internet, media, commercial databases, customer declarations, competent authority info). - Enable group-wide information sharing mechanisms. - Integrate PEP detection questions into onboarding forms.

crmp.source: Guidance Note on Politically Exposed Persons (PEP)
crmp.title: RISK MANAGEMENT SYSTEM
crmp.description: FIs should in addition to performing CDD measures, establish appropriate risk management systems to determine whether a potential customer or existing customer or the beneficial owner is a PEP.  6.1 PEPs Screening The conduct of PEP screening in each FI will depend on the size and complexity of each institution and the inherent risk of PEPs using the FI’s products and services to launder the proceeds of crime. FI should conduct onboarding screening and ongoing screening on all customers. Where appropriate, PEP screening should be automated. However, manual screening may be acceptable depending on the size of the institution and the materiality of the inherent risk posed by PEPs. PEP screening should be carried out in accordance with FI’s risk appetite while applying RBA and take place at least: a) During onboarding process; b) at periodic customer review; c) when there is a trigger event which warrants a customer due diligence review. d) Upon notification/tip-off from reliable sources. It should be noted that, in many instances, PEP screening is not the primary control for identifying PEPs.  6.2 Customer Risk Assessment 6.2.1 FIs should understand their customer’s risk profiles in order to apply appropriate procedures and processes to manage and mitigate risk. FIs should be consistent with a risk-based approach, the level and type of CDD should be commensurate with the risks presented by the customer relationship. 6.2.2 FIs must have appropriate risk-based procedures for conducting ongoing CDD to understand the nature and purpose of customer relationships, and to develop a customer risk profile. It must be consistent with a risk-based approach for conducting ongoing CDD, FI should obtain more customer information for those customers with higher risk profile and ensure ongoing monitoring. 6.2.3 The information collected to create a customer risk profile should also assist FIs in conducting ongoing monitoring to identify and report suspicious transactions and activity. Furthermore, conducting appropriate level of ongoing CDD commensurate with the customer’s risk profile will assist the FI in determining whether a customer’s transactions or activities are suspicious. 6.2.4 Based on the customer risk profile, the FI may consider obtaining, at account opening (and throughout the relationship), more customer information and updates in order to understand the nature and purpose of the customer relationship. 6.2.5 The following information may be useful to FI in understanding the nature and purpose of the customer relationship and in determining the ML/TF/PF and other illicit financial activity risk profile of its identified PEP customers: a) The type of products and services used. b) The volume and nature of transactions. c) Geographies associated with the customer’s activity and domicile. d) The customer’s official government responsibilities. e) The level and nature of the customer’s authority or influence over government activities or officials. f) The customer’s access to significant government assets or funds. 6.2.6 FIs may leverage existing processes for assessing geographically specific ML/TF/PF and other illicit financial activity risks when developing the customer risk profile. Existing processes may also take into account the legal and enforcement frameworks, including ethical reporting and oversight requirements. 6.2.7 When developing customer risk profiles and determining when to collect additional customer information, and what to collect, FIs may take into account such factors as the customer’s public office or position of public trust (or that of the customer’s family members or close associates), as well as any indication that the identified PEP misuses or might misuse his or her authority or influence for personal gain.  6.3 Approval For Relationship With PEP FIs are required to obtain senior management approval for establishing (or continuing, for existing customers) business relationships with PEPs as provided by the CBN AML/CFT/CPF Regulations.  6.4 Enhanced Monitoring For PEP Relationships/Accounts Higher risk PEPs require enhanced ongoing monitoring of the business relationship. FIs should implement electronic and/or manual monitoring systems to constantly monitor the business relationship and detect unusual and potential suspicious transactions and activities. This process should include: a) Understanding and documenting the circumstances that warrant the classification of the customer as a PEP (such as the title or position and country in which the PEP holds/held political exposure and duration of appointment). If the individual customer is a close family member or close associate, the relationship of the person to the PEP must be documented. b) Understanding and documenting the nature and intended purpose of the relationship/account, the source of the initial funds (where appropriate) and the anticipated levels of account activity. c) Understanding and documenting the customer’s source of funds and source of wealth (e.g. salary and compensation from official duties and wealth derived from other sources). d) When the due diligence on an immediate family member or close associate of a PEP indicates that the source of funds originates from the PEP, the FI should determine and document the PEP’s sources of funds and wealth. e) Conduct searches including internet and media searches to screen customers for adverse reports/news.
crmp.plain: The Bank shall: 6.1 – PEP Screening: - Conduct PEP screening during onboarding, at periodic reviews, upon trigger events or tip-offs. - Choose manual or automated screening based on institution size and PEP risk.  6.2 – Customer Risk Assessment: - Build risk profiles using CDD info. - Apply risk-based approach to determine level of due diligence. - Collect more data for higher-risk customers.  6.3 – Approval for PEP Relationships: - Obtain senior management approval before entering/continuing a business relationship with a PEP.  6.4 – Enhanced Monitoring: - Conduct enhanced ongoing monitoring of higher-risk PEPs. - Document source of funds, wealth, political exposure, and perform adverse media searches.
crmp.riskDescription: Failure to detect or monitor PEPs may expose the bank to ML/TF/PF risks, reputational damage, and regulatory sanctions.
crmp.owner: Compliance Officer, Risk Management Unit, Relationship Managers, IT (screening systems)
crmp.primaryControl: - Implement automated/manual PEP screening systems. - Use customer questionnaires and onboarding checks. - Maintain a structured customer risk profiling process. - Require senior management approval for all PEPs. - Monitor PEP accounts regularly using risk triggers.

crmp.source: Guidance Note on Politically Exposed Persons (PEP)
crmp.title: RISK MANAGEMENT SYSTEM
crmp.description: 6.5 Time Limit For PEP Status It is often stated that once a PEP will always remain a PEP, however the handling of a client who is no longer entrusted with a prominent public function should be based on an assessment of risk and not on prescribed time limits. The risk-based approach requires that FIs assess the ML/TF risk of a PEP who is no longer entrusted with a prominent public function or has lost such power and influence (such as the case of deceased) and take effective action to mitigate this risk. However, where the corruption risk remains even if a PEP has been out of office for a certain time, the FI may continue to treat a customer as a PEP. Possible factors to consider in determining whether the customer is no longer a PEP include:  the level of (formal and informal) influence or control that the individual could still exercise; the seniority of the position that the individual held as a PEP; or whether the individual’s previous and current function are linked in any way (e.g., formally by appointment of the PEPs successor, or informally by the fact that the PEP continues to deal with the same substantive matters);  the corruption risks or links to any industries that are high risk for corruption; and  How politically connected they remain once they have left office.
crmp.plain: The Bank shall:  1.Not automatically stop treating someone as a Politically Exposed Person (PEP) just because they’ve left public office.  2.Assess the customer’s risk level based on their current influence, past position, and possible links to corruption or high-risk industries.  3.Continue to treat a former PEP as high-risk if they still have power, connections, or are involved in related business matters.  4.Use a risk-based approach to decide whether the person still poses a money laundering or terrorism financing risk, instead of relying on fixed timelines.
crmp.riskDescription: If the Bank automatically removes a former PEP from enhanced monitoring without a proper risk assessment, it may overlook ongoing corruption risks. This could expose the Bank to money laundering, reputational damage, regulatory breaches, and penalties. Continued influence or industry ties may still pose high-risk factors.
crmp.owner: Compliance Officer, Risk Management Unit, Relationship Managers, IT (screening systems)
crmp.primaryControl: - Implement automated/manual PEP screening systems. - Use customer questionnaires and onboarding checks. - Maintain a structured customer risk profiling process. - Require senior management approval for all PEPs. - Monitor PEP accounts regularly using risk triggers.

crmp.source: Guidance Note on Politically Exposed Persons (PEP)
crmp.title: PEPs AS BENEFICIAL OWNERS
crmp.description: When conducting CDD, FIs are required to identify the beneficial owner and take reasonable measures to verify the identity of the beneficial owner. If there are reasonable grounds to believe that a beneficial owner is a PEP EDD shall be mandatory.
crmp.plain: When conducting Customer Due Diligence (CDD), the Bank shall: - Identify and verify the identity of all beneficial owners. - If there is reasonable ground to believe that the beneficial owner is a PEP, the bank must apply Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD).
crmp.riskDescription: Failure to identify PEPs as beneficial owners may result in undetected exposure to ML/TF/PF risks, reputational harm, regulatory penalties, and misuse of the financial system.
crmp.owner: Compliance Officer, Customer Onboarding Unit, KYC/CDD Unit
crmp.primaryControl: - Mandatory verification of all beneficial owners. - Risk-based screening to flag PEPs among beneficial owners. - Automated checks against internal and external PEP lists. - Escalation for EDD if beneficial owner is a PEP.

crmp.source: Guidance Note on Politically Exposed Persons (PEP)
crmp.title: DOMESTIC/INTERNATIONAL ORGANISATION PEPS WHEN NOT HIGHER RISK
crmp.description: When the risk assessment established that the business relationship with a domestic/international organization PEP does not present a higher risk, the PEP in question can be treated like any other normal customer, i.e. the FI should apply normal customer due diligence measures and monitoring as required under the CBN-AML/CFT/CPF Regulations.
crmp.plain: When a PEP is assessed not to pose a higher risk, the bank must treat them as a normal customer, applying standard CDD and ongoing monitoring in line with the CBN AML/CFT/CPF Regulations.
crmp.riskDescription: Misclassification of a low-risk PEP who later engages in illicit activity may result in regulatory scrutiny or reputational damage due to perceived negligence in risk categorization.
crmp.owner: Compliance Officer, Customer Due Diligence (CDD) Team
crmp.primaryControl: - Perform risk assessments to determine the correct PEP risk level. - Apply standard CDD measures for low/medium-risk PEPs. - Document justification for risk classification. - Ensure consistent application of procedures across branches.

crmp.source: Guidance Note on Politically Exposed Persons (PEP)
crmp.title: PERIODIC REVIEW FOR PEP CUSTOMERS
crmp.description: 9.1 CDD should continue after establishing a relationship with the customer. On a regular basis, transactions and account activities should be monitored and scrutinized for ML/TF/PF risks. The behavior of the customer, transactions and accounts should be in line with the expected level of activity. Ongoing monitoring is crucial as a customer risk profile may change over time. 9.2 PEP accounts should be subject to periodic reviews as may be determined by the FI in line with risk assessment. Frequency of the periodic reviews should be determined by the risk of the customer and documented appropriately. FIs should also review their PEP database frequently.
crmp.plain: The Bank shall conduct ongoing monitoring and periodic reviews of PEP accounts based on their risk level. The frequency and depth of the reviews must align with the risk assessment, and any changes in customer behavior or risk profile must be addressed.
crmp.riskDescription: Failure to perform ongoing or risk-based reviews of PEP accounts could result in undetected ML/TF/PF activities, leading to regulatory penalties and reputational damage.
crmp.owner: Compliance Officer, Relationship Managers, Risk Management Team
crmp.primaryControl: - Establish a risk-based schedule for reviewing PEP accounts. - Update PEP risk profiles periodically. - Flag and investigate deviations in expected account behavior. - Review PEP database regularly to capture status changes.

crmp.title: Record Keeping
crmp.description: Financial Institutions (FIs) should ensure that the records maintained are as provided in extant laws and Regulations. The records should be readily available in a timely and appropriate format to competent authorities upon request.
crmp.plain: The Bank shall maintain records in line with existing AML/CFT laws and regulations. These records must be easily retrievable and available promptly in a proper format when requested.
crmp.riskDescription: - Inability to provide records promptly may result in regulatory penalties, loss of critical evidence, investigation delays, and non-compliance with AML/CFT laws.
crmp.owner: - Chief Compliance Officer (CCO)- Records & Information Management Unit- IT/Database Administrators
crmp.primaryControl: - Centralized digital archiving system- Documented Record Retention Policy- Access control logs- Retrieval SLA for regulatory data requests

crmp.title: Reporting
crmp.description: 11.1 FIs should closely monitor the transactions of all foreign PEPs and high-risk domestic or international organization PEPs. If there is a suspicion that a transaction involves funds linked to any form of criminal activity, a Suspicious Transaction/Activity Report (STR) must be filed with the Nigerian Financial Intelligence Unit (NFIU).

crmp.source: Guidance Note on Politically Exposed Persons (PEP)
crmp.title: Training and Education
crmp.description: AML/CFT/CPF training policies of FIs should include ongoing employee training programmes. These training programmes need to address effective ways of determining whether clients are PEPs, and understanding, assessing and handling the potential risks associated with PEPs. Training should also incorporate real-life case studies and examples to make it up to date. Emphasis should be placed on human input and analysis from experienced and trained employees rather than on automated software programmed for detecting and handling the risks associated with PEPs.
crmp.plain: The Bank shall implement ongoing AML/CFT/CPF training for all employees. Training must include how to identify PEPs, assess related risks, and handle such risks effectively. It should include real-life case studies and emphasize human judgment alongside system automation.
crmp.riskDescription: Inadequate training may result in failure to detect PEPs, missed STRs, and regulatory non-compliance, potentially leading to fines, sanctions, or reputational damage.
crmp.owner: Human Resources (Training), Compliance Officer, Departmental Heads
crmp.primaryControl: - Develop a structured AML/CFT/CPF training plan. - Include PEP risk handling modules. - Use case-based learning. - Mandate periodic assessments to ensure knowledge retention.

crmp.source: Guidelines on Targeted Financial Sanctions Related to Terrorism and Terrorism Financing
crmp.title: Screening
crmp.description: FIs are required to carry out regular and ongoing screening against the latest updates of Sanction Lists prior to conducting any transaction or undertaking any financial Services to ascertain whether or not the name of such a person or entity is on the Lists. Specifically, screening should be conducted during the following:  a) Onboarding a new customer; b) Facilitating an occasional transaction; c) Establishing any relationship with any person or entity; d) Before carrying out any transaction; and e) Upon review of Know Your Customer (KYC) or changes to a customer’s information.  Screening must be conducted immediately and without delay to ensure compliance with implementing freezing measures without delay (within 24 hours). FIs are required to screen their entire customer base to prevent dissipation of funds of the designated persons or entities.  FIs (including those operating in free trade zones) must constantly screen their customers, potential customers, beneficial owners, and transactions to identify possible matches to the UN Consolidated Lists.  4.2.1 Screening of Customers – Related and Third Parties FIs shall undertake further screening and analysis on designated persons or entities whose properties or accounts are jointly owned and/or indirectly controlled by the designated persons or entities.  FIs shall conduct further CDD on parties related to frozen accounts including checking on the control and conduct of the frozen accounts and other related or third parties accounts connected to designated persons or entities.  The requirements for CDD on legal persons and legal arrangements and beneficial owners in the respective provisions under the CBN AML/CFT/CPF Regulations and Guidelines should be applied in determining the funds are directly or indirectly owned or controlled.  FIs are also advised to screen the names of the beneficiary of wire transfers and make an assessment whether such transaction should be blocked or rejected.  FIs are also advised to search, examine and analyse past financial activities of the designated persons or entities, related or third parties.  4.2.2 Confirmed Match A confirmed match is when an individual, entity, or group matches all the key identifiers published on the Sanctions Lists. The range of information that constitute identifiers of designated individuals, entities, or groups are as follows:  For natural person:  ✓ Name  ✓ Aliases/also known as/formerly known as  ✓ Date of birth  ✓ Nationality  ✓ ID or passport information  ✓ Last known address  For legal persons:  ✓ Name(s)  ✓ Aliases also known as/formerly known as  ✓ Certificate of Registration (RC No.)  ✓ Registered Address  ✓ Address of branches  ✓ Other information  Where the individual, entity, or group matches all the key identifiers published on the Sanctions Lists, the result is considered a ‘confirmed match’. In case the confirmed match is an existing customer, FIs are required to immediately, identify and freeze, without delay and without prior notice, all funds and assets owned or controlled by the designated person or entity in their possession.  Where the confirmed match is a potential customer, the FIs are required to reject the transaction immediately and report to the NSC. However, before rejecting the transaction, FIs are required to search their records to confirm whether the potential customer is a BO and where the search is positive, FIs are required to immediately identify and freeze, without delay and without prior notice, all funds and assets owned or controlled by the BO in their possession.  In cases of confirmed matches (for either existing or potential customer and closed/dormant relationships), FIs are required to report to the NSC, within 24 hours, any assets frozen or actions taken in compliance with the prohibition requirements of the relevant UNSCRs including attempted transactions.  In addition, FIs are required to immediately file STR to the NFIU, including all cases of name matching in financial transactions prior to or after publication or update of the lists for further analysis.  4.2.3 False Positive A false positive is a potential match to listed individuals, entities, or groups, either due to the common nature of the name or due to ambiguous identifying data, which on examination proves not to be a confirmed match.  FIs are required to obtain additional information and identification documents from the customer or a third party to ascertain whether a customer is a designated person or entity in the case of similar names.  FIs are required to forward queries to NSC to ascertain whether or not the customer is a designated person or entity in the case of similar names. Any query submitted to NSC is to be accompanied by additional information, copies of identification documents and the FIs assessments.  Where FIs are satisfied that the customer (potential or BO) is not a designated individual, entity, or group, i.e. a ‘False Positive Result’, FIs do not need to implement any TFS measures. FIs may allow the transaction or business to continue its normal course, and are required to maintain evidence of this process in their records.  Where FIs’ customers feel that their accounts have been mistakenly frozen or transactions have been mistakenly rejected or blocked, the FIs may advise their customers to contact the NSC to verify the false positive match. The contact details for the NSC in relation to TFS on TF is: https://nigsac.gov.ng/  4.2.4 Potential Match A potential match is when there is a partial match between identifiers in the Sanctions Lists with any information in FIs databases, and the FIs are unable to conclude a false positive or a confirmed match.  Due to prevalence of some names, FIs may find various potential matches. However, it does not necessarily mean that the individual, entity, or group they are dealing with is subject to TFS. FIs are required to cross-check their customers’ database with the identifiers published on the Sanctions Lists when identifying the potential match, by taking into consideration their knowledge of the customer (potential and BO) or transaction, through CDD and/or other sources of information.  Where FIs are unable to internally verify whether the ‘potential match’ is a false positive result or a confirmed match, they transaction should be suspended and the case reported to the NSC. The reported transaction should remain suspended until a response is received on the status of the potential match.
crmp.plain: The Bank shall screen all customers, beneficial owners, and transactions against updated sanction lists before any financial service or transaction. This must happen during onboarding, transactions, changes in customer data, and periodically. If a match is found, funds must be frozen immediately and NSC and NFIU notified. False positives and potential matches must be investigated and verified before action.
crmp.riskDescription: Failure to conduct proper and timely screening can lead to dealing with sanctioned individuals or entities, resulting in regulatory penalties and reputational damage.
crmp.primaryControl: Automated sanction screening tools; real-time transaction screening; trained compliance team; periodic full customer base screening; documented procedures for potential and confirmed matches.

points.text: Screening of Customers – Related and Third Parties FIs shall undertake further screening and analysis on designated persons or entities whose properties or accounts are jointly owned and/or indirectly controlled by the designated persons or entities. crmp.title: Application of targeted financial sanctions
crmp.description: FIs are required to immediately implement TFS by identifying and freezing, without delay and without prior notice, all funds and assets owned or controlled by the designated person or entity in their possession.  The following are the TFS measures that must be implemented if a match with the Sanctions Lists is identified.  i. Freeze all funds or other assets without delay: freeze without delay (immediately or in any case within 24 hours) and without prior notice to the designated individual, entity, or group, all the funds or other assets: a) Owned or controlled, wholly or jointly, directly, or indirectly, by an individual, entity, or group designated in the Sanctions Lists; b) Derived or generated from funds or other assets under item (a); or c) Any individual or entity acting on behalf of or at the direction of any designated individual, entity, or group.  ii. Prohibition of making funds or other assets or services available: FIs are prohibited from providing funds or other assets to or rendering financial services or other services related to, whether in whole or in part, directly or indirectly, or for the benefit of any designated individual, entity, or group on the Sanctions Lists.
crmp.plain: The Bank shall freeze all funds and assets of designated persons or entities immediately (within 24 hours) and without giving notice. They must not provide funds, services, or access to assets—directly or indirectly—to anyone on the Sanctions List.
crmp.riskDescription: Delay or failure to freeze assets or continuing business with designated individuals or entities may result in regulatory sanctions, criminal liability, or reputational damage.

crmp.primaryControl: Real-time sanctions screening system; immediate transaction freeze protocols; periodic staff training; access to updated Sanctions Lists; defined escalation procedures.

crmp.title: Categories of Funds Subject to Freezing Obligations
crmp.description: All types of funds or other assets are subject to freezing measures. The funds or other assets that can be subject to freezing measure includes the following:  i. Cash, cheques, claims on money, drafts, money orders, bearer instruments, internet-based and other electronic or digital payment instruments, including virtual currencies.  ii. Deposits with FIs or other entities and balances on accounts, including but not limited to: fixed or term deposit accounts, balances on share trading accounts with banks, or other investment trading accounts.  iii. Debts and debt obligations, including trade debts.  iv. Other accounts receivable, notes receivable, and other claims of money on others.  v. Other financial interest in a sole trader or partnership.  vi. Publicly and privately traded securities and debt instruments, including stocks and shares, certificates representing securities, bonds, notes, warrants, debentures, and derivatives contracts.  vii. Interest, dividends, or other income on or value accruing from or generated by assets.  viii. Credit, right of set-off, guarantees, performance bonds or other financial commitments.  ix. crmp.description: The freezing measures, including the prohibition of making funds available, apply to:  a) Any individual, group, or entity listed in the Sanctions Lists.  b) Any entity directly or indirectly owned or controlled by an individual or entity listed under (a).  c) Any individual or entity acting on behalf of or at the direction of any individual or Entity listed under (a) and (b).

crmp.title: Approval for usage of frozen funds by designated persons and entities on the UN List
crmp.description: FIs may advise customer or related party of the frozen accounts, blocked or rejected transactions to submit any query or appeal for variation to the frozen accounts, delisting or any other matters to the NSC.  The NSC, where necessary, may approve the utilization of frozen funds, assets or any part thereof:  a) to meet the basic needs and expenses of a designated person or entity a person or an entity whose funds have been frozen including the amounts required to meet expenditures on food, medical needs and such other general expenses;  b) for reasonable professional fees and settlement of expenses, including legal services, bank and related charges; or  c) for any other exceptional expenses that the NSC is of the view are permitted expenses in accordance with procedures under UNSCR 1373 and all successor resolutions.  Upon approval of the utilization of the frozen funds, FIs that are in custody of frozen funds are required to, upon receipt of a written directive by the NSC, implement the approval and furnish a report to the NSC of the action taken.

crmp.riskDescription: Misuse of frozen funds or acting without NSC approval may lead to violation of TFS obligations and international sanctions.

crmp.title: Reporting Requirements
crmp.description: 4.8.1 Filing suspicious transaction with NFIU i. Where FI is required to file STR to the NFIU, the report should state: (a) the information or other matter on which knowledge or suspicion is based; (b) any information it holds about the person by knowledge of which the person can be identified; and (c) the nature and amount of funds held by the FI for the person at any time up to 5 years prior to the designation being made.  4.8.2 Attempted transaction FIs are to report as suspicious transaction to NFIU any attempted transaction undertaken by designated persons or entities or related parties in the case of joint accounts. This may include any transaction that is subsequently rejected or blocked, incomplete in the event of failure to satisfactorily complete CDD and attempt for redemption of assets where repayment has been fulfilled.
crmp.plain: The Bank shall file Suspicious Transaction Reports (STRs) to the Nigerian Financial Intelligence Unit (NFIU) in the following situations:  1. Filing STR The STR should include: - The information or matter that triggered the suspicion. - Any identifiable information about the designated person/entity. - The nature and amount of funds held (even historically, up to 5 years before the designation).  2. Attempted Transactions They must report as STR: - Any attempted transactions by designated persons or related parties. - Transactions that were rejected, blocked, or incomplete due to failed CDD. - Any redemption attempts after payment fulfillment.
crmp.riskDescription: Failure to properly detect or report transactions (actual or attempted) by designated persons or entities may expose the FI to legal penalties, reputational damage, or indirect facilitation of terrorism financing.
crmp.owner: - Chief Compliance Officer - AML Reporting Officer - Transaction Monitoring Team
crmp.primaryControl: - Automated alert systems for name matching.  - Detailed STR templates capturing historical fund relationships.  - Block or reject functionality built into transaction systems.  - Clear workflow for reporting attempted transactions. - Secure reporting line to NFIU with internal escalation protocols.

crmp.source: Guidelines on Targeted Financial Sanctions Related to Terrorism and Terrorism Financing
crmp.title: Additional Obligations for Fis
crmp.description: In addition to alerts of updates received from the NSC upon subscription by FIs, the CBN may also issue notifications of TFS to FIs.  FIs shall on receipt of the notification from the CBN: i. immediately take steps to identify any funds, assets or any economic resources in their possession belonging to designated persons or entities and carry out freezing obligations in respect of PF as contained in the TPPA, 2022, and report to the NSC. ii. immediately file STR to the NFIU for further analysis on the financial activities of such an individual or entity; and iii. report, as STR to the NFIU, all cases of name matching in financial transactions prior to or after receipt of the Sanctions List.  For the purposes of this section, “immediately” means not later than 24 hours. In addition to the above, FIs are required to fulfill the following obligations: i. Cooperate with the NSC in verifying the accuracy of the submitted information. ii. Implement the freezing, cancellation, or lifting decision, when appropriate, without delay. iii. Cooperate with competent authorities to provide information on TFS timeously when required. iv. Set and implement policies, procedures, and internal controls to: a) Ensure conduct of customer due diligence b) Ensure trade finance is integrated into compliance procedure (including the identification of final destination of goods and services) c) Ensure compliance with the obligations imposed by the TPPA and TFS Regulations. d) Conduct ongoing TFS training and awareness sessions to Board, senior management and employees. e) Prohibit staff from, directly or indirectly, informing the customer or any third party that freezing actions or any other measures will be implemented. f) Ensure appropriate resources are allocated to meet the obligations of implementing TFS.  It shall be the responsibility of all FIs, to monitor their accounts and transactions against the UN Consolidated List and Nigeria List.
crmp.plain: The Bank shall: i. Act immediately (within 24 hours) on CBN notifications to freeze assets of designated individuals/entities per TPPA 2022 and report to NSC. ii. File Suspicious Transaction Reports (STRs) to NFIU on such individuals/entities and name-matching cases. iii. Cooperate with NSC in verifying information accuracy and implementing freeze/lift decisions. iv. Set and enforce internal policies to: - Conduct effective CDD - Integrate trade finance into TFS compliance - Implement TFS Regulations - Train staff at all levels - Prevent tipping-off - Allocate adequate resources v. Continuously screen accounts and transactions against the UN and Nigeria Sanctions Lists.
crmp.riskDescription: Failure to comply may result in regulatory penalties, facilitation of terrorism financing, legal liabilities, asset forfeiture, and reputational damage.
crmp.owner: Chief Compliance Officer, Sanctions/AML Compliance Team, IT/Security Teams, Operations
crmp.primaryControl: - Real-time automated screening system for name matching and sanctions alerts. - Immediate escalation and freezing protocols. - TFS Compliance Manual outlining procedures for CDD, trade finance compliance, and escalation. - Staff training on handling TFS alerts and reporting requirements.

crmp.title: Record Keeping
crmp.description: FIs are required to keep record of all actions taken in respect of TFS and should be kept in an easily retrievable manner.
crmp.plain: The Bank shall keep clear and easily accessible records of all actions taken regarding TFS.

crmp.source: Anti-Money Laundering/Combating the Financing of Terrorism (AML/CFT) Policy and Procedure Manual
crmp.title: Relevant to CBN - Remove
Freezing order in respect of designated persons or entities
crmp.description: (1) Upon the publication of the UN Consolidated List of persons and entities designated by the UN in accordance with UNSCR 1267(1999) and its successor resolutions, and the Nigeria Sanctions List, all natural and legal persons in Nigeria, including financial institutions, designated non-financial business and professions, and other entities in Nigeria shall— (a) immediately, identify and freeze, without prior notice, all funds, assets, and any other economic resources belonging to the designated person or entity in their possession and report same to the Sanctions Committee; (b) report to the Sanctions Committee any assets frozen or actions taken in compliance with the prohibition requirements of the relevant UNSCRs, including attempted transactions; (c) immediately file a Suspicious Transactions Report to the NFIU for further analysis on the financial activities of such an individual or entity; and (d) report as a Suspicious Transactions Report to the NFIU, all cases of name matching in financial transactions prior to or after receipt of the Nigerian Sanctions List.  (2) The freezing obligation under subsection (1), shall extend to— (a) all funds or other assets that are owned or controlled by the designated person or entity, and not just those that can be tied to a particular act, plot, or threat of terrorism or terrorism financing; (b) those funds or other assets that are wholly or jointly owned or controlled, directly or indirectly, by designated persons or entities; (c) the funds or other assets derived or generated from funds or other assets owned or controlled directly or indirectly by designated persons or entities; and (d) funds or other assets of persons and entities acting on behalf of, or at the direction of designated persons or entities.
crmp.plain: The Bank shall: i. Immediately identify and freeze—without prior notice—any funds, assets, or resources belonging to persons/entities on the UN Consolidated List or Nigeria Sanctions List. ii Report freezing actions and attempted transactions to the Sanctions Committee. iii File Suspicious Transaction Reports (STRs) with the NFIU concerning:  (a) frozen assets;  (b) actions taken;  (c) name matches in financial transactions. iv. Apply freezing orders to:  - All assets owned or controlled by designated persons/entities (fully or jointly),  - Assets derived from their funds,  - Assets controlled on behalf of, or under direction of, designated persons/entities.
crmp.riskDescription: Failing to freeze or report terrorist-related assets could: - Result in legal liability and regulatory sanctions; - Lead to association with terrorism financing; - Cause reputational and financial losses; - Trigger international blacklisting and derisking by correspondent banks.
crmp.owner: Chief Compliance Officer, Head of Sanctions Desk, AML/CFT Officer
crmp.primaryControl: - Real-time automated name screening against UN/Nigeria Sanctions Lists - Daily updates of sanctions watchlists - Policy for immediate account freezing and escalation - STR reporting system integrated with sanctions alerts

crmp.title: Confiscated and Forfeited Assets Account
crmp.description: All forfeited funds, and funds realized from the proceeds of sale, management, or other forms of disposal of seized, attached and forfeited assets under this Act and vested in the Federal Government shall be paid into the Confiscated and Forfeited Assets Account established under any enactment dealing with the proceeds of crime.
crmp.plain: The bank must: 1. Ensure that all forfeited funds and funds from the sale, management, or disposal of seized or forfeited assets (when handled or received) are paid into the Confiscated and Forfeited Assets Account established under relevant proceeds of crime laws. 2. Ensure no diversion or misplacement of such funds.
crmp.riskDescription: - Mismanagement or failure to remit forfeited assets may result in regulatory sanctions and loss of banking license. - Legal liability for non-compliance with asset forfeiture handling regulations. - Reputational risk linked to mishandling proceeds of crime.

crmp.title: Obligation to develop counter-financing of terrorism programmes and strategies
crmp.description: (1) Subject to the provisions of the Money Laundering (Prohibition) Act, all financial institutions and designated non-financial institutions shall— (a) develop and implement programmes and strategies for combating the financing of terrorism; and (b) keep a record of any complex, unusual large and unusual pattern of transaction, which has no apparent economic or visible lawful source or purpose.  (2) A report detailing all the parties involved in such transactions shall be kept and made available on request by the relevant agency.
crmp.plain: The Bank shall:  - Develop and implement programmes and strategies specifically designed to combat terrorism financing (CFT). - Maintain comprehensive records of complex, unusually large, or suspicious patterns of transactions without a lawful source. - Keep detailed reports of all parties involved in such transactions and provide them to relevant authorities upon request.
crmp.riskDescription: - Inability to detect and prevent terrorism financing. - Regulatory and criminal liability for aiding terrorism financing unknowingly. - Reputational damage and possible license revocation.
crmp.owner: Chief Compliance Officer, MLRO, Risk Management Department
crmp.primaryControl: - Establish robust CFT policies and frameworks. - Conduct ongoing risk assessments to detect unusual patterns. - Deploy automated transaction monitoring systems to flag suspicious activities. - Escalate and investigate flagged transactions.

crmp.title: Obligation to report suspicious transactions
crmp.description: (1) Subject to the provisions of the Money Laundering (Prohibition) Act, a financial institution or designated non-financial institution shall, within 24 hours, forward reports of suspicious transactions relating to terrorism or terrorism financing, or proliferation financing to the NFIU, which shall immediately process and forward the information to the relevant agency, where there are sufficient reasons to suspect that the funds— (a) are derived from legal or illegal sources, and are intended to be used for an act of terrorism or terrorism financing, or proliferation financing; (b) are proceeds of a crime related to terrorism or terrorism financing, or proliferation financing; or (c) belong to a person, entity or organisation considered as terrorist.  (3) A breach of the provisions of this section is an offence under this Act, and is liable on conviction to— (a) in the case of a director, chief compliance officers, or other employees— (i) imprisonment for a term of not more than five years, (ii) a fine of at least N5,000,000, or (iii) both fine and imprisonment; and (b) in the case of a financial institution or non–financial institution— (i) a fine of at least N10,000,000 and N1,000,000 for every day the offence persists, (ii) the withdrawal of licence or forfeiture of assets of the institution, or (iii) all the prescribed penalties.
crmp.plain: The Bank shall: - Report all suspicious transactions related to terrorism, terrorism financing, or proliferation financing to the NFIU within 24 hours. - Reports must be filed where there are reasons to suspect that the funds: a) Are linked to acts of terrorism or terrorism financing (legal or illegal sources). b) Are proceeds of terrorism-related crimes. c) Belong to persons, entities, or organizations designated as terrorists.
crmp.riskDescription: - Non-compliance may result in severe regulatory sanctions including fines, license withdrawal, or criminal prosecution of employees. - Failure may expose the bank to being used for terrorist financing activities.
crmp.owner: Chief Compliance Officer (CCO), MLRO, Compliance Unit
crmp.primaryControl: - Automated transaction monitoring system to flag suspicious activity. - STR (Suspicious Transaction Report) filing procedures aligned with 24-hour rule. - Internal escalation protocol for urgent review and reporting. - PEP and Sanctions list screening integration.

crmp.title: Institutional PF Risk Assessment
crmp.description: 1) FIs are required to identify, assess, monitor and mitigate PF risks. FIs should document their understanding and analysis of PF risks in their risk assessment Framework taking cognizance of their size and complexity. The risk assessment should at a minimum include country/geographic risks; customer/vendor risks and product and service risks.  2) Where there are higher risks, FIs should take commensurate measures to manage and mitigate the risks, including applying enhanced screening measures. Correspondingly, where the risks are lower, they should ensure that the screening measures are commensurate with the lower level of risk. FIs shall ensure full implementation of TFS relating to PF in any risk scenario.
crmp.plain: The Bank shall: 1. Identify, assess, monitor, and mitigate Proliferation Financing (PF) risks. 2. Document their PF risk understanding and analysis in a risk assessment framework tailored to their size and complexity. 3. Assess risks across country/geographic, customer/vendor, and product/service dimensions. 4. Apply enhanced screening measures for higher-risk areas and ensure all PF-related Targeted Financial Sanctions (TFS) are implemented fully regardless of risk level.
crmp.riskDescription: Failure to identify and mitigate PF risks can result in:  - Regulatory sanctions  - Involvement in global proliferation financing schemes  - Reputational damage  - De-risking by international correspondent banks
crmp.owner: Chief Compliance Officer / Risk Management Department
crmp.primaryControl: - Develop and maintain a PF Risk Assessment Framework - Conduct periodic risk assessments covering geographic, customer, and product/service risks - Implement enhanced due diligence and sanctions screening for higher-risk areas - Integrate PF risk considerations into onboarding and transaction monitoring

The risk assessment should at a minimum include country/geographic risks; customer/vendor risks and product and service risks.

points.text: Where there are higher risks, FIs should take commensurate measures to manage and mitigate the risks, including applying enhanced screening measures. Correspondingly, where the risks are lower, they should ensure that the screening measures are commensurate with the lower level of risk. FIs shall ensure full implementation of TFS relating to PF in any risk scenario.

crmp.source: Guidelines on Targeted Financial Sanctions Relating to Proliferation Financing
crmp.title: Screening
crmp.description: FIs are required to carry out regular and ongoing screening against updated Sanctions Lists issued by the UN and the Nigeria Sanctions Committee (NSC) prior to conducting any transaction or undertaking any financial Services to ascertain whether the name of such a person or entity is on the Lists. Specifically, screening should be conducted during the following: a) Onboarding a new customer; b) Facilitating an occasional transaction; c) Establishing any relationship with any person or entity; d) Upon updates on the Nigeria Sanctions List, UN Consolidated List; and e) Upon review of Know-Your-Customer (KYC) or changes to a customer’s information.  Screening must be conducted immediately and without delay to ensure compliance with the requirement for implementing freezing measures immediately or within 24 hours. Furthermore, FIs are required to screen their entire customer database daily and whenever an update has been made to the UN Consolidated List or Nigerian List, to prevent dissipation of funds of the designated persons or entities.  FIs must establish group-wide screening and transaction monitoring systems (including those operating in free trade zones). Screening should be undertaken for existing customers, potential customers, beneficial owners, and transactions to identify possible matches.  (a) Confirmed Match A confirmed match is when an individual, entity, or group matches all the key identifiers published on the Sanctions Lists. The range of information that constitute identifiers of designated individuals, entities, or groups are as follows:  For natural person: Name, Aliases, Date of birth, Nationality, ID or passport information, Last known address.  For legal persons: Name(s), Aliases, Certificate of Registration (RC No.), Registered Address, Address of branches, Other information.  Where the individual, entity, or group matches all the key identifiers published on the Sanctions Lists, the result is considered a ‘confirmed match’. Where the confirmed match is an existing customer, FIs are required to immediately, identify and freeze, without delay and without prior notice, all funds and assets owned or controlled by the designated person or entity in their possession.  Where the confirmed match is a potential customer, the FIs are required to reject the transaction immediately and report to the Nigeria Sanctions Committee (NSC). However, before rejecting the transaction, FIs are required to search their records to confirm whether the potential customer is a Beneficial Ownership (BO). Where the search is positive, FIs are required to immediately identify and freeze, without delay and without prior notice, all funds and assets owned or controlled by the BO in their possession.  In cases of confirmed matches (for either existing or potential customer), FIs are required to report to the NSC, within 24 hours, any assets frozen or actions taken in compliance with the prohibition requirements of the relevant UNSCRs including attempted transactions.  In addition, FIs are required to immediately file STRs to the NFIU, including all cases of name matching in financial transactions prior to, or after publication or update of the lists for further analysis.  (b) False Positive A false positive is a potential match to listed individuals, entities, or groups, either due to the common nature of the name or due to ambiguous identifying data, which on evaluation proves not to be a confirmed match.  FIs are required to obtain additional information and identification documents from the customer or a third party to ascertain whether a customer is a designated person or entity in the case of similar names.  FIs are required to forward queries to the NSC to ascertain whether the customer is a designated person or entity in the case of similar names. Any query submitted to the NSC is to be accompanied by additional information, copies of identification documents and the FIs assessments.  Where FIs are satisfied that the customer (potential or BO) is not a designated individual, entity, or group, that there is a ‘False Positive Result’, FIs do not need to implement any TFS measures. FIs may allow the transaction or business to continue its normal course, and maintain evidence of this process in their records.  Where FIs’ customers feel that their accounts have been mistakenly frozen or transactions have been mistakenly rejected or blocked, the FIs may advise their customers to contact the NSC to verify the false positive match.  The contact details for the NSC in relation to TFS on PF is: info@nigsac.gov.ng  (c) Potential Match A potential match is when there is a partial match between identifiers in the Sanctions Lists with any information in FIs databases, and the FIs are unable to conclude a false positive or a confirmed match.  Due to prevalence of some names, FIs may find various potential matches. However, it does not necessarily mean that the individual, entity, or group they are dealing with is subject to TFS. FIs are required to cross-check their customers’ database with the identifiers published on the Sanctions Lists when identifying the potential match, by taking into consideration their knowledge of the customer (potential and BO) or transaction, through CDD and/or other sources of information.  Where FIs are unable to internally verify whether the ‘potential match’ is a false positive result or a confirmed match, the transaction should be suspended, and the case reported to NSC. The reported transaction should remain suspended, until a response is received on the status of the potential match.  4.3.1 Screening of Customers – Related and Third Parties FIs are required to undertake further screening and analysis of designated persons or entities whose properties or accounts are jointly owned and/or indirectly controlled by the designated persons or entities.  FIs are required to conduct further Customer Due Diligence (CDD) on parties related to frozen accounts including checking on the control and conduct of the frozen accounts and other related or third parties accounts connected to designated persons or entities.  The requirements for CDD on legal persons and legal arrangements and beneficial owners in the respective provisions under the CBN AML/CFT/CPF Regulations, 2022 and extant laws should be applied in determining whether the funds are directly or indirectly owned or controlled.  FIs are required to screen the names of beneficiaries of wire transfers and assess whether such transaction should be blocked or rejected.  FIs are also required to search, examine and analyse past financial activities of designated persons or entities and related or third parties.
crmp.plain: The Bank shall: - Conduct regular and ongoing screening of all customers, transactions, and beneficial owners against the UN Consolidated List and Nigeria Sanctions List. - Screen at onboarding, occasional transactions, relationship establishment, updates to Sanctions Lists, and KYC reviews. - Screen daily and immediately after any update to sanctions lists. - Implement group-wide screening, including free trade zones. - Take actions based on screening results:   - Confirmed match: Freeze assets immediately, report to NSC and NFIU within 24 hours.   - Potential match: Suspend transaction, escalate to NSC and await verification.   - False positive: Obtain additional documents, confirm, and retain proof if not a match. - Screen related or third-party accounts and wire transfer beneficiaries. - Conduct retrospective analysis of designated persons' past activities.
crmp.riskDescription: - Risk of facilitating transactions for sanctioned individuals/entities - Exposure to regulatory penalties, reputational loss, and international restrictions (e.g., correspondent banking limits)
crmp.owner: Compliance Officer Sanctions & AML Monitoring Unit IT/System Admin for automated screening
crmp.primaryControl: - Deploy automated screening tools with real-time alerts - Perform daily batch screening and immediate screening upon list updates - Maintain Sanctions List integration in onboarding and transaction systems - Define workflows for handling matches (Confirmed, False Positive, Potential Match) - Maintain audit trail of all screening actions and decisions

crmp.source: Guidelines on Targeted Financial Sanctions Relating to Proliferation Financing
crmp.title: Application of targeted financial sanctions
crmp.description: FIs are required to immediately implement TFS by identifying and freezing, without delay and without prior notice, all funds and assets owned or controlled by the designated person or entity in their possession.  FIs may advise the customer or related party of the frozen accounts, blocked or rejected transactions to submit any query or appeal for variation to the frozen accounts, delisting or any other matters to the NSC for approval.  The following are the TFS measures that must be implemented if a match with the Sanctions Lists is identified.  i. Freeze all funds or other assets without delay: freeze without delay (immediately or in any case within 24 hours) and without prior notice to the designated individual, entity, or group, all the funds or other assets: a) Owned or controlled, wholly or jointly, directly, or indirectly, by an individual, entity, or group designated in the Sanctions Lists; b) Derived or generated from funds or other assets under item (a); or c) Of Any individual or entity acting on behalf of or at the direction of any designated individual, entity, or group.  ii. Prohibition from making funds or other assets or services available: FIs are prohibited from providing funds or other assets or rendering financial services or other related services, whether in whole or in part, directly or indirectly, for the benefit of any designated individual, entity, or group on the Sanctions Lists.
crmp.plain: The Bank shall: 1. Immediately freeze, without prior notice, any funds or assets in their possession that:   - are owned or controlled (wholly or jointly, directly or indirectly) by individuals, entities, or groups on the Sanctions Lists;   - are derived from such funds or assets; or   - belong to anyone acting on behalf of or under the direction of a designated person or group. 2. Prohibit the provision of funds, financial services, or related support to designated persons/entities/groups. 3. Where a customer's funds or services are frozen or blocked, the bank may inform the affected party that they may submit queries or appeals to the Nigeria Sanctions Committee (NSC) for review or delisting.
crmp.riskDescription: - Failure to freeze assets of designated persons may expose the bank to criminal liability, reputational damage, regulatory sanctions, and international countermeasures. - Risk of inadvertently facilitating terrorism financing or proliferation activities.

points.content: FIs are required to immediately implement TFS by identifying and freezing, without delay and without prior notice, all funds and assets owned or controlled by the designated person or entity in their possession. FIs may advise the customer or related party of the frozen accounts, blocked or rejected transactions to submit any query or appeal for variation to the frozen accounts, delisting or any other matters to the NSC for approval. The following are the TFS measures that must be implemented if a match with the Sanctions Lists is identified.

points.text: Freeze all funds or other assets without delay: freeze without delay (immediately or in any case within 24 hours) and without prior notice to the designated individual, entity, or group, all the funds or other assets: a) Owned or controlled, wholly or jointly, directly, or indirectly, by an individual, entity, or group designated in the Sanctions Lists; b) Derived or generated from funds or other assets under item (a); or c) Of Any individual or entity acting on behalf of or at the direction of any designated individual, entity, or group.
points.content: Freeze all funds or other assets without delay: freeze without delay (immediately or in any case within 24 hours) and without prior notice to the designated individual, entity, or group, all the funds or other assets: a) Owned or controlled, wholly or jointly, directly, or indirectly, by an individual, entity, or group designated in the Sanctions Lists; b) Derived or generated from funds or other assets under item (a); or c) Of Any individual or entity acting on behalf of or at the direction of any designated individual, entity, or group.

points.text: Prohibition from making funds or other assets or services available: FIs are prohibited from providing funds or other assets or rendering financial services or other related services, whether in whole or in part, directly or indirectly, for the benefit of any designated individual, entity, or group on the Sanctions Lists.

crmp.title: Receipt of additional funds into frozen accounts
crmp.description: Where a frozen account is entitled to: i. interests or other earnings; or ii. payments due under contracts, agreements or obligations that were concluded or arose before the account became a frozen account shall be received and credited into the frozen account.  FIs are required to file a report of the receipt of such additional funds with the NFIU. Where there is no existing account for the receipt of additional funds, the FIs are required to create an Escrow account and inform the Attorney-General for appropriate action to be taken in this respect.
crmp.plain: The Bank shall: 1. Receive and credit additional funds into a frozen account if the funds are:   i. Interest or other earnings; or   ii. Payments due under pre-existing contracts (concluded before the account was frozen). 2. File a report of such credit with the NFIU. 3. If no existing frozen account exists for the funds, the bank must:   i. Create an Escrow account, and   ii. Inform the Attorney-General for further instructions.
crmp.riskDescription: - Risk of Non-compliance with freezing obligations and misreporting. - Potential Regulatory sanctions or legal consequences for failing to credit or Report such funds appropriately. - risk of unauthorized access to or movement of additional frozen funds.
crmp.owner: - Compliance Department (Sanctions Unit) - Operations Department - Legal Department (for notification to Attorney-General)
crmp.primaryControl: - Automate flagging and routing of incoming transactions to frozen accounts. - Maintain a frozen account monitoring register. - Develop a process flow for Escrow account creation and documentation. - Implement internal workflow for timely reporting to the NFIU.

crmp.title: Condition for Approval for usage of frozen funds by designated persons and entities under the UN Consolidated List
crmp.description: An application to utilize monies from frozen funds shall be made to the NSC. FIs should not make any payment to a designated person or entity except with the approval of the NSC.  Upon receipt of written approval from the NSC to utilize frozen funds, FIs that are in custody of frozen funds are required to implement the approval and furnish a report of the action taken to the NSC.

Upon receiving such approval, they must carry out the directive and submit a report of the action taken to the NSC.
crmp.riskDescription: - Unauthorized release of frozen funds could lead to violation of UN/NSC sanctions, reputational damage, regulatory sanctions, or complicity in terrorism financing.

crmp.primaryControl: - Maintain a central register of frozen accounts. - Require written NSC approval before executing any debit or release. - Implement a workflow checklist before processing any transaction on a frozen account.

crmp.title: Reporting Requirements
crmp.description: (6) Filing suspicious transaction with NFIU Where a FI is required to file an STR to the NFIU, the report should state: a) the information or other matter on which knowledge or suspicion is based; b) any information it holds about the person by which the person can be identified; and c) the nature and amount or quantity of funds held by FIs for the person at any time up to 5 years prior to the designation being made.  (7) Attempted transaction FIs are to report, as suspicious transaction, to NFIU any attempted transaction undertaken by designated persons or entities or related parties in the case of joint accounts. This may include any transaction that is subsequently rejected or blocked, incomplete in the event of failure to satisfactorily complete CDD and attempt for redemption of assets where repayment has been made.
crmp.plain: The Bank shall: - Identify and report all attempted transactions by designated persons, entities, or related parties (e.g., in joint accounts), even if the transaction was:   a) Rejected or blocked   b) Incomplete due to failed CDD   c) An attempted redemption of assets - File a Suspicious Transaction Report (STR) to the NFIU for every such attempt.
crmp.riskDescription: - Risk of facilitating or failing to report attempted terrorist financing transactions. - Reputational and regulatory risk for non-reporting of incomplete or blocked terrorist-related activities.
crmp.owner: - Sanctions Compliance Unit - Operations Department (Transaction flagging) - AML Monitoring Team
crmp.primaryControl: - Implement automated systems to detect and flag blocked, rejected, or failed transactions involving designated names. - Maintain a log of attempted transactions tied to CDD failures or sanctions list matches. - Escalate all flagged incidents to Compliance for review and STR filing.

crmp.title: Additional Obligations for Fis
crmp.description: In addition to alerts of updates received from the NSC upon subscription by FIs, the CBN may also issue notifications of TFS to FIs.  FIs shall on receipt of the notification from the CBN: i. immediately take steps to identify any funds, assets or any economic resources in their possession belonging to designated persons or entities and carry out freezing obligations in respect of PF as contained in the TPPA, 2022, and report to the NSC. ii. immediately file STR to the NFIU for further analysis on the financial activities of such an individual or entity; and iii. report, as STR to the NFIU, all cases of name matching in financial transactions prior to or after receipt of the Sanctions List.  For the purposes of this section, “immediately” means not later than 24 hours.  In addition to the above, FIs are required to fulfill the following obligations: i. Cooperate with the NSC in verifying the accuracy of the submitted information. ii. Implement the freezing, cancellation, or lifting decision, when appropriate, without delay. iii. Cooperate with competent authorities to provide information on TFS timeously when required. iv. Set and implement policies, procedures, and internal controls to: a) Ensure conduct of customer due diligence b) Ensure trade finance is integrated into compliance procedure (including the identification of final destination of goods and services) c) Ensure compliance with the obligations imposed by the TPPA and TFS Regulations. d) Conduct ongoing TFS training and awareness sessions to Board, senior management and employees. e) Prohibit staff from, directly or indirectly, informing the customer or any third party that freezing actions or any other measures will be implemented. f) Ensure appropriate resources are allocated to meet the obligations of implementing TFS.  It shall be the responsibility of all FIs, to monitor their accounts and transactions against the UN Consolidated List and Nigeria List.
crmp.plain: On receipt of TFS notification from NSC or CBN, The bank must: i. Identify and freeze all funds/assets linked to designated persons/entities and report to NSC within 24 hours. ii. File STR to the NFIU on such financial activities. iii. Report all name matches (before or after Sanctions List receipt) to the NFIU as STRs.  Additionally, they must: - Cooperate with NSC and competent authorities in information verification. - Implement all TFS decisions without delay. - Establish robust policies, procedures, and internal controls covering:   a) CDD processes   b) Trade finance compliance (destination checks)   c) TPPA/TFS regulation compliance   d) Ongoing staff training   e) Strict confidentiality (no tipping off)   f) Allocation of adequate resources. - Monitor all accounts and transactions against the UN Consolidated List and Nigeria Sanctions List.
crmp.riskDescription: - Failure to freeze, report, or cooperate could result in aiding proliferation financing, legal sanctions, reputational damage, and regulatory penalties.
crmp.owner: - Sanctions Compliance Unit - Legal & Regulatory Compliance - Internal Audit - Trade Finance & Operations Units
crmp.primaryControl: - Maintain active subscription to NSC/CBN alert systems. - Daily screening against updated sanctions lists. - TFS response protocol and escalation procedures documented. - Enforce no tipping-off protocols. - Incorporate TFS clauses into Trade Finance and CDD policies.

crmp.title: Record Keeping
crmp.description: FIs are required to keep records of all actions taken in respect of TFS, which should be kept in an easily accessible and retrievable manner.
crmp.plain: The bank must maintain complete records of all actions taken regarding the implementation of Targeted Financial Sanctions (TFS). These records must be stored in a way that allows for quick and easy retrieval when needed.
crmp.riskDescription: Failure to maintain proper records could hinder regulatory audits, investigations, or legal compliance, and may result in penalties or reputational damage.
crmp.owner: Chief Compliance Officer (CCO), Records/Documentation Unit, IT/Data Management Team
crmp.primaryControl: - Standard Operating Procedures for documentation of all TFS-related actions- Secure digital storage system with indexing and search functionality- Periodic audit of TFS recordkeeping practices
