crmp.title: Duties of insured institutions in relation to examination
crmp.description: (1) An insured institution shall produce to the examiner as and when required, all books, accounts, documents, management information systems and all information as the examiner may deem necessary or request in the performance of his functions.  (2) Any insured institution, its director or officer that— (a) wilfully refuses to produce any book, account, document or such other information, (b) negligently, wilfully or with intent to defraud, gives information which is false in any material particular, or (c) refuses examiners access to their premises or any hardware or software utilised in its business, commits an offence.
crmp.plain: The bank must:  1. Produce all books, accounts, documents, MIS data, and any information requested by NDIC examiners as needed to carry out their functions. 2. The bank, its directors, or officers must not: – Wilfully refuse to produce documents; – Provide false or misleading information; or – Deny access to premises, systems, or infrastructure used for business.
crmp.riskDescription: - Non-compliance can lead to prosecution, criminal liability for directors/officers, reputational damage, NDIC sanctions, and increased regulatory scrutiny.
crmp.owner: - Chief Compliance Officer- Regulatory Affairs/NDIC Liaison- Head of Internal Audit- Department Heads- ICT/Operations Lead
crmp.primaryControl: - Create and maintain an NDIC Examination Protocol. - Centralized digital archive for examiner-requested records. - Regular training for staff on regulatory cooperation. - Track and monitor all information requests and responses. - Ensure secure access to systems and data for NDIC examiners.

crmp.title: Report of Examination
crmp.description: The insured institution shall within two weeks of the presentation to its board of directors convey to the Corporation the reaction of the board of directors to the written report and proposals for implementation of the recommendations.
crmp.plain: The bank must, within two weeks after the NDIC report is presented to its Board of Directors, send to NDIC the Board’s reaction to the report and its implementation plan for the recommendations.
crmp.riskDescription: - Failure to meet this obligation may result in: ▪ Regulatory sanctions ▪ Escalated NDIC supervision ▪ Reputational damage ▪ Weak internal control oversight
crmp.owner: - Company Secretary- Chief Compliance Officer- Regulatory Affairs/NDIC Liaison- Head of Internal Audit- Executive Management
crmp.primaryControl: - Establish a formal NDIC examination response process. - Maintain a compliance calendar for regulatory timelines. - Designate a compliance reporting coordinator. - Document all Board-level discussions on examination reports. - Escalate delays to executive leadership.

crmp.title: Fidelity Insurance
crmp.description: All insured institutions shall have fidelity insurance coverage up to such level as may be prescribed by the Corporation.
crmp.plain: The bank must maintain fidelity insurance coverage up to the level prescribed by NDIC.
crmp.riskDescription: - Inadequate or no fidelity insurance could lead to: ▪ Exposure to financial losses from employee dishonesty or fraud ▪ Non-compliance penalties from NDIC ▪ Regulatory reputation risk
crmp.owner: - Chief Risk Officer- Head of Legal & Compliance- Internal Audit- Insurance Desk Officer
crmp.primaryControl: - Periodic review and update of fidelity insurance policies - Ensure policy coverage aligns with NDIC’s prescribed thresholds - Annual renewal monitoring and Board approval - Maintain insurance certificates and audit trail

crmp.title: Obligations in respect of unauthorised disclosure
crmp.description: (1) The members of board, staff and agents of an insured institution shall keep strictly confidential and make no unauthorised disclosure or use of any information in relation to the activities or condition of an insured institution or in relation to its customers which they may either directly or indirectly receive in such capacity, even after they cease to be members or staff or agents of that insured institution.  (2) The obligation specified in subsection (1) is imposed on members of the Board and employees of, and agents or other persons engaged by, the Corporation.
crmp.plain: 1. The members of the board, employees, and agents must not disclose or use confidential information about the bank or its customers unless authorised. 2. This duty of confidentiality continues even after their exit from the bank.
crmp.riskDescription: - Breach of customer trust and confidence - Potential legal or regulatory penalties - Reputational damage - Possible lawsuits or regulatory sanctions
crmp.owner: - Chief Compliance Officer- Human Resources- Legal Department- Information Security Officer
crmp.primaryControl: - Include confidentiality clauses in employment contracts and NDAs - Conduct regular training on information security and data privacy - Restrict access to sensitive information based on roles - Monitor staff access logs

crmp.title: Notification to the corporation of dismissed staff and employment of dismissed staff.
crmp.description: (1) An insured institution shall notify the Corporation of any staff dismissed, terminated or advised to retire or resign on the ground of fraud, forgery or financial malpractice.
crmp.plain: The bank must notify NDIC of any staff who has been dismissed, terminated, or advised to resign or retire due to fraud, forgery, or financial malpractice.
crmp.riskDescription: - Regulatory non-compliance and penalties - Reputational damage for failure to report - Possible exposure to further fraud due to poor controls - Legal consequences from concealment or omission

crmp.primaryControl: - Maintain a fraud-linked staff exit register - Integrate HR exit process with regulatory notification protocol - Escalate all fraud/malpractice-related separations to the compliance team for onward reporting to NDIC

crmp.title: Priority of claims
crmp.description: Where an insured institution is unable to meet its obligations or suspends payment or where its management and control has been taken over by the Central Bank of Nigeria or where its licence has been revoked, the assets of the insured institution shall be available to meet all its deposit liabilities and such deposit liabilities shall have priority over all other liabilities of the insured institution.
crmp.plain: 1. When a bank’s licence is revoked, or the CBN takes over its management or it suspends payments, all deposit liabilities must be settled first before any other liabilities are addressed. 2. The bank’s assets must be applied first to depositor claims.
crmp.riskDescription: - Failure to prioritize deposit liabilities may result in: ▪ Breach of statutory liquidation rules ▪ Legal consequences and penalties ▪ Regulatory sanctions ▪ Erosion of public trust
crmp.owner: - Legal Department- Finance/Treasury Unit- Executive Management
crmp.primaryControl: - Ensure clear documentation and categorization of liabilities in financial records - Include priority rules in bank’s resolution and liquidation manual - Periodic audit of liability classification and stress testing for insolvency scenarios

crmp.title: Advertisement
crmp.description: An insured institution may advertise its insured status without prior approval from the Corporation.
crmp.plain: 1. The bank may advertise that it is insured by NDIC with no prior approval required from the NDIC before making such advertisements.
crmp.riskDescription: - Incorrect or misleading advertisement of insured status can result in: ▪ Reputational risk ▪ Regulatory backlash if misrepresented ▪ Public misinformation
crmp.owner: - Marketing/Corporate Communications Department- Compliance Unit- Legal Department
crmp.primaryControl: - Use pre-approved templates or vetted language for all insurance-related promotions - Ensure marketing materials reflect only valid, current insured status with NDIC

crmp.title: PRE-REQUISITE FOR FINANCIAL ASSISTANCE
crmp.description: Under the liquidity thresholds, a bank is considered significantly illiquid if it records liquidity ratio greater than 10% but less than 20%, its current account with the CBN is overdrawn and not covered on the next working day subsequently for five working days within a month, a net taker of up to 25% of its total deposits, its ratio of total loans to total deposits is above existing prudential ratio by 20% for three consecutive months and if it incurs clearing operations losses continuously for 10 days. Any bank that exhibits a combination of the above thresholds is expected to solicit for short-term liquidity support from the Corporation.  For an insured institution to qualify for the assistance, it must meet the pre-conditions as contained in section 37 [1] [a-c] of the NDIC Act and others including the Contingency Planning Framework as listed below:  i) The applicant insured institution has difficulty in meeting its obligations to its depositors and other creditors,  ii) It persistently suffers liquidity deficiency,  iii) There exist severe financial conditions which threaten the stability of the financial system thereby posing grave risks to depositors,  iv) An insured institution that is a net taker of up to 25% of its total deposits.
crmp.plain: The bank on exhibiting their liquidity distress based on specified thresholds (e.g. net taker > 25% of deposits, liquidity ratio < 20%, CBN overdraft not cleared, high loan-deposit ratio, or 10-day clearing losses) must request short-term liquidity support from the NDIC and meet the eligibility conditions under Section 37(1)(a–c) of the NDIC Act and Contingency Planning Framework.
crmp.riskDescription: Failing to monitor liquidity thresholds or delay in seeking NDIC assistance can result in worsening financial health, regulatory sanctions, and risk to depositors.
crmp.owner: Chief Risk Officer (CRO); Treasurer; Compliance Officer
crmp.primaryControl: Daily liquidity monitoring; automated alerts; Board-level review of liquidity breaches; prompt NDIC notification procedure.

crmp.source: GUIDELINES ON FINANCIAL AND TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE TO OPERATING INSURED BANKS AND DEPOSIT TAKING FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS
crmp.title: REQUIREMENTS FOR FINANCIAL ASSISTANCE
crmp.description: a] A formal Application for financial assistance stating the amount required.  b] The purpose of the request i.e. the causes and extent of the problem to be addressed.  c] Tenor/Repayment period.  d] Sources and Mode of the loan repayment  e] The current and projected monthly Cash Flow, Statement of Comprehensive Income and Statement of Financial Position, clearly stating the underlying assumptions for the projections, the impact of the expected facility and its amortization over the period of repayment.  f] Board Resolution authorizing the request for the facility.  g] Evidence of the repayment of all insider related credits.  h] Evidence of repayment of any outstanding indebtedness to other banks by the Directors of the applicant bank.  i] Schedule of existing borrowings by the bank  j] The schedule of non-performing credits as well as the major liabilities that have matured.  k] A statement in quantifiable terms of measures taken to address the institution’s liquidity problem. E.g. debt recovery, cost saving measures adopted.  l] Evidence of compliance with the recommendations of the CBN/NDIC Examiners.  m] A certified true copy of the Articles and Memorandum of Association of the insured institution.  n] The list of major shareholders [5% and above] and their shareholding as well as resumes of the Board and Management of the insured institution.  o] An acceptable joint and several guarantees of the members of the Board of Directors and Principal Shareholders of the insured institution.  p] Identification and Description of the specific property being offered as collateral, accompanied with recent Estate Valuers Report on same, stating the open market and Forced Sale Values.  q] Evidence of comprehensive insurance of the property.  r] A Strategic Business Plan indicating how the Management intends to address the insured institution’s problem, repay the loan, to attain and sustain the N25 billion minimum capital requirement.  s] Any other information that may assist in the processing of the request of the particular insured institution.
crmp.plain: The bank must: 1. Submit a formal application for financial assistance, stating the required amount. 2. Provide details of the purpose of the loan request, outlining the cause and extent of the issue. 3. Indicate the tenor and repayment plan of the loan. 4. Clearly state sources and mode of repayment. 5. Include current and projected monthly cash flows, profit/loss statement, and balance sheet, along with assumptions, expected impact of the facility, and amortization plan. 6. Attach a Board resolution authorizing the request. 7. Submit evidence of repayment of insider-related credits. 8. Provide evidence of directors’ loan repayment to other banks. 9. Submit schedule of existing borrowings. 10. Provide a schedule of non-performing credits and major matured liabilities. 11. Present a quantifiable statement of remedial measures (e.g., debt recovery, cost savings). 12. Submit evidence of compliance with CBN/NDIC examiner recommendations. 13. Attach certified true copy of the Memorandum & Articles of Association. 14. Provide a list of major shareholders (5% and above) and resumes of board/management. 15. Submit joint and several guarantees from directors and principal shareholders. 16. Identify and describe property offered as collateral, with valuation report. 17. Present evidence of insurance on the property. 18. Submit a strategic business plan to address problems, repay the loan, and meet capital requirements. 19. Provide any other relevant information to aid assessment.
crmp.riskDescription: - Failure to provide complete and accurate documentation can result in: ▪ Rejection of financial assistance request ▪ Regulatory delays or sanctions ▪ Further deterioration of liquidity condition ▪ Loss of regulatory confidence and possible resolution action
crmp.owner: - Chief Financial Officer (CFO)- Head of Regulatory Affairs- Company Secretary- Head, Credit and Recovery- Executive Management/Board
crmp.primaryControl: - Maintain an NDIC/CBN assistance documentation checklist - Establish a dedicated compliance team to compile and validate all required documents - Review financial statements and schedules monthly for accuracy - Secure board approvals in advance for strategic applications - Pre-audit collateral valuation, guarantees, and insurance prior to application

crmp.source: GUIDELINES ON FINANCIAL AND TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE TO OPERATING INSURED BANKS AND DEPOSIT TAKING FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS
crmp.title: SECURITY AND REPAYMENT
crmp.description: Any application for financial assistance must provide for repayment of such assistance. The facility shall be fully secured by tangible security. The applicant bank or insured institution for financial assistance must submit joint and several guarantees from the members of its Board as well as principal shareholders for the repayment of any financial assistance granted.
crmp.plain: If the bank is applying for NDIC financial assistance, it must ensure full repayment provisions. The loan must be backed by tangible security, and all board members and principal shareholders must jointly guarantee repayment.
crmp.riskDescription: Failure to provide sufficient security or enforceable guarantees may result in rejection of the financial assistance request or legal/financial penalties.
crmp.owner: CFO; Head of Legal; Company Secretary; MD/CEO
crmp.primaryControl: Pre-verification of security assets; legal due diligence on enforceability of guarantees; NDIC-compliant loan documentation

crmp.source: GUIDELINES ON FINANCIAL AND TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE TO OPERATING INSURED BANKS AND DEPOSIT TAKING FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS
crmp.title: FORMAL AGREEMENT WITH THE CORPORATION FOR FINANCIAL AND TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE
crmp.description: The terms and conditions for a facility will vary from one insured institution to the other depending on the nature of the problem and the type of facility being sought. In general, the terms and conditions will cover pre and post-disbursement conditions to be met by the applicant bank. These include but are not limited to the following:  i] The insured institution should show evidence of substantial debt repayment by shareholders and their related interests.  ii] The insured institution should not default in premium payment.  iii] Every applicant insured institution will submit a time-framed turn-around plan, the evaluation of which will determine the extent of financial and technical assistance to be granted by the Corporation.  iv] The agreement will contain among others, the following terms and conditions that will be determined on a case by case basis: - Purpose of facility - Amount of financial facility - Tenor - Repayment - Interest rate - Security – essentially government securities [e.g. investment certificates] or other acceptable collateral.  v] Applicant insured institution will submit joint and several guarantees from the members of its Board as well as the principal shareholders for the repayment of any financial assistance granted.  vi] The insured institution will suspend the repayment of dividends and bonus where it is in default of its repayment schedule.  vii] The insured institution will embark on intensive deposit drive particularly from non-interbank sources.
crmp.plain: The bank must:  1. Show evidence of substantial debt repayment by shareholders and related parties. 2. Ensure no default in NDIC premium payments. 3. Submit a time-bound turnaround plan to the NDIC; the plan will influence the type and extent of assistance granted. 4. Enter into an agreement with NDIC specifying:     - Purpose of the facility     - Amount     - Tenor and repayment terms     - Interest rate     - Security (e.g., government securities or acceptable collateral) 5. Provide joint and several guarantees from board members and principal shareholders. 6. Suspend dividends and bonuses during any repayment default period. 7. Implement an aggressive deposit mobilization strategy, excluding inter-bank sources. 8. Submit monthly returns to NDIC including:     - Debt recovery     - Performing/non-performing loans     - New deposits     - New lending     - Asset/Liability maturity profile     - Cash flow     - Financial position     - Comprehensive income     - Fraud/forgery incidents and disciplinary actions 9. Prepare for post-assistance monitoring by NDIC via onsite (target examinations, spot checks) and offsite reviews (return analysis and NDIC directives).
crmp.riskDescription: - Failure to meet pre/post-disbursement conditions can result in: ▪ Withdrawal of financial support ▪ Regulatory sanctions or license suspension ▪ Public confidence erosion ▪ Increased liquidity crisis and reputational risk
crmp.owner: - Managing Director/CEO- Chief Financial Officer- Board of Directors- Head of Regulatory Affairs- Chief Compliance Officer
crmp.primaryControl: - Maintain an NDIC Agreement Compliance Tracker - Establish a turnaround plan review committee with measurable KPIs - Secure board and shareholder guarantees and collateral documentation in advance - Create automated templates for monthly NDIC returns - Set internal reminders for premium payments and dividend restrictions - Schedule internal audits and mock inspections ahead of NDIC visits

crmp.title: DUE DILIGENCE
crmp.description: The bank, or financial institution, must consent to unrestricted on-site due diligence reviews by any potential acquirer that is cleared by the Corporation in consultation with the CBN.
crmp.plain: The bank must allow full, unrestricted on-site due diligence by any potential acquirer who has been approved by the NDIC in consultation with the CBN.
crmp.riskDescription: Failure to grant access to approved acquirers may result in delays or rejection of potential rescue, acquisition, or recapitalization plans; it may also lead to regulatory penalties.
crmp.owner: MD/CEO; Company Secretary; Compliance Officer; Head of Risk
crmp.primaryControl: Due diligence access protocols; regulatory communication logs; internal NDIC/CBN clearance verification process

crmp.title: OTHER COVENANTS
crmp.description: i) Submission of a Time-framed Strategic Turn-around Plan The applicant bank, or financial institution, must submit a time-framed strategic turn-around plan which shall include, among others: Viability projections based on reasonable assumptions regarding the use of the assistance, Earnings, Reserve levels, Asset quality Trends, Anticipated dividends and Needs. This will be evaluated by the Corporation in determining the extent of assistance to be granted.
crmp.plain: The bank when applying for NDIC assistance must submit a strategic turn-around plan with a clear timeline. The plan must include realistic projections on viability, earnings, reserves, asset quality, dividend outlook, and capital needs.
crmp.riskDescription: Failure to submit or submission of an inadequate turn-around plan may lead to delay or denial of financial or technical support from NDIC.
crmp.owner: MD/CEO; CFO; Head of Strategy; Compliance Officer
crmp.primaryControl: Internal review committee for strategic plans; approval workflow; board ratification of turn-around plans; templates and planning tools

crmp.title: Compliance with Statutory and Regulatory Requirements
crmp.description: The Board and Senior Management of all insured financial institutions shall ensure compliance with all relevant statutes and regulations, such as NDIC Act 2006, BOFIA 2020, the CBN Supervisory Intervention Framework for the Nigerian Banking Sector, Prudential Guidelines, Corporate Governance Guidelines, and all CBN directives to avoid breaches of legal, statutory, regulatory obligations related to compliance with the requirement of the DPAS Framework.
crmp.plain: The Board and Senior Management of the bank must ensure full compliance with all applicable laws, regulations, and directives, including the NDIC Act 2006, BOFIA 2020, CBN guidelines, and all relevant frameworks to meet the requirements of the Differential Premium Assessment System (DPAS).
crmp.riskDescription: Failure to comply with statutory or regulatory provisions could lead to sanctions by NDIC and/or CBN, negative risk classification, or reputational and financial loss under the DPAS.
crmp.owner: Board of Directors; MD/CEO; Chief Compliance Officer; Head of Legal; Head of Risk
crmp.primaryControl: Regulatory compliance monitoring system; periodic internal audits; external compliance reviews; regular staff training on regulatory obligations

crmp.source: Exposure Draft of the Revised Consumer Protection Regulations 2.0
crmp.title: FAIR TREATMENT
crmp.description: The bank shall comply with the following minimum standards at all stages of the relationship with consumers:  4.1.1 Treat consumers with courtesy and honesty.  4.1.2 Communicate in plain language, devoid of technical terms that would make it difficult for consumers to understand their rights and obligations.  4.1.3 Provide access to basic financial services without regard to demographic status such as gender, age, religion, literacy level, region and disability.  4.1.4 Provide support to consumers with special needs such as multilingual assistance, ramp, visual and hearing aids.  4.1.5 Promptly oblige consumers’ request for account closure or to switch providers, without unreasonable closing/switching barriers.  4.1.6 Execute variations to contracts, including interest rate, fees or charges, only if expressly provided for in the contract and notify customers at least five (5) working days in advance of execution.  4.1.7 Acknowledge enquiries from consumers within 24 hours.  4.1.8 Respond to customers’ enquiries within five (5) working days of receipt.  4.1.9 Not charge early liquidation fee on Consumer and Micro, Small and Medium Enterprise loans with variable interest rate.  4.1.10 Be accountable for improper functioning of their banking applications.  4.1.11 Deploy flexible banking applications to meet regulatory requirements for good consumer outcomes.  4.1.12 Disclose similar product offerings within the institution to enable consumers to make comparisons and informed choices.  4.1.13 Not engage in bundling or cross-selling practices that unduly limit consumer choices.  4.1.14 Be held accountable for employing any practice that could be considered unfair.
crmp.plain: The bank shall: 1. Treat customers with courtesy and honesty. 2. Use plain language and avoid technical jargon in all communication. 3. Ensure equal access to basic services regardless of gender, age, religion, disability, or literacy level. 4. Provide special support for consumers with special needs (e.g., ramps, hearing/visual aids, multilingual support). 5. Allow customers to close or switch accounts without unreasonable barriers. 6. Make contract variations (e.g., interest or fees) only if provided for, and notify customers at least 5 working days prior. 7. Acknowledge all customer enquiries within 24 hours. 8. Respond to all customer enquiries within 5 working days. 9. Do not charge early liquidation fees on MSME/consumer loans with variable interest rates. 10. Take responsibility for any failures or issues with the bank’s mobile or web applications. 11. Ensure bank apps are flexible and support regulatory consumer outcomes. 12. Disclose similar products for comparison and informed customer decisions. 13. Avoid forced product bundling or cross-selling that limits consumer choice. 14. Avoid all forms of unfair treatment and be accountable for misconduct.
crmp.riskDescription: - Breach of these standards can lead to: ▪ Regulatory sanctions ▪ Erosion of customer trust ▪ Customer attrition and reputational damage ▪ Fines or license limitations ▪ Negative media and public backlash
crmp.owner: - Chief Compliance Officer- Head of Customer Experience- Branch Managers- Head of Digital Channels- Legal and Contracting Team
crmp.primaryControl: - Deploy customer-friendly communication templates and training for frontline staff. - Periodic testing of app accessibility and compliance with special-needs support. - Track response times to enquiries and escalate delays. - Ensure disclosure templates for similar products exist. - Set up independent compliance reviews of switching/closure procedures. - Embed interest and fee variation protocols into core banking system with alert triggers. - Conduct annual reviews of bundled offerings to check for undue customer restriction.

crmp.source: Exposure Draft of the Revised Consumer Protection Regulations 2.0
crmp.title: BUSINESS ETHICS
crmp.description: To promote good business practices, FSPs shall comply with the following minimum standards:  4.2.1 Conduct business in a responsible, professional, and ethical manner.  4.2.2 Train staff to promote competence, efficiency, and professionalism in the discharge of their duties.  4.2.3 Provide clear information about product features, terms and conditions as well as the applicable charges.  4.2.4 Comply with the rates, fees, charges, or prices published or disclosed at the engagement points.  4.2.5 Obtain relevant and sufficient information about consumers, before providing advice or concluding a contract, to enable it to offer suitable products that meet the consumer’s needs and financial capacity.  4.2.6 Not impose product, service, or channel on consumers.  4.2.7 Not charge fees for issuance and renewal of products or services which have not been requested by the customer.  4.2.8 Not compel consumers to buy a product or service as a pre-condition for the purchase of another product or service unless where the products or services are directly dependent.  4.2.9 Apply non-credit related fees/charges only to the extent of the balance in the account and defer the outstanding fees/charges until the account is funded and the customer notified accordingly.  4.2.10 Communicate a decision (acceptance or decline) on applications for waivers, extensions, and other concessions to a customer within ten (10) working days, otherwise the application shall be deemed granted.  4.2.11 Be responsible for digitally generated advise, recommendations and evidence of transactions.  4.2.12 Notify customers within twelve (12) hours of service interruptions and at least 48 hours for anticipated disruptions and take measures to mitigate the impact.  4.2.13 Sale of products through digital channels should only proceed after customers have confirmed that they have read mandatory information.  4.2.14 Avoid offering incentives that promote misconduct.  4.2.15 Structure remuneration of employees and authorized agents to promote responsible business conduct.  4.2.16 Avoid conflict of interest in dealing with consumers. Where conflicts cannot be avoided, disclose and establish mechanisms to manage such conflict, or decline to provide the service.  4.2.17 Carry out impact assessment where an issue has been identified on an account with a view to addressing other accounts in similar circumstance. The resolution should be communicated to the affected customers.
crmp.plain: The bank shall: 1. Conduct business in a responsible, professional, and ethical manner. 2. Train staff to ensure competence and professionalism. 3. Disclose clear product features, terms, and fees. 4. Adhere strictly to published rates, fees, and charges. 5. Assess customer’s financial profile before offering financial advice or closing a sale. 6. Not force products, services, or delivery channels on customers. 7. Not charge issuance or renewal fees unless requested by the customer. 8. Avoid tying one product’s purchase to another, except when directly dependent. 9. Apply non-credit fees only against available balances and defer excess with notification. 10. Respond to customer applications for waivers or concessions within 10 working days or consider it granted. 11. Be fully accountable for digital advice, recommendations, and transaction records. 12. Notify customers within 12 hours of service interruptions and 48 hours in advance for scheduled outages. 13. Not sell products through digital channels unless the customer confirms reading mandatory information. 14. Avoid incentives that may encourage misconduct. 15. Ensure staff compensation supports ethical and responsible behavior. 16. Avoid conflicts of interest; where unavoidable, disclose and manage them or decline the service. 17. Assess impact across similar accounts and notify affected customers when systemic issues are discovered.
crmp.riskDescription: - Regulatory non-compliance due to unethical practices. - Loss of customer trust and public backlash. - Legal action from mis-selling or improper charges. - Potential fines, reputational damage, or loss of license. - Staff behavior leading to operational misconduct.
crmp.owner: - Chief Compliance Officer- Head of Customer Experience- Product Managers- Sales/Relationship Management Heads- Internal Audit- Legal & Digital Operations Units
crmp.primaryControl: - Enforce Code of Business Conduct and Ethics. - Mandatory onboarding and annual ethical conduct training. - Automate disclosure of terms and fees in onboarding portals. - Review compensation models to remove misconduct-inducing incentives. - Integrate financial suitability assessments into product advisory tools. - Enforce system-based application tracking for waivers/extensions. - Deploy real-time notification systems for service disruptions. - Implement system-based checks to block tied product sales unless linked. - Embed conflict-of-interest disclosures in CRM processes.

crmp.title: SALES PROMOTION AND ADVERTISEMENT
crmp.description: FSPs shall be required to ensure that their advertising and promotional materials comply with the following minimum standards:  4.3.1 Disclose contact details and its regulatory authority.  4.3.2 Disclose cost of products, including all fees and other associated charges.  4.3.3 Disclose the nature and value of benefits, where an advertisement refers to, or is linked to other value adding benefits.  4.3.4 Avoid mentioning the names of or making comparisons with competitors.  4.3.5 Avoid making reference to unaudited financial statements.  4.3.6 The content of advertisements shall be factual, unambiguous, not offensive, misleading, deceptive, or likely to cause damage.  4.3.7 The overall impression of advertisements shall not emphasize benefits while de-emphasizing its associated risks.  4.3.8 Unsolicited advertisements shall be at no cost to consumers.  4.3.9 Honor obligations in sales promotions as advertised and offered.  4.3.10 Establish a process to periodically evaluate the competence and conduct of employees.  4.3.11 Provide consumers with the option to opt-out of receiving marketing materials.  4.3.12 Not make opt-in for promotional materials a prerequisite for on-boarding consumers to products.  4.3.13 Be accountable for downplaying or dismissing warnings or cautionary statements in written sales materials.  4.3.14 Disclose to consumers potential or actual conflict of interest, particularly when the customer receives advice before executing agreements.  4.3.15 Promotional materials shall not use terminologies such as “free”, “zero cost”, or similar words or phrases, where associated costs to the product or service exists.  4.3.16 Use the word “free”, “zero cost”, only to indicate that the specific component of the product would not attract charges.  4.3.17 Notify the Director, Consumer Protection Department of the CBN prior to the commencement of advertisement by submitting a description of the content of the advertisement.
crmp.plain: The bank shall: 1. Clearly state contact information and regulatory authority in all ads. 2. Disclose all product costs, including fees and charges. 3. State the nature and value of advertised benefits. 4. Not reference competitors’ names or compare with them. 5. Not use unaudited financial statements in advertisements. 6. Ensure advertisements are factual, clear, respectful, and not misleading. 7. Present risks clearly without downplaying them compared to benefits. 8. Not charge customers for unsolicited advertisements. 9. Fulfill all offers made during promotions. 10. Regularly evaluate staff competence and conduct in sales and marketing. 11. Allow customers to opt out of marketing communications. 12. Not require opt-in to marketing materials as a condition for account opening. 13. Not dismiss or understate cautionary notes in sales materials. 14. Disclose any conflicts of interest when offering financial advice. 15. Avoid misleading words like “free” or “zero cost” unless absolutely true. 16. Only use “free” or “zero cost” when a specific product component is truly free. 17. Notify CBN Consumer Protection Department with ad content before publishing
crmp.riskDescription: - Regulatory penalties for misleading or non-compliant promotions - Legal liability for false claims or failure to deliver promised benefits - Consumer distrust and reputational damage - Loss of operating license for recurring violations
crmp.owner: - Chief Marketing Officer- Head of Compliance- Legal and Regulatory Affairs Team- Brand Communications Unit- Consumer Protection Desk
crmp.primaryControl: - Mandatory legal/compliance review of all advertisement materials - Marketing policy aligned with CBN Consumer Protection standards - Checklist to validate fee disclosure and benefit representation - Automated opt-out management system - Internal approvals and record-keeping of all promotions - Scheduled staff training on ethical promotions and disclosure requirements - System to track and report fulfillment of promotional commitments

crmp.source: Exposure Draft of the Revised Consumer Protection Regulations 2.0
crmp.title: UNFAIR CONTRACT TERMS
crmp.description: FSPs shall comply with the following minimum standards to ensure that terms and conditions in contracts are fair and reasonable:  4.4.1 Contracts with consumers shall not contain unfair terms. A contract term shall be considered unfair if it:  a. Eliminates or limits the liability of an FSP to loss caused to a consumer by misrepresentation, negligence or misleading information on its products or services.  b. Binds a consumer to an obligation while the corresponding obligation on the FSP is conditional.  c. Eliminates or limits FSP’s liability with respect to actions or commitments undertaken by their employees, agents, or intermediaries.  d. Allows unilateral change to a contract without stating the circumstances under which the change could be made.  e. Excludes or restricts any legal requirement on the part of an FSP to act with skill, care, diligence, or professionalism toward the consumer in connection with the provision of any product or service and/or any liability for failing to do so.  4.4.2 Unfair terms used in contracts are void and shall not be binding on consumers.  4.4.3 Where there is any doubt or ambiguity about the meaning of a term used in a contract, the interpretation most favorable to the consumer shall prevail.
crmp.plain: The bank must: 1. Ensure all consumer contracts do not contain unfair terms, such as:  a. Clauses that eliminate/limit liability for losses caused by misrepresentation, negligence, or misleading information.  b. Obligations imposed on the consumer while making the bank’s obligation conditional or unclear.  c. Clauses that limit the bank's liability for staff, agents, or intermediaries’ conduct.  d. Allowing unilateral contract changes without stating clear conditions.  e. Excluding the bank’s legal duty to act with skill, care, and diligence. 2. Recognize that unfair contract terms are void and unenforceable. 3. Ensure the interpretation most favorable to the consumer must apply if contract terms are ambiguous.
crmp.riskDescription: - Use of unfair terms can result in:  - Regulatory sanctions  - Legal challenges or lawsuits  - Loss of customer trust and reputational damage  - Contracts being declared void and unenforceable
crmp.owner: - Head, Legal & Compliance- Head of Products- Contract Management Unit- Risk Management Department
crmp.primaryControl: - Standardized contract templates vetted by Legal and Compliance. - Checklist for unfair terms during contract drafting and review. - Consumer-facing documents written in plain, clear language. - Legal review of all amendments or unilateral changes to consumer contracts. - Establish approval workflow for all new or revised contract terms. - Regular updates of contract templates based on evolving regulatory standards.

crmp.title: LENDING PRACTICES
crmp.description: FSPs shall comply with the following requirements:  4.5.1 Apply lending fees only to the extent of the amount disbursed in respect of term loans, except for fees that are applicable to committed facility.  4.5.2 Obtain customers’ written authorization where repayment of facility is sought before due date.  4.5.3 Assess customers’ capability to repay facilities in a sustainable manner taking into consideration their financial circumstances.  4.5.4 Monitor loan performance and upon early detection of repayment difficulties, engage customers on repayment options.  4.5.5 Not compel consumers to buy products or services, such as insurance or valuation from a particular third-party provider as a pre-condition for the grant of a credit facility, but can provide the option to choose from at least three (3) providers or as may be prescribed by CBN from time to time.  4.5.6 Ensure that guarantors confirm in writing that they have read and understood their commitments, potential implications, and the maximum amount they are guaranteeing.  4.5.7 Provide update to Guarantors immediately a facility is in default to enable parties (lender, borrower and guarantor) engage on repayment options, until the facility returns to performing status and the likelihood of the guarantors being called upon to discharge their commitments in the loan agreement becomes minimal.  4.5.8 Issue a Discharge Letter at no cost to customers within 5 working days after loan liquidation, and where the loan is guaranteed, the guarantor be notified accordingly.  4.5.9 Notify customers where loan requests are declined with reason(s) within 10 working days from the date of receipt.
crmp.plain: The bank must: 1. Only apply lending fees on the actual disbursed amount for term loans (except committed facilities). 2. Get written authorization from customers before collecting loan repayments earlier than due date. 3. Assess customer affordability based on their financial situation before granting loans. 4. Monitor loans and engage borrowers early when signs of difficulty in repayment are detected. 5. Allow customers to choose from at least three third-party providers (e.g. insurance, valuation) where services are required as part of a loan process. 6. Ensure guarantors confirm in writing that they understand their obligations and the guaranteed amount. 7. Update guarantors immediately when a loan is in default and continue engagement until the loan performs again. 8. Issue a Discharge Letter at no cost within 5 working days of loan repayment; guarantors must also be notified. 9. Inform customers within 10 working days with reasons when their loan application is declined.
crmp.riskDescription: Non-compliance could result in regulatory penalties, reputational damage, customer dissatisfaction, legal liability from aggrieved customers or guarantors, and increased default rates due to poor lending decisions.
crmp.owner: - Head of Retail/Consumer Lending- Legal & Compliance Unit- Credit Risk Department- Loan Operations Team- Relationship Managers
crmp.primaryControl: - Lending policy approved by Board - Affordability checks in loan origination system - Automated loan tracking tools - Loan decline templates- Standard operating procedure for loan closure

crmp.title: DEBT RECOVERY
crmp.description: To ensure that debt recovery processes are transparent, courteous, and fair, regulated entities shall:  4.6.1 Engage and give customers notice(s) of outstanding obligations prior to the commencement of a debt collection.  4.6.2 Initiate foreclosures only when other recovery options have been unsuccessful.  4.6.3 Give customers the option of a private sale, to be exercised within 30 days before commencing foreclosure, except where the customer waives the right.  4.6.4 Ensure that the net proceeds from foreclosures are immediately applied to the loan account and customers informed of the balance.  4.6.5 Provide customers with a report of the sale of the collateral. At a minimum, the report shall state the process, proceeds, incidental expenses, and net proceeds.  4.6.6 Be liable for the actions of their agents engaged for debt collection.  4.6.7 Not contact friends, employer, relatives, or neighbors of a customer for any information other than information on employment status, telephone numbers or address, except where the person has guaranteed the loan or has consented to be contacted.
crmp.plain: The bank as a regulated entity must: 1. Notify customers of unpaid debts before starting debt recovery actions. 2. Only initiate foreclosure if all other recovery methods have failed. 3. Offer customers a 30-day window to sell the collateral privately before foreclosure, unless they waive the right. 4. Immediately apply any foreclosure sale proceeds to the loan and inform the customer of the remaining balance. 5. Provide a detailed report to the customer after the sale of collateral, including process, proceeds, expenses, and net amount. 6. Be responsible for the conduct and actions of third-party agents or debt collectors. 7. Do not contact a borrower's relatives, neighbors, friends, or employer except to confirm address, phone, or employment – unless they are guarantors or have consented.
crmp.riskDescription: Improper or aggressive debt recovery practices can lead to regulatory sanctions, lawsuits, reputational harm, customer complaints, and loss of business license.
crmp.owner: - Credit Recovery & Collections Unit- Legal Department- Compliance Department- Customer Experience Unit- Third-party Collection Agents
crmp.primaryControl: - Standard notice templates for overdue accounts- Escalation procedures for foreclosure approval- Agent Code of Conduct- Collateral sales reporting template- Call logs and CRM audit trails

crmp.title: FORMAT AND MANNER OF DISCLOSURE
crmp.description: 5.1.1 Documents provided to consumers shall:  a. Be written in clear, simple English language and legible with a minimum font size of 10 and spacing of 1.0.  b. Not be misleading or deceptive.  c. Be provided in a durable form for ease of future reference.  d. State the name and contact details of the FSP.  e. State the type of license of the FSP and provide the name as well as contact details of the regulatory authority.  5.1.2 Clearly explain technical terms to consumers to aid understanding and decision.  5.1.3 Disclose the agreed communication channel(s) to be used for all correspondences and adopt same for information dissemination.  5.1.4 Display at customer engagement points, accurate information on all products and services, including:  a. Prime and maximum lending rates.  b. Deposit rates.  c. Applicable exchange rates for transactions that require currency conversion.  d. How to lodge a complaint to the FSP and escalation option to the CBN where necessary.  5.1.5 Ensure that their websites and other information dissemination channels are functional and regularly updated with the current features of products and services offered.
crmp.plain: The bank shall: 1. Provide documents to consumers that:  a. Are written in clear, simple English, minimum font size 10, and spacing 1.0.  b. Are not misleading or deceptive.  c. Are given in a durable format for future reference.  d. Clearly state the name and contact details of the bank.  e. Include the license type of the bank and contact details of its regulator. 2. Explain all technical terms clearly to ensure consumer understanding. 3. Disclose and use the agreed communication channel for all customer correspondence. 4. Display at all customer engagement points:  a. Lending rates (prime and max)  b. Deposit rates  c. Exchange rates where applicable  d. Complaint procedure and CBN escalation steps. 5. Ensure websites and all info channels are functional and regularly updated.
crmp.riskDescription: - Inadequate or misleading disclosures can result in:  - Regulatory sanctions or fines  - Loss of customer trust  - Legal action from misled consumers  - Customer churn or reputational damage
crmp.owner: - Product Managers - Compliance & Legal Team - Corporate Communications - Customer Experience Unit - IT/Web Team
crmp.primaryControl: - All product documents reviewed by Legal before public release. - Content template standardization for disclosures. - Pre-launch checklists for regulatory and consumer protection compliance. - Quarterly audits of all product-related content online and in-branch. - Centralized update control for websites and marketing content.

crmp.source: Exposure Draft of the Revised Consumer Protection Regulations 2.0
crmp.title: DISCLOSURE OF TERMS AND CONDITIONS
crmp.description: FSPs shall comply with the following minimum standards during the lifecycle of contractual relationship with consumers:  5.2.1 Disclose in writing, all terms and conditions of a product or service on offer, as well as the features, risks, benefits, fees, and other associated charges.  5.2.2 Provide oral explanation on contractual agreements:  a. At customer’s request; or  b. If it is obvious that the customer is vulnerable or cannot understand the agreement.  5.2.3 The phrase “Terms and Conditions Apply” or any other phrase conveying a similar meaning shall not be used, except where such terms have been disclosed in the contract. Where terms and conditions are disclosed in other medium accessible to consumers, the consumers attention shall be drawn.  5.2.4 Make opt-out option available for customers to unsubscribe from digital services at the time of establishing the contractual relationship.  5.2.5 Provide information on cancellation or switching procedures, including when products and services are delivered through agents or digital channels.  5.2.6 Disclose in contracts, the possibility of variations in interest or foreign exchange rates due to changes in market conditions.  5.2.7 Allow consumers a minimum of two (2) working days from date of receipt, to review draft contract before execution except where they waive this in writing.  5.2.8 Give consumers a cooling-off period of three (3) working days after the execution of a credit contract, within which they may cancel without having to pay any penalty or charges. However, the consumer may waive the option with written notification.  5.2.9 Embed a pre-read or pause function before any purchase decision or transaction via digital channels, to enable brief time to review transaction and key terms and conditions before authorization or consent.  5.2.10 Provide information on product usage and how to obtain support services when the need arises.  5.2.11 Credit contracts shall contain the following:  a. Name and contact details of customer.  b. Type, purpose of credit, tenor of the contract, amount or credit limit, and moratorium (where applicable).  c. Applicable interest rate, details of lending fees including late payment/default (where applicable), variable rate information (where applicable) and total cost of the credit.  d. Key features and risks, conditions precedent to drawdown, insurance requirements (where applicable), early liquidation terms.  e. Applicable Annual Percentage Rate (APR) to be calculated using the formula stated in Annexures B and C.  f. Repayment schedule for term loans, collateral pledged and its estimated value.  5.2.12 Provide consumers, a Key Facts Statement (KFS) in the format attached as Annexure A stating a summary of key information on consumer loans.  5.2.13 State the rights and responsibilities of consumers, including the conditions that may lead to termination or cancellation of contract.  5.2.14 State how disputes can be resolved and the contact information of the established internal complaints handling units as well as the details of the external complaints’ resolution unit.  5.2.15 Implement disclosures that are commensurate to targeted consumer segments.
crmp.plain: The bank must: 1. Disclose in writing all terms, conditions, features, risks, benefits, fees, and charges of a product/service. 2. Provide oral explanation of contracts if requested or if the customer is vulnerable or lacks understanding. 3. Use “Terms and Conditions Apply” only if the terms are fully disclosed and accessible; draw consumer’s attention to external media if used. 4. Provide an opt-out option from digital services at the start of contract. 5. Disclose cancellation/switching procedures (including for agents and digital channels). 6. Disclose in contracts the possibility of rate variations due to market changes. 7. Allow 2 working days review period before contract execution (unless waived). 8. Allow 3 working days cooling-off period after executing a credit contract (unless waived). 9. Implement a pre-read or pause function before digital purchases or approvals. 10. Provide product usage info and support contact details. 11. Credit contracts must contain:  a. Customer name/contact  b. Credit type, amount, tenor, purpose, moratorium  c. Interest rate, all charges, late/default terms  d. Key risks, drawdown conditions, insurance if applicable  e. APR and how it's calculated (Annex B & C)  f. Repayment schedule, collateral, estimated value 12. Provide a Key Facts Statement (KFS) (Annex A). 13. State consumer rights/responsibilities including termination terms. 14. Provide complaints resolution process (internal & external contacts). 15. Tailor disclosures to targeted consumer segments.
crmp.riskDescription: - Non-disclosure or inadequate disclosure can lead to:  - Consumer complaints or lawsuits  - Contract disputes  - Regulatory sanctions for unfair consumer treatment  - Loss of consumer trust and reputational damage
crmp.owner: - Legal & Compliance Department - Product Managers - Risk Management - IT/Digital Channels Unit - Customer Service & Relationship Officers
crmp.primaryControl: - Use standard contract templates vetted by legal/compliance. - Implement digital contract platforms with embedded pause/pre-read functions. - Pre-launch legal and consumer protection review of all new products. - Training of front-line staff on disclosure obligations. - System-enforced delay (2-day review period) and cooling-off period for credit contracts. - Built-in APR calculator tool and KFS generator. - Standard cancellation/opt-out procedures on all platforms.

crmp.title: NOTIFICATION OF CHANGES IN RATES, TERMS AND CONDITIONS
crmp.description: FSPs shall comply with the following minimum standards to promote transparency in dealing with customers:  5.3.1 Not vary terms and conditions, without the consent of customers. However, this does not apply to interest rate variations.  5.3.2 Notify customers of possible variations in interest rates and other terms and conditions, through the agreed channel of communication. In the case of interest rates, the notice shall state:  a. Reason for the variation.  b. Commencement date.  c. Revised repayment schedule (where necessary).  d. Alternatives available such as concession, restructuring, re- negotiation, opt-out or termination of the contract.  5.3.3 Notify consumers in default of credit repayment within 3 working days from the day of default, that a default charge would be applied after 7 working days in the case of Deposit Money Banks (DMBs), and 3 working days for Other Financial Institutions (OFIs).
crmp.plain: The bank shall:  1. Not vary the terms and conditions of contracts without the customer’s consent, except for interest rate changes. 2. Provide advance notice of possible variations in interest rates or terms using the agreed communication channel. 3. In case of interest rate changes, notify customers with details of:  a. The reason for the change  b. The start date of the new rate  c. The updated repayment schedule, if applicable  d. Available alternatives such as concessions, restructuring, renegotiation, opting out, or terminating the contract 4. If a customer defaults on repayment, the bank shall:  a. Notify the customer of the default within 3 working days  b. Inform them that a default charge will apply after:   - 7 working days for Deposit Money Banks (DMBs)   - 3 working days for Other Financial Institutions (OFIs)
crmp.riskDescription: - Lack of timely and proper communication regarding changes can result in:  - Regulatory non-compliance  - Customer disputes and dissatisfaction  - Financial penalties and reputational damage
crmp.owner: - Legal & Compliance Unit- Customer Service Department- Product/Loan Management Team- IT/CRM Team
crmp.primaryControl: - Integrate system triggers to auto-generate notifications for changes and defaults - Use standardized templates with all required elements (reason, effective date, alternatives) - Include rate variation provisions in contracts and disclose clearly - Maintain audit trail of all customer notifications and confirmations - Align CRM systems with regulatory timing for default communications

crmp.title: ACCOUNT STATEMENT
crmp.description: FSPs shall comply with the following minimum standards to promote disclosure of financial transactions:  5.4.1 Provide monthly statements (confirmation/investment advice as the case may be) for all products and account types, at no cost.  5.4.2 Make account balances and statements available on customers’ request.  5.4.3 Notify consumers of transactions on their account immediately it occurs. At a minimum, the notification shall include date, currency, amount, payer, transaction reference, channel, and the cleared account balance.  5.4.4 Notify consumers when their accounts have become inactive or dormant, and the related consequences.  5.4.5 Ensure clarity in descriptions on account statements. At a minimum, it shall include, transaction reference, payer transaction channel, location, and account balance.  5.4.6 Disclose default charges in account statements separate from the interest charge.  5.4.7 Provide consumers with a closing statement when a contract is terminated or concluded.
crmp.plain: The bank must: 1. Send monthly account statements or investment advice for all account types free of charge. 2. Make account balances and statements available upon customer request. 3. Immediately notify customers of every account transaction with key details: date, currency, amount, payer, transaction reference, channel, and cleared balance. 4. Alert customers when accounts become inactive or dormant, stating the implications. 5. Ensure clear descriptions in statements with transaction details including reference, channel, location, and balance. 6. Clearly separate default charges from interest in statements. 7. Issue a closing statement when a product or contract ends.
crmp.riskDescription: Failure to comply with these provisions can result in poor transparency, regulatory penalties, loss of customer trust, disputes, or miscommunication over charges and balances.
crmp.owner: - Operations Department- Customer Service Team- IT / Core Banking System Admins- Compliance Department
crmp.primaryControl: - Automated monthly e-statements - Real-time transaction alerts (SMS/email) - Dormancy alert systems - Core banking integration for real-time balances - Statement description format templates

crmp.title: PROTECTION OF CONSUMER ASSETS AND PRIVACY
crmp.description: To ensure adequate protection of consumer assets and privacy, FSPs shall comply with the following minimum standards:  6.1 DATA PROTECTION 6.1.1 Protect the privacy and confidentiality of consumer information and assets against unauthorized access and be accountable for acts or omissions in respect thereof.  6.1.2 Embed personal data protection in the design of products or systems.  6.1.3 Obtain written consent of consumers to collect and process their personal data for specific purposes and provide them with the option to withdraw the consent at any time.  6.1.4 Not share personal data of consumers to a third party without their express consent and provide details of information to be shared.  6.1.5 Design clear and simple “Opt-in” and “Opt-Out” options for data sharing with 3rd parties.  6.1.6 Review data processing and privacy procedures to ensure that consumers’ data are accurate and used only for the purposes for which it was initially obtained.  6.2 FRAUD PREVENTION 6.2.1 Protect customers’ assets against fraud or misuse at all times and be liable for losses arising from breach of required controls.  6.2.2 Test product suitability with consumers and make necessary modifications to reduce the incidence of fraud or transaction errors.  6.2.3 Implement the following measures across transaction channels:  a. Multi-variant customer identification and multifactor authentication mechanisms for transactions consummated.  b. Automated transaction monitoring, alert functions and behavioral monitoring to detect and prevent fraud.  6.2.4 Sensitize customers on fraud threats or scams.  6.2.5 State and periodically communicate procedures for reporting suspicious, unauthorized, fraud, lost or stolen payment instruments and/or authentication information to consumers.  6.2.6 Provide secure and simple user interfaces for digital financial services that will minimize the risk of mistake or double transactions.
crmp.plain: The bank must ensure the protection of consumer data and assets by doing the following:  Data Protection 1. Safeguard consumer personal information and financial data from unauthorized access. 2. Build data protection into the design of systems and financial products. 3. Get written permission from consumers before collecting/using their data and allow them to withdraw that consent at any time. 4. Only share consumer data with third parties when the consumer agrees in writing and is informed of what data will be shared. 5. Design easy-to-use opt-in/opt-out features for data sharing.6. Regularly review data practices to ensure data is correct and used only for its original purpose.  Fraud Prevention 1. Keep customers’ money safe from fraud and take responsibility if systems fail. 2. Test products with consumers to fix issues that might lead to fraud. 3. Deploy the following controls:   - Strong customer ID and multifactor authentication   - Automated systems to monitor and flag suspicious transactions 4. Educate customers about fraud risks and scams. 5. Provide clear instructions for reporting fraud, stolen cards, or unauthorized activity. 6. Design secure and user-friendly digital platforms to reduce errors or duplicate transactions.
crmp.riskDescription: - Breaches of personal data and privacy due to poor access control or data sharing without consent. - Financial loss due to fraud, phishing, identity theft, or inadequate digital platform design. - Regulatory sanctions and reputational damage due to non-compliance with data and fraud requirements.
crmp.owner: - Data Protection Officer (DPO) - Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) - Head, Digital Banking - IT Security/Infrastructure Team - Customer Education Team - Compliance Department
crmp.primaryControl: - Data Protection Policy (aligned with NDPA) - Data Sharing Agreements - Consent forms and opt-in/out options - Multifactor authentication - Fraud monitoring software - Cybersecurity awareness campaigns

crmp.title: FINANCIAL LITERACY AND AWARENESS
crmp.description: To enhance financial literacy and awareness, FSPs shall comply with the following minimum standards:  7.1 Design and implement consumer education programs for various segments, to:  a. Build skills, knowledge, understanding and confidence in the use of financial products and services.  b. Safeguard account and confidential information.  7.2 Disseminate consumer education and awareness programs through diverse channels that are appropriate for various consumer segments.  7.3 Disseminate fraud prevention tips in English or local languages (where applicable) to all customer segments through appropriate channels.  7.4 Provide information that will enable consumers differentiate digital financial services from conventional banking products.  7.5 Render quarterly returns on financial literacy programs conducted.  7.6 Provide user education at product sign-up stage.  7.7 Ensure access to information on all product offerings to enable consumers make informed decisions.  7.8 Contribute resources towards industry-wide implementation of financial literacy and capability programs.
crmp.plain: The bank must: 1. Create and implement education programs tailored to different consumer segments to build knowledge, skills, and confidence in using financial products. 2. Educate consumers on protecting their account and confidential information. 3. Disseminate financial literacy programs through various suitable channels for different consumer segments. 4. Share fraud prevention tips in English and relevant local languages via appropriate channels. 5. Explain differences between digital and traditional financial services to consumers. 6. Report quarterly on all financial literacy initiatives conducted. 7. Provide product education at the point of signing up new consumers. 8. Ensure product information is easily accessible to support informed decision-making. 9. Support industry-wide financial literacy programs by contributing resources.
crmp.riskDescription: - Inadequate consumer education may lead to: ▪ Increased cases of fraud and cybercrime ▪ Low customer trust and satisfaction ▪ Regulatory sanctions for non-compliance ▪ Poor usage of digital platforms or financial products
crmp.owner: - Head of Compliance- Corporate Communications- Financial Inclusion/CSR Team- Product Managers- IT/Digital Channels Team
crmp.primaryControl: - Develop a financial literacy strategy with measurable goals and timelines - Use multi-lingual content and diverse media (SMS, email, radio, social media, webinars) - Track and report quarterly to regulators - Integrate product awareness modules during onboarding - Maintain content approval and review processes for accuracy and relevance

crmp.title: INTERNAL COMPLAINT RESOLUTION
crmp.description: Complaints shall first be lodged with the FSP for timely resolution. For effective resolution of complaints, FSPs shall:  8.1.1 Provide access to efficient and free complaint resolution mechanisms.  8.1.2 Develop policies and processes on complaints handling that will guarantee fairness, transparency, responsiveness, and independence of the complaint handling mechanism.  8.1.3 Allocate adequate resources and structure for complaints handling under the oversight of an Executive Compliance Officer or its equivalent in Other Financial Institutions.  8.1.4 Designate a function for complaints handling independent of other business functions taking into consideration, the nature and complexity of their business.  8.1.5 Provide information on how to lodge a complaint, including the type of information to be provided by the complainant.  8.1.6 Disclose contact details, channels for lodging complaints, timelines for resolution and options for escalation at all customer engagement points. Where it is not practicable to comply with this, refer customers to where the information required could be obtained.  8.1.7 Make available a range of channels (such as walk-in, telephone, email, call center, portals, website, and social media) for submitting complaints appropriate to the type of consumers served.  8.1.8 Upon receipt of a complaint (inclusive of oral submission), communicate to the consumer immediately an acknowledgment containing:  a. A unique identification or tracking number,  b. Contact details of the complaints desk,  c. Expected resolution timeline,  d. Escalation options; and  e. An assurance that the complaint is being addressed.  8.1.9 Ensure that staff responsible for handling complaints declare any conflict of interest that may affect their objectivity.  8.1.10 Integrate all complaints collection channels to the enterprise complaints management platform.  8.1.11 Provide toll-free telephone lines for customers to make enquiries and lodge complaints.  8.1.12 Continuously engage customers until complaints are fully resolved.  8.1.13 Use the unique identification or tracking number in all correspondence with the complainant.  8.1.14 Keep records of all complaints, including transcripts of verbal complaint for a minimum of 6 years.  8.1.15 Provide emergency channels for reporting time-sensitive issues especially fraud-related complaints at all times.  8.1.16 Reconstruct customers’ accounts to establish underpayment or excess charges, where applicable.  8.1.17 Refund identified excess charges, non-payment, under-payment of interest on deposits or unauthorized debits to the customer’s account along with interest as provided in the extant Monetary, Credit, Foreign Trade and Exchange Policy Guidelines or any regulation issued by the CBN.  8.1.18 Resolve complaints received within the time specified in the Timelines for Complaints Resolution by Institutions.  8.1.19 Provide a Summary Resolution Communication (SRC) for resolved complaints to the complainant within 24 hours after resolution. The summary shall convey at a minimum:  a. The basis of the decision(s).  b. The right of appeal available to the complainant for a second level review by the entity.  c. The right of escalation to the CBN, or other Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) where the complainant is dissatisfied.  8.1.20 Where a complainant is dissatisfied with a decision of an FSP, the complainant shall, within 30 days from the date of the receipt of the SRC, request in writing for a second level review.  8.1.21 A complaint shall be considered resolved where the complainant has indicated acceptance of the resolution in writing within 30 days after the receipt of the SRC, otherwise the complaint shall be deemed resolved or closed in the records of the FSP.  8.1.22 Upon receipt of a request for a second level review, the FSP shall review and communicate decision(s) within the timelines for complaints resolution for second level review.  8.1.23 Submit a Root Cause Analysis Report (RCAR) on quarterly basis to capture recurring complaint types, category and code, number of occurrences, root cause(s), planned remedial actions and implementation timelines. The report should be submitted to the Director, Consumer Protection Department, CBN on or before the 5th day of January, April, July, and October respectively.  8.1.24 Report complaints statistics in annual reports and the abridged Financial Statement in line with the approved format provided in Annexure D or any other format as may be prescribed by the CBN from time to time.
crmp.plain: The bank must have fair and easy ways for customers to complain when things go wrong. These complaints should be handled by a well-trained, independent team with enough resources. Customers must be told how to complain, where to do it, and how long it will take. Institutions must allow complaints through many channels like walk-ins, phone, email, and social media.  Once a complaint is received, it should be acknowledged immediately with a tracking number and contact information. The bank must stay in touch with the customer until the complaint is resolved. Staff handling complaints should be honest and declare any conflicts of interest.  All complaints (even verbal ones) should be recorded and kept for six years. Customers must be refunded with interest if they were overcharged. Emergency channels must be available for fraud-related complaints. A summary of the resolution must be given within 24 hours, and customers must be informed of their rights to appeal or escalate.  The bank must also send quarterly reports to the CBN about complaint trends and how they’re being addressed, and include complaint statistics in their annual reports.
crmp.riskDescription: - Regulatory penalties for delayed, unfair, or untracked complaint handling. - Poor customer trust and reputational damage from unresolved or mishandled complaints. - Risk of litigation due to non-compliance with redress timelines and transparency obligations. - System inefficiencies if complaints are not tracked, resolved, or addressed at root cause level.
crmp.owner: - Executive Compliance Officer - Complaints Management Unit - Customer Service Team - Legal/Compliance Department - IT/System Integration Team - Internal Audit
crmp.primaryControl: - Complaints Management Policy - Consumer redress workflow with timelines - Dedicated complaints team with oversight - Toll-free numbers and online channels - Customer communication scripts and FAQs - Tracking systems for SRC and RCAR submission

crmp.title: COMPLIANCE
crmp.description: The Executive Compliance Officer shall be responsible for ensuring compliance with this Guidelines. In the case of Other Financial Institutions, the responsibility shall expressly be assigned to a Senior Management staff.
crmp.plain: The bank shall: 1. Designate an Executive Compliance Officer to take full responsibility for ensuring compliance with the Consumer Protection Guidelines.
crmp.riskDescription: - Absence of clear accountability for consumer protection compliance may result in: ▪ Regulatory breaches ▪ Operational lapses ▪ Penalties and reputational damage

crmp.title: Responsible Business Conduct
crmp.description: Financial Institutions shall observe high ethical standards and professionalism in their business transactions with consumers. They are required to assess the financial capabilities of consumers and offer only suitable products/services based on their needs and capability. In addition, they shall provide channels for consumers to make enquiries and complaints. The following specific areas will be addressed under Responsible Business Conduct:  Communication: All requests for information must be responded to timely and with clarity.  Provision of financial advice: FIs shall provide consumers with objective advice to enable them make informed decisions.  Responsible lending: FIs shall carry out proper credit worthiness assessment on consumers before granting credit to avoid reckless lending.  Debt collection: financial institutions shall adopt debt recovery processes that are courteous and fair to consumers. Consumers must be proactively engaged and given early notice of outstanding obligations prior to the commencement of debt collection efforts.  Sales promotion: marketing of products and services using incentives should be carried out in an ethical and professional manner.
crmp.plain: The Bank shall:  1. Observe high ethical standards and professionalism in all business transactions with consumers. 2. Assess consumers’ financial capabilities and offer only products or services that are suitable to their needs and financial situation. 3. Provide channels for consumers to make enquiries and complaints. 4. Respond to all requests for information from consumers in a timely and clear manner. 5. Provide consumers with objective financial advice to support informed decision-making. 6. Carry out proper creditworthiness assessments before granting credit, to avoid reckless lending. 7. Ensure that debt recovery processes are fair and courteous, giving consumers early notice and proactive engagement before starting debt collection actions. 8. Conduct sales promotions and marketing using incentives in an ethical and professional manner.
crmp.riskDescription: Reputational damage, consumer complaints, regulatory sanctions, mis-selling, credit defaults, unfair practices
crmp.owner: All Departments: Compliance, Risk, Sales, Advisory, Customer Service, Collections, Marketing
crmp.primaryControl: Code of Conduct, Ethics Training, Suitability and Credit Assessment Tools, Complaint Channels, SLA for Response, Marketing Approval Process

crmp.title: Communication
crmp.description: 1. All requests for information shall be responded to clearly, timeously and in writing or via the customers means of communication with appropriate documentation. For this purpose, mere acknowledgement of a request would not suffice as a response.  2. In any communication with customers, FIs shall act in the best interest of customers. Remuneration and incentives structure in the industry shall encourage ethics and integrity.  3. Customer shall be notified when an activity threatens to violate the terms of contract.
crmp.plain: The bank shall: 1. Respond to customer information requests clearly, promptly, and in writing or via their preferred channel, with appropriate supporting documents. Acknowledgment alone is not sufficient. 2. Communicate with customers in their best interest, guided by ethics and integrity. 3. Notify customers if an action may breach contract terms.
crmp.riskDescription: - Delayed or unclear communication may lead to: ▪ Regulatory breaches ▪ Customer dissatisfaction or complaints ▪ Loss of trust and reputational damage ▪ Potential legal liabilities
crmp.owner: - Head of Customer Experience - Executive Compliance Officer - Relationship Managers - Contact Centre Supervisor
crmp.primaryControl: - Establish and monitor response time SLAs for all customer queries - Enable omni-channel communication platforms (email, SMS, app, etc.) - Train staff on ethical and timely communication - Automate alerts for potential contract breach triggers

crmp.title: Provision of Financial Advice
crmp.description: 1. Financial Institutions shall act in the best interest of consumers in the provision of advice and execution of transactions. For consumers to make informed decisions in choosing financial products and services, they must be acquainted with the features, costs, risks, penalties, terms and conditions. Thus, before consumers sign up for any financial products, FIs shall: a) Give clear information on the features of the services and products; b) Assess whether the products or services of interest suit the consumers’ needs. Where a product requested does not meet the needs of the customer, the FI is obliged to advise or caution the customer in writing before granting such; and c) Assess the consumers’ ability to fulfill the terms and conditions associated with the financial products and services;  2. Financial institutions shall provide appropriate financial advice to consumers before the sale of any financial product or service. For financial products or services that are complex or potentially risky to consumers, financial institutions shall document pre-contractual and subsequent deliberations with consumers. The records shall reflect the financial institutions’ efforts in taking the aforementioned steps (Section 2.2.2.(1)) before reaching an agreement with the consumer on the product or service. In addition, records of meetings must be acknowledged by the consumer.  3. The CBN shall use appropriate mechanisms (such as examining FIs’ records of pre-contractual deliberations with customers (see Section 2.2.2.(2)), mystery shopping amongst others) to monitor financial institutions and ensure that they properly engage customers prior to the sale of financial products or services.
crmp.plain: The bank shall: 1. Provide financial advice that is in the best interest of consumers. 2. Before offering financial products/services, FIs must:     a) Disclose clear product/service features, costs, risks, and terms.     b) Assess if the product fits the consumer’s needs; if not, caution the consumer in writing.     c) Evaluate the consumer’s ability to meet product terms. 3. Keep documented records of advice sessions and have them acknowledged by the consumer for complex or risky products. 4. Allow the CBN access to such records for supervision (e.g., mystery shopping).
crmp.riskDescription: - Failure to offer appropriate financial advice and document advisory interactions can result in: ▪ Breach of regulatory expectations ▪ Customer disputes or litigation ▪ Fines or sanctions by the CBN ▪ Damage to consumer trust and institutional reputation
crmp.owner: - Head of Product Management - Executive Compliance Officer - Customer Relationship Managers - Advisory Team
crmp.primaryControl: - Implement Customer Suitability & Risk Profiling tools - Provide product fact sheets and risk disclosures for each offering - Require documented customer acknowledgments of advisory sessions - Introduce a compliance checklist for high-risk or complex products - Maintain audit trails for all advisory engagements
