crmp.title: Responsible Lending
crmp.description: 1. To promote positive credit culture in the industry, FIs shall establish structures to prohibit reckless and predatory lending.  2. Financial institutions shall provide credit counselling to prevent consumers’ indebtedness due to limited financial knowledge. Credit counselling is the process of educating consumers on borrowing and debt settlement.  3. Credit counselling facilities shall be available and accessible to all consumers. Consumers shall be made aware of such services and shall be encouraged to take advantage of such facilities provided by the financial institutions.  4. FIs shall provide detailed information on the terms and conditions of a credit agreement to consumers prior to executing the loan agreement. Such information must at a minimum include the pricing, repayment schedule, repayment amount, tenure and opt out options.
crmp.plain: The bank shall: 1. Establish systems to prohibit reckless and predatory lending practices. 2. Offer credit counselling services to consumers to improve financial knowledge and prevent over-indebtedness. 3. Ensure that credit counselling is accessible to all consumers and actively inform and encourage them to use the service. 4. Disclose detailed credit terms to consumers before they sign any credit agreement. Disclosure must include:     - Pricing     - Repayment schedule and amount     - Tenure     - Opt-out options
crmp.riskDescription: - Inadequate consumer education and poor disclosure may lead to: ▪ Consumer defaults and credit risk ▪ Regulatory sanctions ▪ Reputational damage ▪ Increased cost of debt recovery
crmp.owner: - Head of Credit - Executive Compliance Officer - Loan Officers - Customer Service and Advisory Team
crmp.primaryControl: - Integrate credit risk assessments and debt-to-income analysis before loan approval - Provide mandatory credit counselling for all loan applicants - Make credit counselling visible and accessible via digital platforms and branches - Use loan summary sheets to explain key loan terms before signing

crmp.title: Debt Collection
crmp.description: 1. The CBN shall set guidelines for ethical debt collection practices in the industry. These guidelines shall be based on dialogue, respect for the consumers’ privacy and longevity of consumer-FI relationships amongst others.  2. Where consumers are unable to meet their financial obligations, financial institutions shall be encouraged to adopt fair and ethical debt recovery practices.  3. FIs shall ensure that personnel assigned to recover debts are properly trained. Consumers shall be informed in advance before a recovery process is initiated.
crmp.plain: The bank shall: 1. Adhere to CBN’s ethical debt collection guidelines, including maintaining respect, consumer privacy, and the integrity of consumer relationships. 2. Adopt fair and ethical recovery practices when consumers default on obligations. 3. Ensure debt recovery staff are properly trained. 4. Inform consumers ahead of any debt recovery action.
crmp.riskDescription: - Unethical or aggressive debt recovery could lead to: ▪ Regulatory penalties ▪ Litigation and legal liabilities ▪ Reputational harm ▪ Erosion of consumer trust
crmp.owner: - Head of Recovery & Collections - Compliance Officer - Customer Relationship Management Team - Legal and Ethics Officers
crmp.primaryControl: - Implement a Debt Collection Code of Conduct based on CBN guidelines - Conduct mandatory training for recovery personnel - Establish pre-notification protocols before initiating recovery - Monitor and audit collection activities regularly

crmp.title: Sales Promotion
crmp.description: 1. Sales promotions or related activities shall be conducted professionally and ethically. In a bid to generate increased business volumes or attract new customers, financial institutions shall provide factual information and shall not mislead consumers.  2. Financial institutions shall be required to fulfil the terms of promotional offers. In addition, before the launch of any sales promotion, FIs shall provide the CBN with evidence of capability to manage the influx of customers without diminishing service quality.
crmp.plain: The bank shall: 1. Conduct all sales promotions ethically and professionally using only factual, non-misleading information. 2. Fulfill all promises made under promotional offers. 3. Obtain CBN approval by providing evidence of the institution’s capacity to handle increased customer traffic before launching a promotional campaign.
crmp.riskDescription: - Misleading promotions or failure to meet advertised promises can result in: ▪ Regulatory penalties from the CBN ▪ Customer complaints and reputational damage ▪ Service failure due to unanticipated customer volume ▪ Litigation and financial loss
crmp.owner: - Marketing Department - Compliance Unit - Legal Department - Customer Service/Experience Unit
crmp.primaryControl: - Implement a Sales Promotion Policy aligned with CBN requirements - Obtain internal compliance and legal vetting before campaign launch - Submit required evidence of capacity to CBN before launch - Establish tracking system to monitor fulfillment of promotional terms

crmp.title: Disclosure and Transparency
crmp.description: Financial institutions shall provide accurate information on financial products and services to consumers at all times to enable them make informed decisions. Such information must be timely, detailed and clear. The primary coverage areas to be addressed are:  Contract terms: contract terms should contain adequate information that will enhance consumers’ decision making process prior to execution of the contract. Financial institutions shall also inform consumers of the possibility of variations in terms and conditions of contracts due to changes in economic conditions before such contracts are executed. Customers shall be provided with the statement of financial position at all times.  Notice of Variations: FIs shall give prior notice to consumers within the time specified in contracts, before implementing variations in terms and conditions of contracts.  Advertisement: Advertisements and marketing materials must convey complete and accurate information on the products and services being advertised.
crmp.plain: The Bank shall:  1. Provide accurate, timely, detailed, and clear information on financial products and services to enable consumers make informed decisions. 2. Ensure that all contract terms include sufficient information to help consumers evaluate and understand the agreement before signing. 3. Inform consumers, before contract execution, about the potential for changes in contract terms due to economic conditions. 4. Make consumers’ statements of financial position available at all times. 5. Issue prior notice to consumers — within the period specified in the contract — before applying any changes to contract terms and conditions. 6. Ensure that all advertisements and marketing materials contain complete and accurate information about the products and services offered.
crmp.riskDescription: Consumer confusion, misinterpretation, mis-selling, reputational damage, regulatory penalties for misleading info or lack of transparency
crmp.owner: Legal, Compliance, Product Teams, Marketing, Customer Service
crmp.primaryControl: Product Disclosure Templates, Review of Contracts and Ads, Pre-approval of materials, Notice systems

crmp.title: Contract Terms
crmp.description: 1. Financial Institutions shall disclose and document all terms and conditions including inherent risks, fees, charges and other payments to be made by a consumer for a product or service.  2. The CBN shall issue guidelines on disclosure requirements for products and services in contract agreements between financial institutions and consumers of financial products and services. These guidelines at a minimum shall cover areas such as: a) fees and charges; b) penalties (prepayment costs and default charges); c) interests (payable or receivable); d) payment and termination modalities; and e) risks.  3. Financial Institutions shall proactively inform consumers of the possibility of variations in terms and conditions of contracts.  4. Contractual agreements shall be precise and clear. Information must be communicated in simple language to avoid misinterpretation. Contractual agreements must be in legible font size. Where technical terms are used, the financial institution shall ensure that such technical terms are clearly explained to the understanding of the consumer to avoid confusion or miscommunication.  5. Financial Institutions shall conspicuously display specific and up-to-date information (such as certificate of incorporation, banking license, interest rates, foreign exchange rates, helpdesk contact details etc.) at customer engagement areas.  6. Financial institutions shall provide financial calculation tools on their websites to assist consumers to perform simple calculations that may be required to ascertain the suitability of certain financial products. In addition, financial institutions have a responsibility to make reasonable effort towards ensuring that consumers of financial products are knowledgeable about the products/service they wish to purchase.  7. The CBN shall publish rates offered by financial institutions to enable consumers make informed decisions in the selection of suitable products and services.  8. While the contract subsists, customers shall be provided with the statement of financial position at all times such as loan statement, account statement.
crmp.plain: The bank shall: 1. Disclose and document all terms and conditions, including risks, fees, charges, and payments for each product or service. 2. Adhere to CBN disclosure guidelines covering fees, penalties, interests, termination procedures, and risks. 3. Proactively inform customers about possible changes in contract terms. 4. Ensure contracts are clear, precise, legible, and written in simple language; explain any technical terms. 5. Display updated corporate and product information at customer engagement points. 6. Provide financial tools on website and educate customers about products. 7. Respect CBN’s publication of rates for transparency. 8. Make financial statements (e.g., loan/account statements) available at all times during contract lifecycle.

crmp.title: Notice of Variation
crmp.description: 1. Within a minimum timeline specified by the CBN, financial institutions shall notify consumers about changes to terms and conditions of contracts prior to the implementation of such changes.  2. Notice to consumers on variations to terms and conditions must at a minimum contain the following details: a) Changes in rates / charges (existing rate and new rate that is being introduced) b) Rationale for variation; c) Commencement date of new terms and conditions; d) Revised repayment schedule in line with the new rates (where applicable); e) Options available to the consumer, including the opt-out options.  3. Variation notice must be at no cost to the consumer and there must be evidence of dispatch to address on file or via the usual means of communication with the consumer.  4. FIs shall respond to requests for waivers, concession or other variations on credit facilities within specified timelines, failing which such requests would be deemed to have been accepted.
crmp.plain: The bank shall: 1. Notify consumers of changes to contract terms and conditions within the minimum timeline set by the CBN, before implementing such changes. 2. Ensure that the notice includes:     a) Existing and revised rates/charges     b) Justification for the changes     c) Commencement date of the new terms     d) Revised repayment schedule (if applicable)     e) Options available to the customer (including opt-out) 3. Issue variation notices at no cost to consumers and provide evidence of delivery through preferred communication channels. 4. Respond to customer requests for waivers, concessions, or variations within the CBN’s timeline or the request is deemed approved.
crmp.riskDescription: - Failure to issue variation notices or delays in response may result in: ▪ Regulatory penalties for non-compliance ▪ Erosion of customer trust ▪ Legal actions or disputes over contract terms ▪ Loss of business or account closures
crmp.owner: - Legal & Compliance Department - Credit Risk Department - Retail/Corporate Lending Teams - Customer Service Unit
crmp.primaryControl: - Create a standard variation notice template including required fields - Embed compliance checkpoints in contract modification workflows - Track dispatch and delivery of notices using automated systems - Maintain a SLA log for responding to waiver/concession requests

crmp.title: Advertisement
crmp.description: 1. Financial Institutions must be factual and clear in all communication (including advertisements) with consumers. Communications/ advertisements on financial products and services must at a minimum: a) Not be misleading; b) Be clear and explicitly state the features of the products/services as approved; c) Not seek to misrepresent or exaggerate the benefits of the products/services  2. Adverts shall disclose all conditions associated with the products and services. For example, where a promotional material makes reference to interest rates, financial institutions shall indicate all other applicable charges. In addition, measures shall be provided for consumers to make further enquiries.  3. FIs shall ensure that adverts align with approved product features. Adverts not in line with approved product features will attract appropriate sanctions.
crmp.plain: The bank shall: 1. Ensure all advertisements and communications on financial products and services are factual and clear. 2. Communications and adverts must:     a) Not mislead consumers     b) Clearly and explicitly state approved features of products/services     c) Avoid exaggerating or misrepresenting benefits 3. Disclose all conditions related to products and services in promotional content. 4. Also disclose other applicable charges if referencing interest rates. 5. Provide channels for further enquiries. 6. Ensure that all adverts align with product approvals; non-compliance may lead to sanctions.
crmp.riskDescription: - Misleading or exaggerated ads may result in: ▪ Regulatory fines or sanctions ▪ Legal liabilities from consumers ▪ Customer dissatisfaction or reputational damage ▪ Product recalls or forced withdrawals
crmp.owner: - Marketing & Corporate Communications - Legal & Compliance Unit - Product Management Team - Customer Experience Team
crmp.primaryControl: - Implement pre-approval review process for all marketing materials - Maintain a compliance checklist for advertisement content - Keep repository of approved product features for cross-verification - Provide staff training on ethical advertising practices

crmp.title: Fair Treatment
crmp.description: Consumers shall be treated equitably without bias at all stages of their relationship with financial institutions. Every consumer shall be given equal access to basic banking services and consideration accorded to the needs of vulnerable groups. Key themes to be addressed are:  Access to finance: eligible consumers must be granted access to financial products and services;  Equity: consumers shall be treated equitably at all times in a manner devoid of discrimination;  Unfair Contract Terms: contract terms must not undermine the rights of consumers giving FIs undue advantage.
crmp.plain: The Bank shall:  1. Treat all consumers equitably and without bias throughout their relationship with the institution. 2. Ensure all eligible consumers have equal access to financial products and services, including basic banking services. 3. Consider the needs of vulnerable groups in service design and delivery. 4. Avoid discriminatory practices and ensure fairness in every consumer interaction. 5. Refrain from including unfair terms in contracts that undermine consumer rights or provide the Bank with an undue advantage.
crmp.riskDescription: Discrimination claims, regulatory sanctions, loss of trust, legal disputes over unfair terms
crmp.owner: Compliance, Legal, Credit, Product, Customer Service
crmp.primaryControl: Equal Access Policy, Fair Lending Guidelines, Contract Review Processes

crmp.title: Equity
crmp.description: 1. Financial institutions shall not discriminate against consumers’ access to basic financial services on the basis of attributes such as social status, physical ability, marital status, gender, age, religion or tribe.  2. FIs shall treat consumers with respect and shall not engage in practices such as threats, intimidation, humiliation, misrepresentation, deception or unfair inducements.
crmp.plain: The bank shall: 1. Provide equal access to basic financial services for all consumers, regardless of social status, gender, age, marital status, religion, tribe, or physical ability. 2. Ensure that all consumer interactions are conducted with respect, free from threats, intimidation, deception, misrepresentation, or unfair inducement.
crmp.riskDescription: - Discriminatory practices can result in: ▪ Regulatory penalties and CBN sanctions ▪ Loss of customer trust and business ▪ Negative publicity and reputational damage ▪ Legal action and compliance breaches

crmp.title: Unfair Contract Terms
crmp.description: 1. Terms and conditions shall clearly set out the respective rights and obligations of all parties to transactions in simple language. The use of technical terminologies/languages shall be limited or avoided in contract documents, where they are used, FIs shall ensure that these terminologies are clearly explained to consumers.  Contract terms shall be considered unfair where there is a significant imbalance in one party’s rights and obligations to the detriment of the other. The following amongst others are considered to be unfair terms;  a) Limiting the liability of the financial institution in the event of total or partial non-performance of contractual obligations; b) Excluding the liability of the FI in the event of its negligence which is detrimental to the consumer; c) Clauses that bind a consumer while the corresponding obligation on the FI is conditional; d) Termination of agreements or alteration of clauses without reasonable notice to the consumer; e) Limiting the financial institutions’ liability with respect to actions or commitments undertaken by their agents; f) Giving the FI the possibility of transferring its rights and obligations under the contract, where this may reduce the rights of the consumers, without their consent; g) Excluding or limiting the right of the consumer to take legal action should infraction occur.  2. Contract terms that conflict with regulations are null and void ab initio.  3. Consumers or other stakeholders are encouraged to report contract terms that are in conflict with any regulation.
crmp.plain: The bank shall: 1. Draft contract terms in simple, clear language, avoiding or clearly explaining technical terms. 2. Ensure that contract terms do not create a significant imbalance in the rights and obligations of the bank and the consumer. 3. Avoid including the following in contracts: a. Limit or exclude the bank’s liability in case of non-performance or negligence. b. Make customer obligations binding while the bank’s obligations are conditional. c. Alter or terminating contracts without reasonable notice. d. Exclude the consumer’s right to take legal action. e. Transfer bank rights that reduce consumer rights without consent. 4. Recognize that any contract term that conflicts with regulation is void. 5. Encourage consumers to report any unfair contract terms.
crmp.riskDescription: - Use of unfair contract terms may lead to: ▪ Regulatory penalties from the CBN ▪ Legal disputes and invalidation of contracts ▪ Reputational damage ▪ Customer dissatisfaction and attrition
crmp.owner: - Legal Department - Product Development Team - Customer Experience Team - Compliance Department
crmp.primaryControl: - Review all product contracts to ensure alignment with CBN regulations on fairness - Implement standardized contract templates vetted by Legal & Compliance - Include disclosures and explanatory notes for any complex terms - Maintain an internal review and approval process for all contract terms

crmp.title: Protection of Consumer Assets and Privacy
crmp.description: Appropriate measures shall be established to guarantee protection of consumer assets and privacy. Consumer’s financial and personal information shall be protected by FIs at all times and shall not be released to a third party without the consent of the consumer, except as required by law.  The following information are considered to be confidential and shall be protected at all times; Contact details, account number and balance, statement of accounts and any other information known to the financial institution.  The Bank shall establish guidelines to safeguard consumer assets and privacy against unauthorized access. The primary areas to be covered are:  Fraud: the need for adequate controls to be put in place to prevent incidences of fraud.  Data Privacy: the need for adequate controls to be put in place to prevent unauthorized access to consumers’ confidential information.
crmp.plain: The Bank shall:  1. Establish and maintain adequate controls to protect consumer assets and personal data against unauthorized access, loss, or misuse. 2. Ensure that consumers’ financial and personal information — including contact details, account numbers, balances, and statements — is treated as confidential at all times. 3. Prevent disclosure of consumer information to third parties, unless required by law or with the explicit consent of the consumer. 4. Implement fraud prevention measures to safeguard consumer assets from unauthorized or illegal activity. 5. Put in place robust data privacy policies and controls to ensure the protection of consumer information from breaches or misuse.
crmp.riskDescription: Fraud, data breaches, legal/regulatory penalties, reputational damage
crmp.primaryControl: Information Security Policy, Access Controls, Data Protection Guidelines, Consent Management

crmp.title: Fraud
crmp.description: 1. Financial institutions shall establish policies and controls to safeguard consumer assets against fraud. These policies and protocols may include the use of sophisticated software and transaction monitoring systems to monitor the internal processes/operations of financial institutions. Therefore, key policies shall include: a) Segregation of duties: the initiation and conclusion of transactions shall not rest with an individual. Necessary hierarchical controls, second level authentications amongst others, shall be put in place to prevent fraud; b) Access to information: appropriate access control systems shall be established by financial institutions. FIs shall restrict and monitor access to customer’s data base; c) Security (physical and electronic): consumer data and records must be securely stored at all times and accessed only by authorized personnel; d) Adequate data storage infrastructure: specification of technical requirements for data storage infrastructure; and e) Periodic audit: financial institutions shall ensure periodic audit of control systems to ascertain adequacy and effectiveness to guard against breaches.  2. Electronic payment instruments/systems shall be embedded with safety mechanisms; institutions shall ensure regular systems updates to guard against possible security lapses. The CBN shall specify minimum technology standards for payments platforms.  3. Financial institutions shall perform periodic internal risk assessment to identify and assess data security risks on their systems.  4. Financial institutions shall enforce disciplinary action against employees involved in fraud and report same to the regulator. Where required, the CBN shall blacklist such employee from further employment within the industry.  5. Financial institutions shall promptly refund customers for actual amounts lost due to fraud with interest at the CBN prescribed rate unless it can be proved that loss occurred as a result of customer’s negligence or through fraudulent behavior.  6. Financial institutions shall require customers to update their details within the timeline specified by the CBN. Customers are obliged to update their records as need arises in order to ensure data accuracy and ultimately enhance protection. Financial institutions shall create convenient avenues through which customers can make these updates.  7. Financial institutions shall continually create awareness on fraudulent practices and consumers’ responsibilities to guard against such.
crmp.plain: The bank shall: 1. Establish internal policies and controls to protect customer assets from fraud, including: a. Segregation of duties in transactions b. Access control systems for customer data c. Secure storage of customer records (physical and digital) d. Adequate data storage infrastructure e. Periodic audit of systems and controls 2. Embed security features in all e-payment platforms and ensure regular updates in line with CBN technology standards. 3. Conduct periodic internal risk assessments on data and fraud vulnerabilities. 4. Take disciplinary action against employees involved in fraud and report them to the CBN; blacklist where necessary. 5. Refund customers promptly for amounts lost to fraud (with CBN interest) unless fraud was due to customer’s negligence. 6. Require and facilitate timely customer data updates; create easy update channels. 7. Educate consumers regularly on fraud risks and prevention.
crmp.riskDescription: - Exposure to internal/external fraud may lead to: ▪ Regulatory sanctions ▪ Loss of consumer trust and market reputation ▪ Financial loss and legal liability

crmp.title: Data Protection
crmp.description: 1. All personal information of customers (including those with closed accounts) shall be kept in confidence by FIs. As a duty of care, financial institutions are obliged to safeguard the privacy of their customers’ data.  2. Financial institutions shall not reveal consumers/customers information to a third party except in the following cases: a) With the express permission of the customer; b) As required by the CBN and other regulatory bodies; c) Where there is a court order; d) In pursuance of public duty/interest;  3. Appropriate data protection measures and staff training programs shall be put in place to prevent unauthorized access, alteration, disclosure, accidental loss or destruction of customer data.  4. The consent of consumers shall be obtained in writing before their data is shared with third parties. For this purpose, a third party includes a subsidiary or an associated company.  5. Financial institutions shall obtain the prior consent of customers in writing before using such information for future promotional offers via e-mail, SMS, phone calls and other channels.  6. Consumers partaking in sales promotions shall be informed if they would be required for any publicity or advertisement by the financial institution.
crmp.plain: The bank shall: 1. Keep all personal information of customers confidential, including for closed accounts. 2. Do not disclose customer data to any third party, except:     a. With the customer's written consent;     b. When required by CBN or regulators;     c. Upon court order;     d. In the public interest. 3. Implement strong data protection systems and train staff on data privacy. 4. Obtain written consent from customers before sharing data with third parties, including subsidiaries. 5. Get prior written consent before using customer data for marketing or promotional offers. 6. Inform customers participating in promotions if they will be used for advertising.

crmp.title: Complaints Handling and Redress
crmp.description: Adequate measures shall be established to address disputes that may arise from interactions and relationships between the FI and the consumer. The existence of effective complaints handling mechanisms that are affordable, fair, timely, transparent, accessible and independent would enhance overall consumer confidence in the financial system. The primary areas to be addressed are:  Complaints channels: avenues for lodging complaints shall be readily available and easily accessible to consumers. Consumers shall be made aware of the various channels.  Complaints management processes or procedures: The processes and procedures for complaints management shall be simple and efficient supporting the effective resolution of consumer complaints. Consumers shall be made aware of the various recourse mechanisms.  Complaints redress: provisions shall exist for the fair redress and compensation of consumers in the event of wrongful treatment.  Collaborations with other bodies: effective collaborations with other dispute resolution bodies in the industry shall be established to ensure a full coverage of consumer complaints handling.
crmp.plain: The Bank shall:  1. Establish adequate, fair, and transparent complaints handling and redress mechanisms to resolve disputes arising from interactions with consumers.  2. Provide multiple, easily accessible channels for consumers to lodge complaints and ensure consumers are informed about these options.  3. Design and implement simple, efficient, and effective procedures for managing and resolving complaints.  4. Inform consumers of available recourse and redress mechanisms.  5. Ensure fair redress and compensation is provided to consumers in cases of wrongful treatment.  6. Collaborate with industry dispute resolution bodies to ensure broad and effective coverage of consumer complaints handling.
crmp.riskDescription: Customer dissatisfaction, reputational damage, regulatory penalties for poor handling, legal actions
crmp.primaryControl: Complaints Management Policy, Dedicated Helpdesk, Grievance Redress Framework

crmp.title: Complaints Channels
crmp.description: 1. Financial institutions shall have multiple channels (including electronic and non-electronic channels) for consumers to lodge complaints. Examples of complaints channels may include provision of dedicated email addresses, telephone numbers, help desk, web chat etc. Such channels shall be toll-free, easily accessible and available to consumers or their agents at all times.  2. Financial institutions and Alternate Dispute Resolution institutions shall provide consumers with information on available mechanisms for handling complaints. At a minimum, such information shall include: a) Available channels for complaints handling and redress; b) Timeline for complaints resolution; c) Responsibility of the complainant at each stage of the process; d) Obligation of the financial institution or ADR institution; and e) Escalation processes.  This information shall be provided at no cost to complainants at the point of commencing a contractual relationship, upon request or when acknowledging a consumer complaint.  3. Complaints channels shall be staffed by courteous individuals with experience in handling consumer issues. Supervision of the complaints handling process must be carried out by senior management staff.  4. Financial Institutions shall provide relevant training for staff involved in the development and approvals of complaints handling policies, practices and procedures as well as for staff who interface directly with consumers.  5. The CBN shall set minimum standards for the operations of the various complaints handling channels, including the electronic and non-electronic channels. Periodically, there shall be audits or checks on the availability and adequacy of these channels, as well as a comprehensive evaluation of financial institutions’ compliance with the minimum standards set.  6. The CBN shall promote Alternative Dispute Resolution in the industry.  7.The Consumer Protection Department (CPD) shall be responsible for managing all consumer complaints at the CBN.
crmp.plain: The bank shall: 1. Provide multiple accessible, toll-free complaints channels (email, phone, helpdesk, chat, etc.). 2. Share clear information on complaint resolution procedures, including:     a. Available channels     b. Timeline for resolution     c. Complainant's responsibilities     d. Bank's responsibilities     e. Escalation steps. 3. Ensure this info is provided at onboarding, on request, or during complaint acknowledgment at no cost. 4. Ensure complaints channels are managed by courteous, trained staff and overseen by senior management. 5. Train staff developing or operating complaints processes. 6. Comply with minimum standards set by CBN and prepare for periodic audits. 7. Promote and cooperate with Alternative Dispute Resolution mechanisms.
crmp.riskDescription: Non-compliance can lead to regulatory sanctions, poor customer experience, reputational damage, and reduced customer retention.

crmp.title: Complaints Management Processes or Procedures
crmp.description: 1. Financial institutions shall have clear procedures (including timelines which must be in accordance with minimum standards set by CBN) for receiving and resolving complaints. FIs are expected to automate their complaints management processes or procedures.  2. Financial institutions shall establish and implement effective and transparent processes for handling complaints.  3. The complaints management processes of financial institutions shall include proactive measures to minimize the incidences of complaints. Complaints statistics shall be published in financial statements of FIs.  4. Consumer complaints shall first be lodged with the relevant FIs and only be escalated to alternate dispute resolution organs in the event that the consumer is dissatisfied or the complaint is not resolved within the stipulated time.  5. If complaints are not resolved by the financial institution or consumers are dissatisfied with the outcome of the complaints handling process, the FIs must inform consumers of the alternative recourse mechanisms available, and the process involved in seeking redress through these channels.  6. To avoid duplication of effort by ADRs, consumers shall lodge complaints with one ADR at a time and state categorically where complaints have earlier been reported to other ADRs as well as provide the decision reached.  7. Financial institutions shall provide consumers with status update on complaints. Consequently, the following must be addressed in the course of managing a consumer complaints: a) The timelines stipulated by the CBN; b) Financial institution’s acknowledgement of complaints received stating the timeline within which a response will be made available; c) Provision of reference numbers for all complaints received; d) In the event of delays, reason for delayed resolution including status in the event that complaint remains unresolved at the expiration of the agreed/ communicated resolution or response timeline; e) For complaints that have been resolved, resolution shall be provided in writing and acknowledged by the consumer. It is also advised that the consumer’s concurrence or objection is sought or obtained within a stipulated time.  8. To ensure easy resolution of complaints, the CBN may place a time limit or bar for lodging consumer complaints. However, time restrictions shall not apply in exceptional cases such as fraud.  9. ADRs shall not investigate cases concurrently with financial institutions; a case shall be admissible at the ADR only after a decision has been made by the FI. It is upon dissatisfaction with the decisions that such consumer may proceed to an alternate dispute resolution institution.  10. To fast-track resolution of complaints, ADR institutions shall encourage mediation or reconciliatory meetings between complainants and the financial institutions.  11. To promote disclosure and instill accountability amongst FIs, information on consumer complaints shall be published by FIs in their financial statements. The CBN shall in addition, publicize these statistics across financial institutions on a regular basis. This would enable institutions compare their performance against peers and provide consumers with additional source of information for financial decision making.  12. The CBN shall not handle cases that fall within these categories: a) Time barred complaints; and b) Cases before the courts or cases already ruled upon by the courts of law (except where directed by the court through an order).
crmp.plain: The bank shall: 1. Establish and automate a transparent and efficient complaints management procedure with timelines compliant with CBN standards. 2. Implement proactive measures to minimize complaints. 3. Include complaint statistics in annual financial statements. 4. Ensure all consumer complaints are first handled internally before referring to ADR. 5. Inform customers of available ADR options if unresolved or disputed. 6. Ensure consumers lodge complaints with only one ADR at a time and disclose any prior ADR action. 7. Provide complaint status updates covering:     a) CBN-stipulated timelines     b) Acknowledgment with timeline for response     c) Complaint reference number     d) Reason for delay, if any     e) Written resolution with consumer acknowledgment and feedback 8. Observe CBN’s time-bar policy (except in fraud cases). 9. Avoid parallel handling of complaints with ADRs; ADRs come in only after internal resolution is exhausted. 10. Promote mediation via ADRs for unresolved cases. 11. Publicize consumer complaint statistics in financial reports. 12. Not forward time-barred or court-resolved cases to CBN (unless court-ordered).

crmp.title: Complaints Redress
crmp.description: 1. Financial institutions shall develop a Customer Compensation Policy to address various category of complaints which may arise due to service failures. FIs must publicly display this policy on various media such as bank websites, branches.  2. The Customer Compensation Policy shall be in line with guidelines issued by the CBN and shall contain provisions for probable infractions such as: a) Unauthorized or erroneous debits; b) Excess charges; and c) Financial loss to consumers due to staff negligence/fraudulent activities.  3. Where there is a complaint on excess charges, FIs shall carry out account reconstruction where necessary, in order to put the account into proper perspective.  4. FI shall provide evidence of complaints resolution to customers, ADRs and regulators, where required.  5. Complainants shall provide written acknowledgement confirming satisfaction or otherwise with the outcome of the dispute resolution process within a specified time.  6. Where a complainant fails to acknowledge resolution within the specified timeline, the complainant would be deemed to be satisfied and the case closed.  7. Decisions of ADR institutions may be appealed through the internal process prescribed by such institutions.
crmp.plain: The bank shall: 1. Develop a Customer Compensation Policy to handle complaints due to service failures. 2. Publicly display the policy on the bank’s website and branches. 3. Align the policy with CBN guidelines and include provisions for:     a) Unauthorized/erroneous debits     b) Excess charges     c) Consumer losses from staff negligence or fraud 4. Conduct account reconstruction when excess charges complaints arise. 5. Provide documented evidence of complaint resolution to the customer, ADRs, and regulators if required. 6. Require written acknowledgment from complainants stating satisfaction or dissatisfaction with the resolution. 7. Treat the complaint as resolved and closed if acknowledgment is not received within a specified timeline. 8. Allow decisions of ADRs to be appealed using the process set by the ADR institution.
crmp.riskDescription: - Failure to compensate fairly may lead to legal disputes. - Non-compliance with CBN rules may attract penalties. - Loss of customer trust and negative brand perception. - Poor documentation can harm credibility before regulators and ADRs.

crmp.title: Collaborations with other bodies
crmp.description: 1. Institutions involved in complaints management shall collaborate with relevant agencies to enhance the efficiency of the dispute resolution process. Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) shall be signed between institutions involved in financial consumer protection or dispute resolution. The details of the Memorandum of Understanding shall include amongst others: a) Roles and responsibilities of parties; b) Recourse in the event of non-resolution; and c) Escalation path along the various institutions during a dispute resolution process.
crmp.plain: The bank shall: 1. Collaborate with relevant agencies involved in financial consumer protection and dispute resolution. 2. Sign Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) with these agencies. 3. Ensure each MoU includes:     a) Clear roles and responsibilities of each party;     b) Defined procedures for cases where resolution is not achieved;     c) A clear escalation path for handling complaints across institutions.
crmp.riskDescription: - Lack of collaboration could delay or derail complaint resolutions. - Absence of formal agreements can create accountability gaps. - Poor inter-agency engagement could result in regulatory non-compliance or consumer dissatisfaction.
crmp.owner: - Legal Department- Compliance Unit- Customer Experience Unit- Liaison Officers with CBN and ADR Institutions
crmp.primaryControl: - Draft and review MoUs with all relevant agencies - Define and document responsibilities and escalation processes - Maintain a database of all signed MoUs - Regular stakeholder engagement meetings

crmp.title: Competition
crmp.description: Competitive markets should be promoted in order to encourage innovation, offer consumers diverse range of financial products and services, excellent service delivery and ultimately ensure that consumers benefit from the practice of competition.  To promote competition within the industry, financial institutions shall collaborate with financial regulators and other stakeholders. The critical themes to be covered are:  Free Market: regulators should encourage innovation as well as free entry and exit in the industry.  Switching Barriers: consumers should be allowed to terminate contracts or engage in banking transactions with their preferred financial institution without any restrictions.
crmp.plain: The Bank shall:  1. Promote competition by supporting innovation and ensuring consumers have access to a variety of financial products and services. 2. Collaborate with financial regulators and relevant stakeholders to encourage a competitive financial ecosystem. 3. Ensure that consumers are free to switch between financial institutions or terminate contracts without facing undue restrictions or barriers. 4. Encourage practices that support free market entry and exit to enhance service delivery and consumer choice.
crmp.riskDescription: Regulatory scrutiny, loss of consumer trust, penalties for anti-competitive practices

crmp.title: Free market
crmp.description: 1. The CBN shall encourage product development by financial institutions to enable consumers have access to variety of innovative products and services.  2. The CBN shall monitor the market to restrict practices which may inhibit competition.  3. The CBN shall discourage anti-competitive practices such as: a) Price-fixing or pegging of charges – any act by one or more FIs to fix charges on products and services for their benefit but to the detriment of consumers; b) Market allocation – agreement amongst FIs to form territories so that specific institutions are found in certain regions to the exclusion of others; c) Abuse of dominance – any act by one or more FIs with significant market power or share which have adverse effect on competition; and d) Tied selling – any act by financial institutions forcing consumers to buy or subscribe to other products or services along with the desired products or services.
crmp.plain: The bank shall: 1. Develop a variety of innovative and competitive financial products/services to give consumers more choices. 2. Avoid anti-competitive behaviors such as:     a) Price fixing (agreeing with others to set prices);     b) Market allocation (restricting operations to specific regions in agreement with other FIs);     c) Abuse of dominance (using size/power to block competition);     d) Tied selling (forcing customers to buy an additional product/service). 3. Support a fair, open, and competitive market environment.
crmp.riskDescription: - Sanctions or penalties for anti-competitive practices. - Legal and reputational risks. - Loss of consumer trust and market credibility. - Regulatory intervention and fines by the CBN.
crmp.owner: - Compliance Unit- Strategy & Innovation Department- Legal Department- Product Development Team
crmp.primaryControl: - Internal policy prohibiting anti-competitive practices. - Legal review of all partnership and pricing arrangements. - Regular product and pricing audits. - Whistleblowing mechanism for unethical practices.

crmp.title: Switching Barriers
crmp.description: 1. Consumers shall be allowed to engage in banking transactions with their preferred financial institutions.  2. Consumers shall have the right to terminate contracts, change or switch FIs, products and/or services subject to contractual terms. It is unethical and anti-competitive for FIs to place restrictions on consumers that discourage switching.  3. Where a customer decides to switch, the financial institution shall provide the necessary information to the new financial institution.
crmp.plain: The bank shall: 1. Allow consumers to freely choose and switch to any financial institution, product, or service without unnecessary restrictions. 2. Honor customer requests to terminate existing contracts or switch providers in line with contract terms. 3. Provide all necessary account and transaction information to the receiving/new financial institution to facilitate the switch.

crmp.source: Deployment of the Consumer Complaints Management System (CCMS)
crmp.title: CPD/DIR/GEN/CIR/01/001
crmp.description: The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN), in furtherance of its mandate to promote a stable financial system embarked on the development of the Consumer Complaints Management System (CCMS), an automated system aimed at easing complaints management to engender public confidence in the financial system.  With effect from 2nd January, 2019, Banks and Other Financial Institutions (BOFIs) are required to:  1. Assign Tracking Number for every complaint received from their customers;  2. Issue an acknowledgement, which shall contain the assigned Tracking Number, to the customer; and  3. Commence upload of complaints to the CCMS on a daily basis.  In addition, BOFIs are enjoined to always comply with the timelines stipulated in the CCMS for resolution of the various categories of complaints.
crmp.plain: The bank must: 1. Assign a Tracking Number to every customer complaint received. 2. Issue an acknowledgement to the customer that includes the Tracking Number. 3. Upload all customer complaints to the Consumer Complaints Management System (CCMS) daily. 4. Comply with resolution timelines specified in the CCMS for each complaint category.
crmp.riskDescription: - Regulatory sanction for non-compliance with CCMS requirements. - Loss of customer confidence due to poor complaint handling. - Reduced transparency and poor relationship with the CBN. - Reputation damage and potential fines.
crmp.owner: - Complaints Management Unit- Customer Experience Team- IT Department- Compliance Department
crmp.primaryControl: - Automated complaints tracking system integrated with CCMS. - SOP (Standard Operating Procedure) for assigning tracking numbers and acknowledging complaints. - Daily upload scheduling and monitoring. - Real-time compliance dashboard to track resolution timelines.

crmp.source: Requirement to Display Corporate Names on Websites, Portals, Applications, and Other Online Business Platforms
crmp.title: FPR/PRD/CIR/INT/001/003
crmp.description: The Central Bank of Nigeria has observed with concern that some licensed entities that operate transaction websites/portals or online applications do not conspicuously display their corporate names to facilitate recognition by the public. This practice portends risk to consumers of such products and services, including potential negative perception of the products or services, misleading consumers and difficulty to seek redress when the need arises.  In view of the above and to engender trust and confidence in the use of such products and services, all licensed financial institutions are hereby required to:  1. Conspicuously display their corporate names on all their websites, portals and online applications.  2. Include ‘Licensed by the Central Bank of Nigeria’ beside or under their names.
crmp.plain: The bank shall: 1. Clearly display the institution’s corporate name on all websites, portals, and mobile/web applications. 2. Add the phrase “Licensed by the Central Bank of Nigeria” next to or directly beneath the corporate name on each platform.
crmp.riskDescription: - Non-compliance could lead to regulatory sanctions or penalties. - Loss of consumer trust and difficulty in brand recognition. - Exposure to reputational damage and potential legal issues when consumers cannot trace or verify the provider.
crmp.owner: - Corporate Communications- Digital Channels Unit / Product Owners- IT & Web Development Team- Compliance Department
crmp.primaryControl: - Periodic compliance check of all online platforms. - Pre-launch compliance checklist for new digital products or portals. - Regular IT audits to verify compliance with naming display rules. - Branding guidelines updated to enforce proper name usage.

crmp.title: GENERAL PROVISIONS
crmp.description: Institutions shall comply with the following provisions to ensure fair treatment of consumers:  3.1.1 Treat consumers equitably without bias at all stages of the relationship. 3.1.2 Give consumers who meet the minimum legal and non – discriminatory eligibility requirements, equal access to basic services without regard to their social status, physical ability, marital status, gender, age, religion, tribe or ideology. 3.1.3 Consider the needs of the financially excluded, including the vulnerable groups such as low-income consumers, women, seniors, physically challenged and the non-literate in the development and implementation of their business models, strategies and processes.
crmp.plain: Banks must:  1. Treat all consumers fairly and without discrimination at every stage of their interaction.  2. Provide equal access to basic services for all eligible consumers, regardless of status or identity.  3. Design and implement services that also consider the needs of vulnerable and financially excluded groups (e.g., low-income earners, women, elderly, physically challenged, and non-literate individuals).
crmp.riskDescription: Failure to uphold fairness and non-discrimination may result in reputational damage, customer complaints, regulatory penalties, and loss of consumer trust.
crmp.owner: Chief Customer Experience Officer, Head of Retail/Consumer Banking, Compliance Officer, CSR/Financial Inclusion Officer
crmp.primaryControl: - Develop inclusive service policies and procedures. - Train staff on equitable treatment and non-discrimination. - Provide alternative access channels for vulnerable groups (e.g., USSD, local language support). - Monitor and report consumer complaints and resolution trends.

crmp.title: EQUITY
crmp.description: It shall be the duty of Institutions to treat consumers equitably always. Therefore, Institutions shall:  3.2.1 Treat consumers with courtesy and respect and shall not engage in practices such as threats, intimidation, use of abusive or offensive language, humiliation, misrepresentation, deception or unfair inducements. 3.2.2 Apply lending fees on disbursed amounts only in respect of term loans, except for fees which are normally applicable on undisbursed portions. 3.2.3 Apply non-credit related fees/charges on an account only to the extent of the balance in the account, and defer the outstanding fees/charges until the account is funded and the customer notified of the deferred fees/charges. 3.2.4 Promptly oblige consumers’ request for account closure or to switch providers, without unreasonable closing/switching barriers. 3.2.5 Ensure that variations to contracts including interest rate, fees or charges are only made if expressly provided for in the contract and shall notify consumer of any such variation. 3.2.6 Respond to customers’ enquiries/requests within five (5) working days of receiving the enquiries/requests. 3.2.7 Communicate a decision (acceptance or decline) on applications for waivers, extensions, and other concessions to a customer within ten (10) working days, otherwise the application shall be deemed to have been granted. 3.2.8 Not act in a manner that is inconsistent with the terms and conditions of their contracts with their customers. 3.2.9 Not seek repayment or withhold, in part or in full, customer’s funds to secure repayment before the due date, except with the written authorization of the customer. 3.2.10 Not charge early liquidation fees for consumer and SME loans with variable interest rate.
crmp.plain: The bank must:  1. Treat all customers with respect and avoid threats, deception, or unfair practices.  2. Only charge lending fees on actual loan amounts disbursed (unless otherwise specified).  3. Only apply non-credit fees up to the available balance and defer the rest, with clear customer notification.  4. Allow customers to close accounts or switch providers easily, without delays or hurdles.  5. Notify customers of any contract changes only if stated in the contract and with proper notice.  6. Respond to all customer enquiries/requests within 5 working days.  7. Communicate decisions on waivers/concessions within 10 working days, or such requests are considered granted.  8. Honor all contract terms and avoid acting contrary to agreements with customers.  9. Do not withhold customer funds or demand early repayment unless authorized in writing.  10. Do not charge early liquidation fees on variable interest loans to consumers and SMEs.
crmp.riskDescription: Failure to comply may result in regulatory sanctions, customer complaints, reputational damage, financial penalties, and increased litigation risk.

crmp.primaryControl: - Staff training on ethical customer interaction.  - Automated fee application rules.  - Account closure and switching procedures.  - Contract template review and approval process. - Complaint handling and escalation workflow.  - CRM system tracking timelines for all enquiries and waiver decisions.

crmp.title: GENERAL PROVISIONS
crmp.description: To promote transparency and enhance disclosure practices, Institutions shall comply with the following provisions:  4.1.1. Ensure that documents provided or made available to consumers shall: a. Be written in clear, legible and simple English language and in a minimum font size of 10. b. Be provided in a durable form for future reference. c. State the name, contact details of the Institution and the consumer. d. Contain a statement that the Institution is regulated by the Central Bank of Nigeria. e. Not be misleading or deceptive.  4.1.2. Put procedures in place to ensure that an oral explanation of the document is provided to the consumer in a language that he or she understands if: a. the consumer requests; or b. it is reasonably obvious that the consumer is illiterate or visually impaired or, for any other reason, cannot understand the document.  4.1.3. Conspicuously display in their banking halls and publish on their websites and internet banking platforms, accurate and up to date information on all their products and services. Such information shall include: a. prime and maximum lending rates; b. deposit rates; and c. exchange rates of foreign currencies.  4.1.4. Disclose to the consumer in writing, all Terms and Conditions of a transaction agreement. 4.1.5. Ensure that the disclaimer “Terms and Conditions Apply” or any other phrase conveying a similar meaning shall only be used if the terms and conditions have been explained and disclosed in the contract or in other medium accessible by the customer. The Institution shall at all times, draw the consumer’s attention to such disclosure. 4.1.6. Clearly explain technical terms used in documents to the consumer to aid understanding. 4.1.7. Agree with consumers on the communication channel(s) to be used for all correspondences and include the channel(s) in all contract documents. 4.1.8. Ensure that their websites and other information dissemination channels are functional and regularly updated with the current features of products and services offered. 4.1.9. Comply with the rates, fees, charges, or prices published or disclosed at the engagement points. 4.1.10. Inform consumers of applicable and indicative foreign exchange rates through customer engagement points and advise consumers to always check the rates before consummating foreign exchange transactions. 4.1.11. Bear all costs associated with disclosures to customers required by the Regulations, except for deposits and withdrawals by or on behalf of the customer.
crmp.plain: The bank must: 1. Use clear, simple English (minimum font size 10) in customer-facing documents, and ensure documents are durable and personalized (with names, contacts, CBN disclosure, etc.). 2. Provide oral explanations for documents when requested or needed (e.g., for illiterate or visually impaired customers). 3. Clearly display on all platforms: up-to-date lending, deposit, and FX rates. 4. Disclose all transaction terms and conditions clearly in writing.5. Only use "Terms and Conditions Apply" if the T&Cs are explained and accessible.6. Explain all technical terms to consumers. 7. Agree on a communication channel with the customer and include it in the contract. 8. Ensure all dissemination platforms (website, mobile app, etc.) are functional and current. 9. Honour the rates and charges displayed at the point of engagement. 10. Inform customers of applicable FX rates at the point of transaction. 11. Bear the cost of disclosures required by law.
crmp.riskDescription: Non-compliance may result in poor customer experience, regulatory penalties, loss of trust, reputational damage, legal actions, and customer attrition.

crmp.title: ADVERTISEMENT
crmp.description: Institutions shall comply with the following disclosures for all advertisements and promotional materials:  4.2.1 The content of advertisements shall be factual and unambiguous, expressed in clear and simple language and shall not be offensive, misleading, deceptive, injurious, or exaggerate the benefits of the products or services being advertised. 4.2.2 The overall impression of advertisements shall not emphasize benefits of a product or service while de-emphasizing its associated risks. 4.2.3 Disclose their contact details in any advertisement or promotional material. 4.2.4 Clearly disclose details of the cost of a product or services, including all fees and other associated charges. 4.2.5 Fully disclose the nature and value of benefits, where an advertisement refers to, or is linked to other value adding benefits. 4.2.6 Not make references to unaudited financial statements. 4.2.7 Not mention names of competitors or make comparisons in their advertisements. 4.2.8 Unsolicited advertisements through emails, text messages, voice calls and other channels sent by or on behalf of a Institution shall be at no cost to the consumer and shall contain an opt-out provision for future advertisements. 4.2.9 Notify the Director, Consumer Protection Department of the CBN prior to the commencement of advertisement of product or service by submitting a description of the content of the advertisement.
crmp.plain: The bank must: 1. Ensure advertisements are factual, clear, and not misleading. 2. Avoid exaggerating benefits or hiding product/service risks. 3. Display contact details in all adverts. 4. Disclose full cost of products/services, including fees and charges. 5. Clearly state the value and nature of any benefits tied to a product. 6. Not reference unaudited financials. 7. Avoid mentioning competitors or making comparisons. 8. Be free to recipients and must include an opt-out option from unsolicited ads via email/SMS/calls. 9. Notify CBN before launching any product/service advertisement with content details.
crmp.riskDescription: - Non-compliance may result in regulatory sanctions or fines. - Could lead to consumer mistrust and reputational damage. - Legal liabilities due to deceptive advertising or omitted cost disclosures. - May be accused of anti-competitive practices if competitors are referenced. - Failure to notify CBN could cause regulatory breaches.

crmp.title: PRE-CONTRACT DISCLOSURES
crmp.description: Institutions shall comply with the following requirements prior to the execution of any contract with consumers:  4.3.1 Disclose all terms and conditions of a product or service on offer, as well as the features, risks, benefits, fees and other associated charges. 4.3.2 Disclose in contracts, the possibility of variations in interest rates or foreign exchange due to changes in market conditions. 4.3.3 Disclose similar products and services within the Institution, to enable consumers make comparisons and informed choices. 4.3.4 Provide the consumer, a Key Facts Statement (KFS) in the format attached as Annexure A stating a summary of key information on consumer loans. 4.3.5 Allow consumers a minimum of two (2) days from date of receipt, to review draft contract before execution except where the customer waives this in writing. 4.3.6 Give a consumer a cooling-off period of three (3) working days after the signing of a credit contract within which the consumer may cancel the contract without having to pay any penalty or charges. However, the consumer may choose to waive the option by notifying the bank in writing.
crmp.plain: The bank must: 1. Disclose all terms, conditions, features, risks, benefits, fees, and charges of the product or service before contract execution. 2. Clearly state in the contract if interest rates or FX rates may vary due to market conditions. 3. Provide information on similar products and services to help customers make comparisons. 4. Issue a Key Facts Statement (KFS) in the required format for consumer loans. 5. Give consumers at least 2 days to review draft contracts before signing, unless waived in writing. 6. crmp.title: CONTRACTUAL DISCLOSURES
crmp.description: Institutions shall comply with the following requirements during the lifecycle of any contract with consumers:  4.4.1 Notify consumers of any transaction on their account immediately it is made. At a minimum, the notification shall include date, amount, payer, transaction reference, channel and the cleared account balance. 4.4.2 Ensure that descriptions in account statements are clear. At a minimum, it shall include, transaction reference, payer transaction channel, location and account balance. 4.4.3 Ensure that, at a minimum, credit contracts contain the following information: a. Key features and risks; b. Tenor of the contract; c. The nature, amount and method of calculation of any interest, fee or charge and when it is payable; d. The applicable Annual Percentage Rate (APR) to be calculated using the formula stated in Annexure B1 and B2; e. Notice of possible variations in interest rates, and how the consumer will be informed of changes; and f. Information on how to lodge a complaint to the Institution and escalate complaint to the CBN where necessary.  4.4.4 Provide consumer with monthly statements (or confirmation/investment advice as the case may be) for all products and account types, including loan accounts, special accounts and other related accounts at no cost. 4.4.5 Provide account balances to consumers on request. 4.4.6 Give prior notice of variation in interest rates to customers. At a minimum, the notice shall state: a. The reason for the variation; b. The commencement date; c. The revised repayment schedule (where necessary); and d. The alternatives available such as concession, restructuring, re-negotiation, opt-out or termination of the contract.  4.4.7 Ensure that variations in interest shall only be implemented after requisite notification to consumers: 10 working days (DMB) and 5 working days for other Institutions.
crmp.plain: The bank must: 1. Send instant alerts to customers for every transaction, showing date, amount, payer, channel, reference, and new balance. 2. Make sure account statements are clear and include transaction reference, payer, channel, location, and balance. 3. Ensure credit contracts show key features, risks, tenor, interest/fees/charges (with calculations), APR (as per formula), rate variation process, and complaint channels. 4. Provide monthly statements (or confirmation/advice) for all account and product types (loans, investments, etc.) free of charge. 5. Provide account balances when requested by customers. 6. Before changing interest rates, give prior notice stating: reason, start date, revised schedule, and customer options (restructure, renegotiate, exit, etc.). 7. Delay interest changes until 10 working days’ notice for DMBs or 5 working days for others has been given.
crmp.riskDescription: Failure to comply can lead to customer complaints, regulatory sanctions, disputes over unfair charges or changes in terms, reputational damage, and class-action lawsuits.

crmp.title: GENERAL PROVISIONS
crmp.description: To promote good business practices, Institutions shall comply with the following provisions:  5.1.1 Conduct their business in a responsible, professional and ethical manner. 5.1.2 Train their staff to promote competence, efficiency and professionalism in the discharge of their duties. 5.1.3 Provide clear information about products and services, features, terms and conditions and the applicable fees and charges. 5.1.4 Provide and inform consumers of the channels to make enquiries and complaints. 5.1.5 Notify customers of circumstances or situations that may affect the terms of their contracts or relationships. 5.1.6 Display all applicable fees for electronic payment services with the option to accept or decline before a transaction is consummated. This should include a notice that third-party charges may apply. 5.1.7 Not impose any product, service or channel on consumers. 5.1.8 Not charge fees for issuance and renewal of products or services which have not been requested by the customer. 5.1.9 Not compel consumers to buy a product or service as a condition for the purchase of another product or service unless where the products or services are directly dependent.
crmp.plain: The bank shall: 1. Conduct all business dealings professionally, ethically, and responsibly. 2. Train staff to uphold competence and professionalism. 3. Provide clear, accurate product/service information, including terms, conditions, and fees. 4. Inform customers about available complaint/enquiry channels. 5. Notify customers of any change that affects their contracts. 6. Display all e-payment fees and allow customer consent before transactions. 7. Not force products/services on consumers. 8. Not charge for unrequested products. 9. Not compel bundling of products unless they're interdependent.
crmp.riskDescription: - Risk of CBN sanctions and legal penalties for failure to comply. - Potential customer dissatisfaction, complaints, and churn. - Reputational damage due to unethical or misleading practices. - Risk of class-action lawsuits or regulator intervention from bundled/forced product offerings.
crmp.owner: - Legal and Compliance Department- Product Management Team- Customer Experience/Service Department- Marketing and Sales Team- IT/Business Process Automation Team
crmp.primaryControl: - Develop a Consumer Protection Compliance Policy. - Ensure product/service literature is standardized and approved before publication. - Implement staff training and compliance onboarding. - Automate fee display and consent features in digital channels. - Maintain and publicize a complaints resolution framework. - Regular reviews of bundled offerings and customer opt-in records.

crmp.title: RESPONSIBLE LENDING
crmp.description: To ensure that the capability of consumers to repay credits are professionally assessed, Institutions shall comply with the following requirements:  5.2.1 Include in credit risk assessment procedures, the type and circumstances for which a credit will be suitable as well as clear lines of authority for approving the product. 5.2.2 Before granting credit to consumers, assess their capability to repay in a sustainable manner taking into consideration their financial circumstances. 5.2.3 Ascertain the credit history of consumers from the Credit Risk Management System, Credit Bureau and other sources of credit reference before advancing credits. 5.2.4 Have a policy to deal with consumers who are in financial difficulty. 5.2.5 Monitor loan performance and upon early detection of repayment difficulties engage the customer to discuss alternative repayment options. 5.2.6 Not compel consumers to buy products or services, such as insurance or valuation from a particular third-party provider as a pre-condition for the grant of a credit facility, but can provide the option to choose from at least three (3) providers or any number as may be prescribed by CBN from time to time. 5.2.7 Ensure that guarantors confirm in writing that they have read and understood their commitments, potential implications and the maximum amount they are guaranteeing, and have either: a. sought and obtained independent professional advice before executing the guarantee; or b. declared that they do not need independent advice. 5.2.8 Provide periodic update to Guarantors on the loan performance to enable them to assess the likelihood of being called upon to discharge their commitments. 5.2.9 Issue Letter of Discharge at no cost to customers within 5 business days after liquidation of their loans, and where the loan is guaranteed, the guarantor shall also be notified accordingly. 5.2.10 Notify customers where their loan requests are declined. The reason(s) for decline shall be provided upon request.
crmp.plain: The bank shall: 1. Include credit suitability criteria and approval authority in credit risk procedures. 2. Assess a consumer's ability to repay before granting credit, considering their financial situation. 3. Check consumer credit history from CRMS, credit bureaus, or other sources before loan approval. 4. Maintain policies for dealing with consumers in financial difficulty. 5. Monitor loans and engage struggling customers early to find repayment solutions. 6. Not force customers to use specific service providers (e.g., insurance); offer at least 3 options. 7. Ensure guarantors provide written confirmation of understanding and advice status. 8. Send guarantors periodic updates on loan performance. 9. Issue free Loan Discharge Letters within 5 business days post-loan repayment and notify guarantors. 10. Inform customers of declined loan applications and provide reasons upon request.
crmp.riskDescription: - Regulatory sanctions for non-compliance with responsible lending principles. - Increased loan defaults due to poor credit assessment. - Reputational damage and customer complaints due to unfair practices or lack of transparency. - Legal liability from guarantors or consumers who were not properly informed. - Potential CBN penalties for compelling use of third-party services.
crmp.owner: - Credit Risk Management Unit- Loan Approval Officers- Legal and Compliance Department- Customer Service/Experience- Loan Monitoring/Collections Team
crmp.primaryControl: - Incorporate responsible lending checks into credit policy and procedures. - Embed income and affordability checks in loan application systems. - Set automated CRMS and credit bureau validation before approval. - Develop SOPs for handling financial difficulty cases. - Train staff on third-party product disclosure rules. - Require written declarations and advice confirmations from guarantors. - Automate alerts for periodic loan performance updates to guarantors. - Automate discharge letter issuance within 5 business days.

crmp.title: SALES PROMOTION
crmp.description: To ensure that advertisements and promotional materials on products and services are clear and not misleading, Institutions shall:  5.3.1 Provide information that would aid consumers’ decisions. 5.3.2 Carry out marketing of products and services in an ethical and professional manner. 5.3.3 Ensure that sales and marketing staff are properly trained and competent to perform their functions. The staff should be knowledgeable in key features, risks and critical terms of product offering. 5.3.4 Establish a process to periodically check and monitor the competence and conduct of sales and marketing staff. 5.3.5 The remuneration of marketing/sales staff shall not be solely based on sales volume/target but must give consideration to the interests and circumstances of the customers. 5.3.6 Provide consumers with the option to opt out from receiving marketing materials.
crmp.plain: The bank shall: 1. Ensure all product/service ads and promotions are clear and not misleading. 2. Disclose adequate information to help customers make informed decisions. 3. Conduct marketing activities in a professional and ethical manner. 4. Ensure marketing/sales staff are well-trained and competent on key product features, risks, and terms. 5. Establish a system to regularly assess staff conduct and competence. 6. Sales staff remuneration must not be solely based on targets – it must reflect customer welfare. 7. Allow customers to opt-out of marketing messages.
crmp.riskDescription: - Regulatory sanctions for misleading advertising or unethical marketing practices. - Reputational damage and loss of customer trust. - Legal claims from mis-sold products or deceptive marketing. - Customer churn due to aggressive or unethical sales tactics. - Poorly trained staff may lead to non-compliance and increased complaints.

crmp.title: DATA PROTECTION AND PRIVACY
crmp.description: To ensure data protection and privacy of consumers, Institutions shall:  5.4.1 Protect the privacy and confidentiality of consumer information and assets against unauthorized access, and be accountable for acts or omissions in respect thereof. 5.4.2 Obtain the written consent of consumers to collect and process their personal data for specific purpose and provide them with the option to withdraw the consent at any time. 5.4.3 Not transfer personal data of consumers to a third party without their express consent, except in compliance with a legal obligation. 5.4.4 Inform consumers whenever their data is exchanged with an authorized third party, stating details of the exchange. 5.4.5 Review data processing and privacy procedures to ensure that the purpose(s) for which initial consent was granted remained valid. 5.4.6 Keep accurate and updated data of consumers always.
crmp.plain: The bank must: 5.4.1 Ensure customer information is secure, confidential, and protected from unauthorized access, and be accountable for any misuse or exposure. 5.4.2 Get written consent from customers before collecting or processing their personal data, and give them the option to withdraw it anytime. 5.4.3 Do not share personal data with third parties unless the customer explicitly agrees or there’s a legal requirement. 5.4.4 Always notify customers when their data is shared with any authorized third party, including who received it and why. 5.4.5 Regularly review data processing practices to ensure they still align with the customer’s original consent. 5.4.6 Keep customer records accurate and current at all times.
crmp.riskDescription: Data breaches, unauthorized disclosures, or failure to get proper consent can lead to heavy fines (NDPA/NDPR/CBN), loss of customer trust, reputational damage, and litigation.

crmp.title: GENERAL PROVISIONS
crmp.description: The resolution of disputes shall be the responsibility of Institutions. Consumer complaints shall first be lodged with Institutions for timely resolution and redress. Institutions shall:  6.1.1 Develop documented processes on Complaints Handling that will guarantee fairness, transparency, responsiveness and independence of the complaint handling mechanism. 6.1.2 Allocate adequate resources for complaints handling/redress and the processes manned by skilled and well-trained members of staff. 6.1.3 At all customer engagement points, disclose channels and contact details for lodging complaints, timeframe for resolution, and options for escalation. Where it is not practicable to comply with this, refer customers to where the information required could be obtained.
crmp.plain: The bank: 6.1.1 They have a clear, written policy on how customer complaints will be handled. The policy must ensure fairness, openness, quick response times, and independence. 6.1.2 Adequate resources (budget, personnel, technology) are provided to handle complaints, and the team is made up of well-trained professionals. 6.1.3 At all customer service points (physical branches, digital platforms, ATMs, mobile apps), information must be made available on:– How to make a complaint– Contact details– Timeframe for resolution– How customers can escalate unresolved issuesIf not feasible in a location, direct the customer to where this information can be obtained.
crmp.riskDescription: Poor complaints handling could lead to regulatory sanctions, reputational damage, erosion of customer trust, and increased litigation or escalations to the CBN Consumer Protection Department.

crmp.primaryControl: - Complaint Management Policy (documented and approved). - Dedicated complaints handling unit with escalation matrix. - CRM system for tracking and resolving complaints. - Complaint channels published on websites, mobile apps, branches. - Periodic staff training on dispute resolution protocols.
