crmp.description: Institutions shall provide multiple dedicated channels to receive and handle consumer complaints including verbal complaints. The channels may include letters, e-mails, telephone lines, social media and digital software platforms. The following requirements shall apply in the deployment of the channels:  6.2.1 Be effective, functional, efficient and accessible always. 6.2.2 Generate a unique identification number and acknowledge complaints within 24 hours of lodgment, including transcription of verbal complaints. 6.2.3 Accord special consideration to the needs of vulnerable groups, especially the physically challenged persons and seniors. 6.2.4 Provide emergency channels for reporting time-sensitive issues especially fraud-related complaints at all times.
crmp.plain: The bank must: 6.2 Provide multiple complaint channels, such as phone, email, social media, apps, and physical letters, including for verbal complaints. 6.2.1 Ensure these channels are always working, fast, easy to use, and accessible. 6.2.2 For every complaint:– Generate a unique ID number– Acknowledge receipt within 24 hours– Transcribe all verbal complaints. 6.2.3 Ensure vulnerable groups (e.g., physically challenged, seniors) are given special support when lodging complaints.6.2.4 Provide emergency channels (hotlines or 24/7 platforms) for time-sensitive complaints, especially fraud-related cases.
crmp.riskDescription: Failure to deploy effective, accessible, and timely complaint channels may lead to regulatory breaches, delayed resolution of fraud, customer dissatisfaction, reputational damage, and penalties.
crmp.owner: - Customer Service/Experience Department- IT Department (Digital Platforms)- Contact Center Operations- Social Media/Communications Team- Compliance Unit
crmp.primaryControl: - Multiple complaint channels (email, SMS, call centers, social media, branch desks). - CRM or ticketing system that logs and tracks complaints. - Acknowledgement templates for complaint response. - Fraud hotlines available 24/7. - Complaint SOP (Standard Operating Procedures).

crmp.title: INTERNAL DISPUTE RESOLUTION
crmp.description: Institutions shall establish Internal Dispute Resolution (IDR) structures and processes for the effective management of consumer complaints. The IDR mechanism shall satisfy the following requirements:  6.3.1 Be under the oversight of the Executive Compliance Officer or an equivalent. 6.3.2 Upon receipt of a complaint, communicate to the consumer within 24 hours, an acknowledgment containing: a. a unique identification or tracking number, b. contact details of the complaints desk, c. expected resolution timeline, d. escalation options; and e. an assurance that the complaint is being addressed.  6.3.3 Use the unique identification or tracking number in all correspondence with the complainant. 6.3.4 Designate a unit for complaints handling independent of other products or business functions taking into consideration, the nature and complexity of their business. 6.3.5 Staff responsible for handling complaints shall be required to declare any conflict of interest that may affect their objectivity in handling a complaint. 6.3.6 Resolve complaints received within the time specified in the Timelines for Complaints Resolution by Institutions in Annexure D. 6.3.7 Refund identified excess charges, non-payment or under-payment of interest on deposits, unauthorized debits, etc. along with interest as provided in the extant Monetary, Credit, Foreign Trade and Exchange Policy Guidelines or any regulation issued by the CBN. 6.3.8 Issue a letter of apology to the complainant where the above applies. 6.3.9 Reconstruct customers' accounts to establish excess charges on overdrawn accounts, and pay interest on the identified excess charges after reconstruction, in accordance with extant CBN Regulations. 6.3.10 Remit established refunds and interest thereon to the complainants' accounts within the prescribed Timelines for Complaints Resolution by Institutions contained in Annexure D. 6.3.11 Send a Summary Resolution Communication (SRC) for resolved complaints, to the complainant by the next business day conveying: a. the basis for the decision(s); b. the right of appeal available to the complainant for a second level review by the Institution; and c. the right of escalation to the CBN, or other Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) avenues where the complainant is not satisfied with decisions arrived at.  6.3.12 A complaint shall be considered as resolved where the complainant has indicated acceptance of the resolution in writing to the Institution within 30 days after the receipt of the SRC, otherwise the complaint shall be deemed resolved and closed in the records of the Institution. 6.3.13 Where a complainant is dissatisfied with a decision communicated by a Institution, the complainant shall, within 30 days from the date of the receipt of the SRC, request in writing for a 2nd level review. 6.3.14 Upon receipt of a request for 2nd level review, the Institution shall review, resolve and communicate decision(s) within the Timelines for Complaints Resolution by Institutions as contained in Annexure D for second level review. 6.3.15 Identify recurring complaint types, identify their root cause(s), implement remedial measures, and generate a Root Cause Analysis Report (RCAR). 6.3.16 Prepare quarterly RCAR and submit to the Central Bank of Nigeria on or before 14th day of January, April, July and October respectively. 6.3.17 The RCAR shall contain the frequency of occurrence, identified root cause(s) and the remedial actions implemented. 6.3.18 Report complaints statistics in annual reports and the abridged Financial Statement in line with the approved format or any other format as may be prescribed by the CBN from time to time. 6.3.19 Institutions may outsource complaints handling functions subject to CBN approval.
crmp.plain: The bank shall: 1. Establish an Internal Dispute Resolution (IDR) structure and process. 2. Place the IDR under the oversight of the Executive Compliance Officer or equivalent. 3. Upon receiving a complaint, send an acknowledgment within 24 hours that includes:  a. A unique tracking number for the complaint.  b. Contact details of the officer responsible for handling the complaint.
crmp.riskDescription: - Regulatory sanctions for failing to acknowledge or resolve complaints within timelines. - Reputational damage due to poor complaint management. - Increase in customer attrition and public distrust if complaints are not promptly or transparently handled. - Risk of legal action from dissatisfied customers. - Operational disruptions caused by poorly managed complaints.
crmp.owner: - Executive Compliance Officer- Customer Experience/Service Team- Head of Operations- IT/Complaint Management System Administrator
crmp.primaryControl: - Develop and maintain a formal IDR policy. - Automate complaint logging and tracking system with timestamped acknowledgment. - Assign dedicated complaint handling officers with SLAs. - Implement workflow alerts to ensure timely escalation and response. - Regular training for staff on customer complaint handling. - Set up a central complaint database for monitoring resolution timelines.

crmp.title: COMPLIANCE
crmp.description: Institutions shall, not later than three months after the issuance of the Regulations, develop a policy approved by the Board of Directors that documents the processes, procedures and systems designed to ensure compliance with the provisions of the Regulations.
crmp.plain: The bank must, within 3 months of the issuance of these regulations, develop a Consumer Protection Compliance Policy, which must be:– Approved by the Board of Directors– Document the processes, procedures, and systems the bank will use to ensure compliance with all parts of the Consumer Protection Regulation.
crmp.riskDescription: Failure to develop and obtain Board approval for a Consumer Protection Compliance Policy within the required timeframe may lead to non-compliance with regulatory requirements, reputational risk, enforcement actions, and fines by the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN).
crmp.owner: - Head of Compliance- Legal Department- Company Secretary- Head of Risk Management- Board of Directors
crmp.primaryControl: - Compliance Unit established - Regulatory Monitoring Function in place - General policies on regulatory compliance exist - Board policy review calendar maintained

crmp.title: Exceptions to Financial Institutions posting and authorized posting options.
crmp.description: (1) From the commencement of this Act, no Financial Institution shall give posting and authorising access to any single employee. (3) Financial Institutions shall, as a duty to their customers, put in place effective counter-fraud measures to safeguard their sensitive information, where a security breach occurs the proof of negligence lies on the customer to prove the Financial Institution in question could have done more to safeguard its information integrity.
crmp.plain: The bank shall: 1. Not allow one employee to both initiate (post) and authorize financial transactions. 2. Ensure segregation of duties in financial operations. 3. Implement effective counter-fraud controls to protect customers’ sensitive information. 4. Be proactive in information security, or risk being held liable if a breach occurs and due diligence was not demonstrable.
crmp.riskDescription: - Fraudulent transactions due to weak access controls. - Legal liabilities from customers if found negligent during a data breach. - Regulatory sanctions from failure to implement prescribed internal controls. - Reputational damage from perceived operational and data security lapses.
crmp.owner: - Head of Operations- Chief Information Security Officer (CISO)- Compliance Officer- Internal Control Unit
crmp.primaryControl: - Enforce segregation of duties in transaction workflows. - Deploy dual-authentication systems for transaction posting and authorization. - Implement real-time fraud monitoring systems. - Carry out periodic security audits and access reviews. - Conduct employee training on cyber risk awareness and information security.

crmp.title: Reporting Cyber Threats
crmp.description: (1) Any person or institution, who operates a computer system or a network, whether public or private, must immediately inform the National Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT) Coordination Centre through their respective sectoral CERTS or sectoral security operations centres (SOC) of any attacks, intrusions and other disruptions liable to hinder the functioning of another computer system or network, so that the National CERT can take the necessary measures to tackle the issues. (2) In such cases mentioned in subsection (1) above, and in order to protect computer systems and networks, the National CERT Coordination Center may propose the isolation of affected computer systems or network pending the resolution of the issues.
crmp.plain: The bank must:  1. Immediately report any cyberattacks, intrusions, or disruptions that may affect other systems or networks to the National Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT) through the bank's sectoral CERT or Security Operations Centre (SOC). 2. Cooperate with CERT recommendations, including isolating affected systems until the issue is resolved.
crmp.riskDescription: - Failure to report threats could lead to non-compliance penalties. - Delay in reporting may worsen the impact of a cyberattack on the bank or other institutions. - Operational disruptions if systems are not properly isolated or handled per CERT guidelines. - Reputational risk for not acting swiftly during a cybersecurity incident.
crmp.owner: - Chief Information Security Officer (CISO)- Head of IT Security- Head of Risk Management- Chief Compliance Officer
crmp.primaryControl: - Establish a Cyber Incident Response Plan aligned with National CERT protocols. - Maintain an updated communication flowchart for threat reporting. - Train IT and security staff to identify and escalate threats immediately. - Set up real-time threat detection systems integrated with SOC/CERT frameworks.

crmp.title: Electronic Cards Related Fraud.
crmp.description: (16) An Institution that obtains the list of cardholders from an unlicensed Credit Bureau, which seeks to determine only the cardholders' ability and fails to protect the cardholders and their addresses with the permission of the cardholder but shall, within 7 working days, give notice granting or the disclosure to the cardholder and the institution which fails to comply with the requirement to notify the cardholder, commits an offence and is liable on conviction to a fine of ₦10,000,000.00.
crmp.plain: The bank shall not obtain cardholder lists from unlicensed Credit Bureaus. If cardholder data is shared (with permission), the bank must protect the cardholder and their address. They must notify the cardholder and the relevant institution within 7 working days of such disclosure. Failure to notify is a criminal offence attracting a ₦10,000,000.00 fine.
crmp.riskDescription: - Legal and regulatory risk due to non-compliance. - ₦10 million fine per offence if cardholders are not notified. - Exposure to data privacy breaches and associated litigation. - Reputational damage due to misuse or poor handling of sensitive customer data. - Increased supervisory scrutiny from regulators (e.g., NITDA, CBN, NDPC).
crmp.owner: - Chief Compliance Officer- Head of Data Protection/Privacy- Head of Cards Operations- Legal and Regulatory Affairs Department
crmp.primaryControl: - Only engage with licensed Credit Bureaus approved by regulators. - Obtain explicit consent from customers before any data sharing. - Implement data protection policies aligned with NDPR and NITDA rules. - Document and track all disclosures of cardholder data. - Ensure timely notification to cardholders within the 7-day window via email/SMS or other agreed means.

crmp.title: Duties of Financial Institutions.
crmp.description: (1) A Financial Institution shall— (a) verify the identity of its customers carrying out electronic financial transactions by requiring the customers to present National Identity Number issued by the National Identity Managment Commission and other valid documents bearing their names, addresses and other relevant information before issuance of ATM cards, credit cards, debit cards and other related electronic devices ; and (b) apply the principle of know your customer in documentation of customers preceding execution of customers electronic transfer, payment, debit and issuance orders.
crmp.plain: The bank must: (a) Verify customer identity before issuing any ATM card, debit/credit card, or electronic device, by collecting: – National Identity Number (NIN) from NIMC – Other valid documents with name, address, and other identifying information. (b) Apply Know Your Customer (KYC) principles before processing any: – Electronic transfers – Payments – Debit orders – Issuance orders
crmp.riskDescription: - Violation of customer onboarding regulations. - Exposure to fraud and identity theft risks. - Regulatory sanctions from CBN, NIMC, or NDPC. - Reputational damage due to weak KYC practices. - Increased AML/CFT exposure if identities are not properly verified.
crmp.owner: - Head of Operations- Chief Compliance Officer- Head of Risk Management- Customer Service/Account Opening Unit- Head of e-Channels/Card Services
crmp.primaryControl: - Enforce mandatory NIN collection at point of card issuance. - Conduct KYC checks (name, address, ID) during customer onboarding. - Implement automated identity verification systems (e.g., NIMC API integration). - Maintain secure documentation and storage of all KYC information. - Integrate KYC checks before electronic transfer or debit order execution.

crmp.title: Records Retention and Protection of Data
crmp.description: (1) A service provider shall keep and protect specific traffic data and subscriber information in accordance with the provision of the Nigeria Data Protection Act and as may be prescribed by the relevant authority for the time being, responsible for the regulation of communication services in Nigeria, for a period of two years. (2) A Service Provider shall, at the request of the relevant authority referred to in subsection (1) of this section or any Law Enforcement Agency— (a) preserve, hold or retain any traffic data, subscriber information, non-content information, and content data ; or (b) release any information required to be kept under subsection (1) of this section.
crmp.plain: The bank must: 1. Retain subscriber and traffic data securely for at least 2 years, in accordance with the Data Protection Act and relevant regulations. 2. Upon request by Law Enforcement Agencies or regulators, preserve, retain, and release traffic, subscriber, non-content, and content data as required by law.
crmp.riskDescription: - Hinder criminal investigations or prosecutions. - Result in regulatory sanctions and fines. - Expose the bank to data privacy violations or legal claims. - Lead to loss of public trust.
crmp.owner: - Chief Information Officer (CIO) - Chief Compliance Officer (CCO) - Data Protection Officer (DPO)
crmp.primaryControl: - Implement automated data retention systems with access logs and secure backups. - Ensure strict access controls and encryption on retained data. - Maintain policies for responding to law enforcement and regulator requests. - Align retention and disclosure practices with NDPC and NCC guidelines.

crmp.title: Failure of Service Providers to perform certain duties
crmp.description: (1) Every Service Provider in Nigeria shall comply with all the provisions of this Act and disclose information requested by any Law Enforcement Agency or otherwise render assistance in any inquiry or proceeding under this Act. (2) Without prejudice to the generality of the foregoing, a service provider shall, at the request of any law enforcement agency in Nigeria or at its own initiative, provide assistance towards— (a) the identification, apprehension and prosecution of offenders ; (b) the identification, tracking and tracing of proceeds of any offence or any property, equipment or device used in the commission of any offence ; or (c) the freezing, removal, erasure or cancellation of the services of the offender which enables the offender to either commit the offence, hide or preserve the proceeds of any offence or any property, equipment or device used in the commission of the offence.
crmp.plain: The bank must: 1. Comply fully with all provisions of the Cybercrime Act. 2. Disclose information requested by any Law Enforcement Agency. 3. Provide assistance (on request or voluntarily) in:    a) Identifying, apprehending, and prosecuting offenders.    b) Tracing proceeds, property, or equipment used in cybercrime.    c) Freezing, removing, erasing, or cancelling offender services used in commission or concealment of crimes.
crmp.riskDescription: - Obstruct cybercrime investigations. - Breach legal obligations under national laws. - Attract regulatory or criminal penalties. - Damage reputation and public trust.
crmp.owner: - Chief Compliance Officer (CCO) - Chief Legal Officer (CLO) - Head of IT/Security - DPO (for data privacy intersections)
crmp.primaryControl: - Maintain up-to-date Cybercrime Act compliance procedures. - Establish Law Enforcement Liaison Desk or protocol. - Maintain secure records to support investigations. - Integrate cybercrime intelligence sharing procedures. - Create internal Service Suspension/Deactivation Policy aligned with legal requests.

crmp.title: Cybersecurity Programme
crmp.description: SFIs are required to implement a cybersecurity programme which should, at a minimum, include: - Risk assessment - Security policy development - Incident response planning - Vulnerability management - Log monitoring - Data backup and recovery plan - Security awareness and training - Initiatives to attain target maturity level - Metrics to assess the effectiveness of the programme
crmp.plain: The bank must implement a comprehensive Cybersecurity Programme that includes the following components: - Risk Assessment - Security Policy Development - Incident Response Planning - Vulnerability Management - Log Monitoring - Data Backup and Recovery Plan - Security Awareness and Training - Initiatives to attain target cybersecurity maturity level - Defined metrics to assess effectiveness of the cybersecurity programme
crmp.riskDescription: - Increased exposure to cyberattacks or breaches - Inability to detect or respond effectively to incidents - Data loss, service disruption, or regulatory non-compliance - Legal liabilities, financial penalties, and reputational damage
crmp.owner: - Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) - Chief Compliance Officer (CCO) - Head of IT Risk - Cybersecurity Programme Manager
crmp.primaryControl: - Implement all 9 components listed in the guideline - Regularly update cybersecurity risk assessments - Establish a formal Incident Response Plan (IRP) - Conduct periodic vulnerability scans and penetration tests - Maintain real-time log monitoring and alerts - Enforce a routine backup/recovery strategy - Run quarterly security awareness trainings - Monitor and report on cybersecurity maturity improvement - Track key metrics (e.g., time to detect/respond to incidents)

crmp.source: Issuance of Risk-Based Cybersecurity Framework and Guidelines for Deposit Money Banks and Payment Service Providers
crmp.title: Other Risk Management Control Functions
crmp.description: All SFIs shall ensure the effectiveness of their cybersecurity governance by reviewing their processes and controls annually. In this regard, these risk management control functions shall have the following responsibilities:  1.6.1. Risk Management i. The Risk Management function, internal or outsourced, shall independently and proactively evaluate all cybersecurity risks. This should be executed using appropriate tools and methodologies for risk identification, analysis and control. The assessment report shall be presented to Senior Management monthly and the Board Risk Management Committee quarterly. ii. Senior Management shall ensure that staff or external risk management professionals engaged to evaluate the institution’s cybersecurity posture possess the requisite qualifications and experience.  1.6.2. Audit i. The Audit function shall be independent and the scope of cybersecurity audits shall be clearly defined. ii. The SFI’s cybersecurity programme shall be reviewed by the Audit function, internal or external, to determine the effectiveness of the controls put in place and ascertain if they are adequate for the institution’s risk exposure. iii. Senior Management shall ensure that internal or outsourced audit staff engaged to review the institution’s cybersecurity posture, possess requisite qualifications and experience.  1.6.3. Compliance The Compliance function of SFIs shall periodically review the cybersecurity programmes and processes to ensure adherence to relevant CBN directives and extant regulations.
crmp.plain: The bank must: 1. Review cybersecurity governance processes and controls at least annually. 2. Assign a Risk Management function (internal or external) to independently and proactively assess all cybersecurity risks using suitable tools and methodologies. 3. Present risk assessment reports to Senior Management monthly and to the Board Risk Management Committee quarterly. 4. Ensure Risk Management staff or external professionals have appropriate qualifications and experience. 5. Maintain an independent Audit function with a clearly defined scope for cybersecurity reviews. 6. Conduct cybersecurity audits to evaluate the effectiveness and adequacy of implemented controls. 7. Ensure Audit personnel (internal or external) possess the requisite qualifications and experience. 8. Assign the Compliance function to periodically review cybersecurity programmes for compliance with CBN directives and applicable regulations.
crmp.riskDescription: - Weakness or absence of risk, audit, or compliance oversight may lead to unidentified cybersecurity threats, ineffective governance, non-compliance with regulations, and security breaches.
crmp.owner: - Head of Risk Management - Head of Internal Audit - Chief Compliance Officer - Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) - Board Risk Management Committee - Senior Management
crmp.primaryControl: - Implement formal and structured risk assessment tools and methodologies. - Submit monthly reports to Senior Management and quarterly to the Board Risk Committee. - Conduct periodic independent cybersecurity audits. - Verify qualifications of all audit, risk, and compliance staff or consultants. - Maintain clearly defined cybersecurity audit scope and periodic compliance reviews.

crmp.title: The Risk Management System
crmp.description: 2.1.1. Risk Identification SFIs shall identify associated threats and vulnerabilities to the confidentiality, integrity and availability of their information assets to determine their cyber risk exposure.  2.1.2. Risk assessment SFIs are required to evaluate risks to their operations, probability of occurrence, impact of risk crystallisation, and security controls to mitigate identified risks. This process should be carried out annually and whenever major changes occur within the institution such as an acquisition, merger or when new technology is deployed to handle key business processes. The outcome of this process should be documented in a Cybersecurity Risk Control Self-Assessment. An independent Audit function shall be responsible for ensuring that the methodology used in risk assessment is reviewed periodically.  2.1.4. Risk mitigation/Risk treatment SFIs should implement risk mitigation and control measures consistent with the criticality of information assets. Risk treatment options such as risk reduction, acceptance, avoidance, transfer and management of residual risk should be selected based on the outcome of the risk assessment. Risk acceptance criteria should be as defined and approved by the Board. In cases where the SFI chooses to transfer risk, a detailed risk assessment for outsourcing or cyber risk insurance should be documented.
crmp.plain: The bank must: 1. Identify all threats and vulnerabilities that may affect the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of their information assets (2.1.1). 2. Assess risks to operations, evaluate likelihood and potential impact, and review current security controls (2.1.2). 3. Conduct these assessments annually and during major changes like acquisitions, mergers, or implementation of new technologies. 4. Document the result of each assessment in a Cybersecurity Risk Control Self-Assessment. 5. Ensure the Audit function periodically reviews the risk assessment methodology for adequacy (2.1.2). 6. Apply risk mitigation and control measures based on the criticality of affected assets (2.1.4). 7. Choose and document appropriate risk treatment options—such as risk reduction, acceptance, avoidance, or transfer. 8. Define and get Board approval for risk acceptance criteria (2.1.4). 9. For risk transfers (e.g., outsourcing or insurance), conduct and document a detailed risk assessment (2.1.4).
crmp.riskDescription: - Failure to properly identify, assess, and treat cyber risks may lead to data breaches, financial losses, regulatory penalties, and reputational damage.
crmp.owner: - Chief Risk Officer (CRO) - Chief Compliance Officer (CCO) - Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) - Head of Internal Audit - Board Risk Management Committee
crmp.primaryControl: - Maintain a risk register identifying threats and vulnerabilities. - Perform and document Cybersecurity Risk Control Self-Assessments. - Ensure annual and change-triggered risk assessments. - Establish Board-approved risk acceptance criteria. - Maintain audit-reviewed risk assessment methodology. - Maintain documentation for risk treatment decisions (e.g., acceptance, transfer).

crmp.title: Third party risk management
crmp.description: i. SFIs shall implement a third-party risk management framework to assess and mitigate the risks associated with such relationships. The third-party risk management framework should include processes for vendor selection, due diligence, contract negotiations, ongoing monitoring and incident response. ii. Third-party cybersecurity awareness programme shall be conducted at least annually to inform stakeholders about their roles and responsibilities around cybersecurity. iii. Contracts with third parties shall be used to implement appropriate measures designed to meet the objectives of the SFI’s cybersecurity programme. iv. Third parties shall be routinely assessed using audits, test results, or other forms of evaluations to confirm that contractual obligations are fulfilled. vii. Business continuity response and recovery planning and testing shall be conducted with third-party providers. viii. SFIs shall implement Insurance cover for various insurable technology risks to mitigate financial losses.
crmp.plain: The bank must  1. Implement a Third-Party Risk Management (TPRM) Framework covering vendor selection, due diligence, contract terms, monitoring, and incident response. 2. Conduct annual cybersecurity awareness programs for third-party stakeholders. 3. Ensure contracts with vendors reflect cybersecurity expectations aligned with internal policies. 4. crmp.title: Cybersecurity Maturity Assessment
crmp.description: An SFI shall conduct annual evaluation using the CBN Cybersecurity Self-Assessment tool (CSAT) to determine its maturity level.  2.4.1. Determining the Current Cybersecurity Profile (current state) To determine its current state, an SFI shall carry out the following: i. Identify its Inherent Cyber risks. ii. Assess existing Cybersecurity mitigants.  2.4.2. Establishing a Target Cybersecurity Profile (desired state) An SFI shall determine its desired state of cybersecurity maturity. The information security function shall ensure that a roadmap towards achieving the target cybersecurity profile is included in the SFI’s corporate strategy.
crmp.plain: The bank must:  1. Conduct a yearly self-assessment using the CBN Cybersecurity Self-Assessment Tool (CSAT). 2. Develop a roadmap, aligned with corporate strategy, to close gaps between current and target maturity levels.
crmp.riskDescription: Without a clear understanding of cybersecurity maturity and gaps, the bank may leave critical risks unaddressed, resulting in exposure to cyber threats and possible regulatory sanctions.

crmp.title: Enhancing Cybersecurity Resilience
crmp.description: Cyber resilience is the SFI’s ability to prevent, withstand and recover from cyber incidents. SFIs are required to establish procedures to enhance their cyber resilience. This will ultimately strengthen the financial industry’s cybersecurity posture. The following are the minimum controls that an SFI shall put in place to ensure the confidentiality, integrity and availability of critical information assets among others. 3.1 Know Your Environment An SFI shall proactively familiarise itself with its business environment and identify its critical assets. To ensure effective security measures, an SFI shall establish mechanisms for maintaining up-to-date inventory of authorised software, hardware as well as internal and external network connections. Additionally, an SFI shall identify and document its data, assets and capabilities. Also, potential threats and vulnerabilities associated with its assets shall be monitored. Employees and contractors providing information technology and cybersecurity services shall also be identified and documented. Details on specific controls are contained in Appendix II. 3.2 Implement Preventive Controls An SFI shall implement appropriate measures/controls/safeguards for IT systems, processes and people to mitigate cyber risks. These can be administrative, logical or physical controls. Details on specific controls are contained in Appendix III. 3.3 Monitor and Detect An SFI shall establish capability for ongoing (24/7) monitoring of its IT systems, infrastructure, applications, services, and other relevant components to promptly detect anomalies or cyber incidents. This capability may be managed internally or outsourced to a third-party provider. Notwithstanding the approach chosen, monitoring should be adequate to detect cyber threats. 3.4 Respond and Remediate An SFI shall ensure that the capability for responding to cyber incidents is available in-house or, if outsourced, can be accessed at short notice. Details on specific controls are contained in Appendix III. 3.5 Restore Service Operations An SFI shall aim at recovering its operations timeously to reduce the overall impact of cyber incidents. 3.6 Cyber-Threat Intelligence An SFI is expected to possess knowledge of emerging threats, cyber-attacks, attack vectors, mechanisms and indicators of attack/compromise that may impact its information assets. 3.7 Sector-specific Cyber Resilience An SFI is required to participate in industry cyber exercises and programmes to evaluate its level of preparedness to recover from cyber incidents. These exercises may include cyber drills, war games or as defined by the CBN from time to time. SFIs shall avoid creating single points of failure in the industry and proactively define plans to mitigate such risks.
crmp.plain: The bank must: 1. Maintain an updated inventory of all hardware, software, network components, and authorized personnel. 2. Implement and maintain preventive controls (administrative, physical, and logical) to secure IT systems, data, and personnel. 3. Ensure 24/7 monitoring to detect anomalies and cyber threats. 4. Establish in-house or outsourced incident response capabilities to contain threats. 5. Participate in cybersecurity simulations or sector-wide cyber drills.
crmp.riskDescription: Lack of asset tracking, insufficient preventive controls, delayed threat detection, or poor incident response can result in data breaches, operational disruptions, financial loss, and regulatory sanctions.
crmp.owner: - IT & Cybersecurity Team - Risk & Compliance Officer - Incident Response Team
crmp.primaryControl: - Maintain real-time asset inventory tools and auditing schedules - Enforce layered security controls (firewalls, encryption, access control) - Use SIEM solutions and external SOC support where needed - Maintain an Incident Response Plan (IRP) and CSIRT or retainer with external experts - Participate in industry drills and simulate cyber scenarios internally

crmp.title: Open Banking
crmp.description: Open Banking refers to the practice of sharing financial data, such as account and transaction information, products and services with other financial institutions and third parties through API connections. The Regulatory Framework for Open Banking in Nigeria establishes principles for data sharing across the banking and payments system to promote innovation and broaden the range of financial products and services available to bank customers. Cyber-risks associated with open banking include data privacy, fraud, identity theft and API compromise. SFIs shall ensure compliance with the provisions of the Regulatory Framework for Open Banking in Nigeria and Operational Guidelines for Open Banking in Nigeria.
crmp.plain: The bank must: 1. Comply with the Regulatory Framework for Open Banking in Nigeria and the Operational Guidelines for Open Banking in Nigeria. 2. Ensure that data sharing via APIs is secure, transparent, and consent-based. 3. Put controls in place to address cyber risks such as data privacy breaches, fraud, identity theft, and API compromise.
crmp.riskDescription: Failure to secure open banking APIs can lead to data breaches, regulatory violations, customer trust erosion, identity theft, fraud, and reputational damage.
crmp.owner: - Chief Information Officer (CIO) - Chief Compliance Officer - API Management Team - IT Security Team
crmp.primaryControl: - Enforce strong API access control (authentication, authorization, encryption) - Conduct regular API vulnerability assessments and penetration testing - Apply data minimization and anonymization for customer data - Ensure customer consent management systems are implemented - Align internal processes with Open Banking regulations and train staff accordingly

crmp.title: Adoption of Emerging Technology
crmp.description: SFIs are required to comply with the following regulations in the use of emerging technologies: 1. obtain CBN approval before deploying emerging technologies or products. 2. ensure products and services are not provided by parties or countries on sanction lists. 3. refrain from establishing API connections or granting access to organisations not licensed by the CBN without prior regulatory approvals. 4. maintain professional due diligence and care in the adoption of emerging/evolving technologies.
crmp.plain: The bank must: 1. Obtain CBN approval before deploying any new or emerging technology or product. 2. Ensure that no product or service is provided to or through parties or countries listed on sanction lists. 3. Do not integrate with or grant API access to organizations not licensed by the CBN without prior CBN approval. 4. Conduct professional due diligence and risk assessments before adopting any new or evolving technology.
crmp.riskDescription: - Unauthorized deployment of emerging tech can lead to regulatory sanctions. - Engaging with blacklisted entities could result in reputational, legal, and financial damage. - Improper API integration with unlicensed parties may expose systems to cyber-attacks. - Poorly vetted technologies could result in operational disruptions, data loss, or fraud.
crmp.owner: - Chief Compliance Officer - Chief Technology Officer (CTO) - Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) - Head of Risk Management
crmp.primaryControl: - Establish a technology governance committee to review and approve innovations. - Implement a regulatory approval checklist for new tech deployments. - Conduct sanctions screening on vendors, partners, and geographies before deployment. - Vet APIs and third-party providers for CBN licensing status. - Include risk assessments and regulatory compliance reviews in all innovation processes.

crmp.title: Metrics, Monitoring and Reporting
crmp.description: SFIs are required to measure the effectiveness of their cybersecurity programme and provide assurance to relevant authorities by defining and implementing performance metrics. Defined metrics should be aligned with strategic objectives and provide the information needed for effective decision-making at the strategic, management and operational levels. i. To assess the effectiveness of the SFIs’ cybersecurity programme and measure its performance and efficiency, metrics that may be employed include key performance indicators, key risk indicators, key goal indicators etc. Defined metrics should be reviewed at least annually. ii. The metrics should help to identify deficiencies, failed security controls as well as highlight the progress made in resolving issues. iii. SFIs shall establish effective communication channels to disseminate relevant security requirements to employees for effective implementation of the cybersecurity programme. iv. The Board shall be provided with quarterly reports to inform them of the status of the Cybersecurity programme. The contents of the reports shall be as defined in Section 1.1(viii) of this framework. v. SFIs are required to report all cyber incidents (as defined in Appendix I) not later than 24 hours after such incident is detected to the Director of Banking Supervision, Central Bank of Nigeria using the report format in Appendix VII or any other format that may be advised from time to time. Where necessary and applicable, additional information should be provided afterwards.
crmp.plain: The bank must: 1. Define and implement performance metrics (KPIs, KRIs, KGIs) to assess the effectiveness and efficiency of the cybersecurity programme. 2. Align metrics with strategic objectives and review them at least annually. 3. Use metrics to identify deficiencies, failed controls, and monitor resolution progress. 4. Establish communication channels to inform staff of cybersecurity requirements. 5. Provide quarterly cybersecurity status reports to the Board as outlined in Section 1.1(viii). 6. Report all cyber incidents to the Director of Banking Supervision (CBN) within 24 hours of detection using the format in Appendix VII (or updated format), and provide additional information when necessary.
crmp.riskDescription: -  Ineffective or absent performance metrics may lead to poor cybersecurity oversight. - Lack of communication may result in employee non-compliance. - Delays in incident reporting could attract regulatory sanctions and damage reputation. - Absence of board-level visibility into cybersecurity posture may lead to poor risk governance.
crmp.owner: - Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) - Cybersecurity Risk Officer - Head of Compliance - Internal Audit - IT Security Department - Board Secretariat
crmp.primaryControl: - Establish and maintain performance dashboards tracking KPIs/KRIs. - Schedule annual metric reviews and update as needed. - Use employee portals or emails to circulate cybersecurity obligations. - Adopt standardised reporting templates for quarterly board updates. - Maintain an Incident Response Plan with notification protocols to CBN.

crmp.title: Compliance with Statutory and Regulatory Requirements
crmp.description: i. The Board and Senior Management of SFIs shall ensure compliance with all relevant statutes and regulations to avoid breaches of legal, statutory and regulatory requirements on Cybersecurity. These include the Nigerian Cybercrimes Prohibition, Prevention Act, 2015, NDPA, 2023, National Cybersecurity Policy and Strategy, 2021 and all CBN directives. ii. An SFI is required to participate in industry cyber exercises and programmes to evaluate its level of preparedness to recover from cyber incidents. These exercises may include cyber drills, war games or as defined by the CBN from time to time. Such exercises may be conducted by the Nigeria Financial Nigeria Computer Emergency Response Team (NigFinCERT) or any other body as may be advised periodically.
crmp.plain: The bank must: 1. Ensure the Board and Senior Management comply with all statutory, legal, and regulatory requirements on cybersecurity, including:   - Cybercrimes (Prohibition, Prevention) Act, 2015   - Nigeria Data Protection Act (NDPA), 2023   - National Cybersecurity Policy and Strategy, 2021   - CBN circulars and directives 2. Participate in industry cyber preparedness programmes and exercises (e.g. cyber drills, war games) as organized or directed by CBN, NigFinCERT, or any other recognized authority.
crmp.riskDescription: - Non-compliance with applicable laws could lead to sanctions, fines, and reputational damage. - Lack of preparedness may increase vulnerability to cyberattacks and delay recovery efforts. - Failure to engage in regulatory exercises may limit awareness of evolving threats.
crmp.owner: - Board of Directors - Managing Director/CEO - Chief Compliance Officer - Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) - Legal and Regulatory Compliance Team - Cybersecurity Risk Officer
crmp.primaryControl: - Maintain a compliance checklist covering key laws and CBN circulars. - Appoint a regulatory liaison officer for CBN/NigFinCERT communication. - Enrol in annual cyber drills and maintain attendance records. - Periodically review alignment with NDPA and national policies.

(2) In the case of the Private Sector, the Scheme shall apply to employees who are in the employment of an organization in which there are 15 or more employees.  (3) Notwithstanding the provisions of subsection (2) of this section, employees of organisations with less than three employees as well as self-employed persons shall be entitled to participate under the scheme in accordance with guidelines issued by the Commission.

crmp.title: Objectives of the Act
crmp.description: The objectives of the Act are to— (a) provide for an open and fair system of guaranteed and adequate compensation for all employees or their dependants for any death, injury, disease or disability arising out of or in the course of employment; (b) provide rehabilitation to employees with work-related disabilities as provided in this Act; (c) establish and maintain a solvent compensation fund managed in the interest of employees and employers; (d) provide for fair and adequate assessments for employers; (e) provide an appeal procedure that is simple, fair and accessible, with minimal delays; and (f) combine efforts and resources of relevant stakeholders for the prevention of workplace disabilities, including the enforcement of occupational safety and health standards
crmp.plain: The Act aims to ensure that all employees, including those in banks, or their dependants, receive fair and guaranteed compensation in cases of death, injury, illness, or disability caused by work; it also provides for the rehabilitation of affected employees, requires the maintenance of a financially sound compensation fund, ensures that employer assessments are fair, establishes a simple and accessible appeals process, and mandates joint action among stakeholders to prevent workplace disabilities through the enforcement of safety and health standards.
crmp.riskDescription: Non-compliance with overall compensation principles could result in reputational/legal risks.
crmp.primaryControl: Embed Act's principles into internal HR, health, and safety policies.

crmp.title: Employee’s Notification of injury
crmp.description: (1) In every case of an injury or disabling occupational disease to an employee in a workplace within the scope of this Act, the employee, or in case of death of the dependant, shall within 14 days of the occurrence or receipt of the information of the occurrence, inform the employer by giving information of the disease or injury to a manager, supervisor, first-aid attendant, an agent in charge of the work where the injury occurred or other appropriate representative of the employer, and the information shall include—  (a) the name of the employee ;  (b) the time and place of the occurrence ; and  (c) in ordinary language, the nature and cause of the disease or injury if known.  (2) In the case of a disabling occupational disease, the employer to be informed of the death or disability is the employer who last employed the employee in the employment to the nature of which the disease was due.  (3) The employee shall, if he or she is fit to do so and on request of the employer, provide to the employer particulars of the injury or occupational disease on a form prescribed by the Board, and supplied to the employee or the dependant by the employer.
crmp.plain: When a bank employee suffers a work-related injury or disabling occupational disease, or dies from it, the employee (or their dependant) must report the incident to the bank within 14 days of the occurrence or receiving information about it. The report must be made to a manager, supervisor, first-aid officer, or any authorized bank representative and must include the employee’s name, the time and place it happened, and a simple description of the injury or disease and its cause, if known.  If it is an occupational disease, the report must be made to the last bank or employer where the employee worked under the conditions that likely caused the disease.  The employee must also fill out and submit a prescribed form with details of the incident if the bank requests it and provides the official form issued by the Board.
crmp.riskDescription: Failure to report/record on time may invalidate claims and expose bank to legal action.
crmp.primaryControl: Maintain clear internal reporting procedure; provide forms and education to staff.

crmp.description: (1) An application for compensation shall be made on the form prescribed by the Board and shall be signed by the employee or the deceased employee’s dependant.

crmp.title: Compensation for Injury
crmp.description: Any employee, whether or not in a workplace, who suffers any disabling injury arising out of or in the course of employment shall be entitled to payment of compensation in accordance with Part IV of this Act.
crmp.plain: The bank must ensure that any employee who suffers a disabling injury during the course of their official duties—regardless of whether the injury occurred within the bank premises—is entitled to compensation under Part IV of the Employees’ Compensation Act.

crmp.title: Compensation for Injury
crmp.description: Where an injury disables an employee from earning full remuneration at the workplace, compensation shall be payable pursuant to this Act from the first working day following the day of the injury, except that only a health care benefit shall be payable in respect of the day of the injury.
crmp.plain: If a bank employee is injured and can no longer earn their full salary at work, the bank must ensure that compensation begins from the first working day after the injury. On the actual day of the injury, only medical (health care) benefits are payable.

crmp.title: Compensation for Injury
crmp.description: Where an injury or disease is superimposed on an already existing disability, compensation shall be allowed only for the proportion of the disability following the personal injury or disease that may reasonably be attributed to the personal injury or disease, the measure of the disability attributable to the personal injury or disease shall, unless the contrary is shown, be the amount of the difference between the employee’s disability before and disability after the occurrence of the personal injury or disease.
crmp.plain: If an employee already has a disability and then suffers a new injury or disease related to their work, the bank must ensure compensation is paid only for the part of the disability that is caused by the new injury or disease. To determine this, the difference between the employee’s disability before and after the new injury or disease will be used—unless there is evidence proving otherwise. The bank should cooperate with the Board in providing any necessary information to make this assessment accurately.
crmp.riskDescription: Overcompensation risk; potential audit queries or fund mismanagement.

crmp.title: Compensation for Mental Stress
crmp.description: (1) Subject to sub-section (2) of this section, an employee shall be entitled to compensation for mental stress not resulting from an injury for which the employee is otherwise entitled to compensation, only if the mental stress is— (a) an acute reaction to a sudden and unexpected traumatic event arising out of or in the course of the employee's employment; or (b) diagnosed by an accredited medical practitioner as a mental or physical condition amounting to mental stress arising out of the nature of work or the occurrence of any event in the course of the employee's employment.
crmp.plain: A bank employee is entitled to compensation for mental stress that is not linked to a physical injury only if the stress results either from a sudden, unexpected traumatic event at work, or if it is diagnosed by a qualified medical practitioner as a mental or physical condition caused by the nature of the employee’s job or a specific event that occurred during the course of their employment.
crmp.riskDescription: Failure to recognize or report such cases could lead to liability for unpaid compensation or reputational harm.
crmp.primaryControl: Employee wellness monitoring; ensure HR collects trauma/stress claims; allow employee access to certified mental health professionals.

crmp.title: Compensation for Hearing Impairment
crmp.description: An application for compensation under this section shall be accompanied or supported by— (a) a report of a medical practitioner who specializes in ailments of ear or hearing accredited by the Board; (b) an audiogram and a report by the employer of the working environment where the employee has been in employment; or (c) other evidence of hearing impairment, as the Board may, from time to time, determine.
crmp.plain: When the bank submits a compensation claim for an employee suffering from hearing loss due to work-related causes, it must include supporting documentation such as: (a) a report from a Board-accredited medical specialist in hearing-related conditions, (b) an audiogram along with a report describing the employee’s work environment at the bank, or (c) any other evidence of hearing impairment as required by the Employees’ Compensation Board. The bank must ensure all required documents are compiled and submitted promptly to support the employee’s claim.
crmp.riskDescription: Failure to comply may result in claim denial, liability, regulatory penalties, or legal disputes with affected employees.

crmp.title: Compensation for Injuries occurring outside the normal Workplace.
crmp.description: Where the injury to an employee occurs while the employee is working outside the normal workplace which would otherwise entitle the employee to compensation under this Act if the injury occurred in the workplace, compensation shall be paid to the employee under this Act if—  (a) the nature of the business of the employer extends beyond the usual workplace; (b) the nature of the employment is such that the employee is required to work both in and out of the workplace; or (c) the employee has the authority or permission of the employer to work outside the normal work place.
crmp.plain: If a bank employee is injured while working outside the regular office or workplace, they are still entitled to compensation under the Act—as long as the bank’s business normally operates beyond the office, the employee’s role requires working both inside and outside the office, or the employee had the bank’s permission or authority to work off-site when the injury occurred.
crmp.riskDescription: Bank may be liable if off-site work injuries are not recognized and reported, especially for mobile or field-based staff.
crmp.primaryControl: Maintain a register of mobile or authorized off-site staff; issue written permissions; educate staff on off-site injury reporting.

crmp.title: Limitations of Actions, Subrogation
crmp.description: 91). The provisions of this Act are in lieu of any right of action, statutory or otherwise, founded on a breach of duty of care or any other cause of action, whether that duty or cause of action is imposed by or arises by reason of law or contract, express or implied, to which an employee, dependant or member of the family of the employee is or may be entitled against the employer of the employee, or against any employer within the scope of this Act, or against any employee, in respect of any death, injury or disability arising out of and in the course of employment and where no action in respect of it lies.  (2). The provisions of sub-section (1) of this section shall apply only when the action or conduct of the employer, the servant or agent of the employer or the employee, which caused the breach of duty, arose out of and in the course of employment within the scope of this Act.  (8). Nothing in this Act shall prevent an employer of the injured or deceased from maintaining an action upon contract or indemnity agreement against another employer or independent contractor in respect of the personal injury or death of an employee.
crmp.plain: (1). If a bank employee suffers injury, disability, or death arising out of and during the course of their work, the employee or their dependants cannot sue the bank, its employees, or any other employer for negligence or breach of duty. Instead, compensation must be pursued through the process provided by the Employees’ Compensation Act.  (2). This protection from legal action only applies if the incident (injury, disability, or death) happened while the bank, its staff, or agents were acting within the scope of their official duties. If the act occurred outside work responsibilities, this protection does not apply.  (8). The bank can still take legal action against another employer or an independent contractor if their actions led to the injury or death of the bank’s employee. This allows the bank to seek recovery through contract or indemnity, separate from the compensation process.
crmp.riskDescription: Legal liability or reputational damage if employee or family sues the bank outside the Act; financial loss if the bank fails to recover costs from a responsible third party.
crmp.primaryControl: 1. Educate employees/dependants on compensation procedures. 2. Include waivers during onboarding. 3. Monitor and document third-party causes of incidents. 4. Prompt internal incident reporting.

crmp.title: Compensation Cannot Be Waived
crmp.description: No employee shall agree with his employer to waive or to forego any benefit or right to compensation to which the employee or the dependants are or may become entitled under this Act.
crmp.plain: The bank is not allowed to enter into any agreement with an employee that waives or removes the employee’s or their dependants’ right to receive compensation under this Act; any such agreement is invalid, even if the employee agrees to it.
crmp.riskDescription: Risk of illegal contracts that waive employee compensation rights, leading to legal action, fines, and reputational harm.
crmp.primaryControl: Review and approval of all employment contracts; staff training on Act requirements; policy prohibiting waiver agreements.

crmp.title: Compensation Cannot Be Waived
crmp.description: Any agreement in whatever form between the employer and the employee in contravention of sub-section (1) of this section shall be void and unenforceable.
crmp.plain: If the bank enters into any agreement with an employee that tries to waive or take away the employee’s right to compensation under this Act, that agreement is automatically invalid and has no legal effect—it cannot be enforced under any circumstance.
crmp.riskDescription: Risk of unenforceable agreements causing confusion, disputes, and potential financial liability for the bank.
crmp.primaryControl: Legal review of contracts; internal communication on the invalidity of waiver agreements.

crmp.title: Contribution by Employees Prohibited
crmp.description: (1) No employer shall, either directly or indirectly, deduct from the remuneration of an employee any part of a sum which the employer is or may become liable to pay into the Fund established under section 56 of this Act, or to require or permit the employee to contribute in any manner towards indemnifying the employer against a liability which the employer has incurred or may incur under this Act.
crmp.plain: The bank must not deduct any amount from an employee’s salary, either directly or indirectly, to cover the bank’s required contributions to the Employees’ Compensation Fund, nor may the bank ask or allow the employee to pay or reimburse any part of the bank’s legal liability under the Act.
crmp.riskDescription: Illegal deduction from staff salary may trigger penalties or labour disputes.
crmp.primaryControl: Explicit internal policy prohibiting such deductions; audit payroll systems to ensure zero deductions for compensation fund.

crmp.title: Compensation not assignable or liable to attachment.
crmp.description: A sum payable as compensation by or way of computation of a periodic payment in respect of it shall not be assigned, charged or attached, or shall not pass to any other person except to a personal representative, and a claim shall not be set off against it except for a debt due to the Board by way of financial or other social welfare assistance owing to the Federal, State or Local Government, or for money owing to the Board.
crmp.plain: Any compensation paid to a bank employee under the Act—whether as a lump sum or regular payment—cannot be transferred, used as collateral, seized, or claimed by anyone else, except the employee’s legal personal representative in case of death. The only allowable deductions from the compensation are debts the employee owes to the Employees’ Compensation Board or to the government for financial or welfare assistance received.
crmp.riskDescription: Wrongful diversion or assignment of employee benefits can lead to litigation or Board sanctions.
crmp.primaryControl: Verify legal representatives with formal documentation before disbursing posthumous payments; maintain clear payment logs.

crmp.title: Compensation in Fatal Cases.
crmp.description: (1) Where death results from the injury of an employee, compensation shall be paid to the dependants of the deceased— (a) where the deceased employee leaves dependants wholly dependent upon his earnings a widow or widower— (i) and two or more children, a monthly payment of a sum equal to 90 per cent of the total monthly remuneration of the employee as at the date of death, (ii) and one child, a monthly payment of a sum equal to 85 per cent of the total monthly remuneration of the deceased employee as at the date of death,
crmp.plain: If a bank employee dies due to a work-related injury, compensation must be paid monthly to the employee’s dependants. If the deceased leaves behind a widow or widower and two or more children, they are entitled to 90% of the employee’s last total monthly salary. If the deceased leaves behind a widow or widower and only one child, they are entitled to 85% of the employee’s last total monthly salary.
crmp.riskDescription: Failure to facilitate accurate and timely compensation to dependants can lead to legal or reputational risk.
crmp.primaryControl: Notify NSITF and provide full employment and salary records for calculation; verify dependants through legal documents.

crmp.title: Compensation relating to enemy warlike actions
crmp.description: Where death, injury, disability or disease of an employee occurs in the course of the employment as a direct result of enemy warlike action or counteraction and compensation has been made for compensation in respect of such action for the employee or the deceased employee’s dependants by the Government, the employer, or his or her dependants are entitled to compensation under this Act only when the compensation provided by the Government is less than that provided by the Act, and shall be only to the extent of the difference.
crmp.plain: If a bank employee dies, is injured, disabled, or becomes ill due to enemy warlike action or counteraction during the course of their work, and the government has already paid compensation, the bank or the employee’s dependants are only entitled to additional compensation under this Act if the government payment is less than what the Act provides—and only up to the difference in amount.
crmp.riskDescription: Duplicate claims or overcompensation if employer fails to confirm amounts paid by government.
crmp.primaryControl: Obtain formal records of compensation already received from government before filing additional claim to the Board.

crmp.title: Permanent Total Disability.
crmp.description: (1) Subject to this Act, if a permanent total disability results from the injury of an employee, the Board shall pay to the employee compensation that is a periodic payment equal to 90 per cent of the remuneration of the employee. (2) The compensation awarded under this section shall be payable monthly.

crmp.title: Permanent Partial Disability or Disfigurement
crmp.description: (1) Subject to this Act, if a permanent partial disability results from the injury of the employee, the Board shall— (a) estimate the impairment of earning capacity from the nature and degree of the injury; and (b) pay the employee’s compensation that is a periodic payment equal to 90 per cent of an estimate of the loss of remuneration resulting from the impairment.  (2) The compensation referred to in sub-section (1) of this section shall be determined and calculated in accordance with the Second Schedule to this Act.  (3) The Board may, by regulations published in the Federal Gazette, revise or amend the Second Schedule to this Act.  (4) Subject to this Act, if— (a) a permanent partial disability results from the injury of an employee; and (b) the Board makes a determination under sub-section (5) of this section with respect to the employee, the Board may pay the employee compensation with a periodic payment that is equal to 90 per cent of the difference between the remuneration of the worker before the injury and whichever of the following amounts the Board considers better represents the loss of earnings of the employee the remuneration that— (i) the employee is earning after the injury; or (ii) the Board estimates the employee is capable of earning in a suitable occupation after the injury.  (5) A payment may be made under sub-section (4) of this section only if the Board determines that the combined effect of the occupation of the employee at the time of the injury and the disability resulting from the injury is so exceptional that an amount determined under sub-section (1) does not appropriately compensate the employee for the injury.  (6) In making a determination under sub-section (5) of this section, the Board shall consider the ability of the employee to continue in his or her occupation at the time of the injury or to adapt to another suitable occupation.  (7) Where permanent partial disability results from the injury, the minimum compensation awarded under this section shall be calculated in the same manner as provided by section 24 of this Act for temporary total disability but to the extent only of the partial disability.  (8) Where the employee has suffered a serious and permanent disfigurement which the Board considers is capable of impairing the employee’s earning capacity, a lump sum in compensation may be paid, although the amount the employee was earning before the injury has not been diminished.
crmp.plain: If a bank employee suffers a permanent partial disability due to a work-related injury:  1. Earning Loss Estimation: The Employees’ Compensation Board will estimate how the injury has reduced the employee’s ability to earn based on the nature and extent of the injury.  2. Standard Compensation Payment: The employee will receive a regular (periodic) payment equal to 90% of the estimated loss in earnings. This is calculated according to the method outlined in the Second Schedule of the Act. The Board can revise that schedule if needed.  3. Exceptional Circumstances Adjustment: If the employee’s situation is exceptional (e.g., their injury and previous job type make continued employment or transition unusually difficult), and the standard formula under subsection (1) would not fairly compensate them, the Board may: - Compare what the employee earned before the injury with either: - what they are earning after the injury, or - what the Board believes they could earn in a suitable alternative job. Then, pay 90% of the income difference as compensation.  4. Occupation Suitability Check: The Board must assess whether the employee can continue in their previous job or reasonably adapt to another suitable occupation before deciding to apply this exceptional approach.  5. Minimum Compensation Rule: The minimum compensation for permanent partial disability must be calculated in the same way as temporary total disability under Section 24, but adjusted to reflect the level of partial disability.  6. Disfigurement Lump Sum: If the employee suffers a serious and permanent disfigurement (e.g. visible injury) that may reduce their ability to earn, the Board can also pay a lump sum—even if their current earnings haven’t decreased.

crmp.title: Health Care and Disability Support
crmp.description: The Board may authorize employers to provide health care at the expense of the Board on terms fixed by the Board and the employer shall provide to an injured employee, when necessary, immediate conveyance and transport to a hospital or accredited medical practitioner for initial treatment.
crmp.plain: The Board may allow the bank to provide health care to an injured employee, with the cost covered by the Board under terms they set. However, the bank must, without delay, ensure that any injured employee is immediately transported to a hospital or accredited medical practitioner for initial treatment whenever needed.
crmp.riskDescription: Delay or failure in transporting injured employees may worsen health outcomes and create legal/reputational risks.
crmp.primaryControl: Emergency response protocol; designated HSE officers; approved vendor for staff medical transport

crmp.title: Provisional Assessment
crmp.description: (1) Where— (a) an employer fails to comply with section 39 of this Act within the time required under this Act; or (b) the information provided under section 39 of this Act does not, in the opinion of the Board, reflect the probable amount of the payroll of the employer or correctly describe the nature of the work carried on, the Board may assess such sum as it is in its opinion, the probable payroll of the employer or nature of the employer’s industry.  (2) If it is later determined that the assessment under sub-section (1) of this section, is different from the required assessment, the employer or the Board shall be liable to pay to the other the difference.
crmp.plain: If the bank fails to submit its payroll details on time as required under Section 39 of the Act, or if the payroll information submitted is considered inaccurate or misleading by the Employees’ Compensation Board, the Board has the authority to estimate what it believes is the bank’s likely payroll or correct industry classification and use that for assessment. If it is later discovered that the Board’s estimate was too high or too low, the bank must pay the difference if it underpaid, or the Board must refund the excess if the bank overpaid.
crmp.riskDescription: Inaccurate or late payroll reporting may result in overpayment or underpayment and compliance penalties.
crmp.primaryControl: Payroll reconciliation processes; deadlines monitored; review by finance and compliance teams before submission.

crmp.title: Payment of Minimum Wage
crmp.description: (1) Every employer shall pay a national minimum wage of not less than N70,000.00 per month to every worker under his establishment, except otherwise provided under this Act.
crmp.plain: The bank must ensure that every employee on its payroll is paid a minimum monthly wage of ₦70,000, in line with the national minimum wage requirement. This is a mandatory baseline, and no employee should earn below this amount, unless a specific exemption is provided under the Act

crmp.title: Exemptions
crmp.description: (1) Section 3 (1) does not apply to— (a) an establishment in which workers are employed or paid on— (i) part-time basis, and (ii) commission or piece-rate ; (b) an establishment employing less than 25 persons ; (c) workers in seasonal employment like agriculture ; and (d) any person employed in a vessel or aircraft to which the laws regulating merchant shipping or civil aviation apply.
crmp.plain: The bank must note that the national minimum wage requirement does not apply to the following categories:  - Workers employed on a part-time, commission-only, or piece-rate basis, - Establishments with fewer than 25 employees, - Workers engaged in seasonal employment (e.g., agriculture), - Employees working on vessels or aircrafts governed by merchant shipping or civil aviation laws.

crmp.title: Enforcement.
crmp.description: The national minimum wage may be enforced by the aggrieved worker, trade unions and Minister of Labour and Employment as follows— (a) a worker who is paid an amount less than the national minimum wage is contractually entitled to whichever is the higher amount of the difference between his pay and the amount of the national minimum wage that he should have been paid ;
crmp.plain: If the bank pays any worker less than the national minimum wage, the affected employee has a legal right to claim the difference between what was paid and what should have been paid. This claim can be enforced directly by the employee, through a trade union, or by the Minister of Labour and Employment. crmp.title: Procedure before dispute is reported.
crmp.description: If there exists agreed means for settlement of the dispute apart from this Act, whether by virtue of the provisions of any agreement between organisations representing the interests of employers and organisation of workers or any other agreement, the parties to the dispute shall first attempt to settle it by that means.
crmp.plain: Before reporting a trade dispute under the Act, the Bank must ensure that all agreed internal or external dispute resolution methods (e.g., collective agreements, union-employer frameworks, industry arrangements) have been attempted first.

crmp.title: Apprehension of trade dispute by the Minister.
crmp.description: (1) Notwithstanding the foregoing provisions of this Act, where a trade dispute is apprehended by the Minister he may in writing inform the parties or their representative of his apprehension and of the steps he proposes to take for the purpose of resolving the dispute.  (2) Such steps as the Minister may, pursuant to this section, take may include— (a) the appointment of a conciliator under section 8 of this Act; or (b) a reference of the dispute or any matter relating thereto for settlement to the Industrial Arbitration Panel under section 9 of this Act; or (c) a reference of the dispute to a board of inquiry under section 33 of this Act.
crmp.plain: If the Minister believes a trade dispute is about to arise involving the Bank, the Minister may formally notify the Bank and outline the steps to resolve it. crmp.title: Notice requiring compliance with sections 4 and 6.
crmp.description: (1) The Minister shall, if not satisfied that the requirements of sections 4 and 6 of this Act have been substantially complied with, issue to the parties a notice in writing specifying the steps which must be taken to satisfy those requirements and may specify in the notice the time within which any particular steps must be taken. (2) Where after the expiration of the period specified in the notice issued under subsection (1) above or, if no period is specified, after the expiration of fourteen days following the date the notice is issued, the dispute remains unsettled and the Minister is satisfied— (a) that the steps specified in the notice have been taken; or (b) that either party is, for its part, refusing to take those steps or any of them, the Minister may proceed to exercise such of his powers under section 8, 9, 17 or 33 of this Act as may appear to him appropriate.
crmp.plain: If the Minister believes that the Bank (or any other party to a dispute) has not properly followed the procedures in Sections 4 and 6, the Minister will issue a written notice listing the steps that must be taken to comply. The Bank must act within the time stated in the notice (or within 14 days if no time is specified). If the dispute is still unresolved after that time—and either the steps have been taken or the Bank refuses to take them—the Minister may move the matter forward using legal options such as appointing a conciliator, referring the case to arbitration, or establishing a board of inquiry.

crmp.title: Appointment of conciliator, etc.
crmp.description: (1) The Minister may for the purposes of section 7 of this Act appoint a fit person to act as conciliator for the purpose of effecting a settlement of the dispute. (2) The person appointed as conciliator under this section shall inquire into the causes and circumstances of the dispute and by negotiation with the parties endeavour to bring about a settlement. (3) If a settlement of this dispute is reached within seven days of his appointment, the person appointed as conciliator shall report the fact to the Minister and shall forward to him a memorandum of the terms of the settlement signed by the representative of the parties, and as from the date on which the memorandum is signed (or such earlier or later date as may be specified therein), the terms recorded therein shall be binding on the employers and workers to whom those terms relate.
crmp.plain: Once the Minister determines that intervention is necessary, the Bank must cooperate with the conciliator appointed by the Minister to help resolve the dispute. The conciliator will investigate the cause of the dispute and negotiate with both parties. If a settlement is reached within seven days, a written agreement must be signed by both sides and submitted to the Minister. That agreement becomes legally binding on the Bank and its employees from the date stated in the document.

crmp.description: (1) An employer shall not declare or take part in a lock-out and a worker shall not take part in a strike in connection with any trade dispute where— (a) the procedure specified in section 4 or 6 of this Act has not been complied with in relation to the dispute; or (b) a conciliator has been appointed under section 8 of this Act for the purpose of effecting a settlement of the dispute; or (c) the dispute has been referred for settlement to the Industrial Arbitration Panel under section 9 of this Act; or (d) an award by an arbitration tribunal has become binding under section 13 (3) of this Act; or (e) the dispute has subsequently been referred to the National Industrial Court under section 14 (1) or 17 of this Act; or (f) the National Industrial Court has issued an award on the reference.
crmp.plain: The bank (as an employer) must not declare a lock-out, and workers must not go on strike in connection with any trade dispute if any of the following has occurred or applies:  The required settlement steps haven’t been followed – If the parties have not first tried to settle the dispute themselves (Section 4) or reported the failure to the Minister (Section 6), a strike or lock-out is illegal.  A conciliator has been appointed by the Minister (Section 8) – Once the Minister appoints a conciliator to help resolve the dispute, strikes or lock-outs must stop while the process is ongoing.  The dispute has been sent to the Industrial Arbitration Panel (IAP) (Section 9) – If the Minister has referred the case to the IAP for arbitration, no industrial action can take place while the panel is handling it.  An arbitration award has become binding (Section 13(3)) – Once the IAP makes a decision (award) and it becomes legally binding, no one can strike or lock out over that matter.  The dispute has been sent to the National Industrial Court (NIC) (Section 14(1) or Section 17) – If the Minister sends the dispute directly to the NIC—either because one party objects to the award (Section 14(1)) or the case involves essential services or urgent matters (Section 17)—industrial action must stop.  The National Industrial Court has issued a decision – If the NIC has already ruled on the dispute, no further strike or lock-out is allowed on that issue.
crmp.riskDescription: Reputational and legal risk from illegal strike or lock-out during official dispute processes
crmp.primaryControl: Enforce internal disciplinary and compliance protocols prohibiting unauthorized industrial action
