crmp.source: Discontinuation of Death Benefits Account (DBA) for Deceased Employees under the Contributory Pension Scheme
crmp.title: Mandatory Opening of RSA & Discontinuation of DBA
crmp.description: Section 11(1) of the Pension Reform Act (PRA) 2014 mandates every eligible employee to maintain a Retirement Savings Account (RSA) with a Pension Fund Administrator of his/her choice. The Act also mandates every employer to open a nominal RSA within six months of assumption of duty for the employee who fails to open an RSA in accordance with section 11(5) of the PRA 2014. Employers are therefore required to ensure that RSAs are opened for all their employees. Prior to the PRA 2014, Death Benefits Accounts (DBA) have been used by legal beneficiaries to access the benefits of the deceased employees who did not open RSA during their lifetime. However, pursuant to the above cited statutory provisions, this practice is no longer valid. Accordingly, the general public is hereby notified that the processing of DBA for death benefits claims would be discontinued with effect from 1 February, 2020. All PFAs have been directed to stop the opening of DBAs with effect from 31 January, 2020.
crmp.plain: Every eligible employee must open an RSA with a PFA. If not opened within 6 months, the employer (bank) must open a nominal RSA. As of 1 Feb 2020, banks can no longer rely on DBAs to access death benefits for deceased employees without RSAs.
crmp.riskDescription: Failure to ensure RSAs are opened for all staff could result in beneficiaries being unable to claim death benefits, leading to legal, reputational, and regulatory risks.

crmp.source: De-marketing of Banks by Other Banks
crmp.title: BSD/DIR/CIR/07/VOL.2/016
crmp.description: The CBN has again noted with serious concern the recent practice whereby some officers of deposit money banks engage in the de-marketing of other banks through disparaging comments and the use of negative text messages. This development, which constitutes a threat to the safety and soundness of the banking system, is unprofessional, unethical and unacceptable. Banks and their staff are by this circular reminded that the responsibility for ensuring the safety and soundness of the banking system is a collective one for all stakeholders.
crmp.plain: The Bank and its employees must not engage in de-marketing other banks. This includes making disparaging remarks, spreading negative messages, or using text messages, social media, or any other means to damage the reputation of competitor banks.  Such actions are unethical, unprofessional, and threaten the safety and soundness of the financial system. The Bank is required to uphold professional conduct and must ensure that its staff refrain from any form of negative campaigning against other financial institutions.
crmp.riskDescription: Reputational and regulatory risk due to unprofessional conduct; possible CBN sanctions for unethical behavior; erosion of public confidence in the banking system

crmp.source: Revised Guidelines for Blacklisting for Banks and Other Financial Institutions in Nigeria
crmp.title: Blacklisting by FIs
crmp.description: In order to ensure fairness and accountability, FIs shall adhere to the following procedure before the decision to blacklist an individual: i. Where an alleged offence as outlined in this Guidelines is discovered/reported/made against an individual, an investigation shall be conducted by the FI to determine the veracity of the allegations. ii. Upon verification of the existence of grounds for blacklisting, the FI shall notify the affected individual in writing, of the allegations timeously and he/she shall be required to respond to the allegations within 14 days from the receipt of the notification. iii. Upon receipt of the individual’s response, a Disciplinary Committee (DC) shall be setup to review the matter. iv. The individual shall be invited by the DC to present evidence that may aid in his/her defense. This invitation shall be received within 14 days prior to the sitting of the committee. v. Where an individual fails to appear before the DC after invitation, without any written notice stating the reasons for not appearing, the DC shall proceed with the process. However, where the individual has justifiable reasons for not appearing, the DC shall extend the invitation for a reasonable period that may allow the  individual to appear. vi. Based on the evidence presented during the hearing, the DC shall make a decision regarding the individual. vii. If the individual is indicted, the case shall be referred to an IRP for further review and validation. viii.In the course of the review, the IRP is at liberty to invite parties or call for any evidence presented at the sitting of the DC. ix. The decision(s) of the DC and the IRP shall be communicated to the individual involved. x. Where there is a conflict between the decisions of the DC and IRP, the decision of the IRP shall prevail. xi. The above procedure shall also apply to individuals who have resigned prior to discovery of an eligible offence.
crmp.plain: The Bank must follow a documented, step-by-step process before blacklisting any individual (whether current or former staff). The guideline outlines exact timelines, specific procedural steps, and communication duties. These include: - Investigation of the alleged offence. - Written notification to the individual with a 14-day response window. - Formation of a Disciplinary Committee (DC). - Notice period of 14 days before the DC hearing. - Opportunity for the individual to defend themselves. - Referral to an Independent Review Panel (IRP) if indicted. - Final decision by the IRP prevails if there is conflict.  The entire process is mandatory and must also apply to individuals who resigned before the alleged offence was discovered.
crmp.riskDescription: Non-compliance could lead to legal disputes, CBN sanctions, or employee victimization claims.
crmp.primaryControl: Step-by-step procedure checklist; documentation maintained for each case.

crmp.source: Chartered Institute of Bankers of Nigeria Act, 2007
crmp.title: Registrations of members
crmp.description: 10. Registration of members  (1) An individual, other than one whose membership has been suspended by a directive of the Disciplinary Tribunal shall be entitled to be registered as a member in the following categories:  (a)  Ordinary Member, where the person does not satisfy the conditions for registration as a Student Member, Graduate, Associate, Honorary Senior Member, Honorary Fellow or Fellow specified in paragraphs (b) to (g) of this section;  (b)  Student Member, where the person-  (i) works in a financial institution and has a degree or equivalent qualification or the minimum qualification prescribed by the Council; or  (ii)  does not work in a financial institution, but has the basic qualification approved by the Council, from time to time, for registration as a student; or                  (iii) satisfies any other condition which the Council may, from time to time, approve;  (c) Graduate Member where the person-  (i) has passed the associateship examination specified by the Council but has not had the period of on-the-job practical experience prescribed by the Council;  (ii) not being a member of the Institute at the time of application for membership, has passed the qualifying examinations of an Institute of Bankers in any other country acceptable to the Council; or                 (iii) has not been elected a Fellow or an Associate by recognised  foreign Institute of Bankers  (d)          Associate Member where the person-                                  (i)            has passed the associateship examination specified by the Council;  (ii)           not being a member of the Institute at the time of application for membership, has passed the qualifying examinations of an Institute of Bankers in any other country acceptable to the Council; or  (iii)          has had a period of on-the-job practical experience not less than the minimum period prescribed by the Council for the category of membership sought; or                                  (iv)         has been elected by any recognized foreign Institute to that category of membership  (e)          Honorary Senior Member, where the person-  (i)            does not satisfy the condition for registration as an Associate or Fellow specified in paragraphs (d) and (g) of this subsection, but has obtained the academic qualifications prescribed by the Council for honorary senior membership; and  (ii)           occupies a senior management position in a bank, any other financial institution or tertiary educational institution;   (g)          Fellow, where the person-  (i)            satisfies the Council that he is a fit and proper person to be so registered and has for a number of years (to be specified by the Council) been an Associate Member, and  (ii)           satisfies all other criteria as may be specified by the Council from time to time .  (2) An applicant for registration shall in addition to evidence of qualification, satisfy the Council that-                  (a)          he is of good character; and                  (b)            he has not been convicted in Nigeria or elsewhere of an offence involving fraud or  dishonesty.                (3) A banking institution shall be entitled to be registered as a corporate member where it has been-  (a) licensed to carry out the business of banking in Nigeria; and  (b) satisfied any other condition which the Council may from time to time approve.
crmp.plain: The individual staff applying for CIBN membership are registered in the appropriate category (Ordinary, Student, Graduate, Associate, Honorary Senior Member, Fellow) based on qualifications, experience, and criteria set by the CIBN Council. Before nominating or supporting any staff for CIBN registration, the bank must ensure the individual is of good character and has not been convicted of fraud or dishonesty in Nigeria or abroad. The bank itself (as a legal entity) must be registered as a corporate member of the CIBN if it is licensed to operate as a bank in Nigeria, and it must meet any other conditions set by the CIBN Council.
crmp.riskDescription: Wrong membership classification or onboarding of unqualified staff.

crmp.title: Approval of qualifications, etc.
crmp.description: 11. Approval of qualifications, etc.  (1) The Council may approve any qualification for the purposes of this Act and may for those purposes approve-  (a) any course of training at any approved institution which is intended for persons seeking to become members of the banking profession and which the Council considers is designed to confer on persons completing it, sufficient knowledge and skill for registration with the Institute; and  (b) any qualification which as a result of an examination taken in conjunction with a course of training approved by the Council under this section, is granted to candidates having reached a standard at the examination, indicating in the opinion of the Council that the candidates have sufficient knowledge and skill to be registered with the Institute.  (2) The Council may, if it thinks fit, withdraw any approval given under this sections in respect of any course, qualification or institution but before withdrawing such an approval the Council shall-  (a) give notice that it proposes to do so to persons in Nigeria appearing to the Council to be a person by whom the course is conducted or the qualification is granted or the institution is controlled, as the case may be;  (b) afford such a person an opportunity of making to the Council representations with regard to the proposal; and  (c) take into consideration any representations made in respect of the proposal in pursuance of paragraph (b) of this subsection.  (3) A course, qualification or institution shall not be treated as approved during any period the approval is withdrawn under subsection (2) of this section.  (4) Notwithstanding the provisions of subsection (3) of this section, the withdrawal of an approval under subsection (2) of this section shall not prejudice the registration or eligibility for registration, of any person who by virtue of the approval was registered or was eligible for registration (either unconditionally or subject to his obtaining a certificate or experience), immediately before the approval was withdrawn.  (5) The giving or withdrawal of an approval under this section, shall have effect from such date, whether before or after the execution of the instrument signifying the giving or withdrawal of the approval, as the Council may specify in the instrument and the Council shall-  (a)   as soon as may be possible, publish a copy of every such instrument; and  (b)  not later than seven days before its publication, as aforesaid, send a copy of the instrument to the institution affected.

crmp.source: Chartered Institute of Bankers of Nigeria Act, 2007
crmp.title: Establishment of Investigation Panel and Disciplinary Tribunal.
crmp.description: (1) There shall be constituted a body to be known as the Chartered Institute of Bankers of Nigeria Investigating Panel (in this Act referred to as "the Investigating Panel") which shall be charged with the duty to-  (a) conduct a preliminary investigation into any case where it is alleged that a member of the Institute has violated the provisions of the Institute’s Code of Conduct or shall for any other reason be the subject of proceedings before the Disciplinary Tribunal;  (b)   decide whether the case should be referred to the Disciplinary Tribunal or not.  (3) The Investigating Panel shall be appointed by the Council and shall consist of five members as follows-  (a)   two members of the Council, one of whom shall be Chairman of the Panel; and (b)   three members of the Institute who are not members of the Council.
crmp.plain: The Bank must cooperate with the CIBN Investigating Panel if a case is brought against any staff for misconduct or breach of the CIBN Code of Conduct. The bank must make relevant documentation and the accused staff available for preliminary investigation. Staff must also uphold ethical and professional banking standards to avoid being referred to the Disciplinary Tribunal.
crmp.riskDescription: Staff misconduct without reporting or disciplinary follow-up.
crmp.primaryControl: Code of Conduct; report protocol for CIBN issues.

crmp.title: Application of this Act to unregistered persons.
crmp.description: A person who is not a member of the Nigerian Institute of Bankers established before the commencement of this Act who but for this Act is qualified to apply for and obtain membership of the Institute may apply for membership of the Chartered Institute of Bankers of Nigeria established by this Act, in such manner as may be prescribed by rules made by the Council and shall be registered in the category of membership appropriate in the current period for holders of the qualification he possesses.
crmp.plain: Any staff working in the bank who was not previously a member of the Nigerian Institute of Bankers before the commencement of the CIBN Act but is otherwise qualified, must be supported to apply for registration with the Chartered Institute of Bankers of Nigeria in the appropriate membership category based on their qualifications.

crmp.source: Chartered Institute of Bankers of Nigeria Act, 2007
crmp.title: Practice as a member of the banking profession.
crmp.description: A person other than a corporate member shall be deemed to practice as a member of the banking profession if, in consideration of remuneration received or to be received and whether by himself or in partnership with any other person- (a)   he engages himself in the practice of banking or holds himself out to the public as a member of the banking profession; or (b)  he renders professional service or assistance in or about matters or principle or detail relating to banking procedure; or (c)  he renders any other service which may be by regulations made by the Council, be designated as service constituting practice as a member of the banking profession.
crmp.plain: Any person practicing banking or offering professional banking services (e.g., advisory, procedure-based, or other services defined by CIBN) for a fee must be a registered member of the Chartered Institute of Bankers of Nigeria (CIBN), either individually or through a registered corporate entity.
crmp.riskDescription: Unauthorized or unlawful practice of banking roles.
crmp.primaryControl: CIBN verification check in recruitment & contracts.

crmp.description: (1) The Council may make rules to guide training in banking methods and practice.

crmp.source: Harmonisation of Job Titles in the Banking Industry, December 2007
crmp.title: Job Title Standardization
crmp.description: "Some banks designate their personnel, particularly the top management staff, with job titles that are different from the conventional ones. While the practice may not be bad in itself, it may be difficult for the public and third parties to know the level of authority and responsibility such designations depict. For simplicity and comparison across banks, it has become necessary to harmonise such designations with those already well known"..  "Banks are reminded that section 5.2.2 of the Code of Corporate Governance for Banks disallows the creation of the position of Executive Vice-Chairman and requires that the position of the Chairman of the Board must be separate and distinct from that of the Chief Executive Officer. Titles like “Group Director” or “Regional Director” are also not permitted designations in the banking industry. All institutions are to note that this directive takes effect from the date of this circular".
crmp.plain: Banks must use only the job titles approved by the CBN for their top and senior management personnel. This ensures uniformity, public understanding of authority levels, and compliance with the CBN's corporate governance framework. Titles not listed in the approved format, such as "Group Director," "Regional Director," or "Executive Vice-Chairman," must not be used. Additionally, the roles of Chairman and Chief Executive Officer must remain separate.
crmp.riskDescription: Use of unapproved or misleading job titles may create regulatory breaches, reputational damage, or stakeholder confusion.
crmp.primaryControl: Review and update job titles to conform with approved designations; ensure segregation of Chairman and CEO roles.

crmp.title: Entry for business purposes, etc.
crmp.description: (1) No person other than a citizen of Nigeria shall-   (a)  accept employment (not being employment with the Federal Government or a  State Government) without the consent in writing of the Director of Immigra-   tion; or   (2) Any person desirous of entering Nigeria for any of the purposes in subsection (1)  of this section, shall produce the consent to an immigration officer; and the failure to do so shall be an offence under this Act, and any person who commits such an offence shall  be liable on conviction to deportation as a prohibited immigrant.   3) Where any person exempt from any provision of this Act restricting his employment ceases to be so exempt, he shall be deemed to be a person seeking entry into Nigeria  for the first time; and the provisions of this section shall have effect accordingly.
crmp.plain: The Bank must not employ a non-Nigerian (except in federal or state government service) unless it has obtained prior written consent from the Director of Immigration. It must ensure that such consent is presented upon the non-Nigerian’s entry into Nigeria, and must not continue to employ foreign nationals who lose their exemption status without treating them as new entrants, subject to immigration rules.
crmp.riskDescription: Unauthorized employment of foreign nationals, resulting in legal breaches or deportation.
crmp.primaryControl: Immigration verification before employment; recordkeeping of immigration consents

crmp.title: Employment of immigrants.
crmp.description: (1) Where any person in Nigeria is desirous of employing a person who is a national  of any other country he shall, unless exempted under this section, make application to the   Director of Immigration in such manner as may be prescribed and shall give such information as to the provision to be made for repatriation of that national and his dependants   as the Director of Immigration may reasonably require; and no such person shall be employed without the permission of the Director of Immigration given on such terms as he  thinks fit; the provisions of this section shall extend and apply to persons in employment immediately before, as well as to those employed or to be employed at any time after, the commencement of this Act.   (2) The Director of Immigration shall record the information in such form as he thinks necessary; and where he is so satisfied, the Director of Immigration may require provision to be made for repatriation either generally as to all persons so employed by a person in Nigeria and their dependants or with reference to any particular person, by payment into the Consolidated Revenue Fund by way of deposit of such amount as the Minister may prescribe for the repatriation, or by a bond in such form as the Director of Immigration may approve for such purpose.   (3) The Minister may, by notice, exempt any person from the requirements of this section on such conditions as he thinks fit, and subject thereto any person to whom this section applies who is employed in Nigeria, shall on ceasing for any reason to be so employed be deemed to be a prohibited immigrant as from the date of his entry into Nigeria;  and the person who employed him shall be liable to pay all costs of and incidental to deportation of the prohibited immigrant and of his dependants.
crmp.plain: The Bank must not employ a foreign national without obtaining prior permission from the Director of Immigration. It must provide required repatriation arrangements, which may include deposits or bonds. If the foreign employee ceases employment, the bank is responsible for the cost of deportation.
crmp.riskDescription: Financial or legal liability from non-compliance with foreign employment obligations
crmp.primaryControl: Pre-employment immigration clearance; maintain repatriation bonds/deposits where required

crmp.source: Competency Framework for the Nigerian Banking Industry, November 2012
crmp.title: Approved Persons Database
crmp.description: 4.1 To ensure that only Fit and Proper persons man the different job roles and control functions within the banking industry, all persons for the position of Assistant General Manager and above as well as critical operational positions shall be approved for appointment in line with the Assessment Criteria for Approved Persons Regime issued and reviewed from time to time by the CBN. 4.2 In furtherance of this objective, a central database for approved persons shall be created and maintained at the CBN. All banks as reporting institutions shall update the database with details of approved persons and access it as part of their due diligence prior to the engagement and appointment of persons within the industry. 4.3 The database will: i. Assign a unique identifier to each banking practitioner. ii. Be accessed prior to the engagement or appointment of persons to board, top management or critical operational positions in the banking industry. iii. Provide reference information to relevant stakeholders – regulators, employers, employees, auditors, business partners, etc – for the assessment of the continuous Fitness and Propriety of approved persons in the industry iv. Encourage transparency in the recruitment and appointment process.
crmp.plain: The Bank shall:  4.1 Ensure that only qualified, trustworthy, and competent people are appointed into important roles. Anyone being considered for **Assistant General Manager or higher**, or for other key operational roles, must first be approved by the **Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN)** using the **Fit and Proper criteria** set by the CBN and updated from time to time.  4.2 Work with the CBN to support a **central database** that keeps records of all persons approved for such roles. The Bank must update this database with relevant information and also check it during **background checks** before hiring or appointing anyone into these positions.  4.3 Understand that this database will:  * (i) Give each approved banking professional a **unique ID**. * (ii) Be used **before hiring or appointing** anyone into board-level, top management, or other sensitive positions. * (iii) Serve as a **reference tool** for regulators, employers, auditors, and other stakeholders to regularly assess whether the individual remains “fit and proper.” * (iv) Help promote **fairness and openness** in how people are hired and appointed in the banking industry.
crmp.riskDescription: Hiring unfit individuals without approval could lead to sanctions and governance failures.
crmp.primaryControl: Due diligence and CBN vetting process

crmp.source: Competency Framework for the Nigerian Banking Industry, November 2012
crmp.title: Code of Practice for Approved Persons
crmp.description: 5.1 An approved person, performing a controlled function, must act with integrity, due skill, care and diligence. He/she must observe proper standards of market conduct and deal with regulators in an open and cooperative way, disclosing any information of which regulators would reasonably expect to be notified. 5.2 An approved person performing a significant influence function must: i. Take reasonable steps to ensure that the business of the financial institution for which he is responsible is organized so that it can be controlled effectively. ii. Exercise due skill, care and diligence in managing the business of the financial institution for which he is responsible in his controlled function. iii. Take reasonable steps to ensure that the business of the financial institution for which he is responsible complies with relevant laws, rules, guidelines and other regulatory requirements
crmp.plain: The Bank shall:  5.1 Ensure that any person approved to perform a **controlled function** (such as a director or top executive) must:  * Always act **honestly**, and with the necessary **skills**, **care**, and **attention** required. * Follow the proper rules and behavior expected in the financial industry. * Be **open and cooperative** with regulators, and must share any information that regulators would reasonably expect to be told.  5.2 Where the approved person holds a **significant influence role** (such as a Managing Director or Executive Director), the person must:  * (i) Take all necessary steps to **organize the bank’s operations** in a way that allows effective management and control. * (ii) Use the required **skills, care, and judgment** when managing the bank’s affairs. * (iii) Make sure the bank **follows all applicable laws, rules, guidelines, and regulatory requirements**.
crmp.riskDescription: Misconduct or negligence can expose the bank to sanctions or regulatory interventions.
crmp.primaryControl: Code of Conduct, training, monitoring

crmp.source: Competency Framework for the Nigerian Banking Industry, November 2012
crmp.title: Training and Certification
crmp.description: 6.1 The framework seeks to ensure that persons engaged in the various job families/controlled functions have adequate skills and competencies to carry out the roles for which they have been certified. 6.2 There shall be structured generic and function or role-specific training and certification process that provides a reliable and objective assessment of an employee‟s competence and ability to perform and meet the demands of a job consistently over time. Competencies and their related certifications will be based on job roles rather than job titles. 6.3 Training and certification will be provided by industry-recognized and/or accredited local and overseas training service providers. The minimum requirements for certification of each job role/control function are as indicated in Appendix B. 6.4 A training service provider could be any of the following:  An individual  A profit-oriented consultancy outfit or commercial entity  A not-for-profit entity  The training/learning centres of banks  Relevant professional bodies  A university, polytechnic or other relevant educational institutions of higher learning. 6.5 Banks are expected to put in place policies that ensure quality and equitable training for all their staff. In this regard, training programmes attended by bank personnel over a period will be evaluated on the basis of total credit points obtained within a given period of time. 6.6 To attain and maintain competency in a particular job role, the individual responsible for a controlled function is expected to accumulate a minimum number of predetermined credit points, through attendance at and successful completion of accredited training programmes. 6.7 The credit points for training programmes attended shall be awarded by designated accreditation agencies, taking into cognisance such factors as:  Duration and coverage of the programme,  The faculty of the programme,  Quality and relevance of the programme,  The pedigree of the training provider. 6.8 To ensure objectivity and credibility in accumulating the required credit points, not more than 25 per cent shall be obtainable through an institution‟s in-house training programmes. 6.9 The number of relevant accredited training attended and credit points accumulated shall be one of the assessment criteria in determining the suitability of approved persons for specific job roles/functions. Consequently, banks shall be required to populate the Approved Persons Database with details of credit points earned by approved persons in their employ.
crmp.plain: The Bank shall:  6.1 Make sure that anyone hired into key job roles or control functions has the **right skills and abilities** needed to do the job they were approved for.  6.2 Set up a structured system of **general and role-specific training and certification**. This system must provide a **fair and reliable way to assess** whether an employee is competent and able to meet the demands of their job **consistently over time**. Training requirements will be tied to **job roles**, not just job titles.  6.3 Use only **recognized training providers**—both local and international—for all certification programs. The **minimum certification requirements** for each job role or function are listed in **Appendix B** of the framework.  6.4 Training providers may include:  * Independent individuals * Commercial training firms * Not-for-profit organizations * Banks’ own training centers * Professional bodies * Universities, polytechnics, and other higher institutions  6.5 Put in place policies to ensure that all employees get **equal access to high-quality training**. Staff training will be **measured by credit points** earned over time.  6.6 Require that anyone performing a **controlled function** must reach a minimum number of **credit points** to prove their competence, which must be earned by **attending and completing accredited training programs**.  6.7 Ensure that credit points are awarded by **approved accrediting agencies**, based on:  * How long the program lasts and what it covers * The quality and experience of the trainers * The usefulness and relevance of the content * The reputation of the training provider  6.8 Limit the number of credit points that can come from **in-house training** to **no more than 25%** of the total required, to keep the system fair and credible.  6.9 Keep track of and report the **credit points earned** by approved persons in the bank. These points will be used to **evaluate whether an individual is suitable** for specific roles or functions. Banks must **update the CBN’s Approved Persons Database** with this information regularly.
crmp.riskDescription: Incompetency due to lack of training may result in regulatory breaches or operational failures.
crmp.primaryControl: Structured training plans, credit tracking

crmp.source: Competency Framework for the Nigerian Banking Industry, November 2012
crmp.title: Accreditation of Training Service Providers
crmp.description: 7.1 The accreditation of a training service provider will be conducted by an industry-recognized accreditation agency. The agency will carry out extensive review and evaluation in order to ascertain if the provider has the competence to conduct the training programme(s) envisaged under the Framework. 7.2 An agency shall be designated as an accreditation agency, subject to meeting the qualifying criteria to be prescribed by the Bankers‟ Committee and approved by the CBN from time to time. 7.3 An accreditation agency could be any of the following: i. A recognized professional institute/body ii. A recognized educational institution of higher learning iii. A recognized training consultancy outfit iv. Other duly recognized body, institution or company. 7.4 The accreditation of training providers is a quality assurance mechanism to ensure that the training provider is qualified to provide the desired training and the programmes of the training provider meet the learning objectives and will impact the requisite knowledge, skills and competencies required for each job role. 7.5 The accreditation agency shall be responsible for accrediting training service providers. This will involve the endorsement of the training provider and its programmes based on an assessment of its curricula, competence, capacity, capability, faculty, resources, facilities, credibility, independence and integrity among other criteria, in carrying out specific training programme(s). The accreditation agency shall:  Register training service providers  Undertake an annual review of all training service providers and periodic review of their facilities for continuous quality assurance and relevance 7.6 There shall be two types of accreditation of training service providers, namely Solicited or Unsolicited. 7.7 Accreditation may not be solicited in respect of:  well established and/or industry-recognized training and certification programmes offered by qualified and eligible training service providers under this framework.  A training service provider duly accredited by a competent accreditation agency in Nigeria. 7.8 In every other case, training service providers wishing to offer their services in the Nigerian banking industry shall solicit and be duly accredited by a competent accreditation agency under this framework. Where accreditation is solicited, the cost of accreditation shall be borne by the service provider.
crmp.plain: The Bank shall:  7.1 Ensure that all training service providers used by the Bank are **accredited** by a **recognized accreditation agency**. This agency will thoroughly review and evaluate the provider to confirm that it is capable of delivering the type of training required under the Competency Framework.  7.2 Only an agency that meets the **eligibility standards** set by the **Bankers’ Committee** and **approved by the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN)** can be designated as an accreditation agency.  7.3 An accreditation agency may include:  * (i) A well-known **professional body or institute** * (ii) A **reputable higher education institution** * (iii) A **recognized training consulting firm** * (iv) Any other legitimate and reputable **institution, company, or body**  7.4 The purpose of accreditation is to ensure **quality and reliability**. It confirms that the training provider is capable of delivering effective training that meets learning goals and builds the right skills and competencies for each job role.  7.5 The accreditation agency will:  * **Approve (accredit) training providers and their programs**, after checking their course content, qualifications, resources, trainers, reputation, independence, and professionalism. * **Register accredited training providers** * **Review their programs and facilities each year** and from time to time, to make sure quality and relevance are maintained.  7.6 There will be **two types of accreditation**:  * **Solicited accreditation**: when the provider applies to be accredited. * **Unsolicited accreditation**: when accreditation is automatically recognized based on existing credibility or prior approval.  7.7 **Unsolicited accreditation** may apply to:  * Reputable and well-known training programs that are already recognized in the industry. * Training providers already accredited by a **qualified Nigerian accreditation agency** under this framework.  7.8 In all other cases, **any training provider that wants to offer training to banks** must **formally apply (solicit) for accreditation** from a competent agency. The **training provider must pay the cost** of the accreditation process.
crmp.riskDescription: Unaccredited training can invalidate competency status of approved persons.
crmp.primaryControl: Maintain list of CBN-approved providers

crmp.source: Competency Framework for the Nigerian Banking Industry, November 2012
crmp.title: Role of Stakeholders
crmp.description: The financial institutions will provide specification of minimum competencies needed for each job role along with inputs for the specification of career paths, job descriptions and training curriculum needed for the development of the framework. Furthermore they are expected to:   Comply with data protection requirements.  Update the database with details of training programmes and credit units obtained by each officer performing a controlled function.  Periodically review the requirements of each controlled function.  Financial institutions are expected to continually satisfy themselves that the persons performing controlled functions have the necessary qualifications, experience, competence and capacity to carry out their duties
crmp.plain: The Bank shall:  * Provide clear information on the **minimum skills and competencies** required for each job role. This includes contributing to the development of **career paths**, **job descriptions**, and **training curriculum** needed under the Competency Framework.  * In addition, the Bank shall:    * **Follow data protection rules** to safeguard employee information.   * **Update the central database** regularly with details of all **training programs attended** and **credit points earned** by staff performing **controlled functions**.   * **Periodically review the job requirements** for all controlled functions to ensure they remain relevant and up to date.  * The Bank must also **continuously verify** that everyone performing a controlled function has the **right qualifications, skills, experience, and capacity** to do their job effectively and responsibly.
crmp.riskDescription: Non-compliance may result in outdated job-role specifications or regulatory default.
crmp.primaryControl: Ongoing role review and data update

crmp.title: Liability to Contribute to the Fund
crmp.description: (1) Every employer having either 5 or more employees in its establishment, or having less than 5 employees but with a turnover of N50m and above per annum, shall, in respect of each calendar year and or the prescribed date, contribute to the Fund one per centum of its total annual payroll.
crmp.plain: The bank must contribute 1% of its total annual payroll to the Employees’ Compensation Fund every calendar year if it has 5 or more employees. Even if the bank has fewer than 5 employees, it is still required to contribute if its annual turnover is ₦50 million or more. This contribution must be made by the prescribed deadline each year.
crmp.riskDescription: Legal action or regulatory disqualification due to non-compliance
crmp.primaryControl: Payroll triggers & ITF compliance calendar

crmp.title: Refund
crmp.description: (a) The Council may make a refund of up to fifty per centum of the amount paid by an employer if the Council is satisfied that the training programme of the employer is in accordance with the Fund's reimbursement schemes. (b) The Council shall notify the Federal Board of Inland Revenue of any refund made pursuant to this Act.
crmp.plain: If the bank conducts employee training that aligns with the ITF approved reimbursement schemes, it may be eligible to receive a refund of up to 50% of its training contribution. To qualify, the bank must submit its training programme for assessment by the ITF. If approved, the ITF will notify the Federal Inland Revenue Service (FIRS) of any refund granted.

crmp.title: The Objectives & Application
crmp.description: (4) The categories of data subjects in whom Sub-Airieds 3 relates are:  (a) A data subject who is within the territory of Nigeria - regardless of nationality and migration status;  (b) A data subject whose personal data has been transferred to Nigeria;  (c) A data subject whose personal data is in transit through Nigeria - without more - provided that the obligation of the data controller or data processor responsible for the transmission through Nigeria to another jurisdiction shall be limited to data confidentiality, integrity and availability;  (d) A Nigerian citizen who is not within Nigeria - taking into account the universal right to privacy under the United Nations Universal Declaration of Human Rights, 1948, as well as the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights, 1976, provided that:  In this circumstance, the Commission may seek mutual legal assistance from the relevant authorities in the country where such citizen is resident in order to safeguard his or her privacy right as may be recognised under International Law; and  The obligation of the data controller or data processor in this circumstance of Article 1(4)(d) shall be limited to the terms of mutual legal assistance and any applicable International Law.
crmp.plain: The Bank must ensure that the personal data of all data subjects is protected, including: - Anyone physically in Nigeria, regardless of whether they are a Nigerian citizen or a foreign national. - Individuals whose personal data is sent into Nigeria, even if they are not in the country. - Individuals whose personal data passes through Nigeria (e.g. during international data transfers), ensuring the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of such data. - Nigerian citizens living abroad, with responsibilities limited to what is permitted by international law or mutual legal assistance agreements.  The Bank must implement proper policies, systems, and controls to secure personal data for all these categories, in compliance with the Nigerian Data Protection Act (NDPA), 2023.
crmp.riskDescription: Failure to apply NDPA protections to all relevant categories of data subjects (especially foreigners in Nigeria, or Nigerians abroad) could result in non-compliance, reputational damage, and sanctions.

crmp.title: Material Context of Data Processing and Priority of the NDP Act
crmp.description: (a) Every person, body or authority owes a duty of care to data subjects, to carefully examine the material context of personal data processing with a view to ascertaining whether the processing required in the said context is consistent with the constitutional right to privacy and the objectives set forth in section 1 of the NDP Act.  (c) The implication of the itemisation in Sub-Article 2(b) above is that personal data is fundamental to the performance of transnational and inherent functions of the Federal Government of Nigeria as well as to trade and commerce – by persons or entities – which transcend subnational levels; the Act, therefore, applies as a common statutory authority for the protection of privacy of data subjects in the Federal Republic of Nigeria; and  (d) Data controllers and data processors shall take into consideration the material character of data – particularly its value, volume, variety, velocity and veracity – as it flows within and beyond the Nigerian territory and put in place appropriate technical and organisational measures to mitigate associated risks.
crmp.plain: (a). The Bank must evaluate every data processing activity to ensure it aligns with the right to privacy guaranteed under the Constitution and the objectives of the Nigeria Data Protection Act (NDPA), 2023.  (c). Since personal data plays a critical role in cross-border trade, commerce, and national governance, the NDPA serves as the primary law for protecting the privacy of all data subjects in Nigeria.  (d). The Bank must assess the nature of personal data it processes—including its value, volume, speed, type, and accuracy—and must implement adequate technical and organizational controls to reduce data risks, especially for data moving within or outside Nigeria

crmp.title: Statutory Remedy in Respect of Double or Multiple Regulatory Framework on Data Protection
crmp.description: (1) In order to guarantee certainty, harmony and efficacy on the regulation of: a) Informational self-determination (fundamental right to privacy); b) Data sovereignty (the inherent right of an independent country to govern data processing pertaining to persons in her territory); c) National and cross-border data flows; and d) Treaty obligations (particularly in the material context highlighted in Article 2(b) of this GAID), it is imperative to uphold the provision of section 63 of the NDP Act in all proceedings and transactions pertaining to the processing of personal data. For ease of reference Section 63 of the NDP Act provides: “Where the provisions of any other law or enactment, in so far as they provide or relate directly or indirectly to the processing of personal data, are inconsistent with any of the provisions of this Act, the provisions of this Act shall prevail.”  (2) In the event of a conflict between the NDP Act and this GAID, the NDP Act shall prevail.  (3) Upon the issuance of the GAID, the Commission shall cease to apply the Nigeria Data Protection Regulation (NDPR) 2019 as a legal instrument for regulating data privacy and protection. In line with Section 64 of the NDP Act relating to transitional provisions, this measure shall not affect anything done under the NDPR prior to the issuance of this GAID.
crmp.plain: The Bank must ensure that in all data processing activities, the provisions of the Nigeria Data Protection Act (NDPA), 2023 shall take precedence over any other law or regulation that conflicts with it. If there's a conflict between the NDPA and any existing data privacy law (including the older Nigeria Data Protection Regulation, NDPR 2019), the NDPA must be followed. The bank must immediately stop relying on NDPR 2019 as a legal basis for data protection compliance and must fully align with the new NDPA provisions and any directive (GAID) issued under it.
crmp.riskDescription: Risk of relying on outdated laws like NDPR 2019 or applying conflicting sectoral regulations, leading to legal non-compliance.
crmp.primaryControl: Legal review and policy updates to align with NDPA; decommission old NDPR-based policies

crmp.title: Cooperation between the Commission and a Public Authority
crmp.description: (2) Without prejudice to the provisions of Section 63 of the NDP Act, the Commission shall cooperate with relevant public authorities in the development of sub-national or sectoral guidelines on data protection.  (3) The Commission shall conduct periodic reviews of sub-national or sectoral guidelines to determine whether such guidelines or instruments comply with the NDP Act, taking into account the provisions of Articles 1 & 2, of this GAID.  (4) Where the Commission determines that a guideline by a public authority relating to the processing of personal data negates the objectives of the NDP Act, it shall communicate its decisions to the public authority and it may in addition, request joint reviews with a view to developing a harmonious sub-national or sectoral guideline.   (5) The Commission shall take proactive steps in collaborating with public authorities and relevant institutions for the purposes of setting up Data Privacy Service Units, Legal Clinics for Data Privacy, Centres of Excellence or similar forums at sub-national, sectoral and organisational levels.
crmp.plain: The Bank must align with any sector-specific or sub-national data protection guidelines that are developed in collaboration with the Nigeria Data Protection Commission (NDPC). It should regularly review such guidelines to ensure they comply with the NDPA. If any directive or practice issued by a public authority (such as the CBN or NDIC) conflicts with the NDPA, the NDPC has the power to request a review to bring such guidelines into compliance. Therefore, the bank must defer to harmonized NDPA-compliant guidelines and stay updated on changes initiated by the Commission.
crmp.riskDescription: Failure to align with evolving sectoral data protection guidelines may result in regulatory action or reputational risk.
crmp.primaryControl: Liaison with NDPC and regulatory bodies (e.g., CBN) on data protection directives; review internal policies accordingly

crmp.title: Evaluation of Exemptions to the NDP Act
crmp.description: (1) A data controller, a data processor or an individual who relies on or intends to rely on any exemption pursuant to Section 3 of the NDP Act, shall abide by other provisions which are not exempted by the NDP Act.  (2) A data processing activity which falls within the exemptions under Section 3 of the NDP Act is at the minimum, bound by the following provisions of the NDP Act: a) S. 24 – Principles of personal data processing b) S. 25 – Lawful basis of personal data processing c) S. 32 - Designation of Data Protection Officers d) S. 40 – Personal data breaches notification e) Part VI - Data subjects’ rights  (3) Exemptions under the NDP Act apply to the obligations under Chapter V of the NDP Act apart from the sections mentioned in Sub-Article 2 of this Article. Thus, the Commission shall hold a data controller or data processor accountable for the infraction of any other provision of the NDP Act not covered by the exemption.
crmp.plain: If the Bank relies on any exemption under Section 3 of the NDPA, it must still comply with key requirements including: principles of data processing, lawful basis, appointment of a Data Protection Officer (DPO), breach notifications, and the rights of data subjects. The NDPC will still hold the Bank accountable for breaches of these non-exempted sections.
crmp.riskDescription: Misinterpreting exemptions could lead to non-compliance with key NDPA provisions, exposing the Bank to regulatory penalties.
crmp.primaryControl: Maintain a compliance checklist that identifies all applicable NDPA obligations even when exemptions apply

crmp.title: General NDP Act Compliance Measures by Data Controllers and Data Processors
crmp.description: a) Register with the Commission as a data controller or data processor of major importance as the Commission may determine in accordance with the NDP Act. d) Identify all its obligations under the NDP Act and prepare schedules of compliance; f) Prepare and follow Schedules on Monitoring Evaluation and Maintenance of Data Security System in order to guarantee data confidentiality, integrity and availability; g) Prepare and follow schedules on organisation-wide, internal sensitisation and training on data privacy and protection in order to foster a culture of compliance with the NDP Act and best practices; i) In the case of a data controller or data processor of major importance, designate a Data Protection Officer (DPO). Associate DPOs/Privacy Champions may be designated to support the DPO where the data controller or the data processor carries out data processing or interfaces with data subjects on multiple platforms and places; j) Develop or review its organisational privacy policies, the privacy policy shall be in compliance with the NDP Act; k) Publish its organisational privacy policies on its platforms with a view to sensitising data subjects on data processing activities as well as rights and duties in connection therewith;  l) Provide privacy and cookie notices at the homepage of its website. The cookie notice should give a data subject the opportunity to decline or accept the notice; A cookie notice must be displayed in such a way that it significantly obstructs the middle, the left or the right side of the home page of a website. Displaying a cookie notice at the bottom of a webpage where it may be ignored or be  unnoticed by a data subject is tantamount to lack of transparency in data processing. m) Ensure that the privacy policy and notice is transparent and appropriately provided on platforms/places where data processing is taking place; and without prejudice to the NDP Act, it shall also take into account specific directions on privacy by relevant Application Hosting Platforms through which a data subject may access its services; n) Develop and circulate an internal data protection strategy or policy and basic privacy checklist to help members of staff and other relevant persons (such as vendors, agents and contractors) understand the organisation’s direction in connection with the processing of personal data and outline the steps they are to take to ensure the organisation’s direction is maintained; o) Conduct a Data Privacy Impact Assessment (DPIA) when required under the NDP Act, or when directed by the Commission; q) Notify a data subject immediately after becoming aware of a personal data breach that may pose high risk to his or her privacy; r) Update agreements with third party processors to ensure compliance with the NDP Act; s) Design systems and processes to make data requests and access seamless for data subjects; t) Design systems and processes to enable data subjects to easily correct or update their personal data; u) Design systems and processes to enable data subjects easily transfer data to another platform or person (natural or artificial); v) At least within the six (6) months of commencement of business and then, at the minimum, on an annual basis, train its personnel on data protection law and practices; and  w) Clearly explain the complaints process to data subjects including the right to lodge a complaint with the Commission.
crmp.plain: 7(a) The bank must register with the Nigeria Data Protection Commission (NDPC) as a data controller or processor of major importance, if so designated.  7(d) The bank must identify all its compliance obligations under the NDPA and create documented schedules to track and fulfill these obligations.  7(f) The bank must implement and maintain regular evaluation and monitoring procedures to ensure the security, confidentiality, and integrity of personal data.  7(g) The bank must organize ongoing internal training and awareness programs for staff to build a culture of data protection compliance.  7(i) If classified as a data controller/processor of major importance, the bank must appoint a Data Protection Officer (DPO). Where needed, assign supporting privacy champions.  7(j) The bank must develop or revise its internal privacy policy to ensure it aligns with the requirements of the NDPA.  7(k) The bank must publish its NDPA-compliant privacy policy on its platforms so that customers understand how their data is collected and used.  7(l) The bank must display cookie notices prominently on its website, allowing users to accept or reject cookies. It must not hide these notices at the bottom of the page.  7(m) The bank must ensure its privacy notices are clearly visible on any platform where personal data is collected, and must comply with relevant hosting platform requirements.  7(n) The bank must develop and distribute an internal privacy strategy and checklist for staff, vendors, and partners, outlining key data protection duties and procedures.  7(o) The bank must conduct a Data Privacy Impact Assessment (DPIA) when legally required or when directed by the NDPC.   7(q) The bank must notify affected data subjects immediately if a personal data breach that could harm their privacy occurs.  7(r)The bank must review and update contracts with third-party service providers to ensure their compliance with the NDPA.  7(s) The bank must implement systems that allow customers to easily request access to their personal data.  7(t) The bank must put in place systems that allow customers to update or correct their personal information easily.  7(u) The bank must provide customers with systems to enable the transfer of their data to another provider or platform (data portability).  7(v) The bank must train its staff on data protection laws and practices within six months of starting operations, and continue with yearly training sessions.  7(w) The bank must provide a clear and accessible complaint process for customers, including how they can escalate issues to the NDPC.

crmp.title: Designation of Data Controllers and Data Processors of Major Importance
crmp.description: (1) Section 65 of the NDP Act provides, “data controller or data processor of major importance” means a data controller or data processor that is domiciled, resident in, or operating in Nigeria and processes or intends to process personal data of more than such number of data subjects who are within Nigeria, as the Commission may prescribe, or such other class of data controller or data processor that is processing personal data of particular value or significance to the economy, society or security of Nigeria as the Commission may designate.
crmp.plain: The Bank that processes the personal data of a large number of individuals in Nigeria — such as customers, employees, or vendors — or processes data that is critical to Nigeria’s economy, financial stability, or national security, may be classified by the Nigeria Data Protection Commission (NDPC) as a Data Controller or Data Processor of Major Importance (DCMI/DPMI). It must monitor NDPC's designation criteria and ensure compliance with all enhanced obligations that apply to DCMIs/DPMIs.
crmp.riskDescription: Failure to identify and comply as a DCMI/DPMI may lead to non-compliance with heightened obligations, NDPC sanctions, or reputational risk.
crmp.primaryControl: Regularly monitor NDPC thresholds and classification updates; conduct internal reviews of data volumes and risk

crmp.description: (2) “Operating in Nigeria” as stated in section 65 includes a data controller or a data processor who targets a data subject in Nigeria. Such data controller or processor may not be domiciled in or resident in Nigeria. This is taking into consideration the provision of section 2(2)(a) of the NDP Act on the Application of the Act as well as sections 24(3) and 44 on the need to hold accountable data controllers and processors whose processing activities significantly impact the economy, society or security of Nigeria.
crmp.plain: The Bank — even if not physically located or registered in Nigeria — is considered to be operating in Nigeria if it targets Nigerian data subjects, such as by offering banking products or services to individuals in Nigeria. Under the NDPA, The Bank will be held accountable if its data processing activities significantly affect the economy, society, or security of Nigeria. The Bank must ensure compliance with Nigerian data protection laws if it falls within this scope of operation.

crmp.description: (3) In carrying out an objective assessment of what is of value or significance to the economy, society or security of Nigeria, the Commission shall take into consideration all relevant factors – including but not limited to the following: a) The risks that the data processing by a data controller or a data processor poses to a data subject if such data controller or data processor is not under the obligation imposed by the NDP Act on a data controller or a data processor of major importance as contemplated by section 29(1)(a) of the NDP Act; b) The implication for data sovereignty where data controllers or data processors may advertently or inadvertently transfer data outside Nigeria’s jurisdiction to the detriment of the economy, society or security of Nigeria; c) The sensitivity of the personal data involved;  d) Data driven financial assets entrusted by data subjects in the care of the data controller or data processor; e) Reliance on third party servers or cloud computing services for the purpose of substantial processing of personal data;  f) Substantial involvement in cross-border data flows; g) Use of filing systems and automation of data processing; h) Number of data subjects involved; and i) The need for international standard certifications for people, processes and technologies involved in data confidentiality, integrity and availability.
crmp.plain: When determining whether The Bank is a Data Controller or Data Processor of Major Importance, the Nigeria Data Protection Commission (NDPC) will assess how The Bank’s data activities may affect Nigeria’s economy, society, or security. This includes reviewing:  Risks to individuals if The Bank is not held to stricter standards, Whether data is being transferred outside Nigeria in a way that harms national interests, - How sensitive the personal data is (e.g., financial, biometric), - Whether The Bank holds data-driven financial assets on behalf of customers, - If it relies on cloud services or third-party servers for significant data processing, - The Bank’s level of cross-border data sharing, - Its use of automated systems and structured databases, - The number of data subjects affected,

crmp.title: Designation of Data Controllers and Data Processors of Major Importance
crmp.description: (4) In order to ensure proportionality of obligations in relation to various levels of major data processing, the Commission classifies data controllers and data processors into 3 (three) levels or categories of major data processing, namely: (a) Ultra-High Level (UHL) (b) Extra-High Level (EHL) (c) Ordinary-High Level (OHL)
crmp.plain: The Bank should be aware that if it is classified as a Data Controller or Data Processor of Major Importance, it will fall into one of three categories based on the scale and sensitivity of its data processing: - Ultra-High Level (UHL) - Extra-High Level (EHL) - Ordinary-High Level (OHL)
crmp.riskDescription: Misclassification or failure to track classification status may result in non-compliance with proportional obligations under the NDPA.
crmp.primaryControl: Annual classification self-assessment and documentation; verify category with NDPC if unclear.

crmp.title: Filing of NDP Act Compliance Audit Returns with the Commission
crmp.description: (1) A data controller or a data processor shall carry out periodic compliance audit of its data processing activities with a view to mitigating the risk of data breaches through appropriate technical and organizational measures.
crmp.plain: The Bank must periodically conduct a compliance audit of its data processing activities. This is to identify and address any weaknesses, and to reduce the risk of data breaches. The audit should assess whether The Bank has in place the appropriate technical and organizational measures to protect personal data in line with the NDPA.
crmp.riskDescription: Failure to conduct regular audits could lead to undetected data vulnerabilities and regulatory penalties.
crmp.primaryControl: Annual data protection compliance audit cycle

crmp.title: Filing of NDP Act Compliance Audit Returns with the Commission
crmp.description: (2) In order to carry out an audit, a data controller or a data processor shall adopt a risk-based approach as may be associated with people, processes and technologies involved in its data processing value chain.
crmp.plain: To perform a proper compliance audit, The Bank must use a risk-based approach that considers the risks associated with its people, processes, and technologies used in the entire data processing value chain. This ensures that The Bank focuses on the most critical areas where data protection failures could occur.
crmp.riskDescription: Using a generic audit method could miss high-risk vulnerabilities specific to banking operations.
crmp.primaryControl: Conduct risk assessments to drive audit scope and focus

crmp.description: (3) A data controller or a data processor shall develop or adopt privacy audit controls in line with global best practices. Each model of audit may comprise of a series of techniques ranging from simple to complex and technical to organizational.
crmp.plain: The Bank must develop or adopt privacy audit controls that align with global best practices. These controls may involve a mix of technical and organizational techniques, ranging from basic checks to advanced assessments, depending on the model of audit chosen. This ensures that The Bank’s data audits are effective, comprehensive, and in line with international standards.
crmp.riskDescription: Poor audit models may lead to incomplete findings, non-compliance, and data breaches.

crmp.title: Filing of NDP Act Compliance Audit Returns with the Commission
crmp.description: (4) A data controller or data processor shall identify each point of risk and determine the techniques and frequency of audit to be carried out on each point of risk subject to any directive by the Commission.
crmp.plain: The Bank must identify every point of risk in its data processing activities and decide how often and by what method each risk point should be audited. This determination must be based on internal assessments, but The Bank must also comply with any specific audit instructions or directives issued by the Nigeria Data Protection Commission (NDPC).
crmp.riskDescription: Failure to tailor audit frequency and techniques to specific risks could lead to gaps in protection or missed vulnerabilities.

crmp.description: (5) Where personal data may be accessed from an online device of a data controller or data processor, such personal data is vulnerable to data security breach by means of cyber technology. The audit of such online device shall be as frequently as possible.
crmp.plain: If The Bank uses online devices or systems (e.g. servers, apps, platforms) through which personal data can be accessed, that data is at high risk of cyber-related breaches. Therefore, The Bank must audit these online systems as frequently as possible to detect and prevent data breaches through cyber technology.

crmp.title: Designation of a Data Protection Officer
crmp.description: (1) Section 32 of the NDP Act mandates the designation of a DPO, accordingly, the DPO may be a member of staff of the data controller or data processor, or fulfil the tasks on the basis of a service contract.
crmp.plain: Under Section 32 of the NDPA, The Bank is required to appoint a Data Protection Officer (DPO). The DPO can be either an internal staff member, or an external professional engaged under a service contract.
crmp.riskDescription: Absence of DPO may result in non-compliance with NDPA and poor oversight of data privacy controls.
crmp.primaryControl: Appointment letter, DPO job description, HR onboarding

crmp.title: Position of the Data Protection Officer
crmp.description: (1) A data controller or a data processor shall actively engage its DPO in all issues which relate to the processing of personal data.
crmp.plain: The Bank must actively involve its Data Protection Officer (DPO) in all matters related to the processing of personal data. This includes decisions, reviews, and policies that affect how personal data is collected, stored, shared, or protected. The DPO must be a central part of The Bank’s data governance process
crmp.riskDescription: Excluding DPO may lead to flawed data governance and breaches.
crmp.primaryControl: Policies requiring DPO sign-off

crmp.title: Position of the Data Protection Officer
crmp.description: (2) The data controller or data processor shall give appropriate support to the DPO in performing the data protection responsibilities as prescribed by the NDP Act or by the Commission. Accordingly, the data controller or data processor shall put in place the necessary organisational measures, namely: a) Provide necessary resources to the DPO to carry out data protection tasks;
crmp.plain: The Bank must support its Data Protection Officer (DPO) by ensuring they have the resources needed to perform their responsibilities effectively. This includes providing access to tools, personnel, training, systems, or funding necessary to carry out data protection duties as required by the NDPA or directed by the NDPC.
crmp.riskDescription: Inadequate resourcing may hinder effective data protection oversight.
crmp.primaryControl: Budget allocation and performance KPIs

crmp.title: Position of the Data Protection Officer
crmp.description: 2b) Ensure access to personal data processing activities and processing operations; and
crmp.plain: The Bank must ensure that its DPO has full access to all personal data processing activities and operations. This access is essential for the DPO to effectively monitor compliance, identify risks, and guide The Bank in upholding data protection standards.
crmp.riskDescription: Restricted access could prevent DPO from identifying and addressing risks.
crmp.primaryControl: Access rights and documentation protocols

crmp.title: Position of the Data Protection Officer
crmp.description: 2c) Make adequate provision for continuous training for the DPO.
crmp.plain: The Bank must ensure its DPO receives ongoing training to stay updated on data protection laws, best practices, and emerging risks. Continuous professional development is required so the DPO can perform their role effectively and in compliance with the NDPA.
crmp.riskDescription: Poor training may result in poor risk detection and outdated compliance practices.
crmp.primaryControl: Training schedules, CPD tracking

crmp.title: Position of the Data Protection Officer
crmp.description: (3) The data controller or data processor shall ensure that the DPO does not carry out his or her task under duress, coercion, covert or overt influence.
crmp.plain: The Bank must ensure that its DPO operates independently and without interference. The DPO must not be subjected to pressure, coercion, or any form of influence whether hidden or open that could compromise their ability to carry out their duties under the NDPA.
crmp.riskDescription: Coerced DPOs may compromise data protection standards.
crmp.primaryControl: DPO autonomy policy and whistleblowing channels

crmp.title: Position of the Data Protection Officer
crmp.description: (4) He or she shall not be dismissed or penalised by the data controller or the data processor for performing his or her tasks.
crmp.plain: The Bank must not dismiss, punish, or penalize its DPO for carrying out their legally mandated duties. The DPO must be able to act freely and independently in ensuring The Bank’s compliance with the NDPA, without fear of retaliation.
crmp.riskDescription: Fear of penalty may prevent the DPO from performing duties effectively.
crmp.primaryControl: Employment contract protection clause

crmp.title: Position of the Data Protection Officer
crmp.description: (5) The DPO shall directly report to the management level of the controller or the processor.
crmp.plain: The Bank must ensure that its DPO reports directly to senior management. This reporting structure enables the DPO to escalate data protection risks and compliance issues without obstruction and ensures that management is actively informed about The Bank’s data protection obligations.
crmp.riskDescription: Poor reporting may delay risk escalation or weaken oversight.
crmp.primaryControl: Organizational reporting chart and SOP

crmp.title: Position of the Data Protection Officer
crmp.description: (6) Data subjects may contact the DPO with regard to all issues relating to the processing of their personal data and to the exercise of their rights under the NDP Act.
crmp.plain: The Bank must ensure that data subjects can easily contact the DPO regarding any issues related to how their personal data is processed or to exercise their rights under the NDPA (such as access, correction, or deletion of their data). The DPO must be accessible and responsive to these requests.
crmp.riskDescription: Inaccessible DPO may lead to complaints, data subject dissatisfaction or non-compliance.
crmp.primaryControl: Website DPO contact form; published email

crmp.title: Position of the Data Protection Officer
crmp.description: (7) The DPO shall be bound by secrecy or confidentiality concerning the performance of his or her tasks, in accordance with relevant legislation.
crmp.plain: The Bank must ensure that its DPO maintains confidentiality in the performance of their duties. The DPO is legally bound to keep sensitive information secret, in line with applicable laws and regulations, while carrying out responsibilities under the NDPA.
crmp.riskDescription: Breach of confidentiality may result in legal liability and loss of trust.
crmp.primaryControl: NDA clauses in contract; access control logs

crmp.title: Position of the Data Protection Officer
crmp.description: (8) The DPO may fulfil other tasks and duties. The data controller or data processor shall ensure that any such tasks and duties do not result in a conflict of interest.
crmp.plain: The Bank may assign the DPO additional roles or responsibilities. However, it must ensure that these extra tasks do not create a conflict of interest with the DPO’s core duty to oversee data protection compliance. The DPO’s independence and objectivity must be maintained at all times.
crmp.riskDescription: Conflict of interest may compromise DPO’s objectivity and compliance oversight.
crmp.primaryControl: Role separation and conflict of interest declaration

crmp.plain: The Bank must ensure that its DPO prepares a semi-annual data protection report and submits it to The Bank’s management. This internal report helps management stay informed about data protection risks, activities, and compliance status.
crmp.riskDescription: Lack of reporting may result in management being unaware of risks or breaches.
crmp.primaryControl: Internal reporting templates and compliance calendar

crmp.title: Principles of Personal Data Protection
crmp.description: (1) The entire principle of data protection are obligatory in any form of data processing.  The principles under section 24 of the NDP Act are:  a) Fairness, lawfulness and transparency of data processing,  b) Purpose limitation,  c) Data minimisation and ethics,  d) Storage limitation,  e) Data accuracy,  f) Data confidentiality, integrity and availability,  g) Accountability, and  h) Duty of care.
crmp.plain: The Bank must ensure that all personal data processing activities comply with the core principles set out in Section 24 of the NDPA, which include:  - Fairness, lawfulness, and transparency: Processing must be honest, legal, and clear to data subjects.  - Purpose limitation: Personal data should only be collected and used for specific, legitimate purposes.  - Data minimisation and ethics: Only collect data that is necessary, and process it ethically.  - Storage limitation: Keep data only as long as necessary.  - Data accuracy: Ensure personal data is accurate and up-to-date.  - Data confidentiality, integrity, and availability: Protect data from unauthorized access or loss and keep it accessible to authorized users.  - Accountability: The Bank must be able to demonstrate compliance with these principles.  - Duty of care: The Bank must take responsibility to protect data and avoid harm to data subjects.
crmp.riskDescription: Failure to comply with any of the eight core principles could result in regulatory sanctions, data breaches, reputational damage, and loss of trust.
crmp.primaryControl: Data Protection Policy, Data Retention Policy, RoPA, Employee Training, IT Security Controls, Privacy Notices

crmp.title: Lawful Bases of Data Processing
crmp.description: (1) In line with Section 25 of the NDP Act, it is important for a data controller to carefully  assess the lawful bases of data processing before embarking on same.  (2) Subject to the provisions of the NDP Act and any regulatory instruments issued by  the Commission, a data controller shall carefully consider and choose the appropriate lawful bases of data processing in order to process personal data. The lawful bases  are:  a) Consent  b) Contractual Obligation  d) Legal Obligation  e) Valid Interest  f) Public Interest  g) Legitimate Interest.  (3) As the party who determines the purpose of data processing, the data controller is ultimately responsible for determining the lawful bases of data processing
crmp.plain: Before processing personal data, The Bank must carefully assess and select the appropriate lawful basis for each data processing activity, as required under Section 25 of the NDPA. The lawful bases include: - Consent from the data subject, - Fulfillment of a contractual obligation, - Compliance with a legal obligation, - Acting in a valid interest, - Serving the public interest, - Or pursuing a legitimate interest.  Since The Bank decides why and how personal data is processed, it is ultimately responsible for ensuring the chosen lawful basis is valid and properly documented.
crmp.riskDescription: Processing personal data without a valid legal basis may lead to regulatory violations, invalid consent claims, data subject complaints, and sanctions.
crmp.primaryControl: Lawful Basis Register; Data Processing Inventory (RoPA); Standard Operating Procedures for data intake and processing
