cybersecurity.title: Metrics, Monitoring and Reporting
cybersecurity.description: SFIs are required to measure the effectiveness of their cybersecurity programme and provide assurance to relevant authorities by defining and implementing performance metrics. Defined metrics should be aligned with strategic objectives and provide the information needed for effective decision-making at the strategic, management and operational levels. i. To assess the effectiveness of the SFIs’ cybersecurity programme and measure its performance and efficiency, metrics that may be employed include key performance indicators, key risk indicators, key goal indicators etc. Defined metrics should be reviewed at least annually. ii. The metrics should help to identify deficiencies, failed security controls as well as highlight the progress made in resolving issues. iii. SFIs shall establish effective communication channels to disseminate relevant security requirements to employees for effective implementation of the cybersecurity programme. iv. The Board shall be provided with quarterly reports to inform them of the status of the Cybersecurity programme. The contents of the reports shall be as defined in Section 1.1(viii) of this framework. v. SFIs are required to report all cyber incidents (as defined in Appendix I) not later than 24 hours after such incident is detected to the Director of Banking Supervision, Central Bank of Nigeria using the report format in Appendix VII or any other format that may be advised from time to time. Where necessary and applicable, additional information should be provided afterwards.
cybersecurity.plain: The Bank shall: 1. Define and implement performance metrics (KPIs, KRIs, KGIs) to assess the effectiveness and efficiency of the cybersecurity programme. 2. Align metrics with strategic objectives and review them at least annually. 3. Use metrics to identify deficiencies, failed controls, and monitor resolution progress. 4. Establish communication channels to inform staff of cybersecurity requirements. 5. Provide quarterly cybersecurity status reports to the Board as outlined in Section 1.1(viii). 6. Report all cyber incidents to the Director of Banking Supervision (CBN) within 24 hours of detection using the format in Appendix VII (or updated format), and provide additional information when necessary.
cybersecurity.deadlineType: - Annual review of metrics - Quarterly board report - Cyber incident report: within 24 hours of detection
cybersecurity.riskDescription: -  Ineffective or absent performance metrics may lead to poor cybersecurity oversight. - Lack of communication may result in employee non-compliance. - Delays in incident reporting could attract regulatory sanctions and damage reputation. - Absence of board-level visibility into cybersecurity posture may lead to poor risk governance.

cybersecurity.additionalControl: - Implement automated cyber performance reporting tools. - Schedule quarterly cybersecurity training/awareness sessions. - Define SOPs for timely cyber incident escalation and CBN reporting.

cybersecurity.title: Compliance with Statutory and Regulatory Requirements
cybersecurity.description: i. The Board and Senior Management of SFIs shall ensure compliance with all relevant statutes and regulations to avoid breaches of legal, statutory and regulatory requirements on Cybersecurity. These include the Nigerian Cybercrimes Prohibition, Prevention Act, 2015, NDPA, 2023, National Cybersecurity Policy and Strategy, 2021 and all CBN directives. ii. An SFI is required to participate in industry cyber exercises and programmes to evaluate its level of preparedness to recover from cyber incidents. These exercises may include cyber drills, war games or as defined by the CBN from time to time. Such exercises may be conducted by the Nigeria Financial Nigeria Computer Emergency Response Team (NigFinCERT) or any other body as may be advised periodically.
cybersecurity.plain: The Bank shall: 1. Ensure the Board and Senior Management comply with all statutory, legal, and regulatory requirements on cybersecurity, including:   - Cybercrimes (Prohibition, Prevention) Act, 2015   - Nigeria Data Protection Act (NDPA), 2023   - National Cybersecurity Policy and Strategy, 2021   - CBN circulars and directives 2. Participate in industry cyber preparedness programmes and exercises (e.g. cyber drills, war games) as organized or directed by CBN, NigFinCERT, or any other recognized authority.

consumer_protection.source: Exposure Draft of the Revised Consumer Protection Regulations 2.0
consumer_protection.title: FAIR TREATMENT
consumer_protection.description: The bank shall comply with the following minimum standards at all stages of the relationship with consumers:  4.1.1 Treat consumers with courtesy and honesty.  4.1.2 Communicate in plain language, devoid of technical terms that would make it difficult for consumers to understand their rights and obligations.  4.1.3 Provide access to basic financial services without regard to demographic status such as gender, age, religion, literacy level, region and disability.  4.1.4 Provide support to consumers with special needs such as multilingual assistance, ramp, visual and hearing aids.  4.1.5 Promptly oblige consumers’ request for account closure or to switch providers, without unreasonable closing/switching barriers.  4.1.6 Execute variations to contracts, including interest rate, fees or charges, only if expressly provided for in the contract and notify customers at least five (5) working days in advance of execution.  4.1.7 Acknowledge enquiries from consumers within 24 hours.  4.1.8 Respond to customers’ enquiries within five (5) working days of receipt.  4.1.9 Not charge early liquidation fee on Consumer and Micro, Small and Medium Enterprise loans with variable interest rate.  4.1.10 Be accountable for improper functioning of their banking applications.  4.1.11 Deploy flexible banking applications to meet regulatory requirements for good consumer outcomes.  4.1.12 Disclose similar product offerings within the institution to enable consumers to make comparisons and informed choices.  4.1.13 Not engage in bundling or cross-selling practices that unduly limit consumer choices.  4.1.14 Be held accountable for employing any practice that could be considered unfair.
consumer_protection.plain: The Bank shall: 1. Treat customers with courtesy and honesty. 2. Use plain language and avoid technical jargon in all communication. 3. Ensure equal access to basic services regardless of gender, age, religion, disability, or literacy level. 4. Provide special support for consumers with special needs (e.g., ramps, hearing/visual aids, multilingual support). 5. Allow customers to close or switch accounts without unreasonable barriers. 6. Make contract variations (e.g., interest or fees) only if provided for, and notify customers at least 5 working days prior. 7. Acknowledge all customer enquiries within 24 hours. 8. Respond to all customer enquiries within 5 working days. 9. Do not charge early liquidation fees on MSME/consumer loans with variable interest rates. 10. Take responsibility for any failures or issues with the bank’s mobile or web applications. 11. Ensure bank apps are flexible and support regulatory consumer outcomes. 12. Disclose similar products for comparison and informed customer decisions. 13. Avoid forced product bundling or cross-selling that limits consumer choice. 14. Avoid all forms of unfair treatment and be accountable for misconduct.
consumer_protection.deadlineType: - Continuous (daily operational standard)- Specific timelines:    - 24-hour enquiry acknowledgment    - 5-day enquiry resolution    - 5-day advance notice before variation
consumer_protection.riskDescription: - Breach of these standards can lead to: ▪ Regulatory sanctions ▪ Erosion of customer trust ▪ Customer attrition and reputational damage ▪ Fines or license limitations ▪ Negative media and public backlash
consumer_protection.owner: - Chief Compliance Officer- Head of Customer Experience- Branch Managers- Head of Digital Channels- Legal and Contracting Team

consumer_protection.title: BUSINESS ETHICS
consumer_protection.description: To promote good business practices, FSPs shall comply with the following minimum standards:  4.2.1 Conduct business in a responsible, professional, and ethical manner.  4.2.2 Train staff to promote competence, efficiency, and professionalism in the discharge of their duties.  4.2.3 Provide clear information about product features, terms and conditions as well as the applicable charges.  4.2.4 Comply with the rates, fees, charges, or prices published or disclosed at the engagement points.  4.2.5 Obtain relevant and sufficient information about consumers, before providing advice or concluding a contract, to enable it to offer suitable products that meet the consumer’s needs and financial capacity.  4.2.6 Not impose product, service, or channel on consumers.  4.2.7 Not charge fees for issuance and renewal of products or services which have not been requested by the customer.  4.2.8 Not compel consumers to buy a product or service as a pre-condition for the purchase of another product or service unless where the products or services are directly dependent.  4.2.9 Apply non-credit related fees/charges only to the extent of the balance in the account and defer the outstanding fees/charges until the account is funded and the customer notified accordingly.  4.2.10 Communicate a decision (acceptance or decline) on applications for waivers, extensions, and other concessions to a customer within ten (10) working days, otherwise the application shall be deemed granted.  4.2.11 Be responsible for digitally generated advise, recommendations and evidence of transactions.  4.2.12 Notify customers within twelve (12) hours of service interruptions and at least 48 hours for anticipated disruptions and take measures to mitigate the impact.  4.2.13 Sale of products through digital channels should only proceed after customers have confirmed that they have read mandatory information.  4.2.14 Avoid offering incentives that promote misconduct.  4.2.15 Structure remuneration of employees and authorized agents to promote responsible business conduct.  4.2.16 Avoid conflict of interest in dealing with consumers. Where conflicts cannot be avoided, disclose and establish mechanisms to manage such conflict, or decline to provide the service.  4.2.17 Carry out impact assessment where an issue has been identified on an account with a view to addressing other accounts in similar circumstance. The resolution should be communicated to the affected customers.
consumer_protection.plain: The Bank shall: 1. Conduct business in a responsible, professional, and ethical manner. 2. Train staff to ensure competence and professionalism. 3. Disclose clear product features, terms, and fees. 4. Adhere strictly to published rates, fees, and charges. 5. Assess customer’s financial profile before offering financial advice or closing a sale. 6. Not force products, services, or delivery channels on customers. 7. Not charge issuance or renewal fees unless requested by the customer. 8. Avoid tying one product’s purchase to another, except when directly dependent. 9. Apply non-credit fees only against available balances and defer excess with notification. 10. Respond to customer applications for waivers or concessions within 10 working days or consider it granted. 11. Be fully accountable for digital advice, recommendations, and transaction records. 12. Notify customers within 12 hours of service interruptions and 48 hours in advance for scheduled outages. 13. Not sell products through digital channels unless the customer confirms reading mandatory information. 14. Avoid incentives that may encourage misconduct. 15. Ensure staff compensation supports ethical and responsible behavior. 16. Avoid conflicts of interest; where unavoidable, disclose and manage them or decline the service. 17. Assess impact across similar accounts and notify affected customers when systemic issues are discovered.
consumer_protection.deadlineType: - Continuous compliance.- Time-bound obligations:     - Customer application response: 10 working days     - Disruption notice: within 12 hours (unplanned) or 48 hours (planned)
consumer_protection.riskDescription: - Regulatory non-compliance due to unethical practices. - Loss of customer trust and public backlash. - Legal action from mis-selling or improper charges. - Potential fines, reputational damage, or loss of license. - Staff behavior leading to operational misconduct.
consumer_protection.owner: - Chief Compliance Officer- Head of Customer Experience- Product Managers- Sales/Relationship Management Heads- Internal Audit- Legal & Digital Operations Units
consumer_protection.responsibility: - Executive Management- Ethics and Compliance Team- Customer Protection Unit- HR & Training Department- Digital Channels Lead- Audit and Internal Control Team
consumer_protection.primaryControl: - Enforce Code of Business Conduct and Ethics. - Mandatory onboarding and annual ethical conduct training. - Automate disclosure of terms and fees in onboarding portals. - Review compensation models to remove misconduct-inducing incentives. - Integrate financial suitability assessments into product advisory tools. - Enforce system-based application tracking for waivers/extensions. - Deploy real-time notification systems for service disruptions. - Implement system-based checks to block tied product sales unless linked. - Embed conflict-of-interest disclosures in CRM processes.
consumer_protection.additionalControl: - Conduct routine audits of product sales scripts and application outcomes. - Independent ethics review board for high-risk cases. - Whistleblower platform with escalation process. - Set up digital product disclaimers with confirmation checks. - Require documented customer financial profiling in advisory processes.

consumer_protection.title: SALES PROMOTION AND ADVERTISEMENT
consumer_protection.description: FSPs shall be required to ensure that their advertising and promotional materials comply with the following minimum standards:  4.3.1 Disclose contact details and its regulatory authority.  4.3.2 Disclose cost of products, including all fees and other associated charges.  4.3.3 Disclose the nature and value of benefits, where an advertisement refers to, or is linked to other value adding benefits.  4.3.4 Avoid mentioning the names of or making comparisons with competitors.  4.3.5 Avoid making reference to unaudited financial statements.  4.3.6 The content of advertisements shall be factual, unambiguous, not offensive, misleading, deceptive, or likely to cause damage.  4.3.7 The overall impression of advertisements shall not emphasize benefits while de-emphasizing its associated risks.  4.3.8 Unsolicited advertisements shall be at no cost to consumers.  4.3.9 Honor obligations in sales promotions as advertised and offered.  4.3.10 Establish a process to periodically evaluate the competence and conduct of employees.  4.3.11 Provide consumers with the option to opt-out of receiving marketing materials.  4.3.12 Not make opt-in for promotional materials a prerequisite for on-boarding consumers to products.  4.3.13 Be accountable for downplaying or dismissing warnings or cautionary statements in written sales materials.  4.3.14 Disclose to consumers potential or actual conflict of interest, particularly when the customer receives advice before executing agreements.  4.3.15 Promotional materials shall not use terminologies such as “free”, “zero cost”, or similar words or phrases, where associated costs to the product or service exists.  4.3.16 Use the word “free”, “zero cost”, only to indicate that the specific component of the product would not attract charges.  4.3.17 Notify the Director, Consumer Protection Department of the CBN prior to the commencement of advertisement by submitting a description of the content of the advertisement.
consumer_protection.plain: The Bank shall: 1. Clearly state contact information and regulatory authority in all ads. 2. Disclose all product costs, including fees and charges. 3. State the nature and value of advertised benefits. 4. Not reference competitors’ names or compare with them. 5. Not use unaudited financial statements in advertisements. 6. Ensure advertisements are factual, clear, respectful, and not misleading. 7. Present risks clearly without downplaying them compared to benefits. 8. Not charge customers for unsolicited advertisements. 9. Fulfill all offers made during promotions. 10. Regularly evaluate staff competence and conduct in sales and marketing. 11. Allow customers to opt out of marketing communications. 12. Not require opt-in to marketing materials as a condition for account opening. 13. Not dismiss or understate cautionary notes in sales materials. 14. Disclose any conflicts of interest when offering financial advice. 15. Avoid misleading words like “free” or “zero cost” unless absolutely true. 16. Only use “free” or “zero cost” when a specific product component is truly free. 17. Notify CBN Consumer Protection Department with ad content before publishing

consumer_protection.riskDescription: - Regulatory penalties for misleading or non-compliant promotions - Legal liability for false claims or failure to deliver promised benefits - Consumer distrust and reputational damage - Loss of operating license for recurring violations

consumer_protection.additionalControl: - Deploy consumer feedback monitoring tools to flag misleading ads - Require signed attestations from responsible officers before each campaign - Maintain advertising archive for regulatory audit - Pre-submission review and approval workflow for CBN notification - Third-party agency compliance certification before publishing

consumer_protection.title: UNFAIR CONTRACT TERMS
consumer_protection.description: FSPs shall comply with the following minimum standards to ensure that terms and conditions in contracts are fair and reasonable:  4.4.1 Contracts with consumers shall not contain unfair terms. A contract term shall be considered unfair if it:  a. Eliminates or limits the liability of an FSP to loss caused to a consumer by misrepresentation, negligence or misleading information on its products or services.  b. Binds a consumer to an obligation while the corresponding obligation on the FSP is conditional.  c. Eliminates or limits FSP’s liability with respect to actions or commitments undertaken by their employees, agents, or intermediaries.  d. Allows unilateral change to a contract without stating the circumstances under which the change could be made.  e. Excludes or restricts any legal requirement on the part of an FSP to act with skill, care, diligence, or professionalism toward the consumer in connection with the provision of any product or service and/or any liability for failing to do so.  4.4.2 Unfair terms used in contracts are void and shall not be binding on consumers.  4.4.3 Where there is any doubt or ambiguity about the meaning of a term used in a contract, the interpretation most favorable to the consumer shall prevail.
consumer_protection.plain: The Bank must: 1. Ensure all consumer contracts do not contain unfair terms, such as:  a. Clauses that eliminate/limit liability for losses caused by misrepresentation, negligence, or misleading information.  b. Obligations imposed on the consumer while making the bank’s obligation conditional or unclear.  c. Clauses that limit the bank's liability for staff, agents, or intermediaries’ conduct.  d. Allowing unilateral contract changes without stating clear conditions.  e. Excluding the bank’s legal duty to act with skill, care, and diligence. 2. Recognize that unfair contract terms are void and unenforceable. 3. Ensure the interpretation most favorable to the consumer must apply if contract terms are ambiguous.
consumer_protection.deadlineType: - At the contract drafting stage. - On a continuous basis for contract reviews and customer feedback. - Upon CBN or NDIC regulation updates impacting contract content.
consumer_protection.riskDescription: - Use of unfair terms can result in:  - Regulatory sanctions  - Legal challenges or lawsuits  - Loss of customer trust and reputational damage  - Contracts being declared void and unenforceable
consumer_protection.owner: - Head, Legal & Compliance- Head of Products- Contract Management Unit- Risk Management Department
consumer_protection.responsibility: - Legal & Compliance Team- Risk & Internal Audit- Product Development Heads- Executive Management for Oversight
consumer_protection.primaryControl: - Standardized contract templates vetted by Legal and Compliance. - Checklist for unfair terms during contract drafting and review. - Consumer-facing documents written in plain, clear language. - Legal review of all amendments or unilateral changes to consumer contracts. - Establish approval workflow for all new or revised contract terms. - Regular updates of contract templates based on evolving regulatory standards.
consumer_protection.additionalControl: - Annual contract audit to identify and correct potentially unfair terms. - Consumer feedback loop to flag difficult or ambiguous terms. - Legal advisory notes issued to internal stakeholders outlining current regulatory expectations. - Pre-launch Legal/Compliance sign-off for all consumer product documents.

consumer_protection.source: Exposure Draft of the Revised Consumer Protection Regulations 2.0
consumer_protection.title: LENDING PRACTICES
consumer_protection.description: FSPs shall comply with the following requirements:  4.5.1 Apply lending fees only to the extent of the amount disbursed in respect of term loans, except for fees that are applicable to committed facility.  4.5.2 Obtain customers’ written authorization where repayment of facility is sought before due date.  4.5.3 Assess customers’ capability to repay facilities in a sustainable manner taking into consideration their financial circumstances.  4.5.4 Monitor loan performance and upon early detection of repayment difficulties, engage customers on repayment options.  4.5.5 Not compel consumers to buy products or services, such as insurance or valuation from a particular third-party provider as a pre-condition for the grant of a credit facility, but can provide the option to choose from at least three (3) providers or as may be prescribed by CBN from time to time.  4.5.6 Ensure that guarantors confirm in writing that they have read and understood their commitments, potential implications, and the maximum amount they are guaranteeing.  4.5.7 Provide update to Guarantors immediately a facility is in default to enable parties (lender, borrower and guarantor) engage on repayment options, until the facility returns to performing status and the likelihood of the guarantors being called upon to discharge their commitments in the loan agreement becomes minimal.  4.5.8 Issue a Discharge Letter at no cost to customers within 5 working days after loan liquidation, and where the loan is guaranteed, the guarantor be notified accordingly.  4.5.9 Notify customers where loan requests are declined with reason(s) within 10 working days from the date of receipt.
consumer_protection.plain: The Bank must: 1. Only apply lending fees on the actual disbursed amount for term loans (except committed facilities). 2. Get written authorization from customers before collecting loan repayments earlier than due date. 3. Assess customer affordability based on their financial situation before granting loans. 4. Monitor loans and engage borrowers early when signs of difficulty in repayment are detected. 5. Allow customers to choose from at least three third-party providers (e.g. insurance, valuation) where services are required as part of a loan process. 6. Ensure guarantors confirm in writing that they understand their obligations and the guaranteed amount. 7. Update guarantors immediately when a loan is in default and continue engagement until the loan performs again. 8. Issue a Discharge Letter at no cost within 5 working days of loan repayment; guarantors must also be notified. 9. Inform customers within 10 working days with reasons when their loan application is declined.
consumer_protection.deadlineType: Upon finalization of Regulation 2.0 or as directed by CBN
consumer_protection.riskDescription: Non-compliance could result in regulatory penalties, reputational damage, customer dissatisfaction, legal liability from aggrieved customers or guarantors, and increased default rates due to poor lending decisions.
consumer_protection.owner: - Head of Retail/Consumer Lending- Legal & Compliance Unit- Credit Risk Department- Loan Operations Team- Relationship Managers
consumer_protection.responsibility: Chief Risk Officer, Head of Credit Operations, Chief Compliance Officer, Head of Legal, Product Managers
consumer_protection.primaryControl: - Lending policy approved by Board - Affordability checks in loan origination system - Automated loan tracking tools - Loan decline templates- Standard operating procedure for loan closure
consumer_protection.additionalControl: - Update lending SOPs and digital workflows to reflect all 4.5 obligations. - Include guarantor acknowledgment templates and early default alert protocols.  - Automate loan decline notices and discharge letter issuance in core banking system. - Train relationship managers and credit officers on fair lending expectations and 3rd-party provider flexibility. - Monitor compliance quarterly through internal audit or compliance reviews.

consumer_protection.source: Exposure Draft of the Revised Consumer Protection Regulations 2.0
consumer_protection.title: DEBT RECOVERY
consumer_protection.description: To ensure that debt recovery processes are transparent, courteous, and fair, regulated entities shall:  4.6.1 Engage and give customers notice(s) of outstanding obligations prior to the commencement of a debt collection.  4.6.2 Initiate foreclosures only when other recovery options have been unsuccessful.  4.6.3 Give customers the option of a private sale, to be exercised within 30 days before commencing foreclosure, except where the customer waives the right.  4.6.4 Ensure that the net proceeds from foreclosures are immediately applied to the loan account and customers informed of the balance.  4.6.5 Provide customers with a report of the sale of the collateral. At a minimum, the report shall state the process, proceeds, incidental expenses, and net proceeds.  4.6.6 Be liable for the actions of their agents engaged for debt collection.  4.6.7 Not contact friends, employer, relatives, or neighbors of a customer for any information other than information on employment status, telephone numbers or address, except where the person has guaranteed the loan or has consented to be contacted.
consumer_protection.plain: The Bank as a regulated entity must: 1. Notify customers of unpaid debts before starting debt recovery actions. 2. Only initiate foreclosure if all other recovery methods have failed. 3. Offer customers a 30-day window to sell the collateral privately before foreclosure, unless they waive the right. 4. Immediately apply any foreclosure sale proceeds to the loan and inform the customer of the remaining balance. 5. Provide a detailed report to the customer after the sale of collateral, including process, proceeds, expenses, and net amount. 6. Be responsible for the conduct and actions of third-party agents or debt collectors. 7. Do not contact a borrower's relatives, neighbors, friends, or employer except to confirm address, phone, or employment – unless they are guarantors or have consented.
consumer_protection.deadlineType: Upon adoption of Regulation 2.0 or as directed by CBN
consumer_protection.riskDescription: Improper or aggressive debt recovery practices can lead to regulatory sanctions, lawsuits, reputational harm, customer complaints, and loss of business license.
consumer_protection.owner: - Credit Recovery & Collections Unit- Legal Department- Compliance Department- Customer Experience Unit- Third-party Collection Agents
consumer_protection.responsibility: Chief Compliance Officer, Head of Recovery, Chief Risk Officer, Head of Legal, Collections Manager
consumer_protection.primaryControl: - Standard notice templates for overdue accounts- Escalation procedures for foreclosure approval- Agent Code of Conduct- Collateral sales reporting template- Call logs and CRM audit trails
consumer_protection.additionalControl: - Embed foreclosure timing and private sale option into recovery workflow.- Train collection teams and vendors on fair recovery practices.- Automate issuance of debt notices and post-sale reports.- Add clauses in debt collection contracts holding agents accountable for misconduct.- Conduct periodic audit and mystery shopper checks on recovery practices.

consumer_protection.title: FORMAT AND MANNER OF DISCLOSURE
consumer_protection.description: 5.1.1 Documents provided to consumers shall:  a. Be written in clear, simple English language and legible with a minimum font size of 10 and spacing of 1.0.  b. Not be misleading or deceptive.  c. Be provided in a durable form for ease of future reference.  d. State the name and contact details of the FSP.  e. State the type of license of the FSP and provide the name as well as contact details of the regulatory authority.  5.1.2 Clearly explain technical terms to consumers to aid understanding and decision.  5.1.3 Disclose the agreed communication channel(s) to be used for all correspondences and adopt same for information dissemination.  5.1.4 Display at customer engagement points, accurate information on all products and services, including:  a. Prime and maximum lending rates.  b. Deposit rates.  c. Applicable exchange rates for transactions that require currency conversion.  d. How to lodge a complaint to the FSP and escalation option to the CBN where necessary.  5.1.5 Ensure that their websites and other information dissemination channels are functional and regularly updated with the current features of products and services offered.
consumer_protection.plain: The Bank shall: 1. Provide documents to consumers that:  a. Are written in clear, simple English, minimum font size 10, and spacing 1.0.  b. Are not misleading or deceptive.  c. Are given in a durable format for future reference.  d. Clearly state the name and contact details of the bank.  e. Include the license type of the bank and contact details of its regulator. 2. Explain all technical terms clearly to ensure consumer understanding. 3. Disclose and use the agreed communication channel for all customer correspondence. 4. Display at all customer engagement points:  a. Lending rates (prime and max)  b. Deposit rates  c. Exchange rates where applicable  d. Complaint procedure and CBN escalation steps. 5. Ensure websites and all info channels are functional and regularly updated.

consumer_protection.source: Exposure Draft of the Revised Consumer Protection Regulations 2.0
consumer_protection.title: DISCLOSURE OF TERMS AND CONDITIONS
consumer_protection.description: FSPs shall comply with the following minimum standards during the lifecycle of contractual relationship with consumers:  5.2.1 Disclose in writing, all terms and conditions of a product or service on offer, as well as the features, risks, benefits, fees, and other associated charges.  5.2.2 Provide oral explanation on contractual agreements:  a. At customer’s request; or  b. If it is obvious that the customer is vulnerable or cannot understand the agreement.  5.2.3 The phrase “Terms and Conditions Apply” or any other phrase conveying a similar meaning shall not be used, except where such terms have been disclosed in the contract. Where terms and conditions are disclosed in other medium accessible to consumers, the consumers attention shall be drawn.  5.2.4 Make opt-out option available for customers to unsubscribe from digital services at the time of establishing the contractual relationship.  5.2.5 Provide information on cancellation or switching procedures, including when products and services are delivered through agents or digital channels.  5.2.6 Disclose in contracts, the possibility of variations in interest or foreign exchange rates due to changes in market conditions.  5.2.7 Allow consumers a minimum of two (2) working days from date of receipt, to review draft contract before execution except where they waive this in writing.  5.2.8 Give consumers a cooling-off period of three (3) working days after the execution of a credit contract, within which they may cancel without having to pay any penalty or charges. However, the consumer may waive the option with written notification.  5.2.9 Embed a pre-read or pause function before any purchase decision or transaction via digital channels, to enable brief time to review transaction and key terms and conditions before authorization or consent.  5.2.10 Provide information on product usage and how to obtain support services when the need arises.  5.2.11 Credit contracts shall contain the following:  a. Name and contact details of customer.  b. Type, purpose of credit, tenor of the contract, amount or credit limit, and moratorium (where applicable).  c. Applicable interest rate, details of lending fees including late payment/default (where applicable), variable rate information (where applicable) and total cost of the credit.  d. Key features and risks, conditions precedent to drawdown, insurance requirements (where applicable), early liquidation terms.  e. Applicable Annual Percentage Rate (APR) to be calculated using the formula stated in Annexures B and C.  f. Repayment schedule for term loans, collateral pledged and its estimated value.  5.2.12 Provide consumers, a Key Facts Statement (KFS) in the format attached as Annexure A stating a summary of key information on consumer loans.  5.2.13 State the rights and responsibilities of consumers, including the conditions that may lead to termination or cancellation of contract.  5.2.14 State how disputes can be resolved and the contact information of the established internal complaints handling units as well as the details of the external complaints’ resolution unit.  5.2.15 Implement disclosures that are commensurate to targeted consumer segments.
consumer_protection.plain: The Bank must: 1. Disclose in writing all terms, conditions, features, risks, benefits, fees, and charges of a product/service. 2. Provide oral explanation of contracts if requested or if the customer is vulnerable or lacks understanding. 3. Use “Terms and Conditions Apply” only if the terms are fully disclosed and accessible; draw consumer’s attention to external media if used. 4. Provide an opt-out option from digital services at the start of contract. 5. Disclose cancellation/switching procedures (including for agents and digital channels). 6. Disclose in contracts the possibility of rate variations due to market changes. 7. Allow 2 working days review period before contract execution (unless waived). 8. Allow 3 working days cooling-off period after executing a credit contract (unless waived). 9. Implement a pre-read or pause function before digital purchases or approvals. 10. Provide product usage info and support contact details. 11. Credit contracts must contain:  a. Customer name/contact  b. Credit type, amount, tenor, purpose, moratorium  c. Interest rate, all charges, late/default terms  d. Key risks, drawdown conditions, insurance if applicable  e. APR and how it's calculated (Annex B & C)  f. Repayment schedule, collateral, estimated value 12. Provide a Key Facts Statement (KFS) (Annex A). 13. State consumer rights/responsibilities including termination terms. 14. Provide complaints resolution process (internal & external contacts). 15. Tailor disclosures to targeted consumer segments.
consumer_protection.deadlineType: - At product onboarding and prior to execution of any contract. - Ongoing updates whenever product features or fees change. - Ensure KFS and oral/written explanations are available during every new contract cycle.
consumer_protection.riskDescription: - Non-disclosure or inadequate disclosure can lead to:  - Consumer complaints or lawsuits  - Contract disputes  - Regulatory sanctions for unfair consumer treatment  - Loss of consumer trust and reputational damage
consumer_protection.owner: - Legal & Compliance Department - Product Managers - Risk Management - IT/Digital Channels Unit - Customer Service & Relationship Officers
consumer_protection.responsibility: - Head, Legal & Compliance - Product Development Manager - Customer Experience Lead - Digital Channels/UX Manager - Internal Audit
consumer_protection.primaryControl: - Use standard contract templates vetted by legal/compliance. - Implement digital contract platforms with embedded pause/pre-read functions. - Pre-launch legal and consumer protection review of all new products. - Training of front-line staff on disclosure obligations. - System-enforced delay (2-day review period) and cooling-off period for credit contracts. - Built-in APR calculator tool and KFS generator. - Standard cancellation/opt-out procedures on all platforms.
consumer_protection.additionalControl: - Internal audit review of executed contracts against disclosure checklist. - Consumer testing of contract language readability. - Embedded alerts and disclaimers for digital credit products. - Real-time chat or call-back options during onboarding for clarification.

consumer_protection.title: NOTIFICATION OF CHANGES IN RATES, TERMS AND CONDITIONS
consumer_protection.description: FSPs shall comply with the following minimum standards to promote transparency in dealing with customers:  5.3.1 Not vary terms and conditions, without the consent of customers. However, this does not apply to interest rate variations.  5.3.2 Notify customers of possible variations in interest rates and other terms and conditions, through the agreed channel of communication. In the case of interest rates, the notice shall state:  a. Reason for the variation.  b. Commencement date.  c. Revised repayment schedule (where necessary).  d. Alternatives available such as concession, restructuring, re- negotiation, opt-out or termination of the contract.  5.3.3 Notify consumers in default of credit repayment within 3 working days from the day of default, that a default charge would be applied after 7 working days in the case of Deposit Money Banks (DMBs), and 3 working days for Other Financial Institutions (OFIs).
consumer_protection.plain: The Bank shall:  1. Not vary the terms and conditions of contracts without the customer’s consent, except for interest rate changes. 2. Provide advance notice of possible variations in interest rates or terms using the agreed communication channel. 3. In case of interest rate changes, notify customers with details of:  a. The reason for the change  b. The start date of the new rate  c. The updated repayment schedule, if applicable  d. Available alternatives such as concessions, restructuring, renegotiation, opting out, or terminating the contract 4. If a customer defaults on repayment, the bank shall:  a. Notify the customer of the default within 3 working days  b. Inform them that a default charge will apply after:   - 7 working days for Deposit Money Banks (DMBs)   - 3 working days for Other Financial Institutions (OFIs)
consumer_protection.deadlineType: - Before any change in interest or terms and conditions- Within 3 working days of default (initial notice)- 7 working days after default before applying penalty (DMBs)- 3 working days after default before applying penalty (OFIs)
consumer_protection.riskDescription: - Lack of timely and proper communication regarding changes can result in:  - Regulatory non-compliance  - Customer disputes and dissatisfaction  - Financial penalties and reputational damage

consumer_protection.additionalControl: - Implement dashboard monitoring to track all rate change notices sent - Train staff on timelines and consequences of non-compliance - Periodic system audit of communication logs

consumer_protection.title: ACCOUNT STATEMENT
consumer_protection.description: FSPs shall comply with the following minimum standards to promote disclosure of financial transactions:  5.4.1 Provide monthly statements (confirmation/investment advice as the case may be) for all products and account types, at no cost.  5.4.2 Make account balances and statements available on customers’ request.  5.4.3 Notify consumers of transactions on their account immediately it occurs. At a minimum, the notification shall include date, currency, amount, payer, transaction reference, channel, and the cleared account balance.  5.4.4 Notify consumers when their accounts have become inactive or dormant, and the related consequences.  5.4.5 Ensure clarity in descriptions on account statements. At a minimum, it shall include, transaction reference, payer transaction channel, location, and account balance.  5.4.6 Disclose default charges in account statements separate from the interest charge.  5.4.7 Provide consumers with a closing statement when a contract is terminated or concluded.
consumer_protection.plain: The Bank shall: 1. Send monthly account statements or investment advice for all account types free of charge. 2. Make account balances and statements available upon customer request. 3. Immediately notify customers of every account transaction with key details: date, currency, amount, payer, transaction reference, channel, and cleared balance. 4. Alert customers when accounts become inactive or dormant, stating the implications. 5. Ensure clear descriptions in statements with transaction details including reference, channel, location, and balance. 6. Clearly separate default charges from interest in statements. 7. Issue a closing statement when a product or contract ends.
consumer_protection.deadlineType: Immediately or within 90 days of final regulation issuance
consumer_protection.riskDescription: Failure to comply with these provisions can result in poor transparency, regulatory penalties, loss of customer trust, disputes, or miscommunication over charges and balances.

consumer_protection.additionalControl: - Periodic review of statement formats for clarity - Internal audits of transaction alert accuracy - Dormancy alert trigger review and escalation process - Ensure final statement generation is part of account closure process - System flags for correct tagging of default charges vs. interest

consumer_protection.source: Exposure Draft of the Revised Consumer Protection Regulations 2.0
consumer_protection.title: PROTECTION OF CONSUMER ASSETS AND PRIVACY
consumer_protection.description: To ensure adequate protection of consumer assets and privacy, FSPs shall comply with the following minimum standards:  6.1 DATA PROTECTION 6.1.1 Protect the privacy and confidentiality of consumer information and assets against unauthorized access and be accountable for acts or omissions in respect thereof.  6.1.2 Embed personal data protection in the design of products or systems.  6.1.3 Obtain written consent of consumers to collect and process their personal data for specific purposes and provide them with the option to withdraw the consent at any time.  6.1.4 Not share personal data of consumers to a third party without their express consent and provide details of information to be shared.  6.1.5 Design clear and simple “Opt-in” and “Opt-Out” options for data sharing with 3rd parties.  6.1.6 Review data processing and privacy procedures to ensure that consumers’ data are accurate and used only for the purposes for which it was initially obtained.  6.2 FRAUD PREVENTION 6.2.1 Protect customers’ assets against fraud or misuse at all times and be liable for losses arising from breach of required controls.  6.2.2 Test product suitability with consumers and make necessary modifications to reduce the incidence of fraud or transaction errors.  6.2.3 Implement the following measures across transaction channels:  a. Multi-variant customer identification and multifactor authentication mechanisms for transactions consummated.  b. Automated transaction monitoring, alert functions and behavioral monitoring to detect and prevent fraud.  6.2.4 Sensitize customers on fraud threats or scams.  6.2.5 State and periodically communicate procedures for reporting suspicious, unauthorized, fraud, lost or stolen payment instruments and/or authentication information to consumers.  6.2.6 Provide secure and simple user interfaces for digital financial services that will minimize the risk of mistake or double transactions.
consumer_protection.plain: The Bank shall ensure the protection of consumer data and assets by doing the following:  Data Protection 1. Safeguard consumer personal information and financial data from unauthorized access. 2. Build data protection into the design of systems and financial products. 3. Get written permission from consumers before collecting/using their data and allow them to withdraw that consent at any time. 4. Only share consumer data with third parties when the consumer agrees in writing and is informed of what data will be shared. 5. Design easy-to-use opt-in/opt-out features for data sharing.6. Regularly review data practices to ensure data is correct and used only for its original purpose.  Fraud Prevention 1. Keep customers’ money safe from fraud and take responsibility if systems fail. 2. Test products with consumers to fix issues that might lead to fraud. 3. Deploy the following controls:   - Strong customer ID and multifactor authentication   - Automated systems to monitor and flag suspicious transactions 4. Educate customers about fraud risks and scams. 5. Provide clear instructions for reporting fraud, stolen cards, or unauthorized activity. 6. Design secure and user-friendly digital platforms to reduce errors or duplicate transactions.
consumer_protection.riskDescription: - Breaches of personal data and privacy due to poor access control or data sharing without consent. - Financial loss due to fraud, phishing, identity theft, or inadequate digital platform design. - Regulatory sanctions and reputational damage due to non-compliance with data and fraud requirements.

consumer_protection.title: FINANCIAL LITERACY AND AWARENESS
consumer_protection.description: To enhance financial literacy and awareness, FSPs shall comply with the following minimum standards:  7.1 Design and implement consumer education programs for various segments, to:  a. Build skills, knowledge, understanding and confidence in the use of financial products and services.  b. Safeguard account and confidential information.  7.2 Disseminate consumer education and awareness programs through diverse channels that are appropriate for various consumer segments.  7.3 Disseminate fraud prevention tips in English or local languages (where applicable) to all customer segments through appropriate channels.  7.4 Provide information that will enable consumers differentiate digital financial services from conventional banking products.  7.5 Render quarterly returns on financial literacy programs conducted.  7.6 Provide user education at product sign-up stage.  7.7 Ensure access to information on all product offerings to enable consumers make informed decisions.  7.8 Contribute resources towards industry-wide implementation of financial literacy and capability programs.
consumer_protection.plain: The Bank shall: 1. Create and implement education programs tailored to different consumer segments to build knowledge, skills, and confidence in using financial products. 2. Educate consumers on protecting their account and confidential information. 3. Disseminate financial literacy programs through various suitable channels for different consumer segments. 4. Share fraud prevention tips in English and relevant local languages via appropriate channels. 5. Explain differences between digital and traditional financial services to consumers. 6. Report quarterly on all financial literacy initiatives conducted. 7. Provide product education at the point of signing up new consumers. 8. Ensure product information is easily accessible to support informed decision-making. 9. Support industry-wide financial literacy programs by contributing resources.

consumer_protection.additionalControl: - Partner with schools, community leaders, and fintech platforms for grassroots education - Launch online/mobile financial literacy portals and chatbots - Conduct periodic consumer surveys to assess awareness levels and adjust strategy accordingly

consumer_protection.title: INTERNAL COMPLAINT RESOLUTION
consumer_protection.description: Complaints shall first be lodged with the FSP for timely resolution. For effective resolution of complaints, FSPs shall:  8.1.1 Provide access to efficient and free complaint resolution mechanisms.  8.1.2 Develop policies and processes on complaints handling that will guarantee fairness, transparency, responsiveness, and independence of the complaint handling mechanism.  8.1.3 Allocate adequate resources and structure for complaints handling under the oversight of an Executive Compliance Officer or its equivalent in Other Financial Institutions.  8.1.4 Designate a function for complaints handling independent of other business functions taking into consideration, the nature and complexity of their business.  8.1.5 Provide information on how to lodge a complaint, including the type of information to be provided by the complainant.  8.1.6 Disclose contact details, channels for lodging complaints, timelines for resolution and options for escalation at all customer engagement points. Where it is not practicable to comply with this, refer customers to where the information required could be obtained.  8.1.7 Make available a range of channels (such as walk-in, telephone, email, call center, portals, website, and social media) for submitting complaints appropriate to the type of consumers served.  8.1.8 Upon receipt of a complaint (inclusive of oral submission), communicate to the consumer immediately an acknowledgment containing:  a. A unique identification or tracking number,  b. Contact details of the complaints desk,  c. Expected resolution timeline,  d. Escalation options; and  e. An assurance that the complaint is being addressed.  8.1.9 Ensure that staff responsible for handling complaints declare any conflict of interest that may affect their objectivity.  8.1.10 Integrate all complaints collection channels to the enterprise complaints management platform.  8.1.11 Provide toll-free telephone lines for customers to make enquiries and lodge complaints.  8.1.12 Continuously engage customers until complaints are fully resolved.  8.1.13 Use the unique identification or tracking number in all correspondence with the complainant.  8.1.14 Keep records of all complaints, including transcripts of verbal complaint for a minimum of 6 years.  8.1.15 Provide emergency channels for reporting time-sensitive issues especially fraud-related complaints at all times.  8.1.16 Reconstruct customers’ accounts to establish underpayment or excess charges, where applicable.  8.1.17 Refund identified excess charges, non-payment, under-payment of interest on deposits or unauthorized debits to the customer’s account along with interest as provided in the extant Monetary, Credit, Foreign Trade and Exchange Policy Guidelines or any regulation issued by the CBN.  8.1.18 Resolve complaints received within the time specified in the Timelines for Complaints Resolution by Institutions.  8.1.19 Provide a Summary Resolution Communication (SRC) for resolved complaints to the complainant within 24 hours after resolution. The summary shall convey at a minimum:  a. The basis of the decision(s).  b. The right of appeal available to the complainant for a second level review by the entity.  c. The right of escalation to the CBN, or other Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) where the complainant is dissatisfied.  8.1.20 Where a complainant is dissatisfied with a decision of an FSP, the complainant shall, within 30 days from the date of the receipt of the SRC, request in writing for a second level review.  8.1.21 A complaint shall be considered resolved where the complainant has indicated acceptance of the resolution in writing within 30 days after the receipt of the SRC, otherwise the complaint shall be deemed resolved or closed in the records of the FSP.  8.1.22 Upon receipt of a request for a second level review, the FSP shall review and communicate decision(s) within the timelines for complaints resolution for second level review.  8.1.23 Submit a Root Cause Analysis Report (RCAR) on quarterly basis to capture recurring complaint types, category and code, number of occurrences, root cause(s), planned remedial actions and implementation timelines. The report should be submitted to the Director, Consumer Protection Department, CBN on or before the 5th day of January, April, July, and October respectively.  8.1.24 Report complaints statistics in annual reports and the abridged Financial Statement in line with the approved format provided in Annexure D or any other format as may be prescribed by the CBN from time to time.
consumer_protection.plain: The Bank shall have fair and easy ways for customers to complain when things go wrong. These complaints should be handled by a well-trained, independent team with enough resources. Customers must be told how to complain, where to do it, and how long it will take. Institutions must allow complaints through many channels like walk-ins, phone, email, and social media.  Once a complaint is received, it should be acknowledged immediately with a tracking number and contact information. The bank must stay in touch with the customer until the complaint is resolved. Staff handling complaints should be honest and declare any conflicts of interest.  All complaints (even verbal ones) should be recorded and kept for six years. Customers must be refunded with interest if they were overcharged. Emergency channels must be available for fraud-related complaints. A summary of the resolution must be given within 24 hours, and customers must be informed of their rights to appeal or escalate.  The bank must also send quarterly reports to the CBN about complaint trends and how they’re being addressed, and include complaint statistics in their annual reports.
consumer_protection.riskDescription: - Regulatory penalties for delayed, unfair, or untracked complaint handling. - Poor customer trust and reputational damage from unresolved or mishandled complaints. - Risk of litigation due to non-compliance with redress timelines and transparency obligations. - System inefficiencies if complaints are not tracked, resolved, or addressed at root cause level.

consumer_protection.primaryControl: - Complaints Management Policy - Consumer redress workflow with timelines - Dedicated complaints team with oversight - Toll-free numbers and online channels - Customer communication scripts and FAQs - Tracking systems for SRC and RCAR submission
consumer_protection.additionalControl: - Automate tracking and resolution alerts for complaint handlers - Integrate fraud complaints reporting with security incident management - Train staff on conflict of interest declaration - Establish clear SLA for second-level reviews - Audit complaints database quarterly for closure and escalation accuracy - Ensure quarterly RCAR submissions are signed off by senior management before CBN submission

consumer_protection.title: Responsible Business Conduct
consumer_protection.description: Financial Institutions shall observe high ethical standards and professionalism in their business transactions with consumers. They are required to assess the financial capabilities of consumers and offer only suitable products/services based on their needs and capability. In addition, they shall provide channels for consumers to make enquiries and complaints. The following specific areas will be addressed under Responsible Business Conduct:  Communication: All requests for information must be responded to timely and with clarity.  Provision of financial advice: FIs shall provide consumers with objective advice to enable them make informed decisions.  Responsible lending: FIs shall carry out proper credit worthiness assessment on consumers before granting credit to avoid reckless lending.  Debt collection: financial institutions shall adopt debt recovery processes that are courteous and fair to consumers. Consumers must be proactively engaged and given early notice of outstanding obligations prior to the commencement of debt collection efforts.  Sales promotion: marketing of products and services using incentives should be carried out in an ethical and professional manner.
consumer_protection.plain: The Bank shall:  1. Observe high ethical standards and professionalism in all business transactions with consumers. 2. Assess consumers’ financial capabilities and offer only products or services that are suitable to their needs and financial situation. 3. Provide channels for consumers to make enquiries and complaints. 4. Respond to all requests for information from consumers in a timely and clear manner. 5. Provide consumers with objective financial advice to support informed decision-making. 6. Carry out proper creditworthiness assessments before granting credit, to avoid reckless lending. 7. Ensure that debt recovery processes are fair and courteous, giving consumers early notice and proactive engagement before starting debt collection actions. 8. Conduct sales promotions and marketing using incentives in an ethical and professional manner.

consumer_protection.title: Communication
consumer_protection.description: 1. All requests for information shall be responded to clearly, timeously and in writing or via the customers means of communication with appropriate documentation. For this purpose, mere acknowledgement of a request would not suffice as a response.  2. In any communication with customers, FIs shall act in the best interest of customers. Remuneration and incentives structure in the industry shall encourage ethics and integrity.  3. Customer shall be notified when an activity threatens to violate the terms of contract.
consumer_protection.plain: The Bank shall: 1. Respond to customer information requests clearly, promptly, and in writing or via their preferred channel, with appropriate supporting documents. Acknowledgment alone is not sufficient. 2. Communicate with customers in their best interest, guided by ethics and integrity. 3. Notify customers if an action may breach contract terms.

consumer_protection.title: Provision of Financial Advice
consumer_protection.description: 1. Financial Institutions shall act in the best interest of consumers in the provision of advice and execution of transactions. For consumers to make informed decisions in choosing financial products and services, they must be acquainted with the features, costs, risks, penalties, terms and conditions. Thus, before consumers sign up for any financial products, FIs shall: a) Give clear information on the features of the services and products; b) Assess whether the products or services of interest suit the consumers’ needs. Where a product requested does not meet the needs of the customer, the FI is obliged to advise or caution the customer in writing before granting such; and c) Assess the consumers’ ability to fulfill the terms and conditions associated with the financial products and services;  2. Financial institutions shall provide appropriate financial advice to consumers before the sale of any financial product or service. For financial products or services that are complex or potentially risky to consumers, financial institutions shall document pre-contractual and subsequent deliberations with consumers. The records shall reflect the financial institutions’ efforts in taking the aforementioned steps (Section 2.2.2.(1)) before reaching an agreement with the consumer on the product or service. In addition, records of meetings must be acknowledged by the consumer.  3. The CBN shall use appropriate mechanisms (such as examining FIs’ records of pre-contractual deliberations with customers (see Section 2.2.2.(2)), mystery shopping amongst others) to monitor financial institutions and ensure that they properly engage customers prior to the sale of financial products or services.
consumer_protection.plain: The Bank shall: 1. Provide financial advice that is in the best interest of consumers. 2. Before offering financial products/services, FIs must:     a) Disclose clear product/service features, costs, risks, and terms.     b) Assess if the product fits the consumer’s needs; if not, caution the consumer in writing.     c) Evaluate the consumer’s ability to meet product terms. 3. consumer_protection.title: Responsible Lending
consumer_protection.description: 1. To promote positive credit culture in the industry, FIs shall establish structures to prohibit reckless and predatory lending.  2. Financial institutions shall provide credit counselling to prevent consumers’ indebtedness due to limited financial knowledge. Credit counselling is the process of educating consumers on borrowing and debt settlement.  3. Credit counselling facilities shall be available and accessible to all consumers. Consumers shall be made aware of such services and shall be encouraged to take advantage of such facilities provided by the financial institutions.  4. FIs shall provide detailed information on the terms and conditions of a credit agreement to consumers prior to executing the loan agreement. Such information must at a minimum include the pricing, repayment schedule, repayment amount, tenure and opt out options.

Offer credit counselling services to consumers to improve financial knowledge and prevent over-indebtedness. 3. Ensure that credit counselling is accessible to all consumers and actively inform and encourage them to use the service. 4. Disclose detailed credit terms to consumers before they sign any credit agreement. Disclosure must include:     - Pricing     - Repayment schedule and amount     - Tenure     - Opt-out options

consumer_protection.title: Debt Collection
consumer_protection.description: 1. The CBN shall set guidelines for ethical debt collection practices in the industry. These guidelines shall be based on dialogue, respect for the consumers’ privacy and longevity of consumer-FI relationships amongst others.  2. Where consumers are unable to meet their financial obligations, financial institutions shall be encouraged to adopt fair and ethical debt recovery practices.  3. FIs shall ensure that personnel assigned to recover debts are properly trained. Consumers shall be informed in advance before a recovery process is initiated.

Adopt fair and ethical recovery practices when consumers default on obligations. 3. Ensure debt recovery staff are properly trained. 4. Inform consumers ahead of any debt recovery action.

consumer_protection.title: Sales Promotion
consumer_protection.description: 1. Sales promotions or related activities shall be conducted professionally and ethically. In a bid to generate increased business volumes or attract new customers, financial institutions shall provide factual information and shall not mislead consumers.  2. Financial institutions shall be required to fulfil the terms of promotional offers. consumer_protection.title: Disclosure and Transparency
consumer_protection.description: Financial institutions shall provide accurate information on financial products and services to consumers at all times to enable them make informed decisions. Such information must be timely, detailed and clear. The primary coverage areas to be addressed are:  Contract terms: contract terms should contain adequate information that will enhance consumers’ decision making process prior to execution of the contract. Financial institutions shall also inform consumers of the possibility of variations in terms and conditions of contracts due to changes in economic conditions before such contracts are executed. Customers shall be provided with the statement of financial position at all times.  Notice of Variations: FIs shall give prior notice to consumers within the time specified in contracts, before implementing variations in terms and conditions of contracts.  Advertisement: Advertisements and marketing materials must convey complete and accurate information on the products and services being advertised.
consumer_protection.plain: The Bank shall:  1. Provide accurate, timely, detailed, and clear information on financial products and services to enable consumers make informed decisions. 2. Ensure that all contract terms include sufficient information to help consumers evaluate and understand the agreement before signing. 3. Inform consumers, before contract execution, about the potential for changes in contract terms due to economic conditions. 4. Make consumers’ statements of financial position available at all times. 5. Issue prior notice to consumers — within the period specified in the contract — before applying any changes to contract terms and conditions. 6. Ensure that all advertisements and marketing materials contain complete and accurate information about the products and services offered.

consumer_protection.title: Contract Terms
consumer_protection.description: 1. Financial Institutions shall disclose and document all terms and conditions including inherent risks, fees, charges and other payments to be made by a consumer for a product or service.  2. The CBN shall issue guidelines on disclosure requirements for products and services in contract agreements between financial institutions and consumers of financial products and services. These guidelines at a minimum shall cover areas such as: a) fees and charges; b) penalties (prepayment costs and default charges); c) interests (payable or receivable); d) payment and termination modalities; and e) risks.  3. Financial Institutions shall proactively inform consumers of the possibility of variations in terms and conditions of contracts.  4. Contractual agreements shall be precise and clear. Information must be communicated in simple language to avoid misinterpretation. Contractual agreements must be in legible font size. Where technical terms are used, the financial institution shall ensure that such technical terms are clearly explained to the understanding of the consumer to avoid confusion or miscommunication.  5. Financial Institutions shall conspicuously display specific and up-to-date information (such as certificate of incorporation, banking license, interest rates, foreign exchange rates, helpdesk contact details etc.) at customer engagement areas.  6. Financial institutions shall provide financial calculation tools on their websites to assist consumers to perform simple calculations that may be required to ascertain the suitability of certain financial products. In addition, financial institutions have a responsibility to make reasonable effort towards ensuring that consumers of financial products are knowledgeable about the products/service they wish to purchase.  7. The CBN shall publish rates offered by financial institutions to enable consumers make informed decisions in the selection of suitable products and services.  8. While the contract subsists, customers shall be provided with the statement of financial position at all times such as loan statement, account statement.
consumer_protection.plain: The bank shall: 1. Disclose and document all terms and conditions, including risks, fees, charges, and payments for each product or service. 2. Adhere to CBN disclosure guidelines covering fees, penalties, interests, termination procedures, and risks. 3. Proactively inform customers about possible changes in contract terms. 4. Ensure contracts are clear, precise, legible, and written in simple language; explain any technical terms. 5. Display updated corporate and product information at customer engagement points. 6. Provide financial tools on website and educate customers about products. 7. Respect CBN’s publication of rates for transparency. 8. Make financial statements (e.g., loan/account statements) available at all times during contract lifecycle.

consumer_protection.title: Notice of Variation
consumer_protection.description: 1. Within a minimum timeline specified by the CBN, financial institutions shall notify consumers about changes to terms and conditions of contracts prior to the implementation of such changes.  2. Notice to consumers on variations to terms and conditions must at a minimum contain the following details: a) Changes in rates / charges (existing rate and new rate that is being introduced) b) Rationale for variation; c) Commencement date of new terms and conditions; d) Revised repayment schedule in line with the new rates (where applicable); e) Options available to the consumer, including the opt-out options.  3. Variation notice must be at no cost to the consumer and there must be evidence of dispatch to address on file or via the usual means of communication with the consumer.  4. FIs shall respond to requests for waivers, concession or other variations on credit facilities within specified timelines, failing which such requests would be deemed to have been accepted.
consumer_protection.plain: The bank shall: 1. Notify consumers of changes to contract terms and conditions within the minimum timeline set by the CBN, before implementing such changes. 2. Ensure that the notice includes:     a) Existing and revised rates/charges     b) Justification for the changes     c) Commencement date of the new terms     d) Revised repayment schedule (if applicable)     e) Options available to the customer (including opt-out) 3. Issue variation notices at no cost to consumers and provide evidence of delivery through preferred communication channels. 4. Respond to customer requests for waivers, concessions, or variations within the CBN’s timeline or the request is deemed approved.

consumer_protection.title: Advertisement
consumer_protection.description: 1. Financial Institutions must be factual and clear in all communication (including advertisements) with consumers. Communications/ advertisements on financial products and services must at a minimum: a) Not be misleading; b) Be clear and explicitly state the features of the products/services as approved; c) Not seek to misrepresent or exaggerate the benefits of the products/services  2. Adverts shall disclose all conditions associated with the products and services. For example, where a promotional material makes reference to interest rates, financial institutions shall indicate all other applicable charges. In addition, measures shall be provided for consumers to make further enquiries.  3. FIs shall ensure that adverts align with approved product features. Adverts not in line with approved product features will attract appropriate sanctions.
consumer_protection.plain: The bank shall: 1. Ensure all advertisements and communications on financial products and services are factual and clear. 2. Communications and adverts must:     a) Not mislead consumers     b) Clearly and explicitly state approved features of products/services     c) Avoid exaggerating or misrepresenting benefits 3. Disclose all conditions related to products and services in promotional content. 4. Also disclose other applicable charges if referencing interest rates. 5. Provide channels for further enquiries. 6. Ensure that all adverts align with product approvals; non-compliance may lead to sanctions.

consumer_protection.title: Fair Treatment
consumer_protection.description: Consumers shall be treated equitably without bias at all stages of their relationship with financial institutions. Every consumer shall be given equal access to basic banking services and consideration accorded to the needs of vulnerable groups. Key themes to be addressed are:  Access to finance: eligible consumers must be granted access to financial products and services;  Equity: consumers shall be treated equitably at all times in a manner devoid of discrimination;  Unfair Contract Terms: contract terms must not undermine the rights of consumers giving FIs undue advantage.
consumer_protection.plain: The Bank shall:  1. Treat all consumers equitably and without bias throughout their relationship with the institution. 2. Ensure all eligible consumers have equal access to financial products and services, including basic banking services. 3. Consider the needs of vulnerable groups in service design and delivery. 4. Avoid discriminatory practices and ensure fairness in every consumer interaction. 5. Refrain from including unfair terms in contracts that undermine consumer rights or provide the Bank with an undue advantage.

consumer_protection.title: Unfair Contract Terms
consumer_protection.description: 1. Terms and conditions shall clearly set out the respective rights and obligations of all parties to transactions in simple language. The use of technical terminologies/languages shall be limited or avoided in contract documents, where they are used, FIs shall ensure that these terminologies are clearly explained to consumers.  Contract terms shall be considered unfair where there is a significant imbalance in one party’s rights and obligations to the detriment of the other. The following amongst others are considered to be unfair terms;  a) Limiting the liability of the financial institution in the event of total or partial non-performance of contractual obligations; b) Excluding the liability of the FI in the event of its negligence which is detrimental to the consumer; c) Clauses that bind a consumer while the corresponding obligation on the FI is conditional; d) Termination of agreements or alteration of clauses without reasonable notice to the consumer; e) Limiting the financial institutions’ liability with respect to actions or commitments undertaken by their agents; f) Giving the FI the possibility of transferring its rights and obligations under the contract, where this may reduce the rights of the consumers, without their consent; g) Excluding or limiting the right of the consumer to take legal action should infraction occur.  2. Contract terms that conflict with regulations are null and void ab initio.  3. Consumers or other stakeholders are encouraged to report contract terms that are in conflict with any regulation.
consumer_protection.plain: The bank shall: 1. Draft contract terms in simple, clear language, avoiding or clearly explaining technical terms. 2. Ensure that contract terms do not create a significant imbalance in the rights and obligations of the bank and the consumer. 3. Avoid including the following in contracts: a. Limit or exclude the bank’s liability in case of non-performance or negligence. b. Make customer obligations binding while the bank’s obligations are conditional. c. Alter or terminating contracts without reasonable notice. d. Exclude the consumer’s right to take legal action. e. Transfer bank rights that reduce consumer rights without consent. 4. Recognize that any contract term that conflicts with regulation is void. 5. Encourage consumers to report any unfair contract terms.

consumer_protection.title: Protection of Consumer Assets and Privacy
consumer_protection.description: Appropriate measures shall be established to guarantee protection of consumer assets and privacy. Consumer’s financial and personal information shall be protected by FIs at all times and shall not be released to a third party without the consent of the consumer, except as required by law.  The following information are considered to be confidential and shall be protected at all times; Contact details, account number and balance, statement of accounts and any other information known to the financial institution.  The Bank shall establish guidelines to safeguard consumer assets and privacy against unauthorized access. The primary areas to be covered are:  Fraud: the need for adequate controls to be put in place to prevent incidences of fraud.  Data Privacy: the need for adequate controls to be put in place to prevent unauthorized access to consumers’ confidential information.
consumer_protection.plain: The Bank shall:  1. Establish and maintain adequate controls to protect consumer assets and personal data against unauthorized access, loss, or misuse. 2. Ensure that consumers’ financial and personal information — including contact details, account numbers, balances, and statements — is treated as confidential at all times. 3. Prevent disclosure of consumer information to third parties, unless required by law or with the explicit consent of the consumer. 4. Implement fraud prevention measures to safeguard consumer assets from unauthorized or illegal activity. 5. Put in place robust data privacy policies and controls to ensure the protection of consumer information from breaches or misuse.
