consumer_protection.title: Fraud
consumer_protection.description: 1. Financial institutions shall establish policies and controls to safeguard consumer assets against fraud. These policies and protocols may include the use of sophisticated software and transaction monitoring systems to monitor the internal processes/operations of financial institutions. Therefore, key policies shall include: a) Segregation of duties: the initiation and conclusion of transactions shall not rest with an individual. Necessary hierarchical controls, second level authentications amongst others, shall be put in place to prevent fraud; b) Access to information: appropriate access control systems shall be established by financial institutions. FIs shall restrict and monitor access to customer’s data base; c) Security (physical and electronic): consumer data and records must be securely stored at all times and accessed only by authorized personnel; d) Adequate data storage infrastructure: specification of technical requirements for data storage infrastructure; and e) Periodic audit: financial institutions shall ensure periodic audit of control systems to ascertain adequacy and effectiveness to guard against breaches.  2. Electronic payment instruments/systems shall be embedded with safety mechanisms; institutions shall ensure regular systems updates to guard against possible security lapses. The CBN shall specify minimum technology standards for payments platforms.  3. Financial institutions shall perform periodic internal risk assessment to identify and assess data security risks on their systems.  4. Financial institutions shall enforce disciplinary action against employees involved in fraud and report same to the regulator. Where required, the CBN shall blacklist such employee from further employment within the industry.  5. Financial institutions shall promptly refund customers for actual amounts lost due to fraud with interest at the CBN prescribed rate unless it can be proved that loss occurred as a result of customer’s negligence or through fraudulent behavior.  6. Financial institutions shall require customers to update their details within the timeline specified by the CBN. Customers are obliged to update their records as need arises in order to ensure data accuracy and ultimately enhance protection. Financial institutions shall create convenient avenues through which customers can make these updates.  7. Financial institutions shall continually create awareness on fraudulent practices and consumers’ responsibilities to guard against such.
consumer_protection.plain: The bank shall: 1. Establish internal policies and controls to protect customer assets from fraud, including: a. Segregation of duties in transactions b. Access control systems for customer data c. Secure storage of customer records (physical and digital) d. Adequate data storage infrastructure e. Periodic audit of systems and controls 2. Embed security features in all e-payment platforms and ensure regular updates in line with CBN technology standards. 3. Conduct periodic internal risk assessments on data and fraud vulnerabilities. 4. Take disciplinary action against employees involved in fraud and report them to the CBN; blacklist where necessary. 5. Refund customers promptly for amounts lost to fraud (with CBN interest) unless fraud was due to customer’s negligence. 6. Require and facilitate timely customer data updates; create easy update channels. 7. Educate consumers regularly on fraud risks and prevention.

consumer_protection.title: Data Protection
consumer_protection.description: 1. All personal information of customers (including those with closed accounts) shall be kept in confidence by FIs. As a duty of care, financial institutions are obliged to safeguard the privacy of their customers’ data.  2. Financial institutions shall not reveal consumers/customers information to a third party except in the following cases: a) With the express permission of the customer; b) As required by the CBN and other regulatory bodies; c) Where there is a court order; d) In pursuance of public duty/interest;  3. Appropriate data protection measures and staff training programs shall be put in place to prevent unauthorized access, alteration, disclosure, accidental loss or destruction of customer data.  4. The consent of consumers shall be obtained in writing before their data is shared with third parties. For this purpose, a third party includes a subsidiary or an associated company.  5. Financial institutions shall obtain the prior consent of customers in writing before using such information for future promotional offers via e-mail, SMS, phone calls and other channels.  6. Consumers partaking in sales promotions shall be informed if they would be required for any publicity or advertisement by the financial institution.
consumer_protection.plain: The bank shall: 1. Keep all personal information of customers confidential, including for closed accounts. 2. Do not disclose customer data to any third party, except:     a. With the customer's written consent;     b. When required by CBN or regulators;     c. Upon court order;     d. In the public interest. 3. Implement strong data protection systems and train staff on data privacy. 4. Obtain written consent from customers before sharing data with third parties, including subsidiaries. 5. Get prior written consent before using customer data for marketing or promotional offers. 6. Inform customers participating in promotions if they will be used for advertising.

consumer_protection.title: Complaints Handling and Redress
consumer_protection.description: Adequate measures shall be established to address disputes that may arise from interactions and relationships between the FI and the consumer. The existence of effective complaints handling mechanisms that are affordable, fair, timely, transparent, accessible and independent would enhance overall consumer confidence in the financial system. The primary areas to be addressed are:  Complaints channels: avenues for lodging complaints shall be readily available and easily accessible to consumers. Consumers shall be made aware of the various channels.  Complaints management processes or procedures: The processes and procedures for complaints management shall be simple and efficient supporting the effective resolution of consumer complaints. Consumers shall be made aware of the various recourse mechanisms.  Complaints redress: provisions shall exist for the fair redress and compensation of consumers in the event of wrongful treatment.  Collaborations with other bodies: effective collaborations with other dispute resolution bodies in the industry shall be established to ensure a full coverage of consumer complaints handling.
consumer_protection.plain: The Bank shall:  1. Establish adequate, fair, and transparent complaints handling and redress mechanisms to resolve disputes arising from interactions with consumers.  2. Provide multiple, easily accessible channels for consumers to lodge complaints and ensure consumers are informed about these options.  3. Design and implement simple, efficient, and effective procedures for managing and resolving complaints.  4. Inform consumers of available recourse and redress mechanisms.  5. Ensure fair redress and compensation is provided to consumers in cases of wrongful treatment.  6. Collaborate with industry dispute resolution bodies to ensure broad and effective coverage of consumer complaints handling.
consumer_protection.riskDescription: Customer dissatisfaction, reputational damage, regulatory penalties for poor handling, legal actions

consumer_protection.responsibility: Compliance / Customer Experience / Legal

consumer_protection.additionalControl: Regular reviews of complaint trends, Staff training, Independent reviews

consumer_protection.title: Complaints Channels
consumer_protection.description: 1. Financial institutions shall have multiple channels (including electronic and non-electronic channels) for consumers to lodge complaints. Examples of complaints channels may include provision of dedicated email addresses, telephone numbers, help desk, web chat etc. Such channels shall be toll-free, easily accessible and available to consumers or their agents at all times.  2. Financial institutions and Alternate Dispute Resolution institutions shall provide consumers with information on available mechanisms for handling complaints. At a minimum, such information shall include: a) Available channels for complaints handling and redress; b) Timeline for complaints resolution; c) Responsibility of the complainant at each stage of the process; d) Obligation of the financial institution or ADR institution; and e) Escalation processes.  This information shall be provided at no cost to complainants at the point of commencing a contractual relationship, upon request or when acknowledging a consumer complaint.  3. Complaints channels shall be staffed by courteous individuals with experience in handling consumer issues. Supervision of the complaints handling process must be carried out by senior management staff.  4. Financial Institutions shall provide relevant training for staff involved in the development and approvals of complaints handling policies, practices and procedures as well as for staff who interface directly with consumers.  5. The CBN shall set minimum standards for the operations of the various complaints handling channels, including the electronic and non-electronic channels. Periodically, there shall be audits or checks on the availability and adequacy of these channels, as well as a comprehensive evaluation of financial institutions’ compliance with the minimum standards set.  6. The CBN shall promote Alternative Dispute Resolution in the industry.  7.The Consumer Protection Department (CPD) shall be responsible for managing all consumer complaints at the CBN.
consumer_protection.plain: The Bank shall: 1. Provide multiple accessible, toll-free complaints channels (email, phone, helpdesk, chat, etc.). 2. Share clear information on complaint resolution procedures, including:     a. Available channels     b. Timeline for resolution     c. Complainant's responsibilities     d. Bank's responsibilities     e. Escalation steps. 3. Ensure this info is provided at onboarding, on request, or during complaint acknowledgment at no cost. 4. Ensure complaints channels are managed by courteous, trained staff and overseen by senior management. 5. Train staff developing or operating complaints processes. 6. Comply with minimum standards set by CBN and prepare for periodic audits. 7. Promote and cooperate with Alternative Dispute Resolution mechanisms.

consumer_protection.title: Complaints Management Processes or Procedures
consumer_protection.description: 1. Financial institutions shall have clear procedures (including timelines which must be in accordance with minimum standards set by CBN) for receiving and resolving complaints. FIs are expected to automate their complaints management processes or procedures.  2. Financial institutions shall establish and implement effective and transparent processes for handling complaints.  3. The complaints management processes of financial institutions shall include proactive measures to minimize the incidences of complaints. Complaints statistics shall be published in financial statements of FIs.  4. Consumer complaints shall first be lodged with the relevant FIs and only be escalated to alternate dispute resolution organs in the event that the consumer is dissatisfied or the complaint is not resolved within the stipulated time.  5. If complaints are not resolved by the financial institution or consumers are dissatisfied with the outcome of the complaints handling process, the FIs must inform consumers of the alternative recourse mechanisms available, and the process involved in seeking redress through these channels.  6. To avoid duplication of effort by ADRs, consumers shall lodge complaints with one ADR at a time and state categorically where complaints have earlier been reported to other ADRs as well as provide the decision reached.  7. Financial institutions shall provide consumers with status update on complaints. Consequently, the following must be addressed in the course of managing a consumer complaints: a) The timelines stipulated by the CBN; b) Financial institution’s acknowledgement of complaints received stating the timeline within which a response will be made available; c) Provision of reference numbers for all complaints received; d) In the event of delays, reason for delayed resolution including status in the event that complaint remains unresolved at the expiration of the agreed/ communicated resolution or response timeline; e) For complaints that have been resolved, resolution shall be provided in writing and acknowledged by the consumer. It is also advised that the consumer’s concurrence or objection is sought or obtained within a stipulated time.  8. To ensure easy resolution of complaints, the CBN may place a time limit or bar for lodging consumer complaints. However, time restrictions shall not apply in exceptional cases such as fraud.  9. ADRs shall not investigate cases concurrently with financial institutions; a case shall be admissible at the ADR only after a decision has been made by the FI. It is upon dissatisfaction with the decisions that such consumer may proceed to an alternate dispute resolution institution.  10. To fast-track resolution of complaints, ADR institutions shall encourage mediation or reconciliatory meetings between complainants and the financial institutions.  11. To promote disclosure and instill accountability amongst FIs, information on consumer complaints shall be published by FIs in their financial statements. The CBN shall in addition, publicize these statistics across financial institutions on a regular basis. This would enable institutions compare their performance against peers and provide consumers with additional source of information for financial decision making.  12. The CBN shall not handle cases that fall within these categories: a) Time barred complaints; and b) Cases before the courts or cases already ruled upon by the courts of law (except where directed by the court through an order).
consumer_protection.plain: The Bank shall: 1. Establish and automate a transparent and efficient complaints management procedure with timelines compliant with CBN standards. 2. Implement proactive measures to minimize complaints. 3. Include complaint statistics in annual financial statements. 4. Ensure all consumer complaints are first handled internally before referring to ADR. 5. Inform customers of available ADR options if unresolved or disputed. 6. Ensure consumers lodge complaints with only one ADR at a time and disclose any prior ADR action. 7. Provide complaint status updates covering:     a) CBN-stipulated timelines     b) Acknowledgment with timeline for response     c) Complaint reference number     d) Reason for delay, if any     e) Written resolution with consumer acknowledgment and feedback 8. Observe CBN’s time-bar policy (except in fraud cases). 9. Avoid parallel handling of complaints with ADRs; ADRs come in only after internal resolution is exhausted. 10. Promote mediation via ADRs for unresolved cases. 11. Publicize consumer complaint statistics in financial reports. 12. Not forward time-barred or court-resolved cases to CBN (unless court-ordered).

consumer_protection.title: Complaints Redress
consumer_protection.description: 1. Financial institutions shall develop a Customer Compensation Policy to address various category of complaints which may arise due to service failures. FIs must publicly display this policy on various media such as bank websites, branches.  2. The Customer Compensation Policy shall be in line with guidelines issued by the CBN and shall contain provisions for probable infractions such as: a) Unauthorized or erroneous debits; b) Excess charges; and c) Financial loss to consumers due to staff negligence/fraudulent activities.  3. Where there is a complaint on excess charges, FIs shall carry out account reconstruction where necessary, in order to put the account into proper perspective.  4. FI shall provide evidence of complaints resolution to customers, ADRs and regulators, where required.  5. Complainants shall provide written acknowledgement confirming satisfaction or otherwise with the outcome of the dispute resolution process within a specified time.  6. Where a complainant fails to acknowledge resolution within the specified timeline, the complainant would be deemed to be satisfied and the case closed.  7. Decisions of ADR institutions may be appealed through the internal process prescribed by such institutions.
consumer_protection.plain: The Bank shall: 1. Develop a Customer Compensation Policy to handle complaints due to service failures. 2. Publicly display the policy on the bank’s website and branches. 3. Align the policy with CBN guidelines and include provisions for:     a) Unauthorized/erroneous debits     b) Excess charges     c) Consumer losses from staff negligence or fraud 4. Conduct account reconstruction when excess charges complaints arise. 5. Provide documented evidence of complaint resolution to the customer, ADRs, and regulators if required. 6. Require written acknowledgment from complainants stating satisfaction or dissatisfaction with the resolution. 7. Treat the complaint as resolved and closed if acknowledgment is not received within a specified timeline. 8. Allow decisions of ADRs to be appealed using the process set by the ADR institution.

consumer_protection.title: Collaborations with other bodies
consumer_protection.description: 1. Institutions involved in complaints management shall collaborate with relevant agencies to enhance the efficiency of the dispute resolution process. Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) shall be signed between institutions involved in financial consumer protection or dispute resolution. The details of the Memorandum of Understanding shall include amongst others: a) Roles and responsibilities of parties; b) Recourse in the event of non-resolution; and c) Escalation path along the various institutions during a dispute resolution process.
consumer_protection.plain: The Bank shall: 1. Collaborate with relevant agencies involved in financial consumer protection and dispute resolution. 2. Sign Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) with these agencies. 3. Ensure each MoU includes:     a) Clear roles and responsibilities of each party;     b) Defined procedures for cases where resolution is not achieved;     c) A clear escalation path for handling complaints across institutions.

consumer_protection.title: Competition
consumer_protection.description: Competitive markets should be promoted in order to encourage innovation, offer consumers diverse range of financial products and services, excellent service delivery and ultimately ensure that consumers benefit from the practice of competition.  To promote competition within the industry, financial institutions shall collaborate with financial regulators and other stakeholders. The critical themes to be covered are:  Free Market: regulators should encourage innovation as well as free entry and exit in the industry.  Switching Barriers: consumers should be allowed to terminate contracts or engage in banking transactions with their preferred financial institution without any restrictions.
consumer_protection.plain: The Bank shall:  1. Promote competition by supporting innovation and ensuring consumers have access to a variety of financial products and services. 2. Collaborate with financial regulators and relevant stakeholders to encourage a competitive financial ecosystem. 3. Ensure that consumers are free to switch between financial institutions or terminate contracts without facing undue restrictions or barriers. 4. Encourage practices that support free market entry and exit to enhance service delivery and consumer choice.

consumer_protection.title: Free market
consumer_protection.description: 1. The CBN shall encourage product development by financial institutions to enable consumers have access to variety of innovative products and services.  2. The CBN shall monitor the market to restrict practices which may inhibit competition.  3. The CBN shall discourage anti-competitive practices such as: a) Price-fixing or pegging of charges – any act by one or more FIs to fix charges on products and services for their benefit but to the detriment of consumers; b) Market allocation – agreement amongst FIs to form territories so that specific institutions are found in certain regions to the exclusion of others; c) Abuse of dominance – any act by one or more FIs with significant market power or share which have adverse effect on competition; and d) Tied selling – any act by financial institutions forcing consumers to buy or subscribe to other products or services along with the desired products or services.
consumer_protection.plain: The Bank shall: 1. Develop a variety of innovative and competitive financial products/services to give consumers more choices. 2. Avoid anti-competitive behaviors such as:     a) Price fixing (agreeing with others to set prices);     b) Market allocation (restricting operations to specific regions in agreement with other FIs);     c) Abuse of dominance (using size/power to block competition);     d) Tied selling (forcing customers to buy an additional product/service). 3. Support a fair, open, and competitive market environment.
consumer_protection.riskDescription: - Sanctions or penalties for anti-competitive practices. - Legal and reputational risks. - Loss of consumer trust and market credibility. - Regulatory intervention and fines by the CBN.
consumer_protection.owner: - Compliance Unit- Strategy & Innovation Department- Legal Department- Product Development Team
consumer_protection.responsibility: - Chief Compliance Officer- Chief Legal Officer- Chief Product Officer
consumer_protection.primaryControl: - Internal policy prohibiting anti-competitive practices. - Legal review of all partnership and pricing arrangements. - Regular product and pricing audits. - Whistleblowing mechanism for unethical practices.
consumer_protection.additionalControl: - Staff training on fair competition laws and ethics. - External legal compliance review. - Monitoring by internal audit. - Reports to Board Risk Committee.

consumer_protection.title: Switching Barriers
consumer_protection.description: 1. Consumers shall be allowed to engage in banking transactions with their preferred financial institutions.  2. Consumers shall have the right to terminate contracts, change or switch FIs, products and/or services subject to contractual terms. It is unethical and anti-competitive for FIs to place restrictions on consumers that discourage switching.  3. Where a customer decides to switch, the financial institution shall provide the necessary information to the new financial institution.
consumer_protection.plain: The Bank shall: 1. Allow consumers to freely choose and switch to any financial institution, product, or service without unnecessary restrictions. 2. Honor customer requests to terminate existing contracts or switch providers in line with contract terms. 3. Provide all necessary account and transaction information to the receiving/new financial institution to facilitate the switch.
consumer_protection.riskDescription: - Regulatory sanctions for anti-competitive practices. - Legal actions or fines. - Customer dissatisfaction and reputational damage. - Reduced trust in the institution’s transparency.

consumer_protection.source: Deployment of the Consumer Complaints Management System (CCMS)
consumer_protection.title: CPD/DIR/GEN/CIR/01/001
consumer_protection.description: The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN), in furtherance of its mandate to promote a stable financial system embarked on the development of the Consumer Complaints Management System (CCMS), an automated system aimed at easing complaints management to engender public confidence in the financial system.  With effect from 2nd January, 2019, Banks and Other Financial Institutions (BOFIs) are required to:  1. Assign Tracking Number for every complaint received from their customers;  2. Issue an acknowledgement, which shall contain the assigned Tracking Number, to the customer; and  3. Commence upload of complaints to the CCMS on a daily basis.  In addition, BOFIs are enjoined to always comply with the timelines stipulated in the CCMS for resolution of the various categories of complaints.
consumer_protection.plain: The Bank shall: 1. Assign a Tracking Number to every customer complaint received. 2. Issue an acknowledgement to the customer that includes the Tracking Number. 3. Upload all customer complaints to the Consumer Complaints Management System (CCMS) daily. 4. Comply with resolution timelines specified in the CCMS for each complaint category.
consumer_protection.riskDescription: - Regulatory sanction for non-compliance with CCMS requirements. - Loss of customer confidence due to poor complaint handling. - Reduced transparency and poor relationship with the CBN. - Reputation damage and potential fines.

consumer_protection.source: Requirement to Display Corporate Names on Websites, Portals, Applications, and Other Online Business Platforms
consumer_protection.title: FPR/PRD/CIR/INT/001/003
consumer_protection.description: The Central Bank of Nigeria has observed with concern that some licensed entities that operate transaction websites/portals or online applications do not conspicuously display their corporate names to facilitate recognition by the public. This practice portends risk to consumers of such products and services, including potential negative perception of the products or services, misleading consumers and difficulty to seek redress when the need arises.  In view of the above and to engender trust and confidence in the use of such products and services, all licensed financial institutions are hereby required to:  1. Conspicuously display their corporate names on all their websites, portals and online applications.  2. Include ‘Licensed by the Central Bank of Nigeria’ beside or under their names.
consumer_protection.plain: The Bank shall: 1. Clearly display the institution’s corporate name on all websites, portals, and mobile/web applications. 2. Add the phrase “Licensed by the Central Bank of Nigeria” next to or directly beneath the corporate name on each platform.

consumer_protection.additionalControl: - Include compliance review in digital product development lifecycle. - Internal quarterly monitoring reports. - Require approvals from Legal and Compliance before launching new websites/apps.

consumer_protection.title: GENERAL PROVISIONS
consumer_protection.description: Institutions shall comply with the following provisions to ensure fair treatment of consumers:  3.1.1 Treat consumers equitably without bias at all stages of the relationship. 3.1.2 Give consumers who meet the minimum legal and non – discriminatory eligibility requirements, equal access to basic services without regard to their social status, physical ability, marital status, gender, age, religion, tribe or ideology. 3.1.3 Consider the needs of the financially excluded, including the vulnerable groups such as low-income consumers, women, seniors, physically challenged and the non-literate in the development and implementation of their business models, strategies and processes.
consumer_protection.plain: The Bank shall:  1. Treat all consumers fairly and without discrimination at every stage of their interaction.  2. Provide equal access to basic services for all eligible consumers, regardless of status or identity.  3. Design and implement services that also consider the needs of vulnerable and financially excluded groups (e.g., low-income earners, women, elderly, physically challenged, and non-literate individuals).
consumer_protection.riskDescription: Failure to uphold fairness and non-discrimination may result in reputational damage, customer complaints, regulatory penalties, and loss of consumer trust.

consumer_protection.additionalControl: - Conduct regular audits on customer interaction points.  - Include fairness and inclusion KPIs in staff performance appraisals.  - Launch financial literacy and inclusion programs.  - Establish feedback mechanisms accessible to all consumer categories.

consumer_protection.title: EQUITY
consumer_protection.description: It shall be the duty of Institutions to treat consumers equitably always. Therefore, Institutions shall:  3.2.1 Treat consumers with courtesy and respect and shall not engage in practices such as threats, intimidation, use of abusive or offensive language, humiliation, misrepresentation, deception or unfair inducements. 3.2.2 Apply lending fees on disbursed amounts only in respect of term loans, except for fees which are normally applicable on undisbursed portions. 3.2.3 Apply non-credit related fees/charges on an account only to the extent of the balance in the account, and defer the outstanding fees/charges until the account is funded and the customer notified of the deferred fees/charges. 3.2.4 Promptly oblige consumers’ request for account closure or to switch providers, without unreasonable closing/switching barriers. 3.2.5 Ensure that variations to contracts including interest rate, fees or charges are only made if expressly provided for in the contract and shall notify consumer of any such variation. 3.2.6 Respond to customers’ enquiries/requests within five (5) working days of receiving the enquiries/requests. 3.2.7 Communicate a decision (acceptance or decline) on applications for waivers, extensions, and other concessions to a customer within ten (10) working days, otherwise the application shall be deemed to have been granted. 3.2.8 Not act in a manner that is inconsistent with the terms and conditions of their contracts with their customers. 3.2.9 Not seek repayment or withhold, in part or in full, customer’s funds to secure repayment before the due date, except with the written authorization of the customer. 3.2.10 Not charge early liquidation fees for consumer and SME loans with variable interest rate.
consumer_protection.plain: The Bank shall:  1. Treat all customers with respect and avoid threats, deception, or unfair practices.  2. Only charge lending fees on actual loan amounts disbursed (unless otherwise specified).  3. Only apply non-credit fees up to the available balance and defer the rest, with clear customer notification.  4. Allow customers to close accounts or switch providers easily, without delays or hurdles.  5. Notify customers of any contract changes only if stated in the contract and with proper notice.  6. Respond to all customer enquiries/requests within 5 working days.  7. Communicate decisions on waivers/concessions within 10 working days, or such requests are considered granted.  8. Honor all contract terms and avoid acting contrary to agreements with customers.  9. Do not withhold customer funds or demand early repayment unless authorized in writing.  10. Do not charge early liquidation fees on variable interest loans to consumers and SMEs.
consumer_protection.riskDescription: Failure to comply may result in regulatory sanctions, customer complaints, reputational damage, financial penalties, and increased litigation risk.

consumer_protection.additionalControl: - Daily/weekly compliance checklist on fee application and waiver response timelines.  - System alerts for pending enquiries or waiver requests.  - Internal audit on adherence to contract terms and switching procedures.  - Review and update fee application logic in core banking systems.  - Introduce dashboard for tracking compliance with notification timelines.

consumer_protection.title: GENERAL PROVISIONS
consumer_protection.description: To promote transparency and enhance disclosure practices, Institutions shall comply with the following provisions:  4.1.1. Ensure that documents provided or made available to consumers shall: a. Be written in clear, legible and simple English language and in a minimum font size of 10. b. Be provided in a durable form for future reference. c. State the name, contact details of the Institution and the consumer. d. Contain a statement that the Institution is regulated by the Central Bank of Nigeria. e. Not be misleading or deceptive.  4.1.2. Put procedures in place to ensure that an oral explanation of the document is provided to the consumer in a language that he or she understands if: a. the consumer requests; or b. it is reasonably obvious that the consumer is illiterate or visually impaired or, for any other reason, cannot understand the document.  4.1.3. Conspicuously display in their banking halls and publish on their websites and internet banking platforms, accurate and up to date information on all their products and services. Such information shall include: a. prime and maximum lending rates; b. deposit rates; and c. exchange rates of foreign currencies.  4.1.4. Disclose to the consumer in writing, all Terms and Conditions of a transaction agreement. 4.1.5. Ensure that the disclaimer “Terms and Conditions Apply” or any other phrase conveying a similar meaning shall only be used if the terms and conditions have been explained and disclosed in the contract or in other medium accessible by the customer. The Institution shall at all times, draw the consumer’s attention to such disclosure. 4.1.6. Clearly explain technical terms used in documents to the consumer to aid understanding. 4.1.7. Agree with consumers on the communication channel(s) to be used for all correspondences and include the channel(s) in all contract documents. 4.1.8. Ensure that their websites and other information dissemination channels are functional and regularly updated with the current features of products and services offered. 4.1.9. Comply with the rates, fees, charges, or prices published or disclosed at the engagement points. 4.1.10. Inform consumers of applicable and indicative foreign exchange rates through customer engagement points and advise consumers to always check the rates before consummating foreign exchange transactions. 4.1.11. Bear all costs associated with disclosures to customers required by the Regulations, except for deposits and withdrawals by or on behalf of the customer.
consumer_protection.plain: The Bank shall: 1. Use clear, simple English (minimum font size 10) in customer-facing documents, and ensure documents are durable and personalized (with names, contacts, CBN disclosure, etc.). 2. Provide oral explanations for documents when requested or needed (e.g., for illiterate or visually impaired customers). 3. Clearly display on all platforms: up-to-date lending, deposit, and FX rates. 4. Disclose all transaction terms and conditions clearly in writing.5. Only use "Terms and Conditions Apply" if the T&Cs are explained and accessible.6. Explain all technical terms to consumers. 7. Agree on a communication channel with the customer and include it in the contract. 8. Ensure all dissemination platforms (website, mobile app, etc.) are functional and current. 9. Honour the rates and charges displayed at the point of engagement. 10. Inform customers of applicable FX rates at the point of transaction. 11. Bear the cost of disclosures required by law.
consumer_protection.riskDescription: Non-compliance may result in poor customer experience, regulatory penalties, loss of trust, reputational damage, legal actions, and customer attrition.

consumer_protection.additionalControl: - Deploy plain-language checks during internal policy reviews.  - Conduct periodic mystery shopper audits for disclosure practices. - Embed compliance checklist in document issuance workflow.  - Update communication templates with multi-language support and accessibility considerations.  - Automate update logs and alerts for changes in rates/fees published online.

consumer_protection.title: ADVERTISEMENT
consumer_protection.description: Institutions shall comply with the following disclosures for all advertisements and promotional materials:  4.2.1 The content of advertisements shall be factual and unambiguous, expressed in clear and simple language and shall not be offensive, misleading, deceptive, injurious, or exaggerate the benefits of the products or services being advertised. 4.2.2 The overall impression of advertisements shall not emphasize benefits of a product or service while de-emphasizing its associated risks. 4.2.3 Disclose their contact details in any advertisement or promotional material. 4.2.4 Clearly disclose details of the cost of a product or services, including all fees and other associated charges. 4.2.5 Fully disclose the nature and value of benefits, where an advertisement refers to, or is linked to other value adding benefits. 4.2.6 Not make references to unaudited financial statements. 4.2.7 Not mention names of competitors or make comparisons in their advertisements. 4.2.8 Unsolicited advertisements through emails, text messages, voice calls and other channels sent by or on behalf of a Institution shall be at no cost to the consumer and shall contain an opt-out provision for future advertisements. 4.2.9 Notify the Director, Consumer Protection Department of the CBN prior to the commencement of advertisement of product or service by submitting a description of the content of the advertisement.
consumer_protection.plain: The Bank shall: 1. Ensure advertisements are factual, clear, and not misleading. 2. Avoid exaggerating benefits or hiding product/service risks. 3. Display contact details in all adverts. 4. Disclose full cost of products/services, including fees and charges. 5. Clearly state the value and nature of any benefits tied to a product. 6. Not reference unaudited financials. 7. Avoid mentioning competitors or making comparisons. 8. Be free to recipients and must include an opt-out option from unsolicited ads via email/SMS/calls. 9. Notify CBN before launching any product/service advertisement with content details.

consumer_protection.title: PRE-CONTRACT DISCLOSURES
consumer_protection.description: Institutions shall comply with the following requirements prior to the execution of any contract with consumers:  4.3.1 Disclose all terms and conditions of a product or service on offer, as well as the features, risks, benefits, fees and other associated charges. 4.3.2 Disclose in contracts, the possibility of variations in interest rates or foreign exchange due to changes in market conditions. 4.3.3 Disclose similar products and services within the Institution, to enable consumers make comparisons and informed choices. 4.3.4 Provide the consumer, a Key Facts Statement (KFS) in the format attached as Annexure A stating a summary of key information on consumer loans. 4.3.5 Allow consumers a minimum of two (2) days from date of receipt, to review draft contract before execution except where the customer waives this in writing. 4.3.6 Give a consumer a cooling-off period of three (3) working days after the signing of a credit contract within which the consumer may cancel the contract without having to pay any penalty or charges. However, the consumer may choose to waive the option by notifying the bank in writing.
consumer_protection.plain: The Bank shall: 1. Disclose all terms, conditions, features, risks, benefits, fees, and charges of the product or service before contract execution. 2. Clearly state in the contract if interest rates or FX rates may vary due to market conditions. 3. Provide information on similar products and services to help customers make comparisons. 4. Issue a Key Facts Statement (KFS) in the required format for consumer loans. 5. Give consumers at least 2 days to review draft contracts before signing, unless waived in writing. 6. Allow a 3-working-day cooling-off period post-signing for contract cancellation without penalties, unless waived by the consumer in writing.
consumer_protection.riskDescription: - Regulatory non-compliance penalties. - Consumer complaints or litigation for lack of disclosure or coercion. - Reputational risk due to perceived lack of transparency. - Breach of consumer protection laws leading to enforcement actions.
consumer_protection.owner: - Legal Department- Product Managers- Compliance Department- Retail/Consumer Banking Unit- Credit/Risk Department
consumer_protection.responsibility: - Chief Compliance Officer- Head of Legal- Head of Retail/Consumer Banking- Head, Credit Risk
consumer_protection.primaryControl: - Standardized product disclosure templates (including the KFS). - Mandatory pre-contract disclosure checklist. - Internal review of draft contracts by Legal and Compliance. - Staff training on disclosure obligations. - Automated systems to flag contracts not meeting the 2-day review or cooling-off rule.
consumer_protection.additionalControl: - Quarterly audits of contract documentation and disclosure processes. - Consumer feedback channels to track violations. - System-enforced delays before contract execution to honor the 2-day review period. - Inclusion of a standard waiver template for customer use (if they choose to waive review/cooling-off periods).

consumer_protection.title: CONTRACTUAL DISCLOSURES
consumer_protection.description: Institutions shall comply with the following requirements during the lifecycle of any contract with consumers:  4.4.1 Notify consumers of any transaction on their account immediately it is made. At a minimum, the notification shall include date, amount, payer, transaction reference, channel and the cleared account balance. 4.4.2 Ensure that descriptions in account statements are clear. At a minimum, it shall include, transaction reference, payer transaction channel, location and account balance. 4.4.3 Ensure that, at a minimum, credit contracts contain the following information: a. Key features and risks; b. Tenor of the contract; c. The nature, amount and method of calculation of any interest, fee or charge and when it is payable; d. The applicable Annual Percentage Rate (APR) to be calculated using the formula stated in Annexure B1 and B2; e. Notice of possible variations in interest rates, and how the consumer will be informed of changes; and f. Information on how to lodge a complaint to the Institution and escalate complaint to the CBN where necessary.  4.4.4 Provide consumer with monthly statements (or confirmation/investment advice as the case may be) for all products and account types, including loan accounts, special accounts and other related accounts at no cost. 4.4.5 Provide account balances to consumers on request. 4.4.6 Give prior notice of variation in interest rates to customers. At a minimum, the notice shall state: a. The reason for the variation; b. The commencement date; c. The revised repayment schedule (where necessary); and d. The alternatives available such as concession, restructuring, re-negotiation, opt-out or termination of the contract.  4.4.7 Ensure that variations in interest shall only be implemented after requisite notification to consumers: 10 working days (DMB) and 5 working days for other Institutions.
consumer_protection.plain: The Bank shall: 1. Send instant alerts to customers for every transaction, showing date, amount, payer, channel, reference, and new balance. 2. Make sure account statements are clear and include transaction reference, payer, channel, location, and balance. 3. Ensure credit contracts show key features, risks, tenor, interest/fees/charges (with calculations), APR (as per formula), rate variation process, and complaint channels. 4. Provide monthly statements (or confirmation/advice) for all account and product types (loans, investments, etc.) free of charge. 5. Provide account balances when requested by customers. 6. Before changing interest rates, give prior notice stating: reason, start date, revised schedule, and customer options (restructure, renegotiate, exit, etc.). 7. Delay interest changes until 10 working days’ notice for DMBs or 5 working days for others has been given.
consumer_protection.riskDescription: Failure to comply can lead to customer complaints, regulatory sanctions, disputes over unfair charges or changes in terms, reputational damage, and class-action lawsuits.
consumer_protection.owner: - Legal and Compliance Unit - Retail/Commercial Lending Teams - Core Banking Product Managers - Customer Experience/Operations - IT/Alert Notification & Statement Delivery Team
consumer_protection.responsibility: Compliance Team, IT Systems Admin, Retail Lending Head, Customer Communications Lead
consumer_protection.primaryControl: - Automated transaction alert system.  - Template-based contract documents reviewed by Legal.  - System-generated monthly statements.  - SMS/email balance inquiry processes.  - Interest variation approval workflows with customer notification embedded.
consumer_protection.additionalControl: - Regular review and audit of contract templates for compliance with APR disclosure formula.  - Automated enforcement of pre-notification for interest rate changes.  - Enforce statement clarity and quality checks.  - Customer feedback loop on statement clarity and transaction alert satisfaction.  - Track SLA for provision of account balance requests.

consumer_protection.description: a. consumer_protection.title: GENERAL PROVISIONS
consumer_protection.description: To promote good business practices, Institutions shall comply with the following provisions:  5.1.1 Conduct their business in a responsible, professional and ethical manner. 5.1.2 Train their staff to promote competence, efficiency and professionalism in the discharge of their duties. 5.1.3 Provide clear information about products and services, features, terms and conditions and the applicable fees and charges. 5.1.4 Provide and inform consumers of the channels to make enquiries and complaints. 5.1.5 Notify customers of circumstances or situations that may affect the terms of their contracts or relationships. 5.1.6 Display all applicable fees for electronic payment services with the option to accept or decline before a transaction is consummated. This should include a notice that third-party charges may apply. 5.1.7 Not impose any product, service or channel on consumers. 5.1.8 Not charge fees for issuance and renewal of products or services which have not been requested by the customer. 5.1.9 Not compel consumers to buy a product or service as a condition for the purchase of another product or service unless where the products or services are directly dependent.
consumer_protection.plain: The Bank shall: 1. Conduct all business dealings professionally, ethically, and responsibly. 2. Train staff to uphold competence and professionalism. 3. Provide clear, accurate product/service information, including terms, conditions, and fees. 4. Inform customers about available complaint/enquiry channels. 5. Notify customers of any change that affects their contracts. 6. Display all e-payment fees and allow customer consent before transactions. 7. Not force products/services on consumers. 8. Not charge for unrequested products. 9. Not compel bundling of products unless they're interdependent.
consumer_protection.riskDescription: - Risk of CBN sanctions and legal penalties for failure to comply. - Potential customer dissatisfaction, complaints, and churn. - Reputational damage due to unethical or misleading practices. - Risk of class-action lawsuits or regulator intervention from bundled/forced product offerings.
consumer_protection.owner: - Legal and Compliance Department- Product Management Team- Customer Experience/Service Department- Marketing and Sales Team- IT/Business Process Automation Team
consumer_protection.responsibility: - Chief Compliance Officer- Head, Legal and Regulatory Affairs- Head, Customer Experience- Head, Products- Head, Digital Channels/IT
consumer_protection.primaryControl: - Develop a Consumer Protection Compliance Policy. - Ensure product/service literature is standardized and approved before publication. - Implement staff training and compliance onboarding. - Automate fee display and consent features in digital channels. - Maintain and publicize a complaints resolution framework. - Regular reviews of bundled offerings and customer opt-in records.
consumer_protection.additionalControl: - Conduct mystery shopping and customer surveys to validate compliance. - Establish a compliance helpdesk for customer complaints on ethics. - Perform internal audits and periodic compliance self-assessments. - Quarterly compliance performance reviews with department heads.

consumer_protection.title: RESPONSIBLE LENDING
consumer_protection.description: To ensure that the capability of consumers to repay credits are professionally assessed, Institutions shall comply with the following requirements:  5.2.1 Include in credit risk assessment procedures, the type and circumstances for which a credit will be suitable as well as clear lines of authority for approving the product. 5.2.2 Before granting credit to consumers, assess their capability to repay in a sustainable manner taking into consideration their financial circumstances. 5.2.3 Ascertain the credit history of consumers from the Credit Risk Management System, Credit Bureau and other sources of credit reference before advancing credits. 5.2.4 Have a policy to deal with consumers who are in financial difficulty. 5.2.5 Monitor loan performance and upon early detection of repayment difficulties engage the customer to discuss alternative repayment options. 5.2.6 Not compel consumers to buy products or services, such as insurance or valuation from a particular third-party provider as a pre-condition for the grant of a credit facility, but can provide the option to choose from at least three (3) providers or any number as may be prescribed by CBN from time to time. 5.2.7 Ensure that guarantors confirm in writing that they have read and understood their commitments, potential implications and the maximum amount they are guaranteeing, and have either: a. sought and obtained independent professional advice before executing the guarantee; or b. declared that they do not need independent advice. 5.2.8 Provide periodic update to Guarantors on the loan performance to enable them to assess the likelihood of being called upon to discharge their commitments. 5.2.9 Issue Letter of Discharge at no cost to customers within 5 business days after liquidation of their loans, and where the loan is guaranteed, the guarantor shall also be notified accordingly. 5.2.10 Notify customers where their loan requests are declined. The reason(s) for decline shall be provided upon request.
consumer_protection.plain: The Bank shall: 1. Include credit suitability criteria and approval authority in credit risk procedures. 2. Assess a consumer's ability to repay before granting credit, considering their financial situation. 3. Check consumer credit history from CRMS, credit bureaus, or other sources before loan approval. 4. Maintain policies for dealing with consumers in financial difficulty. 5. Monitor loans and engage struggling customers early to find repayment solutions. 6. Not force customers to use specific service providers (e.g., insurance); offer at least 3 options. 7. Ensure guarantors provide written confirmation of understanding and advice status. 8. Send guarantors periodic updates on loan performance. 9. Issue free Loan Discharge Letters within 5 business days post-loan repayment and notify guarantors. 10. Inform customers of declined loan applications and provide reasons upon request.
consumer_protection.riskDescription: - Regulatory sanctions for non-compliance with responsible lending principles. - Increased loan defaults due to poor credit assessment. - Reputational damage and customer complaints due to unfair practices or lack of transparency. - Legal liability from guarantors or consumers who were not properly informed. - Potential CBN penalties for compelling use of third-party services.
consumer_protection.owner: - Credit Risk Management Unit- Loan Approval Officers- Legal and Compliance Department- Customer Service/Experience- Loan Monitoring/Collections Team
consumer_protection.responsibility: - Chief Compliance Officer- Head of Credit Risk- Head, Collections & Monitoring- Head of Legal- Head of Customer Experience
consumer_protection.primaryControl: - Incorporate responsible lending checks into credit policy and procedures. - Embed income and affordability checks in loan application systems. - Set automated CRMS and credit bureau validation before approval. - Develop SOPs for handling financial difficulty cases. - Train staff on third-party product disclosure rules. - Require written declarations and advice confirmations from guarantors. - Automate alerts for periodic loan performance updates to guarantors. - Automate discharge letter issuance within 5 business days.
consumer_protection.additionalControl: - Quarterly audits of loan files to check compliance with responsible lending requirements. - Review of system logs for CRMS/bureau checks. - Periodic staff training on loan suitability, disclosures, and guarantor rights. - Internal compliance reviews of customer notification practices (declined loans, discharge letters, etc.).

consumer_protection.title: SALES PROMOTION
consumer_protection.description: To ensure that advertisements and promotional materials on products and services are clear and not misleading, Institutions shall:  5.3.1 Provide information that would aid consumers’ decisions. 5.3.2 Carry out marketing of products and services in an ethical and professional manner. 5.3.3 Ensure that sales and marketing staff are properly trained and competent to perform their functions. The staff should be knowledgeable in key features, risks and critical terms of product offering. 5.3.4 Establish a process to periodically check and monitor the competence and conduct of sales and marketing staff. 5.3.5 The remuneration of marketing/sales staff shall not be solely based on sales volume/target but must give consideration to the interests and circumstances of the customers. 5.3.6 Provide consumers with the option to opt out from receiving marketing materials.
consumer_protection.plain: The Bank shall: 1. Ensure all product/service ads and promotions are clear and not misleading. 2. Disclose adequate information to help customers make informed decisions. 3. Conduct marketing activities in a professional and ethical manner. 4. Ensure marketing/sales staff are well-trained and competent on key product features, risks, and terms. 5. Establish a system to regularly assess staff conduct and competence. 6. Sales staff remuneration must not be solely based on targets – it must reflect customer welfare. 7. Allow customers to opt-out of marketing messages.
consumer_protection.deadlineType: Ongoing (training quarterly, audits bi-annually, reviews prior to promotions)
consumer_protection.riskDescription: - Regulatory sanctions for misleading advertising or unethical marketing practices. - Reputational damage and loss of customer trust. - Legal claims from mis-sold products or deceptive marketing. - Customer churn due to aggressive or unethical sales tactics. - Poorly trained staff may lead to non-compliance and increased complaints.

consumer_protection.responsibility: - Chief Compliance Officer- Head of Sales/Marketing- Head of Internal Audit- Head of Learning & Development
consumer_protection.primaryControl: - Implement a compliance review process for all advertisements and promotions. - Develop and deliver regular training for all marketing and sales staff. - Enforce a code of ethics for marketing and sales. - Conduct regular performance assessments and competency reviews of staff. - Design a balanced scorecard for sales incentives that includes customer satisfaction. - Include opt-out options clearly in all promotional messages (SMS, emails, etc.).
consumer_protection.additionalControl: - Periodic mystery shopper tests to verify ethical sales behavior. - Maintain an audit trail for customer opt-out requests. - Include pre-approval from Compliance before running any major sales promotion. - Establish feedback loops for customer reactions to marketing campaigns. - Include disclosure reviews in internal audit programs.

consumer_protection.title: DATA PROTECTION AND PRIVACY
consumer_protection.description: To ensure data protection and privacy of consumers, Institutions shall:  5.4.1 Protect the privacy and confidentiality of consumer information and assets against unauthorized access, and be accountable for acts or omissions in respect thereof. 5.4.2 Obtain the written consent of consumers to collect and process their personal data for specific purpose and provide them with the option to withdraw the consent at any time. 5.4.3 Not transfer personal data of consumers to a third party without their express consent, except in compliance with a legal obligation. 5.4.4 Inform consumers whenever their data is exchanged with an authorized third party, stating details of the exchange. 5.4.5 Review data processing and privacy procedures to ensure that the purpose(s) for which initial consent was granted remained valid. 5.4.6 Keep accurate and updated data of consumers always.
consumer_protection.plain: The Bank shall: 5.4.1 Ensure customer information is secure, confidential, and protected from unauthorized access, and be accountable for any misuse or exposure. 5.4.2 Get written consent from customers before collecting or processing their personal data, and give them the option to withdraw it anytime. 5.4.3 Do not share personal data with third parties unless the customer explicitly agrees or there’s a legal requirement. 5.4.4 Always notify customers when their data is shared with any authorized third party, including who received it and why. 5.4.5 Regularly review data processing practices to ensure they still align with the customer’s original consent. 5.4.6 Keep customer records accurate and current at all times.
consumer_protection.riskDescription: Data breaches, unauthorized disclosures, or failure to get proper consent can lead to heavy fines (NDPA/NDPR/CBN), loss of customer trust, reputational damage, and litigation.

consumer_protection.responsibility: Data Protection Officer (DPO), Head of IT Security, Head of Compliance, Customer Experience Lead, Legal Department
consumer_protection.primaryControl: - Data Protection & Privacy Policy (aligned with NDPA/NDPR). - Consent forms embedded in digital/onboarding journeys. - Encryption, firewalls, and access control protocols. - Periodic internal audits on data access logs. - Customer communication protocols and records. - Data quality and KYC validation processes.
consumer_protection.additionalControl: - Implement automated data consent dashboards (opt-in/opt-out history).- Consent renewal prompts at intervals. - Data sharing logs with customer alerts.- Staff training on data privacy & compliance. - Real-time update validation for critical customer data (e.g., email, phone). - Periodic compliance reviews with NDPA/CBN standards.

consumer_protection.title: GENERAL PROVISIONS
consumer_protection.description: The resolution of disputes shall be the responsibility of Institutions. Consumer complaints shall first be lodged with Institutions for timely resolution and redress. Institutions shall:  6.1.1 Develop documented processes on Complaints Handling that will guarantee fairness, transparency, responsiveness and independence of the complaint handling mechanism. 6.1.2 Allocate adequate resources for complaints handling/redress and the processes manned by skilled and well-trained members of staff. 6.1.3 At all customer engagement points, disclose channels and contact details for lodging complaints, timeframe for resolution, and options for escalation. Where it is not practicable to comply with this, refer customers to where the information required could be obtained.
consumer_protection.plain: The Bank shall: 1. They have a clear, written policy on how customer complaints will be handled. The policy must ensure fairness, openness, quick response times, and independence.   2. Adequate resources (budget, personnel, technology) are provided to handle complaints, and the team is made up of well-trained professionals.  3. At all customer service points (physical branches, digital platforms, ATMs, mobile apps), information must be made available on:– How to make a complaint– Contact details– Timeframe for resolution– How customers can escalate unresolved issuesIf not feasible in a location, direct the customer to where this information can be obtained.
consumer_protection.riskDescription: Poor complaints handling could lead to regulatory sanctions, reputational damage, erosion of customer trust, and increased litigation or escalations to the CBN Consumer Protection Department.
consumer_protection.owner: - Customer Service / Customer Experience Team- Compliance Team- Branch Managers- Contact Center Managers- IT / Digital Channels Team
consumer_protection.responsibility: Head of Customer Experience, Compliance Officer, Contact Center Lead, Head of Digital Channels, Internal Control Unit
consumer_protection.primaryControl: - Complaint Management Policy (documented and approved). - Dedicated complaints handling unit with escalation matrix. - CRM system for tracking and resolving complaints. - Complaint channels published on websites, mobile apps, branches. - Periodic staff training on dispute resolution protocols.
consumer_protection.additionalControl: - Publish complaint resolution SLAs (e.g., 5–10 business days) visibly across channels. - Auto-acknowledgement system when complaints are lodged. - Monthly review of complaint trends and escalations. - Regular training updates for complaint handling staff. - Internal audit review of complaint resolution performance.

consumer_protection.title: COMPLAINTS MANAGEMENT CHANNELS
consumer_protection.description: Institutions shall provide multiple dedicated channels to receive and handle consumer complaints including verbal complaints. The channels may include letters, e-mails, telephone lines, social media and digital software platforms. The following requirements shall apply in the deployment of the channels:  6.2.1 Be effective, functional, efficient and accessible always. 6.2.2 Generate a unique identification number and acknowledge complaints within 24 hours of lodgment, including transcription of verbal complaints. 6.2.3 Accord special consideration to the needs of vulnerable groups, especially the physically challenged persons and seniors. 6.2.4 Provide emergency channels for reporting time-sensitive issues especially fraud-related complaints at all times.
consumer_protection.plain: The Bank shall provide multiple complaint channels, such as phone, email, social media, apps, and physical letters, including for verbal complaints.   1.  Ensure these channels are always working, fast, easy to use, and accessible.  2.  For every complaint:– Generate a unique ID number– Acknowledge receipt within 24 hours– Transcribe all verbal complaints.  3. Ensure vulnerable groups (e.g., physically challenged, seniors) are given special support when lodging complaints. 4.  Provide emergency channels (hotlines or 24/7 platforms) for time-sensitive complaints, especially fraud-related cases.
consumer_protection.riskDescription: Failure to deploy effective, accessible, and timely complaint channels may lead to regulatory breaches, delayed resolution of fraud, customer dissatisfaction, reputational damage, and penalties.

consumer_protection.primaryControl: - Multiple complaint channels (email, SMS, call centers, social media, branch desks). - CRM or ticketing system that logs and tracks complaints. - Acknowledgement templates for complaint response. - Fraud hotlines available 24/7. - Complaint SOP (Standard Operating Procedures).
consumer_protection.additionalControl: - Enforce automatic ID and 24-hour acknowledgment for every complaint. - Track and test functionality of complaint channels weekly. - Develop escalation framework for emergency fraud-related complaints. - Train frontline staff on handling complaints from vulnerable persons. - Audit all complaint systems for uptime and accessibility.

consumer_protection.title: INTERNAL DISPUTE RESOLUTION
consumer_protection.description: Institutions shall establish Internal Dispute Resolution (IDR) structures and processes for the effective management of consumer complaints. The IDR mechanism shall satisfy the following requirements:  6.3.1 Be under the oversight of the Executive Compliance Officer or an equivalent. 6.3.2 Upon receipt of a complaint, communicate to the consumer within 24 hours, an acknowledgment containing: a. a unique identification or tracking number, b. contact details of the complaints desk, c. expected resolution timeline, d. escalation options; and e. an assurance that the complaint is being addressed.  6.3.3 Use the unique identification or tracking number in all correspondence with the complainant. 6.3.4 Designate a unit for complaints handling independent of other products or business functions taking into consideration, the nature and complexity of their business. 6.3.5 Staff responsible for handling complaints shall be required to declare any conflict of interest that may affect their objectivity in handling a complaint. 6.3.6 Resolve complaints received within the time specified in the Timelines for Complaints Resolution by Institutions in Annexure D. 6.3.7 Refund identified excess charges, non-payment or under-payment of interest on deposits, unauthorized debits, etc. along with interest as provided in the extant Monetary, Credit, Foreign Trade and Exchange Policy Guidelines or any regulation issued by the CBN. 6.3.8 Issue a letter of apology to the complainant where the above applies. 6.3.9 Reconstruct customers' accounts to establish excess charges on overdrawn accounts, and pay interest on the identified excess charges after reconstruction, in accordance with extant CBN Regulations. 6.3.10 Remit established refunds and interest thereon to the complainants' accounts within the prescribed Timelines for Complaints Resolution by Institutions contained in Annexure D. 6.3.11 Send a Summary Resolution Communication (SRC) for resolved complaints, to the complainant by the next business day conveying: a. the basis for the decision(s); b. the right of appeal available to the complainant for a second level review by the Institution; and c. the right of escalation to the CBN, or other Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) avenues where the complainant is not satisfied with decisions arrived at.  6.3.12 A complaint shall be considered as resolved where the complainant has indicated acceptance of the resolution in writing to the Institution within 30 days after the receipt of the SRC, otherwise the complaint shall be deemed resolved and closed in the records of the Institution. 6.3.13 Where a complainant is dissatisfied with a decision communicated by a Institution, the complainant shall, within 30 days from the date of the receipt of the SRC, request in writing for a 2nd level review. 6.3.14 Upon receipt of a request for 2nd level review, the Institution shall review, resolve and communicate decision(s) within the Timelines for Complaints Resolution by Institutions as contained in Annexure D for second level review. 6.3.15 Identify recurring complaint types, identify their root cause(s), implement remedial measures, and generate a Root Cause Analysis Report (RCAR). 6.3.16 Prepare quarterly RCAR and submit to the Central Bank of Nigeria on or before 14th day of January, April, July and October respectively. 6.3.17 The RCAR shall contain the frequency of occurrence, identified root cause(s) and the remedial actions implemented. 6.3.18 Report complaints statistics in annual reports and the abridged Financial Statement in line with the approved format or any other format as may be prescribed by the CBN from time to time. 6.3.19 Institutions may outsource complaints handling functions subject to CBN approval.
consumer_protection.plain: The Bank shall:  1. Establish Internal Dispute Resolution (IDR) structures and processes for effective consumer complaint management.  2. Place the IDR mechanism under the oversight of the Executive Compliance Officer or equivalent.  3. Upon receipt of a complaint, acknowledge it within 24 hours, providing: a) a unique identification or tracking number; b) contact details of the complaints desk; c) expected resolution timeline; d) escalation options; and e) an assurance that the complaint is being addressed.  4. Use the unique identification or tracking number in all correspondence with the complainant.  5. Designate a complaints handling unit independent of other products or business functions, considering the nature and complexity of its business.  6. Require staff handling complaints to declare any conflict of interest that may affect their objectivity.  7. Resolve complaints within the timelines specified in Annexure D of the regulation.  8. Refund excess charges, non-payment or under-payment of interest on deposits, unauthorized debits, etc., along with interest as provided in extant Monetary, Credit, Foreign Trade and Exchange Policy Guidelines or other CBN regulations.  9. Issue a letter of apology to the complainant where such refunds apply.  10. Reconstruct customers’ accounts to identify excess charges on overdrawn accounts, and pay interest on those charges after reconstruction in accordance with CBN regulations.  11. Remit established refunds and interest thereon to complainants’ accounts within the prescribed timelines in Annexure D.  12. Send a Summary Resolution Communication (SRC) for resolved complaints to the complainant by the next business day, stating: a) the basis for the decision(s); b) the right of appeal for a second-level review by the Bank; and c) the right of escalation to the CBN or Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) avenues if dissatisfied.  13. Consider a complaint resolved if the complainant confirms acceptance of the resolution in writing within 30 days of receiving the SRC; otherwise deem the complaint resolved and closed in the records of the Bank.  14. Allow a dissatisfied complainant to request a second-level review within 30 days of the SRC.  15. Upon such a request, review, resolve, and communicate the decision within the timelines in Annexure D for second-level review.  16. Identify recurring complaint types, determine their root causes, implement remedial measures, and prepare a Root Cause Analysis Report (RCAR).  17. consumer_protection.source: Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Act (FCCPA), 2018
consumer_protection.title: Prohibition of Restrictive Agreements
consumer_protection.description: (1) Any agreement among undertakings or a decision of an association of undertakings that has the purpose of actual or likely effect of preventing, restricting or distorting competition in any market is unlawful and, subject to section 61 of this Act, void and of no legal effect. (2) The prohibited acts under subsection (1) include, in particular— (a) directly or indirectly fixing a purchase or selling price of goods or services, subject to section 107 of this Act; (b) dividing markets by allocating customers, suppliers, territories or specific types of goods or services; (c) limiting or controlling production or distribution of any goods or services, markets, technical development or investment, subject to section 108 of this Act; (d) engaging in collusive tendering, subject to section 109 of this Act; or (e) making the conclusion of an agreement subject to acceptance by the other parties of supplementary obligations which, by their nature or according to commercial usage, have no connection  with the subject of such agreement
consumer_protection.plain: The Bank shall be careful not to enter into any agreement or make any decision with other businesses that could limit or distort competition in the market. Specifically, the Bank must not:  1. Set or agree on buying or selling prices with other companies (directly or indirectly).  2. Divide or allocate customers, suppliers, geographic areas, or types of products/services with competitors.  3. Agree to limit production, distribution, technical development, or investment.  4. Collude in tenders — i.e., rig or pre-arrange the outcome of tenders or contract bids.  5. Include unrelated conditions — i.e., make an agreement conditional on accepting extra obligations that have no connection to the subject of the deal.
consumer_protection.riskDescription: Regulatory sanctions, reputational damage, and invalidated contracts due to anti-competitive practices.

consumer_protection.source: Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Act (FCCPA), 2018
consumer_protection.title: Dominance and Abuse
consumer_protection.description: (1) For the purpose of this Act, an undertaking is considered to be in a dominant position if it is able to act without taking account of the reaction of its customers, consumers or competitors. (2) A dominant position in a relevant market exists where an undertaking enjoys a position of economic strength enabling it to prevent effective competition being maintained on the relevant market and having the power to behave to an appreciable extent independently of its competitors, customers and ultimately consumers.
consumer_protection.plain: The Bank shall not abuse any dominant market position. A dominant position exists when the Bank has significant market power that allows it to operate independently of competitors, customers, or consumers.  If the Bank can act without needing to consider how others in the market might respond, it must take extra care not to prevent fair competition or limit market access for others.  Holding such economic strength comes with a responsibility to act transparently, avoid anti-competitive behavior, and support a level playing field for all market participants.
consumer_protection.riskDescription: Abuse of market power leading to regulatory penalties or restrictions.

consumer_protection.title: Criteria for Dominance
consumer_protection.description: For the purpose of delineating the relevant market under this Act, the criteria that shall be taken into account include the— (a) geographical boundaries that identify groups of sellers and buyers of goods or services within which competition is likely to be restrained; (b) goods or services which are regarded as interchangeable or substitutable by the consumer by reason of their characteristics, prices and the intended use; and (c) suppliers to which consumers may turn to in the short term, if the abuse of dominance leads to a significant increase in price or to other detrimental effect upon the consumer.
consumer_protection.plain: The Bank shall assess its market power by identifying its geographic reach, determining whether its banking services are substitutable by consumers based on features, price, and purpose, and evaluating whether consumers have other providers they can switch to in the short term if the Bank increases prices or engages in anti-competitive practices.

consumer_protection.description: (3) For the purpose of assessing market dominance, account shall be taken in particular of— (a) the market share of the undertaking or undertakings concerned in the relevant market; (b) its or their financial power; (c) its or their access to supplies or markets; (d) its or their links with other undertakings; (e) legal or factual barriers to market entry by other undertakings; (f) actual or potential competition by undertakings established within or outside the scope of application of this Act; (g) its or their ability to shift supply or demand to other goods or services; and (h) the ability of the opposite market side to resort to other undertakings.
consumer_protection.plain: The Bank shall assess whether it holds a dominant position in a relevant market by considering: (a) its market share; (b) its financial strength; (c) its access to key supplies or distribution channels; (d) its affiliations or partnerships with other companies; (e) any legal or practical obstacles preventing competitors from entering the market; (f) the presence or likelihood of competitors, both local and international; (g) its flexibility in switching between different goods or services; and (h) whether customers can easily switch to alternative providers.

consumer_protection.title: False or Misleading Representations
consumer_protection.description: (2) For the purpose of this Act, the following types of representations shall be deemed to be made to the public by, and only by, the undertaking who caused it to be expressed, made or contained, that is to say, a representation that is— (a) expressed on goods or services offered or displayed for sale; (b) expressed on anything attached to, inserted in or accompanying goods offered or displayed for sale, their wrapper or container, or anything on which the goods are mounted for display or sale; (c) expressed on a display in the place where the goods or services are sold; (d) made in the course of selling goods or services to the ultimate consumer; or (e) contained in or on anything that is sold, sent, delivered, transmitted or in any other manner made available to a member of the public. (3) Where the undertaking referred to in subsection (2) is outside Nigeria, the representation shall be deemed to be made— (a) in a case described in subsection (2)(a), (b) or (e), by the undertaking that imported the goods or services; and (b) in the case described in subsection (2)(c), by the undertaking that imported the display into Nigeria.
consumer_protection.plain: The Bank shall ensure that all representations made to the public about its products or services are truthful, accurate, and not misleading in any way—regardless of how or where those representations are made.  The Bank shall ensure that no false or misleading claims appear:  1. On products or services offered or displayed for sale; 2. On packaging, labels, inserts, containers, or anything attached to or accompanying those products or services; 3. On displays located at the place where products or services are sold; 4. During sales interactions or communications with customers; 5. In any material (digital or physical) that is sold, delivered, sent, or otherwise made available to the public.  If such representations are created outside Nigeria, the Bank will be responsible as the importer if:  - They appear on products, packaging, or materials sent to the public (2(a), (b), or (e)); or - They appear on displays brought into Nigeria (2(c)).
