consumer_protection.title: Unfair Terms in Contracts
consumer_protection.description: (1) Any notice to consumers or potential consumers, or provision of a consumer agreement, which purports to— (a) limit in any way the risk or liability of an undertaking supplying goods or services or any other person, (b) constitute an assumption of risk or liability by the consumer, (c) impose an obligation on the consumer to indemnify an undertaking supplying goods or services or any other person for any cause, or (d) be an acknowledgement of any fact by the consumer, shall be drawn to the attention of the consumer in a conspicuous manner and form that is likely to attract the attention of an ordinarily alert consumer having regard to the circumstances. (2) Before the consumer enters into the transaction, or is required or expected to offer consideration for the transaction or agreement, the consumer shall be given adequate opportunity in the circumstances to receive and comprehend the provision or notice.

consumer_protection.source: Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Act (FCCPA), 2018
consumer_protection.title: Notice of Material Terms
consumer_protection.description: (1) An undertaking shall not make a transaction or agreement subject to any term or condition if— (a) its general purpose or effect is to defeat the purposes and policy of this Act, mislead or deceive the consumer, or subject a consumer to fraudulent conduct; (b) it directly or indirectly purports to— (i) waive or deprive a consumer of a right to return defective goods or any right set out in this Act, (ii) avoid the undertaking's obligation or duty under this Act, (iii) set aside or override the effect of any provision of this Act, (iv) authorise the undertaking to do anything that is unlawful under this Act, and (v) or fail to do anything that is required under this Act; (c) it purports to— (i) limit or exempt the undertaking from liability for any loss directly or indirectly attributable to the gross negligence of the undertaking or any person acting for or controlled by the undertaking, (ii) constitute an assumption of risk or liability by a consumer for the said loss, (iii) impose an obligation on a consumer to pay for damage, or (iv) otherwise assume the risk of handling any goods displayed by the supplier; (d) it falsely expresses an acknowledgment by the consumer that before an agreement was made, no representations or warranties were made in connection with the agreement by the undertaking or a person acting on behalf of the undertaking or the consumer has received goods or services, or a document that is required by this Act to be delivered to the consumer; and (e) it expresses an agreement by the consumer to— (i) deposit with the undertaking, or with any other person at the direction of the undertaking, an identity document, credit or debit card, bank account or automatic teller machine access card, or any similar identifying document or device, and (ii) provide a personal identification code or number to be used to access an account.
consumer_protection.plain: The Bank shall not include any term in a transaction or agreement that:  1. Undermines the purpose of the FCCPA, misleads or deceives the consumer, or allows for fraudulent conduct.  2. Tries to take away or reduce a consumer's legal rights, such as: a) The right to return defective goods. b) Any other right protected under the FCCPA. c) The bank’s obligations under the law.  3. Limits or avoids the bank’s liability, especially where: a) The loss is due to gross negligence by the bank or its agents. b) The customer is made to bear the risk or cost of that loss. c) The customer is made responsible for damages to displayed goods.  4. Falsely claims that: a) No promises or warranties were made by the bank. b) The customer received required goods, services, or documents when they didn’t.  5. Requires or implies agreement by the customer to: a) Deposit ID documents, bank cards, or access devices with the bank or a third party. b) Provide personal PINs or access codes.

consumer_protection.source: Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Act (FCCPA), 2018
consumer_protection.title: Prohibited Terms and Conditions
consumer_protection.description: When an undertaking agrees to perform any service for or on behalf of a consumer, the consumer has a right to— (a) the timely performance and completion of those services, and timely notice of any unavoidable delay in the performance of the services; (b) performance of the services in a manner and quality that reasonable persons are generally entitled to expect; (c) the use, delivery or installation of goods that are free of defects and of a quality that persons are generally entitled to expect, if the goods are required for the performance of the services; and (d) the return of any property or control over any property of the consumer in at least as good a condition as it was when the consumer made it available to the undertaking for the purpose of performing the services, having regard to the circumstances of the supply, and any specific criteria or conditions agreed between the undertaking and the consumer before or during the performance of the services. (2) Where an undertaking fails to perform a service to the standards contemplated in subsection (1), the consumer may require the undertaking to either— (a) remedy any defect in the quality of the services performed or goods supplied; or
consumer_protection.plain: The Bank shall:  1. Perform services for or on behalf of a consumer in a timely manner and notify the consumer promptly of any unavoidable delay.  2.  Ensure that services are performed with the level of quality and care that reasonable persons would generally expect.  3. Use, deliver, or install only defect-free goods of acceptable quality if such goods are necessary for providing the service.  4. Return any consumer’s property in at least as good condition as it was when received, considering the circumstances and any agreed criteria.  5. Where the Bank fails to meet the expected service standard, it must, upon consumer request, take steps to remedy any defect in the service or goods supplied.

consumer_protection.source: Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Act (FCCPA), 2018
consumer_protection.title: Quality and Safety of Services
consumer_protection.description: (1) Every consumer has a right to receive goods that— (a) are reasonably suitable for the purposes for which they are generally intended; (b) are of good quality, in good working order and free of defects; (c) will be useable and durable for a reasonable period of time, having regard to the use to which they would normally be put and to all the surrounding circumstances of their supply; and (d) comply with any applicable standards set by industry sector regulators. (2) In addition to the right set out in subsection (1), if a consumer has specifically informed an undertaking of the particular purpose for which the consumer wishes to acquire any goods, or the use to which the consumer intends to apply those goods, and the undertaking ordinarily offers to supply such goods or acts in a manner consistent with being knowledgeable about the use of those goods, the consumer has a right to expect that the goods are reasonably suitable for the specific purpose that the consumer has indicated.
consumer_protection.plain: The Bank shall:  1. Ensure that any product or service provided to customers (e.g., ATM cards, tokens, mobile apps, online banking platforms, POS terminals) is reasonably suitable for the general purpose for which it is intended.  2. Provide goods that are of good quality, in proper working condition, and free from defects.  3. Ensure that any device or product issued is durable and usable for a reasonable period of time, taking into account how the product is typically used and the context in which it was supplied.  4. Make sure all goods or products supplied to customers comply with relevant industry or regulatory standards, such as those set by the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN), Nigeria Inter-Bank Settlement System (NIBSS), or other sector regulators.  5. Where a customer informs the Bank of a specific purpose for which they are acquiring a product or service, ensure that the product or service is suitable for that specific purpose, especially where the Bank holds itself out as experienced or knowledgeable in providing such products or services.

consumer_protection.source: Industry Dispute Resolution System - Notification of Go-Live Date
consumer_protection.title: Circular -PSM/DIR/CON/OWO/048/071
consumer_protection.description: As part of the efforts to promote financial system stability, enhance consumer protection and further improve the reliability of the payments system, the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) has concluded the pilot phase of the Industry Dispute Resolution System (IDRS).  The IDRS is designed to provide a centralised dispute resolution and chargeback platform for ATM, web and POS channels for card-based transactions by banks and processors.  It will also complement existing efforts of the CBN Consumer Complaint Management System to track and resolve consumer complaints in a timely manner.
consumer_protection.plain: The Bank shall  integrate and actively use the Industry Dispute Resolution System (IDRS) for resolving consumer disputes and chargebacks related to ATM, web, and POS card transactions. The Bank shall also ensure timely updates and reporting of disputes in line with CBN directives
consumer_protection.riskDescription: Failure to adopt or properly use IDRS could lead to delays in dispute resolution, consumer dissatisfaction, loss of trust, and regulatory sanctions for non‑compliance with CBN directives.

abac.source: ECONOMIC AND FINANCIAL CRIMES COMMISSION (ESTABLISHMENT) ACT 2004
abac.title: Freezing Order on Banks or Other Financial Institutions
abac.description: (1) Notwithstanding anything contained in any other enactment or law, the Chairman of the Commission or any officer authorized by him may, if satisfied that the money in the account of a person is made through the commission of an offence under this Act or any enactments specified under section 6 (2) (a)-(f) of this Act, apply to the Court ex parte for power to issue or instruct a bank examiner or such other appropriate regulatory authority to issue an order as specified in Form B of the Schedule to this Act, addressed to the manager of the bank or any person in control of the financial institution where the account is or believed by him to be or the head office of the bank or other financial institution to freeze the account.  (2) The Chairman of the Commission, or any officer authorized by him may by an order issued under subsection (1) of this section, or by any subsequent order, direct the bank or other financial institution to supply any information and produce books and documents relating to the account and to stop all outward payments, operations or transactions (including any bill of exchange) in respect of the account of the arrested person.  (3) The manager or any other person in control of the financial institution shall take necessary steps to comply with the requirements of the order made pursuant to subsection (2) of this section.
abac.plain: The Bank shall, upon receipt of a valid EFCC freezing order:  1. Immediately freeze the specified account(s) and halt all outward payments, operations, or transactions, including any bills of exchange.  2. Provide the EFCC with all required account information, books, and documents.  3. Take all necessary steps to fully comply with the instructions contained in the order.
abac.deadlineType: Immediately upon receipt of EFCC order (no delay permissible).
abac.riskDescription: Failure to promptly comply may result in criminal liability, regulatory penalties, loss of license, or legal consequences for the bank and its officers.
abac.owner: - Branch Manager - Compliance Officer - Operations & Legal Department
abac.responsibility: - Branch Manager - Head of Compliance - Head of Legal - Chief Risk Officer
abac.primaryControl: - Internal escalation protocol for freezing orders. - Automated alert systems to flag EFCC directives. - Training for branch managers and key officers on EFCC compliance. - Maintain EFCC order compliance logs.

abac.title: Gratification by and through agents
abac.description: (1) Any person who corruptly—  (a) accepts, obtains or agrees to accept or obtain or attempts to obtain from any person for himself or for any other person, any gift or consideration as an inducement or reward for doing, forbearing to do, or for having done, or forborne to do, any act or thing, or  (b) gives or agrees to give or offers any gift or consideration to any agent as an inducement or reward for doing or forbearing to do, or for having done, or forborne to do, any act or thing in relation to his principal’s affairs or business, or  (c) knowingly gives to any agent, or being an agent knowingly uses with intent to deceive his principal, any receipt, account or other document in respect of which the principal is interested and which contains any statement which is false or erroneous or defective in any material particular, and which, to his knowledge, is intended to mislead his principal or any other person,  is guilty of an offence, and on conviction be liable to five (5) years imprisonment or a fine of not less than ₦200,000.00.  (2) For the purposes of this section:  “consideration” includes valuable consideration of any kind;  “agent” includes any person employed by or acting for another;  “principal” includes an employer.
abac.plain: The Bank shall ensure that no employee, officer, agent, or representative of the Bank shall—  (a) accept, obtain, agree to obtain, or attempt to obtain, for themselves or for any other person, any gift or consideration as an inducement or reward for performing, refraining from performing, or having performed or refrained from performing, any act or thing;  (b) give, agree to give, or offer any gift or consideration to any agent as an inducement or reward for performing, refraining from performing, or having performed or refrained from performing, any act or thing in relation to that agent’s principal’s affairs or business; or  (c) knowingly give to any agent—or, being an agent, knowingly use with intent to deceive the principal—any receipt, account, or other document concerning the principal’s interests that contains any false, erroneous, or materially defective statement intended to mislead the principal or any other person.  Any breach of this provision constitutes an offence punishable, upon conviction, by imprisonment for five (5) years or a fine of not less than ₦200,000.

abac.title: Bribery of public officers
abac.description: Any person who offers to any public officer, or being a public officer solicits, counsels or accepts any gratification as an inducement or a reward for:  (a) voting or abstaining from voting at any meeting of the public body in favour or against any measure, resolution or question submitted to the public body,  (b) performing or abstaining from performing or aiding in procuring, expediting, delaying, hindering or preventing the performance of any official act,  (c) aiding in procuring or preventing the passing of any vote or the granting of any contract, award, recognition or advantage in favour of any person, or  (d) showing or forbearing to show any favour or disfavour in his capacity as such officer is guilty of an offence. shall, notwithstanding that the officer did not have the power, right or opportunity so to do, or that the inducement or reward was not in relation to the affairs of the public body, is guilty of an offence and on conviction be liable to five (5) years imprisonment with hard labour.
abac.plain: The Bank shall ensure that no employee, officer, or representative of the Bank shall—  (a) offer to any public officer, or, being a public officer, solicit, counsel, or accept any gratification as an inducement or reward for:  - voting or abstaining from voting at any meeting of a public body in favour of or against any measure, resolution, or question submitted to that public body;  - performing or abstaining from performing, or aiding in procuring, expediting, delaying, hindering, or preventing the performance of any official act;  - aiding in procuring or preventing the passing of any vote or the granting of any contract, award, recognition, or advantage in favour of any person;  - showing or refraining from showing any favour or disfavour in their official capacity.  (b) engage in such acts even where the public officer did not have the power, right, or opportunity to carry them out, or where the inducement or reward was unrelated to the affairs of the public body.  Any breach of this provision constitutes an offence punishable, upon conviction, by imprisonment for five (5) years with hard labour.

abac.title: Bribery for giving assistance  et.c in regards to contracts
abac.description: Any person who, without lawful authority or reasonable excuse, offers an advantage to a public servant as an inducement to or reward for or otherwise on account of such public servant’s giving assistance or using influence in, or having given assistance or used influence in— (a) the promotion, executing, or procuring of—  (i) any contract with a public body for the performance of any work, the providing of any service, the doing of anything or the supplying of any article, material or substance, or  (ii) any subcontract to perform any work, provide any article, materials or substance required to be performed, provided, done or supplied under any contract with a public body, or (b) the payment of the price, consideration or other moneys stipulated or otherwise provided for in any such contract or sub-contract as aforesaid, is guilty of an offence.
abac.plain: The Bank shall ensure that no employee, officer, or representative of the Bank shall, without lawful authority or reasonable excuse, offer any advantage to a public servant as an inducement to, or reward for, or otherwise on account of such public servant—  (a) giving assistance or using influence in, or having given assistance or used influence in:  (i) the promotion, execution, or procurement of any contract with a public body for the performance of any work, the provision of any service, the doing of anything, or the supplying of any article, material, or substance; or  (ii) any subcontract to perform any work, provide any article, materials, or substance required to be performed, provided, done, or supplied under any such contract with a public body; or  (b) facilitating the payment of the price, consideration, or other moneys stipulated or otherwise provided for in any such contract or subcontract.  Any breach of this provision constitutes an offence.

abac.title: . Official corruption: person giving bribes, etc., on account of actions of public official
abac.description: (1) Any person who‐   (a)   corruptly gives, confers or procures any property or benefit of any kind to, on or for a  public official (as defined in section 98D) or to, on or for any other person; or   (b)   corruptly promises or offers to give or confer or to procure or attempt to procure any  property or benefit of any kind to, on or for a public official or to, on or for any other  person, on account of any such act, omission, favour or disfavour on the part of the public official as is mentioned in section 98 (1) (i) or (ii) of this Code, is guilty of the felony of official corruption and is liable to imprisonment for seven years.
abac.plain: The Bank shall ensure that neither it nor its employees, agents, or representatives give, offer, promise, or procure any money, gifts, or benefits to public officials (or to anyone else for the benefit of a public official) with the intent to influence the official’s actions or decisions. Such conduct is prohibited by law and can result in criminal penalties.
abac.riskDescription: Employees or agents may pay or promise bribes to public officials to obtain favourable acts or omissions, leading to criminal liability and reputational damage.
abac.primaryControl: Anti-bribery policy; employee code of conduct; regular training on corruption laws; whistleblowing hotline.
abac.additionalControl: Periodic due diligence on engagements with public officials; enhanced monitoring & auditing of transactions involving officials.

abac.title: Official corruption: person inviting bribes, etc., on account of actions of public official
abac.description: (1) Any person who‐   (a)   corruptly asks for, receives or obtains any property or benefit of any kind for himself or  any other person; or   (b)   corruptly agrees or attempts to receive or obtain any property or benefit of any kind for himself or any other person,  on account of‐   (i)    anything already done or omitted, or any favour or disfavour already shown to any person, by a public official (as defined in section 98D of this Code) in the discharge of his official duties or in relation to any matter connected with the functions, affairs or business of a government department, public body or other organisation or institution in which the public official is serving as such; or   (ii)    anything to be afterwards done or omitted, or any favour or disfavour to be afterwards shown to any person, by a public official in the discharge of his official duties or in relation to any such matter as aforesaid,  is guilty of the felony of official corruption and is liable to imprisonment for seven years.   (2) In any proceedings for an offence under this section it shall not be necessary to prove- (a) that any public official counselled the commission of the offence; or (b) that in the course of committing the offence the accused mentioned any particular public official; or (c) that (in a case to which subsection (1)(ii) is relevant) the accused believed that any public official would do, make or show the act, omission, favour or disfavour in question; or (d) that the accused intended to give the property or benefit in question, or any part thereof, to a public official.
abac.plain: The Bank shall ensure that no employee, officer, or representative of the Bank shall—  (a) corruptly ask for, receive, or obtain any property or benefit of any kind for themselves or for any other person; or (b) corruptly agree or attempt to receive or obtain any property or benefit of any kind for themselves or for any other person,  on account of—  (i) anything already done or omitted, or any favour or disfavour already shown to any person by a public official (as defined in Section 98D of this Code) in the discharge of official duties or in relation to any matter connected with the functions, affairs, or business of a government department, public body, or other organisation or institution in which the public official serves; or  (ii) anything to be afterwards done or omitted, or any favour or disfavour to be afterwards shown to any person by a public official in the discharge of official duties or in relation to such matters.  For the purpose of this provision, it is immaterial whether— i. any public official counselled the commission of the act; ii. any specific public official was mentioned; iii. the accused believed the public official would perform the act, omission, favour, or disfavour in question; or iv. the property or benefit in question, or any part thereof, was intended to be given to a public official.  Any breach of this provision constitutes official corruption and is liable to criminal prosecution and penalties, including imprisonment for up to seven years.
abac.riskDescription: Employees or agents might solicit or accept bribes or benefits linked to official acts, exposing the Bank to severe legal penalties and reputational damage.
abac.primaryControl: Anti-bribery policy; employee code of conduct; regular training on corruption laws; whistleblowing hotline.
abac.additionalControl: Gift and hospitality register; enhanced due diligence and monitoring of interactions with public officials.

points.text: The Bank shall ensure that no employee, officer, or representative of the Bank shall— (a) corruptly ask for, receive, or obtain any property or benefit of any kind for themselves or for any other person; or (b) corruptly agree or attempt to receive or obtain any property or benefit of any kind for themselves or for any other person, on account of— (i) anything already done or omitted, or any favour or disfavour already shown to any person by a public official (as defined in Section 98D of this Code) in the discharge of official duties or in relation to any matter connected with the functions, affairs, or business of a government department, public body, or other organisation or institution in which the public official serves; or (ii) anything to be afterwards done or omitted, or any favour or disfavour to be afterwards shown to any person by a public official in the discharge of official duties or in relation to such matters. For the purpose of this provision, it is immaterial whether— i. any public official counselled the commission of the act; ii. any specific public official was mentioned; iii. the accused believed the public official would perform the act, omission, favour, or disfavour in question; or iv. the property or benefit in question, or any part thereof, was intended to be given to a public official. Any breach of this provision constitutes official corruption and is liable to criminal prosecution and penalties, including imprisonment for up to seven years.

amlcft.title: Designated categories of predicate offences
amlcft.description: (1) Financial Institutions shall identify and file suspicious transaction reports to the NFIU, where funds, assets or property are suspected to have been derived from any, but not limited to, the following criminal activities— (a) participation in an organized criminal group and racketeering; (b) terrorism, including terrorism financing; (c) financing the proliferation of weapons of mass destruction; (d) trafficking in persons and migrant smugglings; (e) sexual exploitation, including sexual exploitation of children; (f) illicit trafficking in narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances; (g) illicit arms trafficking; (h) illicit trafficking in stolen and other goods; (i) corruption; (j) bribery; (k) fraud; (l) currency counterfeiting; (m) counterfeiting and piracy of products; (n) environmental crime; (o) murder; (p) grievous bodily injury; (q) kidnapping, illegal restraint and hostage-taking; (r) robbery or theft; (s) smuggling, including smuggling done in relation to customs and excise duties and taxes; (t) tax crimes, related to direct taxes and indirect taxes; (u) extortion; (v) forgery; (w) piracy; (y) insider trading and market manipulation; or (z) any other predicate offence under the MLPPA, TPPA, other relevant laws and regulations.
amlcft.plain: (1) The Bank  shall identify and file suspicious transaction reports to the NFIU, where funds, assets or property are suspected to have been derived from any, but not limited to, the following criminal activities— (a) participation in an organized criminal group and racketeering; (b) terrorism, including terrorism financing; (c) financing the proliferation of weapons of mass destruction; (d) trafficking in persons and migrant smugglings; (e) sexual exploitation, including sexual exploitation of children; (f) illicit trafficking in narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances; (g) illicit arms trafficking; (h) illicit trafficking in stolen and other goods; (i) corruption; (j) bribery; (k) fraud; (l) currency counterfeiting; (m) counterfeiting and piracy of products; (n) environmental crime; (o) murder; (p) grievous bodily injury; (q) kidnapping, illegal restraint and hostage-taking; (r) robbery or theft; (s) smuggling, including smuggling done in relation to customs and excise duties and taxes; (t) tax crimes, related to direct taxes and indirect taxes; (u) extortion; (v) forgery; (w) piracy; (y) insider trading and market manipulation; or (z) any other predicate offence under the MLPPA, TPPA, other relevant laws and regulations.
amlcft.deadlineType: Continuous (real-time monitoring and prompt reporting)
amlcft.riskDescription: Failure to detect or report suspicious transactions tied to predicate offences can expose the bank to regulatory sanctions, loss of license, reputational damage, or facilitation of serious crimes.
amlcft.owner: Compliance Department, AML/CFT Unit, Internal Audit, Transaction Monitoring Teams
amlcft.responsibility: Head of Compliance (overall), AML Compliance Officer (STR filing), IT Security (system alerts), Branch Managers (frontline awareness)
amlcft.primaryControl: Implement automated transaction monitoring systems and red flag indicators for each predicate offence category; train staff to recognize patterns and escalate promptly.
amlcft.additionalControl: Regular review of red flag indicators; quarterly audits of STR filings; maintain updated typology lists aligned with NFIU/Central Bank advisories.

amlcft.title: Targeted Financial Sanctions Related to Terrorism Financing and Proliferation Financing
amlcft.description: (1)  Financial Institutions shall undertake targeted financial sanctions in relation to TP and PF as provided for under TPPA and Regulations. (2) Financial Institutions shall report to the NFIU any assets frozen, or actions taken in compliance with— (a) the prohibition requirements of the relevant United Nations Security Council Resolutions ('UNSCRs') on terrorism, financing of proliferation of weapons of mass destruction, any future successor resolutions; and (b) the TPPA and Regulations and any amendments that may be reflected by the competent authorities. (3) The reports in sub-regulation (2) of this regulation shall include all transactions involving attempted and concluded transactions in compliance with the MLPPA, TPPA and Regulations and any amendments that may be reflected by the competent authorities.
amlcft.plain: The Bank shall: 1. Implement targeted financial sanctions related to terrorism financing (TF) and proliferation financing (PF) in line with the TPPA and applicable regulations. 2. Report to the NFIU any frozen assets or compliance actions taken under:  a. UN Security Council Resolutions (UNSCRs) on terrorism or proliferation of weapons of mass destruction.  b. TPPA, related regulations, and any amendments from competent authorities. 3. Include in such reports all related transactions—both attempted and completed—in line with TPPA, MLPPA, and applicable regulations.
amlcft.deadlineType: Ongoing; reporting within 24 hours of detection
amlcft.riskDescription: Non-compliance with targeted financial sanctions may expose the Bank to regulatory penalties and reputational damage.
amlcft.owner: Compliance Officer, AML/CFT/CPF Desk, Operations Head
amlcft.responsibility: Execution: Compliance Unit / Transaction Monitoring TeamReporting: Compliance Officer / MLROOversight: Internal Audit / Risk Management
amlcft.primaryControl: - Sanctions screening against designated lists - System-based flagging of attempted or completed suspicious transactions - Prompt asset freezing mechanisms - Timely reporting to NFIU
amlcft.additionalControl: - Real-time watchlist updates - Sanctions training for relevant staff - Periodic system audit to validate effectiveness of sanctions screening

amlcft.title: AML/CFT/CPF  Institutional Policy Framework
amlcft.description: (1) A Financial Institution shall— (a) adopt policies stating its commitment to comply with Anti-Money Laundering (‘AML’), Combating Financing of Terrorism (‘CFT’) and Countering Proliferation Financing of Weapons of Mass Destructions (‘CPF’) obligations under subsisting laws, regulations and regulatory directives and to actively prevent any transaction that otherwise facilitates criminal activities, Money Laundering, Terrorism Financing and Proliferation Financing (ML, TF and PF); (b) formulate and implement internal controls and other procedures to deter criminals from using its facilities for ML, TF and PF; (c) adopt a risk-based approach in the identification, assessment and management of their ML, TF and PF risks in line with the requirements of these Regulations; (d) comply promptly with requests made pursuant to AML, CFT and CPF legislations and provide information to the Central Bank of Nigeria (“CBN”), Nigeria Financial Intelligence Unit (“NFIU”) and other competent authorities; (e) not in any way inhibit the implementation of the provisions of these Regulations and shall co-operate with the regulators and law enforcement agencies in the implementation of a robust AML, CFT and CPF regime in Nigeria; (f) render statutory reports to competent authorities as required by law and shall guard against any act that will cause a customer or client to avoid compliance with AML, CFT and CPF Legislations; (g) identify, review and record other areas of potential ML, TF or PF risks not covered by these Regulations and report same to the CBN; (h) reflect AML, CFT and CPF policies and procedures in their strategic policies; (i) conduct on-going due diligence and where appropriate, enhanced due diligence on all business relationships and shall obtain information on the purpose and intended nature of the business relationship of their potential customers; and (j) ensure that their employees, agents and others doing business with them, clearly understand the AML, CFT and CPF programme.
amlcft.plain: The Bank shall: (a) Create a clear policy showing their full commitment to follow anti-money laundering (AML), terrorism financing (CFT), and proliferation financing (CPF) laws. (b) Set up internal systems to stop criminals from using the bank for illegal financial activities. (c) Use a risk-based method to find and manage money laundering, terrorism financing, and proliferation risks. (d) Respond quickly to information or data requests from CBN, NFIU, or other regulators. (e) Always cooperate with regulators and law enforcement and avoid doing anything that blocks AML/CFT/CPF work. (f) Send all reports required by law on time and do not help customers avoid AML/CFT/CPF checks. (g) Look out for new areas of risk and report them to the CBN if not already covered in the policy. (h) Make sure their AML/CFT/CPF policy is part of their overall business strategy. (i) Regularly check customer information and understand why the customer is opening or using an account. (j) Make sure that all staff, agents, and partners fully understand and follow the bank’s AML/CFT/CPF programme.
amlcft.deadlineType: Ongoing, with mandatory annual review or when laws/regulations change
amlcft.riskDescription: Inadequate oversight by the Board and senior management may result in weak AML/CFT/CPF governance, delayed policy implementation, poor regulatory reporting, and increased risk of non-compliance, enforcement actions, and reputational damage.
amlcft.owner: Board of Directors, Chief Compliance Officer (CCO), Heads of Business Units
amlcft.responsibility: Board of Directors (oversight), Chief Compliance Officer (implementation), All Staff (execution)
amlcft.primaryControl: - Develop and approve a clear AML/CFT/CPF policy - Train all employees on AML/CFT/CPF rules - Use risk-based KYC and transaction monitoring - Carry out internal AML risk assessments regularly - Monitor and update controls as needed
amlcft.additionalControl: - Perform independent AML audits- Use automated systems to detect suspicious activities- Regularly update policies based on new threats- Present AML/CFT reports to the board

amlcft.title: Formal board approval of the AML, CFT and CPF compliance
amlcft.description: (1) The ultimate responsibility for AML/CFT/CPF compliance is placed on the Board and top Management of every Financial Institution in Nigeria. (2) The Board of a Financial Institution shall ensure that a comprehensive operational AML/CFT/CPF Policy and Procedure is formulated by Management and presented to the Board for consideration and formal approval. (3) Copies of the approved AML/CFT/CPF Policy and Procedure referred to in sub-regulation (2) of this regulation shall be forwarded to the CBN and NFIU within six months of the release of these Regulations. (4) Monthly reports on the AML/CFT/CPF compliance status of a Financial Institution shall be presented to the Board by the CCO for its information and necessary action.
amlcft.plain: The Bank shall: (1) Ensure the Board of Directors and top management take full responsibility for compliance with AML, CFT, and CPF laws. (2) Ensure management prepares a full AML/CFT/CPF policy and procedure, and presents it to the Board for review and official approval. (3) Send  copies of the AML/CFT/CPF policy and procedure to the NFIU  and CBN. (4) Ensure the Chief Compliance Officer (CCO) presents monthly reports on AML/CFT/CPF compliance status to the Board for review and follow-up action.
amlcft.deadlineType: Within 6 months of the regulation’s release – for submission to NFIUMonthly – for compliance reporting to the BoardOngoing – for policy review and oversight
amlcft.riskDescription: Lack of Board involvement can lead to weak compliance culture, poor oversight, delayed responses to AML/CFT/CPF threats, regulatory sanctions, or financial crimes going undetected.
amlcft.owner: Board of Directors, Managing Director/CEO, Chief Compliance Officer
amlcft.responsibility: Policy approval & oversight – Board of DirectorsPolicy formulation & updates – Senior ManagementReporting – Chief Compliance Officer (CCO)
amlcft.primaryControl: - Assign Board-level ownership of AML/CFT/CPF compliance - Develop and document a robust policy and procedures - Approve the policy through formal Board resolution - Submit policy topics to the NFIU within 6 months - Mandate the CCO to submit monthly reports to the Board
amlcft.additionalControl: - Create a Board Compliance Committee - Include AML/CFT/CPF updates as a permanent item in Board meetings - Use dashboards or scorecards to track compliance KPIs - Conduct independent reviews of policy adequacy

amlcft.title: Comprehensive AML/CFT/CPF Compliance Programme
amlcft.description: Financial Institutions shall have a comprehensive AML/CFT/CPF— compliance programme to guide its efforts, ensure diligent implementation of its programme, entrench in the institution a culture of compliance to minimize the risks of being used to launder the proceeds of crime, or the funding of terrorism and proliferation of weapons of mass destruction and provide protection against fraud, reputational and financial risks.
amlcft.plain: The Bank shall establish and maintain a comprehensive AML/CFT/CPF compliance programme. This programme should: - Guide all AML/CFT/CPF efforts; - Ensure proper implementation of compliance obligations; - Build a strong internal culture of compliance; - Minimize the risk of being used for money laundering, terrorism financing, or proliferation financing; - Provide protection against fraud, reputational harm, and financial losses.
amlcft.deadlineType: Immediate and ongoing
amlcft.riskDescription: Without a comprehensive compliance programme, the institution may be exposed to significant legal, financial, reputational, and operational risks stemming from non-compliance or involvement in illicit activities.
amlcft.owner: Board of Directors, Executive Management, Chief Compliance Officer
amlcft.responsibility: Development & Oversight: Board of Directors / Executive ManagementImplementation & Review: Chief Compliance Officer
amlcft.primaryControl: - Develop and document AML/CFT/CPF policies and procedures - Integrate compliance into strategic and operational plans - Regularly review and update the programme - Ensure institution-wide awareness and commitment
amlcft.additionalControl: - Independent audit of the compliance programme - Annual board review and approval of the programme - Benchmarking against industry best practices - Mandatory training and awareness campaigns

amlcft.title: Risk Assessment
amlcft.description: Financial Institutions shall— (a) take appropriate steps to identify, assess and understand its ML, TF and PF risks for customers, countries or geographic areas of its operations, products, services and delivery channels; (b) document its risk assessments profile; (c) consider all relevant risk factors before determining the overall level of risk and the appropriate level and type of mitigation to be applied; (d) keep the risk assessments up to date; and (e) have the appropriate mechanisms to provide risk assessments reports periodically.
amlcft.plain: The Bank shall: (a) Identify, assess, and understand the risks of money laundering (ML), terrorism financing (TF), and proliferation financing (PF) across their customers, products, services, delivery channels, and locations. (b) Keep written documentation of all their risk assessments. (c) Consider all important risk factors before deciding how risky a relationship, transaction, or service is and how best to reduce that risk. (d) Review and update their risk assessments regularly. (e) Put systems in place to prepare and submit risk assessment reports from time to time.
amlcft.deadlineType: Initial risk assessment – at onboarding or product launchReview – annually or when significant changes occurReporting – periodically (e.g., quarterly or semi-annually)
amlcft.riskDescription: Poor risk assessment can lead to unmitigated exposure to ML/TF/PF threats, resulting in regulatory sanctions, financial loss, reputational damage, or being used as a channel for financial crime.
amlcft.owner: Chief Risk Officer (CRO), Chief Compliance Officer (CCO), Heads of Business Units
amlcft.responsibility: Execution – Risk & Compliance DepartmentsApproval – Executive ManagementOversight – Board Risk Committee
amlcft.primaryControl: - Conduct enterprise-wide AML/CFT/CPF risk assessments - Use a structured framework to assess risks by customer type, geography, products, and channels - Maintain detailed records of all risk assessments - Establish a periodic review schedule (e.g., annually) - Ensure management reviews and signs off on risk reports
amlcft.additionalControl: - Deploy automated risk assessment tools - Integrate risk scoring into customer onboarding and periodic review - Conduct independent review of the risk assessment framework - Benchmark risk ratings against industry trends and typologies

amlcft.title: Risk Mitigation
amlcft.description: Financial Institutions shall— (a) have policies, controls and procedures which are approved by its board of directors to enable it manage and mitigate the risks that have been identified (either by the CBN and other competent authorities or by the financial institution); (b) monitor the implementation of the controls and enhance them where necessary; and (c) apply enhanced measures to manage and mitigate the risks where higher risks are identified.
amlcft.plain: The Bank shall:  (a) Create and implement risk management policies, controls, and procedures approved by the Board to manage and reduce AML, CFT, and CPF risks identified by the bank or by regulators. (b) Continuously monitor how well the controls are working and improve them when needed. (c) Apply stronger (enhanced) controls in situations where there are higher risks, such as high-risk customers, products, or countries.
amlcft.deadlineType: Initial implementation – upon identification of risksOngoing monitoring and improvement – continuousEDD – whenever high-risk cases are detected
amlcft.riskDescription: Failure to implement and maintain effective AML/CFT/CPF risk management controls may result in undetected high-risk exposures, regulatory breaches, and increased vulnerability to financial crime.
amlcft.owner: Board of Directors, Chief Compliance Officer (CCO), Chief Risk Officer (CRO), Heads of Departments
amlcft.responsibility: Policy Approval – Board of DirectorsPolicy Design & Implementation – Risk & Compliance DepartmentsControl Monitoring – Internal Audit / Compliance Review Units
amlcft.primaryControl: - Approve AML/CFT/CPF mitigation policies at Board level - Design controls linked to specific risks (e.g., customer type, delivery channel) - Monitor performance of controls via internal audit or compliance reviews - Use a risk-rating model to trigger enhanced due diligence (EDD) for high-risk cases
amlcft.additionalControl: - Deploy automated risk monitoring tools - Link high-risk triggers to real-time alerts - Perform stress testing of risk mitigation controls - Engage external consultants to review risk frameworks periodically

amlcft.title: Designation and duties of compliance officer
amlcft.description: (1) Financial Institutions shall designate a Chief Compliance Officer with the relevant competence, authority and independence to implement the institution’s AML, CFT and CPF compliance programme. (2) The CCO shall be appointed at management level and shall be responsible for— (a) developing an AML/CFT/CPF Compliance Programme; (b) receiving and vetting suspicious transaction reports ('STRs') from staff; (c) filing STRs with the NFIU; (d) filing other regulatory returns with the CBN and other relevant regulatory and supervisory authorities; (e) rendering "nil" reports to the CBN and NFIU, where necessary to ensure compliance; (f) ensuring that the financial institution’s compliance programme is implemented; (g) coordinating the training of board, management and staff in AML, CFT and CPF awareness, detection methods and reporting requirements; and (h) serving both as a liaison officer between his institution, the CBN and NFIU and a point-of-contact for all employees on issues relating to ML, TF and PF.
amlcft.plain: The bank shall: (1) Designate a Chief Compliance Officer (CCO) with the required competence, independence, and authority to implement the AML/CFT/CPF programme. (2) Appoint the CCO at management level, who shall be responsible for: (a) Developing an AML/CFT/CPF compliance programme. (b) Receiving and vetting Suspicious Transaction Reports (STRs) from staff. (c) Filing STRs with the NFIU. (d) Filing other regulatory returns with CBN and relevant authorities. (e) Submitting nil reports when applicable. (f) Ensuring the compliance programme is properly implemented. (g) Coordinating AML/CFT/CPF training for board, management, and staff. (h) Acting as liaison between the institution, CBN, NFIU, and as point-of-contact for all staff on ML, TF, and PF issues.
amlcft.deadlineType: Within 7 days of the transaction
amlcft.riskDescription: Without a competent and independent CCO, the institution may fail to detect or report money laundering, terrorism financing, or proliferation financing risks, leading to serious legal and reputational consequences.
amlcft.owner: Board of Directors, Executive Management, Compliance Department
amlcft.responsibility: Triggering & Initial Review: Front Office, Operations TeamFinal Filing & Reporting: AML/CFT Compliance OfficerOversight: Head of Compliance / Internal Control
amlcft.primaryControl: - Appointment of qualified CCO at management level - Defined job description with clear reporting lines - STR reporting protocols - Scheduled training and regulatory filing calendar - Formal liaison procedures with regulators
amlcft.additionalControl: - Annual CCO performance review by the board - Internal audit checks on reporting duties - Training effectiveness assessments - Board-approved compliance policy with CCO responsibilities outlined
