amlcft.title: Internal controls, compliance and audit
amlcft.description: (1) Financial Institutions shall establish and maintain internal procedures, policies and controls to prevent ML, TF and PF, which have regard to their ML or TF risks and the size of the business and communicate these to their employees. (2) The procedures, policies and controls established by Financial Institutions shall cover operational matters including the CDD, record retention, detection of unusual and suspicious transactions and the reporting obligations. (3) The Compliance Officer and appropriate staff are to have timely access to CDD information, account and transaction records, including information and all analysis of transactions and activities and other relevant information. (4) Financial Institutions are accordingly required to develop programmes against ML, TF and PF, such as— (a) the development of internal policies, procedures and controls, including appropriate compliance management arrangement and adequate screening procedures to ensure high standards when hiring employees; (b) on-going employee training programmes to ensure that employees are kept informed of new developments, including information on current ML, TF and PF techniques, methods and trends; (c) providing clear explanation of all aspects of AML, CFT and CPF laws and obligations, and in particular, requirements concerning CDD and suspicious transaction reporting; and (d) adequately resourced and independent audit function to test compliance with the procedures, policies and controls. (5) Financial groups shall implement group-wide programmes against ML, TF and PF, applicable and appropriate to all branches and majority-owned subsidiaries of the group, including the measures as set out in sub-regulation (4), of this Regulations and— (a) policies and procedures for sharing information required for the purposes of CDD and ML, TF and PF risk management; (b) the provision at group-level, audit and AML, CFT and CPF functions of the information as included in sub-regulation (3) of this regulation from branches and subsidiaries when necessary for AML, CFT and CPF purposes; provided that branches and subsidiaries should receive such information from these group-level functions when relevant and appropriate to risk management; and (c) adequate safeguards on the confidentiality and use of information exchange, including safeguards to prevent tipping-off. (6) Financial Institutions shall put in place a structure that ensures the operational independence of the CCO and Compliance Officers.
amlcft.plain: The Bank shall: (1) Set up and maintain internal AML/CFT/CPF policies and controls, based on their risk level and business size, and share them with staff. (2) These controls must cover key areas like customer due diligence (CDD), recordkeeping, detecting suspicious transactions, and reporting obligations. (3) Ensure the Compliance Officer and staff have timely access to customer data, transaction records, and analysis reports. (4) Build a strong AML/CFT/CPF programme that includes: (a) Internal policies, controls, and staff screening procedures. (b) Regular staff training on emerging ML/TF/PF risks and methods. (c) Clear explanation of legal duties, especially CDD and reporting. (d) Independent, well-funded audit function to check compliance. (5) Financial groups must apply these programmes across all branches and major subsidiaries, including: (a) Policies for sharing CDD and AML-related information within the group. (b) Group-level AML teams must receive and provide info to/from branches/subsidiaries when needed. (c) Ensure shared information is kept confidential and protected from misuse or tipping-off. (6) Ensure the CCO and other Compliance Officers are operationally independent.
amlcft.deadlineType: Ongoing – Internal control implementation and compliance structureQuarterly or Annually – Internal audit reviewImmediately – Independence of CCO
amlcft.riskDescription: Weak internal controls or limited compliance independence can lead to failure in detecting financial crimes, poor regulatory reporting, and potential legal and reputational damage.
amlcft.owner: Board of Directors, Managing Director/CEO, Chief Compliance Officer, Internal Audit
amlcft.responsibility: Oversight & Approval – Board of DirectorsImplementation – CCO, Compliance Team, Internal AuditTraining & Operations – HR, Risk & Compliance Functions
amlcft.primaryControl: - Approve and implement AML/CFT/CPF procedures and controls - Ensure regular staff training - Enable full access to records for compliance team - Assign independent audit and compliance functions - Implement group-wide AML policies and data-sharing protocols
amlcft.additionalControl: - Annual independent audit of AML/CFT systems - Risk-based testing of branches and business lines - Compliance reporting lines directly to Board or Board committee - Secure internal communication tools for AML-related info sharing

amlcft.title: Testing for the adequacy of the AML, CFT and CPF compliance programme
amlcft.description: (1) Financial Institutions shall subject its AML, CFT and CPF Compliance Programme to independent-testing or require its internal audit function to determine the adequacy, completeness and effectiveness of the programme. (2) Report of compliance by Financial Institutions shall be rendered to the CBN by 31st December of every financial year and any identified weaknesses or inadequacies promptly addressed by the Financial Institutions.
amlcft.plain: The Bank shall: (1) Regularly test their AML/CFT/CPF compliance programme to confirm it is complete and working. This must be done by internal audit or an independent reviewer. (2) Submit a compliance report to the CBN by 31st December each year, and quickly fix any problems found.
amlcft.deadlineType: Annual compliance testing – each financial yearCBN report submission – by 31st DecemberRemediation – as soon as weaknesses are identified
amlcft.riskDescription: If the AML/CFT/CPF programme is not tested, gaps may go unnoticed, leading to poor controls, regulatory breaches, and exposure to financial crime.
amlcft.owner: Internal Audit, Chief Compliance Officer (CCO), Board Audit/Compliance Committee
amlcft.responsibility: Testing – Internal Audit / External ReviewerReporting – Chief Compliance OfficerOversight – Board Audit/Compliance Committee
amlcft.primaryControl: - Schedule annual AML/CFT/CPF compliance tests - Use qualified internal auditors or independent professionals - Review all policy areas including STR filing, CDD, risk assessments - Document findings and remediation actions
amlcft.additionalControl: - Engage third-party compliance consultants for deeper review - Include testing outcomes in board reports - track correction of deficiencies via a compliance action log

amlcft.title: Prohibition of numbered or anonymous accounts, accounts in fictitious names and shell banks
amlcft.description: (1) Financial Institutions shall not keep anonymous accounts or accounts in fictitious names. (2) Financial Institutions shall not establish or continue correspondent relationships with shell banks with no physical presence in any country or with correspondent banks that permit their accounts to be used by such banks. (3) Shell banks are prohibited from operating in Nigeria as provided in MLPPA. (4) Financial Institutions shall take all necessary measures to satisfy itself that respondent Financial Institutions in a foreign country do not permit their accounts to be used by shell banks.
amlcft.plain: The Bank shall: (1) Not open or operate accounts that are anonymous, in fake names, or without proper identification. (2) Not start or keep correspondent banking relationships with shell banks (banks with no physical offices anywhere). (3) Not allow any shell bank to operate in Nigeria. (4) Confirm that foreign partner banks (respondent institutions) do not allow shell banks to use their accounts.
amlcft.deadlineType: Immediately – for existing accounts and relationshipsOngoing – during onboarding and periodic due diligence reviews
amlcft.riskDescription: Allowing anonymous or shell bank-related accounts increases the risk of money laundering and terrorism financing, and could lead to severe regulatory sanctions or loss of correspondent banking relationships.
amlcft.owner: Chief Compliance Officer (CCO), Head of Operations, Relationship Managers
amlcft.responsibility: Policy & Oversight – Board and CCOExecution – Operations, Legal, Relationship Management TeamsVerification – Internal Audit / Compliance Review
amlcft.primaryControl: - Enforce strict customer identification (KYC) before opening any account - Screen and assess all correspondent banking relationships - Include shell bank checks in due diligence process - Monitor account usage for unusual patterns linked to shell banks
amlcft.additionalControl: - Include shell bank risk in the AML risk assessment model - Use automated tools to flag anonymous or incomplete account details - Obtain written confirmation from correspondent banks that they do not deal with shell banks

amlcft.title: Foreign branches and subsidiaries
amlcft.description: (1) Financial Institutions shall ensure that foreign branches and subsidiaries observe AML, CFT and CPF measures consistent with the provisions of these Regulations and apply the measures to the extent that the local or host country’s laws and Regulations permit. (2) Financial Institutions shall ensure that the principle referred to in sub-regulation (1) of this regulation is observed by their branches and subsidiaries in countries which do not or insufficiently apply the requirements of these Regulations. (3) Where the minimum AML, CFT and CPF requirements contained in these Regulations and those of the host country differ, branches and subsidiaries of Nigerian Financial Institutions in the host country shall apply the higher standard provided in these Regulations and such standards shall be applied to the extent that the host country’s laws, regulations or other measures permit. (4) Financial Institutions shall inform the CBN in writing when their foreign branches or subsidiaries are unable to observe the appropriate AML, CFT and CPF measures where they are prohibited to observe such measures by the host country’s laws, regulations or other measures. (5) Financial Institutions shall subject to the AML, CFT and CPF principles contained in these Regulations, apply consistently the CDD measures at their group levels, taking into consideration the activity of the customer with the various branches and subsidiaries.
amlcft.plain: The Bank shall: (1) Make sure all foreign branches and subsidiaries follow AML/CFT/CPF rules similar to Nigeria’s regulations, as much as the host country allows. (2) Apply this principle even in countries with weak or no AML/CFT/CPF standards. (3) If Nigerian and host country rules are different, apply the stricter (higher) standard where legally possible. (4) Notify the CBN in writing if any foreign branch or subsidiary is legally restricted from applying Nigeria’s AML/CFT/CPF rules. (5) Apply customer due diligence (CDD) measures consistently across all group branches and subsidiaries, considering the customer’s activities across the group.
amlcft.deadlineType: Immediately – Implement higher standards where possibleOngoing – Ensure regular CDD and group-level complianceAs required – Report any host country restriction to CBN
amlcft.riskDescription: Inconsistent AML/CFT practices across foreign branches can expose the bank to cross-border regulatory violations, ML/TF risks, and damage to the bank’s international reputation.
amlcft.owner: Chief Compliance Officer, Group Compliance Head, Country Heads, Board Risk/Compliance Committee
amlcft.responsibility: Policy Direction – Board & Group Risk CommitteeImplementation – Group Compliance, Foreign Subsidiary ManagementReporting – Chief Compliance Officer to CBN
amlcft.primaryControl: - Develop group-wide AML/CFT/CPF standards aligned with Nigerian regulations - Require all foreign branches to conduct risk-based CDD - Review local legal restrictions and escalate where conflicts arise - Document and track compliance status of all foreign entities - Establish reporting lines from foreign branches to head office compliance
amlcft.additionalControl: - Conduct periodic reviews or audits of foreign branches - Include foreign subsidiaries in group compliance dashboards - Train foreign staff on Nigerian AML/CFT expectations - Use centralized CDD systems for global customer profiling

amlcft.title: Co-operation with competent authorities
amlcft.description: (1) Financial Institutions shall promptly comply with all the requests made pursuant to the provisions of relevant AML, CFT and CPF laws and regulations and provide all requested information to the CBN and other competent authorities. (2) Financial Institutions’s procedures for responding to authorized requests for information on ML, TF and PF shall meet the following— (a) searching immediately the financial institution’s records to determine whether it maintains or has maintained any account for, or has engaged in any transaction with any individual, entity or organization named in the request; (b) reporting promptly to the requesting authority the outcome of the search; and (c) protecting the security and confidentiality of such requests.
amlcft.plain: The Bank shall: (1) Respond quickly and completely to any request for information from the CBN, NFIU, or other authorized agencies under AML, CFT, and CPF laws. (2) Have clear procedures in place to: (a) Immediately search their records to check if they have or had any dealings (accounts or transactions) with a person or entity named in an official request. (b) Quickly report the findings of the search to the authority that made the request. (c) Keep all such requests and responses secure and confidential.
amlcft.deadlineType: Immediately – upon receipt of a requestOngoing – ensure process readiness and staff awareness
amlcft.riskDescription: Failure to cooperate or delay in responding to regulatory requests may lead to penalties, regulatory distrust, reputational damage, or failure to prevent financial crimes.
amlcft.owner: Chief Compliance Officer (CCO), Legal Department, IT/Data Management Team
amlcft.responsibility: Execution – Compliance Officer, Legal & IT TeamOversight – Board Compliance CommitteeReporting – CCO to CBN or relevant authority
amlcft.primaryControl: - Set up a documented procedure for handling information requests - Designate officers responsible for receiving and responding to requests - Maintain searchable customer and transaction databases - Log all requests and responses securely - Regularly train staff on confidentiality and cooperation requirements
amlcft.additionalControl: - Test response procedures through mock drills - Implement escalation procedures for high-risk or urgent requests - Use encryption and Secure platforms for communication - Conduct regular audits of request-handling compliance

amlcft.title: Customer Due Diligence (‘CDD’) measures
amlcft.description: (1) Financial Institutions shall undertake Customer Due Diligence (‘CDD’) measures when— (a) business relationships are established; (b) carrying out occasional transactions above the applicable and designated threshold of US$1,000 or its equivalent in other currencies or as may be determined by the CBN from time to time, including where the transaction is carried out in a single operation or several operations that appear to be linked; (c) carrying out occasional transactions that are wire transfers, including cross-border and domestic transfers between Financial Institutions and when credit or debit cards are used as a payment method to effect money transfer; (d) there is a suspicion of ML, TF and PF regardless of any exemptions or any other thresholds referred to in these Regulations; or (e) there are doubts on the veracity or adequacy of previously obtained customer identification data. (2) The measures in paragraphs (a), (b) and (c) of sub-regulation (1) of this regulation, shall not apply to payments in respect of— (a) any transfer flowing from a transaction carried out using a credit or debit card so long as the credit or debit card number accompanying such transfers flow from the transactions such as withdrawals from a bank account through an ATM machine, cash advances from a credit card or payment for goods; and (b) Inter-financial institution transfers and settlements where both the originator-person and the beneficial-person are Financial Institutions acting on their own behalf. (3) Financial Institutions are not required to repeatedly perform identification and verification exercise every time a customer conducts a transaction except there is a suspicion that the previously obtained information is not complete or has changed.
amlcft.plain: The Bank shall: (1) Perform CDD (i.e., verify customer identity and gather key info) when: (a) A business relationship is being opened. (b) A one-time or related set of transactions is over US$1,000 or its equivalent. (c) Any wire transfer is being done (domestic or cross-border), especially using cards for fund transfer. (d) There is any suspicion of money laundering, terrorism or proliferation financing — even if the transaction is small or exempt. (e) There are doubts about the accuracy or completeness of earlier customer identity info. (2) CDD is not required when: (a) The transaction is clearly a normal use of a card (e.g. ATM withdrawal, card payment for goods). (b) The transfer is between financial institutions acting on their own behalf. (3)The bank  does not need to repeat CDD for every transaction unless the customer’s info is suspected to be wrong or outdated.
amlcft.deadlineType: Immediately – for all new relationships and qualifying transactionsOngoing – update when suspicion or data doubts arise
amlcft.riskDescription: Failure to perform proper CDD can expose the bank to customer impersonation, undetected ML/TF/PF activities, regulatory penalties, and reputational damage.
amlcft.owner: Relationship Managers, Operations Staff, Chief Compliance Officer (CCO), Front Desk/Teller Teams
amlcft.responsibility: Execution – Account Officers, Operations, ComplianceOversight – Chief Compliance OfficerMonitoring – Internal Audit, CBN Examiners
amlcft.primaryControl: - Implement CDD checklists at onboarding and for high-value or suspicious transactions - Configure core banking system to flag qualifying transactions - Train staff to recognize suspicious activity triggers - Review and update customer info periodically - Automate card/payment monitoring exclusions based on CBN exemptions
amlcft.additionalControl: - Integrate CDD with real-time transaction monitoring tools - Apply tiered CDD based on customer risk rating - Use alerts for missing or outdated customer info - Conduct periodic quality assurance reviews on KYC files

amlcft.title: Identification and verification of customers
amlcft.description: (1) Financial Institutions shall identify customers, whether permanent or occasional, natural or legal persons, or legal arrangements, and verify the customers’ identities using reliable, independently sourced documents, data or information. (2) Financial Institutions shall carry out the full range of the CDD measures contained in these Regulations, the relevant provisions of the MLPPA and any other relevant laws or regulations. (3) Financial Institutions shall apply the CDD measures on a risk-sensitive basis. (4) Types of customer information to be obtained and identification data to be used to verify the information shall be as provided by the CBN from time to time. (5) Financial Institutions shall determine whether any person purporting to act on behalf of the customer is so authorized, and identify and verify the identity of that person. (6) Where the customer is a legal person or a legal arrangement, the Financial Institution shall identify and verify its identity through the following information— (a) the name and the legal status of the legal person or legal arrangement by obtaining proof of incorporation from the Corporate Affairs Commission ('CAC') or similar evidence of establishment or existence and any other relevant information; (b) the powers that regulate and bind the legal persons or arrangement; (c) the names of the relevant persons holding senior management positions in the legal persons or arrangement; and (d) the address of the registered office, and if different, a principal place of business.
amlcft.plain: The Bank shall: (1) Identify and verify all customers (whether regular or one-time, individuals, companies, or legal structures) using trusted documents or data from independent sources. (2) Apply all required CDD steps in line with these Regulations, MLPPA, and other laws. (3) Apply CDD based on the risk level of the customer or transaction. (4) Follow CBN’s guidance on the types of customer info and verification documents to use. (5) Confirm if a person acting on behalf of a customer is truly authorized, and verify that person’s identity. (6) For companies or legal entities, obtain and verify: (a) Proof of legal status (e.g. CAC documents); (b) Rules or documents that govern the entity’s powers; (c) Names of top managers or controllers; (d) Registered and main business addresses.
amlcft.deadlineType: Immediately – during onboardingOngoing – for updates, changes in control, or re-verification triggers
amlcft.riskDescription: If customers are not properly identified and verified, the bank may unknowingly serve criminals or sanctioned entities, leading to serious regulatory and reputational consequences.
amlcft.owner: Relationship Managers, Account Officers, KYC Team, Compliance Officer
amlcft.responsibility: Execution – KYC Unit, Account Officers, ComplianceOversight – Chief Compliance Officer (CCO), Internal Audit
amlcft.primaryControl: - Collect and verify customer ID with government-issued documents - Obtain CAC documents and board resolutions for companies - Maintain updated KYC templates with CBN-prescribed data - Verify that agents or representatives have valid authority (e.g. POA or mandate) - Apply additional checks for high-risk customers or complex legal entities
amlcft.additionalControl: - Use electronic KYC (e-KYC) tools for faster and more reliable validation - Conduct ongoing monitoring for KYC data consistency - Use facial/biometric ID validation where possible - Maintain an internal checklist of high-risk customer types/entities

amlcft.title: Verification of beneficial ownership
amlcft.description: (1) Financial Institutions shall— (a) understand the nature of the customer's business, its ownership and control structure including board and senior management; (b) identify and take reasonable steps to verify the identity of a beneficial-owner, using relevant information or data obtained from reliable sources to satisfy itself that it knows who the beneficial owner is through methods including— (i) for legal persons— (a) identifying and verifying the natural persons, where they exist, that have ultimate controlling ownership interest in a legal person, taking into cognizance the fact that ownership interests can be so diversified that there may be no natural persons, whether acting alone or with others, exercising control of the legal person or arrangement through ownership; (b) to the extent that there is doubt under sub-paragraph (i) of this paragraph that the persons with the controlling ownership interest are the beneficial owners or where no natural person exerts control through ownership interests, identify and verify the natural persons, where they exist, exercising control of the legal person or arrangement through other means; and (c) where a natural person is not identified under sub-paragraph (i) or (ii) of this paragraph, Financial Institutions shall identify and take reasonable measures to verify the identity of the relevant natural person who holds senior management position in the legal person; (ii) for legal arrangements such as trust arrangement, Financial Institutions shall identify and verify the identity of the settlor, the trustee, the protector where they exist, the beneficiaries or class of beneficiaries, and any other natural person exercising ultimate or effective control over the trust including through a chain of control or ownership; and (iii) for other types of legal arrangements, the Financial Institutions shall identify and verify persons in equivalent or similar positions.
amlcft.plain: The Bank shall: (1a) Understand the customer's business, including its ownership, board, and senior management structure. (1b) Identify and verify who the beneficial owner is — the real person(s) who ultimately owns or controls the customer. This includes: (i) For companies: • Identify natural persons with significant ownership or control. • If no such person is clearly found, identify those who control the company in other ways. • If no individual can be identified, verify the identity of someone in senior management. (ii) For trusts and similar legal arrangements: • Identify and verify the settlor, trustee, protector (if any), beneficiaries (or class of beneficiaries), and anyone with ultimate control. (iii) For other legal setups: • Identify and verify persons who play equivalent key roles.
amlcft.deadlineType: Immediately – at onboarding of any legal entity or trustOngoing – when changes occur in ownership or control
amlcft.riskDescription: Failure to identify and verify beneficial owners allows criminals to hide behind legal entities or trusts, exposing the bank to financial crime and regulatory breaches.
amlcft.owner: Relationship Managers, KYC Officers, Compliance Officers, Legal & Corporate Services
amlcft.responsibility: Execution – KYC/Onboarding Team, Relationship OfficersOversight – Compliance Officer, Legal Unit
amlcft.primaryControl: - Require full ownership and control documentation at onboarding - Use CBN-prescribed beneficial ownership forms - Cross-check names against sanctions lists and watchlists - Update beneficial ownership info regularly - Require organizational charts for complex structures
amlcft.additionalControl: - Use digital beneficial ownership registries (e.g., CAC BO portal) - Implement enhanced due diligence for high-risk entities or jurisdictions - Require declarations under oath for opaque or layered ownership structures - Perform media and database checks for red flags in ownership trails

amlcft.title: Timing of Verification
amlcft.description: (1) Financial Institutions shall obtain and verify the identity of the customer, beneficial-owner and occasional customers before or during the course of establishing a business relationship or conducting transactions for them. (2) Financial Institutions are permitted to complete the verification of the identity of the customer and beneficial owner following the establishment of the business relationship, only where— (a) this can be done within 48 hours; (b) it is essential not to interrupt the normal business conduct of the customer in cases of non-face-to-face business; or (c) the money laundering risks can be effectively managed. (3) Where a customer is permitted to utilize the business relationship prior to verification, Financial Institutions shall adopt risk management procedures relevant to the conditions under which this may occur. (4) The procedures contemplated under sub-regulation (3) of this regulation shall include a set of measures such as— (a) limitation of the number, types or amount of transactions that may be performed; and (b) the monitoring of large or complex transactions being carried out outside the expected norms for that type of relationship.
amlcft.plain: The Bank shall: (1) Verify the identity of the customer and beneficial owner before or during account opening or conducting transactions. (2) Verification can be completed after onboarding only if: • It is done within 48 hours; • It’s necessary to avoid disrupting the customer's normal business (especially online or non-face-to-face cases); • ML/TF risks are low and well-managed. (3) If a customer starts using an account before full verification, the bank must put risk controls in place. (4) These controls must include: • Setting limits on transaction types, volume, or amount; • Monitoring large or unusual transactions that don’t fit the customer’s profile.
amlcft.deadlineType: Immediately – for all onboarding casesWithin 48 hours – if post-onboarding verification is used
amlcft.riskDescription: Delayed verification increases the risk of onboarding criminals, being used as a channel for laundering funds, or violating AML/CFT regulations.
amlcft.owner: Account Officers, KYC/Onboarding Team, Compliance Officers
amlcft.responsibility: Execution – Account Opening/KYC TeamsMonitoring – Compliance Officer, Internal Control
amlcft.primaryControl: - Verify identity documents before or during onboarding wherever possible - Where post-verification is allowed, ensure 48-hour rule is enforced - Apply transaction limits and monitoring rules until full verification is done - Keep logs of exceptions and approvals - Risk-assess each non-verified onboarding case
amlcft.additionalControl: - Automate triggers for blocking accounts if verification exceeds 48 hours - Escalate unverified accounts to Compliance after 24 hours - Conduct post-onboarding reviews on all non-face-to-face relationships - Apply enhanced monitoring on temporary-access accounts

amlcft.title: Application of CDD to existing customers
amlcft.description: (1) Financial Institutions shall apply CDD requirements to existing customers on the basis of materiality and risk, and continue to conduct due diligence on such existing relationships at appropriate times. (2) The appropriate time to conduct CDD by Financial Institutions in the following non-limitative cases, when— (a) a transaction of significant value takes place; (b) a customer documentation standards change substantially; (c) there is a material change in the way that the account is operated; or (d) the institution becomes aware that it lacks sufficient information about an existing customer. (3) Financial Institution shall properly identify the customer in accordance with the criteria contained in these Regulations and the customer identification records shall be made available to the compliance officer, other appropriate staff and competent authorities.
amlcft.plain: The Bank shall: (1) Re-assess existing customers using CDD based on risk and importance of the relationship. (2) Re-do CDD when any of the following happen: • A large or unusual transaction occurs; • CBN or internal KYC documentation standards change; • There is a major change in how the customer operates the account; • The bank finds it lacks enough information on the customer. (3) Ensure that customer identification info is accurate, up to date, and accessible to the compliance officer, relevant staff, and regulators.
amlcft.deadlineType: Ongoing – based on risk or trigger eventsImmediately – upon material change or discovery of incomplete info
amlcft.riskDescription: Not updating or re-verifying CDD for existing customers may allow criminal abuse of dormant or low-risk accounts, leading to breaches of AML laws and reputational damage.
amlcft.owner: Account Officers, Compliance Officer, Relationship Managers, KYC/Operations Unit
amlcft.responsibility: Execution – Account Officers, KYC UnitOversight – Compliance Officer, Internal Audit
amlcft.primaryControl: - Use a risk-based schedule to refresh KYC on existing customers - Monitor account activity to flag changes in operation or large transactions - Reconfirm customer info when regulatory documentation standards change - Provide compliance staff access to KYC files and CDD updates - Maintain audit trail of all KYC updates and decisions
amlcft.additionalControl: - Automate reminders for periodic KYC review based on customer risk - Link transaction monitoring systems to customer profiles to trigger CDD reviews - Conduct periodic internal audits of CDD compliance for legacy accounts

amlcft.title: Failure to Complete CDD
amlcft.description: (1) A Financial Institution that is unable to comply with the CDD measures pursuant to these Regulations shall—  (a) not be permitted to open the account, commence business relations or perform the transaction with the concerned persons; and (b) be required to render a Suspicious Transaction Report to the NFIU.  (2) A Financial Institution that has commenced the business relationship prior to the conduct of CDD shall terminate the business relationship and render Suspicious Transaction Reports to the NFIU (3) Where Financial Institutions suspects that transactions relate to money laundering, terrorism financing or proliferation financing, during the establishment or course of the customer relationship, or when conducting occasional transactions, it shall immediately— (a) obtain and verify the identity of the customer and the beneficial owner, whether permanent or occasional, irrespective of any exemption or any designated threshold that might otherwise apply; and (b) render a Suspicious Transaction Report to the NFIU immediately.  (4) Where Financial Institutions suspects that a transaction relates to ML, TF and PF and it believes that performing the CDD process shall tip-off the customer, it shall— (a) not pursue the CDD process, and (b) file an STR to the NFIU immediately.  (5) A Financial Institution shall ensure that its employees are aware of, and sensitive to the issues mentioned under this regulation.  (6) When assessing risk, Financial Institutions shall consider all the relevant risk factors before determining the level of overall risk and the appropriate level of mitigation to be applied.
amlcft.plain: The Bank shall:  (1) If the Bank is unable to complete the required Customer Due Diligence (CDD) in accordance with applicable regulations: 1.It must not open an account, initiate any business relationship, or proceed with a transaction involving the concerned customer. 2.It must file a Suspicious Transaction Report (STR) with the Nigerian Financial Intelligence Unit (NFIU) without delay. (2) Where the Bank has already established a business relationship without conducting CDD: 1. The relationship must be terminated immediately, and 2.An STR must be submitted to the NFIU. (3) If it suspects ML/TF/PF during onboarding or transaction execution:  1. Obtain and verify the customer and beneficial owner’s identity—regardless of thresholds or exemptions.  2. File a Suspicious Transaction Report (STR) to the NFIU immediately. (4) If it suspects ML/TF/PF and believes that CDD will alert the customer (i.e., tip-off):  1. Discontinue the CDD process.  2. File an STR immediately. (5) Ensure employees are trained and alert to these obligations. (6) Consider all relevant risk factors when assessing overall risk level and mitigation measures.
amlcft.deadlineType: Immediate upon suspicion; ongoing monitoring and training
amlcft.riskDescription: Failure to complete CDD or incorrectly assessing tipping-off scenarios may lead to undetected financial crime, regulatory breach, or aiding criminals.
amlcft.owner: Compliance Officer, Relationship Officers, AML/CFT Desk
amlcft.responsibility: Execution: Relationship Managers, Operations, and Frontline StaffReporting: Compliance Officer/MLROOversight: Internal Audit and Risk Unit
amlcft.primaryControl: - Transaction screening - STR procedure and escalation flow - Staff awareness and training - Risk-based customer onboarding
amlcft.additionalControl: - Enhanced staff training on STR and tipping-off scenarios - Supervisory approval before continuing risky onboarding - Internal alert system for flagged relationships

amlcft.title: Tiered Know-Your-Customer measures
amlcft.description: (1) Financial Institutions may adopt physical or electronic Know-Your-Customer (e-KYC) approach to on-board customers; and the procedures adopted by Financial Institutions on e-KYC shall comply with the requirements of CBN’s Guidance on e-KYC. (2) A tiered KYC standard shall be utilized to ensure application of flexible account opening requirements for low-value and medium value accounts which shall be subject to caps and restrictions. (3) As the transactions and value increases, the account opening requirements shall increase progressively with less restrictions as may be specified by the CBN on operations. (4) Financial Institutions shall have mechanisms in place for monitoring of accounts opened under the Tiered Know Your Customer procedures to ensure that such accounts are not misused for ML or TF.
amlcft.plain: The Bank shall: (1) Use either physical or electronic KYC (e-KYC) to onboard customers, ensuring e-KYC complies with CBN guidelines. (2) Use tiered KYC to allow easier onboarding for low- and medium-value accounts, with clear limits and restrictions. (3) As transaction volumes increase, apply stricter account opening requirements and relax restrictions based on CBN guidance. (4) Actively monitor tiered KYC accounts to prevent their misuse for money laundering or terrorism financing.
amlcft.deadlineType: Immediately – for onboarding via physical or e-KYCOngoing – as accounts evolve or limits are reviewed
amlcft.riskDescription: Poor controls on tiered accounts can make them vulnerable to abuse, especially if low-value accounts are used to structure or layer illicit funds.
amlcft.owner: KYC/Onboarding Officers, Compliance Officer, Digital Banking Team, IT/Operations
amlcft.responsibility: Execution – KYC/Digital Onboarding TeamsOversight – Chief Compliance Officer, Internal Control
amlcft.primaryControl: - Implement tiered KYC levels with specific onboarding rules per CBN’s e-KYC Guidance - Set daily/monthly transaction limits for each account tier - Require more detailed documents for accounts with higher usage - Monitor account activity for deviations from expected behavior - Use automated flags to escalate suspicious behavior in low-tier accounts
amlcft.additionalControl: - Integrate tiered KYC with real-time monitoring tools - Conduct regular system audits of e-KYC onboarding - Track account upgrades and revalidate KYC during transitions - Restrict high-risk transactions (e.g., international wires) on low-tier accounts

amlcft.title: Reliance on intermediaries and third parties on CDD function
amlcft.description: (1) A Financial Institution that relies upon another FI or DNFBP to conduct its CDD shall— (a) ensure that the Financial Institution and DNFBP are subject to and have measures in place for compliance with the record keeping requirements prescribed under these Regulations; and (b) satisfy itself that copies of identification data and other relevant documentation relating to the CDD requirements shall be made available from the third party upon request without delay. (2) A Financial Institution shall satisfy itself that a third party is a regulated and supervised institution and that it has measures in place to comply with requirements of CDD reliance on intermediaries and other third parties on CDD as contained in these Regulations. (3) Financial Institutions relying on intermediaries or other third parties who have no outsourcing, agency, business relationships, accounts or transactions with it or their clients shall perform some of the elements of the CDD process on the introduced business. (4) The criteria to be met in carrying out the elements of the CDD process by the financial institution referred to in sub-regulation (3) of this regulation are to— (a) immediately obtain from the third party the necessary information concerning certain elements of the CDD process; (b) take adequate steps to satisfy itself that copies of identification data and other relevant documentation relating to CDD requirements shall be made available from the third party upon request without delay; (c) satisfy themselves that the third party is regulated and supervised in accordance with core principles of AML, CFT and CPF and has measures in place to comply with the CDD requirements set out in these Regulations; and (d) ensure that adequate Know-Your-Customer (“KYC”) provisions are applied to the third party in order to obtain account information for competent authorities. (5) Notwithstanding the conditions specified in this regulation, the ultimate responsibility for customer identification and verification shall be with the Financial Institution relying on the third party. (6) When determining in which countries the third party that meets the conditions can be based, Financial Institutions shall have regard to information available on the level of country risk. (7) For Financial Institutions that rely on a third party that is part of the same financial group, relevant competent authorities may also consider that the requirements of the criteria above are met in the following circumstances— (a) the group applies CDD and record-keeping requirements, in line with programmes against ML, TF or PF; (b) the implementation of those CDD and record-keeping requirements and AML, CFT and CPF programmes is supervised at a group level by a competent authority; and (c) any higher country risk is adequately mitigated by the group’s AML, CFT and CPF policies.
amlcft.plain: If the Bank relies on another Financial Institution (FI) or Designated Non-Financial Business and Profession (DNFBP) to do CDD, it shall: (1) Confirm that the third party follows CBN record-keeping rules and can quickly provide CDD documents when asked. (2) Make sure the third party is regulated and supervised, and follows proper CDD procedures. (3) If the third party has no direct business/account relationship with the bank or its clients, the bank must still perform key CDD steps. (4) The bank must: • Get CDD data from the third party immediately; • Confirm CDD docs can be shared quickly when needed; • Ensure the third party has AML/CFT controls aligned with CBN rules; • Apply its own KYC checks on the third party to assist authorities if needed. (5) The bank remains fully responsible for CDD even if a third party helps. (6) When deciding which countries third parties can be based in, consider the country’s ML/TF risk level. (7) If the third party is from the same financial group, the reliance is allowed if: • The group applies uniform AML/CFT standards; • Group-level compliance is supervised; • Higher country risks are managed through group-wide policies.
amlcft.deadlineType: Immediately – before reliance beginsOngoing – with periodic reviews
amlcft.riskDescription: Over-reliance on weak or unregulated third parties can expose the bank to poor customer verification, undetected ML/TF risks, regulatory breaches, and legal liabilities.
amlcft.owner: Relationship Managers, KYC Unit, Compliance Officer, Legal Department
amlcft.responsibility: Execution – KYC Unit, Legal, ComplianceOversight – Chief Compliance Officer, Internal Audit
amlcft.primaryControl: - Only rely on third parties that are CBN-compliant and regulated - Conduct due diligence on third party’s AML/CFT framework - Sign formal agreements with third parties for CDD obligations - Require immediate access to all KYC and verification data - Maintain audit trail of third-party reliance justifications
amlcft.additionalControl: - Use a third-party approval register for all CDD dependencies - Reassess third-party risk annually - Conduct random spot checks on CDD files from third parties - Limit reliance to third parties in low-risk jurisdictions or regulated groups

amlcft.title: Application of enhanced due diligence to higher risk customers and activities
amlcft.description: Financial Institutions shall perform Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) for higher risk customers, business relationship or transactions including— (a) non-resident customers; (b) private banking customers; (c) legal persons or legal arrangements such as trusts that are personal assets-holding vehicles; (d) companies that have nominee-shareholders or shares in bearer form; (e) Politically Exposed Persons (‘PEPs’); (f) cross-border banking and business relationships, and (g) any other businesses, activities or professions as may be prescribed by regulatory, supervisory or competent authorities.
amlcft.plain: The Bank shall apply Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) measures to customers, relationships, or transactions that pose higher risk of money laundering or terrorism financing. These include: (a) Non-resident customers (b) Private banking clients (c) Legal entities or trusts used to hold personal assets (d) Companies with nominee shareholders or bearer shares (e) Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) (f) Cross-border business or banking relationships (g) Any other high-risk category directed by CBN or relevant authorities
amlcft.deadlineType: Immediately – when onboarding any high-risk customerOngoing – periodic EDD reviews and monitoring
amlcft.riskDescription: High-risk customers or structures are often used to hide identities, move illicit funds, or avoid detection, exposing banks to legal and reputational damage.
amlcft.owner: Relationship Managers, KYC Unit, Compliance Officer, Risk Management Department
amlcft.responsibility: Execution – KYC Analysts, Relationship OfficersOversight – Compliance Officer, MLRO (Money Laundering Reporting Officer)
amlcft.primaryControl: - Identify high-risk categories at onboarding using a CBN-aligned risk scoring model - Collect additional information (e.g., source of funds, wealth, business purpose) - Get senior management approval before establishing high-risk relationships - Perform more frequent reviews and transaction monitoring - Conduct site visits or verify customer declarations independently if necessary
amlcft.additionalControl: - Automate flagging of high-risk customers in onboarding platforms - Integrate PEP screening tools - Conduct regular training for staff on red flags and EDD procedures - Maintain an updated internal EDD checklist based on evolving risk categories

amlcft.title: Politically Exposed Person (PEP)
amlcft.description: (3) Financial Institutions shall in addition to performing CDD measures, establish appropriate risk management systems to determine whether a potential customer or existing customer or the beneficial owner is a PEP. (4) Financial Institutions shall obtain senior management approval before they establish business relationships with a PEP and shall render monthly returns on all transactions with PEPs to the CBN and NFIU. (5) Where a customer has been accepted or has an ongoing relationship with a Financial Institution and the customer or beneficial-owner is subsequently found to be or becomes a PEP, the Financial Institution shall obtain senior management approval to continue the business relationship. (6) Financial Institutions shall take reasonable measures to establish the source of wealth and the source of funds of customers and any beneficial-owner identified as PEP. (7) A Financial Institution that is in a business relationship with a PEP shall conduct enhanced on-going monitoring of that relationship and in the event of any abnormal transaction, the Financial Institutions shall flag the account and report the transaction immediately to the NFIU as a suspicious transaction.
amlcft.plain: The Bank shall: (3) Set up risk systems to identify if a customer or beneficial owner is a Politically Exposed Person (PEP). (4) Get senior management approval before opening an account for a PEP and submit monthly reports of all PEP transactions to the CBN and NFIU. (5) If an existing customer is later identified as a PEP, get senior management approval to continue the relationship. (6) Find out and verify the source of funds and source of wealth of all PEPs. (7) Monitor PEP accounts more closely and report any suspicious activity immediately to the NFIU.
amlcft.deadlineType: Immediately – upon onboarding or identifying a PEPMonthly – for transaction reports to CBN/NFIUOngoing – for enhanced monitoring and risk reviews
amlcft.riskDescription: PEPs pose higher ML/TF risks due to their influence and possible involvement in corruption or misuse of public funds. Failure to identify or monitor them properly can result in major regulatory penalties and reputational damage.
amlcft.owner: Relationship Officers, Compliance Officer, KYC Unit, Senior Management
amlcft.responsibility: Execution – KYC Analysts, Relationship ManagersApproval – Senior ManagementOversight – Chief Compliance Officer, MLRO
amlcft.primaryControl: - Use PEP screening tools during onboarding and periodic reviews - Require senior management sign-off before onboarding or continuing PEP relationships - Obtain verified documents on source of wealth/funds - Implement automated transaction monitoring for PEP accounts - Submit monthly PEP returns to CBN/NFIU and report suspicious transactions immediately
amlcft.additionalControl: - Conduct periodic independent audits of PEP handling procedures - Use adverse media checks and international databases to enhance screening - Review all PEP accounts quarterly, even if no red flags have emerged - Maintain a separate watchlist for domestic and foreign PEPs

amlcft.title: Cross-border and correspondent banking
amlcft.description: (1) For cross-border and correspondent banking and other similar relationships, Financial Institutions shall, in addition to performing the normal CDD measures, take the following measures— (a) gather sufficient information about a respondent institution to understand fully the nature of its business and determine from publicly available information, the reputation of the institution and the quality of supervision, including whether or not it has been subject to ML, TF or PF investigation or regulatory action; (b) assess the respondent institution’s AML, CFT and CPF controls and ascertain that they are in compliance with FATF Standards; (c) obtain approval from senior management before establishing correspondent relationships; and (d) clearly understand and document the respective AML, CFT and CPF responsibilities of each respondent institution. (2) Where a correspondent relationship involves the maintenance of payable through-account, the financial institution shall— (a) be satisfied that its customer (the respondent bank or Financial Institution) has performed the normal CDD obligations on its customer that have direct access to the accounts of the correspondent Financial Institution; and (b) be satisfied that the respondent financial institution is able to provide relevant CDD information upon request to the correspondent financial institution. (3) A Financial Institution shall establish clear understanding of the respective AML, CFT and CPF responsibilities of each corresponding institution.
amlcft.plain: The Bank shall: (1) For all cross-border or correspondent banking relationships: • Gather enough information about the respondent bank to understand its business, check public sources for its reputation, and confirm if it has faced any ML/TF issues or regulatory actions. • Review the respondent’s AML/CFT/CPF controls and confirm they meet FATF standards. • Get senior management approval before starting the relationship. • Clearly document which party is responsible for what AML/CFT obligations. (2) If the relationship involves a payable-through account, ensure: • The respondent bank has done proper CDD on its own customers who use the account. • The respondent can give you full CDD info on those customers when asked. (3) Have a written agreement or understanding outlining each party’s AML/CFT/CPF duties.
amlcft.deadlineType: Before onboarding – respondent bankAnnually – for relationship review and documentation updates
amlcft.riskDescription: Poor due diligence on foreign respondent banks can allow indirect access by high-risk or anonymous customers, increasing exposure to money laundering, terrorism financing, and reputational damage.
amlcft.owner: Correspondent Banking Desk, Compliance Officer, Risk Management Unit, Senior Management
amlcft.responsibility: Execution – Correspondent Banking/KYC DeskApproval – Senior ManagementOversight – Chief Compliance Officer
amlcft.primaryControl: - Conduct enhanced CDD on all foreign respondent banks - Require public and regulatory reputation checks - Obtain senior management sign-off before onboarding - Use a correspondent banking questionnaire (e.g. Wolfsberg) to assess AML controls - Establish documented agreement detailing each party’s AML/CFT responsibilities
amlcft.additionalControl: - Conduct annual re-assessments of all correspondent relationships - Set risk-based limits on transaction volumes or services - Require periodic attestations from respondent institutions about AML/CFT compliance - Engage external compliance consultants to validate high-risk correspondent relationships

amlcft.title: New technologies and non-face-to-face transactions
amlcft.description: (1) A Financial Institution shall identify and assess the ML, TF and PF risks that may arise in relation to the development and deployment of new products and business practices including new delivery mechanisms and the use of new or developing technologies for both new and pre-existing products. (2) Financial Institutions are required to undertake risk assessment prior to the launch of the new products, business practices or the use of new or developing technologies, which shall be documented and appropriate measures taken to manage and mitigate such risks on a continuous basis. (3) Financial Institutions shall have policies and procedures in place to address any specific risk associated with non-face-to-face business relationships or transactions. (4) The policies and procedures required to be taken shall be applied automatically when establishing customer relationships and conducting ongoing due diligence and measures for managing the risks are to include specific and effective CDD procedures that apply to non-face-to-face customers.
amlcft.plain: The Bank shall: (1) Identify and assess money laundering, terrorism financing, and proliferation financing (ML/TF/PF) risks that come with new technologies, products, services, or delivery methods—including those added to existing services. (2) Conduct and document a risk assessment before launching any new product or technology and manage those risks on an ongoing basis. (3) Create specific AML/CFT policies and procedures to manage risks from non-face-to-face customers or transactions. (4) Automatically apply enhanced Customer Due Diligence (CDD) when onboarding and transacting with non-face-to-face customers.
amlcft.deadlineType: Before product launch – for risk assessmentsImmediately and ongoing – for monitoring and updating controls
amlcft.riskDescription: New digital tools or non-face-to-face channels may increase anonymity, reduce oversight, and expose the bank to undetected illicit transactions if risks are not properly managed.
amlcft.owner: Product Development, IT/Digital Banking, Compliance Officer, Risk Management
amlcft.responsibility: Execution – Product/IT/Digital Teams, Compliance UnitApproval – Chief Compliance Officer, Head of Risk
amlcft.primaryControl: - Conduct documented ML/TF risk assessments for all new or modified digital products - Implement real-time identity verification tools for non-face-to-face onboarding - Enforce multi-factor authentication and geolocation checks - Develop procedures specific to virtual banking and remote transactions - Automate enhanced due diligence (EDD) for remote customer relationships
amlcft.additionalControl: - Conduct third-party cybersecurity audits of digital platforms - Use AI/ML transaction monitoring to detect unusual patterns - Regularly train staff on emerging risks tied to new tech - Perform periodic risk re-evaluations post-deployment

amlcft.title: Money or Value Transfer (MVT) Services
amlcft.description: (1) All natural and legal persons performing Money or Value Transfer Service (‘MVTS operators’) shall be licensed by the CBN and shall be subject to the provisions of these Regulations, the relevant provisions of the MLPPA, TPPA and other relevant laws or regulations. (2) MVTS Operators shall maintain a current list of their agents and render quarterly returns to the CBN and the NFIU. (3) In addition to the requirement specified in this regulation, MVTS Operators shall gather and maintain sufficient information about their agents and correspondent operators or any other operators or institutions they are or likely to do business with. (4) MVTS Operators shall— (a) assess their agents’ and correspondent operators’ AML, CFT and CPF controls and ascertains that such controls are adequate and effective; (b) obtain approval from the CBN before establishing new correspondent relationships; (c) document and maintain a checklist of the respective AML, CFT and CPF responsibilities of each of their agents and correspondent operators; (d) provide accurate originator and beneficiary information, on wire transfers and related messages, and that the information remains with the wire transfer or related message throughout the payment chain; (e) take appropriate measures to monitor all transfers for the purpose of detecting those which lack originator and beneficiary information; and (f) take freezing action in processing transfers to prohibit transactions with designated persons and entities in line with the obligations set out in the relevant United Nations Security Council resolutions, Nigerian laws, and other relevant authorities. (5) MVTS provider that controls both the ordering and the beneficiary side of the wire transfer shall— (a) take into account all the information from both the ordering and beneficiary sides in order to determine whether STR should be filed; and (b) file an STR of the wire transfer and provide relevant transaction information to the NFIU.
amlcft.plain: The Bank, if involved in Money or Value Transfer Services (MVTS) shall: (1) Be licensed by the CBN and comply with AML/CFT/CPF laws. (2) Keep an updated list of agents and report quarterly to CBN and NFIU. (3) Collect and maintain detailed information on all agents, correspondents, and partner institutions. (4) MVTS Operators must: • Review AML/CFT systems of all agents and partners • Get CBN approval before starting any new correspondent relationship • Clearly define and document AML/CFT duties for each agent and partner • Include accurate sender and receiver information in all wire transfers and keep this information through the entire payment chain • Monitor all transfers and flag any lacking originator/beneficiary info • Block/freeze any transfers involving sanctioned individuals or entities per UN Resolutions and Nigerian laws. (5) Where the MVTS provider handles both ends of the transaction (sending & receiving): • Use data from both sides to assess if a Suspicious Transaction Report (STR) is needed • File STRs with the NFIU, with full transaction details
amlcft.deadlineType: Before onboarding agents/correspondentsQuarterly – returns to CBN and NFIUImmediately – for sanctions or suspicious transaction flags
amlcft.riskDescription: Unregulated or loosely controlled MVT operations can be exploited for anonymous transfers, terrorist financing, or bypassing financial controls, which can expose banks to regulatory fines, loss of license, or reputational damage.
amlcft.owner: MVTS Compliance Officer, Operations Unit, IT/Transaction Monitoring, Risk & Internal Control, CBN-Licensing Desk
amlcft.responsibility: Execution – MVTS/Remittance Unit, AML DeskOversight – Chief Compliance OfficerApproval – CBN-licensed team & Senior Management
amlcft.primaryControl: - Enforce strict licensing of MVTS services through CBN - Keep and regularly update agent lists, send quarterly returns - Use AML/CFT due diligence checklists for agents and correspondent partners - Implement automated monitoring systems for wire transfers - Validate sender/beneficiary info during onboarding and transaction processing - Apply screening systems for sanctions lists (UN/CBN/NFIU) - File STRs when suspicious transactions are flagged across either end of the payment chain
amlcft.additionalControl: - Conduct independent audits of MVTS operations semi-annually - Integrate name screening tools into the wire transfer system - Train staff on new typologies in value transfer abuse - Include STR filing timelines in compliance KPIs

amlcft.title: Wire Transfers
amlcft.description: (1) For every wire transfer of US$ 1,000 or its equivalent in other foreign currencies or more, the ordering Financial Institution shall obtain and maintain the following information relating to the originator of the wire transfer— (a) the name of the originator and beneficiary; (b) the originator’s account number (or a unique reference number where no account number exists); (c) the originator’s address which may be substituted with a national identity number; (d) unique identification number; and (e) the beneficiary account number where such an account is used to process the transaction or, in the absence of an account, a unique transaction reference number which permits traceability of the transaction. (2) For every wire transfer of US$ 1,000 or its equivalent in other foreign currencies— (a) the ordering Financial Institution shall obtain and verify the identity of the originator in accordance with the CDD requirements contained in these Regulations; (b) the beneficiary Financial Institution shall obtain and verify the identity of the beneficiary and maintain record of information in accordance with the CDD and record keeping requirements contained in these Regulations where it has not been previously obtained. (3) For cross-border wire transfers of US$ 1,000 or its equivalent in other foreign currencies, the ordering Financial Institution shall include the full originator information in sub-regulation (1) of this regulation in the message or the payment form accompanying the wire transfer. (4) Where however, several individual cross-border wire transfers of US$1,000 or its equivalent in other foreign currencies, from a single originator are bundled in a batch-file for transmission to beneficiaries in another country, the ordering Financial Institution should only include the originator’s account number or unique identifier and full beneficiary information that is fully traceable on each individual cross-border wire transfer, provided that the batch-file (in which the individual transfers are batched) contains full originator information that is fully traceable within the recipient country. (5) For every domestic wire transfer, the ordering financial institution shall— (a) include the full originator and beneficiary information in the message or the payment form accompanying the wire transfer; or (b) include only the originator and beneficiary account number or a unique identifier, within the message or payment form provided that this number or identifier will permit the transaction to be traced back to the originator or the beneficiary and can be made available to the beneficiary Financial Institution and to the competent authorities within three business days of receiving the request. (6) The inclusion of the originator’s account number or the originator’s unique identifier alone should be permitted by Financial Institutions only where the originator’s full information can be made available to the beneficiary financial institution and to the appropriate authorities within three business days of receiving the request. (7) Each intermediary and beneficiary Financial Institution in the payment chain shall ensure that all the originator and beneficiary information that accompanies a wire transfer is transmitted with the transfer. (8) Where cross boarder wire transfers that lacked required originator or beneficiary information, or where technical limitations prevent the full originator information accompanying a cross-border wire transfer from being transmitted with a related domestic wire transfer, during the necessary time to adapt payment systems, a record shall be kept for five years by the receiving intermediary Financial Institution of all the information received from the ordering financial institution. (9) intermediary Financial Institution shall take reasonable measures that are consistent with straight-through processing to identify cross border transfer that lack required originator or beneficiary information. (10) Beneficiary and intermediary Financial Institution shall adopt effective risk-based policies and procedures for determining— (a) when to execute, reject or suspend a wire transfer lacking required originator or beneficiary information; and (b) reasonable measures and appropriate follow up actions to be taken, not later than 24 hours. (11) The lack of complete originator’s information shall be considered as a factor in assessing whether a wire transfer or related transactions are suspicious and Financial Institution shall immediately file a STR on wire transfers with incomplete originator’s transaction information to the NFIU or where necessary, request the NFIU to contact the FIU of the country affected by the suspicious wire transfers. (12) The beneficiary’s Financial Institution shall restrict or even terminate its business relationship with the Financial Institutions that fail to meet the standards specified in this regulation. (13) For every wire transfer, Financial Institutions shall take freezing action and prohibit transactions with persons and entities designated as terrorists or with terrorist activities under any relevant United Nations Security Council resolutions, Nigerian laws and other relevant authorities. (14) Cross-border and domestic transfers between Financial Institutions are not applicable to the following types of payments— (a) any transfer that flows from a transaction carried out using a credit or debit card so long as the credit or debit card number accompanies all transfers flowing from the transaction, such as withdrawals from a bank account through an ATM machine, cash advances from a credit card or payments for goods and services, provided that where credit or debit card are used as a payment system to effect a money transfer the necessary information should be included in the message; and (b) transfers and settlements between Financial Institution where both the originator and the beneficiary are Financial Institutions acting on their own behalf. (15) The information required under sub-regulation (14) need not be verified for accuracy, provided that Financial Institutions should be required to verify the information pertaining to its customer where there is a suspicion of ML, TF or PF.
amlcft.plain: The Bank shall: (1) For all wire transfers of US$1,000 and above, collect and maintain: (a) the name of the originator and beneficiary; (b) the originator’s account number (or a unique reference number where no account number exists); (c) the originator’s address which may be substituted with a national identity number; (d) unique identification number; and (e) the beneficiary account number where such an account is used to process the transaction or, in the absence of an account, a unique transaction reference number which permits traceability of the transaction. (2) Verify the identity of both sender and beneficiary per CDD rules. (3) For cross-border transfers, include full originator information in payment messages. (4) When bundling multiple cross-border payments, each record must be traceable. (5) For domestic transfers, include full or traceable sender/beneficiary info. (6) Allow minimal info (e.g. just account number) only if full info can be provided to authorities within 3 days. (7) All intermediary and receiving banks must pass along all originator and beneficiary data. (8) Keep 5-year records of incomplete cross-border originator info where systems cannot carry full data. (9) Take reasonable steps to detect incomplete information. (10) Adopt risk-based policies to decide when to process, reject, or delay such transfers and follow up within 24 hours. (11) Incomplete info may indicate suspicious activity – file STRs to NFIU immediately. (12) End relationships with institutions that consistently violate these standards. (13) Block and freeze transactions with sanctioned persons/entities. (14) Exemptions apply to: • Normal credit/debit card purchases or ATM withdrawals • Transfers between banks acting on their own behalf. (15) Verification not required unless there’s ML/TF/PF suspicion.
amlcft.deadlineType: Immediately – for new/ongoing transactionsDaily – wire transfer screening and STR triggersWithin 24 hours – risk-based decisions and follow-up actions
amlcft.riskDescription: Incomplete or unverified wire transfers can enable anonymous movement of funds, conceal terrorist financing or ML, and expose banks to heavy regulatory sanctions.
amlcft.owner: Operations, Compliance, Transaction Monitoring, IT, Risk Management
amlcft.responsibility: Execution – Transaction Operations, SWIFT/Payments TeamMonitoring – Compliance Unit, AML DeskOversight – Chief Compliance Officer, Head of Risk
amlcft.primaryControl: - Integrate mandatory data fields for wire transfers - Block submission of wire transfers without required info - Implement rule-based transaction monitoring - Maintain automated alerts for incomplete or suspicious wires - Include screening for terrorist lists (UN/CBN/NFIU) - Define SOPs for STR filing and rejection of non-compliant transfers - Maintain 5-year archives of cross-border messages where needed
amlcft.additionalControl: - Daily reconciliation of wire transfer records - Automated alerts for missing originator/beneficiary data - Quarterly audits of SWIFT and payment messages - Conduct peer-institution due diligence annually - Pre-transaction validation checks for high-risk corridors

amlcft.title: Attention to high-risk countries
amlcft.description: (1) A Financial Institution shall apply enhanced due diligence, proportionate to the risks, to business relationships and transactions with natural or legal persons (including financial institutions) from countries for which the FATF raised such concerns. (2) Pursuant to section 66 (2) of the BOFIA 2020, the CBN shall, proportionate to the risks, call for specific counter measures to be applied by Financial Institutions against high-risk countries, including the mandatory application of enhanced due diligence measures as provided under Parts IV, V and IX of these Regulations. (3) Counter measures may include, inter alia— (a) limiting business relationships or financial transactions with the high-risk countries or with persons located in the country concerned; (b) reviewing and amending or, if necessary, terminating the agreement or arrangement governing the correspondent banking or business relationships with Financial Institutions or other counterpart institutions in the country concerned; (c) conducting enhanced external audit, by increasing the intensity and frequency, for branches and subsidiaries of the reporting entity located in the country concerned; (d) prohibiting reporting entities from relying on third parties located in the country concerned to conduct elements of the due diligence process; and (e) conducting any other measures as may be specified by the CBN. (4) For the purposes of this regulations, “high-risk countries” means— (a) countries which are subject to a call for application of counter measures by the FATF; (b) countries identified by CBN or other competent authorities as having strategic deficiencies in their AML, CFT and CPF regimes or posing a risk to the AML, CFT and CPF regime of Nigeria. (5) The CBN shall publish the list of high-risk countries and any subsequent update to the list on its official website. (6) The list of high-risk countries shall be promptly updated by the CBN as and when there are— (a) any amendments to the FATF’s list of countries subject to a call for counter measures; or (b) any revisions to the list identified by the CBN pursuant to this regulation. (7) A Financial Institution shall implement counter measures proportionate to the risks when called for by the CBN pursuant to this regulation. (8) Financial Institutions may apply additional counter measures including the following— (a) stringent requirements for identifying clients and enhancement of advisories, including jurisdiction-specific financial advisories to Financial Institutions for identification of the beneficial owners before business relationships are established with individuals or companies from that jurisdiction; (b) enhanced relevant reporting mechanisms or systematic reporting of financial transactions on the basis that financial transactions with such countries are more likely to be suspicious; (c) limit business relationships or financial transactions with the identified country or persons in that country.
amlcft.plain: The Bank shall: (1) Apply Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) to transactions and business relationships involving people or institutions from countries flagged by FATF or CBN as high-risk. (2) Implement countermeasures as directed by the CBN, such as: • Limiting or ending financial dealings with high-risk countries or entities within them • Reviewing or terminating correspondent banking agreements • Conducting more frequent and intense external audits of overseas branches in such countries • Avoiding reliance on third parties in those countries for due diligence • Taking other actions as instructed by the CBN. (3) Use the official CBN list of high-risk countries, which will be updated regularly. (4) Apply additional measures such as: • Extra client identity verification and beneficial ownership checks • Special reporting procedures for dealings with such countries •  limit business relationships or financial transactions with the identified country or persons in that country
amlcft.deadlineType: Immediate – for current and new business relationshipsOngoing – as CBN updates list of high-risk countriesWithin 24 hrs – for reporting suspicious transactions
amlcft.riskDescription: Doing business with high-risk countries increases exposure to terrorism financing, money laundering, reputational damage, and sanctions from regulators.
amlcft.owner: Compliance Unit, Transaction Monitoring, Legal, International Banking Desk
amlcft.responsibility: Execution – International Banking, EDD Analysts, Compliance OperationsOversight – Chief Compliance Officer, Head of Risk Management
amlcft.primaryControl: - Use FATF/CBN lists to flag high-risk countries in the system - Enforce automated EDD triggers for flagged jurisdictions - Pre-screen and limit onboarding of clients from these countries - Block or escalate transactions from flagged regions for review - Monitor and audit offshore branches in high-risk zones - Issue internal advisories on specific jurisdictions
amlcft.additionalControl: - Subscribe to FATF/CBN watchlist updates - Establish escalation matrix for high-risk jurisdiction reviews - Train staff regularly on how to handle clients from high-risk countries - Restrict third-party reliance in high-risk zones unless cleared by compliance - Notify CBN proactively on flagged activities involving listed countries

amlcft.title: Keeping and maintenance of transaction records
amlcft.description: (1) Financial Institutions shall maintain all necessary records of transactions, both domestic and international for at least five years after completion of the transaction or such longer period as may be required by the CBN and other competent authorities provided that this requirement shall apply regardless of whether the account or business relationship is on-going or has been terminated. (2) The components of records of transactions to be maintained by Financial Institutions shall include the— (a) records of customers and beneficial owners obtained through CDD measures inducing copies of records of official identification documents like passports, identity cards, drivers’ licenses or allied documents and beneficiary’s names, addresses or other identifying information normally recorded by the intermediary; (b) nature and date of the transaction; (c) type and amount of currency involved; (d) type and identifying number of any account involved in the transaction; (e) results of any analysis including inquiries to establish the background and purpose of complex unusual large transactions; and (f) business correspondence including paper and electronic. (3) Financial Institutions shall maintain records of the identification data, account files business correspondence and results of any analysis undertaken for at least five years after the termination of an account or business relationship, or such longer period as may be specified by the CBN and other competent authorities. (4) A Financial Institution shall ensure that all customer-transaction records and information are available on request to the CBN and other competent authorities on a timely basis, not later than 48 hours. (5) Transaction records kept by Financial Institutions shall be sufficient to permit reconstruction of individual transactions to provide, where necessary, evidence for prosecution of any criminal activity.
amlcft.plain: The Bank shall: (1) Keep records of all domestic and international transactions for at least five years, even if the account is closed. (2) Maintain full CDD records (IDs, documents, names, addresses, etc.) and key transaction data such as: • Date and nature of transaction • Type and amount of currency involved • Account numbers used • Analysis results for suspicious or large transactions • Business correspondence (paper or electronic). (3) Store these documents for five years after account closure or as directed by the CBN. (4) Make these records available to the CBN or other authorities within 48 hours when requested. (5) Ensure transaction records are detailed enough to reconstruct the transaction for possible investigations.
amlcft.deadlineType: - Ongoing for transaction records- 48 hours maximum for regulatory access requests
amlcft.riskDescription: Inadequate record-keeping can hinder regulatory investigations, expose the bank to sanctions, and allow undetected financial crimes.
amlcft.owner: Compliance Department, IT/Data Management, Records/Archives, Internal Audit
amlcft.responsibility: Execution – IT Data Team, Compliance Operations, Documentation UnitOversight – Chief Compliance Officer (CCO), Head of Risk/Records Management
amlcft.primaryControl: - Automate retention of customer and transaction data in central systems - Implement secure storage and backup protocols (on-prem & cloud) - Tag and index high-risk or suspicious transactions - Periodic review of data retention compliance - Train staff on documentation standards
amlcft.additionalControl: - Set up audit trails and change logs for record integrity - Restrict and monitor access to sensitive records - Use DLP (Data Loss Prevention) tools - Include record-keeping review in internal audits - Maintain offsite or disaster recovery storage

amlcft.title: Recording Identification Evidence
amlcft.description: 36.—(1) Records of the supporting evidence and methods used to verify identity shall be retained for a minimum period of five years after the account is closed or the business relationship has ended.  (2) Where the supporting evidence cannot be copied at the time it was presented, the reference numbers and other relevant details of the identification evidence shall be recorded to enable the documents to be obtained later.
