amlcft.source: Guidelines on Targeted Financial Sanctions Related to Terrorism and Terrorism Financing
amlcft.title: Target for Freezing Measures
amlcft.description: The freezing measures, including the prohibition of making funds available, apply to:  a) Any individual, group, or entity listed in the Sanctions Lists.  b) Any entity directly or indirectly owned or controlled by an individual or entity listed under (a).  c) Any individual or entity acting on behalf of or at the direction of any individual or Entity listed under (a) and (b).
amlcft.plain: Freezing and fund restrictions apply not only to sanctioned individuals/entities but also to those they own, control, or direct, including representatives acting on their behalf.
amlcft.deadlineType: Immediate and ongoing
amlcft.riskDescription: Missing indirect links to sanctioned parties may result in regulatory breaches and misuse of financial services for illegal purposes.
amlcft.owner: Compliance Officer, Legal Unit, Customer Due Diligence (CDD) Team
amlcft.responsibility: Compliance Department, Relationship Managers, Legal Advisory Team
amlcft.primaryControl: Enhanced due diligence, ownership and control structure analysis, relationship mapping tools, and regular updates to screening software.
amlcft.additionalControl: Implement automated beneficial ownership tracing; conduct periodic reviews of related-party linkages; obtain declarations on control from customers during onboarding and periodic KYC updates.

amlcft.source: Guidelines on Targeted Financial Sanctions Related to Terrorism and Terrorism Financing
amlcft.title: Receipt of additional funds into frozen accounts
amlcft.description: Where a frozen account is entitled to:  i. interests or other earnings; or ii. payments due under contracts, agreements or obligations that were concluded or arose before the account became a frozen account;  FIs are required to receive such funds and credit a designated account opened for the purpose which shall constitute part of the frozen funds. Thereafter, a report of the receipt of such additional funds be filed with the NFIU.
amlcft.plain: If frozen accounts receive interest, earnings, or payments from past obligations, the funds shall be received into a special designated account and reported to the NFIU.
amlcft.deadlineType: Immediate upon occurrence of transaction
amlcft.riskDescription: Failure to properly manage or report new inflows to frozen accounts may result in non-compliance with TFS obligations and misuse of blocked funds.
amlcft.owner: Compliance Officer, Operations Department, Treasury Unit
amlcft.responsibility: Compliance Department, Account Operations Team
amlcft.primaryControl: Open and maintain designated frozen accounts; system flagging of inflows; automatic routing of interest and payments to designated accounts; prompt reporting mechanism.
amlcft.additionalControl: Automate alerts for inflows into frozen accounts and auto-generate NFIU report templates; periodic reconciliation to ensure no misrouting of funds.

amlcft.source: Guidelines on Targeted Financial Sanctions Related to Terrorism and Terrorism Financing
amlcft.title: Approval for usage of frozen funds by designated persons and entities on the UN List
amlcft.description: FIs may advise customer or related party of the frozen accounts, blocked or rejected transactions to submit any query or appeal for variation to the frozen accounts, delisting or any other matters to the NSC.  The NSC, where necessary, may approve the utilization of frozen funds, assets or any part thereof:  a) to meet the basic needs and expenses of a designated person or entity a person or an entity whose funds have been frozen including the amounts required to meet expenditures on food, medical needs and such other general expenses;  b) for reasonable professional fees and settlement of expenses, including legal services, bank and related charges; or  c) for any other exceptional expenses that the NSC is of the view are permitted expenses in accordance with procedures under UNSCR 1373 and all successor resolutions.  Upon approval of the utilization of the frozen funds, FIs that are in custody of frozen funds are required to, upon receipt of a written directive by the NSC, implement the approval and furnish a report to the NSC of the action taken.
amlcft.plain: Frozen account holders may seek NSC’s approval to use blocked funds for basic or exceptional needs. The Bank shall act only on NSC’s written directive and report any action taken.
amlcft.deadlineType: Immediately upon receipt of NSC approval
amlcft.riskDescription: Misuse of frozen funds or acting without NSC approval may lead to violation of TFS obligations and international sanctions.
amlcft.owner: Compliance Officer, Legal Department, Account Services
amlcft.responsibility: Compliance Department, Account Services Team
amlcft.primaryControl: Internal protocol to reject all usage requests unless accompanied by NSC written directive; documented implementation of approval; timely reporting to NSC.
amlcft.additionalControl: Maintain a log of all frozen fund access requests; conduct regular compliance audits on frozen account activity; integrate NSC communication into compliance workflow system.

amlcft.source: Guidelines on Targeted Financial Sanctions Related to Terrorism and Terrorism Financing
amlcft.title: Reporting Requirements
amlcft.description: 4.8.1 Filing suspicious transaction with NFIU i. Where FI is required to file STR to the NFIU, the report should state: (a) the information or other matter on which knowledge or suspicion is based; (b) any information it holds about the person by knowledge of which the person can be identified; and (c) the nature and amount of funds held by the FI for the person at any time up to 5 years prior to the designation being made.  4.8.2 Attempted transaction FIs are to report as suspicious transaction to NFIU any attempted transaction undertaken by designated persons or entities or related parties in the case of joint accounts. This may include any transaction that is subsequently rejected or blocked, incomplete in the event of failure to satisfactorily complete CDD and attempt for redemption of assets where repayment has been fulfilled.
amlcft.plain: The Bank shall file Suspicious Transaction Reports (STRs) to the Nigerian Financial Intelligence Unit (NFIU) in the following situations:  1. Filing STR The STR should include: - The information or matter that triggered the suspicion. - Any identifiable information about the designated person/entity. - The nature and amount of funds held (even historically, up to 5 years before the designation).  2. Attempted Transactions They must report as STR: - Any attempted transactions by designated persons or related parties. - Transactions that were rejected, blocked, or incomplete due to failed CDD. - Any redemption attempts after payment fulfillment.
amlcft.deadlineType: - STRs must be filed immediately upon suspicion or attempted transaction.
amlcft.riskDescription: Failure to properly detect or report transactions (actual or attempted) by designated persons or entities may expose the FI to legal penalties, reputational damage, or indirect facilitation of terrorism financing.
amlcft.owner: - Chief Compliance Officer - AML Reporting Officer - Transaction Monitoring Team
amlcft.responsibility: - AML/CFT Desk Officer (Initiation) - Chief Compliance Officer (Approval) - IT/Data Team (Historical account review)
amlcft.primaryControl: - Automated alert systems for name matching.  - Detailed STR templates capturing historical fund relationships.  - Block or reject functionality built into transaction systems.  - Clear workflow for reporting attempted transactions. - Secure reporting line to NFIU with internal escalation protocols.
amlcft.additionalControl: - Conduct periodic back-testing to detect missed attempted transactions.  - Ensure that historical account activity (up to 5 years) is readily retrievable and linked to STR framework.  - Use AI-based tools to flag high-risk profiles and related parties.

amlcft.source: Guidelines on Targeted Financial Sanctions Related to Terrorism and Terrorism Financing
amlcft.title: Additional Obligations for Fis
amlcft.description: In addition to alerts of updates received from the NSC upon subscription by FIs, the CBN may also issue notifications of TFS to FIs.  FIs shall on receipt of the notification from the CBN: i. immediately take steps to identify any funds, assets or any economic resources in their possession belonging to designated persons or entities and carry out freezing obligations in respect of PF as contained in the TPPA, 2022, and report to the NSC. ii. immediately file STR to the NFIU for further analysis on the financial activities of such an individual or entity; and iii. report, as STR to the NFIU, all cases of name matching in financial transactions prior to or after receipt of the Sanctions List.  For the purposes of this section, “immediately” means not later than 24 hours. In addition to the above, FIs are required to fulfill the following obligations: i. Cooperate with the NSC in verifying the accuracy of the submitted information. ii. Implement the freezing, cancellation, or lifting decision, when appropriate, without delay. iii. Cooperate with competent authorities to provide information on TFS timeously when required. iv. Set and implement policies, procedures, and internal controls to: a) Ensure conduct of customer due diligence b) Ensure trade finance is integrated into compliance procedure (including the identification of final destination of goods and services) c) Ensure compliance with the obligations imposed by the TPPA and TFS Regulations. d) Conduct ongoing TFS training and awareness sessions to Board, senior management and employees. e) Prohibit staff from, directly or indirectly, informing the customer or any third party that freezing actions or any other measures will be implemented. f) Ensure appropriate resources are allocated to meet the obligations of implementing TFS.  It shall be the responsibility of all FIs, to monitor their accounts and transactions against the UN Consolidated List and Nigeria List.
amlcft.plain: The Bank shall: i. Act immediately (within 24 hours) on CBN notifications to freeze assets of designated individuals/entities per TPPA 2022 and report to NSC. ii. File Suspicious Transaction Reports (STRs) to NFIU on such individuals/entities and name-matching cases. iii. Cooperate with NSC in verifying information accuracy and implementing freeze/lift decisions. iv. Set and enforce internal policies to: - Conduct effective CDD - Integrate trade finance into TFS compliance - Implement TFS Regulations - Train staff at all levels - Prevent tipping-off - Allocate adequate resources v. Continuously screen accounts and transactions against the UN and Nigeria Sanctions Lists.
amlcft.deadlineType: Ongoing (with action within 24 hours upon receipt of CBN/NSC notifications)
amlcft.riskDescription: Failure to comply may result in regulatory penalties, facilitation of terrorism financing, legal liabilities, asset forfeiture, and reputational damage.
amlcft.owner: Chief Compliance Officer, Sanctions/AML Compliance Team, IT/Security Teams, Operations
amlcft.responsibility: Compliance Department (reporting & monitoring), IT (screening systems), Internal Audit (review), Operations (execution of freeze/lift)
amlcft.primaryControl: - Real-time automated screening system for name matching and sanctions alerts. - Immediate escalation and freezing protocols. - TFS Compliance Manual outlining procedures for CDD, trade finance compliance, and escalation. - Staff training on handling TFS alerts and reporting requirements.
amlcft.additionalControl: - Regular audit of sanctions screening process. - Periodic review of sanctions lists integration. - Mock drills for rapid freezing response. - Annual review of TFS compliance policy.

amlcft.source: Guidelines on Targeted Financial Sanctions Related to Terrorism and Terrorism Financing
amlcft.title: Record Keeping
amlcft.description: FIs are required to keep record of all actions taken in respect of TFS and should be kept in an easily retrievable manner.
amlcft.plain: The Bank shall keep clear and easily accessible records of all actions taken regarding TFS.
amlcft.deadlineType: Ongoing
amlcft.riskDescription: Poor record keeping may result in non-compliance, inability to demonstrate actions taken, and regulatory sanctions.
amlcft.owner: Compliance Officer, Records Management Unit
amlcft.responsibility: Compliance Department, IT/Records Unit
amlcft.primaryControl: Use centralized digital record-keeping system with tagging for TFS actions; ensure consistent file naming and tracking.
amlcft.additionalControl: Conduct periodic audits of TFS records; maintain secure backup; assign access controls and logging.

amlcft.source: Proceeds of Crime (Recovery and Management) Act, 2022
amlcft.title: Appointment of asset manager for property subject to a preservation order
amlcft.description: (b) order a person holding any property subject to a preservation order to surrender the property into the custody of the asset manager, immediately or within such period as the Court may determine ;
amlcft.plain: The Bank shall, where applicable, comply with any court order requiring a person holding property under a preservation order to surrender the property into the custody of the designated asset manager, either immediately or within the timeframe specified by the Court.
amlcft.deadlineType: Ongoing
amlcft.riskDescription: The Bank risks legal penalties and reputational damage if it fails to promptly surrender property under a court preservation order to the designated asset manager.
amlcft.owner: Legal, Compliance, Operations
amlcft.responsibility: Head of Legal, Compliance Officer
amlcft.primaryControl: Court order tracking process; secure handling of frozen assets
amlcft.additionalControl: Implement internal alert system for immediate escalation of court orders involving preservation of assets

amlcft.source: Proceeds of Crime (Recovery and Management) Act, 2022
amlcft.title: Contravening restraint orders
amlcft.description: A person who knowingly disposes of or deals with property that is under a restraint order commits an offence and is liable, upon conviction, to a fine of at least ₦5,000,000, or imprisonment for two years, or both.
amlcft.plain: The Bank shall not sell, transfer, or handle any property that is under a court-ordered restriction. Doing so knowingly is a criminal offence and can lead to a fine of at least ₦5 million, a prison sentence of two years, or both.
amlcft.deadlineType: Ongoing
amlcft.riskDescription: If the Bank deals with property under a restraint order, it risks criminal prosecution, significant financial penalties, and reputational damage.
amlcft.owner: Legal, Compliance, Operations
amlcft.responsibility: Head of Compliance, Head of Operations
amlcft.primaryControl: System flags for accounts/assets under restraint orders; restricted transactions protocol
amlcft.additionalControl: Periodic review of restricted asset list; mandatory staff training on handling restraint orders

amlcft.title: Freezing order in respect of designated persons or entities
amlcft.description: (1) Upon the publication of the UN Consolidated List of persons and entities designated by the UN in accordance with UNSCR 1267(1999) and its successor resolutions, and the Nigeria Sanctions List, all natural and legal persons in Nigeria, including financial institutions, designated non-financial business and professions, and other entities in Nigeria shall— (a) immediately, identify and freeze, without prior notice, all funds, assets, and any other economic resources belonging to the designated person or entity in their possession and report same to the Sanctions Committee; (b) report to the Sanctions Committee any assets frozen or actions taken in compliance with the prohibition requirements of the relevant UNSCRs, including attempted transactions; (c) immediately file a Suspicious Transactions Report to the NFIU for further analysis on the financial activities of such an individual or entity; and (d) report as a Suspicious Transactions Report to the NFIU, all cases of name matching in financial transactions prior to or after receipt of the Nigerian Sanctions List.  (2) The freezing obligation under subsection (1), shall extend to— (a) all funds or other assets that are owned or controlled by the designated person or entity, and not just those that can be tied to a particular act, plot, or threat of terrorism or terrorism financing; (b) those funds or other assets that are wholly or jointly owned or controlled, directly or indirectly, by designated persons or entities; (c) the funds or other assets derived or generated from funds or other assets owned or controlled directly or indirectly by designated persons or entities; and (d) funds or other assets of persons and entities acting on behalf of, or at the direction of designated persons or entities.
amlcft.plain: The Bank shall: i. Immediately identify and freeze—without prior notice—any funds, assets, or resources belonging to persons/entities on the UN Consolidated List or Nigeria Sanctions List. ii Report freezing actions and attempted transactions to the Sanctions Committee. iii File Suspicious Transaction Reports (STRs) with the NFIU concerning:  (a) frozen assets;  (b) actions taken;  (c) name matches in financial transactions. iv. Apply freezing orders to:  - All assets owned or controlled by designated persons/entities (fully or jointly),  - Assets derived from their funds,  - Assets controlled on behalf of, or under direction of, designated persons/entities.
amlcft.deadlineType: Immediately upon publication of UN/Nigeria sanctions lists
amlcft.riskDescription: Failing to freeze or report terrorist-related assets could: - Result in legal liability and regulatory sanctions; - Lead to association with terrorism financing; - Cause reputational and financial losses; - Trigger international blacklisting and derisking by correspondent banks.
amlcft.owner: Chief Compliance Officer, Head of Sanctions Desk, AML/CFT Officer
amlcft.responsibility: Compliance Department, Sanctions Monitoring Team, MLRO
amlcft.primaryControl: - Real-time automated name screening against UN/Nigeria Sanctions Lists - Daily updates of sanctions watchlists - Policy for immediate account freezing and escalation - STR reporting system integrated with sanctions alerts
amlcft.additionalControl: - Periodic testing and audit of screening systems - Staff training on identifying designated persons - Clear SOPs for escalation to management and regulatory bodies

amlcft.title: Freezing obligation in respect of Proliferation Financing
amlcft.description: (4) A financial institution, designated non-financial businesses and professions, and other entities shall— (a) immediately freeze, without prior notice, all funds or other assets belonging to the designated person or entity in their possession and report same to the Sanctions Committee; (b) immediately file a Suspicious Transactions Report to the NFIU for further analysis on the financial activities of such an individual or entity; and (c) report, as a Suspicious Transactions Report to the NFIU, all cases of name matching in financial transactions prior to or after receipt of the List.
amlcft.plain: The Bank shall: - Immediately freeze all funds or assets of designated persons/entities without prior notice. - Report the freezing action to the Sanctions Committee. - File a Suspicious Transaction Report (STR) to the NFIU( within 24hrs) for analysis of the financial activity of the affected person/entity. - Report all name-matching transactions (before or after receiving the sanctions list) as STRs to the NFIU.
amlcft.deadlineType: Immediate (within 24 hours of name match or notification)
amlcft.riskDescription: - Risk of violating national or international obligations if freezing is delayed or not done. - Legal, reputational, and regulatory sanctions for failing to report to the Sanctions Committee or NFIU. - Possible facilitation of proliferation financing through negligence.
amlcft.owner: Chief Compliance Officer (CCO), Sanctions Compliance Officer, Money Laundering Reporting Officer (MLRO)
amlcft.responsibility: Compliance Department, IT (Screening Systems), Legal and Regulatory Affairs Unit
amlcft.primaryControl: - Automated name-screening system against the UN and Nigeria Sanctions Lists. - Immediate alert escalation procedures. - STR filing checklist and audit trail tracking system. - Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for asset freezing and notification.
amlcft.additionalControl: - Daily sanctions list update and reconciliation. - Periodic audit of sanctions implementation process. - Staff refresher training on handling sanctions and STR obligations. - Compliance testing and scenario simulations.

amlcft.title: Freezing order on banks or other financial institutions
amlcft.description: (2) The relevant agency may, in addition, direct the bank or other financial institution to— (a) supply necessary information, and produce books and documents relating to the account; and (b) stop all outward payments, operations, or transactions, including any bill of exchange, in respect of the account of the arrested person or a person under investigation.  (3) The manager or person in charge of the bank or a financial institution shall take necessary steps to comply with the requirements of the order made under subsections (1) and (2).
amlcft.plain: 1) Upon receiving a freezing order from a relevant agency, the bank shall:   a) Supply necessary information and produce books/documents relating to the specified account.   b) Stop all outward payments and operations (e.g., fund transfers, cheque payments, bills of exchange) on the account. 2) The bank manager or officer in charge must take immediate steps to comply fully with the freezing order.
amlcft.deadlineType: Immediate (upon receipt of the order)
amlcft.riskDescription: - Non-compliance may result in legal and regulatory sanctions. - Risk of aiding terrorism financing by allowing continued operations on frozen accounts. - Reputational damage and breach of statutory obligations.
amlcft.owner: Chief Compliance Officer (CCO), Branch Manager, Legal & Regulatory Unit, MLRO
amlcft.responsibility: Branch Operations Team, Compliance Department, Legal Department
amlcft.primaryControl: - Centralized alert system for freezing orders. - Standard protocol to escalate to legal and compliance units. - Restriction flagging in core banking system. - Internal checklist to track compliance with orders (information supply, documentation, transaction blocks).
amlcft.additionalControl: - Regular training for branch managers and operations officers. - Simulated drills to test account freezing and information supply response. - Independent audit reviews of account freeze procedures.

amlcft.title: Confiscated and Forfeited Assets Account
amlcft.description: All forfeited funds, and funds realized from the proceeds of sale, management, or other forms of disposal of seized, attached and forfeited assets under this Act and vested in the Federal Government shall be paid into the Confiscated and Forfeited Assets Account established under any enactment dealing with the proceeds of crime.
amlcft.plain: The Bank shall: 1. Ensure that all forfeited funds and funds from the sale, management, or disposal of seized or forfeited assets (when handled or received) are paid into the Confiscated and Forfeited Assets Account established under relevant proceeds of crime laws. 2. Ensure no diversion or misplacement of such funds.
amlcft.deadlineType: As soon as funds are forfeited and vested in the Federal Government.
amlcft.riskDescription: - Mismanagement or failure to remit forfeited assets may result in regulatory sanctions and loss of banking license. - Legal liability for non-compliance with asset forfeiture handling regulations. - Reputational risk linked to mishandling proceeds of crime.
amlcft.owner: Compliance Officer, Treasury Operations, Legal Department, MLRO
amlcft.responsibility: Legal & Compliance Units, Treasury Department, AML Unit
amlcft.primaryControl: - Dedicated procedures for handling and transferring forfeited funds. - Mandatory use of designated Confiscated and Forfeited Assets Account. - Dual-authorization system for any transaction involving forfeited assets. - Escalation and reporting to appropriate asset management authority.
amlcft.additionalControl: - Independent review and audit of forfeited funds processes. - Ongoing staff training on asset forfeiture obligations and designated accounts. - Integration of proceeds of crime tracking software.

points.text: Ensure that all forfeited funds and funds from the sale, management, or disposal of seized or forfeited assets (when handled or received) are paid into the Confiscated and Forfeited Assets Account established under relevant proceeds of crime laws.
points.content: Ensure that all forfeited funds and funds from the sale, management, or disposal of seized or forfeited assets (when handled or received) are paid into the Confiscated and Forfeited Assets Account established under relevant proceeds of crime laws.

points.text: Ensure no diversion or misplacement of such funds.
points.content: Ensure no diversion or misplacement of such funds.

amlcft.title: Obligation to develop counter-financing of terrorism programmes and strategies
amlcft.description: (1) Subject to the provisions of the Money Laundering (Prohibition) Act, all financial institutions and designated non-financial institutions shall— (a) develop and implement programmes and strategies for combating the financing of terrorism; and (b) keep a record of any complex, unusual large and unusual pattern of transaction, which has no apparent economic or visible lawful source or purpose.  (2) A report detailing all the parties involved in such transactions shall be kept and made available on request by the relevant agency.
amlcft.plain: The Bank shall:  - Develop and implement programmes and strategies specifically designed to combat terrorism financing (CFT). - Maintain comprehensive records of complex, unusually large, or suspicious patterns of transactions without a lawful source. - Keep detailed reports of all parties involved in such transactions and provide them to relevant authorities upon request.
amlcft.deadlineType: Ongoing – Policies must be in place and updated continuously.
amlcft.riskDescription: - Inability to detect and prevent terrorism financing. - Regulatory and criminal liability for aiding terrorism financing unknowingly. - Reputational damage and possible license revocation.
amlcft.owner: Chief Compliance Officer, MLRO, Risk Management Department
amlcft.responsibility: MLRO, Compliance Officer, IT/Monitoring Unit
amlcft.primaryControl: - Establish robust CFT policies and frameworks. - Conduct ongoing risk assessments to detect unusual patterns. - Deploy automated transaction monitoring systems to flag suspicious activities. - Escalate and investigate flagged transactions.
amlcft.additionalControl: - Periodic audits and external reviews of the CFT programme. - Regular employee training on CFT risk indicators. - Maintain up-to-date terrorist watchlists integrated with transaction monitoring.

amlcft.title: Obligation to report suspicious transactions
amlcft.description: (1) Subject to the provisions of the Money Laundering (Prohibition) Act, a financial institution or designated non-financial institution shall, within 24 hours, forward reports of suspicious transactions relating to terrorism or terrorism financing, or proliferation financing to the NFIU, which shall immediately process and forward the information to the relevant agency, where there are sufficient reasons to suspect that the funds— (a) are derived from legal or illegal sources, and are intended to be used for an act of terrorism or terrorism financing, or proliferation financing; (b) are proceeds of a crime related to terrorism or terrorism financing, or proliferation financing; or (c) belong to a person, entity or organisation considered as terrorist.  (3) A breach of the provisions of this section is an offence under this Act, and is liable on conviction to— (a) in the case of a director, chief compliance officers, or other employees— (i) imprisonment for a term of not more than five years, (ii) a fine of at least N5,000,000, or (iii) both fine and imprisonment; and (b) in the case of a financial institution or non–financial institution— (i) a fine of at least N10,000,000 and N1,000,000 for every day the offence persists, (ii) the withdrawal of licence or forfeiture of assets of the institution, or (iii) all the prescribed penalties.
amlcft.plain: The Bank shall: - Report all suspicious transactions related to terrorism, terrorism financing, or proliferation financing to the NFIU within 24 hours. - Reports must be filed where there are reasons to suspect that the funds: a) Are linked to acts of terrorism or terrorism financing (legal or illegal sources). b) Are proceeds of terrorism-related crimes. c) Belong to persons, entities, or organizations designated as terrorists.
amlcft.deadlineType: Within 24 hours of detecting the suspicious transaction.
amlcft.riskDescription: - Non-compliance may result in severe regulatory sanctions including fines, license withdrawal, or criminal prosecution of employees. - Failure may expose the bank to being used for terrorist financing activities.
amlcft.owner: Chief Compliance Officer (CCO), MLRO, Compliance Unit
amlcft.responsibility: MLRO (STR preparation and submission), CCO (oversight and governance), Compliance Analysts (detection and investigation)
amlcft.primaryControl: - Automated transaction monitoring system to flag suspicious activity. - STR (Suspicious Transaction Report) filing procedures aligned with 24-hour rule. - Internal escalation protocol for urgent review and reporting. - PEP and Sanctions list screening integration.
amlcft.additionalControl: - Periodic refresher training for all compliance and frontline staff. - Ongoing audit of STR compliance timelines. - Regular testing of automated alert systems and manual override functionality.

amlcft.source: Guidelines on Targeted Financial Sanctions Relating to Proliferation Financing
amlcft.title: Alert System
amlcft.description: All FIs shall subscribe to the alert system for receiving automated email notifications of the sanction lists through the following links:  https://www.un.org/securitycouncil/content/un-sc-consolidated-list   https://www.nigsac.gov.ng
amlcft.plain: The Bank shall subscribe to automated alert systems to receive email notifications of sanctions lists from: - UN Sanctions List - https://www.un.org/securitycouncil/content/un-sc-consolidated-list  - Nigerian Sanctions Committee Portal - https://www.nigsac.gov.ng/
amlcft.deadlineType: Immediate upon issuance of the regulation and continuous thereafter.
amlcft.riskDescription: Failure to receive timely sanctions list updates may result in non-compliance with freezing obligations, allowing transactions with designated individuals/entities and exposing the bank to regulatory penalties and reputational damage.
amlcft.owner: Compliance Officer / IT Security Team
amlcft.responsibility: Compliance Officer (subscription oversight); IT/Systems Team (technical integration); Sanctions Screening Team (monitoring and action)
amlcft.primaryControl: - Ensure active and verified subscription to the UN and NIGSAC alert systems. - Assign a responsible officer to monitor updates and notify relevant departments. - Integrate alert systems with sanction screening software.
amlcft.additionalControl: - Test alert systems periodically to confirm receipt. - Maintain evidence/logs of alert emails received and reviewed. - Automate sanctions list downloads for real-time update in screening tools.

amlcft.source: Guidelines on Targeted Financial Sanctions Relating to Proliferation Financing
amlcft.title: Institutional PF Risk Assessment
amlcft.description: 1) FIs are required to identify, assess, monitor and mitigate PF risks. FIs should document their understanding and analysis of PF risks in their risk assessment Framework taking cognizance of their size and complexity. The risk assessment should at a minimum include country/geographic risks; customer/vendor risks and product and service risks.  2) Where there are higher risks, FIs should take commensurate measures to manage and mitigate the risks, including applying enhanced screening measures. Correspondingly, where the risks are lower, they should ensure that the screening measures are commensurate with the lower level of risk. FIs shall ensure full implementation of TFS relating to PF in any risk scenario.
amlcft.plain: The Bank shall: 1. Identify, assess, monitor, and mitigate Proliferation Financing (PF) risks. 2. Document their PF risk understanding and analysis in a risk assessment framework tailored to their size and complexity. 3. Assess risks across country/geographic, customer/vendor, and product/service dimensions. 4. Apply enhanced screening measures for higher-risk areas and ensure all PF-related Targeted Financial Sanctions (TFS) are implemented fully regardless of risk level.
amlcft.deadlineType: Immediate and ongoing (at least annually or when risk changes significantly)
amlcft.riskDescription: Failure to identify and mitigate PF risks can result in:  - Regulatory sanctions  - Involvement in global proliferation financing schemes  - Reputational damage  - De-risking by international correspondent banks
amlcft.owner: Chief Compliance Officer / Risk Management Department
amlcft.responsibility: Chief Compliance Officer (policy & framework); Risk Management (risk assessment); Sanctions Screening Team (implementation)
amlcft.primaryControl: - Develop and maintain a PF Risk Assessment Framework - Conduct periodic risk assessments covering geographic, customer, and product/service risks - Implement enhanced due diligence and sanctions screening for higher-risk areas - Integrate PF risk considerations into onboarding and transaction monitoring
amlcft.additionalControl: - Perform annual PF risk reviews - Use external PF risk data sources (e.g., FATF, UN) - Conduct internal audits of PF risk controls - Train staff specifically on PF risks and TFS implementation

amlcft.source: Guidelines on Targeted Financial Sanctions Relating to Proliferation Financing
amlcft.title: Screening
amlcft.description: FIs are required to carry out regular and ongoing screening against updated Sanctions Lists issued by the UN and the Nigeria Sanctions Committee (NSC) prior to conducting any transaction or undertaking any financial Services to ascertain whether the name of such a person or entity is on the Lists. Specifically, screening should be conducted during the following: a) Onboarding a new customer; b) Facilitating an occasional transaction; c) Establishing any relationship with any person or entity; d) Upon updates on the Nigeria Sanctions List, UN Consolidated List; and e) Upon review of Know-Your-Customer (KYC) or changes to a customer’s information.  Screening must be conducted immediately and without delay to ensure compliance with the requirement for implementing freezing measures immediately or within 24 hours. Furthermore, FIs are required to screen their entire customer database daily and whenever an update has been made to the UN Consolidated List or Nigerian List, to prevent dissipation of funds of the designated persons or entities.  FIs must establish group-wide screening and transaction monitoring systems (including those operating in free trade zones). Screening should be undertaken for existing customers, potential customers, beneficial owners, and transactions to identify possible matches.  (a) Confirmed Match A confirmed match is when an individual, entity, or group matches all the key identifiers published on the Sanctions Lists. The range of information that constitute identifiers of designated individuals, entities, or groups are as follows:  For natural person: Name, Aliases, Date of birth, Nationality, ID or passport information, Last known address.  For legal persons: Name(s), Aliases, Certificate of Registration (RC No.), Registered Address, Address of branches, Other information.  Where the individual, entity, or group matches all the key identifiers published on the Sanctions Lists, the result is considered a ‘confirmed match’. Where the confirmed match is an existing customer, FIs are required to immediately, identify and freeze, without delay and without prior notice, all funds and assets owned or controlled by the designated person or entity in their possession.  Where the confirmed match is a potential customer, the FIs are required to reject the transaction immediately and report to the Nigeria Sanctions Committee (NSC). However, before rejecting the transaction, FIs are required to search their records to confirm whether the potential customer is a Beneficial Ownership (BO). Where the search is positive, FIs are required to immediately identify and freeze, without delay and without prior notice, all funds and assets owned or controlled by the BO in their possession.  In cases of confirmed matches (for either existing or potential customer), FIs are required to report to the NSC, within 24 hours, any assets frozen or actions taken in compliance with the prohibition requirements of the relevant UNSCRs including attempted transactions.  In addition, FIs are required to immediately file STRs to the NFIU, including all cases of name matching in financial transactions prior to, or after publication or update of the lists for further analysis.  (b) False Positive A false positive is a potential match to listed individuals, entities, or groups, either due to the common nature of the name or due to ambiguous identifying data, which on evaluation proves not to be a confirmed match.  FIs are required to obtain additional information and identification documents from the customer or a third party to ascertain whether a customer is a designated person or entity in the case of similar names.  FIs are required to forward queries to the NSC to ascertain whether the customer is a designated person or entity in the case of similar names. Any query submitted to the NSC is to be accompanied by additional information, copies of identification documents and the FIs assessments.  Where FIs are satisfied that the customer (potential or BO) is not a designated individual, entity, or group, that there is a ‘False Positive Result’, FIs do not need to implement any TFS measures. FIs may allow the transaction or business to continue its normal course, and maintain evidence of this process in their records.  Where FIs’ customers feel that their accounts have been mistakenly frozen or transactions have been mistakenly rejected or blocked, the FIs may advise their customers to contact the NSC to verify the false positive match.  The contact details for the NSC in relation to TFS on PF is: info@nigsac.gov.ng  (c) Potential Match A potential match is when there is a partial match between identifiers in the Sanctions Lists with any information in FIs databases, and the FIs are unable to conclude a false positive or a confirmed match.  Due to prevalence of some names, FIs may find various potential matches. However, it does not necessarily mean that the individual, entity, or group they are dealing with is subject to TFS. FIs are required to cross-check their customers’ database with the identifiers published on the Sanctions Lists when identifying the potential match, by taking into consideration their knowledge of the customer (potential and BO) or transaction, through CDD and/or other sources of information.  Where FIs are unable to internally verify whether the ‘potential match’ is a false positive result or a confirmed match, the transaction should be suspended, and the case reported to NSC. The reported transaction should remain suspended, until a response is received on the status of the potential match.  4.3.1 Screening of Customers – Related and Third Parties FIs are required to undertake further screening and analysis of designated persons or entities whose properties or accounts are jointly owned and/or indirectly controlled by the designated persons or entities.  FIs are required to conduct further Customer Due Diligence (CDD) on parties related to frozen accounts including checking on the control and conduct of the frozen accounts and other related or third parties accounts connected to designated persons or entities.  The requirements for CDD on legal persons and legal arrangements and beneficial owners in the respective provisions under the CBN AML/CFT/CPF Regulations, 2022 and extant laws should be applied in determining whether the funds are directly or indirectly owned or controlled.  FIs are required to screen the names of beneficiaries of wire transfers and assess whether such transaction should be blocked or rejected.  FIs are also required to search, examine and analyse past financial activities of designated persons or entities and related or third parties.
amlcft.plain: The Bank shall: - Conduct regular and ongoing screening of all customers, transactions, and beneficial owners against the UN Consolidated List and Nigeria Sanctions List. - Screen at onboarding, occasional transactions, relationship establishment, updates to Sanctions Lists, and KYC reviews. - Screen daily and immediately after any update to sanctions lists. - Implement group-wide screening, including free trade zones. - Take actions based on screening results:   - Confirmed match: Freeze assets immediately, report to NSC and NFIU within 24 hours.   - Potential match: Suspend transaction, escalate to NSC and await verification.   - False positive: Obtain additional documents, confirm, and retain proof if not a match. - Screen related or third-party accounts and wire transfer beneficiaries. - Conduct retrospective analysis of designated persons' past activities.
amlcft.deadlineType: Immediate and daily thereafter, as well as trigger-based (onboarding, list updates, KYC review)
amlcft.riskDescription: - Risk of facilitating transactions for sanctioned individuals/entities - Exposure to regulatory penalties, reputational loss, and international restrictions (e.g., correspondent banking limits)
amlcft.owner: Compliance Officer Sanctions & AML Monitoring Unit IT/System Admin for automated screening
amlcft.responsibility: Compliance & Sanctions Team (Operational) Head of Risk (Oversight) IT/Security (Screening System Maintenance)
amlcft.primaryControl: - Deploy automated screening tools with real-time alerts - Perform daily batch screening and immediate screening upon list updates - Maintain Sanctions List integration in onboarding and transaction systems - Define workflows for handling matches (Confirmed, False Positive, Potential Match) - Maintain audit trail of all screening actions and decisions
amlcft.additionalControl: - Conduct regular system validations and list updates - Provide sanctions screening training - Run mock drills/simulations - Review past financial activity of designated and related parties - Use secondary validation through NSC when in doubt

amlcft.source: Guidelines on Targeted Financial Sanctions Relating to Proliferation Financing
amlcft.title: Application of targeted financial sanctions
amlcft.description: FIs are required to immediately implement TFS by identifying and freezing, without delay and without prior notice, all funds and assets owned or controlled by the designated person or entity in their possession.  FIs may advise the customer or related party of the frozen accounts, blocked or rejected transactions to submit any query or appeal for variation to the frozen accounts, delisting or any other matters to the NSC for approval.  The following are the TFS measures that must be implemented if a match with the Sanctions Lists is identified.  i. Freeze all funds or other assets without delay: freeze without delay (immediately or in any case within 24 hours) and without prior notice to the designated individual, entity, or group, all the funds or other assets: a) Owned or controlled, wholly or jointly, directly, or indirectly, by an individual, entity, or group designated in the Sanctions Lists; b) Derived or generated from funds or other assets under item (a); or c) Of Any individual or entity acting on behalf of or at the direction of any designated individual, entity, or group.  ii. Prohibition from making funds or other assets or services available: FIs are prohibited from providing funds or other assets or rendering financial services or other related services, whether in whole or in part, directly or indirectly, for the benefit of any designated individual, entity, or group on the Sanctions Lists.
amlcft.plain: The Bank shall: 1. Immediately freeze, without prior notice, any funds or assets in their possession that:   - are owned or controlled (wholly or jointly, directly or indirectly) by individuals, entities, or groups on the Sanctions Lists;   - are derived from such funds or assets; or   - belong to anyone acting on behalf of or under the direction of a designated person or group. 2. Prohibit the provision of funds, financial services, or related support to designated persons/entities/groups. 3. Where a customer's funds or services are frozen or blocked, the bank may inform the affected party that they may submit queries or appeals to the Nigeria Sanctions Committee (NSC) for review or delisting.
amlcft.deadlineType: - Immediately, and in no case later than 24 hours of a confirmed match
amlcft.riskDescription: - Failure to freeze assets of designated persons may expose the bank to criminal liability, reputational damage, regulatory sanctions, and international countermeasures. - Risk of inadvertently facilitating terrorism financing or proliferation activities.
amlcft.owner: - Compliance Officer (Sanctions) - AML/CFT Desk - Operations Department - IT Security (System-level blocks)
amlcft.responsibility: - Head of Compliance (Final authority for action) - Sanctions Monitoring Officer (Execution) - Internal Audit (Periodic review of freezing processes)
amlcft.primaryControl: - Integrate automated systems to identify and freeze assets immediately upon a confirmed match - Maintain a workflow escalation procedure for handling designated matches - Restrict access to frozen accounts and ensure blocking of outgoing transactions - Establish a communication protocol for informing affected parties about appeal mechanisms via NSC - Maintain audit logs of all freezing actions and related correspondence
amlcft.additionalControl: - Conduct regular mock testing of the freezing procedures - Maintain a watchlist review committee to verify complex cases - Periodic training for staff on "freezing without delay" principle - Implement an automated alert escalation system to ensure no delays in freezing actions

amlcft.source: Guidelines on Targeted Financial Sanctions Relating to Proliferation Financing
amlcft.title: Receipt of additional funds into frozen accounts
amlcft.description: Where a frozen account is entitled to: i. interests or other earnings; or ii. payments due under contracts, agreements or obligations that were concluded or arose before the account became a frozen account shall be received and credited into the frozen account.  FIs are required to file a report of the receipt of such additional funds with the NFIU. Where there is no existing account for the receipt of additional funds, the FIs are required to create an Escrow account and inform the Attorney-General for appropriate action to be taken in this respect.
amlcft.plain: The Bank shall: 1. Receive and credit additional funds into a frozen account if the funds are:   i. Interest or other earnings; or   ii. Payments due under pre-existing contracts (concluded before the account was frozen). 2. File a report of such credit with the NFIU. 3. If no existing frozen account exists for the funds, the bank must:   i. Create an Escrow account, and   ii. Inform the Attorney-General for further instructions.
amlcft.deadlineType: Immediately upon receipt of funds into a frozen account
amlcft.riskDescription: - Risk of Non-compliance with freezing obligations and misreporting. - Potential Regulatory sanctions or legal consequences for failing to credit or Report such funds appropriately. - risk of unauthorized access to or movement of additional frozen funds.
amlcft.owner: - Compliance Department (Sanctions Unit) - Operations Department - Legal Department (for notification to Attorney-General)
amlcft.responsibility: - Head of Compliance (Oversight) - Sanctions Compliance Officer (Execution and NFIU filing) - Legal Officer (Communication with Attorney-General)
amlcft.primaryControl: - Automate flagging and routing of incoming transactions to frozen accounts. - Maintain a frozen account monitoring register. - Develop a process flow for Escrow account creation and documentation. - Implement internal workflow for timely reporting to the NFIU.
amlcft.additionalControl: - Regular reconciliation of frozen accounts to monitor for unexpected credits. - Establish automated triggers for report generation and alerts for credits to frozen accounts. - Maintain communication templates for prompt notification to the Attorney-General.

amlcft.source: Guidelines on Targeted Financial Sanctions Relating to Proliferation Financing
amlcft.title: Condition for Approval for usage of frozen funds by designated persons and entities under the UN Consolidated List
amlcft.description: An application to utilize monies from frozen funds shall be made to the NSC. FIs should not make any payment to a designated person or entity except with the approval of the NSC.  Upon receipt of written approval from the NSC to utilize frozen funds, FIs that are in custody of frozen funds are required to implement the approval and furnish a report of the action taken to the NSC.
amlcft.plain: 1. The Bank shall not make any payment or allow use of frozen funds by a designated person or entity unless there is written approval from the Nigeria Sanctions Committee (NSC). 2. Upon receiving such approval, they must carry out the directive and submit a report of the action taken to the NSC.
amlcft.deadlineType: - Immediately upon receiving NSC approval and before effecting any payment.
amlcft.riskDescription: - Unauthorized release of frozen funds could lead to violation of UN/NSC sanctions, reputational damage, regulatory sanctions, or complicity in terrorism financing.
amlcft.owner: - Compliance Officer (Sanctions Desk) - Operations Department (Funds release execution) - Legal Department (Verification and interpretation of NSC approval)
amlcft.responsibility: - Head of Compliance (Oversight) - Sanctions Compliance Officer (Execution & Reporting to NSC) - Legal Officer (Validation of NSC directive)
amlcft.primaryControl: - Maintain a central register of frozen accounts. - Require written NSC approval before executing any debit or release. - Implement a workflow checklist before processing any transaction on a frozen account.
amlcft.additionalControl: - Embed approval verification step into core banking system. - Conduct periodic compliance audits of all frozen fund approvals. - Maintain a secure archive of all NSC approvals and reports sent.

amlcft.source: Guidelines on Targeted Financial Sanctions Relating to Proliferation Financing
amlcft.title: Reporting Requirements
amlcft.description: (6) Filing suspicious transaction with NFIU Where a FI is required to file an STR to the NFIU, the report should state: a) the information or other matter on which knowledge or suspicion is based; b) any information it holds about the person by which the person can be identified; and c) the nature and amount or quantity of funds held by FIs for the person at any time up to 5 years prior to the designation being made.  (7) Attempted transaction FIs are to report, as suspicious transaction, to NFIU any attempted transaction undertaken by designated persons or entities or related parties in the case of joint accounts. This may include any transaction that is subsequently rejected or blocked, incomplete in the event of failure to satisfactorily complete CDD and attempt for redemption of assets where repayment has been made.
amlcft.plain: The Bank shall: - Identify and report all attempted transactions by designated persons, entities, or related parties (e.g., in joint accounts), even if the transaction was:   a) Rejected or blocked   b) Incomplete due to failed CDD   c) An attempted redemption of assets - File a Suspicious Transaction Report (STR) to the NFIU for every such attempt.
amlcft.deadlineType: Within 24 hours of identifying the attempted transaction
amlcft.riskDescription: - Risk of facilitating or failing to report attempted terrorist financing transactions. - Reputational and regulatory risk for non-reporting of incomplete or blocked terrorist-related activities.
amlcft.owner: - Sanctions Compliance Unit - Operations Department (Transaction flagging) - AML Monitoring Team
amlcft.responsibility: - Head of Compliance (STR Filing Oversight) - Transaction Monitoring Officer (Initial Flagging & Escalation) - IT/Technology Support (Automated Alert Systems)
amlcft.primaryControl: - Implement automated systems to detect and flag blocked, rejected, or failed transactions involving designated names. - Maintain a log of attempted transactions tied to CDD failures or sanctions list matches. - Escalate all flagged incidents to Compliance for review and STR filing.
amlcft.additionalControl: - Conduct real-time transaction screening with sanction list integration. - Include attempted transaction scenarios in employee training. - Require dual authorization for rejection of suspicious high-risk transactions.

amlcft.source: Guidelines on Targeted Financial Sanctions Relating to Proliferation Financing
amlcft.title: Additional Obligations for Fis
amlcft.description: In addition to alerts of updates received from the NSC upon subscription by FIs, the CBN may also issue notifications of TFS to FIs.  FIs shall on receipt of the notification from the CBN: i. immediately take steps to identify any funds, assets or any economic resources in their possession belonging to designated persons or entities and carry out freezing obligations in respect of PF as contained in the TPPA, 2022, and report to the NSC. ii. immediately file STR to the NFIU for further analysis on the financial activities of such an individual or entity; and iii. report, as STR to the NFIU, all cases of name matching in financial transactions prior to or after receipt of the Sanctions List.  For the purposes of this section, “immediately” means not later than 24 hours.  In addition to the above, FIs are required to fulfill the following obligations: i. Cooperate with the NSC in verifying the accuracy of the submitted information. ii. Implement the freezing, cancellation, or lifting decision, when appropriate, without delay. iii. Cooperate with competent authorities to provide information on TFS timeously when required. iv. Set and implement policies, procedures, and internal controls to: a) Ensure conduct of customer due diligence b) Ensure trade finance is integrated into compliance procedure (including the identification of final destination of goods and services) c) Ensure compliance with the obligations imposed by the TPPA and TFS Regulations. d) Conduct ongoing TFS training and awareness sessions to Board, senior management and employees. e) Prohibit staff from, directly or indirectly, informing the customer or any third party that freezing actions or any other measures will be implemented. f) Ensure appropriate resources are allocated to meet the obligations of implementing TFS.  It shall be the responsibility of all FIs, to monitor their accounts and transactions against the UN Consolidated List and Nigeria List.
amlcft.plain: On receipt of TFS notification from NSC or CBN, The bank shall: i. Identify and freeze all funds/assets linked to designated persons/entities and report to NSC within 24 hours. ii. File STR to the NFIU on such financial activities. iii. Report all name matches (before or after Sanctions List receipt) to the NFIU as STRs.  Additionally, they must: - Cooperate with NSC and competent authorities in information verification. - Implement all TFS decisions without delay. - Establish robust policies, procedures, and internal controls covering:   a) CDD processes   b) Trade finance compliance (destination checks)   c) TPPA/TFS regulation compliance   d) Ongoing staff training   e) Strict confidentiality (no tipping off)   f) Allocation of adequate resources. - Monitor all accounts and transactions against the UN Consolidated List and Nigeria Sanctions List.
amlcft.deadlineType: - Within 24 hours of notification for freezing and STR filing. - Ongoing for monitoring, training, and internal control obligations.
amlcft.riskDescription: - Failure to freeze, report, or cooperate could result in aiding proliferation financing, legal sanctions, reputational damage, and regulatory penalties.
amlcft.owner: - Sanctions Compliance Unit - Legal & Regulatory Compliance - Internal Audit - Trade Finance & Operations Units
amlcft.responsibility: - Chief Compliance Officer (Oversight) - TFS Desk Officer (Execution) - Training Manager (Staff education & awareness) - Head of Trade & Operations (Trade-related compliance)
amlcft.primaryControl: - Maintain active subscription to NSC/CBN alert systems. - Daily screening against updated sanctions lists. - TFS response protocol and escalation procedures documented. - Enforce no tipping-off protocols. - Incorporate TFS clauses into Trade Finance and CDD policies.
amlcft.additionalControl: - Set up automated alerts/workflows for TFS notifications. - Conduct quarterly staff drills and refreshers on TFS procedures. - Ensure segregation of duties to prevent internal leaks or lapses. - Conduct annual independent TFS compliance audits.

amlcft.title: Record Keeping
amlcft.description: FIs are required to keep records of all actions taken in respect of TFS, which should be kept in an easily accessible and retrievable manner.
amlcft.plain: The Bank shall maintain complete records of all actions taken regarding the implementation of Targeted Financial Sanctions (TFS). These records must be stored in a way that allows for quick and easy retrieval when needed.
amlcft.deadlineType: Ongoing (continuous obligation)
amlcft.riskDescription: Failure to maintain proper records could hinder regulatory audits, investigations, or legal compliance, and may result in penalties or reputational damage.
amlcft.owner: Chief Compliance Officer (CCO), Records/Documentation Unit, IT/Data Management Team
amlcft.responsibility: CCO, Head of Operations, Head of Records Management, IT Support Lead
amlcft.primaryControl: - Standard Operating Procedures for documentation of all TFS-related actions- Secure digital storage system with indexing and search functionality- Periodic audit of TFS recordkeeping practices
amlcft.additionalControl: - Automation of record capture and tagging for every TFS event- Staff training on documentation standards- Quarterly review of data accessibility and backup protocols

amlcft.source: Exposure of Draft Baseline Standards for Automated Anti-Money Laundering (AML) Solutions
amlcft.title: User Interface & Customization
amlcft.description: Financial institutions shall:  i. Deploy robust automated AML solutions that are user-friendly, customized to their peculiarities, and compliant with all applicable AML/CFT/CPF laws and regulations. The solution may be developed in-house or procured off-the-shelf.  ii. Configure the AML system to allow for rule updates and scenario modifications with minimal vendor dependency.  iii. amlcft.description: i. The solution shall integrate with domestic and global watchlists for sanctions screening.  ii. amlcft.source: Suspicious Transaction Reporting on United Nations Security Council Resolutions on Proliferation Financing
amlcft.title: Suspicious Transaction Reporting on United Nations Security Council Resolutions on Proliferation Financing
amlcft.description: Further to the provisions of Regulation 11 of the CBN AML/CFT Regulations, 2013 and our previous Circulars on targeted financial sanctions, we write to remind all financial institutions on the need to increase surveillance and report all transactions involving persons and entities designated under the United Nations Security Council Resolution 1718 and all other subsequent resolutions relating to the Democratic People's Republic of Korea (DPRK).  Financial Institutions are advised to continuously screen both customers and transactions against Global sanctions lists and stop all transactions; freeze, without delay, all funds, owned or controlled, directly or indirectly by individuals and entities designated by the UN Sanctions Committees.
amlcft.plain: The Bank shall actively monitor and report any transactions linked to persons or entities designated under UN Security Council Resolution 1718 and related resolutions on North Korea (DPRK). They must:  - Screen customers and transactions continuously against global sanctions lists.  - Immediately freeze any funds linked (directly or indirectly) to designated individuals/entities.  - Stop any transaction linked to such persons or entities.
amlcft.deadlineType: Ongoing; STRs must be filed immediately after detection
amlcft.riskDescription: - Failure to screen for DPRK-designated entities may allow proliferation financing to occur. - Failure to report suspicious activity could attract regulatory sanctions and damage the institution’s reputation. - Inadvertent engagement with sanctioned entities may expose the institution to international penalties.

amlcft.source: Guidance on Ultimate Beneficial Owners of Legal Persons and Legal Arrangements
amlcft.title: Identification and Verification of Beneficial Owner
amlcft.description: 1. FIs are to carry out necessary customer due diligence (CDD) when identifying and verifying BO, particularly at the on-boarding stage, based on the risk-assessment of the customer and its BO, and must take all reasonable measures in verifying the information on the BO. 2. In identifying and verifying legal persons, FIs are required to adopt a three-step cascade approach in Regulation 21 of the CBN AML/CFT/CPF Regulations as detailed below: (a) identify and verify the natural persons, where they exist, that have ultimate controlling ownership interest in a legal person, taking into cognizance the fact that ownership interests can be so diversified that there may be no natural persons, whether acting alone or with others, exercising control of the legal person or arrangement through ownership. (b) In the event of doubt as to the persons with the controlling ownership interest as beneficial owners or where no natural person exerts control through ownership interests, identify and verify the natural persons, where they exist, exercising control of the legal person or arrangement through other means. (c) where a natural person is not identified, FIs shall identify and take reasonable measures to verify the identity of the relevant natural person who holds senior management position in the legal person. 3. For legal arrangements, identify and verify the identity of the settlor, the trustee, the protector where they exist, the beneficiaries or class of beneficiaries or persons in equivalent or similar positions, and any other natural person exercising ultimate or effective control over the legal arrangement including through a chain of control or ownership. 4. FIs in verifying the identity of BO, must use reliable and independent documents from sources identified in Sections 5.2 and 5.3 and any other reliable sources.
amlcft.plain: The Bank shall: 1. Conduct Customer Due Diligence (CDD) at onboarding by identifying and verifying the Beneficial Owner (BO) using a risk-based approach. 2. Follow a three-step cascade process to determine the BO:   a. Identify natural persons with ultimate ownership or control.   b. If unclear, identify those who control through other means.   c. If no one is identified, verify senior management personnel as BOs. 3. For legal arrangements, identify and verify all parties (settlor, trustee, beneficiaries, protector, etc.) exercising control. 4. Use reliable and independent documents (as stated in Section 5.2, 5.3) to verify BOs.
amlcft.deadlineType: - During onboarding - Annually or when material ownership/control changes occur
amlcft.riskDescription: - Failure to properly identify BOs may expose the bank to financial crimes such as money laundering, terrorism financing, and fraud. - Regulatory sanctions or reputational damage due to non-compliance with AML/CFT/CPF laws. - Compromise of integrity in customer onboarding and KYC processes.

amlcft.source: Guidance on Ultimate Beneficial Owners of Legal Persons and Legal Arrangements
amlcft.title: Responsibilities of FIs with Respect to Beneficial Ownership Obligations
amlcft.description: In line with the provisions of the CBN AML/CFT/CPF Regulations and global best practice, the responsibilities of FIs with respect to beneficial ownership of their customers include but are not limited to the following. (a) To identify and manage ML/TF/PF risks posed by legal persons and legal arrangements; (b) To understand the nature of the customer’s business, its ownership structure; taking into cognizance the complex ownership structure where shareholders are multiple legal persons, or complex arrangements in different nominee shares, which when aggregated gives a controlling ownership in the entity. In such circumstances, the FI is required to identify the natural person(s) with ultimate control. (c) To identify and take reasonable steps to verify the identity of a BO, board, senior management, settlor, trustee, beneficiary and other positions denoting control using relevant information or data obtained from reliable sources to satisfy itself that it has knowledge of the BO(s) of the customer; (d) To apply Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) on complex corporate vehicle structures that pose higher ML/TF/PF risks; (e) To ensure records of all relevant documents used in determining the BO for legal persons or legal arrangements are kept and updated periodically; and (f) To ensure that relevant authorities have timely access to BO information.
amlcft.plain: The Bank shall: 1. Identify and manage risks related to money laundering (ML), terrorism financing (TF), and proliferation financing (PF) from legal entities and arrangements. 2. Understand the customer's business and ownership structure, especially when ownership involves multiple legal persons or nominee shareholders that result in complex control structures. 3. Identify and verify beneficial owners, including board members, senior management, settlors, trustees, and beneficiaries using reliable data sources. 4. Apply Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) for customers with complex corporate structures posing high ML/TF/PF risks. 5. Keep and periodically update all documentation used in determining beneficial ownership. 6. Ensure timely access to BO information for relevant regulatory or law enforcement authorities.
amlcft.deadlineType: - At onboarding - During periodic reviews (e.g., annually or based on risk triggers)
amlcft.riskDescription: - Failure to properly identify beneficial owners increases the risk of financial crime (e.g., money laundering or terrorism financing). - Legal and regulatory penalties due to non-compliance with AML/CFT/CPF frameworks. - Damage to the institution’s reputation due to involvement in illicit financial flows. - Inability to support law enforcement investigations due to lack of timely access to BO data.

amlcft.additionalControl: - Conduct regular internal audits on BO data management and access. - Cross-check BO data against public registers and regulatory sources. - Introduce system-based alerts for BO data expiration or gaps.

amlcft.source: Guidance on Ultimate Beneficial Owners of Legal Persons and Legal Arrangements
amlcft.title: Risk Management System and Assessment of Beneficial Owner
amlcft.description: 1. FIs should apply a risk-based approach in the identification and verification of BOs. 2. Measures to be applied should be on the risk sensitive basis and should be set out in the FI’s AML/CFT/CPF framework. 3. FIs should conduct enhanced CDD on BOs that pose higher risk and file a suspicious transaction report with the Nigerian Financial Intelligence Unit (NFIU) if there are reasonable reasons to suspect money laundering or terrorism financing. 4. FIs should establish AML/CFT/CPF internal policies and procedures to mitigate identified risks relating to BO. 5. Financial institutions should have effective systems to determine whether a beneficial owner is a politically exposed person (PEP) or a family member or close associate of a PEP. Where a BO is determined to be in one of these categories, the financial institution must take additional measures to manage the risk. Such measures include obtaining senior management approval before establishing or continuing with the customer relationship, establishing the beneficial owner’s source of funds and source of wealth, and conducting enhanced ongoing monitoring of the customer relationship.
amlcft.plain: The Bank shall: 1. Apply a risk-based approach in identifying and verifying beneficial owners (BOs). 2. Ensure risk-sensitive measures are embedded in the FI’s AML/CFT/CPF framework. 3. Conduct Enhanced Customer Due Diligence (EDD) on high-risk BOs. 4. Report Suspicious Transactions to the NFIU where there are indications of money laundering or terrorist financing. 5. Establish internal AML/CFT/CPF policies and procedures to mitigate BO-related risks. 6. Maintain systems to determine whether a BO is a Politically Exposed Person (PEP) or a close associate/family member of a PEP. 7. If BO is a PEP or related:     - Obtain senior management approval before onboarding/continuing relationship     - Identify source of funds and source of wealth     - Conduct enhanced monitoring of the relationship.
amlcft.deadlineType: - At onboarding - Periodically (based on customer risk rating) - Immediately when risk indicators are triggered
amlcft.riskDescription: - Exposure to money laundering/terrorism financing if BO identity and risk are not properly assessed. - Regulatory penalties for failure to implement proper controls under AML/CFT/CPF laws. - Reputational risk from associating with high-risk or criminally exposed entities. - Inability to trace beneficial ownership of illicit funds if risk management controls are inadequate.

amlcft.additionalControl: - Regular training on BO risk assessment and PEP identification. - Integrate BO risk scoring into AML monitoring systems. - Maintain updated records of senior management approvals and EDD steps taken.

amlcft.source: Guidance on Ultimate Beneficial Owners of Legal Persons and Legal Arrangements
amlcft.title: Beneficial Ownership Register
amlcft.description: 1. FIs are expected to use the records or information collected through CDD or other sources to create a BO register of its customers that are legal persons and legal arrangements. 2. FIs are expected to ensure BO information in their register is periodically reviewed and updated annually or when there are changes. 3. FIs are expected to flag and report inconsistency or discrepancies between the BO information in the public register and the BO information in their records to the Corporate Affairs Commission (CAC) through the following links: (a) https://forms.office.com/r/Gs8UprwEdT; and (b) Email: psoverification@cac.gov.ng
amlcft.plain: The Bank shall: 1. Create and maintain a Beneficial Ownership (BO) Register using information obtained through Customer Due Diligence (CDD) or other reliable sources. 2. Review and update the BO register annually or whenever there are changes in beneficial ownership. 3. If there are discrepancies between the bank’s BO records and the public BO register, report such inconsistencies to the Corporate Affairs Commission (CAC) through:      - Online form: https://forms.office.com/r/Gs8UprwEdT      - Email: psoverification@cac.gov.ng
amlcft.deadlineType: - At onboarding - Annually or upon any change in BO information
amlcft.riskDescription: - Regulatory breaches and possible sanctions for failure to maintain and update BO records. - Risk of facilitating money laundering or terrorist financing by relying on outdated or false BO information. - Reputational damage for dealing with entities whose beneficial owners are hidden or not transparent.
amlcft.owner: - Compliance Department - Customer Due Diligence Unit - Risk Management Team
amlcft.responsibility: - Chief Compliance Officer - Head, AML/CFT/CPF Compliance - Head, KYC/CDD Unit
amlcft.primaryControl: - Establish a centralised BO register updated from CDD systems. - Implement automated reminders for annual BO review. - Conduct periodic cross-checks against the CAC’s public register. - Create internal workflows for flagging and reporting discrepancies promptly to the CAC.
amlcft.additionalControl: - Integrate BO register updates into compliance audit and CDD review cycles. - Assign designated officers to handle CAC discrepancy reports and follow-up. - Maintain logs and documentation of all communications with the CAC for accountability.

amlcft.title: Access to Information by Competent Authorities
amlcft.description: 1. FIs shall be required to provide, on request, information on BOs to the CBN and other competent authorities identified under the MLPPA. 2. FIs shall be required to render periodic returns to the CBN on their customers along with details of beneficial owner(s) that are legal persons and legal arrangements in the prescribed format and frequency.
amlcft.plain: The Bank shall: 1. Provide information on Beneficial Owners (BOs) upon request to the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) and other competent authorities identified under the Money Laundering (Prevention and Prohibition) Act (MLPPA). 2. Submit periodic returns to the CBN that include customer information and corresponding BO details for legal persons and legal arrangements, following the prescribed format and schedule.
amlcft.deadlineType: - Upon request by authorities - Periodically, based on CBN’s prescribed frequency and format
amlcft.riskDescription: - Regulatory sanctions for failure to provide timely or accurate BO information to authorities. - Risk of being seen as non-cooperative or non-compliant by CBN and other competent authorities. - Potential AML/CFT vulnerabilities if data sharing processes are not robust or timely.

amlcft.responsibility: - Chief Compliance Officer - Head of Regulatory Reporting - Data Governance Officer
amlcft.primaryControl: - Maintain an up-to-date and centralised BO database with secure access. - Establish a BO reporting calendar to meet all CBN return submission deadlines. - Implement a compliance checklist for validating the completeness and accuracy of submitted BO information.
amlcft.additionalControl: - Conduct quarterly internal reviews to verify compliance with BO reporting requirements. - Automate alerts and escalation protocols for delays or anomalies in BO information requests or returns. - Train staff on proper handling and confidentiality of BO data shared with authorities.

amlcft.title: Record Keeping
amlcft.description: In line with the extant AML/CFT/CPF laws and regulations, FIs are required to: a) keep all records of BOs obtained through CDD measures, account files and business correspondence, and results of any analysis undertaken, either in electronic or written form for at least five years following the termination of the business relationship or after the date of the occasional transaction. b) ensure that documents, data or information collected under the CDD process are kept up-to-date and remain relevant, by undertaking ongoing monitoring and reviews of existing records, particularly for higher risk categories of customers.
amlcft.plain: The Bank shall: 1. Keep all Beneficial Ownership (BO) records, account files, business correspondences, and analysis outcomes for at least five years after the end of the business relationship or occasional transaction.  2. Ensure that Customer Due Diligence (CDD) documents and data are regularly updated and remain relevant, especially for high-risk customers, through ongoing monitoring and reviews.
amlcft.deadlineType: - Ongoing, with updates as required - Retention: Minimum five years post-relationship or transaction
amlcft.riskDescription: - Regulatory penalties for failure to retain records for the required duration. - Loss of evidence in the event of investigations or audits. - Inability to trace or verify BO information, which may impact AML/CFT compliance.

amlcft.primaryControl: - Implement a centralized electronic document management system with retention rules. - Set up automated alerts for periodic review and update of customer and BO records. - Regular data quality checks for BO and CDD records.
amlcft.additionalControl: - Annual internal audit of recordkeeping and data retention policies. - Backup and disaster recovery solutions to protect stored records. - Staff training on data handling, retention periods, and compliance requirements.
