amlcft.source: RE: Reminder on Sanctions Compliance Obligations
amlcft.title: CMD/DIR/PUB/LTI/001/001
amlcft.description: The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) reminds all banks, payment service banks and other financial institutions (Financial Institutions) of their ongoing obligations to comply with applicable sanctions regimes, including but not limited to:  1. The United Nations Consolidated Sanctions List 2. The Nigerian Sanctions List maintained in line with the Terrorism (Prevention and Prohibition) Act, 2022, CBN AML/CFT/CPF Regulations, 2022 and CBN Guidelines on Targeted Financial Sanctions Related to Terrorism and Terrorism Financing, 2022 3. Other relevant regional or international sanctions lists, as applicable.  Financial Institutions are required to maintain a robust and dynamic sanctions compliance framework that enables them to:  - Identify and respond promptly to updates or changes across all applicable sanctions lists - Prevent the use of their systems and platforms for transactions involving designated individuals or entities - Conduct real-time screening of customers, transactions, and beneficial owners; and  File appropriate reports with the Nigerian Financial Intelligence Unit (NFIU) and notify the CBN, where necessary.  The effectiveness of sanctions compliance programmes must be regularly reviewed and aligned with legal and regulatory requirements and expectations.
amlcft.plain: 1. The Bank shall comply with applicable sanctions regimes, including the UN Consolidated Sanctions List, Nigerian Sanctions List, and other relevant regional/international lists. 2. They must establish and maintain a robust, responsive, and dynamic sanctions compliance framework. 3. The bank must also: - Identify and respond quickly to changes in sanctions lists. - Prevent the use of their systems for transactions with designated individuals/entities. - Conduct real-time screening of customers, transactions, and beneficial owners. - File reports with the NFIU and notify the CBN where necessary. 4. The sanctions compliance programme must be regularly reviewed and aligned with regulatory requirements.
amlcft.deadlineType: - Ongoing: Real-time and continuous monitoring. - Immediate response to list updates. - Quarterly internal review of sanctions controls.
amlcft.riskDescription: - Exposure to regulatory fines and sanctions for non-compliance. - Reputational damage from processing transactions linked to sanctioned individuals/entities. - Risk of the bank being used for terrorist financing or proliferation activities. - Operational and legal risks due to outdated or ineffective sanctions screening tools.

amlcft.additionalControl: - Periodic independent audit/review of sanctions compliance framework. - Ongoing employee training on sanctions obligations. - Implement post-alert investigation workflow for documenting actions taken.

amlcft.title: Freezing funds, assets and other economic resources held by a designated persons and entities
amlcft.description: (1) Upon the publication or update of the UN Consolidated List of persons and entities designated by the UN in accordance with UNSCR 1267(1999) and its successor resolutions, and the Nigerian Sanctions List, all natural and legal persons in Nigeria, including financial institutions, Designate Non-financial Business and Professions, and other entities in Nigeria shall (a) immediately, identify and freeze, without delay and without prior notice, all funds, assets, and any other economic resources owned or controlled by the designated person or entity in their possession;  (b) report to the Sanctions Committee any assets frozen or actions taken in compliance with the prohibition requirements of the relevant UNSCRs, including attempted transactions within 24 hours;  (c) The report in referred to in sub-regulation 12(1)(b) above shall be utilized by the Nigeria Sanctions Committee in line with the Committee’s Manual; and  (d) immediately file a Suspicious Transactions Report to the NFIU, including all cases of name matching in financial transactions prior to or after publication or update of the lists for further analysis.  (2) A Person who, in good faith, freezes funds, denies disposal thereof, or refuses to provide financial services relating to listed individual, group or entity, or declined to perform any other obligation in compliance with the provisions of Terrorism (Prevention and Prohibition) Act, 2022 and this shall be exempted from any damages or claims, resulting from such actions, including penal, civil, and/or administrative liability.  (3) In determining whether funds, assets or other economic resources are controlled by a designated person or entity, the fact that such funds are held in the name of an associate or relation is immaterial.  (4) Funds, assets and other economic resources frozen under these Regulations shall be recorded against the names of the owners and beneficial owners for proper management.  (5) For the purpose of determining beneficial ownership or control, a designated person or entity is deemed to be the beneficial owner or in control of a legal entity where he or she directly or indirectly, owns or controls, more than 50% of the shares of that entity. Such a company shall be subject to the sanctions’ restriction applicable to the designated person or entity.  (6) Subject to the provisions of these Regulations –  (a) frozen funds under Resolution 1267 shall be held and the designated person is prohibited from accessing such funds or be provided with financial services except with the approval of the United Nations Security Council Sanction Committee; and  (7) frozen funds under Resolutions 1373 shall not be released without authorization from the Nigerian Sanctions Committee and the designated persons shall be prohibited from accessing funds or financial services as long as they remain designated under the Nigeria List.  (8) without prejudice to the provisions of sub-regulations 12(1-6), the Attorney-General shall without delay apply to the Court ex-parte for a freezing order –  (a) directing financial institutions, Designated Non-Financial Businesses and Professions, other entities, or any person in control of the funds, assets or other economic resources of a designated person or entity to freeze the account; and  (b) freeze funds, assets and other economic resources belonging to the designated person or entity.
amlcft.plain: The Bank shall: 1. Upon updates to the UN Consolidated List or Nigeria Sanctions List, financial institutions and other entities must:    a. Immediately freeze, without prior notice, all funds, assets, and economic resources of designated persons/entities.    b. Report all freezing actions or attempted transactions to the Nigerian Sanctions Committee within 24 hours.    c. File a Suspicious Transaction Report (STR) to the NFIU for all cases of name matches in financial transactions related to designated individuals.    d. Record frozen assets against names of both legal owners and beneficial owners.    e. Recognize indirect ownership of over 50% by designated persons/entities as falling under the sanctions.    f. Not release frozen assets under UNSCR 1267 without UN Sanctions Committee approval.    g. Not release frozen assets under UNSCR 1373 without authorization from the Nigerian Sanctions Committee.    h. Cooperate with Court freezing orders initiated by the Attorney-General.
amlcft.deadlineType: - Immediate and ongoing upon each list update or designation. - STR and freeze action reports: within 24 hours of detection. - Quarterly audit of sanctions controls recommended.
amlcft.riskDescription: - Failure to freeze designated assets promptly exposes the bank to regulatory sanctions, reputational damage, and legal consequences. - Inadequate reporting may be considered a violation of national/international sanctions obligations. - Delayed STR filing could result in money laundering or terrorism financing risks going undetected.
amlcft.owner: - Chief Compliance Officer - AML/CFT Compliance Unit - Sanctions Screening Team - Legal Department
amlcft.responsibility: - Chief Compliance Officer - Sanctions Compliance Manager - AML Monitoring & Reporting Unit - Legal & Regulatory Liaison Officer
amlcft.primaryControl: - Deploy real-time sanctions screening tools integrated with updated UN and Nigeria Sanctions Lists. - Maintain and test automated freeze mechanisms on customer accounts. - Establish 24-hour reporting procedures to the Sanctions Committee and NFIU. - Maintain beneficial ownership registries linked to screening tools. - Train relevant staff on sanctions compliance, freezing protocols, and STR filing. - Ensure legal readiness to respond to freezing orders by the Attorney-General.
amlcft.additionalControl: - Subscribe to automated sanctions list updates (e.g., via World-Check, Dow Jones, etc.). - Engage in periodic sanctions audits and penetration testing. - Implement dual controls for freezing decisions and STR submission. - Regularly update sanctions risk assessments and report to senior management/board.

amlcft.source: REGULATION FOR THE IMPLEMENTATION OF TARGETED FINANCIAL SANCTIONS ON TERRORISM,TERRORISM FINANCING AND OTHER RELATED MEASURES, 2022.
amlcft.title: Reference to Lists by Financial Institutions, Relevant Non-Financial Institutions and Law Enforcement and Security Agencies.
amlcft.description: (1) All natural and legal persons, including financial institutions, Designate Non-financial Business and Professions and other entities within Nigeria shall review the UN Consolidated List and the Nigeria List prior to conducting any transaction, undertaking any financial Services or entering into any relationship with any person or entity to ascertain whether or not the name of such a person or entity is on the Lists.  (2) Where the name of a person or an entity is confirmed to be on the Lists, the person or entity in possession shall block all funds, assets and any other economic resources, or financial services, identified as;  (a) belonging to or connected with the person or entity on the Lists, whether or not such funds are tied to a particular terrorist act, plot or threat.  (b) wholly or jointly owned or controlled, directly or indirectly, by designated persons or entities;  (c) being derived or generated from funds or other assets owned or controlled directly or indirectly by designated persons or entities;  (d) Belonging to persons or entities acting on behalf of or at the direction of, designated person or entities.  (3) The person or entity in possession of the funds referred to in sub-regulation 13(2) above shall within 24 hours file a “Suspicious Transaction Report” including reports or information on all actions taken to freeze the funds and other economic resources to the Nigeria Financial Intelligence a Unit (“NFIU”) who shall make it available to the Nigeria Sanctions Committee.
amlcft.plain: 1. The Bank shall check the UN Consolidated List and the Nigeria Sanctions List before any transaction or business relationship. 2. If the bank appears on the Lists:    a. Immediately freeze all funds, assets, and economic resources associated with them.    b. Freeze funds/assets jointly or indirectly owned or controlled by the listed person.    c. Freeze any asset derived from the listed person’s funds or assets.    d. Freeze assets of persons acting on behalf of or at the direction of listed entities. 3. The bank must file a Suspicious Transaction Report (STR) with the NFIU within 24 hours, detailing all freezing actions taken.
amlcft.deadlineType: - Before any transaction or relationship is initiated. - Within 24 hours of detecting a name match or taking freezing action, an STR must be submitted to the NFIU.
amlcft.riskDescription: - Failure to reference the lists before transactions may result in the bank facilitating terrorism financing. - Non-freezing of funds or late STR filing constitutes a serious regulatory and criminal breach. - May result in CBN penalties, international sanctions, and reputational damage.
amlcft.owner: - Chief Compliance Officer - AML/CFT Officer - Transaction Monitoring Team - Customer Onboarding/Relationship Team - Legal & Sanctions Liaison Officer
amlcft.responsibility: - Head, Sanctions Compliance Unit - Head, Transaction Monitoring - MLRO (Money Laundering Reporting Officer) - Compliance Monitoring Team - Internal Audit (oversight)
amlcft.primaryControl: - Integrate real-time name screening systems linked to UN and Nigeria Sanctions Lists. - Ensure mandatory screening at onboarding, during transactions, and on ongoing basis. - Establish clear freeze protocols once a name match is detected. - Implement automated triggers to generate STR alerts. - Maintain detailed logs of all actions taken. - Train staff on how to identify name matches and report suspicious transactions.
amlcft.additionalControl: - Perform daily list update checks and system refreshes. - Use fuzzy logic matching algorithms to detect similar names. - Conduct external audits of the sanctions screening process. - Periodically test system accuracy with sample names.

amlcft.source: REGULATION FOR THE IMPLEMENTATION OF TARGETED FINANCIAL SANCTIONS ON TERRORISM,TERRORISM FINANCING AND OTHER RELATED MEASURES, 2022.
amlcft.title: Report by an institution to the NFIU
amlcft.description: (1) Where the institution makes a report to the NFIU under sub-regulations 13(1) and 17(3) of these Regulation, it shall state (a) the information or other matter on which knowledge or suspicion is based;  (b) any information it holds about the person by which the knowledge the person can be identified; and  (c) the nature and amount or quantity of funds or economic resources held by the institution for the person at any time up to 5 years prior to the designation being made.  (2) Where an institution credits a frozen account in accordance with regulation 22 of these Regulations, it shall promptly report the transaction or financial services provided to the NFIU which shall inform the Nigeria Sanctions Committee.
amlcft.plain: 1. When the Bank files a report to the Nigerian Financial Intelligence Unit (NFIU) under sanctions-related regulations (Sections 13(1) or 17(3)):    a. The report must include the basis for suspicion or information that triggered it.    b. It must include details that can help identify the person involved.    c. It must state the nature and quantity of funds/assets held for the person up to five years prior to the designation.  2. If a frozen account is credited (e.g. from legitimate deposits), the bank must promptly report the transaction to the NFIU, which will inform the Nigeria Sanctions Committee.
amlcft.deadlineType: - Immediately upon filing STR or identifying credit activity on frozen accounts. - Lookback period for reporting covers up to 5 years before designation.
amlcft.riskDescription: - Failure to report STRs properly or credit activity on frozen accounts can expose the bank to regulatory sanctions, criminal liability, and reputational damage. - Lack of historical transaction tracking increases the risk of non-compliance with 5-year lookback obligations.
amlcft.owner: - Money Laundering Reporting Officer (MLRO) - Compliance Unit - Head of Operations - Sanctions Monitoring Officer
amlcft.responsibility: - Chief Compliance Officer - Head, AML/CFT Unit - MLRO - Internal Audit (Oversight)
amlcft.primaryControl: - Maintain a centralised STR reporting protocol. - Ensure automated transaction monitoring on frozen accounts. - Retain records of client transactions for at least 5 years. - Incorporate alerts for post-designation credits into core banking system. - Set up internal approvals and escalation protocol before allowing any transaction on frozen accounts.
amlcft.additionalControl: - Automate historical data pulls to trace prior relationship with designated entities. - Conduct periodic audits to ensure frozen account activities are properly reviewed and reported. - Create a dedicated sanctions alert dashboard.

amlcft.source: REGULATION FOR THE IMPLEMENTATION OF TARGETED FINANCIAL SANCTIONS ON TERRORISM,TERRORISM FINANCING AND OTHER RELATED MEASURES, 2022.
amlcft.title: Receipt of additional funds into frozen accounts
amlcft.description: (1) Any sum of monies or funds accruing to the frozen account, including –  (a) interests or other earnings due on the account;  (b) payments due under contracts, agreements or obligations that were concluded or arose before the account became a frozen account; or  shall be received and credited into a designated account opened for the purpose and shall constitute part of the frozen funds and the relevant Institution shall file a report of the receipt of such additional funds with the NFIU which shall in turn inform the Nigeria Sanctions Committee accordingly.
amlcft.plain: 1. If a frozen account receives additional funds, such as:    a. Interest or other earnings on the frozen account;    b. Payments due under existing contracts, agreements, or obligations that predate the account’s freezing;  2. The funds must be credited into a designated account created for that purpose. 3. The bank shall report the receipt of such funds to the Nigerian Financial Intelligence Unit (NFIU).
amlcft.deadlineType: - Immediately upon receipt of additional funds into a frozen account. - Report to NFIU without delay after such credit occurs.
amlcft.riskDescription: - Failure to properly credit or report such receipts could result in regulatory sanctions or criminal liability. - Commingling of frozen funds with unrestricted funds can violate asset freezing obligations. - Delay in reporting may expose the bank to non-compliance risk under anti-terrorism laws.
amlcft.owner: - Account Services Unit - Compliance Unit - AML/CFT Officer - Money Laundering Reporting Officer (MLRO)
amlcft.responsibility: - Chief Compliance Officer - Head, Transaction Monitoring - AML Reporting Unit - Internal Audit (oversight on reporting compliance)
amlcft.primaryControl: - Maintain a designated frozen account structure. - Set automated alerts for incoming credits on frozen accounts. - Segregate earnings or receipts tied to frozen accounts into distinct sub-ledgers. - Ensure prompt STR reporting protocols and NFIU notification workflow.
amlcft.additionalControl: - Periodic reconciliation of frozen account balances with reported inflows. - Use of automated sanction screening engines on all account activity. - Train operations and treasury teams on fund handling rules for frozen accounts. - Ensure audit trail for all frozen fund transactions.

amlcft.source: National Identity Management Commission (NIMC) Act, 2007 (As Amended)
amlcft.title: Mandatory Use of NIN for Transactions
amlcft.description: (1) As from the date specified in that regard in regulations made by the Commission, the NATIONAL IDENTIFICATION NUMBER issued to a registered individual must be presented for the following transactions, that is :  (b) opening of individual and or personal bank accounts ;  (h) all consumer credit transactions ;  (j) payment of taxes ;  (2) Any authority or organisation to which a person applies to carry out any transaction listed under subsection (1) of this section shall request such person to produce his National Identification Number. Unauthorised access, refusal to give information etc.
amlcft.plain: The Bank shall ensure that individuals present a valid NIN before carrying out the following transactions: - (b) Opening of individual or personal bank accounts - (h) All consumer credit transactions - (l) Payment of taxes through the bank  The Bank is required to request and verify the NIN before proceeding with any of these transactions, in line with NIMC regulations.
amlcft.deadlineType: Immediate / Ongoing
amlcft.riskDescription: Regulatory penalties and transaction reversals if NIN is not collected or validated.

amlcft.responsibility: Head, Operations
amlcft.primaryControl: Embed NIN check in onboarding and transaction systems.
amlcft.additionalControl: Periodic compliance checks; system validation alerts

amlcft.source: Circular on Tier 1 Wallets and Accounts, Guidance Note, and Profiling of All Customer Accounts/Wallets (PSM/DIR/PUB/CIR/001/053)
amlcft.title: Circular
amlcft.description: the CBN hereby issues an amendment to Section 1.5.3 of the Regulatory Framework for Bank Verification Number (BVN) Operations and Watch-List for the Nigerian Banking Industry (The Guidelines).  In this regard:  1. it is mandatory for ALL Tier-1 bank accounts and wallets for individuals to have BVN and/or NIN;  2. it remains mandatory for Tiers 2 & 3 accounts and wallets for Individual accounts to have BVN and NIN;  3. the process for account opening shall commence by electronically retrieving BVN or NIN related information from the NIBSS’ BVN or NIMC’s NIN databases and for same to become the primary information for onboarding of new customers, and  4. all existing customer accounts/wallets for individuals with validated BVN shall be profiled in the NIBSS’ ICAD immediately and within 24hrs of opening accounts/wallets.
amlcft.plain: The Bank shall:  1. Ensure all Tier-1 individual bank accounts and wallets have either BVN or NIN.  2. Ensure all Tier-2 and Tier-3 individual accounts and wallets have both BVN and NIN.  3. Begin the account opening process by electronically retrieving customer data from NIBSS (BVN) or NIMC (NIN) and use this as the primary onboarding information.  4. For existing individual accounts/wallets with validated BVN, profile the account in the NIBSS’ ICAD system within 24 hours of opening.
amlcft.deadlineType: Ongoing
amlcft.riskDescription: Failure to comply may result in regulatory sanctions, account restrictions, or risk of onboarding fraudulent or unverifiable customers.
amlcft.owner: Compliance / KYC / Operations Teams
amlcft.responsibility: KYC Operations + IT/Tech Team
amlcft.primaryControl: Tiered KYC framework, BVN/NIN verification system, onboarding SOPs, access to NIBSS/NIMC APIs
amlcft.additionalControl: Enforce real-time validations during onboarding; auto-sync with ICAD; monitor exceptions through daily compliance dashboards.

amlcft.source: Regulatory Framework for Bank Verification Number (BVN) Operations and Watch-List for the Nigerian Financial System, October, 2021
amlcft.title: Banks and Financial Institution
amlcft.description: vi. Report the BVNs of individuals in breach to NIBSS for update on the Watch-list within 1 business day of breach; vii. Report the BVNs of confirmed deceased customers to NIBSS for designation as “DECEASED” on the BVN database within 24hrs of confirmation; viii. Use the Watch-list report submitted by participants and duly endorsed by the MD/CEO of the Institution, with clearance from the Director, Risk Management Department of CBN to delist the BVN from the watch-list; ix. Notify NIBSS for enlisting individuals involved in established breaches signed by the Chief Audit Executive; x. Where a participant needs to watch-list a customer of another bank, the Chief Audit Executive of the customer’s bank shall be notified; xi. The Chief Audit Executive of the customer’s bank, upon notification of a breach, shall investigate within one (1) month and after confirmation of the breach, request for the watch-list of the customers’ BVN within two (2) business days. The investigating bank shall inform the requesting bank of its action on the customer. A copy of the finalized report of the internal investigation should be sent to CBN, through the Director, Risk Management Department; xii. Request for the Delisting of individuals from the Watch-list, after clearance from the CBN; xiii. Integrate the banking application to the Watch-list, for online identification/verification of watch-listed individuals as transactions occur; xiv. Enforce appropriate sanctions on customers’ accounts/wallets (except Tier 1) as stipulated in the sanctions grid; xv. Update the terms and conditions of account/wallet opening forms with the following disclaimer for new accounts and communicate the update to existing customers:
amlcft.plain: The Bank shall: vi. Report BVNs of individuals who breach guidelines to NIBSS within 1 business day. vii. Report BVNs of confirmed deceased customers to NIBSS within 24 hours for tagging as “DECEASED”. viii. Use only Watch-list reports endorsed by MD/CEO and cleared by CBN Risk Management Department for BVN delisting. ix. Notify NIBSS for listing individuals involved in verified breaches, with reports signed by the Chief Audit Executive. x. amlcft.title: BVN Operational Processes and Procedures
amlcft.description: These are:   i. Enrollment:  This is the process where individuals have their biometric and demographic data captured in the BVN database.   ii. Identification: This refers to the comparison of an individual's biometrics against the BVN database to confirm the individual had not been previously enrolled and a BVN generated.   iii. Verification: This refers to the process of authenticating the customer by matching his/her biometric template with what had been captured in the database.   iv. Issuance: Following the generation of the BVN, the customer shall be notified of the BVN by the capturing institution through any of the following: card, voucher, email, SMS, letter, etc. v. Linking of Customer’s BVN to all related accounts/wallets (except Tier 1): This is a process of using the customer’s BVN generated after his/her enrolment to link accounts/wallets (except Tier 1) to which he or she is a signatory, after validation. No new account/wallet (except Tier 1) shall be allowed to operate without BVN (except inflows), however, any account/wallet (except Tier 1) without BVN shall be closed within 30 days. vi  Delinking of Customer’s BVN from accounts/wallets (except Tier 1):  This is the process of removing the BVN of a signatory (except for Directors/  Beneficial owners) that is linked to an account/wallet (except Tier 1). The BVN shall be delinked upon the approval of the Chief Audit Executive of  the customer’s bank. This delinking process is for corporate or joint accounts and for activities not associated with breaches. Returns on  delinked accounts/wallets (except Tier 1) shall be rendered to the  Director, Payments System Management Department on a monthly basis. Where there is no linked account a nil report should be submitted vii. Fraud Management: This is a process aimed at using BVN to deter, prevent, detect and mitigate the risks of fraud in the banking industry. viii. Customer Information Update: This is the process by which the customer’s information can be updated on the BVN database.
amlcft.plain: The Bank shall: i. Enroll customers by capturing their biometric and demographic data into the BVN database. ii. Identify customers by checking their biometrics against the BVN database to ensure they have not been previously enrolled. iii. Verify customers by matching their biometric data with what is stored in the database. iv. Notify customers of their BVN after generation via card, voucher, email, SMS, or letter. v. Link customers’ BVNs to all related accounts/wallets (excluding Tier 1). No new Tier 2 or 3 account/wallet shall operate without BVN (except inflows). Close any account/wallet (except Tier 1) without BVN within 30 days. vi. Delink a customer’s BVN from corporate or joint accounts (excluding Tier 1) only with approval from the Chief Audit Executive. Submit monthly reports (including nil reports) on delinked accounts to the Director, Payments System Management Department. vii. Use the BVN system to prevent, detect, and mitigate fraud in the banking industry. viii. Update customer information in the BVN database as necessary.

Failure to notify customers or update BVN info can cause service delays and reputational damage. Delinking without proper authorization or non-submission of returns may result in regulatory non-compliance.

Comply with all applicable Nigerian laws when processing BVN information requests, ensuring data privacy and protection.

amlcft.title: Restrictions on the Use of BVN
amlcft.description: The use of BVN shall be restricted only to purposes specified by the CBN. The following shall constitute abuse of the BVN: i. Use of BVN to sanction individuals for non-financial offences; ii. Use of BVN for identification outside the banking system; and iii. Any other misuse, as may be designated by the CBN.
amlcft.plain: The Bank shall: 1) Avoid misusing the BVN in any of the following ways: a) Sanctioning individuals for non-financial offences using their BVN. b) Using BVN for identification purposes outside the banking sector. c) Any other misuse of the BVN as may be defined by the CBN.  2. Implement internal controls to prevent abuse of the BVN and monitor staff and systems for compliance with CBN’s permitted uses.

amlcft.title: Security and Data Protection
amlcft.description: i. Parties involved in the BVN operations shall put in place secure hardware, software and encryption of messages transmitted through a secured network; ii. BVN data shall be stored within the shores of Nigeria and shall not be routed across borders without the consent of the CBN; iii. Users of the BVN information shall establish adequate security procedures to ensure the safety and security of its information and those of its clients, which shall include physical, logical, network and enterprise security; iv. Access to BVN information by customers shall be obtained through secured channels with appropriate authentication; v. BVN participants shall ensure that BVN information is treated as confidential; and vi. All stakeholders shall comply with Nigeria Data Protection Regulation (NDPR) or any regulation of the Bank on data protection and relevant extant laws.
amlcft.plain: The Bank shall: 1. Implement secure systems and infrastructure (hardware, software, and encrypted communications) for all BVN-related operations, ensuring that data is transmitted over a secured network.  2. Store all BVN data within Nigeria, and do not transmit or route data outside Nigeria without obtaining CBN’s explicit consent.  3. Establish comprehensive security procedures to protect both the bank’s and customers’ information. This includes: - Physical security (e.g., restricted areas), - Logical security (e.g., access controls), - Network security (e.g., firewalls, intrusion detection), and - Enterprise security policies (e.g., audits, governance controls).  4. Allow customers to access their BVN information only through secure and authenticated channels, ensuring data integrity and privacy.  5. Treat all BVN information as strictly confidential and ensure that staff and systems prevent unauthorized disclosure or access.  6. Comply fully with the Nigeria Data Protection Regulation (NDPR) and any other data protection regulation issued by the CBN or applicable under Nigerian law.

amlcft.title: Updating Customer's BVN Records
amlcft.description: Change of customer records shall be allowed as follows: i. Correction of date of birth on BVN record shall be allowed once, with supporting documents, evidencing the correct date of birth; ii. Change of Name due to marriage/divorce/religion shall only be allowed with supporting documents, such as marriage certificate/divorce certificate/affidavit, newspaper adverts, etc.; iii. Minor correction of name, due to misspelling shall only be allowed, with supporting documents and regulatory forms of identification such as international passport, driver's licence and NIMC ID, showing the correct name; iv. Change of names that are totally different or partially different shall only be allowed after the customer has produced supporting documents to the change of the name, and this shall be reported to the Nigerian Financial Intelligence Unit (NFIU) as a suspicious act by the participant. The NFIU shall issue appropriate clearance in the case of a totally different name before effecting the change; v. The customer's name on the BVN database shall be the same in all his/her accounts, across the banking industry; vi. Customers who wish to close their accounts/wallets (except Tier 1) shall be allowed to do so. Where the account/wallet (except Tier 1) is not linked with the BVN, a payment instrument shall be issued in the same name in which the account/wallet was opened. In cases where the balance on the account/wallet(except Tier 1) is more than what is legally allowed on a paper instrument (i.e. N10 million) the bank shall seek and obtain clearance from the NFIU before such accounts/wallets(except Tier 1) can be closed and the balance transferred electronically to another account; vii. Timeline for the resolution of BVN issues shall be 5 working days from the date the customer submits all the required documents; and viii. Following corrections/updating of details, the customer shall be notified by the institution that made the changes through any of the following: email, SMS, letter, etc.
amlcft.plain: The Bank shall: 1. Allow BVN record updates only with valid supporting documents:  a) Date of birth corrections: Only once, with official proof. b) Name changes due to marriage, divorce, or religion: Must be supported by legal documents (e.g., marriage certificate, affidavit, newspaper ad). c) Minor name corrections (e.g., spelling errors): Require proper ID (e.g., passport, NIMC, driver’s license). d) Significant name changes: Must be reported to the NFIU as suspicious. Clearance must be obtained from NFIU before updating the BVN.  2. Ensure that a customer’s name on the BVN database is consistent across all bank accounts.  3. amlcft.title: Fair Hearing
amlcft.description: Once a breach is established, in the process of investigation/fair hearing, a customer's account shall be placed on Post-No-Debit (PND), the customer shall be notified through verifiable means within five (5) business days: i. At a minimum, the notification shall clearly state the breach and the consequences which include watch-listing; ii. The customer(s) shall be given the opportunity to present documentary evidence that may affect the decision within three (3) business days; and iii. Where decision to watch-list the BVN is reached, the customer shall be notified through verifiable means.
amlcft.plain: The Bank shall: 1. Place a customer’s account on Post-No-Debit (PND) once a breach is established during an investigation or fair hearing process.  2. Notify the customer of the breach and possible consequences (including watch-listing) within 5 business days via verifiable means (e.g., email, SMS, letter).  3. Give the customer an opportunity to submit relevant documentary evidence that may influence the outcome, within 3 business days of being notified.  4. If a decision to watch-list the BVN is made, notify the customer again through verifiable means.

amlcft.source: Introduction of Three-Tiered Know Your Customer (KYC) Requirements
amlcft.title: Circular (FPR/DIR/CIR/GEN/02/001)
amlcft.description: "Banks and other financial institutions are hereby required to adopt the provisions of the three-tiered KYC requirements as embodied in the attached guidelines in addition to the provisions of the CBN AML/CFT Regulation 2009 (as amended)".   'The "tiered" KYC requirements regime will ensure application of flexible account opening requirements for low-value and medium value accounts and these are subject to caps and restrictions as the amounts of transactions increase. This means that account opening requirements will increase progressively with less restrictions on operations. However, the main objective of the proposed approach is to promote and deepen financial inclusion'. The structure ensures that the accounts remain attractive to customers of different socio-economic levels while close watch is kept on the risk involved. The Guideline circular shows the caps on deposits on the low-value and medium-value accounts.
amlcft.plain: The Bank shall implement the three-tiered Know Your Customer (KYC) requirements as outlined in the CBN guidelines. This includes adopting flexible KYC processes based on account types: low-value, medium-value, and high-value, with progressively stricter requirements and controls as account risk or transaction size increases, in order to support financial inclusion while managing risk.

amlcft.source: Review of Restrictions and Limits on Level I and II of the Tiered KYC Accounts
amlcft.title: Circular (FPR/DIR/CIR/GEN/06/002 dated 1st July, 2016)
amlcft.description: Following representations made by stakeholders for review of the limits and restrictions on the operations of Tiers I and II accounts, the CBN in furtherance of its efforts to deepen financial inclusion, has reviewed upward the current transaction limits on Tier I and II accounts as shown below:  Single Deposit - N50,000, Cumulative Balance - N300,000 --- Tier 1 Single Deposit - N100,000, Cumulative Balance - N500,000 --- Tier 2
amlcft.plain: The Bank shall implement the revised transaction limits for Tier 1 and Tier 2 accounts as follows:  a) Tier 1 Accounts: Limit single deposits to ₦50,000 and ensure the cumulative balance does not exceed ₦300,000 at any time.  b) Tier 2 Accounts: Limit single deposits to ₦100,000 and ensure the cumulative balance does not exceed ₦500,000.

amlcft.title: Customer  Due  Diligence measures
amlcft.description: (1) FIs shall undertake CDD measures when— (a) establishing business relationships ; (b) carrying out occasional transactions above the applicable and designated threshold of US$1,000 or its equivalent in other currencies or as may be determined by the CBN from time to time, including where the  transaction is carried out in a single or several transactions or operations that appear to be linked ; (c) carrying out occasional transactions that are wire transfers, including cross-border and domestic transfers between FIs and when credit or debit cards are used as a payment method to effect money transfer ; (d) there are doubts as to the veracity or adequacy of previously obtained customer identification data ; or (e) there is a suspicion of ML, TF and PF regardless of any exemptions or any other thresholds referred to in these Regulations or the CBN AML, CFT and CPF Regulations. (2) FIs shall establish internal processes and procedures for conducting CDD measures for all potential and existing customers, including occasional customers. (3) CDD measures shall include — (a) customer identification and verification of identity ; (b) identification and verification of identity of beneficial owners (BOs) ; (c) understanding nature and purpose of business ; (d) understanding the sources of funds ; and (e) conducting ongoing due diligence on the business relationship and monitoring for suspicious activities.
amlcft.plain: The Bank shall:  1. Perform Customer Due Diligence (CDD) when:  a) Opening a new account or establishing any business relationship; b) Processing occasional transactions above US$1,000 or equivalent, whether in one or multiple linked transactions; c) Handling any wire transfers (domestic or cross-border), especially where cards are used to transfer money; d) There are doubts about the accuracy or sufficiency of previously obtained customer data; e) There is any suspicion of money laundering (ML), terrorism financing (TF), or proliferation financing (PF) — regardless of thresholds.  2. Set up internal processes and procedures to conduct CDD for both potential and existing customers, including walk-in or occasional users.  3. Include the following CDD steps:  a) Identify the customer and verify their identity; b) Identify the beneficial owner (BO) and verify their identity; c) Understand the nature and purpose of the customer's business; d) Understand the source of funds; e) Continuously monitor the business relationship and screen for suspicious activities.

amlcft.title: Customer identification
amlcft.description: FIs shall identify their customer (whether permanent or occasional,and whether natural or legal persons or legal arrangements) and obtain the following information — (a) for Individuals — (i) legal name and any other names used (such as maiden name), (ii) permanent address (full physical address), (iii) residential address (where the customer can be located), (iv) telephone number, e-mail address and social media handle, (v) date and place of birth, (vi) Bank Verification Number (BVN), (vii) Tax Identification Number (TIN), (viii) nationality, (ix) occupation, public position held and name of employer, (x) an official personal identification number or other unique identifier contained in an unexpired document issued by a government agency, that bears a name, photograph and signature of the customer such as a passport, national identification card, residence permit, social security records or drivers’ license, (xi) type of account and nature of the banking relationship, and (xii) signature, and (xiii) politically exposed persons (PEPs) status ;
amlcft.plain: The Bank shall collect and verify full identification information for every individual customer, whether they are permanent or occasional. This applies to all natural persons opening an account or conducting transactions. The required information includes: 1. Full legal name and any other names used (e.g., maiden name) 2. Permanent and residential address 3. Telephone number, email address, and social media handle 4. Date and place of birth 5. Bank Verification Number (BVN) 6. Tax Identification Number (TIN) 7. Nationality 8. Occupation, public position held, and employer name 9. A valid government-issued ID with photo, name, and signature (e.g., passport, driver’s license, national ID) 10. Type of account and purpose of the banking relationship 11. Customer’s signature 12. Politically Exposed Person (PEP) status  The Bank must ensure that all the above information is properly documented and verified during account opening or onboarding, in compliance with KYC and AML/CFT requirements

amlcft.plain: The Bank shall collect and verify detailed information before opening an account for any legal entity or legal arrangement (e.g., companies, partnerships, NGOs, trusts). The following information must be obtained and documented: 1. Name of the institution or entity 2. Mailing address 3. Email address and social media handle 4. Phone numbers 5. Corporate registration number 6. Registered address 7. Business/operational address 8. Valid legal identifier, such as a Tax Identification Number (TIN) 9. Nature and purpose of the business or legal activity 10. Certified true copy of incorporation documents (e.g., certificate of incorporation) 11. Certified true copy of the memorandum and articles of association (or similar founding documents) 12. Certified true copy of the list of directors and shareholders (or similar documentation) 13. Board resolution authorizing the opening of the account 14. Identification of authorized signatories (those allowed to operate the account) 15. Legal documents identifying persons who control or influence the entity’s assets (e.g., beneficial owners, trustees) 16. Valid ID documents for those individuals identified in item 15 17. Names and valid ID documents of all individuals in senior management positions 18. The Bank must sight and retain the original versions of all documents listed in items 10–14.  All this information must be collected, verified, and securely documented to establish the legitimacy, control structure, and risk profile of the legal entity. amlcft.title: Verification of customer identity
amlcft.description: —(1) FIs shall verify the identity of customers and BOs using reliable, independent source documents, data or information (identification data). (2) FIs shall verify the identity of individuals by confirming the — (a) date of birth from a valid official document, such as birth certificate, passport, identity card and national or social security records ; Verification of customer identity (b) residential address through physical visitation and use of other sources, including utility bill, tax assessment, bank statement, or letter from a public authority ; (c) contact details provided by the customer through positive feedback from phone call, email or physical letter to the residential address ; (d) validity of the official documentation provided through certification by an authorized person such as embassy official, notary public (in the case of foreign nationals) ; and (e) phone numbers, particularly for wallet providers, through independent process, including validation against the NCC database or geo-mapping.
amlcft.plain: The Bank shall:  1. Verify the identity of all customers and beneficial owners (BOs) using reliable and independent sources (e.g. official documents, databases, or information).  2. For individual customers, the Bank must:  a) Confirm date of birth using a valid official document (e.g. passport, birth certificate, identity card, national/social security record). b) Verify residential address through physical visit or by using supporting documents (e.g. utility bill, tax record, bank statement, public authority letter). c) Confirm contact details (phone, email, or address) through positive feedback such as response to calls, emails, or letters. d) Confirm authenticity of official documents by certification from authorized persons (e.g. embassy, notary) especially for foreign nationals. e) For wallet providers, verify phone numbers using independent means, like the Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC) database or geo-mapping.

amlcft.description: (3) FIs shall verify the identity of a legal person or legal arrangement by — (a) undertaking search on public registry or database such as CAC or similar database, other commercial enquiries and through any other available sources of information to confirm — (i) the existence of the legal person or legal arrangement, (ii) whether the legal person or legal arrangement has not been, or is not in the process of being dissolved, struck off, wound up or terminated, (iii) the information on the directors and shareholders or persons or entities holding similar positions, including their PEP status, (iv) information on person with significant control, and (v) information on BO, and its PEP status ; (b) reviewing a copy of the latest annual report, audited accounts or relevant financial statement, where applicable ; (c) reviewing a copy of the board resolution or applicable resolution ; (d) utilizing the documentation from a reliable independent source proving the name, form and current existence of the customer ; (e) utilizing an independent information verification process, such as accessing public and private databases ; (f ) obtaining prior bank references, where applicable ; (g) visiting the entity ; and (h) confirming the contact details provided through phone call, email and physical letter to the business address.
amlcft.plain: The Bank shall verify the identity of legal persons (e.g. companies, partnerships, foundations) or legal arrangements (e.g. trusts) by:  1. Conducting searches in public registries or databases (e.g. CAC) or other credible sources to confirm:  a) That the entity exists;  b) That it is not being wound up, struck off, or dissolved;  c) The identity of directors, shareholders, or persons in similar roles, including whether they are politically exposed persons (PEPs); d) The identity of persons with significant control (PSC); e) The identity of beneficial owners (BOs) and whether they are PEPs.  2. Reviewing key documents, where applicable:  a) Most recent audited financial statements or annual report; b) Board or organizational resolutions.  3. Using independent documents or sources to confirm:  a) The entity's name, legal form, and current existence; b) Contact details (e.g. via phone call, email, or physical letter to the business address).  4. Carrying out additional verification, such as:  a) Accessing public/private databases; b) Obtaining bank references, where applicable; c) Visiting the entity’s business location.

amlcft.title: Identification and verification of signatories, directors, and  beneficial owners of legal persons and legal arrangements
amlcft.description: When conducting CDD measures in relation to customers that are legal persons or legal arrangements, FIs shall — (a) understand the ownership and control structure ; (b) at the time of establishing new relationships or whenever there is a change in ownership, identify and verify the identity of the BOs who exercise control through ownership or controlling interest, including voting rights ; (c) subject all account signatories, Directors and BOs to the requirements for identification and verification of individuals provided in regulations 6 and 7 of these Regulations ; (d) conduct status enquiry from CRMS and at least two Credit Bureaux to determine their credit status ; (e) ascertain that the customer is not banned from the use of clearing system due to issuance of dud cheque ; and
amlcft.plain: The Bank shall ensure that when dealing with legal entities or arrangements (e.g., companies, trusts), it:  1. Understands the ownership and control structure of the entity.  2. Identifies and verifies the beneficial owners (BOs) — i.e., those who ultimately control the entity, especially those with ownership or voting rights, at onboarding or whenever there is a change in ownership.  3. Ensures all account signatories, directors, and BOs are subjected to individual identification and verification requirements (as stated in Regulations 6 and 7).  4. Checks credit status of signatories, directors, and BOs through credit Risk Management System (CRMS); and at least two licensed Credit Bureaux.  5. Confirms that the customer is not banned from the NIBSS clearing system due to issuance of dud cheques.

amlcft.title: Application of CDD to existing customers
amlcft.description: (1) FIs shall apply CDD requirements to existing customers on the basis of materiality and risk and continue to conduct due diligence on such existing relationship at appropriate times. (2) The appropriate time to conduct CDD for existing customers include, but not limited to when — (a) transaction of significant value or an unusual transaction occurs ; (b) there is significant change in the customer’s profile ; (c) there is a material change in the way that the account is operated ; or (d) the FIs become aware that it lacks sufficient information about an existing customer.
amlcft.plain: The Bank shall:  1. Apply customer due diligence (CDD) measures to existing customers based on risk level and materiality.  2. Conduct periodic CDD reviews for existing customers, especially when:  a) A high-value or unusual transaction occurs. b) There is a significant change in the customer’s profile (e.g., business activity or ownership). c) There is a material change in how the account is operated. d) The Bank realizes it does not have sufficient information about the customer.

amlcft.title: Risk Based Approach to CDD
amlcft.description: (1)  FIs shall conduct initial risk assessment for each prospective customer to ascertain the customer’s risk profile.  (2) The application of CDD measures may be standard, simplified or enhanced depending on the risks posed by each customer, transaction, products or service resulting from a customer risk assessment.  (3)  For low risks customers —  (a)  FIs may adopt simplified CDD measures only where lower risks have been identified through an adequate assessment and analysis of the risks, and the simplified CDD measures shall be forwarded to the CBN for approval before implementation by the FI ;  (b)  notwithstanding the application of simplified CDD on customer identification and verification, the customer is not exempt from ongoing monitoring for other CDD measures ;  (c)  the simplified measures shall be commensurate with the lower risk factors but are not acceptable whenever there is suspicion of ML, TF or PF, or where specific higher risk scenarios apply.  (4)  For high risks customers —  (a)  arising from an initial assessment of a customer, particular attention shall be focused on those customers identified as having a higher risk profile ;  (b)   customers with higher risk profile include, but not limited to, non resident customers, MVTS providers, private banking customers, non-face to-face customers, and PEPs ;  (c)  FIs shall apply enhanced CDD measures to business relationships and transactions with natural and legal persons, and FIs, from countries forwhich this is called for by the FATF ; and  (d)  FIs shall conduct enhanced CDD.
amlcft.plain: The Bank shall:  1. Conduct an initial risk assessment for every prospective customer to determine their risk profile.  2. Apply appropriate CDD measures—standard, simplified, or enhanced—based on the risk level of the customer, transaction, product, or service.  3. For low-risk customers:  a) Adopt simplified CDD measures only after conducting a proper risk analysis and obtaining CBN approval before implementation. b) Continue ongoing monitoring, even where simplified CDD is applied. c) Ensure simplified CDD is proportional to the risk and not applied where there is a suspicion of money laundering (ML), terrorist financing (TF), proliferation financing (PF), or where higher-risk scenarios are identified.  4. For high-risk customers:  a) Give special attention to customers identified with a higher risk profile during the initial assessment. b) Recognise higher-risk customers to include non-residents, money/value transfer service (MVTS) providers, private banking clients, non-face-to-face customers, and politically exposed persons (PEPs). c) Apply enhanced CDD to these customers and to business relationships involving entities or individuals from countries flagged by the FATF.  d) Carry out enhanced due diligence throughout the business relationship with high-risk customers.
amlcft.deadlineType: Ongoing
amlcft.riskDescription: Failure to properly apply risk-based CDD may result in:- Exposure to money laundering or terrorist financing risks- Regulatory sanctions- Onboarding of high-risk clients without adequate safeguards

amlcft.responsibility: Head, ComplianceHead, RiskHead, Retail/Corporate Banking
amlcft.primaryControl: - Customer Risk Assessment Tool- Automated KYC/CDD workflow- Risk profiling in account opening systems- Ongoing transaction monitoring tools
amlcft.additionalControl: - Periodic customer risk re-assessment- Pre-approval workflow for simplified CDD by Compliance and CBN- Enhanced training on high-risk indicators and PEP screening

amlcft.title: Three tiered Know-your-Customer
amlcft.description: (1)  FIs shall comply with Tiered KYC measures as stipulated in the CBN circulars on TKYC and the CBN AML, CFT and CPF Regulations.  (2)  Tiered KYC shall apply to individuals only and shall not apply to legal persons and legal arrangements.
amlcft.plain: The Bank shall:  1. Implement Three-Tiered KYC (TKYC) procedures as outlined in CBN Circulars on TKYC, and the CBN AML, CFT and CPF Regulations.  2. Apply Tiered KYC only to individual customers and do not apply TKYC to legal persons (e.g., companies) or legal arrangements (e.g., trusts or partnerships).

amlcft.title: Enhanced CDD
amlcft.description: —(1)  FIs shall perform enhanced CDD for customers, business relationship or transactions with higher ML, TF, and PF risks.  (2)  The enhanced CDD shall include, but not limited to —  (a)  obtaining additional information on the customer including occupation, volume of assets, information available through public databases, internet, and updating more regularly the identification data of the customer and BO ;  (b)  obtaining additional information on the intended nature of the business relationship ;  (c)  obtaining information on the source of funds and source of wealth o  the customer ;  (d)  obtaining information on the reasons for intended or performed transactions;  (e)  obtaining the approval of senior management to commence or continue the business relationship ;  (f )  conducting enhanced monitoring of the business relationship, by  increasing the number and timing of controls applied, and selecting patterns of transactions that need further examination ; and  (g)  requiring the first payment to be carried out through an account in the customer’s name with a bank subject to similar CDD standards.
amlcft.plain: The Bank shall:  1. Apply enhanced CDD to customers, business relationships, or transactions that pose a high risk of Money Laundering (ML), Terrorist Financing (TF), or Proliferation Financing (PF).  2. As part of enhanced CDD, the Bank shall:  (a) Collect additional customer information such as: Occupation, Volume of assets, Publicly available data (e.g., databases, internet), Regularly updated identity and beneficial ownership details. (b) Obtain extra information on the intended nature of the business relationship. (c) Verify source of funds and source of wealth of the customer. (d) Understand the purpose of intended or actual transactions. (e) Obtain senior management approval before starting or continuing the relationship. (f) Conduct enhanced monitoring of the relationship by: increasing the frequency and scope of controls, examining transaction patterns more closely.  (g) Ensure that the first payment is made from an account in the customer's name held with a bank that also applies similar CDD standards.
amlcft.deadlineType: Ongoing

amlcft.title: Reliance on identification and verification already performed
amlcft.description: (1) FIs may rely on the identification and verification steps that it had previously undertaken, unless it has doubts about the veracity of that information or where there is a material change in the circumstances or profile of the customer. (2) The situations that may lead a FI to have doubts about the veracity of an information include where there is a — (a) suspicion of ML, TF or PF in relation to that customer ; or (b) material change in the way that the customer’s account is operated, which is not consistent with the customer’s business profile.
amlcft.plain: The Bank shall: 1. May rely on previously conducted customer identification and verification only if: a) There are no doubts about the accuracy or truthfulness of the information.  b) There is no material change in the customer’s profile or circumstances.  2. Re-verify the customer’s identity and information when: a) There is a suspicion of money laundering (ML), terrorist financing (TF), or proliferation financing (PF). b) There is a significant change in how the account is being used, inconsistent with the customer’s known business profile.

amlcft.title: Inability to undertake CDD
amlcft.description: 19.—(1)  A  FI that is unable to comply with the CDD measures pursuant  to these Regulations shall—   (a)  not be permitted to open the account, commence business relations  or perform the transaction with the concerned persons ; and   (b)  be required to render a Suspicious Transaction Report (STR) to the  Nigerian Financial Intelligence Unit (NFIU).        (2)  An FI that has commenced the business relationship prior to the conduct of CDD shall terminate the business relationship and render STR to the NFIU.   (3)  Where an FI suspects that transactions relate to money laundering, ,terrorism financing or proliferation financing, during the establishment or course of the customer relationship, or when conducting occasional transactions, it shall immediately, and without delay —   (a) obtain and verify the identity of the customer and the BO, whether permanent or occasional, irrespective of any exemption or any designated threshold that might otherwise apply ; and   (b) render an STR to the NFIU immediately.   (4)  FIs and their employees shall maintain confidentiality in respect of  any STR that may be filed with the NFIU and shall not do anything that may “tip off” any person or entity that is under suspicion of ML, TF or PF.
amlcft.plain: The Bank shall:  1. Not open accounts, begin relationships, or process transactions where CDD cannot be completed.   2. Immediately file a Suspicious Transaction Report (STR) to the NFIU in such cases.   3. If a relationship began before CDD completion, terminate it and file an STR.   4. Where ML/TF/PF is suspected, promptly identify and verify customer and BO, regardless of any exemptions.   5. File an STR without delay when suspicion arises.   6. Maintain strict confidentiality regarding STRs, and avoid tipping off subjects.

amlcft.title: Reliance on third party
amlcft.description: (1) In addition to the provisions of regulation 27 of the CBN AML, CFT and CPF Regulations where a FI relies on other FIs and DNFBPs to conduct its CDD, it shall — (a) immediately obtain the necessary information concerning the identification and verification of the customer and BO and the purpose and intended nature of the business relationship ; (b) take adequate steps to satisfy itself that copies of identification data and other relevant documentation relating to the CDD requirements is going to be made available from the third party upon request without delay ; (c) satisfy itself that the third party is regulated, supervised or monitored for, and has measures in place for compliance with, the CDD and record keeping requirements set out in these Regulations and the CBN AML, CFT and CPF Regulations ; and (d) ensure that adequate KYC provisions are applied to the third party in order to obtain account information for competent authorities. (2) Notwithstanding the conditions specified in sub-regulation (1) (a) to (d) of this regulation, the ultimate responsibility for customer identification and verification shall be with the FI relying on the third party.
amlcft.plain: The Bank shall:  1. If relying on another financial institution (FI) or Designated Non-Financial Business or Profession (DNFBP) to perform CDD, it must:  a) Immediately obtain customer and beneficial owner (BO) identification and verification details, and information on the business relationship’s purpose and nature. b) Ensure copies of all CDD documents can be accessed promptly from the third party upon request. c) Confirm the third party is regulated and supervised, and complies with CDD and recordkeeping obligations under the NDPR and CBN AML/CFT/CPF Regulations. d) Ensure proper KYC measures are in place to enable competent authorities to access required account information.  2. Understand that the Bank remains ultimately responsible for verifying the customer’s identity, even when relying on a third party.

amlcft.description: (1) Where a FI suspects that a transaction relates to ML, TF or PF and it believes that performing the CDD process may tip-off the customer, it shall— (a) not pursue the CDD process ; and  (2) FIs shall ensure that their employees are aware of, and sensitive to, the issues referred to in subregulation (1) of this regulation when conducting CDD.

Ensure that employees are trained and aware of tipping-off risks when performing CDD.

amlcft.title: Record-Keeping
amlcft.description: In addition to the provisions of regulation 35 of the CBN AML, CFT and CPF Regulations, FIs shall — (a) keep all records obtained through CDD measures, account files and business correspondence, and results of any analysis undertaken, either in electronic or written form for at least five years following the termination or cessation of the business relationship or after the date of the occasional transaction ; and (b) ensure that documents, data or information collected under the CDD process is kept up-to-date and relevant, by undertaking reviews of existing records of customers as stipulated below or whenever the need arises, (i) for high risk customers, every 12months, (ii) for medium risk customers, every 18months, and (iii) for low risk customers, every 3years.
amlcft.plain: The Bank shall:  1. Maintain all CDD records (including account files, correspondence, and analysis results) in either electronic or written form for at least 5 years after:  a) The end of the business relationship, or b) The date of an occasional transaction.  2. Keep CDD documents and information up-to-date and relevant by conducting regular reviews:  a) Every 12 months for high-risk customers, b) Every 18 months for medium-risk customers, c) Every 3 years for low-risk customers,

amlcft.title: External and Non-Resident Non-Nigerians Accounts
amlcft.description: (1) In line with Memorandum 17 of the CBN Foreign Exchange Manual, FI shall satisfy itself that a customer is permanently resident outside Nigeria when establishing a banking relationship for external and non-resident non-Nigerian customers. (2) The following are eligible to open external accounts— (a) Embassies; (b) High Commissions; (c) Legations or consulates; (d) career and established members of Embassies, High Commissions, and Legation or Consulates; and (e) other international organisations recognized and accorded diplomatic status and their expatriate officials, such as African Union, United Nations or Commonwealth of Nations. (3) FIs shall obtain the following documentation for external accounts— (a) applicant’s letter of request, showing official position or status and the probable duration of stay in Nigeria; (b) letter of introduction from the relevant Diplomatic Mission or International Organisation certifying the accredited status of the applicant; and (c) relevant pages of the applicant’s international passport. (4) The following are eligible to open non-resident accounts— (a) overseas correspondence and examination bodies; (b) foreign companies executing approved contracts in Nigeria; and (c) foreign professional bodies. (5) FIs shall obtain the following documentation for non-resident accounts— (a) for overseas correspondence and examination bodies, letters of request from applicant, memorandum and articles of the overseas company, letter of accreditation from the Federal Ministry of Education, and Power of Attorney to the Agent in Nigeria; (b) for foreign companies executing approved contracts in Nigeria, contract document, letter of request from applicant, and Memorandum and Articles of Association of the company; and (c) for foreign professional bodies, letters of request from applicant, memorandum and articles of the overseas company, letter of accreditation from the Federal Ministry of Education, Power of Attorney to the Agent in Nigeria and letter of certification from a relevant body in Nigeria. (6) FIs shall— (a) obtain and verify identification directly from the customer’s embassy or through a reputable FI in the applicant’s home country or country of residence, provided that particular care shall be taken when relying on identification evidence obtained from other countries. (b) obtain and verify separate evidence of an applicant’s permanent residential address which shall be notarized; and (c) obtain additional comfort by confirming the customer’s identity and address from a reputable credit institution in the customer’s home country, where necessary (9) Where approvals are granted for individuals (including directors of legal persons) that are non-Nigerian and non-resident, the requirements of regulations 6 and 7 of these Regulations shall apply and the appropriate category of BVN as relates to non-resident individuals shall apply.
amlcft.plain: The Bank shall: 1. Confirm that external or non-resident non-Nigerian customers are permanently resident outside Nigeria, per CBN guidelines.  2. Open external accounts only for Embassies, diplomatic staff, and recognized international organisations (e.g., UN, AU).  3. For external accounts, collect: a) Request letter (with official role and duration), b) Introduction from the embassy/organisation, c) International passport pages.  4. Open non-resident accounts only for overseas exam bodies, foreign contractors, and professional bodies.  5. Collect required documents based on account type: a) Exam bodies: request letter, incorporation docs, Ministry accreditation, power of attorney. b) Contractors: contract, request letter, incorporation docs. c) Professional bodies: same as above plus certification from a Nigerian body.  6. Verify identity via the customer’s embassy or a reputable financial institution abroad.  7. Obtain and notarize proof of permanent address.  8. If necessary, confirm identity and address through a credit institution in the home country.  9. For non-resident individuals (incl. directors): a) Apply CDD and beneficial ownership checks (Reg. 6 & 7), b) Register them with the appropriate non-resident BVN category.

amlcft.title: Correspondent Banking Relationship
amlcft.description: (1) Transactions conducted through correspondent relationships shall be managed in accordance with a risk-based approach. (2) Due diligence procedures shall be established to ascertain whether or not the correspondent bank or the counter-party is itself regulated for prevention of ML, TF or PF, and where regulated, the correspondent respondent shall verify the identity of its customers in accordance with FATF standards. (3) Where the correspondent bank or the counter-party is itself unregulated, additional due diligence shall be required to ascertain and assess the correspondent or respondent’s internal policy for prevention of ML, TF or PF and KYC procedures.  (5) FIs shall maintain records and ensure that sufficient due diligence has been undertaken by the remitting bank on the underlying client and the origin of the funds in respect of the funds passed through their accounts. (6) FIs shall guard against establishing correspondent relationships with high risk foreign banks such as shell banks or with correspondent banks that permit their accounts to be used by such banks. (7) Staff dealing with correspondent banking accounts shall be trained to recognize higher risk circumstances and be prepared to challenge the correspondents over irregular activity whether isolated transactions or trend and to submit a suspicious transaction report to the NFIU.  (8) FIs shall terminate an account with a correspondent bank that fails to provide satisfactory answers to questions including confirming the identity of customers involved in unusual or suspicious circumstances.
amlcft.plain: The Bank shall: 1. Apply a risk-based approach to all transactions conducted through correspondent banking relationships.  2. Conduct due diligence to confirm whether the correspondent bank or counterparty:  a) Is regulated for anti–money laundering (AML), terrorist financing (TF), or proliferation financing (PF), and b) Verifies its own customers’ identities in line with FATF standards.  3. Where the correspondent bank is unregulated, perform enhanced due diligence to assess: a) The bank’s internal AML/CFT policies, and b) Its Know Your Customer (KYC) procedures.  4. Keep proper records and ensure that the remitting bank has conducted due diligence on: a) The underlying client, and b) The source of funds.  5. Avoid relationships with Shell banks, or Banks that allow their accounts to be used by shell banks or other high-risk institutions.  6. Train staff managing correspondent accounts to: a) Identify high-risk activity or trends, b) Challenge suspicious activity, and c) File Suspicious Transaction Reports (STRs) with the NFIU when needed.  7. Terminate correspondent relationships if the correspondent bank: a) Fails to provide satisfactory explanations, or b) Cannot confirm the identity of customers involved in suspicious activities.

amlcft.title: Blind Trusts
amlcft.description: (1) FIs shall obtain and understand the Trust Agreement in a Blind Trust such that the grantor, settlor or trustor and beneficiary are identified. (2) Where the grantor or beneficiary is a PEP, the FI shall apply EDD measures. (3) FIs shall understand the structure of a Blind Trust and determine whether it is revocable or irrevocable. (4) Where the customer is a Revocable Blind Trust, the FI shall apply EDD measures to the customer. (5) FIs shall apply EDD where the BOs of a customer is a Blind Trust and identify the ultimate BO.
amlcft.plain: The Bank shall:  1. Obtain and understand the Trust Agreement of any Blind Trust, ensuring that the:  a) Grantor (settlor/trustor) and b) Beneficiary are clearly identified.  2. If the grantor or beneficiary is a Politically Exposed Person (PEP), apply Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) measures.  3. Understand the legal structure of the Blind Trust and determine whether it is Revocable or Irrevocable.  4. Where the Blind Trust is revocable, apply EDD measures to the customer.  5. Apply EDD if the beneficial owner (BO) of a customer is a Blind Trust, and identify the ultimate BO.

amlcft.title: Minors
amlcft.description: (1) For banking relationships for a minor, FIs shall obtain the birth certificate and passport photo of the minor. (2) FIs shall obtain and verify the identification and home address of the parent or guardian of a minor. (3) For accounts opened through a school-related scheme, the school shall provide the date of birth and permanent address of the minor and complete the standard account opening documentation on behalf of the minor. (4) FIs shall continuously monitor account of a minor to ensure that— (a) it is not used for the purposes of ML or TF; (b) the transactions on the account are in line with the purpose for which the account was opened; and (c) transactions on the account does not exceed a limit pre-determined by the FI in line with its established risk assessment criteria.

amlcft.title: Non-Face-to-Face Customers Identification
amlcft.description: FIs shall— (a) in respect of a non-face-to-face customer, undertake additional measures or checks to supplement the documentary or electronic evidence to ensure that an applicant is who he/she claims to be; (b) apply the additional measures in paragraph (a) of this regulation, whether the applicant is resident in Nigeria or elsewhere, where the applicant is requesting a bank account or other product or service that offers money transmission or third party payments; (c) ensure that there is sufficient evidence either documentary or electronic in its procedures for identification and authentication of its customers, to confirm their address and personal identity and to undertake at least one additional check to guard against impersonation or fraud; (e) undertake checks to ensure that, where reliance is placed on intermediaries to undertake the processing of applications on the customer’s behalf, the intermediaries are regulated for the prevention of ML, TF or PF and that the relevant identification procedures are applied; (f) conduct regular monitoring of internet-based business or customers and where a significant proportion of the business is operated electronically, computerized monitoring systems or solutions that are designed to recognize unusual transactions and related patterns of transactions shall be put in place to recognize suspicious transactions;  (g) ensure that in all cases, evidence as to how identity has been verified shall be obtained and retained with the account opening records.
amlcft.plain: The Bank shall:  1. Apply extra verification checks when dealing with non-face-to-face customers to confirm the person is who they claim to be—this must go beyond standard documentary or electronic evidence.  2. Use these additional verification steps for all such applicants, whether based in Nigeria or abroad, if they are:  a) Opening a bank account, or requesting services involving money transmission or third-party payments.  3. Ensure that the bank has adequate documentary or electronic evidence to:  a) Confirm the customer’s address and personal identity. b) Carry out at least one extra verification step to protect against impersonation or fraud.  4. When using intermediaries to process customer applications:  a) Ensure such intermediaries are regulated for AML/CFT/PF compliance. b) Ensure intermediaries apply proper customer identification procedures.  5. For internet-based banking or e-business:  a) Conduct ongoing monitoring of customer transactions. b) If a large part of the bank’s business is online, use automated monitoring systems that can detect unusual or suspicious patterns of transactions.  6. Always retain documented evidence of how customer identity was verified, and store it with the account opening records.

amlcft.title: Introductions from authorized financial  intermediaries
amlcft.description: (1) An introductory letter shall be issued by the introducing financial intermediary or person in respect of each applicant for business. (2) Where an intermediary introduces a customer and then withdraws from the ensuing relationship, the underlying customer shall become the applicant for the business and shall be identified in line with the requirements for personal, corporate or business customers as appropriate. (3) To ensure that product-providers meet their obligations, satisfactory identification evidence shall be obtained and retained for the necessary statutory period. (4) Each introductory letter shall either be accompanied by certified copies of the identification evidence obtained in line with the usual practice of certification of identification documents or by sufficient details and reference numbers that permits the actual evidence obtained to be re-obtained at a later stage.
amlcft.plain: The Bank shall:  1. Ensure that an introductory letter is obtained from any authorized financial intermediary or individual introducing a customer. The letter must relate to each specific applicant.  2. Where the intermediary withdraws from the customer relationship, the bank must treat the introduced individual or entity as a direct customer and carry out full customer identification (CDD) in line with the applicable requirements (personal, corporate, or business).  3. Obtain and retain satisfactory identification documents of the introduced customer, in accordance with legal requirements and for the prescribed statutory retention period.  4. Require that every introductory letter is:  a) Accompanied by certified copies of the customer's identification documents, or  b) Includes sufficient detail and reference numbers that would allow the bank to retrieve the actual identification documents later.

amlcft.riskDescription: Risk of onboarding customers without accountability or traceability.

amlcft.title: Foreign Intermediaries
amlcft.description: Where business is introduced or received from a financial intermediary regulated for AML and CFT, who is outside Nigeria, the reliance that shall be placed on that intermediary to undertake the verification of identity-check shall be assessed by the Compliance Officer or some other competent persons within the FI, on a case-by-case basis based on the knowledge of the intermediary.
amlcft.plain: The Bank shall:  1. Where a foreign financial intermediary (outside Nigeria) introduces or refers a customer and is regulated for AML/CFT, the bank may rely on the intermediary to carry out identity verification only after:  a) The Compliance Officer or other competent personnel at the bank assesses the reliability of the intermediary on a case-by-case basis, and b) The assessment is based on the bank’s knowledge of the intermediary, including its AML/CFT controls.
