amlcft.title: Corporate Group Introduction
amlcft.description: (1) Where a customer is introduced by one part of a financial sector group to another, the customer’s identity shall be re-verified, and the records shall not be duplicated except— (a) the identity of the customer has not been verified by the introducing parent company, branch, subsidiary or associate in line with the money laundering requirements of equivalent standards and taking account of any specific requirements such as separate address verification; (b) no exemptions or concessions have been applied in the original verification procedures that may not be available to the new relationship; (c) a group introduction letter is obtained and placed with the customer’s account opening records; and (d) in respect of group introducers from outside Nigeria, in which case arrangements shall be put in place to ensure that identity is verified in accordance with requirements and that the underlying records of identity in respect of the introduced customers are retained for the required period. (2) Where an FI has day-to-day access to all the group’s KYC information and records, there is no need to identify an introduced customer or obtain a group introduction letter where the identity of that customer has been previously verified (3) Where the identity of a customer has not been previously verified, then any missing identification evidence shall be obtained and a risk-based approach taken on the extent of KYC information that is available on whether or not additional information shall be obtained. (4) Before relying on group introduction, FIs shall ensure that there are no secrecy or data protection legislation in host or home countries of any of the financial groups that will restrict free access to the records. (5) Where the restrictions referred to in sub-regulation (4) of this regulation applies, copies of the underlying records of identity shall, wherever possible, be sought and retained. (6) Where identification records are held outside Nigeria, it shall be the responsibility of the FI to ensure that the records available meet the requirements of these Regulations and the CBN AML, CFT and CPF Regulations.
amlcft.plain: The Bank shall:  1.Re-verify the identity of any customer introduced by another part of its financial group (e.g., parent company, branch, or subsidiary), unless:  a) The introducing entity properly verified the customer’s identity in line with equivalent AML/CFT standards; b) No exemptions or shortcuts were used in the original KYC process; c) A group introduction letter is placed in the customer's account file; d) For introducers from outside Nigeria, proper arrangements are made to verify identity and ensure identity records are retained for the required period.  2. Skip re-verification if the bank already has day-to-day access to the full KYC records of the group and those records are adequate.  3. Fill any gaps in identification documentation and apply a risk-based approach to determine what additional KYC information is needed.  4. Confirm there are no secrecy or data protection laws in the host/home country of the group entity that would restrict access to identity records.  5. If such legal restrictions exist, obtain and retain copies of the customer's identity documents wherever possible.  6. Where identity records are held outside Nigeria, ensure they meet Nigerian AML/CFT requirements and the CBN AML/CFT/CPF Regulations.

amlcft.title: Acquisition of a Financial Institution and Business
amlcft.description: (1) Where a FI acquires a business and accounts of another FI, it may not be necessary for the identity of the existing customers to be re-identified, provided that all the underlying customers’ records are acquired with the business, but it shall carry out due diligence enquiries to confirm that the acquired institution had conformed with the requirements of the provisions of these Regulations and CBN AML, CFT and CPF Regulations. (2) Verification of identity shall be undertaken for all the transferred customers who were not verified by the transferor in line with the requirements for existing customers that open new accounts, where the— (a) money laundering procedures previously undertaken have not been in accordance with the requirements of these Regulations and CBN AML, CFT and CPF Regulations; or (b) customer records are not available to the acquiring financial institution.
amlcft.plain: The Bank shall:  1. When acquiring another financial institution’s business and customer accounts, verify that all customer identity records are included, and conduct due diligence to confirm that the acquired institution complied with CBN AML/CFT/CPF Regulations.  2. Re-verify customer identity if:  a) The previous AML/CFT procedures were inadequate or non-compliant with regulations; or  b) Customer records are unavailable to the acquiring bank.

amlcft.title: Domiciliary Accounts
amlcft.description: (1) Where a customer wishes to open a Domiciliary Account or make a wholesale deposit by cash or inter-bank transfer, a FI shall obtain identification evidence in accordance with the requirements for individuals, companies or professional intermediaries operating on behalf of third parties as appropriate. (2) Where the funds to a domiciliary account are by inter-bank transfer, FI shall satisfy itself that the transferring institution is regulated for ML, TF or PF prevention in its country of origin.
amlcft.plain: The Bank shall:  1. Obtain full identification of any customer opening a domiciliary account or making a large foreign currency deposit, in line with the rules applicable to: a) Individuals, b) Companies, or c) Professional intermediaries (acting for others), as applicable.  2. If the funds are received via inter-bank transfer, confirm that the sending institution is AML/CFT regulated in its home country.

amlcft.title: Safe Custody and Safety  Deposit Boxes
amlcft.description: 1) FIs shall take precautions in relation to requests to hold boxes, parcels and envelopes in a safe custody. (2) Where such facilities are made available, the identification procedures set out in these Regulations shall be followed, depending on the type of individual involved or risks associated with the business relationship. (3) FIs shall not allow items with unidentified contents to be deposited in safe deposit box and the contents shall be declared and documented at the point of entering the contract. (4) FIs shall maintain registers for on-going monitoring of the activities of persons who use safe custody or safe deposit box services. (5) FIs shall also conduct due diligence on owners of safe deposit boxes.
amlcft.plain: The Bank shall:  1. Exercise caution when handling customer requests to store items (boxes, parcels, envelopes) under safe custody.  2. Follow proper identification procedures, based on the customer type and associated ML/TF risks.  3. Do not allow storage of items with unidentified contents. Ensure all contents are declared and documented when the custody agreement is signed.  4. Maintain activity registers to monitor how customers use safe custody and safety deposit box services.  5. Conduct due diligence on all safe deposit box holders.

amlcft.source: INCLUSION OF INEC VOTER'S REGISTRATION CARD AS A MEANS OF CUSTOMER IDENTIFICATION, SEPTEMBER 2012
amlcft.title: Circular
amlcft.description: Towards the effort to ensure that depositors in banks and other financial institutions provide necessary background information for effective Know Your Customer (KYC) due diligence,the CBN in collaboration with relevant stakeholders has developed Uniform Account Opening Forms. The uniformity is to ensure that Customer Due Diligence (CDD) is consistently and uniformly practiced in account opening process for prospective customers of financial institutions. Individual prospective customers are required to complete account opening FORM A(1), FORM A(2) and FORM A for accounts in Tier I, II and III respectively, while legal entities are to complete FORM B. Whereas prospective customers are required to provide the relevant information applicable to them as prescribed above, existing customers are to regularly update their records in line with the formats.
amlcft.plain: The Bank shall: 1) Ensure prospective individual customers complete the designated FORM A(1), A(2), or A, based on account tier. 2) Ensure corporate/legal entities complete FORM B. 3) Accept INEC Voter’s Card as a valid form of identification. 4) Ensure existing customers update KYC records using the prescribed forms.
amlcft.deadlineType: Immediate (Ongoing compliance)
amlcft.riskDescription: Non-compliance with CBN KYC requirements; potential for onboarding anonymous or high-risk customers, regulatory fines, or AML/CFT breaches.

amlcft.responsibility: Compliance Officer; Internal Control
amlcft.primaryControl: Staff training on uniform forms; KYC checklist during onboarding; KYC refresh for existing customers
amlcft.additionalControl: Periodic internal audit of KYC records and documentation compliance

amlcft.source: National Identity Management Commission (NIMC) Act, 2007 (Access to Register Information in the National Identity Database Regulations, 2017)
amlcft.title: Disclosure of Registered Information
amlcft.description: (1) The Commission may provide any person other than designated persons stipulated under Regulations 5, 6 and 7 of these Regulations with the registered information of a registered individual where— (a) an application for the provision of the information to that person is made by or with the authority of that registered individual ; or (b) the registered individual consents to the provision of that information to that person by submitting his NIN or biometrics to the Commission.  (3) The information that may be provided to a person under regulation 5 (3) of these Regulations shall be limited to— (a) information about the individual falling within paragraph 1, 3 or 4 of the Second Schedule to the Act ; (b) any photograph of the registered individual recorded in the National identity database ; (c) the registered individual’s signature that is so recorded ; (d) information about whether the multipurpose identity card issued to the registered individual is active or inactive and if not active, the reason for it not being active ; (e) information in relation to confirmation whether or not information falling within sub-regulation (2) of this regulation submitted to the Commission corresponds with the information recorded in the registered individual’s entry in the National Identity Database ; and (f ) information in relation to confirmation that the registered individual’s entry in the National Identity Database does not contain information of a particular description falling within sub-regulation (2) of this regulation.
amlcft.plain: The Bank shall:  1) Only request or receive a customer’s NIMC data if they have authorized the request or submitted their NIN/biometrics   2) Ensure that any information accessed is limited to the permitted categories (e.g., name, photo, signature, ID status).   3) Keep a record of such consents or biometric/NIN submissions.
amlcft.deadlineType: Immediate and ongoing
amlcft.riskDescription: Unauthorized access to customer data, privacy breaches, reputational damage, regulatory penalties under NIMC or NDPR.
amlcft.owner: Compliance Unit; IT/Data Privacy Officer
amlcft.responsibility: Compliance Officer; Data Protection Officer (DPO)
amlcft.primaryControl: Obtain express customer consent before querying NIMC; maintain logs of data requests; limit access to trained staff
amlcft.additionalControl: Data Privacy Audits; Integration of NIMC requests into DPO oversight

amlcft.source: ACCEPTANCE OF MACHINE READABLE CONVENTION TRAVEL DOCUMENT (MRCTD) AND REFUGEE IDENTIFICATION CARD AS MEANS OF IDENTIFICATION
amlcft.title: Circular
amlcft.description: To address these concerns, all banks and other financial institutions are referred to the provisions of the CBN AML/CFT Regulations, 2013 (as amended) on customer due diligence, especially, Regulations 40 and Regulations 80, and to note that the Machine Readable Convention Travel Document (MRCTD) issued by the Nigeria Immigration Services; and the Refugee Identity Card issued by the National Commission for Refugees, Migrants and Internally Displaced Persons are adequate as means of identification for banking transactions.  Banks and other financial institutions are also required to continue to ensure that effective customer due diligence policies and procedures are implemented to combat money laundering, financing of terrorist and proliferation of weapons of mass destruction.
amlcft.plain: The Bank shall:  1) Accept MRCTD and Refugee ID Card as valid identification for banking transactions.   2) Ensure that these IDs are verified and documented appropriately.   3) Maintain effective customer due diligence procedures in line with CBN AML/CFT Regulations to prevent money laundering, terrorism financing, and proliferation financing.
amlcft.deadlineType: Immediate and ongoing
amlcft.riskDescription: Failure to recognize valid IDs can lead to exclusion of eligible persons (refugees/migrants). Inadequate CDD may expose the bank to ML/TF/PF risks.

amlcft.responsibility: Compliance Unit; KYC Desk; Training & Development
amlcft.primaryControl: Update account opening policy to include MRCTD and Refugee ID; Train staff; Maintain AML/CFT controls
amlcft.additionalControl: Include document verification in automated onboarding system; perform KYC refresh for refugee/MRCTD holders periodically

amlcft.title: Authorized Signatories Verification Portal for the Nigerian Banking Industry
amlcft.description: The signatories verification portal is expected to replace the printed signature booklets that banks distribute, such that instructions/documents received from other banks can be verified electronically (online). The portal will be used by banks, Registrars, Insurance Companies, Embassies and any other user of the printed signature booklets, to avoid fabrication of letters as coming from the banks. The Portal is meant to digitize the booklet and also ensure that updates can be made quickly, as staff change functions or move to other institutions. amlcft.source: Additional Know Your Customer (KYC) Requirement in respect of Non-profit organization (NPOs)
amlcft.title: Additional Know Your Customer (KYC) Requirement in respect of Non-profit organization (NPOs)
amlcft.description: In line with the requirements of extant AML/CFT/CPF Laws and Regulations and our circular dated 2nd August, 2012 (Ref: FPR/CIR/GEN/VOL.1/028), financial institutions are required to continue to obtain from Non-Profit Organizations (NPOs), evidence of registration with the Special Control Unit against Money Laundering (SCUML) of the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) before establishing business relationship with them.  Consequently, all banks and other financial institutions are hereby required to ensure strict compliance with the above requirement and update their customer account information accordingly.
amlcft.plain: The Bank shall obtain evidence of SCUML registration from any Non‑Profit Organization (NPO) before opening or maintaining an account. The Bank must also update existing NPO account records to include valid SCUML registration details.
amlcft.deadlineType: Immediate (effective on circular date)
amlcft.riskDescription: Failure to verify SCUML registration could lead to onboarding high‑risk or illegal NPOs, exposing the bank to money laundering/terrorism financing risks and regulatory penalties.
amlcft.owner: Compliance Department, Account Opening Unit, AML/CFT Unit
amlcft.responsibility: Head of Compliance, Operations Manager
amlcft.primaryControl: Current CDD/KYC procedures, onboarding checklist requiring mandatory SCUML verification
amlcft.additionalControl: Periodic compliance audits on NPO accounts, staff refresher training, automated system checks for SCUML status

amlcft.source: Addendum to the Revised Regulatory Framework for BANK VERIFICATION NUMBER Operations and Watch- List for the Nigerian Bank Industry
amlcft.title: Addendum to the Revised Regulatory Framework for BANK VERIFICATION NUMBER Operations and Watch- List for the Nigerian Bank Industry
amlcft.description: The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) in line with its mandate of promoting financial system stability hereby issues the following amendments to the Revised Regulatory Framework for Bank Verification (BVN) and Watch-List for the Nigerian Banking Industry 2021. a.	Temporary Watch-list. Financial Institutions are mandated to establish and maintain a temporary watchlist for BVNs implicated in suspected fraudulent transaction(s) reported by a financial institution. A BVN may remain on this temporary Watchlist for a maximum period of twenty-four (24) hours, during this period, the BVN owner shall be contacted to provide clarification regarding the identified transaction(s). b.	Age Requirement for BVN Enrolment Enrolment for BVN is restricted to individuals who have attained the age of eighteen (18) years and above.  c.	Restrictions on Phone Number Amendments Amendments to phone numbers linked to a BVN shall be allowed only once. d.	Access to BVN Data Access to the BVN databases shall be exclusively granted to Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) licensed financial institutions. Notwithstanding this provision, the Central Bank of Nigeria (the Bank) reserves the right to approve access to the BVN databases in extenuating circumstances and in accordance with the provisions of extant laws. Implementation of the above provisions shall take effect from May 1, 2026.
amlcft.plain: The bank shall comply with the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) amended  BVN regulatory framework to enhance financial system stability by introducing a 24-hour temporary watchlist for suspected fraud cases, restricting BVN enrolment to individuals aged 18 and above, limiting phone number changes to one, and tightening access to BVN data to licensed institutions.  The Bank commit to fully complying with these provisions and ensuring effective implementation by May 1, 2026, while maintaining the integrity and security of the financial system.
amlcft.deadlineType: Immediate (effective on circular date)
amlcft.riskDescription: Failure to introduce a 24-hour temporary watchlist for suspected fraud cases, restricting BVN enrolment to individuals aged 18 and above, limiting phone number changes to one, and tightening access to BVN data to licensed institutions before the deadline exposes the bank to regulatory penalties.

amlcft.title: ADDITIONAL FUNCTIONALITIES FOR INSTANT  PAYMENT The  Central  Bank  of  Nigeria  (CBN)  in  line  with  its  mandate  of  promoting  financial system  stability  hereby  issues  additional  guidance  for  the  operations  of  Instant Payments in Nigeria.
amlcft.description: All Financial Institutions (Fls) offering Instant Payment (IP) shall provide the following additional functionalities: 1.   Voluntary Opt-Out /Opt-In functionality: Customers shall have the option to opt-out  of  /  opt-in  to  IP  service  at  any  time  and  for  any  given  period.  This process shall be subject  to Multi-Factor  Authentication (MFA)  control.  Default setting shall be Opt-in upon on-boarding a new customer. In the  opt-out  mode,  a customer  shall not be able to carry  out online instant transfer  of  funds  (intra  or  inter)  from  his/her  account  to  another  customer. However, customer can physically \/isit the financial institution to effect transfer during this period. 2.  Voluntary Transaction  Limit: Subject  to the existing maximum  limits of  million for individuals and 250 million for corporates, customers shall have the option to adjust the limits as needed. Any such adjustment  shall be subject to enhanced  due  diligence  and  appropriate  risk  assessment  by  the  financial institution.   3.  Enterprise  Fraud  Monitoring  functionality:  All  Fls  shall  implement  and activate Enterprise Fraud Monitoring  for both inflows and outflows to facilitate fraud detection and restriction of suspicious transactions. 4.  Liveliness Checks for online account opening / account reactivation: i.      Accounts opened online shall be subjected to liveliness check; ii.      All online account opening / online reactivation, shall be validated real-time with the BVN/NIN database; and iii.     Enhanced    authentication    mechanisms    (such    as    MFA,    biometric authentication, soft token, hard token, liveliness check etc.) shall be adopted for online account reactivation. 5.  Additional   requirements    for   mobile   financial   services   via   Mobile Applications: Mandatory  device binding:  Mobile  financial  services  applications  (apps) shall  only  be  enabled  on  one  device  at  a  time,  and  customers  cannot operate the apps concurrently on multiple devices. ii.     Migration   to  another   device   shall   trigger   automatic   re-activation   and authentication. iii.      For new accounts,  transaction  limits (inflow and outflow)  shall be imposed on a newly  activated  mobile  financial services  app in the  first 24-hours  of activation.  The  limit  shall  be  as  determined  by  the  financial  institution, subject to a maximum transaction limit of N20,000.00. iv.     For  existing  accounts,  transaction  limits  (outflow)  shall  be  imposed  on  a newly  activated  mobile  financial  services   app  in  the  first  24-hours   of activation.  The  limit  shall  be  as  determined  by  the  financial  institution, subject to a maximum transaction limit of N20,000.00." V,        For  internet  banking  access,  first-time  log  on  a  new  device  shall  require additional MFA. The above are the minimum standard requirements  for instant payments in Nigeria.   Implementation of the above pro\visions  shall take effect from July 1, 2026.
amlcft.plain: The bank commits to implementing secure and customer-controlled instant payment services by enabling opt-in/opt-out features, adjustable transaction limits, enterprise fraud monitoring, and robust authentication measures—including MFA, device binding, and real-time identity verification.  The bank further commits to enforcing enhanced security controls for digital channels, including transaction limits for newly activated devices and accounts, with full compliance to these minimum standards effective July 1, 2026.

actmgt.source: CBN Guidelines on Management of Dormant Accounts, Unclaimed Balances and Other Financial Assets
actmgt.title: FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS
actmgt.description: Financial Institutons shall: i. Monitor inactive accounts and notify the customers as well as protect such accounts from unauthorized usage; ii. Establish procedures that will ensure continuous contact with customers to reduce the incidence of inactive/dormant accounts; iii. Maintain records of procedures and periodic efforts to contact customers with inactive accounts; iv. Advise all customers, in writing, on the need to communicate changes in their names, addresses, phone numbers, emails and next-of-kin. In the case of corporate entities, changes in directors, authorized signatories, business addresses etc; v. Bear the costs of maintaining inactive and dormant accounts as well as contacting the customers; vi. Render quarterly reports on dormant accounts in a prescribed format to Banking Supervision Department (BSD) and Other Financial Institutions Supervision Department, (OFISD) CBN as applicable; vii. Notify account owners in writing through the agreed medium such as email, text message, and letter immediately an account becomes inactive/dormant and thereafter on a quarterly basis; viii. Reactivate dormant accounts upon request by the account owner or his/her beneficial owner; ix. Continue to reflect dormant account balances as deposit liabilities and such balances, where applicable, shall continue to earn interest until they are transferred to CBN; x. Maintain a register for funds transferred to CBN for reclaim and audit trail; xi. Publish, on their websites, details of all dormant accounts, six months prior to their eligibility for transfer to CBN. However, other financial institutions (OFIs) without websites shall publish same on their association’s website; xii. Ensure the publication shall indicate the names of individuals authorized to operate the accounts, the type of account and the address of the branch where the account is domiciled. The list so published by the FIs, should provide a “Search” Function; xiii. Publish annually, the list of dormant account owners in at least two national daily newspapers, except for state and Unit microfinance banks, which shall publish in their premises. Information to be published shall include the name of account owner and address of the branch. It should also be stated that the account has been transferred to the register of dormant account; xiv. Display a notice on the process of reclaim of unclaimed balances and other financial assets transferred to CBN in all its branches/offices, websites and other customer engagement points. xv. Transfer unclaimed balances in all eligible accounts in the same currency in which the account is maintained to the ‘UBTF Pool Account’ domiciled at the CBN; xvi. Transfer aggregate of unclaimed balances quarterly with a schedule, not later than fifteen (15) days of the first month of the subsequent quarter; and xvii. Retain all records of communication on the management of dormant accounts for a minimum of ten (10) years after transfer to the ‘UBTF Pool Account’ domiciled at the CBN.
actmgt.plain: The Bank shall:  1.Regularly monitor inactive accounts and inform customers while protecting those accounts from misuse.  2.Set up ways to keep in touch with customers so accounts don’t become inactive or dormant.  3.Keep records of all attempts made to contact customers with inactive accounts.  4.Advise customers in writing to update their personal or business details like names, addresses, phone numbers, emails, and next-of-kin.  5.Pay the cost of maintaining dormant accounts and contacting the account owners.  6.Send quarterly reports on dormant accounts to the CBN departments (BSD and OFISD) using the required format.  7.Notify customers in writing (email, SMS, or letter) as soon as an account becomes dormant, and continue to notify them every quarter.  8.Reactivate a dormant account once the owner or rightful person makes a request.  9.Keep dormant account balances as deposits and continue to pay interest on them (if applicable) until they are sent to the CBN.  10.Keep a register of funds sent to the CBN to track and audit them.  11.Publish the list of dormant accounts on the Bank’s website six months before they are due to be transferred to the CBN (OFIs without websites should publish on their association’s website).  12.Make sure the published list includes account operator names, account types, and the branch location, with a search function on the site.  13.Once a year, publish the list of dormant account owners in at least two national newspapers (or in-branch for state/unit microfinance banks), including name, branch address, and a note that the account is now dormant.  14,Display instructions in all branches, offices, websites, and customer touchpoints on how to reclaim balances or assets sent to the CBN.  15.Transfer all unclaimed balances in their original currencies to the CBN's UBTF Pool Account.  16.Submit total unclaimed balances along with a detailed schedule every quarter—no later than 15 days into the first month of the new quarter.  17.Keep all records of communication related to managing dormant accounts for at least 10 years after transferring the funds to the CBN.
actmgt.riskDescription: Non-compliance could result in regulatory sanctions, reputational damage, customer claims, or audit failures due to mishandled or unreported dormant account balances.

actmgt.title: MANAGEMENT OF DORMANT ACCOUNTS AND UNCLAIMED FINANCIAL ASSETS
actmgt.description: FIs shall treat accounts and financial assets that have become dormant as follows: i. Formulate policies for the recognition and management of dormant accounts and financial assets that are consistent with this Guidelines and other extant regulations; ii. Establish effective controls to ensure surveillance and second level authorization on reactivation of dormant accounts, among other measures; iii. Maintain records including a register of dormant accounts balances; iv. Transfer balances that have remained in the dormant account register for up to ten (10) years to the ‘UBTF Pool Account’.
actmgt.plain: The Bank shall: i. Create internal policies to manage dormant accounts in line with the Guidelines. ii. Put in place strong internal controls, including two-level authorization for account reactivation. iii. Keep detailed records, including a dormant accounts register. iv. Transfer balances in dormant register older than 10 years to the CBN ‘UBTF Pool Account’.
actmgt.riskDescription: Non-compliance may result in regulatory penalties, audit issues, or mishandling of unclaimed assets. It can also expose the institution to fraud and operational losses.
actmgt.owner: - Compliance Department - Branch Operations - Internal Control - Finance Department
actmgt.primaryControl: - Dormant Account Policy - Dual approval for account reactivation - Dormant Accounts Register (system-based) - Automated system flag for 10-year threshold accounts

actmgt.title: RE-ACTIVATION OF DORMANT ACCOUNT
actmgt.description: FIs shall: i. Require the account owner/beneficial owner to complete a reactivation form in person; ii. Obtain from the account owner evidence of ownership of the dormant account with valid means of identification, evidence of present place of residence, and affidavit on the accuracy of the information to reactivate the dormant account. iii. Verify the information provided on the reactivation form; iv. Not charge any fee for reactivation of dormant account; v. Reactivate the dormant account with the approval of two (2) authorized officers with one being at least the Branch Operations Manager; vi. Reactivate dormant accounts within a maximum of three (3) working days of receipt of a written application to that effect; and vii. Notify the account owner, free of charge, upon reactivation of the account.
actmgt.plain: The Bank shall: i. Require in-person completion of reactivation form by account/beneficial owner. ii. Collect valid ID, proof of residence, and sworn affidavit. iii. Verify all submitted documents. iv. Reactivate without charging any fee. v. Obtain approval from two officers (including Branch Ops Manager). vi. Complete reactivation within 3 working days. vii. Notify the customer at no cost upon reactivation.
actmgt.riskDescription: Non-compliance could lead to fraud, regulatory sanctions, legal liability, or customer dissatisfaction.
actmgt.owner: - Branch Operations Manager - Customer Service Unit - Compliance Officer - Internal Control Unit
actmgt.primaryControl: - Reactivation checklist and approval workflow - Face-to-face identity verification - Dual authorization - TAT tracking system (3-day SLA) - No charge flag in transaction system

actmgt.title: DISPUTE RESOULUTION
actmgt.description: The resolution of disputes shall be the responsibility of FIs. Consumer complaints shall first be lodged with FIs for resolution and redress. The resolution of complaints shall be in accordance with the timelines prescribed in the extant CBN Consumer Protection Regulations (CPR). FIs shall disclose the channels and contact details for lodging complaints, timeframe for resolution, and options for escalation, at all customer engagement points. The customer’s complaint will be eligible for escalation to the Consumer Protection Department, CBN when a complaint is not resolved within fifteen (15) days from the date of the receipt or the customer is dissatisfied with the decision of the FI.
actmgt.plain: The Bank shall:  i. Handle all consumer complaints internally in the first instance. ii. Resolve disputes within timelines set in the CBN Consumer Protection Regulations (CPR). iii. Clearly disclose complaint channels, timelines, and escalation options at all customer touchpoints. iv. Allow escalation to the Consumer Protection Department, CBN if the bank fails to resolve within 15 days or if the customer is dissatisfied.
actmgt.riskDescription: Failure to address disputes promptly and transparently can result in regulatory sanctions, reputational damage, and customer attrition.
actmgt.owner: - Customer Experience Unit - Complaint Resolution Desk - Compliance/Legal Team
actmgt.primaryControl: - Complaint resolution procedures aligned with CPR timelines - Complaint management system with case tracking - Clear display of complaint channels and escalation paths

actmgt.source: Guidelines on Operations of Bank Accounts for Virtual Assets Service Providers (VASPs)
actmgt.title: OPERATION OF BANK ACCOUNT BY VASPs
actmgt.description: 7.1 Designation of accounts From the commencement of these Regulations, FI shall not open or permit the operation of any account by any person or entity to conduct the business of virtual/digital assets unless that account is designated for that purpose and opened in line with the requirement of these Guidelines.  7.2 Designated account to be opened with approval of the senior management The designated account shall only be opened with the approval of senior management of the FI.  7.3 Account opening/documentation requirement Any application for opening a designated account by a company providing virtual/digital asset services under these Guidelines shall be supported by the following documents: a. evidence of a valid licence issued by the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) for the entity to engage in the business of VASP/DAX/DAOP. b. certified true copy of the memorandum and article of association. c. certified true copy Form CAC 2 – Statement of share capital and return of allotment of shares. d. certified true copy Form CAC 2.1 particulars of secretary. e. certified true copy Form CAC 3 – notice of registered address. f. certified true copy Form CAC 7 – Particulars of Directors. g. verifiable registered address of the company. h. copy of Certificate of Capital Importation (CCI) (where applicable). i. valid means of identification of all the directors, principal officers and beneficial owners of the company. j. BVN of all the directors, principal officers and beneficial owners of the company. k. Home address of all the directors, principal officers and beneficial owners of the company. l. AML, CFT and CPF Policy of the entity. m. All other requirements of a corporate account in line with the CBN CDD Regulations. n. Any other requirement that the CBN may impose from time to time.  7.4 Restriction on the use of account i. An account opened in accordance with these Guidelines shall only be used for transactions on virtual/digital assets and not for any other purpose. ii. No cash withdrawal shall be allowed from the account. iii. No third-party cheque shall be cleared from the account. iv. Except for settlement of a virtual/digital assets transaction which shall be done through a transfer to another designated account, withdrawal shall be only through a Managers’ Cheque or transfer to an account.  7.5 Returns on the activities of the account to CBN i. FIs shall monitor, on a continuous basis, all activities conducted in designated accounts opened in accordance with these Guidelines. ii. FIs shall, at the end of every month and not later than the 10th day of the following month, submit to the relevant supervisory department of CBN, data and other information on designated account. The content of the returns shall include but not limited to: a. The number of designated accounts opened within the reporting period; b. The value and volume of transactions conducted in each account within the reporting period; c. The details of the counter party(ies) to the transactions; d. Incidents of fraud or theft; and e. Number of customer complaints and remedial measures taken.  7.6 Operational and transactional limits i. FIs shall establish transaction limits for each designated account opened in accordance with these Guidelines in line with its risk assessment criteria. ii. The limits shall be prudent and bear a relationship to the volume of cash moved by the account holder and the risks associated with the conduct and nature of the business of the account holder.  7.7 Designated accounts shall not be run on concession FIs shall not allow or enter into any concession agreement/arrangement with a holder of a designated account. The account shall, at all times be subject to the maximum transaction charges band as provided for under the CBN Guide to Charges for Banks and Other Financial institutions.  7.8 Dormant account i. Any designated account opened in accordance with these Guidelines shall be declared dormant if no customer induced transaction is carried out for three (3) consecutive months. ii. Any account declared dormant in line with the requirement of these Guidelines shall be closed forthwith and a notice of such closure shall be served on the account holder and the balance in such account shall be treated in line with the requirement of Section 72 of BOFIA 2020.  7.9 Provision for Designated Settlement Account i. FIs shall obtain authorisation from the CBN for the opening and operation of designated settlement account of SEC’s VASPs/DA entities. ii. All obligations arising from transactions within the VASPs/DAs entities platform shall be settled into the designated settlement accounts maintained by them in the banks. iii. The designated settlement accounts shall warehouse all Naira positions of individuals with the VASPs/DAs. iv. The designated settlement account, including any associated linked account for warehousing settlement monies, shall not be interest bearing. v. The details of the transactions on the VASP platform leading to settlement on the designated settlement account shall be accessible online, on real-time basis to the FIs at all times. vi. Credit to the designated settlement account shall be for the funding of Naira positions of persons on the VASP/DAs platform. vii. Debit from the designated settlement account shall only be in favour of the specific accounts that was used to fund Naira position on the VASP/DAs platform. viii. Returns on transactions on the designated settlement accounts shall be rendered to the Bank monthly or at any frequency that the Bank may require. ix. The designated settlement account shall not facilitate FX positions of persons on the VASP/DAs platform. x. FIs shall ensure that the SEC-licensed VASP/DA entities always maintain a minimum collateral equal to 150% highest net debit position into the designated settlement account (over the past 10 days). xi. FIs shall not use the designated settlement account as collateral for credit. xii. The settlement cycle for transactions of VASPs/DAs shall be T+3. xiii. Value shall NOT be given to VASP/DAs before settlement occur or earlier than the settlement cycle. xiv. FIs shall not facilitate transfer and settlement from the FX positions of persons on the VASP/DAs platform to any foreign account. xv. Transfers from the Naira position of persons on the VASP platform into their bank account shall not be more than twice in a quarter. xvi. FIs shall ensure that only accounts that have completed full KYC process (Tiered accounts subject to exemptions are excluded) can fund or receive from positions on the VASP/DAs platform. xvii. FIs/NIBSS shall not allow usage/creation of NUBAN accounts by VASPs. xviii. Transactions on the VASP/DA platform shall only be in Naira.
actmgt.plain: The Bank shall:  1. Not open or allow the use of any account for virtual/digital asset business unless it is specifically designated for that purpose and meets the CBN’s requirements.  2. Only open designated accounts for virtual asset service providers (VASPs) with the approval of senior management.  3. Ensure that any company applying for a designated account provides:     * A valid SEC licence for VASP/DAX/DAOP activities.    * Corporate documents from CAC (e.g., incorporation, directors, share capital).    * Address and identification details of key officers and beneficial owners.    * AML/CFT/CPF policy.    * Other documents required for regular corporate accounts or as specified by the CBN.  4. Restrict designated accounts to only virtual/digital asset transactions:     * No cash withdrawals or third-party cheques.    * Funds can only be withdrawn via Manager’s Cheque or bank transfers to another designated account.  5. Monitor all activities in designated accounts continuously and submit monthly reports (by the 10th day of the following month) to the CBN, including:     * Number of such accounts opened.    * Volume and value of transactions.    * Details of parties to the transactions.    * Any fraud or complaints reported.  6. Set transaction limits for each designated account based on risk assessment.  7. Not offer any concessions or reduced charges on designated accounts; standard CBN fees apply.  8. Close any designated account that is inactive for three consecutive months and notify the account holder. The balance must be handled as required under Section 72 of BOFIA 2020.  9. Obtain CBN approval for operating settlement accounts for VASPs:     * These accounts must only warehouse Naira positions (not foreign exchange).    * Transactions must be transparent and viewable by banks in real time.    * Credits and debits must follow strict rules (e.g., linked to specific users).    * No interest shall be paid on these accounts, nor used as collateral for loans.    * VASPs must maintain 150% collateral of the highest recent debit amount.    * Transactions must settle within three days (T+3).    * No early settlements or FX transfers are allowed.    * Users may only transfer funds from their Naira positions to personal accounts twice per quarter.    * Only fully KYC-compliant users can transact on VASP platforms.    * No VASP shall be allowed to create or use standard NUBAN accounts.    * All VASP/DA transactions must be in Naira only.
actmgt.riskDescription: Inadequate controls over VASP accounts could lead to: - Regulatory sanctions - Misuse for money laundering, terrorism financing, or FX infractions - Reputational damage from association with illegal or speculative crypto schemes.

actmgt.source: Guidelines on Operations of Bank Accounts for Virtual Assets Service Providers (VASPs)
actmgt.title: RISK MANAGEMENT FOR ANTI-MONEY LAUNDERING, COMBATING THE FINANCING OF TERRORISM AND COUNTER PROLIFERATION FINANCING (AML, CFT, AND CPF)
actmgt.description: FIs shall establish appropriate risk management systems to determine whether a designated account opened under these Guidelines has been used, is being used or is likely to be used for ML, TF and PF. FIs shall take reasonable measures to establish the Beneficial Ownership, source of wealth and the source of funds of designated account under these Guidelines.  8.1 Customer Due Diligence (CDD) i. The appropriate time to conduct CDD by FI shall be, but not limited to, the following cases, when: a. On boarding a VASPs in a new relationship; b. a transaction of significant value takes place; c. a customer information/documentation change substantially; d. there is a material change in the way that the account is being operated; or e. the institution becomes aware that it lacks sufficient information about an existing customer. ii. FIs shall apply EDD requirements to all designated accounts opened in accordance with these Guidelines on the basis of materiality and risk and continue to conduct due diligence on such existing relationships at appropriate times.  8.2 Continuous Verification, Validation of Address and Documentation Requirement FIs shall independently validate the address and documentation requirement provided under these Guidelines and where it is discovered to be incorrect or invalid, the account shall be placed on Post-No-Debit and the customer shall be asked to update its record. Provided that an STR shall be rendered to the NFIU in that regard.  8.3 Maintenance of Records i. FIs shall maintain all necessary records of transactions of a designated account for at least five years after completion of the transaction or such longer period as may be required by the CBN. Provided that this requirement shall apply regardless of whether the account or business relationship is on-going or has been terminated. ii. The components of records of transactions to be maintained by FIs shall include the: a. records of customers and beneficial owners obtained through CDD measures including copies of records of official identification documents like passports, identity cards, drivers’ licenses or allied documents and beneficiary’s names, addresses or other identifying information normally recorded by the intermediary; b. nature and date of the transaction; c. type and amount involved; d. type and identifying number of any account involved in the transaction; and e. results of any analysis including inquiries to establish the background and purpose of complex unusual large transactions. iii. FIs shall ensure that all customer-transaction records and information are available on request to the CBN on a timely basis, not later than 24 hours from the time of receipt of such request. iv. Records of the supporting evidence and methods used to verify identity shall be retained for a minimum period of five years after the account is closed or the business relationship has ended.  8.4 Monitoring and Reporting of Suspicious Transaction FIs shall: i. be responsible for instituting appropriate know-your customer procedure to reasonably/promptly identify all individuals/entities offering services covered by this regulation, in their books, and ensure they immediately comply with the provisions of this regulation. ii. be responsible for monitoring and supervising all activities in designated account and shall be held responsible for misapplication of any account. iii. have information on the volume and value of transactions carried out for each designated account. iv. monitor effective compliance with set limits for each designated account. v. take all other measures including onsite visits to ensure that the account is being operated strictly within the requirements of these Guidelines and other extant laws and regulations. vi. pay special attention to all complex, unusually large transactions or unusual patterns of transactions that have no visible economic or lawful purpose. vii. investigate suspicious transactions and report its findings to the NFIU immediately, in compliance with the relevant provisions of any law or regulations being in force. viii. Keep records of investigations of reviewed unusual transactions where the transactions were not reported as suspicious transactions to the NFIU.
actmgt.plain: The Bank shall:   1. Establish effective risk management systems to detect whether any designated account is being, has been, or could be used for money laundering, terrorist financing, or proliferation financing. It shall take reasonable measures to confirm the beneficial owner, source of wealth, and source of funds for such accounts.  2. Conduct Customer Due Diligence (CDD) when: i. onboarding a Virtual Asset Service Provider (VASP), ii. a significant transaction occurs, iii. customer information changes substantially, iv. the way the account operates changes materially, or v. it realizes it lacks sufficient customer information.  3. Apply Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) to all designated accounts, with ongoing due diligence at appropriate times.  4. Independently verify customer addresses and documentation. If information is found to be incorrect, the account shall be placed on Post-No-Debit until updated, and a Suspicious Transaction Report (STR) shall be sent to the NFIU.  5. Keep transaction records for at least five years, including identification documents, transaction details, account numbers, and results of any analysis of unusual transactions. These records must be made available to the CBN within 24 hours of a request.  6. Monitor designated accounts, ensure compliance with transaction limits, investigate suspicious activity, pay attention to complex or unusual transactions, and report findings immediately to the NFIU.
actmgt.riskDescription: Weak or absent AML/CFT/CPF controls on VASP accounts may result in: - Laundering of illicit funds or terrorism financing - Breaches of CBN and NFIU regulations - Legal penalties and reputational risk

actmgt.title: CONSUMER PROTECTION MEASURES
actmgt.description: FIs shall: i. ensure that appropriate consumer protection systems against risks of fraud are established. ii. provide a channel for communication of customer complaints against designated account holders. iii. establish complaints redress mechanism and ensure proper communication of this mechanism to the general public. iv. ensure strict adherence to the provision of the Circular issued by the CBN (Referenced CPD/DIR/GEN/CIR/01/001) on the Deployment of the Consumer Complaints Management System (CCMS).
actmgt.plain: The Bank shall: i. Establish robust consumer protection systems to guard against fraud risks. ii. Provide accessible communication channels for customer complaints relating to designated accounts. iii. Set up a complaints redress mechanism and clearly communicate it to the public. iv. Strictly comply with the CBN Circular CPD/DIR/GEN/CIR/01/001 on use of the Consumer Complaints Management System (CCMS) for tracking and resolving complaints.
actmgt.riskDescription: Failure to address fraud and consumer complaints can lead to: - Reputational damage - Regulatory sanctions - Loss of customer trust - Legal liabilities
actmgt.owner: - Head, Customer Service - Compliance Officer - Consumer Protection Unit - IT Department (for CCMS integration)
actmgt.primaryControl: - Implement fraud detection systems on designated accounts - Provide toll-free numbers, emails, and online portals for complaints - Integrate with CBN CCMS - Train staff on complaints handling procedures and timelines - Maintain complaint logs and resolution reports

actmgt.source: RE: Guidelines on Management of Dormant Accounts, Unclaimed Balances and Other Financial Assets in Banks and Other Financial Institutions in Nigeria
actmgt.title: FPR/DIR/PUB/CIR/001/004
actmgt.description: The Guidelines on Management of Dormant Accounts, Unclaimed Balances and Other  Financial Assets in Banks and Other Financial Institutions in Nigeria 2024, requires banks and some other financial institutions to publish on their websites, the names of individuals authorized to operate the accounts, the type of account and the address of the branch where the account is domiciled. In the case of other financial institutions (OFIs) without websites, to publish on their association's website.  In furtherance thereof, and in response to enquiries from stakeholders regarding the possible breach of the Nigeria Data Protection Act, 2023 (NDPA), banks and other financial institutions are required to note the following: 1. Section 25 (b) of the NDPA permits justifiable deviations from the general principles of the Act. Also, Section 72 (ii) of the Banks and Other Financial Institutions Act mandates the Central Bank of Nigeria to issue Guidelines on the administration of unclaimed funds in banks and other financial institutions. 2. Information to be published on banks' websites as well as the association's website (where applicable) shall include the name of the account, the type of account, the name of the bank, and the branch where the account is domiciled ONLY. 3. Information to be published annually in at least two national daily newspapers or the premises of State and Unit microfinance banks, shall also convey the details as listed in (2) above.
actmgt.plain: The Bank shall annually publish only the name on the dormant account, account type, name of the bank, and branch address—on their websites and in two national newspapers. This publication complies with NDPA Section 25(b) and is authorized by BOFIA Section 72(ii).
actmgt.riskDescription: Over-disclosure could breach data protection laws, while under-disclosure may lead to regulatory non-compliance and penalties.
actmgt.owner: Legal, Compliance, Corporate Communications, IT
actmgt.primaryControl: Internal data publishing policy; publication content vetting; annual dormant account disclosure schedule; NDPA compliance checklist.

actmgt.source: Nigerian Deposit Insurance Corporation (NDIC) Act, 2023
actmgt.title: Assessment of insured institutions and special contribution
actmgt.description: (1) Every insured institution shall pay to the Corporation an annual premium as assessed in accordance with the provisions of this section.  (2) Subject to subsection (4), the assessment of premium shall be on a risk-based basis by reference to total deposit liabilities standing in its books as at 31 December of the preceding year.  (3) For the purposes of subsections (1) and (2), the— (a) deposit liabilities shall be as certified by the approved auditor of the insured institution; (b) certified deposit liabilities shall be forwarded to the Corporation on or before 31 January of every year; and (c) annual premium shall be payable not later than two months from the date of the demand notice.  (4) Notwithstanding the provisions of subsection (2), and subject to the approval of the Board, the Corporation shall have the power to vary the rate or basis of assessment of the premium payable to the Corporation by insured institutions or to charge an insured institution or any class of insured institutions premium at a rate or rates as may be determined by the Board.  (5) The rate or basis of assessment of the premium payable to the Corporation by insured institutions shall be published in the Federal Government Gazette.  (6) The premiums payable under subsections (1) and (2) shall not be chargeable to depositors in any form.  (7) Where the funds of the Corporation are not sufficient for giving assistance to insured institutions within the meaning of section 4 (b) of this Act or otherwise insufficient for implementation of the public policy objectives of this Act, every participating insured institution or any category of insured institutions may be obliged without prejudice to subsections (1) and (2) to pay as special contribution out of its profits before tax, a sum equal to its annual premium or such other sum as the Board may require, not exceeding 200% of its annual premium, on such terms and conditions as the Board may determine.  (8) Any premium payable by an insured institution and which remains unpaid for more than three months after a demand notice had been served on such institution, shall attract interest at a rate equivalent to the prevailing Monetary Policy Rate (MPR) of the Central Bank of Nigeria or any other applicable rate as may be specified by the Board.
actmgt.plain: The Bank shall: 1. Pay an annual premium to NDIC as assessed under this section. 2. The premium must be calculated using risk-based methods and total deposit liabilities as at December 31 of the previous year. 3. Deposit liabilities must be certified by an approved auditor and submitted to NDIC by January 31 each year. 4. Premium must be paid within two months from the date of NDIC’s demand notice. 5. NDIC may vary the rate or basis of premium assessment subject to Board approval. 6. The rate/basis must be published in the Federal Government Gazette. 7. The bank must not charge premium to depositors. 8. If NDIC funds are insufficient, the bank may be required to make a special contribution up to 200% of annual premium. 9. Premiums unpaid three months after demand notice will attract interest at the prevailing MPR or other rate set by NDIC.

actmgt.title: Maximum Claim

actmgt.plain: The Bank shall in the event of the revocation of its operating license or suspension of payments to depositors, ensure that each depositor (other than those in a Microfinance Bank) is entitled to receive from the Corporation a maximum compensation of N500,000, in accordance with section 4(a) and section 17(7)(a) of the Act.

actmgt.source: Nigerian Deposit Insurance Corporation (NDIC) Act, 2023
actmgt.title: Application of Global Standing Instruction Scheme and statutory right to funds of obligors in insured institutions
actmgt.description: (1) Without prejudice to the provisions of section 26 of this Act, the Corporation shall be entitled to exercise on behalf of a failed insured institution, the rights which the failed insured institution has under the Global Standing Instruction Scheme operated by the Central Bank of Nigeria under any enactment or regulation in effect.  (2) For the purpose of effecting the Global Standing Instruction mandate, the Corporation acting as liquidator shall have access to the Bank Verification Numbers of obligors in the Industry Customer Account Database, through the Nigeria Interbank Settlement System, as well as connectivity to the Nigeria Central Switch for and on behalf of failed insured institutions.
actmgt.plain: The Bank shall: 1. Allow NDIC, acting on behalf of failed banks, to invoke Global Standing Instructions (GSI) to recover loan obligations. 2. Provide NDIC access to obligors’ Bank Verification Numbers (BVNs) through the NIBSS Industry Customer Account Database and Nigeria Central Switch.
actmgt.riskDescription: - Regulatory penalty for denying NDIC access or obstructing recovery under GSI. - Legal exposure if data sharing is delayed or incomplete. - Risk of loss recovery failures from obligors of failed banks tied to the bank.
actmgt.owner: - Chief Compliance Officer- Head of IT/Data Management- Legal and Recovery Unit
actmgt.primaryControl: - Integrate NDIC-authorized access to BVN and account databases - Maintain updated GSI mandate records for obligors - Establish secure protocols for responding to NDIC requests - Automate compliance checks on NDIC-triggered GSI processes

actmgt.source: Nigerian Deposit Insurance Corporation (NDIC) Act, 2023
actmgt.title: Payment of insured deposit
actmgt.description: (1) Payments of the insured deposit in an insured institution shall be made by the Corporation— (a) within 30 days of the Corporation becoming the liquidator of such insured institution where the licence of that institution is revoked; or (b) with the concurrence of Central Bank of Nigeria, within 30 days, where due to its insolvent status, the insured institution has suspended payment or is otherwise unable to meet its obligation to depositors for a period of 90 days.  (2) The payment in subsection (1) shall be made by— (a) cash; (b) negotiable instrument; or (c) making available to each depositor a transferred deposit in another insured institution in an amount equal to the insured deposit of such depositor: Provided that where the Corporation is— (i) liable to make payment under this section, it shall, at its discretion, require proof of claim from all depositors with the insured institution, and (ii) not satisfied as to the validity of a claim for an insured deposit, it may require the final determination by a court of competent jurisdiction before paying such claim.
actmgt.plain: The Bank shall: 1. Acknowledge that NDIC shall pay insured depositors within 30 days of becoming liquidator if a bank's license is revoked. 2. Recognize NDIC may pay by cash, negotiable instruments, or transferred deposits in another insured institution. 3. Comply with NDIC’s request for valid claims and court determination if required.
actmgt.riskDescription: - Failure to support NDIC claims process may delay depositor settlements. - Poor record-keeping may lead to delays in validating customer claims. - Legal and reputational risk if payment to depositors is delayed due to poor cooperation with NDIC.
actmgt.owner: - Legal Department- Head of Operations- Customer Service and Records Unit
actmgt.primaryControl: - Maintain accurate, updated customer deposit records - Establish a data sharing protocol with NDIC - Develop a claim support system for NDIC engagement - Track and log all requests from NDIC for documentation or proof

actmgt.source: Nigerian Deposit Insurance Corporation (NDIC) Act, 2023
actmgt.title: Payment of insured deposit pending action in Court
actmgt.description: (1) Where the operating licence of an insured institution is revoked or where an insured institution has suspended payment or is otherwise unable to meet its obligation to depositors, the insured deposit shall become payable and the Corporation shall become obligated to pay insured deposits to the depositors of such insured institutions in accordance with the provisions of sections 25 and 28 of this Act: Provided that where an insured institution has suspended payment or is otherwise unable to meet its obligation to depositors, payment of insured deposit shall only be made with the concurrence of the Central Bank of Nigeria.
actmgt.plain: The Bank shall maintain complete and accessible depositor records so that, if their license is revoked or they suspend payments, NDIC can promptly pay insured deposits—provided CBN agrees when payments are stayed pending court action.
actmgt.riskDescription: Incomplete or inaccessible depositor data delaying NDIC’s payout; failure to obtain or process CBN concurrence when required; gaps in coordination between bank, NDIC and CBN.

actmgt.source: Nigerian Deposit Insurance Corporation (NDIC) Act, 2023
actmgt.title: Conditions for participation after termination of insured status
actmgt.description: An insured institution whose insured status is terminated in accordance with this Act but whose licence has not been revoked by the Central Bank of Nigeria may re-apply to participate in the scheme after it has satisfied all the conditions required of it by the Board particularly after the Board had given consideration to the— (a) institution's financial position and its general operational practice has improved satisfactorily since the termination order became effective; (b) grounds for which the institution's participation in the Deposit Insurance Scheme was terminated have been remedied; and (c) future earnings prospects and general character of its management are satisfactory.
actmgt.plain: If the Bank’s insured status was previously terminated (but its CBN licence was not revoked), the bank may reapply to rejoin the Deposit Insurance Scheme only after fixing the issues that led to the termination, improving its financial and operational condition, and satisfying NDIC Board’s requirements.
actmgt.riskDescription: Risk of prolonged exclusion from the Deposit Insurance Scheme if the bank does not meet reapplication conditions—this undermines customer trust and limits deposit mobilisation.
actmgt.owner: MD/CEO, Head of Compliance, CFO, Head of Risk, Board Secretary
actmgt.primaryControl: Clear documentation and resolution of all previous compliance breaches; maintain healthy financials and governance practices; proactive engagement with NDIC Board.

actmgt.source: Nigerian Deposit Insurance Corporation (NDIC) Act, 2023
actmgt.title: Duties of insured institutions in relation to examination
actmgt.description: (1) An insured institution shall produce to the examiner as and when required, all books, accounts, documents, management information systems and all information as the examiner may deem necessary or request in the performance of his functions.  (2) Any insured institution, its director or officer that— (a) wilfully refuses to produce any book, account, document or such other information, (b) negligently, wilfully or with intent to defraud, gives information which is false in any material particular, or (c) refuses examiners access to their premises or any hardware or software utilised in its business, commits an offence.
actmgt.plain: The Bank shall:  1. Produce all books, accounts, documents, MIS data, and any information requested by NDIC examiners as needed to carry out their functions. 2. The bank, its directors, or officers must not: – Wilfully refuse to produce documents; – Provide false or misleading information; or – Deny access to premises, systems, or infrastructure used for business.
actmgt.riskDescription: - Non-compliance can lead to prosecution, criminal liability for directors/officers, reputational damage, NDIC sanctions, and increased regulatory scrutiny.
actmgt.owner: - Chief Compliance Officer- Regulatory Affairs/NDIC Liaison- Head of Internal Audit- Department Heads- ICT/Operations Lead
actmgt.primaryControl: - Create and maintain an NDIC Examination Protocol. - Centralized digital archive for examiner-requested records. - Regular training for staff on regulatory cooperation. - Track and monitor all information requests and responses. - Ensure secure access to systems and data for NDIC examiners.

actmgt.title: Report of Examination
actmgt.description: The insured institution shall within two weeks of the presentation to its board of directors convey to the Corporation the reaction of the board of directors to the written report and proposals for implementation of the recommendations.
actmgt.plain: The Bank shall, within two weeks after the NDIC report is presented to its Board of Directors, send to NDIC the Board’s reaction to the report and its implementation plan for the recommendations.

actmgt.source: Nigerian Deposit Insurance Corporation (NDIC) Act, 2023
actmgt.title: Obligations in respect of unauthorised disclosure
actmgt.description: (1) The members of board, staff and agents of an insured institution shall keep strictly confidential and make no unauthorised disclosure or use of any information in relation to the activities or condition of an insured institution or in relation to its customers which they may either directly or indirectly receive in such capacity, even after they cease to be members or staff or agents of that insured institution.  (2) The obligation specified in subsection (1) is imposed on members of the Board and employees of, and agents or other persons engaged by, the Corporation.

actmgt.source: Nigerian Deposit Insurance Corporation (NDIC) Act, 2023
actmgt.title: Priority of claims
actmgt.description: Where an insured institution is unable to meet its obligations or suspends payment or where its management and control has been taken over by the Central Bank of Nigeria or where its licence has been revoked, the assets of the insured institution shall be available to meet all its deposit liabilities and such deposit liabilities shall have priority over all other liabilities of the insured institution.
actmgt.plain: 1. When a bank’s licence is revoked, or the CBN takes over its management or it suspends payments, all deposit liabilities must be settled first before any other liabilities are addressed. 2. The bank’s assets shall be applied first to depositor claims.
actmgt.riskDescription: - Failure to prioritize deposit liabilities may result in: ▪ Breach of statutory liquidation rules ▪ Legal consequences and penalties ▪ Regulatory sanctions ▪ Erosion of public trust
actmgt.owner: - Legal Department- Finance/Treasury Unit- Executive Management
actmgt.primaryControl: - Ensure clear documentation and categorization of liabilities in financial records - Include priority rules in bank’s resolution and liquidation manual - Periodic audit of liability classification and stress testing for insolvency scenarios

actmgt.source: GUIDELINES ON FINANCIAL AND TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE TO OPERATING INSURED BANKS AND DEPOSIT TAKING FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS
actmgt.title: PRE-REQUISITE FOR FINANCIAL ASSISTANCE
actmgt.description: Under the liquidity thresholds, a bank is considered significantly illiquid if it records liquidity ratio greater than 10% but less than 20%, its current account with the CBN is overdrawn and not covered on the next working day subsequently for five working days within a month, a net taker of up to 25% of its total deposits, its ratio of total loans to total deposits is above existing prudential ratio by 20% for three consecutive months and if it incurs clearing operations losses continuously for 10 days. Any bank that exhibits a combination of the above thresholds is expected to solicit for short-term liquidity support from the Corporation.  For an insured institution to qualify for the assistance, it must meet the pre-conditions as contained in section 37 [1] [a-c] of the NDIC Act and others including the Contingency Planning Framework as listed below:  i) The applicant insured institution has difficulty in meeting its obligations to its depositors and other creditors,  ii) It persistently suffers liquidity deficiency,  iii) There exist severe financial conditions which threaten the stability of the financial system thereby posing grave risks to depositors,  iv) An insured institution that is a net taker of up to 25% of its total deposits.
actmgt.plain: The Bank on exhibiting their liquidity distress based on specified thresholds (e.g. net taker > 25% of deposits, liquidity ratio < 20%, CBN overdraft not cleared, high loan-deposit ratio, or 10-day clearing losses) shall request short-term liquidity support from the NDIC and meet the eligibility conditions under Section 37(1)(a–c) of the NDIC Act and Contingency Planning Framework.
actmgt.riskDescription: Failing to monitor liquidity thresholds or delay in seeking NDIC assistance can result in worsening financial health, regulatory sanctions, and risk to depositors.
actmgt.owner: Chief Risk Officer (CRO); Treasurer; Compliance Officer
actmgt.primaryControl: Daily liquidity monitoring; automated alerts; Board-level review of liquidity breaches; prompt NDIC notification procedure.

actmgt.source: GUIDELINES ON FINANCIAL AND TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE TO OPERATING INSURED BANKS AND DEPOSIT TAKING FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS
actmgt.title: REQUIREMENTS FOR FINANCIAL ASSISTANCE
actmgt.description: a] A formal Application for financial assistance stating the amount required.  b] The purpose of the request i.e. the causes and extent of the problem to be addressed.  c] Tenor/Repayment period.  d] Sources and Mode of the loan repayment  e] The current and projected monthly Cash Flow, Statement of Comprehensive Income and Statement of Financial Position, clearly stating the underlying assumptions for the projections, the impact of the expected facility and its amortization over the period of repayment.  f] Board Resolution authorizing the request for the facility.  g] Evidence of the repayment of all insider related credits.  h] Evidence of repayment of any outstanding indebtedness to other banks by the Directors of the applicant bank.  i] Schedule of existing borrowings by the bank  j] The schedule of non-performing credits as well as the major liabilities that have matured.  k] A statement in quantifiable terms of measures taken to address the institution’s liquidity problem. E.g. debt recovery, cost saving measures adopted.  l] Evidence of compliance with the recommendations of the CBN/NDIC Examiners.  m] A certified true copy of the Articles and Memorandum of Association of the insured institution.  n] The list of major shareholders [5% and above] and their shareholding as well as resumes of the Board and Management of the insured institution.  o] An acceptable joint and several guarantees of the members of the Board of Directors and Principal Shareholders of the insured institution.  p] Identification and Description of the specific property being offered as collateral, accompanied with recent Estate Valuers Report on same, stating the open market and Forced Sale Values.  q] Evidence of comprehensive insurance of the property.  r] A Strategic Business Plan indicating how the Management intends to address the insured institution’s problem, repay the loan, to attain and sustain the N25 billion minimum capital requirement.  s] Any other information that may assist in the processing of the request of the particular insured institution.
actmgt.plain: The Bank shall: 1. Submit a formal application for financial assistance, stating the required amount. 2. Provide details of the purpose of the loan request, outlining the cause and extent of the issue. 3. Indicate the tenor and repayment plan of the loan. 4. Clearly state sources and mode of repayment. 5. Include current and projected monthly cash flows, profit/loss statement, and balance sheet, along with assumptions, expected impact of the facility, and amortization plan. 6. Attach a Board resolution authorizing the request. 7. Submit evidence of repayment of insider-related credits. 8. Provide evidence of directors’ loan repayment to other banks. 9. Submit schedule of existing borrowings. 10. Provide a schedule of non-performing credits and major matured liabilities. 11. Present a quantifiable statement of remedial measures (e.g., debt recovery, cost savings). 12. Submit evidence of compliance with CBN/NDIC examiner recommendations. 13. Attach certified true copy of the Memorandum & Articles of Association. 14. Provide a list of major shareholders (5% and above) and resumes of board/management. 15. Submit joint and several guarantees from directors and principal shareholders. 16. Identify and describe property offered as collateral, with valuation report. 17. Present evidence of insurance on the property. 18. Submit a strategic business plan to address problems, repay the loan, and meet capital requirements. 19. Provide any other relevant information to aid assessment.
actmgt.riskDescription: - Failure to provide complete and accurate documentation can result in: ▪ Rejection of financial assistance request ▪ Regulatory delays or sanctions ▪ Further deterioration of liquidity condition ▪ Loss of regulatory confidence and possible resolution action
actmgt.owner: - Chief Financial Officer (CFO)- Head of Regulatory Affairs- Company Secretary- Head, Credit and Recovery- Executive Management/Board
actmgt.primaryControl: - Maintain an NDIC/CBN assistance documentation checklist - Establish a dedicated compliance team to compile and validate all required documents - Review financial statements and schedules monthly for accuracy - Secure board approvals in advance for strategic applications - Pre-audit collateral valuation, guarantees, and insurance prior to application

actmgt.source: GUIDELINES ON FINANCIAL AND TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE TO OPERATING INSURED BANKS AND DEPOSIT TAKING FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS
actmgt.title: SECURITY AND REPAYMENT
actmgt.description: Any application for financial assistance must provide for repayment of such assistance. The facility shall be fully secured by tangible security. The applicant bank or insured institution for financial assistance must submit joint and several guarantees from the members of its Board as well as principal shareholders for the repayment of any financial assistance granted.
actmgt.plain: If the Bank is applying for NDIC financial assistance, it must ensure full repayment provisions. The loan shall be backed by tangible security, and all board members and principal shareholders must jointly guarantee repayment.
actmgt.riskDescription: Failure to provide sufficient security or enforceable guarantees may result in rejection of the financial assistance request or legal/financial penalties.
actmgt.owner: CFO; Head of Legal; Company Secretary; MD/CEO
actmgt.primaryControl: Pre-verification of security assets; legal due diligence on enforceability of guarantees; NDIC-compliant loan documentation

actmgt.source: GUIDELINES ON FINANCIAL AND TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE TO OPERATING INSURED BANKS AND DEPOSIT TAKING FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS
actmgt.title: FORMAL AGREEMENT WITH THE CORPORATION FOR FINANCIAL AND TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE
actmgt.description: The terms and conditions for a facility will vary from one insured institution to the other depending on the nature of the problem and the type of facility being sought. In general, the terms and conditions will cover pre and post-disbursement conditions to be met by the applicant bank. These include but are not limited to the following:  i] The insured institution should show evidence of substantial debt repayment by shareholders and their related interests.  ii] The insured institution should not default in premium payment.  iii] Every applicant insured institution will submit a time-framed turn-around plan, the evaluation of which will determine the extent of financial and technical assistance to be granted by the Corporation.  iv] The agreement will contain among others, the following terms and conditions that will be determined on a case by case basis: - Purpose of facility - Amount of financial facility - Tenor - Repayment - Interest rate - Security – essentially government securities [e.g. investment certificates] or other acceptable collateral.  v] Applicant insured institution will submit joint and several guarantees from the members of its Board as well as the principal shareholders for the repayment of any financial assistance granted.  vi] The insured institution will suspend the repayment of dividends and bonus where it is in default of its repayment schedule.  vii] The insured institution will embark on intensive deposit drive particularly from non-interbank sources.
actmgt.plain: The Bank shall:  1. Show evidence of substantial debt repayment by shareholders and related parties. 2. Ensure no default in NDIC premium payments. 3. Submit a time-bound turnaround plan to the NDIC; the plan will influence the type and extent of assistance granted. 4. Enter into an agreement with NDIC specifying:     - Purpose of the facility     - Amount     - Tenor and repayment terms     - Interest rate     - Security (e.g., government securities or acceptable collateral) 5. Provide joint and several guarantees from board members and principal shareholders. 6. Suspend dividends and bonuses during any repayment default period. 7. Implement an aggressive deposit mobilization strategy, excluding inter-bank sources. 8. Submit monthly returns to NDIC including:     - Debt recovery     - Performing/non-performing loans     - New deposits     - New lending     - Asset/Liability maturity profile     - Cash flow     - Financial position     - Comprehensive income     - Fraud/forgery incidents and disciplinary actions 9. Prepare for post-assistance monitoring by NDIC via onsite (target examinations, spot checks) and offsite reviews (return analysis and NDIC directives).
actmgt.riskDescription: - Failure to meet pre/post-disbursement conditions can result in: ▪ Withdrawal of financial support ▪ Regulatory sanctions or license suspension ▪ Public confidence erosion ▪ Increased liquidity crisis and reputational risk
actmgt.owner: - Managing Director/CEO- Chief Financial Officer- Board of Directors- Head of Regulatory Affairs- Chief Compliance Officer
actmgt.primaryControl: - Maintain an NDIC Agreement Compliance Tracker - Establish a turnaround plan review committee with measurable KPIs - Secure board and shareholder guarantees and collateral documentation in advance - Create automated templates for monthly NDIC returns - Set internal reminders for premium payments and dividend restrictions - Schedule internal audits and mock inspections ahead of NDIC visits
