actmgt.description: i) Submission of a Time-framed Strategic Turn-around Plan The applicant bank, or financial institution, must submit a time-framed strategic turn-around plan which shall include, among others: Viability projections based on reasonable assumptions regarding the use of the assistance, Earnings, Reserve levels, Asset quality Trends, Anticipated dividends and Needs. This will be evaluated by the Corporation in determining the extent of assistance to be granted.
actmgt.plain: The Bank when applying for NDIC assistance shall submit a strategic turn-around plan with a clear timeline. The plan must include realistic projections on viability, earnings, reserves, asset quality, dividend outlook, and capital needs.
actmgt.riskDescription: Failure to submit or submission of an inadequate turn-around plan may lead to delay or denial of financial or technical support from NDIC.

actmgt.description: The Board and Senior Management of all insured financial institutions shall ensure compliance with all relevant statutes and regulations, such as NDIC Act 2006, BOFIA 2020, the CBN Supervisory Intervention Framework for the Nigerian Banking Sector, Prudential Guidelines, Corporate Governance Guidelines, and all CBN directives to avoid breaches of legal, statutory, regulatory obligations related to compliance with the requirement of the DPAS Framework.

actmgt.description: 2.1. Interest Rate:      2.1.1. Local Currency Loans: Negotiable (the rate should anchor MPR, reflecting the risk-based pricing model). Also, when a bank intends to introduce a new rate different from the agreed rate, the bank should notify its customers of the new rate at least 10 business days in advance of the application of the new rate.         2.1.2. Mortgage Financing: Negotiable         2.1.3. Interest Rate - Foreign Currency Loans: Negotiable         2.1.4. Interest on Authorized OD: Negotiable (the rate should anchor MPR, reflecting the risk-based pricing model). Also, when a bank intends to introduce a new rate different from the agreed rate, the bank should notify its customers of the new rate at least 10 business days in advance of the application of the new rate.         2.1.5. Interest on Authorized OD: Not permissible except as a result of facility repayment (where it occurs, Penal Rate as provided in Section 2.1.9 shall apply)         2.1.6. Drawing against uncleared effects: Negotiable (the rate should anchor MPR, reflecting the risk-based pricing model).         2.1.7. Equipment Leasing: Negotiable (the rate should anchor MPR, reflecting the risk-based pricing model). Also, when a bank intends to introduce a new rate different from the agreed rate, the bank should notify its customers of the new rate at least 10 business days in advance of the application of the new rate.         2.1.8. Discountable Instruments e.g. Usance bill, Bankers' Acceptance,Commercial Papers, Promissory Notes etc: Negotiable  2.2. Lending Fees NB: Total lending fees shall not exceed 2 per cent:           2.2.1.  Management Fee covering processing, appraisal, ancillary and other related fees on a new loan application (one-off charge) - Negotiable subject to maximum of 1% of the principal amount disbursed (one off charge).       2.2.2.   Facility Enhancement Fee: This fee applies when an additional amount is granted to a customer. Where this fee applies, management fee shall not apply - Negotiable subject to maximum of 1% of the additional amount disbursed (one-off charge).        2.2.3. Restructuring Fee: Outstanding balance of customer - Negotiable, subject to a maximum of 0.5% of the outstanding amount (one off charge).        2.2.3. Commitment Fee - Negotiable, subject to a maximum of 1% on the undisbursed amount (one-off charge).  2.3. Charges for Consortium Lending:       2.3.1. Agency Fee - Negotiable          2.3.2. Management Fee - Negotiable subject to a maximum of 1% of principal amount (one-off charge)          2.3.3. Commitment/Non-Drawing Fee - Negotiable subject to a maximum of 0.5% of the undisbursed amount (one-off charge)          2.3.4. Commission Charges for Underwriting Services - Negotiable  2.6. Credit Reference Report - Cost Recovery  2.7. InterBank Borrowing Rate:       2.7.1. Overnight/Call Money - Negotiable          2.7.2. Tenured - Negotiable
actmgt.plain: The Bank shall ensure that all lending interest rates (local and foreign currency loans, overdrafts, equipment leasing, discountable instruments) are negotiated but anchored to the CBN's Monetary Policy Rate (MPR). Where applicable, customers must be notified 10 business days in advance before a rate change. Lending fees must not exceed 2% of loan amount, and specific caps apply to each fee category.
actmgt.riskDescription: Charging interest rates or fees outside permitted limits, failing to anchor pricing on MPR, or not notifying customers of interest rate changes may result in regulatory sanctions and customer litigation.
actmgt.owner: Credit & Risk Department, Treasury, Legal & Compliance, Product Management
actmgt.primaryControl: - Embed MPR-based risk-pricing in all credit product models- Apply caps on management, enhancement, restructuring, and commitment fees via system validations- Ensure all rate change notices are sent at least 10 business days before application- Automate fee rules in loan origination and core banking systems- Apply exception reporting for fee and interest breaches

actmgt.title: CURRENT ACCOUNT MAINTENANCE FEE
actmgt.description: Current Account Maintenance Fee (CAMF) Applicable to current accounts ONLY in respect of customer-induced debit transactions to third parties and debit transfers/lodgments to the customer's account in another bank. Note that CAMF is not applicable to Savings Accounts - Negotiable subject to a maximum of ₦1 per mille
actmgt.plain: The Bank may charge Current Account Maintenance Fee (CAMF) only on customer-initiated debit transactions to third parties and interbank transfers from a current account. The fee must not exceed ₦1 per ₦1,000 (₦1 per mille). CAMF must not be applied to Savings Accounts under any circumstance.
actmgt.riskDescription: Charging CAMF above ₦1 per mille, applying it to transactions not covered (e.g., internal transfers or non-third-party debits), or charging it on Savings Accounts would constitute regulatory non-compliance, leading to penalties, refunds, and reputational damage.
actmgt.owner: Operations Department, Product Control, Internal Audit, Compliance
actmgt.primaryControl: - Configure core banking system to only apply CAMF to current accounts and eligible debit transactions- Block CAMF on all Savings Accounts- Cap CAMF at ₦1 per mille in all system configurations- Run automated transaction-type checks before CAMF deduction

points.text: Current Account Maintenance Fee (CAMF) is applicable to current accounts ONLY in respect of customer-induced debit transactions to third parties and debit transfers/lodgments to the customer's account in another bank, is not applicable to Savings Accounts, and is negotiable subject to a maximum of ₦1 per mille.
points.content: Current Account Maintenance Fee (CAMF) is applicable to current accounts ONLY in respect of customer-induced debit transactions to third parties and debit transfers/lodgments to the customer's account in another bank, is not applicable to Savings Accounts, and is negotiable subject to a maximum of ₦1 per mille.

actmgt.title: COMMISSION ON BONDS GUARANTEES & INDEMNITIES, ETC.
actmgt.description: 4.1. Bid Bond/Tender Security/Bid Security - Negotiable subject to a maximum of 1% of the Bond value for the first year and 0.5% on subsequent years on contingent liabilities 4.2 Performance Bond (chargeable from date of contingent liability) - Negotiable subject to a maximum of 1% of the Bond value for the first year and 0.5% on subsequent years on contingent liabilities 4.3 Advance Payment Guarantee (APG) (chargeable from date of contingent liability) - Negotiable subject to a maximum of 1% of the APG value for the first year and 0.5% on subsequent years on contingent liabilities  Note: Fees shall be charged based on the value of advance payment received by the bank  4.4 Third-party Cheque Indemnities - To be discouraged - However, negotiable for non-clearing financial institution e.g. Micro-finance banks.  4.5 Bank Guarantee - Negotiable subject to a maximum of 1% of the Guarantee value for the first year and 0.5% on subsequent years on contingent liabilities  4.6 Other Bonds, Guarantees and Indemnities - Negotiable subject to a maximum of 1% of the value for the first year and 0.5% on subsequent years on contingent liabilities
actmgt.plain: The Bank may charge commissions on bonds, guarantees, and indemnities, but the fees must not exceed: - 1% of the bond/guarantee value in the first year - 0.5% per annum in subsequent years - Charges apply to contingent liabilities, and fees on APG must be based on the actual advance received - Third-party cheque indemnities are discouraged, except for non-clearing institutions like microfinance banks.
actmgt.riskDescription: Charging above the capped rates or applying fees to unapproved instruments (e.g. third-party cheques in DMBs) violates regulatory limits, exposing the bank to sanctions, refunds, and potential reputation loss.
actmgt.owner: Trade Services, Credit Risk, Operations, Compliance
actmgt.primaryControl: - System parameter setup to cap charges at 1% (first year) and 0.5% (subsequent years) - Define fee structure based on contingent liability creation date - Apply APG charges only on value of advance received - Block setup of third-party cheque indemnities in commercial banks - Include fee rule validations in bond issuance workflow

actmgt.description: 5.1 Purchases from CBN - As may be advised by the CBN.  5.2 Inter-bank Purchases - As may be advised by the CBN  5.3 Inward Telegraphic/SWIFT and other transfers expressed in foreign currency - No charge  5.4 Travelers Cheques - As may be advised by the CBN  5.5 Foreign Currency Purchases from customers - Interbank foreign exchange bid rate  5.6 Outward Telegraphic/SWIFT and other transfers - Swift cost recovery, 0.5% commission on transfer plus associated offshore bank charges (where applicable)  5.7 Foreign Currency Sales to Customers - As may be advised by the CBN  5.8 Commission on Withdrawals from Domiciliary Accounts (whether savings or current account) - 0.05% of transaction value or ₦10, whichever is lower  5.9 Foreign Draft Purchase -  0.1% of the value of the cheque plus offshore charges  5.10 Collection Charge on Cheques - 1% of cheque value or Naira equivalent of US $10, whichever is lower
actmgt.plain: The Bank shall comply with CBN-advised rates and caps for all FX-related charges: - No charge on inward telegraphic/SWIFT transfers - Outward transfers must not exceed: Swift cost recovery + 0.5% commission + offshore charges (if applicable) - Commission on withdrawals from domiciliary accounts must not exceed 0.05% of transaction value or ₦10, whichever is lower - Foreign draft purchase: max 0.1% + offshore charges - Cheque collection charge: max 1% or ₦ equivalent of USD $10, whichever is lower
actmgt.riskDescription: Charging beyond regulatory limits or levying fees where prohibited (e.g., on inward transfers) exposes the bank to penalties, reputational damage, and regulatory sanctions.
actmgt.owner: Treasury Operations, FX Desk, E-Banking Operations, Compliance
actmgt.primaryControl: - System configuration to block fees on inward transfers - Charge caps on domiciliary withdrawals and foreign drafts enforced via core banking systems - Review and align FX commission parameters with latest CBN circulars - Clear documentation of cost recovery elements (e.g., SWIFT fees) for transparency

actmgt.title: BILLS FOR COLLECTION
actmgt.description: 6.1. Bills for Collection (Inward) Collection:          6.1.1 Commission on Bills for Collection - Negotiable subject to a maximum of 0.5% of the bill value          6.1.2 Postage (where applicable) - Actual cost of postage          6.1.3 Communication Charge (where applicable) - Actual cost of communication  6.2 Holding Charges after Non-Payment, Chargeable One Month after Due Date - ₦5,000 per month  6.3 Extension Charges for Sight Bills altered to Tenured (usance) Bills - ₦3,000 plus cost of SWIFT  6.4 Protest Charges plus Notary Public Fees - Cost of postage, (chargeable only where the agreement specifies that the customer will pay)            Bills for Collection (Outward) 6.5 Collection Commission: Commission on Bills for Collection - Negotiable subject to a maximum of 0.5% of the face value of the bill  6.6 Bills for Collection - Negotiation - Negotiable
actmgt.plain: The Bank is required to: - Charge no more than 0.5% of bill value as commission on both inward and outward bills for collection. - Postage and communication charges (if applicable) must reflect actual cost incurred. - Apply ₦5,000 per month as holding charges only after 1 month past due date. - Charge ₦3,000 + SWIFT cost for extension of sight bills to tenured bills. - Protest charges (e.g., notary fees/postage) are chargeable only if the customer agreed to pay in the initial arrangement.
actmgt.riskDescription: Overcharging, charging where not permitted, or failing to disclose terms can result in customer complaints, reputational harm, and CBN sanctions.
actmgt.owner: Trade Services Unit, Operations, Treasury, Compliance
actmgt.primaryControl: - Core banking system to cap collection commission at 0.5% - Manual override disabled for protest charges unless agreement exists - Postage and communication fees must be backed by receipts - Holding charges system-triggered after 30 days only

actmgt.title: STRAIGHT FORWARD HANDLING OF DOCUMENTS
actmgt.description: 7.1. Export Documents Delivery - Negotiable subject to a maximum of ₦5,000 plus cost of courier  7.2. Import Documents:          7.2.1 Delivery - Negotiable subject to a maximum of ₦5,000 plus cost of courier               7.2.2 Bills for Collection against Acceptance -  Negotiable subject to a maximum of ₦5,000 plus cost of courier           7.2.3 Bills for Collection against Payment - Cost of courier
actmgt.plain: The Bank shall: - Charge no more than ₦5,000 plus actual courier cost for delivery of export or import documents. - For Bills for Collection against Acceptance, the same ₦5,000 cap and courier fee applies. - For Bills for Collection against Payment, only actual courier cost is chargeable (no additional fee).
actmgt.riskDescription: Charging more than allowed limits, omitting courier cost justification, or incorrectly charging for services not covered (e.g., charging a fee where only courier cost is allowed).
actmgt.owner: Trade Operations Unit, Compliance, Internal Control
actmgt.primaryControl: - Fee limits pre-configured in trade finance system - Courier costs backed by invoices - System blocks charges exceeding ₦5,000 unless exception justified - Dual authorization for charges related to document handling

actmgt.title: INWARD AND OUTWARD LETTERS OF CREDIT
actmgt.description: Inward Letters of Credit (Export) 8.1. Processing and Registration of Nigerian Export Form - ₦3,000 in addition to maintenance fee on Form NXP as advised by the CBN.  8.2. Advising Commission:        8.2.1 Where a Nigerian bank simply verifies authenticity of the Credit and delivers same: ₦5,000 flat        8.2.2 Where a Nigerian bank has to re-write the Credit at the instance of the customer: 0.05% of the value, subject to a minimum of Naira equivalent of US $25  8.3 Commission on Confirmation of LC - Minimum of ₦5,000 subject to a maximum of 0.5% of the face value  8.4 Letter of Credit - Negotiation - Negotiable         Outward Letters of Credit (Import) 8.5 Purchase of Form A - ₦3,000 in addition to maintenance fee on Form NXP as advised by the CBN.  8.6. Form M:         8.6.1 Processing: ₦3,000 in addition to maintenance fee on Form NXP as advised by the CBN.         8.6.2 Amendment: Negotiable subject to a maximum of ₦5,000         8.6.3 Revocation/Extension: Negotiable subject to a maximum of ₦5,000  8.7 LC Establishment Commission          8.7.1 For credits up to 180 days: 1% of face value         8.7.2 For credits up to 270 days: 1.25% of face value         8.7.3 For credits up to 360 days (these charges are on the period of validity of the credit): 1.5% of face value  8.8 Renewal and Extension in the LC value:         8.8.1 Renewals - Commission on applicable LC establishment as specified in 8.7 above         8.8.2 Extensions - ₦5,000.00 flat  8.9 Increases or Enhancements in the LC value - Additional establishment commission should be charged on the amount of any increase for the unexpired period of validity of credit (in line 8.7 above)  8.10 Amendment of LC at the instance of the Customer - ₦2,000 per application  8.11 Usance Bill under Credit Guarantee Commission:          8.11.1 Where the bill is less than one year - ₦3 per mille per month          8.11.2 Where the bill exceeds one year - ₦5 per mille per month  8.12 Pre-Arrival Assessment Receipt (PAR) - ₦2,500 flat irrespective of payment mode  8.13 Processing of Form NCX - ₦3,000 in addition to maintenance fee on Form NCX as advised by the CBN.
actmgt.plain: The Bank shall ensure the following: Inward LC (Export): - Charge ₦3,000 for NXP form processing + CBN-advised maintenance fee. - Charge ₦5,000 flat if only authenticating LC. - Charge 0.05% (min. US $25 in naira) if rewriting LC. - Confirmations: ₦5,000 minimum; max 0.5% of LC face value. Outward LC (Import): - Charge ₦3,000 for Form A and Form M processing + NXP maintenance fee. - Amendment/Revocation/Extension fees capped at ₦5,000. - LC establishment charges depend on tenor: 180 days – 1%, 270 days – 1.25%, 360 days – 1.5%. - Renewals charged as fresh establishment; extensions ₦5,000 flat. - LC value increase: apply additional commission only on increased portion. - LC Amendment: ₦2,000 flat. - Usance bills: < 1yr = ₦3 per mille/month; > 1yr = ₦5 per mille/month. - PAR fee = ₦2,500 flat. - Form NCX fee = ₦3,000 + CBN-advised fee.
actmgt.riskDescription: - Overcharging or applying multiple fees in contravention of caps. - Charging confirmation, amendment, or renewal fees without client instruction. - Non-compliance with CBN-advised fee component on Forms A, M, NXP, and NCX. - Misapplying LC establishment tiers or not updating increased LC values correctly.
actmgt.owner: Trade Finance Unit, Compliance, Finance Control, IT (fee system config)
actmgt.primaryControl: - Fee templates and transaction screens configured for limit validation. - Segregation of duties between processing and authorising officers. - Review of CBN circulars on LC processing for fee updates. - System control to apply LC tenor-based charges automatically. - Fee audit trail linked to transaction reference.

actmgt.description: 9.1 Bank Draft Charges:        9.1.1 Customer                    Current Account: ₦300                    Savings Account: ₦500         9.1.2 Non-Customer - ₦500 + 0.1% of draft value  9.2 Draft Repurchase - No charge  9.3 Charge paid by non-account holders for returned instruments (e.g. local money transfer, Prepaid Card loading) - ₦200 flat. However, banks are enjoined to undertake KYC on such customers, subject to maximum daily limit of ₦20,000  9.4 Cash Handling charge - As may be advised by the CBN  9.5 Special Clearing of Cheques - Negotiable  9.6 Standing Order Charge (In Branch at the instance of the Customer)            (a) Intra-bank - No charge            (b) maximum of ₦50 per transaction  9.7 Direct Debit            9.7.1 Direct Debit Charge - Same as the cost of platform used            9.7.2 Failed Direct Debit -                    9.7.2.1 Due to reasons other than the account being unfunded - No charge                   9.7.2.2 Due to the account being unfunded - 1% of amount or ₦5,000 whichever is higher (to be borne by drawer only)  9.8 Safe Custody - Negotiable  9.9 Stopped Cheques - ₦500 per order  9.10 a. Processing fee - ₦100 flat              b. Custodian fee – in line with extant Guidelines on Custodianship on Money Market and Other Fixed Income Instruments (applicable on Treasury bills purchase)              c. Settlement Trade Via S4 - Cost Recovery
actmgt.plain: The Bank is required to: Bank Drafts: - Charge ₦300 for draft from current account holders. - Charge ₦500 for draft from savings account holders. - Charge ₦500 + 0.1% of draft value for non-customers. Draft Repurchase: No charge allowed. Returned Instruments (Non-Account Holders): - Charge ₦200 flat. - Apply maximum daily limit of ₦20,000. - Ensure proper KYC documentation. Cash Handling Charges: - To be applied only as advised by CBN. Special Cheque Clearing: - Charges negotiable. Standing Orders: - Intra-bank: No charge. - Inter-bank: Max ₦50 per transaction. Direct Debit: - Fee should reflect actual platform cost. - Failed debit due to unfunded account: Charge 1% or ₦5,000 (whichever is higher), to drawer only. Safe Custody: - Negotiable fees permitted. Stopped Cheques: - Charge ₦500 per request. Processing/Custodian/Settlement: - Processing fee: ₦100 flat. - Custodian fee: Must align with relevant money market custodianship guidelines. - Settlement via S4: Cost recovery only.
actmgt.riskDescription: - Charging fees above prescribed caps or for items mandated to be free (e.g., intra-bank standing orders, draft repurchase). - Deducting failed direct debit charges from beneficiaries. - Failure to apply KYC and daily limits on non-account holder services. - Charging custodian/settlement fees beyond regulatory limits or outside scope.
actmgt.owner: Operations Unit, Compliance, IT (for system enforcement), Retail & E-Banking
actmgt.primaryControl: - Automated fee tables and business rules on transaction platforms. - Internal limits enforced for daily non-customer transfers. - KYC validation prompts during over-the-counter service. - Alerting system for charge exceptions (e.g., unauthorized draft repurchase fee).

actmgt.description: 10.1. Internet Banking:         10.1.1 Hardware Token - Cost recovery subject to a maximum charge of ₦2,500.         10.1.2 Software Token - One Time Password (OTP) - No charge. However, where the OTP is sent to the customer via SMS, charges will be at cost recovery basis.              10.1.3 Hardware Token replacement - Cost recovery subject to a maximum of ₦2,500. (Customer to bear cost only in the event of physical damage, loss of token or replacement after expiration) 10.1.4 Bill Payment (including Bill Payment through other E-channels) - Negotiable subject to a maximum of ₦500 per beneficiary payable by the sender  10.2 Electronic Funds transfer:                                                             Below ₦5,000 - ₦10                                                             ₦5,001 - ₦50,000 - ₦25                                                             Above ₦50,000 - ₦50  10.3 RTGS Card Maintenance Fee - ₦50  10.4 Foreign Currency Denominated Debit/Credit Card          10.4.1 Foreign Currency Denominated Debit/Credit Card - $10 p.a. (or its equivalent)          10.4.2 Naira Debit/Credit Card                                  Cards linked to current account: No charge                                  Cards linked to savings account: maximum of ₦50 quarterly maintenance fee  10.5 Credit Card Charges:          10.5.1 Issuance Fee - ₦1,000 (one-off charge). The same charge applies irrespective of card type (i.e. regular or premium card)               10.5.2 Replacement Fee (at customer's instance for lost or damaged cards) - ₦1,000 (one-off charge). The same charge applies irrespective of card type (i.e. regular or premium card)           10.5.3 Renewal Fee (upon expiry of existing cards) - ₦1,000 (one-off charge). The same charge applies irrespective of card type (i.e. regular or premium card)           10.5.4 Interest Charges - Negotiable  10.6 Debit Card Charges:           10.6.1 Issuance Fee - ₦1,000 (one-off charge). The same charge applies irrespective of card type (i.e. regular or premium card)           10.6.2 Remote-On-Us (from other bank's ATM) in Nigeria - maximum of ₦35 after the third withdrawal within the same month           10.6.2 Replacement Fee (at customer's instance for lost or damaged cards) - ₦1,000 (one-off charge). The same charge applies irrespective of card type (i.e. regular or premium card)            10.6.3 Renewal Fee (upon expiry of existing cards) -  ₦1,000 (one-off charge). The same charge applies irrespective of card type (i.e. regular or premium card) 10.6.4 Prepaid Card Loading/Loading Charge - No charge  10.7 ATM Transactions:            10.7.1 On-Us (withdrawal from issuing bank's ATM) - No charge            10.7.2 Not On-Us (withdrawal from other bank's ATM) in Nigeria - ₦35 after the third withdrawal within the same month            10.7.3 International Withdrawals (outside Nigeria) - Exact cost by international acquirer (cost recovery)  10.8 Merchant Service Commission (MSC): Commission on Transactions (including Domestic, International, Travels and Entertainment) -  0.50% of transaction value but not more than ₦1,000  10.9 Bulk Payments (e.g. Salaries, Dividends etc) - Negotiable subject to a maximum of ₦1.5 per beneficiary payable by the sender  10.10 Transaction Alerts            10.10.1 SMS alert (withdrawal) -  No charge. However, where a customer opts-in to receive SMS alert, the customer should issue an indemnity for all losses that may arise as a result to the bank.            10.10.2 Email notification - Cost recovery (on customer-induced transactions) No charge (for bank-induced transactions)  10.11 PIN Reissue - No charge  10.12 PIN Reset - No charge  10.13 Use of Unstructured Supplementary Service Data (USSD) - Current NIP charges apply  10.14 Purchase with cash-back - ₦100 per ₦20,000 subject to cumulative ₦60,000 daily withdrawal
actmgt.plain: The Bank shall ensure: Tokens & Internet Banking - Hardware token: Max ₦2,500 (cost recovery only). - OTP via software token: Free; via SMS: charge at cost only. - Hardware token replacement (if lost/damaged): Max ₦2,500. - Bill payments (via all e-channels): Max ₦500 per beneficiary (sender bears cost). Electronic Fund Transfers (NIP): - < ₦5,000 = ₦10 - ₦5,001–₦50,000 = ₦25 - > ₦50,000 = ₦50 Card Charges - RTGS maintenance: ₦50 - FX cards: $10 p.a. - Naira cards (current a/c): No fee; (savings): Max ₦50/quarter - Card issuance/renewal/replacement: Max ₦1,000 (all types) ATM Withdrawals - On-us: Free - Not-on-us: Free for first 3 withdrawals/month, then ₦35 - Intl. withdrawal: Cost recovery only Merchant Commission - MSC: 0.5% of transaction value, capped at ₦1,000 Bulk Payments (Salaries, Dividends) - Max ₦1.50/beneficiary Alerts and Notifications - SMS alerts: Free (with opt-in indemnity) - Email alerts: Free for bank-induced, cost recovery for customer-induced PIN Services - Reissue/reset: Free USSD/Other - Apply current NIP charges - Cash-back on purchases: ₦100 per ₦20,000, max ₦60,000/day
actmgt.riskDescription: - Charging above limits or for services that should be free (e.g., PIN reset, on-us ATM use).- Charging customers for unsolicited or non-consensual SMS alerts.- Applying maintenance charges on current account-linked Naira cards.- Incorrect USSD/NIP deductions.- Billing customers more than ₦35 for ATM transactions after the 3rd withdrawal or charging for first 3.- Charging above ₦1.50 for bulk transfers per recipient.
actmgt.owner: Digital Banking, Cards Unit, Operations, Compliance, IT/Platform Development
actmgt.primaryControl: - Pre-configured fee tables and caps in banking systems.- Mandatory opt-in process with indemnity for SMS alerts.- Customer account classification check (savings vs current) before applying maintenance fees.- Regular reconciliation of electronic charges against transaction types.

actmgt.description: 11.1 Reactivation of Accounts - No charge  11.2 Closure of Account (savings, current, or domiciliary) - No charge  11.3 Insurance Premium paid on behalf of customer - Exact Premium (customer to choose from a list of at least 3 insurance companies to be recommended by the bank)  11.4 Insurance of Statement of Account         11.4.1 Mandatory Monthly issuance of Statement of Account on Current and Savings Accounts - No charge             11.4.2 Special Request for Statement of Account (re-quest in a manner other than agreed on mandatory issuance - Maximum of ₦20 per page  11.5 Returned Cheques:          11.5.1 Due to reasons other than the account being unfunded - No charge          11.5.2 Due to the account being unfunded - 1% of amount or ₦5,000 whichever is higher (to be borne by drawer only). This is without prejudice to the Dud Cheque Act  11.6 Business Visit initiated by Customer:          11.6.1 Local - No charge          11.6.2 Foreign - Negotiable  11.7 Status Enquiry at the Request of Customer - ₦500 per request  11.8 Letter of Discharge/Age for Facilities Repaid by Customer - No charge  11.9 Verification of Customers' Documents with Government Agencies:          11.9.1 Search at Corporate Affairs Commission (CAC), land registry, legal search etc. - Cost recovery               11.9.2 Obtaining Certified True Copy (CTC) - Cost recovery                11.9.3 Perfection of Security for Credit Facilities. - Cost recovery  11.10 Confirmation of Overseas Enquiries to Correspondent Bank at the Instance of the Customer - ₦500 plus Cost of Postage (if applicable)  11.11 Issuance of Certified Banker's Report/Commercial Papers (to be borne by the Issuer) - Negotiable  11.12 Issuance of Withdrawal Booklet/Passbook - No charge  11.13 Customized Deposit Booklet - Cost Recovery  11.14 Overridng Cash Withdrawals below the limit set by the CBN cash withdrawal/lodgment policy - No charge  11.15 Intra-bank Cash Deposits/withdrawals within limits approved by the CBN - No charge  11.16 Cost of Cheque Books         11.16.1 Cheque Books - Cost recovery         11.16.2 Counter Cheque -  ₦50 per leaflet  11.17 Advisory/Consultancy fee - Negotiable (only applies where there is a written advisory/consultancy agreement between the bank and the customer)  11.18 Cashless Policy          11.18.1 Individual:                                 Cash deposit - 2% for transactions above ₦500,000                                 Cash withdrawal - 3% for transactions above ₦500,000           11.18.2 Corporate:                                  Cash deposit - 3% for transactions above ₦3,000,000                                  Cash withdrawal - 5% for transactions above ₦3,000,000
actmgt.plain: The Bank shall ensure: Account Services - Reactivation of dormant accounts: Free - Account closure (savings, current, domiciliary): Free Insurance Premium - Charge only actual premium cost. - Customer must choose from at least 3 insurers suggested by the bank. Statement of Account - Monthly statements (mandatory): Free - Special/extra statement requests: Max ₦20/page Returned Cheques - Not due to insufficient funds: Free - Due to insufficient funds: ₦5,000 or 1% (whichever is higher) Customer-Initiated Business Visits - Local: Free - Foreign: Negotiable Status Enquiry & Letters - Status Enquiry: ₦500/request - Letter of Discharge (upon loan repayment): Free Document Verification & Legal - CAC, Land Registry, CTC, Legal Searches, etc.: Cost Recovery Only Overseas Correspondent Enquiry - ₦500 + postage (if any) Banker's Report/CPs: Negotiable (issuer pays) Cheque Book/Passbook - Withdrawal booklet/passbook: Free - Customized deposit booklet: Cost recovery - Cheque books: Cost recovery - Counter cheque: ₦50 per leaf Advisory/Consulting Fee - Negotiable only with written agreement with the customer Cashless Policy Charges - Individuals:   - Deposits > ₦500,000: 2%   - Withdrawals > ₦500,000: 3% - Corporates:   - Deposits > ₦3 million: 3%   - Withdrawals > ₦3 million: 5% - Note: No charge for intra-bank transactions within limits
actmgt.riskDescription: - Charging customers for free services (e.g., account closure, monthly statements)- Charging insurance premium without offering insurer choice- Charging more than ₦20/page for extra statements- Misapplying dud cheque penalties- Charging customers for status enquiry or discharge letters contrary to policy- Applying advisory/consultancy fees without signed agreements- Misapplying cashless policy charges below applicable limits
actmgt.owner: Operations, Legal, Customer Service, Compliance, Retail & Corporate Banking Units
actmgt.primaryControl: - Fee schedules built into Core Banking System (CBS)- Statement generation logs and billing audit- Advisory fee only triggered by signed documentation- System thresholds for cash handling tied to CBN limits

actmgt.source: Review of Automated Teller Machines Transaction Fees
actmgt.title: Review of ATM Fees
actmgt.description: In response to rising costs and the need to improve efficiency of Automated Teller Machine (ATM) services in the banking industry, the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) has reviewed the ATM transaction fees prescribed in Section 10.7 of the extant CBN Guide to Charges by Banks, Other Financial and Non-Bank Financial Institutions, 2020 (the Guide).  This review is expected to accelerate the deployment of ATMs and ensure that appropriate charges are applied by financial institutions to consumers of the service. Accordingly, banks and other financial institutions are advised to apply the following fees with effect from March 1, 2025:  The three free monthly withdrawals previously allowed for Remote-On-Us transactions (i.e., ATM withdrawals by other banks' customers or Not-On-Us consumers) in Nigeria under Section 10.6.2 of the Guide shall no longer apply.  For ATM transaction fees in Nigeria:  * On-Us withdrawals (when a customer withdraws cash from the ATM of their own bank) are free of charge.  * Not-On-Us withdrawals (when a customer uses another bank’s ATM):    * At on-site ATMs (located at bank branches), there is a charge of ₦100 for every ₦20,000 withdrawal.   * At off-site ATMs (not located at bank branches), there is a charge of ₦100 plus a surcharge of no more than ₦500 per ₦20,000 withdrawal. The surcharge is income for the ATM deployer/acquirer and must be clearly disclosed to the customer at the time of withdrawal.  For international withdrawals using either a debit or credit card, the customer will bear the actual cost charged by the international acquirer (cost recovery basis). Furthermore, the three free monthly withdrawals allowed for Remote-On-Us (other bank's customers/Not-On-Us consumers) in Nigeria under Section 10.6.2 of the Guide shall no longer apply.
actmgt.plain: The Bank shall implement the revised ATM transaction fees in line with the new directive of the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN), aimed at addressing rising service costs and improving ATM efficiency across the banking sector.  With effect from March 1, 2025:  * The Bank shall stop offering the three free monthly ATM withdrawals for customers of other banks (Remote-On-Us or Not-On-Us customers), as allowed under Section 10.6.2 of the CBN Guide to Charges.  * The Bank shall not charge customers for On-Us withdrawals, meaning when customers use the Bank’s own ATMs to withdraw cash.  * The Bank shall apply a fee of ₦100 per ₦20,000 when its customers use another bank’s ATM (Not-On-Us):    * If the ATM is located at a bank branch (on-site), the charge shall be ₦100 per ₦20,000 withdrawal.   * If the ATM is not at a bank branch (off-site), the charge shall be ₦100 plus a surcharge of no more than ₦500 per ₦20,000 withdrawal. This surcharge shall be disclosed clearly at the point of withdrawal and will be income to the ATM provider.  * The Bank shall pass on the actual cost (cost recovery) for any international ATM withdrawals done with debit or credit cards, based on the fees charged by the international acquirer.  ---  Let me know if you need a version for customer communication or policy documentation.
actmgt.riskDescription: Failure to implement the revised ATM transaction fee structure as directed by the Central Bank of Nigeria may result in regulatory non-compliance, financial penalties, reputational damage, and potential revenue loss due to improper fee application or customer dissatisfaction.

cash_mgt.title: Deposit of Banknotes by DMBs and CPCs at CBN
cash_mgt.description: In order to enhance the availability of clean notes and effect expeditious withdrawal of dirty notes from circulation, DMBs and CPCs making deposits at CBN, shall observe the procedure of classifying their cash deposits into two types:  a. Fit notes (if depositing notes already sorted by registered processing companies to CBN). b. Unfit notes (mutilated notes should be classified differently).  The notes thus classified shall be packaged into designated boxes according to denomination and as denoted in a & b above.  An unfit banknote refers to a genuine banknote that is no longer fit for circulation in accordance with the quality standard set by the Central Bank of Nigeria. A banknote shall be considered unfit for recirculation when:  a. It is badly soiled or there is a general distribution/localisation of dirt. b. It presents a limp/rag appearance due to excessive folding that results in the breakdown of the texture and structure of the note. c. It has added image or lettering marked on it. d. There is a hole that is more than 10 mm. e. Other defects detected by the approved processing systems.  A currency note shall be considered mutilated when:  i. Torn parts of the banknote are re-joined with adhesive tape in a manner which tries to preserve as nearly as possible the original design and size of the note. ii. The original size of the note has been reduced/lost through wear/tear or has been damaged by fire, rodents, insects, chemicals, defaced or perforated through other causes. iii. It is scorched or burnt to such an extent that although recognisable as such, it has become frail and brittle as to render further handling impossible. iv. More than half of the original size of the banknote is missing.  The financial institutions and the general public are advised to refer to the Central Bank of Nigeria Banknote Fitness Guidelines to acquaint themselves on visual representation of unfit banknotes.
cash_mgt.plain: The Bank shall :  1. Sort all cash deposits into two categories before sending them to the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN):     * *Fit notes* – clean notes that have already been sorted by a CBN-approved cash processing company.    * *Unfit notes* – dirty or damaged notes, which must be sorted separately.  2. Package the notes based on their category (fit or unfit) and by denomination into the boxes specified by the CBN.  3. Treat a banknote as **unfit** (not good for circulation) if:     * It is very dirty or has stains.    * It looks worn out, limp, or weak from folding and handling.    * It has writings, stamps, or extra markings.    * It has holes larger than 10mm.    * It fails any other checks during machine processing.  4. Treat a banknote as **mutilated** if:     * It has been torn and patched with tape.    * It has lost some parts due to wear, fire, chemicals, or other damage.    * It is burned, brittle, or too fragile to handle.    * More than half of the note is missing.  5. Ensure staff and customers are aware of the standards for unfit banknotes by referring to the CBN’s *Banknote Fitness Guidelines*, which show how to recognize bad notes.

cash_mgt.title: Re-Circulation of Banknotes by DMBs and CPCs
cash_mgt.description: To ensure that the banknotes in circulation are clean and of good quality, DMBs shall ensure that they process their banknotes using registered processing companies and classify them into fit and unfit. Any counterfeit notes discovered are to be returned to CBN. Only the banknotes which have been authenticated (i.e. verified free from counterfeit and unfit notes according to CBN standard) will be issued over the counter by banks or through their cash dispensing machines. Unfit banknotes shall not be re-circulated by DMBs and CPCs. However, a penal charge of N12,000 per box, or any amount determined by the Management of the Bank, shall apply for the deposit of unsorted banknotes. In addition, penalties as may be determined by the Bank, shall apply for the re-circulation of unfit banknotes.  There are machines that accept, count or sort banknotes automatically into fit, unfit, suspect or counterfeit. Only cash processing machines which have been duly configured, and approved by the Bank shall be used by CPCs.  The CBN shall set fitness standards/parameters for the processing machines by using test packs which may be changed periodically. The test packs shall serve as the reference notes and may be reviewed from time to time.  Against this background, the CBN on a regular basis shall monitor compliance as set therein.
cash_mgt.plain: The Bank shall: 1. Process banknotes using only registered processing companies. 2. Classify notes into fit and unfit categories. 3. Return all counterfeit notes to the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN). 4. Only issue authenticated banknotes (free from counterfeit or unfit classification) to customers—either over the counter or via ATMs. 5. Not re-circulate unfit banknotes. 6. Use CBN-approved and configured cash processing machines only. 7. Avoid depositing unsorted notes or face a ₦12,000/box penalty (or as revised by the CBN). 8. Avoid re-circulating unfit notes to prevent further CBN-determined penalties. 9. Comply with CBN fitness standards, including using test packs that are periodically reviewed. 10. Be prepared for CBN compliance monitoring at any time.

cash_mgt.description: The following categories of machines must meet specified standards set by the Bank and be adaptable to the features of the existing banknotes and the basic parameters set by the CBN from time to time. The Bank shall ensure conformity to these standards.  i Desktop sorting machines with authentication sensors. ii Banknote validators. iii Medium speed note sorters. iv High speed sorters. v Automated Teller Machines (ATMs).  The processing equipment would be adapted and confirmed by CBN to ensure uniformity and consistency with defined parameters.

cash_mgt.title: Mutilated Banknotes Management
cash_mgt.description: A mutilated banknote refers to a poor quality banknote that requires a special examination to determine its value. The note could be partially/permanently damaged by fire, water, dye, insects, rodents, or destroyed by natural disasters. The Central Bank of Nigeria and deposit money banks (DMBs) shall continue to receive mutilated notes from the public. The procedures for the treatment of mutilated notes and the notes for exchange are as enshrined in the Central Bank Operational Manual for the Operation of Mutilated Notes (refer to www.cbn.gov.ng). The manual provides uniform guidelines for receiving, processing and replacement of mutilated notes in the Bank.
cash_mgt.plain: The Bank shall: i. Continue to receive mutilated banknotes from customers and the public. ii. Follow the uniform procedures for the assessment, handling, and replacement of such notes as specified in the CBN Operational Manual for Mutilated Notes (available at www.cbn.gov.ng).
cash_mgt.riskDescription: - Noncompliance may lead to CBN penalties. - Mishandling or rejecting mutilated notes may cause reputational damage and customer dissatisfaction. - Risk of fraudulent redemption of non-genuine mutilated notes.
cash_mgt.owner: - Branch Operations Manager - Cash Officers / Tellers - Treasury Department - Compliance Unit
cash_mgt.primaryControl: - Train branch staff on CBN-approved mutilated note handling procedures. - Maintain a copy of the CBN Operational Manual at all cash-handling branches. - Use special handling forms and reporting templates for all such transactions. - Keep proper documentation and audit trail for every mutilated note received or replaced.

cash_mgt.title: Publicity Campaign
cash_mgt.description: The Bank shall from time to time carry out public sensitization with the following objectives:  a. Enlighten the public and other cash users on proper handling of the Naira banknotes. b. Promote and maintain public confidence in the legal tender currency. c. Stop the practice of recirculating dirty notes by DMBs as it contributes to the poor quality of notes in circulation. d. Educate the public on the basic security features of the banknotes so as to distinguish genuine notes from counterfeits. e. Underscore the importance of the currency as a symbol of national unity and heritage. f. Conduct training for security agencies and cash handlers using educational materials such as digital tools, instructional CD-ROM etc. g. Sustain the campaign against the abuse of the Naira. h. Establish mutual partnerships with the DMBs, cash handlers, security agencies and the public as stakeholders in currency management.
cash_mgt.plain: The Bank is expected to: i. Collaborate with the CBN in its public sensitization initiatives. ii. Stop recirculating dirty or unfit notes. iii. Support currency handling education efforts, including staff training and public awareness campaigns.
cash_mgt.riskDescription: - Failure to support or comply may result in regulatory sanctions. - Reputational damage if the bank is seen to be contributing to dirty note recirculation. - Undermines public trust in currency quality and brand perception of the bank.
cash_mgt.owner: - Corporate Communications Unit - Operations Department - Branch Operations Managers - Compliance Department
cash_mgt.primaryControl: - Integrate CBN sensitization themes in internal campaigns and customer touchpoints. - Train frontline staff on clean note policy and security features of genuine notes. - Monitor and prevent issuance of unfit or dirty notes from ATMs and counters. - Display anti-naira abuse messages in banking halls and on digital platforms.

cash_mgt.source: Penalty for Payment of Counterfeit Banknotes from ATMs/Teller Points
cash_mgt.title: COD/DIR/GEN/CMF/18/095
cash_mgt.description: The Management of the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) has observed with concern the incidences of counterfeits paid through some Deposit Money Banks' (DMBs) ATMs/Teller points. This situation has continued unabated despite moral suasion to the affected DMBs. To address this amongst others, the CBN in collaboration with key currency management stakeholders developed Banknote Fitness Guidelines and Clean Note Policy documents for the industry. In order to sustain public confidence in the National currency and ensure compliance with the provisions of the policy documents, the CBN has approved the following: i. Spot checks on DMBs' ATMs and Teller points to ensure compliance.
cash_mgt.plain: The Bank shall: i. Prevent dispensing of counterfeit notes via ATMs and teller points. ii. Comply with the Clean Note Policy and Banknote Fitness Guidelines. iii. Prepare for CBN spot checks on cash dispensing points (ATMs/tellers).
cash_mgt.riskDescription: - Regulatory penalties for dispensing counterfeit notes. - Loss of public trust, reputational damage, and possible litigation. - Increased regulatory scrutiny and operational disruption.
cash_mgt.owner: - Cash Management Department - ATM Custodians/Operations Teams - Branch Managers - Internal Audit & Compliance Departments
cash_mgt.primaryControl: - Use CBN-approved cash processing machines that verify authenticity. - Implement regular fitness sorting and counterfeit detection protocols. - Conduct routine spot testing of ATM dispensed notes. - Train staff and custodians on CBN's Clean Note Policy.

points.text: Spot checks on DMBs' ATMs and Teller points to ensure compliance.
points.content: Spot checks on DMBs' ATMs and Teller points to ensure compliance.

cash_mgt.source: Updated Penalty on Inappropriate Cash Disbursement Practices by Deposit Money Banks (DMBs)
cash_mgt.title: COD/DIR/INT/CIR/001/025
cash_mgt.description: The CBN has noted with dismay the prevalence of illicit flow of mint banknotes to currency hawkers and other unscrupulous economic agents that commodity Naira banknotes, thus, impeding efficient and effective cash distribution to banks’ customers and general public.  CBN will continue to intensify the periodic spot checks to the banking halls/ATMs to review cash payouts to banks’ customers, as well as mystery shopping to all identified cash hawking spots, across the country.  In this regard, any erring deposit money banks or financial institutions that is culpable of facilitating, aiding or abetting, by direct actions or inactions, illicit flow of mint banknotes to currency hawkers and unscrupulous economic agents that commodity Naira banknotes, shall be penalised at first instance ₦150,000,000.00 (One hundred and fifty million Naira) only, per erring branch and at later instances apply the full weight of relevant provisions of BOFIA 2020.  Therefore, CBN enjoins all DMBs and financial institutions to strengthen controls, processes and procedures around their Cash Managements Centres, Branch and Teller Operations.
cash_mgt.plain: The Bank shall: i. Prevent the diversion of mint banknotes to hawkers or unauthorized agents. ii. Ensure mint notes are distributed directly to customers through banking halls and ATMs. iii. Strengthen internal controls over Cash Management Centres, branch vaults, and teller operations. iv. Cooperate with CBN spot checks and mystery shopping assessments.
cash_mgt.riskDescription: - ₦150 million fine per branch on first violation. - Potential license revocation or legal sanctions under BOFIA 2020. - Severe reputational damage and media scrutiny.
cash_mgt.owner: - Head of Cash Management - Branch Managers - Teller Supervisors - Internal Control & Audit Units
cash_mgt.primaryControl: - Implement dual authorization for all disbursements of mint notes. - Maintain detailed logs of mint note inflows and disbursement. - Conduct internal surveillance of teller and vault operations. - Limit mint notes to customer-requested withdrawals only.

points.text: The bank must ensure mint notes are distributed directly to customers through banking halls and ATMs.

cash_mgt.title: COD/DIR/INT/CIR/001/006
cash_mgt.description: The Management of the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) observed with concern the increase number of Composed Banknotes deposited by Deposit Money Banks (DMBs) and request for replacement of such banknotes by members of the public. The existence of Composed Banknotes in the economy falsifies the true value of Currency in Circulation and can also be avenue for fraudulent activities.  A Composed Banknote is a banknote that comprises of several parts of different banknotes of the same denomination put together with the intention of receiving value.  Consequently, any Composed Banknote discovered in the deposit of DMBs shall attract penalty of 400% of the value.
cash_mgt.plain: The Bank shall screen all banknotes for composed notes (i.e., notes made from parts of different banknotes of same denomination) before deposit. Any composed banknote must not be included in deposits to the CBN.
cash_mgt.riskDescription: - Composed banknotes distort Currency in Circulation (CIC) reporting. - They can be used in fraudulent activities. - CBN imposes a 400% penalty on the value of such notes found in DMB deposits.
cash_mgt.owner: - Head of Cash Operations - Vault/Treasury Officers - Cash Sorting Units - Branch Managers
cash_mgt.primaryControl: - Use CBN-approved cash sorting machines with image sensors to detect composed notes. - Ensure manual verification by trained staff for doubtful notes. - Maintain segregated logs for suspected mutilated or composed notes.

sanctions.regulation: Chartered Institute of Bankers of Nigeria Act, 2007

sanctions.regulation: Chartered Institute of Bankers of Nigeria Act, 2007

returns.title: Monthly AML compliance status report to Board
returns.description: CCO must present compliance status report to the Board monthly.

returns.title: Annual report on AML/CFT/CPF compliance to CBN
returns.description: Report adequacy of compliance program and address identified weaknesses.

returns.title: Monthly returns on transactions with PEPs
returns.description: Report all transactions with Politically Exposed Persons to CBN and NFIU.

returns.title: Education & Training Compliance Return
returns.description: Submit report on AML/CFT/CPF education and training compliance to CBN.

returns.act: Guidance Note on Politically Exposed Persons (PEP)
returns.title: Monthly return on all transactions with PEPs
returns.sectionRef: CBN Guidance Note on PEPs – Section 11.2; AML/CFT/CPF Regs 2022 Section 29(4)
returns.description: The bank must submit monthly reports of all transactions involving Politically Exposed Persons to CBN and NFIU.

returns.act: Guidelines on Targeted Financial Sanctions Relating to Proliferation Financing
returns.title: Report on TFS Implementation
returns.description: The bank must submit a quarterly report to the CBN detailing the implementation status of Targeted Financial Sanctions (TFS) in a prescribed format.

returns.act: Guidelines on Targeted Financial Sanctions Related to Terrorism and Terrorism Financing
returns.title: Report on TFS Implementation (Terrorism Financing)
returns.description: The bank must submit quarterly reports to the CBN on the status of TFS implementation against terrorism financing, in the format advised by the CBN.

returns.title: Monthly Returns on Frauds, Forgeries, and Theft
returns.description: The bank must submit monthly reports to NDIC on any frauds, forgeries, or theft that occurred during the month, including a detailed report of each event.

returns.act: Exposure Draft of the Revised Consumer Protection Regulations 2.0
returns.title: Returns on Financial Literacy Programs Conducted
returns.description: Financial Institutions are required to submit quarterly reports detailing the financial literacy programs conducted during the period.

returns.act: Exposure Draft of the Revised Consumer Protection Regulations 2.0
returns.title: Submission of Root Cause Analysis Report (RCAR)
returns.description: Submit a quarterly RCAR capturing recurring complaint types, categories and codes, number of occurrences, root causes, planned remedial actions, and implementation timelines.
returns.frequency: Quarterly – on or before 5th of January, April, July, and October

returns.act: Exposure Draft of the Revised Consumer Protection Regulations 2.0
returns.title: Reporting of Complaints Statistics in Annual & Abridged Financial Statements
returns.description: Include complaints statistics in the bank’s annual report and abridged financial statement using the approved format (Annexure D or as updated by CBN).

returns.act: Exposure Draft of the Revised Consumer Protection Regulations 2.0
returns.title: Submission of Quarterly RCAR
returns.description: Submit quarterly RCARs to the CBN by the 14th of January, April, July, and October.

returns.act: Exposure Draft of the Revised Consumer Protection Regulations 2.0
returns.title: Complaints Statistics in Annual Reports
returns.description: Include complaints statistics in the institution’s Annual Report and Abridged Financial Statement using CBN-approved or prescribed format.

returns.act: Issuance of Risk-Based Cybersecurity Framework and Guidelines for Deposit Money Banks and Payment Service Providers
returns.title: Cybersecurity Self-Assessment Report
returns.description: Submit a Cybersecurity Self-Assessment Report for the previous year (Jan–Dec) to the Director, Banking Supervision, CBN. Report must be signed by the CISO and endorsed by Executive Management. Must follow CBN-prescribed format.

returns.title: Submission of Group Life Insurance Certificate
returns.description: Employer must maintain a group life insurance policy (minimum of 3x annual total emolument) and submit evidence of the policy to PenCom

returns.title: Remittance of Pension Contributions
returns.description: Employer must deduct and remit the combined pension contributions of employer and employee to the Pension Fund Custodian through the PFA
returns.frequency: Within 7 working days of salary payment

returns.title: Cost Recovery Reporting for Unremitted Contributions
returns.description: PenCom shall determine the cost of recovering unremitted contributions, which may be charged against the recovered penalty; employer may need to provide documentation

returns.title: RSA Transfer Request Handling
returns.description: An RSA holder may request transfer to another PFA only once per year, and the Bank must ensure smooth processing and non-obstruction

returns.title: Compliance with Fraud and Misconduct Investigations
returns.description: Employer must cooperate with PenCom during investigations of pension-related fraud, misconduct, or violations

returns.title: Submission of Policy Oversight Information
returns.description: Employer may be requested to provide information or updates to assist PenCom in performance monitoring or regulatory enforcement
returns.frequency: On request or as part of supervisory reviews

returns.title: Pension Complaint Review Participation
returns.description: RSA holders may lodge complaints with PenCom; employer must participate in PenCom’s review process without delay

returns.title: Handling of Arbitration or Legal Disputes
returns.description: Either party may escalate unresolved disputes to arbitration or National Industrial Court; outcomes are binding and enforceable with no limitation period

returns.title: NHF Deduction Remittance
returns.description: Deduct 2.5% from qualifying employees’ salaries and remit to Federal Mortgage Bank of Nigeria (FMBN) within one month of deduction.

returns.title: NHF Investment Reporting to CBN
returns.description: The Bank must allocate 10% of loan portfolio to NHF and report this to the Central Bank of Nigeria.

returns.title: NHF Fund Remittance to FMBN (via CBN)
returns.description: After collection by CBN, The Bank must ensure CBN remits funds to FMBN within two months. Requires accurate annual report by banks to CBN.
returns.frequency: Within 1 month after Financial year (FY) end

returns.title: Contributor Annual Statement Support
returns.description: Maintain accurate contributor records to support annual statements sent to employees by FMBN.

returns.title: Report of workplace injury, disease, or death
returns.description: Employer must report any work-related injury, disease, or death to NSITF.

returns.title: Application for compensation (general)
returns.description: Compensation application must be filed or determined.

returns.title: Exception – Late application for compensation with special cause
returns.description: If special circumstances exist, application may still be accepted.

returns.title: Compensation start date for late applications
returns.description: Board may pay compensation from the date of receipt of application if late with justifiable reason.

returns.title: Re-file of occupational disease application with new evidence
returns.description: Compensation can be paid if new medical/scientific evidence emerges later.
returns.frequency: No fixed timeline, but must be re-filed

returns.title: Proof of dependants
returns.description: Employer must provide proof of dependants when requested by the Board.

returns.title: Payroll returns and assessment
returns.description: Employer must submit payroll information for assessment of contribution.

returns.title: Failure to file accurate payroll returns
returns.description: If employer fails to file returns, Board may issue provisional assessment; employer must refund any excess.
returns.frequency: Triggered if Section 30 obligation is unmet

returns.title: Employer’s contribution to the Compensation Fund
returns.description: Mandatory employer contribution to NSITF Compensation Fund.

returns.title: Monthly Payment of National Minimum Wage
returns.description: Every commercial bank must pay each worker not less than ₦30,000.00 (or the prevailing minimum wage).

returns.title: Wages Must Not Be Below Minimum (Post-Deductions)
returns.description: Banks must ensure wages remain at or above the national minimum wage after statutory deductions.

returns.title: Retention of Wage and Payroll Records
returns.description: Commercial banks must keep wage records and payroll data to demonstrate compliance.

returns.title: Respond to Enforcement Notice or Appeal
returns.description: If the bank is served an enforcement notice for wage underpayment, it must either (a) pay arrears to affected workers within 30 days or (b) appeal the notice to the Minister of Labour and Employment within 30 days of receipt.

returns.title: Trade Union Claim on Behalf of Employee
returns.description: A trade union may escalate a non-payment complaint to the National Industrial Court.

returns.title: Inspection: Production of Payroll and Wage Records
returns.description: When requested by a labour officer, banks must present wage sheets, payroll, and employment records for inspection.

returns.title: Routine Inspection: Forwarding Reports to Minister
returns.description: Any non-compliance discovered during inspection is to be reported to the Minister and copied to labour centres.

returns.title: Monitoring of Compliance Commences
returns.description: Banks should be prepared for compliance monitoring.
returns.frequency: 6 months after commencement of the Act

returns.title: Deduction and remittance of union dues
returns.description: Deduct union dues from wages of employees who are members of registered trade unions and remit the deductions to the union’s registered office.
returns.frequency: Within a reasonable period or as prescribed by the Registrar of Trade Unions

returns.title: Reporting of Trade Dispute
returns.description: Any employer or worker involved in a trade dispute must report the dispute to the Minister of Labour and Employment in writing.
returns.frequency: Within 7 days of the dispute arising or being apprehended

returns.act: Compliance with Bank Employees, Etc (Declaration of Assets) Act
returns.title: Initial Asset Declaration for Existing Employees
returns.description: All existing bank employees must make full disclosure of assets.
returns.frequency: Within 14 days of commencement of the Act

returns.act: Compliance with Bank Employees, Etc (Declaration of Assets) Act
returns.title: Initial Asset Declaration for New Employees
returns.description: New employees must declare assets on assuming duty. Transfers/secondments are treated as new employment.
returns.frequency: Within 14 days of assumption of duty

returns.act: Compliance with Bank Employees, Etc (Declaration of Assets) Act
returns.title: Execution & Attestation of Asset Declaration Form
returns.description: Employees must execute Declaration of Assets (Form A) and have it attested by a Registrar of a superior court.
returns.frequency: Within 14 days of duty or Act commencement

returns.act: Compliance with Bank Employees, Etc (Declaration of Assets) Act
returns.title: Submission of Executed Asset Declaration Form
returns.description: Employees must submit completed asset declaration form to the Bank’s Chief Executive.
returns.frequency: Within 14 days of assumption of duty / Act commencement

returns.act: Compliance with Bank Employees, Etc (Declaration of Assets) Act
returns.title: Submission of Initial Asset Declaration to Authority
returns.description: Chief Executive must submit received Forms A & B to the appropriate authority.

returns.act: Compliance with Bank Employees, Etc (Declaration of Assets) Act
returns.title: Annual Asset Declaration (Employee)
returns.description: Employees must submit a declaration of assets acquired/disposed after initial declaration using Form C.
returns.frequency: Annually: Within 7 days of each declaration anniversary

returns.act: Compliance with Bank Employees, Etc (Declaration of Assets) Act
returns.title: Execution of Annual Declaration Form (Form C)
returns.description: Annual declaration must follow the process in Section 2 – attestation and prescribed format (Form C).
returns.frequency: Annually: Within 7 days of each declaration anniversary

returns.act: Compliance with Bank Employees, Etc (Declaration of Assets) Act
returns.title: Submission of Annual Declarations to Authority
returns.description: Chief Executive must submit received annual declarations to the appropriate authority.

returns.act: Compliance with Bank Employees, Etc (Declaration of Assets) Act
returns.title: Post-Employment Asset Declaration
returns.description: Former employees must declare assets annually for 2 years after exit. Bank must make forms available.
returns.frequency: Annually for 2 years post-exit (within 7 days of anniversary)

returns.act: Compliance with Bank Employees, Etc (Declaration of Assets) Act
returns.title: Provision of Forms to Ex-Employees
returns.description: Bank must promptly provide the asset declaration form to ex-employees upon request.

returns.act: Compliance with Bank Employees, Etc (Declaration of Assets) Act
returns.title: Biannual Staff Movement Return
returns.description: Submit list of staff who joined/left in last 6 months using Form D.
returns.frequency: Twice yearly: by 7th January and 7th July

returns.act: Compliance with Bank Employees, Etc (Declaration of Assets) Act
returns.title: Format of Staff Movement Report
returns.description: Staff movement list must comply with the format in Form D of the Schedule.
returns.frequency: Twice yearly: by 7th January and 7th July

returns.act: Revised Guidelines for Blacklisting for Banks and Other Financial Institutions in Nigeria
returns.title: Monthly Return on Blacklisted Individuals
returns.description: Banks and financial institutions must submit a return to the CBN by the 5th of each month showing details of individuals blacklisted. The return must include: (i) a declaration (signed by the MD and ECO or their acting officers) confirming due process; (ii) copies of Disciplinary Committee (DC) and Independent Review Panel (IRP) reports; (iii) evidence of notification and invitation of the individual; and (iv) evidence of communication of the final decision. A nil return is required if there is no blacklisting during the reporting period.
returns.frequency: Monthly, on or before the 5th day
returns.responsibleUnit: Compliance, Human Resources, Legal, Company Secretariat

returns.act: Revised Guidelines for Blacklisting for Banks and Other Financial Institutions in Nigeria
returns.title: Submission of monthly blacklisting returns to the CBN
returns.description: Financial Institutions must render monthly returns to the CBN on all blacklisted individuals in the prescribed format.

returns.act: Revised Guidelines for Blacklisting for Banks and Other Financial Institutions in Nigeria
returns.title: Attestation that due process was followed before blacklisting/delisting
returns.description: The MD and ECO must attest in writing that due process was followed before reaching a blacklisting/delisting decision.

returns.act: Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Act (FCCPA), 2018
returns.title: Notify FCCPC of proposed mergers/acquisitions
returns.description: Parties to a merger must notify the Commission in the prescribed manner before implementation.

returns.act: Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Act (FCCPA), 2018
returns.title: Notify Commission if parties determine merger is not notifiable
returns.description: If the merger is deemed not notifiable, the Commission must still be informed of the determination.

returns.title: Biannual Audit Summary (for >1,000 data subjects)
returns.description: A summary of internal data audits must be submitted to NITDA if >1,000 data subjects are processed within 6 months.

returns.title: Annual NDPR Audit Report (for >2,000 data subjects)
returns.description: Submit audit summary to NITDA detailing privacy controls and practices if >2,000 subjects were processed in a year.
returns.frequency: By March 15 of the following year

returns.title: Compliance Audit Report (CAR)
returns.description: Submission of annual report showing compliance posture and gaps
returns.frequency: Annually (by March 31 or 15 months after establishment)

returns.title: Incorporation of DPIA outcome into Compliance Audit Report (CAR)
returns.description: The results of the DPIA must be included in the organisation’s annual Compliance Audit Report submitted to the Commission.

returns.act: Report on the Three-Tiered Know Your Customer (TKYC) Compliance Exercise (2013)
returns.title: Suspicious Transactions Reporting (STRs)
returns.description: The Bank must report suspicious transactions to the NFIU.

returns.description: Issuers' Portal

returns.description: Issuers' Portal

returns.description: Public Interest Entities must submit a copy of their annual reports and financial statements to FRCN within 60 days after Board approval.

returns.act: Revised Guidelines on Supervisory Review Process of ICAAP

returns.description: Banks must submit to the CBN an annual report outlining their Internal Capital Adequacy Assessment Process (ICAAP)

returns.title: ICAAP Report with Board Resolutions & Senior Management Comments
returns.description: The report should be submitted to the CBN along with relevant board resolutions and senior management reports containing their comments on the ICAAP.

returns.act: Revised Guidelines on Supervisory Review Process of ICAAP
returns.title: Annual ICAAP Report & Supporting Documents
returns.description: Banks should submit to the CBN a comprehensive ICAAP report and supporting documents. The report as at 31st December should be submitted not later than 4 months after year-end (end of April).

returns.title: Monthly Capital Adequacy Return (Solo Basis):
returns.description: Submission of capital adequacy position on a stand-alone (solo) basis using prescribed reporting templates.

returns.title: Quarterly Capital Adequacy Return (Consolidated Basis

returns.act: Basel III Implementation by DMBs in Nigeria
returns.title: Basel III Capital Adequacy Returns
returns.description: Monthly regulatory return on Basel III compliance (capital adequacy, buffers, etc.)

returns.act: Regulatory Framework for Agent Banking in Nigeria
returns.title: Monthly Agent Banking Operations Return
returns.description: Submission of data and other information on agent operations
returns.frequency: Monthly – Not later than the 10th day of the following month

returns.act: Regulatory Framework for Agent Banking in Nigeria
returns.title: Annual Agent Banking Report
returns.description: Inclusion of all activities of agent banking operations in the annual reports and accounts
returns.frequency: Annually – With submission of annual reports and accounts

returns.act: Shared Agency Network Expansion Fund Initiative: Regulatory Data Rendition Requirements
returns.title: Daily Agent Banking Transaction Data Return
returns.description: Submission of agent banking transaction data in the mode and template prescribed by NIBSS for monitoring and evaluation of the Shared Agency Network Expansion Fund initiative

returns.act: Framework for Operation of the Shared Agent Network Expansion Facility (SANEF)
returns.title: Monthly returns on agent registration and onboarding status
returns.description: Submission of returns on agent registration and onboarding status

returns.act: Framework for Operation of the Shared Agent Network Expansion Facility (SANEF)
returns.title: Quarterly returns on repayment
returns.description: Render returns on repayment of facility

returns.act: Framework for Operation of the Shared Agent Network Expansion Facility (SANEF)
returns.title: Monthly records of transactions and services
returns.description: Submission of records of transactions and services onboarded agents conduct

returns.act: Prudential Guidelines for Deposit Money Banks in Nigeria, 2019
returns.title: Credit rating of Banks
returns.description: Submit the credit rating report to the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) within six (6) months after the end of the financial year.
returns.frequency: Within six (6) months after the end of the financial year.

returns.act: Circular To All Commercial, Merchant and Non-Interest Banks on Implementation of the Foreign Currency Disclosure, Deposit, Repatriation and Investment Scheme, 2024
returns.title: Monthly Return on Scheme Operations
returns.description: Every CMNIB shall render monthly returns on the operation of the Scheme.
returns.frequency: Monthly – Not later than the 14th day of the following month

returns.act: Guidelines for the Electronic Foreign Exchange Matching System (EFEMS)
returns.title: Daily Transaction Report
returns.description: Commercial banks must submit daily FX transaction reports to the CBN via EFEMS.
returns.frequency: Daily + Within 10 minutes for RFQ uploads

returns.act: Renewed Guidelines of International Money Transfer Services in Nigeria
returns.title: Weekly/Monthly Returns – IMTO Agent (ADB)
returns.description: Submit weekly and monthly returns using the prescribed template to the Director, Trade and Exchange Department, CBN Abuja

returns.act: Renewed Guidelines of International Money Transfer Services in Nigeria
returns.title: Trade Sheets of FX Sales – IMTO Agent (ADB)
returns.description: Submit weekly returns of trade sheets of FX sales at the Nigerian FX market

returns.act: Renewed Guidelines of International Money Transfer Services in Nigeria
returns.title: Suspicious Transactions Report – ADB
returns.description: Submit STRs to NFIU (Nigeria Financial Intelligence Unit)

returns.title: Quarterly Compliance Report
returns.description: Market Participants are required to submit a quarterly report to the Financial Markets Department (FMD) on the level of compliance to the FX Code.
returns.frequency: Within 14 days after each calendar quarter;

returns.act: Introduction of the Revised Foreign Exchange Manual
returns.title: Monthly FX Returns to CBN
returns.description: Authorized Dealers must submit monthly returns on specified FX transactions to the Central Bank of Nigeria.
returns.frequency: Monthly – not later than the 5th working day of the following month

returns.act: New measures to enhance local currency liquidity for settlement of diaspora remittances
returns.title: Daily FX Regulatory Returns
returns.description: Submission of  daily regulatory returns to the CBN containing relevant information on sources of funds and related transactions.

returns.title: Annual Training Contribution
returns.description: Bank must remit 1% of total annual payroll to the ITF if it has ≥5 employees or turnover ≥ ₦50 million.

returns.title: Breach Notification to the Commission
returns.description: Notify the Commission of a personal data breach likely to pose a risk to individuals' rights and freedoms
returns.frequency: Within 72 hours of becoming aware of the breach

returns.title: Update of Registration Information
returns.description: Notify Commission of any significant change in registration details

returns.act: Regulatory Framework for Bank Verification Number (BVN) Operations and Watch-List for the Nigerian Financial System, October, 2021
returns.title: Report BVNs of individuals in breach to NIBSS
returns.description: Report breach-related BVNs to NIBSS

returns.act: Regulatory Framework for Bank Verification Number (BVN) Operations and Watch-List for the Nigerian Financial System, October, 2021
returns.title: Report deceased customers' BVNs to NIBSS
returns.description: Update BVN database with “DECEASED” status

returns.title: STR – Suspicious Activity
returns.description: If during relationship you suspect ML/TF/PF, complete CDD then file STR.

returns.title: STR – Tipping Off Risk During CDD
returns.description: If conducting CDD may tip off a customer suspected of ML/TF/PF, the Bank must halt CDD and file an STR to the NFIU.

returns.title: Periodic Review of CDD Records
returns.description: Update CDD records: annually for high-risk, 18 months for medium-risk, 3 years for low-risk.

returns.act: National Identity Management Commission (NIMC) Act, 2007 (Mandatory Use of the National Identification Number Regulations, 2017)
returns.title: NIN Compliance Report Submission
returns.description: Submission of monthly compliance report detailing: (i) number of identifications added or renewed, (ii) status of compliance with NIN Regulations 2015, 2017, and Nigeria Biometrics Standards Regulations 2017,
returns.responsibleUnit: Compliance Department / IT Governance / Risk Management

returns.act: Corporate Governance Guidelines for Commercial Banks, Merchant, Non-Interest and Payment Service Banks and Financial Holding Companies in Nigeria
returns.title: Periodic statutory returns
returns.description: The bank shall render to the CBN such periodic returns as may be required under the terms and conditions of its license and extant CBN regulations
returns.frequency: As required under license terms or CBN directives

returns.title: Notification to CBN on outlet activity (commencement, closure, relocation, merger, upgrade, downgrade) and customer notice
returns.description: Banks must notify the CBN within 14 days of the commencement, closure, relocation, merger, upgrade or downgrade of any approved branch or outlet. In addition, a notice must be visibly posted for customers at the outlet prior to the action and must remain posted until the activity is completed.
returns.frequency: - CBN Notification: Within 14 days of the action - Customer Notice: Before and until closure/relocation/merger is completed

returns.act: Guidelines on the Establishment and Rationalization of Branches and Other Outlets for Banks in Nigeria (2014)
returns.title: Annual return on branch and outlet network activities
returns.description: Banks must file annual report on all branches/outlets opened, closed, relocated, or rationalized during the year.

returns.act: Revised Assessment Criteria for Approved Persons' Regime for Financial Institutions
returns.title: Reassessment of fitness and propriety
returns.description: Fitness and propriety of approved persons must be reassessed by the financial institution
returns.frequency: Every 2 years (or as may be directed by the CBN)

returns.act: Guidelines for whistle-blowing for banks and other financial institutions in Nigeria
returns.title: Submission of whistle-blowing policy to the CBN
returns.description: Banks must forward copies of their whistle-blowing policy/guidelines to the CBN.

returns.act: Guidelines for whistle-blowing for banks and other financial institutions in Nigeria
returns.title: Quarterly report on compliance with whistle-blowing guidelines (along with corporate governance returns)
returns.description: Banks must submit periodic reports on their level of compliance with the whistle-blowing guidelines.

returns.act: Guidelines for whistle-blowing for banks and other financial institutions in Nigeria
returns.title: Annual external auditor’s report on whistle-blowing compliance
returns.description: The bank’s external auditor must report annually to the CBN on the institution’s compliance with the whistle-blowing guidelines.

returns.title: Notification of Financial Year-End

returns.description: Must include full statutory information: registered office, directors, shareholders, shareholding structure, etc. Format as in Part I & II of the Seventh Schedule.

returns.title: Deadline for Annual Return

returns.title: Annex to Annual Return

returns.title: Annual Business Name Return

returns.description: Submit audited accounts to AGM and audit committee

returns.description: Submission of monthly balance sheet, liabilities, and advances for head office and branches

returns.act: Banks and Other Financial Institutions Act (BOFIA), 2020
returns.title: Ad-Hoc Statistical Returns
returns.description: Submit any data or returns requested by CBN

returns.act: Banks and Other Financial Institutions Act (BOFIA), 2020
returns.title: Annual Financial Statement Submission
returns.description: Submit audited financial statements to CBN

returns.act: Banks and Other Financial Institutions Act (BOFIA), 2020
returns.title: Publication of Audited Accounts
returns.description: Publish CBN-approved financials in two national newspapers and display in branches

returns.act: Banks and Other Financial Institutions Act (BOFIA), 2020
returns.title: Auditor Appointment Notification
returns.description: Notify CBN of appointment of new auditor (must be on CBN’s approved list)

returns.act: Banks and Other Financial Institutions Act (BOFIA), 2020
returns.title: Auditor Cessation Notification
returns.description: Inform CBN that auditor has ceased to act

returns.act: Banks and Other Financial Institutions Act (BOFIA), 2020
returns.title: Response to CBN Examination Report
returns.description: Submit Board-approved response to examination findings

returns.act: Banks and Other Financial Institutions Act (BOFIA), 2020
returns.title: Capital Adequacy Reports
returns.description: Submit reports demonstrating compliance with capital adequacy guidelines

returns.act: Banks and Other Financial Institutions Act (BOFIA), 2020
returns.title: Cybersecurity Compliance Reports
returns.description: Submit certifications showing compliance with CBN cybersecurity regulations

returns.title: Annual Review and Submission of Agreement
returns.description: Review Shared Services Agreement annually to reflect economic realities and submit to CBN.

returns.description: Banks must render an Interest Rate Risk in the Banking Book (IRRBB) report at the same level as their ICAAP report, covering every major currency where positions exceed 5% of assets or liabilities.

returns.title: Regulatory Submission to CBN (via ICAAP)
returns.description: Supervisory benchmarks (metrics) on reputational risk as part of the Internal Capital Adequacy Assessment Process (ICAAP) to the CBN.

returns.title: Regulatory Submission to CBN (via ICAAP)
returns.description: Submission of ICAAP report including stress test results, assessment of material exposures, and justification of scenario assumptions.
